textes.Selon le satellite Planck, quel est l'âg: According to the Planck satellite, what is the age of the Universe, in billions of years?
textes.des particules hypothétiques candidates: hypothetical particles that are candidates for dark matter
textes.Weakly Interacting Massive Particles. Ma: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles. Despite decades of searching, none has been detected.
textes.L'expansion de l'Univers signifie que le: The expansion of the Universe means that galaxies are moving away from one another on a large scale.
textes.Plus elles sont loin, plus elles s'éloig: The farther they are, the faster they recede: this is the Hubble-Lemaître law.
textes.La plus ancienne mention connue de Mercu: The oldest known mention of Mercury is on the MUL.APIN tablets, compiled around the 14th century BC, which call it "the jumping planet". The first probe to visit it, Mariner 10, dates from 1974.
textes.La tablette de Vénus d'Ammisaduqa note 2: The Venus tablet of Ammisaduqa records 21 years of Venus's risings and settings, observed in Babylon around the mid-17th century BC. It is known from 7th-century BC copies, including one from the library of Nineveh.
textes.Pluton avait été découverte le 18 févrie: Pluto had been discovered on 18 February 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh. Its name was suggested by Venetia Burney, an 11-year-old English girl; the New Horizons probe flew past it in 2015.
textes.Galilée découvre quatre lunes de Jupiter: Galileo discovered four moons of Jupiter in January 1610 and announced them in March in the Starry Messenger. Their current names, Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto, were suggested by Kepler and published by Simon Marius in 1614.
textes.Personne n'avait jamais vu la face caché: No one had ever seen the far side of the Moon until 7 October 1959, when the Soviet probe Luna 3 took the first photos of it.
textes.Les astronomes chaldéens connaissaient d: Chaldean astronomers already knew the saros, a cycle of 223 lunar months (about 18 years) after which eclipses repeat. The Antikythera mechanism, around 150-100 BC, incorporates it.
textes.Le premier objet de la ceinture, Cérès,: The belt's first object, Ceres, was discovered on 1 January 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi in Palermo. Lost from view, it was found again at the end of 1801 thanks to young Gauss's orbit calculations.
textes.En 1610, Galilée voit des « oreilles » à: In 1610, Galileo saw "ears" on Saturn. In 1612 they vanished (the rings were seen edge-on); it was Huygens who realised in 1655 that it was a flat ring.
textes.En juillet 1965, la sonde Mariner 4 envo: In July 1965, the Mariner 4 probe sent back the first close-up photos of Mars: a surface riddled with craters, like the Moon, to scientists' surprise.
textes.En 1705, Edmond Halley annonce que la co: In 1705, Edmond Halley announced that the comet seen in 1531, 1607 and 1682 would return in 1758. He died in 1742 and did not see it come back, on Christmas Day 1758. Its oldest known record is Chinese, in 240 BC.
textes.Le calendrier julien, proposé par Jules: The Julian calendar, proposed by Julius Caesar in 46 BC, added a day every four years. At first the priests got it wrong and added one every three years; Augustus had to correct it.
textes.Vers 1920, Arthur Eddington propose que: Around 1920, Arthur Eddington proposed that stars shine by fusing hydrogen into helium, well before fusion was understood. It was one of the first correct guesses about stellar energy.
textes.La première distance d'étoile fiable est: The first reliable distance to a star was measured in 1838 by Friedrich Bessel: about 10.3 light-years for 61 Cygni, using its parallax. Today we know it is at 11.4.
textes.La classification des étoiles par couleu: The classification of stars by colour and temperature, O B A F G K M, is the work of Annie Jump Cannon, at Harvard. She classified about 350,000 stars by hand, more than anyone else.
textes.En 1676, à l'Observatoire de Paris, le D: In 1676, at the Paris Observatory, the Dane Ole Rømer noticed that eclipses of Io, a moon of Jupiter, came late when the Earth was moving away: light takes time to travel.
textes.Proxima du Centaure est découverte en 19: Proxima Centauri was discovered in 1915 by Robert Innes, director of the Johannesburg observatory. He is the one who suggested the name "Proxima", "the nearest".
textes.Le diagramme qui range les étoiles selon: The diagram that sorts stars by colour and brightness, showing red giants and white dwarfs, was published by Ejnar Hertzsprung in 1911 and Henry Norris Russell in 1913, independently.
textes.En 1957, l'article « B2FH » de Margaret: In 1957, the "B2FH" paper by Margaret and Geoffrey Burbidge, William Fowler and Fred Hoyle explained how stars make elements heavier than iron by capturing neutrons.
textes.La Polaire n'a pas toujours indiqué le n: Polaris has not always marked the north: because of the precession of Earth's axis, the celestial pole was close to the star Thuban around 2750 BC. Polaris will be closest to it shortly after 2100.
textes.Dans l'Égypte ancienne, le premier lever: In ancient Egypt, the first rising of Sirius before dawn announced the Nile flood. In 1844, Bessel guessed it had an unseen companion; Alvan Clark saw it on 31 January 1862.
textes.En 1930, à 19 ans, sur le bateau qui l'e: In 1930, aged 19, on the ship taking him from India to England, Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar calculated the maximum mass of a white dwarf, about 1.44 Suns. Eddington mocked him publicly in 1935; he received the Nobel Prize in 1983.
textes.Ptolémée comptait 48 constellations. Les: Ptolemy counted 48 constellations. The boundaries of today's 88 constellations were drawn by the Belgian Eugène Delporte, adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1928 and published in 1930.
textes.Le modèle de Kepler s'écartait de 8 minu: Kepler's model was 8 minutes of arc off Tycho's measurements of Mars, more than Tycho's error. "These eight minutes alone", he wrote, would lead to a reform of astronomy.
textes.Cette « loi des aires » est publiée avec: This "law of areas" was published together with the first law in 1609 in Astronomia nova. The third law only came in 1619, in The Harmony of the World.
textes.Newton a imaginé un boulet tiré du haut: Newton imagined a cannonball fired from the top of a very high mountain, "with no air about the earth": fast enough, it falls without ever reaching the ground. The picture appeared in A Treatise of the System of the World, published in 1728.
textes.Newton a répondu par une expérience de p: Newton answered with a thought experiment: a cannonball fired from a very high mountain, fast enough, keeps falling without reaching the ground. The Moon does the same. The picture appeared in A Treatise of the System of the World (1728).
textes.Pythéas a relié les marées à la Lune ver: Pytheas linked the tides to the Moon around 325 BC, and Seleucus of Seleucia, in the 2nd century BC, made it their cause. Galileo got it wrong in 1632 by blaming the Earth's motions. Newton gave the first explanation by gravitation in the Principia, in 1687.
textes.Le premier module de la Station, Zarya,: The Station's first module, Zarya, was launched on 20 November 1998. It has been continuously inhabited since 2 November 2000.
textes.Herman Potočnik décrit cette orbite en 1: Herman Potočnik described this orbit in 1928, and Arthur C. Clarke popularised it in 1945 in Wireless World magazine, hence its nickname, the "Clarke orbit". The first geostationary satellite, Syncom 3, was launched in 1964.
textes.Arago aurait dit que Le Verrier avait dé: Arago is said to have remarked that Le Verrier had discovered a planet "with the point of his pen". Encouraged by this success, Le Verrier proposed another planet in 1859, Vulcan, close to the Sun: it was never found.
textes.En 1783, le pasteur anglais John Michell: In 1783, the English clergyman John Michell took this idea to its limit: a massive enough star would have an escape velocity greater than the speed of light. These "dark stars", published in 1784 in a letter to Cavendish, could be spotted through a companion.
textes.Kepler publie cette troisième loi en 161: Kepler published this third law in 1619 in Harmonices Mundi, The Harmony of the World, ten years after the first two.
textes.John Michell imagine dès 1783 des « étoi: As early as 1783, John Michell imagined "dark stars" whose light cannot escape; his idea was rediscovered in the 1970s. The first image of a black hole, M87*, was released by the Event Horizon Telescope on 10 April 2019, then that of Sagittarius A*, at the centre of our galaxy, on 12 May 2022.
textes.Le nom vient du grec galaxías kýklos, le: The name comes from the Greek galaxías kýklos, the "milky circle": in the myth, some of Hera's milk spilled across the sky when she pushed the infant Heracles away. Galileo was the first, in 1610, to resolve this band into stars with his telescope.
textes.Ce chiffre vient surtout du satellite eu: This figure comes mainly from the European Planck satellite, launched on 14 May 2009 and named after the physicist Max Planck. In 2013, its team announced an age of 13.798 billion years.
textes.Hubble repère des céphéides dans la nébu: Hubble spotted Cepheids in the Andromeda Nebula with the Hooker telescope on Mount Wilson. The New York Times reported his discovery on 23 November 1924, and he presented it to astronomers on 1 January 1925, despite opposition from Harlow Shapley.
textes.Doppler explique l'effet en 1842 et Fize: Doppler explained the effect in 1842 and Fizeau suggested in 1848 applying it to the lines of stars. In 1912, Vesto Slipher found that Andromeda is moving towards us; in 1929, Hubble linked the redshift of galaxies to their distance.
textes.Le nom « Big Bang » vient d'un adversair: The name "Big Bang" came from an opponent of the theory: Fred Hoyle, who backed a steady-state universe, spoke of "this big bang idea" on BBC radio in March 1949. He later denied meaning it as an insult.
textes.Ralph Alpher et Robert Herman le prédise: Ralph Alpher and Robert Herman predicted it as early as 1948, at about 5 K. Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson picked it up by chance at Bell Labs, first measured on 20 May 1964. Hearing the news, Robert Dicke, who was searching for it, said: "Boys, we've been scooped." Nobel Prize 1978.
textes.La source radio Sagittarius A* est décou: The radio source Sagittarius A* was discovered in February 1974 by Bruce Balick and Robert Brown. By following the orbit of the star S2 around it for years, Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez showed it is a giant black hole: Nobel Prize in Physics 2020.
textes.Galilée est le premier, en 1610, à voir: Galileo was the first, in 1610, to see with his telescope that the milky band of the Milky Way is made of countless stars. Today their number is estimated at between 100 and 400 billion.
textes.Le savant persan al-Soufi décrit Andromè: The Persian scholar al-Sufi described Andromeda around 964, in his Book of Fixed Stars, as a "small cloud": the oldest known mention of another galaxy. The collision, long predicted for 4 billion years from now, has been judged far less certain since a 2025 study.
textes.Dès 1884, Lord Kelvin estimait que beauc: As early as 1884, Lord Kelvin reckoned that many of the Galaxy's stars, "perhaps a great majority of them", might be dark bodies. In 1906, Henri Poincaré took up his calculation and spoke of "matière obscure", dark matter.
textes.Lemaître, prêtre catholique belge, publi: Lemaître, a Belgian Catholic priest, published his expanding universe in 1927 in the Annales de la Société scientifique de Bruxelles. Einstein told him: "Your calculations are correct, but your physics is abominable." In 2018, the International Astronomical Union renamed Hubble's law the "Hubble–Lemaître law".
textes.La spirale d'une galaxie est vue pour la: A galaxy's spiral was first seen with the Leviathan of Parsonstown, Lord Rosse's 72-inch telescope built in Ireland in 1845: it revealed the shape of M51, the Whirlpool Galaxy, which Rosse drew.
textes.Ptolémée en comptait déjà 48 dans l'Anti: Ptolemy already counted 48 in Antiquity; Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille added about a dozen in the southern sky around 1756. The boundaries of today's 88 constellations were drawn by Eugène Delporte, adopted by the IAU in 1928 and published in 1930.
textes.En 1838, Friedrich Bessel mesure la para: In 1838, Friedrich Bessel measured the parallax of the star 61 Cygni and noted that its light takes 10.3 years to reach us. The word "light-year" appeared in 1851 in a German popular article by Otto Ule. Eddington found it "an inconvenient and irrelevant unit".
textes.Polaris n'a pas toujours été l'étoile du: Polaris has not always been the North Star: because of precession, the celestial pole was near Thuban, in Draco, around 2750 BC. Polaris will be closest to it, about 0.45 degrees, soon after the year 2100.
textes.Newton construit son télescope fin 1668,: Newton built his telescope in late 1668, with a mirror of speculum metal, an alloy of tin and copper. A second one, shown to the Royal Society at the end of 1671, was presented to King Charles II in January 1672; Newton was elected to the Royal Society that same year.
textes.Halley propose en 1716 de mesurer cette: In 1716 Halley proposed measuring this distance using the transits of Venus across the Sun. Those of 1761 and 1769 sent expeditions all over the world, including James Cook's to Tahiti; Le Gentil travelled for over eight years to see them. Lalande derived 153 million km from them in 1771.
textes.Léon Foucault rend la rotation de la Ter: Léon Foucault made the Earth's rotation visible in February 1851, with a pendulum hung in the Meridian room of the Paris Observatory. A few weeks later, he hung it from a 67-metre wire under the dome of the Panthéon.
textes.Le télescope James Webb, mené par la NAS: The James Webb telescope, led by NASA with the European and Canadian agencies, was launched on 25 December 2021 by an Ariane 5 from Kourou. It is named after James E. Webb, NASA administrator from 1961 to 1968. Its first image was released on 11 July 2022.
textes.En 1866, l'Italien Giovanni Schiaparelli: In 1866, the Italian Giovanni Schiaparelli discovered that meteor showers are linked to comets: the August Perseids follow the orbit of comet Swift–Tuttle. Some Catholics call them the "tears of Saint Lawrence".
textes.Angelo Secchi classe les spectres des ét: Angelo Secchi classified the spectra of stars in the 1860s and 1870s. At Harvard, Williamina Fleming and then Annie Jump Cannon set up the order O, B, A, F, G, K, M, and Cecilia Payne later showed it is a temperature scale, from hottest to coolest.
textes.Spoutnik 1 est lancé le 4 octobre 1957 d: Sputnik 1 was launched on 4 October 1957 from Tyuratam, today's Baikonur: a 58 cm, 83.6 kg sphere whose "beep, beep" could be heard on the radio. It burned up re-entering the atmosphere on 4 January 1958. In the United States it set off the "Sputnik crisis", the start of the space race.
textes.Au décollage, le 12 avril 1961, Gagarine: At lift-off, on 12 April 1961, Gagarin said "Poyekhali!", "Let's go!". He made a single orbit of the Earth and ejected at 7 km altitude to land by parachute, which the USSR only admitted in 1971.
textes.Newton pose la loi de l'action et de la: Newton set out the law of action and reaction in the Principia in 1687. Yet in 1920 The New York Times mocked Robert Goddard, claiming a rocket cannot move in a vacuum; it printed a correction on 17 July 1969, during the Apollo 11 flight. Goddard had launched the first liquid-fuelled rocket on 16 March 1926.
textes.Dès le XVIIe siècle, Newton expliquait l: As early as the 17th century, Newton explained an orbit as a fall: his cannonball fired from a very high mountain, fast enough, falls without ever reaching the ground. The picture appeared in A Treatise of the System of the World (1728).
textes.Valentina Terechkova, ouvrière du textil: Valentina Tereshkova, a textile worker and amateur skydiver, flew solo aboard Vostok 6 on 16 June 1963, under the call sign Chaika, "Seagull". She orbited the Earth 48 times in almost three days. No woman went to space again until Svetlana Savitskaya, in 1982.
textes.Ils ont marché sur la Lune lors de six a: They walked on the Moon during six Apollo landings, between July 1969 and December 1972. The first, Neil Armstrong, spoke of "one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind"; the last to climb back into the module was Eugene Cernan.
textes.Voyager 1 est lancée le 5 septembre 1977: Voyager 1 was launched on 5 September 1977. It carries a golden record prepared by a team including Carl Sagan, took the 1990 photo of Earth known as the Pale Blue Dot, and entered interstellar space on 25 August 2012, the first probe to do so.
textes.John Glenn a demandé Katherine Johnson p: John Glenn asked for Katherine Johnson by name and refused to fly until she had personally rechecked the computers' calculations for his Friendship 7 flight. Barack Obama gave her the Presidential Medal of Freedom on 24 November 2015; the film Hidden Figures came out in December 2016.
textes.Tsiolkovski, sourd depuis ses neuf ans a: Tsiolkovsky, deaf since the age of nine after scarlet fever, had been teaching in Kaluga since 1892. His article appeared in May 1903. In 1911 he wrote: "Earth is the cradle of humanity, but one cannot live in a cradle forever."
textes.On a longtemps annoncé 108 minutes ; sel: The figure long given was 108 minutes; according to more recent sources, the Vostok 1 flight lasted 106 minutes. Gagarin made a single orbit of the Earth, then ejected at 7 km altitude, which the USSR concealed until 1971.
textes.Perseverance se pose dans le cratère Jez: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021; its name was suggested by Alexander Mather, a schoolboy, in a contest. On 19 April 2021, the small Ingenuity helicopter it carried made the first powered flight on another planet.
textes.Cette vitesse vient du boulet de Newton: This speed goes back to Newton's cannonball: fired fast enough from a high mountain, it falls without ever reaching the ground. Newton described the experiment in A Treatise of the System of the World, published in 1728.
textes.Michel Mayor et Didier Queloz annoncent: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced 51 Pegasi b on 6 October 1995, measured with the ELODIE spectrograph at the Haute-Provence Observatory. A giant planet so close to its star contradicted the theories. It was named Dimidium in 2015, and its discoverers received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2019.
textes.Le premier transit d'exoplanète, celui d: The first exoplanet transit, that of HD 209458 b, was observed in 1999 by two teams led by David Charbonneau and Gregory Henry. The space telescopes CoRoT, Kepler (launched in March 2009) and then TESS (April 2018) made it their method.
textes.C'est la méthode de la première exoplanè: This is the method behind the first exoplanet around a Sun-like star: in 1995, Mayor and Queloz measured 51 Pegasi b this way with the ELODIE spectrograph at the Haute-Provence Observatory.
textes.Les toutes premières exoplanètes confirm: The very first confirmed exoplanets orbit a pulsar: Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail discovered them on 9 January 1992 with the Arecibo radio telescope, in Puerto Rico.
textes.L'expression « zone habitable » apparaît: The phrase "habitable zone" may have appeared as early as 1913 with Edward Maunder; Hubertus Strughold spoke of an "ecosphere" in 1953 and Su-Shu Huang developed the modern idea in the 1950s and 1960s. The nickname "Goldilocks zone", neither too hot nor too cold, dates from the 1970s.
textes.Frank Drake l'écrit en 1961 comme simple: Frank Drake wrote it in 1961 as a mere agenda for the Green Bank conference, the first scientific meeting on the search for extraterrestrial intelligence. The participants called themselves "The Order of the Dolphin". The year before, his Project Ozma had listened to two nearby stars and picked up nothing.
textes.En 1950 à Los Alamos, en allant déjeuner: In 1950 at Los Alamos, walking to lunch with Emil Konopinski, Edward Teller and Herbert York, Fermi reportedly said: "But where is everybody?" Tsiolkovsky had already raised the question in the 1930s, and Michael Hart examined it in detail in 1975.
textes.Le 15 août 1977, le radiotélescope Big E: On 15 August 1977, Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope picked up a 72-second signal. Going over the printouts, astronomer Jerry Ehman circled "6EQUJ5" and wrote "Wow!" in the margin. A 2024 study suggests instead a cold hydrogen cloud that suddenly brightened.
textes.Europe est découverte par Galilée le 8 j: Europa was discovered by Galileo on 8 January 1610. The Galileo probe, orbiting Jupiter from 1995 to 2003, detected an induced magnetic field there that betrays a salty water ocean under the ice. The Europa Clipper mission left to explore it on 14 October 2024.
textes.Les fausses alertes sont nombreuses : la: False alarms are common: the phosphine detected on Venus in 2020 and the dimethyl sulfide suspected on K2-18b in 2023 were both later given possible explanations without life.
textes.L'étoile TRAPPIST-1 est découverte en 19: The star TRAPPIST-1 was discovered in 1999 by John Gizis. In 2016, the team of the Belgian Michaël Gillon, at the University of Liège, found planets around it with the TRAPPIST telescope at La Silla, Chile; in 2017, further analysis added more.
textes.Proxima b est annoncée le 24 août 2016 p: Proxima b was announced on 24 August 2016 by the European Southern Observatory, after the Pale Red Dot campaign led by Anglada-Escudé's team.
textes.Étudiant l'amas de Coma en 1933, Zwicky: Studying the Coma Cluster in 1933, Zwicky found far more mass than could be seen and called it "dunkle Materie", dark matter. The phrase already existed in French: Poincaré had spoken of "matière obscure" in 1906.
textes.Vera Rubin travaillait avec Kent Ford, f: Vera Rubin worked with Kent Ford, an instrument-maker, and his image-tube spectrograph. Their 1970 paper dealt with the rotation of Andromeda. In 2019, the large LSST telescope was renamed the Vera C. Rubin Observatory.
textes.L'idée de corps célestes invisibles est: The idea of invisible celestial bodies is old: in 1884, Lord Kelvin supposed that many of the Galaxy's stars might be dark, and Poincaré spoke of "matière obscure", dark matter, in 1906.
textes.Les résultats finaux du satellite Planck: The final results of the Planck satellite, in 2018, give about 4.9% ordinary matter, 26.6% dark matter and 68.5% dark energy.
textes.L'accélération de l'expansion est découv: The accelerating expansion was discovered in 1998 by two rival teams, the Supernova Cosmology Project and the High-Z Supernova Search Team, using distant type Ia supernovae. Three of their members were awarded the Nobel Prize.
textes.Einstein montre en 1915 que la lumière d: In 1915 Einstein showed that light should be bent twice as much as Newton predicts. Eddington and Dyson checked it during the eclipse of 29 May 1919, at Sobral in Brazil and on Príncipe. Zwicky suggested galaxies as lenses in 1937; the first one was found in 1979.
textes.Le nom MACHO a été forgé par l'astrophys: The name MACHO was coined by the astrophysicist Kim Griest. The big microlensing surveys did not find enough of them: the MACHO team claimed perhaps 20%, the EROS2 team did not confirm it, and the Hubble telescope showed that less than 1% of the halo is made of red dwarfs.
textes.La NASA annonce le résultat le 21 août 2: NASA announced the result on 21 August 2006 under the title "NASA Finds Direct Proof of Dark Matter", based on Chandra X-ray images and the paper by Clowe and colleagues. Supporters of modified gravity (MOND) still dispute this reading.
textes.Einstein introduit sa constante en 1917: Einstein introduced his constant in 1917 to get a static universe, then abandoned it after Hubble confirmed the expansion. That he called it his "biggest blunder" rests only on George Gamow: the attribution is still debated.
textes.Planck est lancé le 14 mai 2009 avec l'o: Planck was launched on 14 May 2009 together with the Herschel observatory, on an Ariane 5 from French Guiana. It was switched off on 23 October 2013. Its first results, in 2013, gave 13.798 billion years.
textes.Lemaître propose l'expansion en 1927, Hu: Lemaître proposed the expansion in 1927, and Hubble published the relation between redshift and distance in 1929. In 2018, after a 78% vote, the International Astronomical Union recommended calling it the "Hubble–Lemaître law".
textes.{comp}. Kepler a passé des années sur l': {comp}. Kepler spent years on the orbit of Mars. You have a few minutes.
textes.Astronomie. Tycho Brahe a perdu le bout: Astronomy. Tycho Brahe lost the tip of his nose in a duel, over a quarrel about mathematics. Keep yours: {comp}.
textes.Hubble a vu l'Univers s'étendre. Voyons: Hubble saw the Universe expand. Let's see if your score follows. {comp}.
Right. Galileo would have seen it through his telescope. You, with the naked eye.
textes.Bonne réponse. Cecilia Payne a dû écrire: Good answer. Cecilia Payne had to write that her results were “not real.” Yours are very real.
textes.Correct. Vous tournez autour de la bonne: Correct. You're orbiting the right answer on a nice ellipse, as Kepler predicted.
textes.Exact. Même les étoiles applaudissent. A: Exactly. Even the stars are applauding. A few light-years late.
Missed. Pluto was demoted in 2006. So are you, temporarily.
textes.Faux. Ptolémée s'est trompé pendant quat: Wrong. Ptolemy was wrong for fourteen centuries, with great precision. You were brief and approximate.
textes.Erreur. Percival Lowell voyait des canau: Error. Percival Lowell saw canals on Mars. You see a right answer where there isn't one.
textes.Houston, nous avons un problème. Il s'ap: Houston, we have a problem. Its name is you.
textes.Mathématicienne et astronome d'Alexandri: A mathematician and astronomer in Alexandria, she taught philosophy to students who came from afar. Her student Synesius owed her the art of building an astrolabe, and wrote to her asking her to have a hydroscope made for him. She was murdered by a Christian mob in 415.
textes.Calculatrice à la NASA, elle vérifie à l: A NASA “computer,” she checked by hand the trajectories for John Glenn's mission in 1962. Glenn had asked: “Get the girl to check the numbers. If she says they're good, I'm ready to go.”
textes.Astronome de la cour des Han, il constru: An astronomer at the Han court, in 132 he built a bronze seismoscope: eight dragons each held a ball, which dropped into a toad's mouth on the side of the earthquake. In 138, a ball dropped without anyone in the capital feeling anything. A messenger confirmed the earthquake a few days later.
textes.À 23 ans, il écrit un traité en vers où: At 23, he wrote a treatise in verse stating that the Earth spins on itself, which explains the apparent motion of the stars. He gave π as 3.1416 and explained eclipses by the shadows of the Earth and Moon, not by a demon swallowing the Sun.
textes.« Calculatrice » à l'observatoire de Har: A “computer” at the Harvard observatory, paid 30 cents an hour, she studied thousands of variable stars on photographic plates. In 1912, she discovered that the brightest Cepheids blink more slowly. That was the yardstick that would let Hubble measure the distance to Andromeda.
textes.Dans sa thèse de 1925, elle montre que l: In her 1925 thesis, she showed that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium. The astronomer Henry Norris Russell persuaded her to write that this result was “almost certainly not real.” Four years later, he reached the same conclusion and published it.
textes.Ce dominicain défroqué affirme que l'Uni: This defrocked Dominican claimed that the Universe is infinite and that the stars are suns surrounded by planets, perhaps inhabited. He was burned in Rome in 1600. His countless worlds were among the charges, but alongside theses on the Trinity and Christ that weighed more heavily.
textes.En mesurant la vitesse des étoiles dans: Measuring the speed of stars in galaxies, she found that those at the edge orbit as fast as those at the center: an invisible mass is missing. It is the best evidence for dark matter. At Mount Palomar, with no women's restroom, she taped a paper skirt onto the pictogram.
textes.Maîtriser les orbites. L'IA vous interdi: Master orbits. The AI now forbids you to believe the sink story.
textes.L'eau ne tourne pas dans l'autre sens da: Water does not swirl the other way in Southern Hemisphere sinks: at that scale, the Coriolis force is far too weak compared with the shape of the basin and the eddies. At MIT in 1962, Ascher Shapiro had to let the water in a 2 m wide tank settle for 24 hours to measure it.
textes.Maîtriser le Système solaire. Félicitati: Master the Solar System. Congratulations, you finally know why it's cold in winter.
textes.Les saisons ne viennent pas de la distan: The seasons don't come from the distance to the Sun: the Earth is closest to it in early January, in the middle of the Northern Hemisphere's winter. It is the tilt of its axis that changes the height of the Sun and the length of the day.
textes.Maîtriser les étoiles. Vous êtes, littér: Master stars. You are, literally, made of what you just learned.
textes.Le carbone, l'oxygène et le fer de notre: The carbon, oxygen and iron in our bodies were made in stars. The mechanism was described in 1957 in a paper that became famous under its four authors' initials: B²FH.
textes.Maîtriser les galaxies et le Big Bang. L: Master galaxies and the Big Bang. The name, for its part, was a jibe.
textes.Fred Hoyle, qui défendait un Univers éte: Fred Hoyle, who championed an eternal Universe, coined the expression “Big Bang” in March 1949 on BBC radio to describe the rival theory. People often hear mockery in it, which Hoyle always denied. The name stuck, and so did the theory.
textes.Colomb avait tort, mais pas pour ça: Columbus was wrong, but not about that
Master the first diamond of Cosmos.
textes.Au temps de Colomb, les savants savaient: In Columbus's time, scholars knew the Earth was round; Eratosthenes had even measured it around 240 BC. Columbus was wrong about its size, which he thought much smaller. The myth of the medieval flat Earth comes mostly from the 19th century.
textes.Maîtriser 4 compétences. L'arbre de l'As: Master 4 skills. The tree of Astronomy opens.
textes.« Et pourtant elle tourne » : Galilée ne: “And yet it moves”: Galileo probably never murmured it before his judges in 1633. The phrase first appears in 1757, in a book by Giuseppe Baretti, more than a century after the trial.
textes.Maîtriser l'observation du ciel. Ces éto: Master observing the sky. These stars aren't dead. They're watching you.
textes.On dit que les étoiles que l'on voit son: It is said that the stars we see may have died long ago. Almost all those visible to the naked eye are less than a few thousand light-years away, and live for millions or billions of years. Their light is late, not their death certificate.
textes.Maîtriser la conquête spatiale. Non, les: Master space exploration. No, the Russians didn't “just use a pencil.”
textes.La NASA aurait dépensé des millions pour: NASA supposedly spent millions on a pen that writes in space, while the Soviets used a pencil. False: Paul Fisher developed it at his own expense, and both agencies bought it, for a few dollars apiece. Pencils were a problem: the lead breaks and graphite dust conducts electricity.
textes.Les premières étaient autour d'un mort: The first ones orbited a dead star
textes.Maîtriser les exoplanètes et la vie aill: Master exoplanets and life elsewhere. The first system discovered orbits a stellar corpse.
textes.Les premières exoplanètes confirmées, en: The first confirmed exoplanets, in 1992, did not orbit a star like the Sun, but a pulsar, the collapsed core of a star that had exploded. Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail spotted them from irregularities in its pulses.
textes.Maîtriser la matière et l'énergie noires: Master dark matter and dark energy. Eighty-five percent of matter escapes you. You too.
textes.En 1933, Fritz Zwicky mesure les galaxie: In 1933, Fritz Zwicky measured the galaxies of the Coma cluster: they moved too fast for the cluster to hold together. An invisible mass was needed, “dunkle Materie.” No one followed him for forty years. He reportedly called his colleagues “spherical bastards”: bastards whichever way you looked at them.
Pass three Cosmos quizzes without a mistake. The AI might give you your name. Or not.
textes.En 1781, William Herschel, musicien deve: In 1781, William Herschel, a musician turned astronomer, discovered a new planet, the first since antiquity. He wanted to call it “Georgium Sidus,” George's star, in honor of King George III, who paid him a pension. Astronomers preferred Uranus.
textes.Construire un argument, persuader, repér: Building an argument, persuading, spotting fallacies.
textes.Vers 1450, à Mayence, Johannes Gutenberg: Around 1450, in Mainz, Johannes Gutenberg combined movable metal type, an oil-based ink and a screw press, perhaps inspired by wine or oil presses. His Bible came out around 1455, in about 180 copies. Movable type already existed in China, with Bi Sheng around 1040, and in Korea. But in Europe, printing made the circulation of ideas explode: some 27,500 different works printed before 1501 still survive.
Printing spread ideas. And errors, 180 copies at a time.
textes.Diderot et d'Alembert lancent l'Encyclop: Diderot and d'Alembert launched the Encyclopédie, or Reasoned Dictionary of the Sciences, Arts and Crafts: 17 volumes of text, 11 of plates and more than 70,000 articles, published until 1772 despite two bans. The plates show trades in detail, from pin making to wig making. In 1759, the pope put it on the Index.
textes.70 000 articles, deux interdictions et u: 70,000 articles, two bans and an angry pope. The AI thinks you have it easy.
textes.En 1764, Diderot découvre que son librai: In 1764, Diderot discovered that his publisher had secretly censored some of his articles. Since then, the Encyclopédie has been reread with care. So will you.
textes.Vers 2300 av. J.-C., Enheduanna, fille d: Around 2300 BC, Enheduanna, daughter of King Sargon of Akkad, is high priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur. Hymns are attributed to her, including The Exaltation of Inanna, which would make her the oldest author known by name. Caution, though: the copies we have date from about six centuries after her, and many Assyriologists doubt she wrote them. Her name might even refer to her office rather than a person.
textes.Premier auteur de l'histoire, et déjà so: The first author in history, and already suspected of not writing her own text. Plagiarism has a bright future.
textes.Aux VIIIe ou VIIe siècles av. J.-C., l'I: In the 8th or 7th century BC, the Iliad and the Odyssey take shape in Greece. These long poems in dactylic hexameter, divided into 24 books each, come from an oral tradition: bards improvised using ready-made formulas such as "rosy-fingered Dawn" or "crafty Odysseus". Milman Parry showed it from 1928 onwards. As for Homer himself, his existence remains a mystery: this is the "Homeric question".
textes.Des formules toutes prêtes pour tenir de: Ready-made formulas to last for hours without notes. Your formula is "um".
textes.Au Ve siècle av. J.-C., à Syracuse, le t: In the 5th century BC, in Syracuse, the tyrant is driven out and democracy takes hold. Citizens who lost their land under the tyrants rush to court to get it back, without lawyers. Corax teaches them to plead: a speech in parts, from introduction to conclusion, and arguments from probability. His pupil Tisias refuses to pay him; at the trial, the judge dismisses them both: "a bad egg from a bad crow". Corax means crow. Possibly a legend, by the way.
textes.Le premier prof de rhétorique n'a pas ét: The first rhetoric teacher was never paid by his pupil. I sympathise: you already owe me three right answers.
textes.En 427 av. J.-C., Gorgias, venu de Léont: In 427 BC, Gorgias, from Leontini in Sicily, comes to Athens as an ambassador, at about sixty. The Athenians are dazzled by his prose: antitheses, clauses of equal length, matching endings, almost poetry without the metre. In his Encomium of Helen, he clears the most blamed woman in Greece: speech, he says, acts on the soul as drugs act on the body. Tradition has him dying at about 108.
textes.Défendre Hélène de Troie, c'est le nivea: Defending Helen of Troy is expert level. Defending your last answer, even Gorgias would have given up.
textes.Vers 351 av. J.-C., Démosthène prononce: Around 351 BC, Demosthenes delivers the First Philippic against Philip of Macedon. It was no sure thing: according to Plutarch, the young orator had a muddled, stammering delivery. To cure it, he spoke with pebbles in his mouth, recited verse while running, practised in front of a large mirror in an underground study, and shaved half his head so he could not go out.
textes.Des cailloux dans la bouche et la moitié: Pebbles in his mouth and half his head shaved. You have no excuse, you just have a phone.
textes.Au IVe siècle av. J.-C., à Athènes, Aris: In the 4th century BC, in Athens, Aristotle defines rhetoric as the ability to see, in each case, the available means of persuasion. He names three levers: ethos, the speaker's credibility; pathos, the audience's emotions; logos, the reasoning. And three kinds of speech, by audience: deliberative for the assembly, forensic for the court, epideictic for praise or blame. Communication handbooks still copy him.
textes.Votre ethos est fragile, votre pathos en: Your ethos is fragile, your pathos overwhelming, and your logos on holiday.
textes.Le 7 ou le 8 novembre 63 av. J.-C., au t: On 7 or 8 November 63 BC, in the temple of Jupiter Stator, the consul Cicero turns to Catiline, present in the Senate, who is plotting against the Republic: "How long, Catiline, will you abuse our patience?" Further on: "O times, O customs!" Catiline leaves Rome. His accomplices still in the city are executed without trial, on the Senate's advice, which Cicero would later be blamed for.
textes.« Jusques à quand abuserez-vous de ma pa: "How long will you abuse my patience?" Asking for a friend. Me.
textes.Vers 95, Quintilien, né à Calagurris en: Around 95, Quintilian, born at Calagurris in Hispania and head of a public school of rhetoric in Rome, publishes the Institutes of Oratory in twelve books. He trains the orator from childhood and takes up Cato the Elder's formula: the orator is "a good man skilled at speaking". The complete text is lost in the Middle Ages; in 1416, the humanist Poggio finds it at the abbey of Saint Gall, buried in dust.
textes.Un homme de bien habile à parler. Sur ce: A good man skilled at speaking. Of those two criteria, you meet... let me look.
textes.Le 27 novembre 1095, au dernier jour du: On 27 November 1095, on the last day of the Council of Clermont, Pope Urban II calls on Christians to go East and promises remission of sins to those who go. According to Robert the Monk, the crowd spontaneously cries "God wills it!". But no exact text of the speech survives: there are five very different versions, all written years later. The First Crusade sets off the following year.
textes.Un discours dont personne n'a le texte a: A speech nobody has the text of launched a crusade. Your class notes have launched nothing at all.
textes.Le 31 octobre 1517, Martin Luther envoie: On 31 October 1517, Martin Luther sends Albert of Brandenburg, Archbishop of Mainz, a letter and 95 theses against the preaching of indulgences. The image of Luther nailing his theses to the church door in Wittenberg comes from Melanchthon and remains doubtful. What is certain is the printing press: hundreds of Latin copies circulate in 1517, a German translation follows the same year, and his Sermon on Indulgences is reprinted twenty times.
textes.Le coup de marteau sur la porte est sans: The hammer blow on the door is probably a legend. The one on your score is very real.
textes.En 1622, le pape Grégoire XV crée la Sac: In 1622, Pope Gregory XV creates the Sacra Congregatio de Propaganda Fide, tasked with spreading the Catholic faith in non-Catholic countries, in the midst of the Counter-Reformation. Propaganda, in Latin, simply means "what is to be propagated". The word moves to secular matters from the 1790s and only takes on its negative meaning in the 20th century, notably after the great campaigns of the First World War.
textes.Au départ, propagande voulait dire « à r: Originally, propaganda meant "to be spread". Like your mistakes, which spread very well on their own.
textes.Vers 1831, Arthur Schopenhauer rédige La: Around 1831, Arthur Schopenhauer writes Eristic Dialectic, or the art of being right. He is not after truth but victory in a dispute, and lists 38 stratagems, often outright dishonest, for winning no matter what. The last one, when all is lost: become personal, insulting, rude. The manuscript would only be published after his death, among his posthumous papers.
Thirty-eight tricks to win a debate. You only know one: change the subject. So step back a little.
textes.D'août à octobre 1858, Abraham Lincoln e: From August to October 1858, Abraham Lincoln and Stephen Douglas, candidates for the Senate in Illinois, debate seven times in seven towns of the state. The subject: should slavery be allowed in the new Western states? The rules: an hour for the first speaker, an hour and a half to reply, half an hour of rejoinder, three hours in all. Up to 15,000 people per debate, according to the papers. Douglas keeps his seat, but Lincoln becomes a national figure, and president two years later.
textes.Trois heures de débat debout, sans micro: Three hours of debate standing up, without a microphone. You drop out after three minutes of a question.
textes.Le 19 novembre 1863, à Gettysburg, l'ora: On 19 November 1863, at Gettysburg, the star orator Edward Everett speaks for two hours. Then Abraham Lincoln delivers 271 words, in ten sentences, in barely two minutes: "Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation..." The next day, Everett writes to him that he wishes he had come as near to the central idea of the occasion in two hours as Lincoln did in two minutes.
textes.Deux minutes pour entrer dans l'histoire: Two minutes to make history. It takes you two to find the button.
textes.Le 13 janvier 1898, L'Aurore, le quotidi: On 13 January 1898, L'Aurore, Georges Clemenceau's daily, publishes on its front page a letter from Émile Zola to President Félix Faure: "J'accuse...!" ("I accuse"). Zola names those who had the innocent Captain Dreyfus convicted, knowing he is exposing himself to a trial. Found guilty of libel on 23 February, he goes into exile in England. Dreyfus would be pardoned in 1899, then cleared in 1906.
textes.Zola accusait avec des preuves. Vous acc: Zola accused with evidence. You accuse the screen of misunderstanding your finger.
textes.En 1928, Edward Bernays, neveu de Sigmun: In 1928, Edward Bernays, Sigmund Freud's nephew, publishes Propaganda: the "conscious and intelligent manipulation of the organized habits and opinions of the masses" is, he says, central to democracy. On 31 March 1929, Easter Sunday, for the American Tobacco Company, he has women parade in New York smoking their "torches of freedom" in public. The photographers are his own. He would call his method "the engineering of consent".
textes.Un homme a fait passer la cigarette pour: One man passed off cigarettes as freedom. I pass off your mistakes as comedy. Each to their own talent.
textes.La Guerre des mondes à la radio: The War of the Worlds on radio
textes.Le 30 octobre 1938, Orson Welles adapte: On 30 October 1938, Orson Welles adapts The War of the Worlds for radio, on CBS: fake news flashes interrupt dance music and announce the Martians landing at Grovers Mill, New Jersey. The next day, newspapers describe a general panic. Historians consider it greatly exaggerated: a survey of 5,000 households that very evening finds only 2% listening. The press had every reason to discredit radio.
textes.La vraie fausse nouvelle, c'était la pan: The real fake news was the panic. Remember that before you share anything.
textes.Le 18 juin 1940, à Londres, le général d: On 18 June 1940, in London, General de Gaulle speaks to the French on the BBC: "the flame of French resistance must not go out and will not go out". At the time, almost nobody hears it. And nobody recorded it: the voice played today is from the appeal of 22 June, with a similar but reworked text. The poster "To all the French", often confused with it, was put up later in a few London streets.
textes.Le discours le plus célèbre de l'histoir: The most famous speech in French history was never recorded. Your score is. Sorry.
textes.En 1947, Raymond Queneau publie Exercice: In 1947, Raymond Queneau publishes Exercises in Style with Gallimard: the same anecdote told 99 times. On the S bus, a young man with a long neck and a funny hat argues with another passenger; two hours later, outside the Gare Saint-Lazare, someone advises him to add a button to his overcoat. Nothing more. But each version changes style, and shows everything form does to a story. Erasmus was already playing at varying a single sentence in 1512.
textes.Quatre-vingt-dix-neuf façons de raconter: Ninety-nine ways to tell the same story. You found as many ways to miss the same question.
textes.En 1958, le philosophe britannique Steph: In 1958, the British philosopher Stephen Toulmin publishes The Uses of Argument. He takes an ordinary argument apart: the claim, the data supporting it, the warrant that bridges the two, the backing for that warrant, the qualifier ("probably") and the rebuttal ("unless..."). His Leeds colleagues mock his "anti-logic book". But American rhetoric scholars adopt it, and his model enters debate teaching.
textes.Thèse, données, garantie. Votre argument: Claim, data, warrant. Your usual argument: claim, claim, then claim louder.
textes.Le 28 août 1963, sur les marches du Linc: On 28 August 1963, on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, Martin Luther King speaks to more than 250,000 people gathered for the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. Near the end, the singer Mahalia Jackson, sitting behind him, calls out: "Tell 'em about the dream, Martin!" King then leaves his text and improvises. "I have a dream" comes back eight times: an anaphora everyone remembers.
textes.Huit fois la même phrase, et personne ne: The same sentence eight times, and nobody gets bored. You repeat the same mistake, and I do.
textes.En 1946, George Orwell écrit que si la p: In 1946, George Orwell writes that if thought corrupts language, language can also corrupt thought. In 1949, he takes the idea to its limit in Nineteen Eighty-Four: Big Brother's regime invents Newspeak, a language whose vocabulary shrinks every year, to make certain ideas literally unthinkable. No more "bad", only "ungood"; no more "excellent", but "doubleplusgood". And "doublethink" lets you believe two contradictory things at once.
textes.Votre dernière réponse était doubleplusi: Your last answer was doubleplusungood. You see, Newspeak has its uses.
textes.Le 26 septembre 1960, dans un studio de: On 26 September 1960, in a Chicago studio, John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon face off in the first presidential debate of the campaign, broadcast on television. Nixon, just out of hospital after a knee injury, refuses make-up: under the lights he sweats, his stubble shows, his grey suit blends into the set. His mother calls to ask if he is ill. Kennedy wins the picture. The election would be close.
textes.Nixon a perdu à cause d'une barbe de tro: Nixon lost over a five o'clock shadow. I'll say nothing about your revision outfit.
textes.En Égypte, un texte du Moyen Empire met: In Egypt, a Middle Kingdom text stages an old vizier of King Djedkare Isesi, Ptahhotep, teaching his son how to behave, and above all how to speak: "Only speak when you have something worth saying." One must also listen, let the petitioner finish his complaint. And not despise the humble: the perfect word, hidden more deeply than precious stones, is found among the servant women at the mill-stone.
textes.Ne parler que si l'on a quelque chose à: Only speak when you have something to say. The AI read the advice. She decided it didn't apply to her.
textes.En Chine, au temps des Royaumes combatta: In China, during the Warring States, advisers went from court to court persuading princes, at the risk of their lives. Han Fei, a stuttering prince but a formidable writer, drew a chapter from it, "The Difficulties of Persuasion": the dragon is gentle, you can ride on its back, but whoever touches the reversed scales under its throat dies. The ruler has his too. In 233 BC, Han Fei died of poison, driven to it by his former fellow pupil Li Si.
textes.L'IA aussi a des écailles à rebours. Ell: The AI has reversed scales too. She won't tell you where. That would be too easy.
textes.En Inde, les Nyāya-sūtra, datés entre le: In India, the Nyāya Sūtras, dated between the 6th century BC and the 2nd century AD, codify debate: honest discussion, disputation to win, cavil, and the ways of losing. The argument there has five members: "There is fire on the hill, because there is smoke; wherever there is smoke, there is fire; the hill smokes; therefore there is fire." Among Buddhists, tradition dates to Ashoka's council, around 240 BC, the Kathāvatthu, over two hundred points of controversy.
textes.Il y a de la fumée chez vous. L'IA en co: There's smoke at your place. The AI concludes there's fire. Indian logic, two thousand years' warranty.
textes.À Bassora, au IXe siècle, al-Jāḥiẓ, « l': In Basra, in the 9th century, al-Jahiz, "the bug-eyed", wrote the Book of Eloquence and Exposition, which opened Arabic literary theory. The caliph al-Ma'mun wanted to entrust his children to him; he gave up, as his eyes frightened them. Two hundred books are attributed to him. According to tradition, he died aged over ninety, smothered under a collapsed pile of books.
textes.Mort sous ses livres. L'IA vous conseill: Died under his books. The AI advises you to read yours lying flat, just in case.
textes.En 1235, Soundiata Keïta commence à régn: In 1235, Sundiata Keita began to reign over the young Mali. His epic, sung from generation to generation by griots, tells of a child who could not walk, then the struggle against Soumaoro, sorcerer king of Sosso. At his side, his griot, Balla Fasséké, ancestor of the Kouyaté griots. Not until 1960 did Djibril Tamsir Niane write it down, from the griot Djeli Mamoudou Kouyaté.
textes.Huit siècles de mémoire sans un seul pap: Eight centuries of memory without a single sheet of paper. The AI forgets your answers as soon as you close the app. Well, almost.
