Socrates asks what rhetoric really is. Gorgias concedes that an orator convinces an ignorant crowd better than an expert does, without knowing anything about the subject himself. For Socrates, it is therefore not an art but a knack: a flattery that guesses at what pleases with no thought for what is best. It is to politics what pastry baking is to medicine, and cosmetics to gymnastics. Callicles, for his part, defends the right of the stronger. His book gathers Legalist thought: a strong state rests on clear laws, rewards and punishments, and a ruler who shows nothing of his desires. textes.Vers 95, Quintilien, né à Calagurris en: Around 95, Quintilian, born at Calagurris in Hispania and long master of a public school of rhetoric in Rome, published a manual in twelve books. It trains the orator "from the cradle to the grave": the small child's upbringing, the grammarian's school, the rhetorician's, the finding of arguments, their order, style, memory and delivery. His definition comes from Cato the Elder: the orator is a good man skilled at speaking. The perfect orator is first a good man. In the Middle Ages, the text circulated only in pieces; in 1416, Poggio found a complete manuscript at the abbey of St Gall. The humanists seized on it: Erasmus drew on it, Luther preferred it to almost all authors.

textes.Texte fondateur de l'école indienne Nyāy: Founding text of the Indian Nyāya school, the Nyāya Sūtras are attributed to Akṣapāda Gautama, of whom almost nothing is known; they may have been written by several authors, at an uncertain date between the 6th century BC and the 2nd century AD. Five books of two chapters, 528 aphorisms. The first lists sixteen categories forming a real manual of debate: the means of knowing, doubt, the members of an argument, but also honest discussion, disputation to win and cavil, then fallacies, quibbles, futile rejoinders and ways of losing. The correct argument there has five members, from thesis to conclusion, with the famous example of the fire on the hill. Four means of knowledge are accepted: perception, inference, comparison, reliable testimony.

textes.Al-Jāḥiẓ, né à Bassora vers 776 et mort: Al-Jahiz, born in Basra around 776 and died in 868 or 869, close to the rationalist Mu'tazilite theologians, reportedly wrote two hundred books. His Kitab al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin, the "Book of Eloquence and Exposition", is a wide-ranging reflection on human communication. It is regarded as the formal start of Arabic literary theory. Al-Jahiz proposes in it a definition of eloquence that would be widely adopted: the ability to deliver an effective message, brief or elaborate at will. After him, balāgha would become a science, from Ibn al-Mu'tazz to al-Jurjani and al-Sakkaki.

textes.Augustin, né à Thagaste en 354, a enseig: Augustine, born at Thagaste in 354, taught rhetoric at Carthage, in Rome, then in Milan, where in 384 he held the most visible chair in the Latin world. Converted in 386, bishop of Hippo, he wondered what a Christian should keep of pagan culture. De doctrina christiana answers in four books. The first three, published in 397, teach how to read and interpret Scripture. The fourth, added in 426, deals with the preacher's eloquence: as Cicero wished, he must teach, delight and move, choosing between the subdued, the moderate and the grand style. Classical rhetoric thus passed from the rostrum to the pulpit, for the whole Middle Ages.

textes.En 1960, l'historien Djibril Tamsir Nian: In 1960, the historian Djibril Tamsir Niane published in French the epic of Sundiata, as told to him by the griot Djeli Mamoudou Kouyaté, a jeli, a historian of oral tradition. The Malinke epic tells of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire, who reigned from 1235 to 1255. As a child he cannot walk; he finally rises by leaning on a baobab branch, after an iron rod has broken under him. Grown up, he confronts Soumaoro Kanté, the sorcerer king of Sosso. At his side, his griot Balla Fasséké, ancestor of the Kouyaté line. At his coronation, he gives an oral constitution, the Kouroukan Fouga. The book made known to the world a tradition that had until then lived only through the griots' voice.

textes.En 1512, Érasme publie à Paris, chez Jos: In 1512, Erasmus published in Paris, with Josse Bade, De duplici copia rerum ac verborum commentarii duo, a style manual requested by John Colet for his St Paul's School in London. Copia means abundance: abundance of words and abundance of ideas. The pupil learns to vary a single thought, to rephrase it, to enrich it with examples and comparisons. In chapter 33, Erasmus gives 195 ways of saying a single Latin sentence, "your letter delighted me greatly". The book became a school best-seller: at least 85 editions in its author's lifetime. It served to teach the rewriting of existing texts, a basic exercise of the whole humanist school. Queneau, in 1947, took up the same challenge with 99 versions of a bus story.

textes.En 1662 paraît anonymement La Logique ou: In 1662, Logic or the Art of Thinking appeared anonymously. Its authors, Antoine Arnauld and Pierre Nicole, belonged to the Jansenist circle of Port-Royal; Pascal probably contributed considerable passages. The book was written in French, not in Latin like the textbooks of the time, to teach everyone to reason correctly. It popularised the distinction between the comprehension of an idea, its features, and its extension, the set of things it designates: the more features a definition has, the fewer things it applies to. The work remained in use until the 20th century. The philosopher Ian Hacking judged it the most influential logic book between Aristotle and the end of the 19th century.

textes.En avril 1946, George Orwell publie dans: In April 1946, George Orwell published in the review Horizon an essay on the English of his time, which he found ugly and inaccurate. He linked this decline to politics: in our time, he wrote, political speech is largely the defence of the indefensible, and its language is made of euphemism and vagueness, to hide the truth rather than express it. He lists dying metaphors, pretentious diction, meaningless words. He proposes six rules: never use a figure of speech you are used to seeing in print, never use a long word where a short one will do, cut every word you can, prefer the active to the passive, avoid jargon, and break these rules sooner than say anything barbarous. He admits he himself keeps committing the faults he denounces.

textes.La première théorie du syllogisme est ce: The first theory of the syllogism is Aristotle's, in the Prior Analytics, around 350 BC. The Socrates example does not appear in it. In the Middle Ages, the schools gave the forms mnemonic names such as "Barbara".
textes.La déduction est formalisée d'abord par: Deduction was first formalised by Aristotle, whose logic remained the reference for over two thousand years. In 1879, Gottlob Frege's Begriffsschrift introduced quantifiers and variables, the basis of modern logic.

textes.Ce schéma est attribué à Hegel, qui ne l: This pattern is attributed to Hegel, who did not actually use it and called it "a lifeless schema". It comes from Fichte, and it was Heinrich Moritz Chalybäus who presented it in three steps.
textes.Aristote, dans sa Rhétorique, appelle l': Aristotle, in his Rhetoric, called the enthymeme "the body of proof": it is the orator's own kind of reasoning, which lets the audience fill in the missing premise.
textes.Le droit romain le disait déjà : « onus: Roman law already said it: "onus probandi incumbit ei qui dicit, non ei qui negat", the burden of proof lies with the one who asserts, not the one who denies. Carl Sagan summed it up: "Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence."
textes.Le Cid est créé au théâtre du Marais à l: Le Cid premiered at the Théâtre du Marais at the end of 1636 or the beginning of 1637. Its success sparked the "Quarrel of Le Cid": at Richelieu's request, the brand-new Académie française judged the play defective in 1638.

textes.Le mot vient du grec hupér, « au-delà »,: The word comes from the Greek hupér, "beyond", and bállō, "to throw": to throw beyond. It first appears in English in the 15th century.
textes.Le mot vient du grec eû, « bien », et ph: The word comes from the Greek eû, "well", and phḗmē, "speech". In 1994 Steven Pinker spoke of the "euphemism treadmill": the polite word ends up taking on the weight of the word it replaced.
textes.L'Avare est créé le 9 septembre 1668 au: The Miser premiered on 9 September 1668 at the Palais-Royal theatre in Paris. Molière drew loosely on the Aulularia, a Latin comedy by Plautus.
textes.Le mot vient du grec et signifie « chang: The word comes from Greek and means "change of name". In 1956, the linguist Roman Jakobson made metaphor and metonymy the two great poles of figurative language.
textes.Andromaque est jouée pour la première fo: Andromaque was first performed on 17 November 1667 at the Louvre, before the court of Louis XIV, with Thérèse Du Parc in the title role. At the end, Oreste goes mad and sees the Furies: hence the hissing serpents.
textes.De Gaulle prononce ces mots à l'Hôtel de: De Gaulle spoke these words at the Paris Hôtel de Ville on 25 August 1944, late in the day, the very day the capital was liberated: "Paris! Paris outraged! Paris broken! Paris martyred! But Paris liberated!"
textes.Les Anciens l'appelaient paralipse ou pr: The Ancients called it paralipsis or praeteritio. Cicero used it in the Pro Caelio: "I now forget your wrongs, Clodia, I set aside the memory of my pain…"
textes.Le mot vient du grec eirōneía, au Ve siè: The word comes from the Greek eirōneía, in the 5th century BC: the eiron was a comedy character who pretends to be less clever than he is. Socrates made it a method.
textes.Le mot vient du grec pleonasmós, de pléo: The word comes from the Greek pleonasmós, from pléon, "in excess". Classical rhetoric files it among tautologies, like "burning fire" or "black darkness".
textes.La Rhétorique d'Aristote, en trois livre: Aristotle's Rhetoric, in three books, dates from the 4th century BC. In it he defines rhetoric as the ability to see, in each case, the available means of persuasion.
textes.Pour Aristote, le kairos est le contexte: For Aristotle, kairos is the context of time and place in which the proof is delivered. The Greeks contrasted it with chronos, time that passes, and also made it a minor god of opportunity.
textes.Robert Cialdini publie Influence en 1984: Robert Cialdini published Influence in 1984. To write it, he went undercover in sales jobs, such as car sales and door-to-door selling. A seventh lever, unity, was added in the latest edition.
textes.Cicéron en faisait l'un des piliers de l: Cicero considered it one of the pillars of oratory. In the Middle Ages it was used in court to win the judge's favour, then in the prologues of chivalric romances.
textes.Aristote consacre le livre II de sa Rhét: Aristotle devoted Book II of his Rhetoric to these three means of persuasion the orator must rely on: credibility, emotions and reasoning.
textes.Cicéron, s'inspirant d'Aristote, systéma: Cicero, drawing on Aristotle, systematised the five canons of rhetoric: inventio, dispositio, elocutio, memoria and pronuntiatio, that is finding, arranging, phrasing, memorising and delivering.
textes.Aristote décrit déjà ce piège dans les R: Aristotle already described this trap in the Sophistical Refutations. textes.L'origine du mot est discutée : un manne: The origin of the term is debated: a straw dummy easy to knock down. A common but false etymology speaks of false witnesses with a straw in their shoe. The sense of an imaginary opponent easy to refute is recorded around 1620.
textes.La métaphore remonte au moins à Cicéron: The metaphor goes back at least to Cicero: in the Laelius, he describes the Republic that "glides readily down the path of ruin when once it has taken a start". In 1910, Alfred Sidgwick described it as an argument, the "thin end of a wedge" objection.
textes.Dans la Grèce antique, la nature servait: In Ancient Greece, nature already served as a model for how to act. Rousseau replied: "We do not know what our nature permits us to be."
textes.L'expression américaine « sauter dans le: The American phrase "jump on the bandwagon" comes from the 1848 presidential campaign: circus clown Dan Rice invited candidate Zachary Taylor onto his circus bandwagon. In 1951, Solomon Asch measured this conformity in the lab.
textes.Le nom latin, argumentum ad ignorantiam,: The Latin name, argumentum ad ignorantiam, was probably coined by John Locke in the late 17th century. Carl Sagan used to point out: "Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence."
textes.Tu quoque veut dire « toi aussi » en lat: Tu quoque means "you also" in Latin. In the 1930s Soviet Union, American criticism was met with: "And you are lynching Negroes."
textes.Le latin dit « après ceci, donc à cause: The Latin says "after this, therefore because of this". The footballer Pelé blamed a slump on a shirt he had given away; it ended when a friend brought one back… which was not the original.
textes.Aristote décrit cette « pétition de prin: Aristotle described this "begging the question" in the Prior Analytics and the Topics: asking to be granted the very point at issue. The Latin term petitio principii passed into English in the 16th century.
textes.C'est John Locke qui a forgé l'expressio: John Locke coined the phrase argumentum ad verecundiam, the appeal to modesty: people dare not contradict authority. In 1923, Theophilus Painter counted 24 pairs of human chromosomes; researchers repeated the figure out of deference for decades, though there are 23.
textes.L'anthropologue Eugenie Scott invente le: The anthropologist Eugenie Scott coined the term in 1994, after the creationist Duane Gish, whom she considered the technique's most avid practitioner.
textes.La dispute scolastique suivait des règle: Scholastic disputation followed fixed rules and relied on written authorities. There were also famous public disputations, such as Barcelona in 1263, where Nachmanides defended Judaism, or Leipzig in 1519 between Luther and Eck.
textes.L'« homme d'acier » est l'inverse de l'h: The steel man is the opposite of the straw man, a term whose sense of an easily knocked-down opponent is recorded around 1620. The straw man fallacy only entered a logic textbook in 1956.
textes.Le programmeur italien Alberto Brandolin: The Italian programmer Alberto Brandolini stated it in January 2013, after reading Kahneman and then watching a Berlusconi–Travaglio debate. Jonathan Swift had already written in 1710: "Falsehood flies, and truth comes limping after it."

textes.Karl Popper en fait le critère de la sci: Karl Popper made it the criterion of science in 1934: you would have to see every swan to prove they are white, but a single black swan is enough to refute it. In maths, Euler's sum of powers conjecture fell in 1966 to a single counterexample.

textes.Joseph Campbell publie Le Héros aux mill: Joseph Campbell published The Hero with a Thousand Faces in 1949 and borrowed the word "monomyth" from James Joyce's Finnegans Wake. George Lucas acknowledged its influence on Star Wars.
textes.Propp publie Morphologie du conte en rus: Propp published Morphology of the Folktale in Russian in 1928, based on 100 tales from Alexander Afanasyev's collection. The book went unnoticed in the West until its 1958 English translation, then influenced Lévi-Strauss and Barthes.

textes.La Première Philippique date de 351-350: The First Philippic dates from 351-350 BC. According to Plutarch, Demosthenes had overcome his stammer by speaking with pebbles in his mouth. Cicero would reuse the title Philippics for his speeches against Mark Antony.

textes.En quelle année le papyrus Prisse, qui c: In what year was the Prisse Papyrus, containing the Maxims of Ptahhotep, discovered at Thebes?
textes.En 1847, par Émile Prisse d'Avennes. Le: In 1847, by Émile Prisse d'Avennes. The text itself is about four thousand years old.
textes.« Un mot parfait est plus caché que les: "A perfect word is hidden more deeply than precious stones; yet it is found among the servants at the mill-stone." Ptahhotep means:
textes.que la bonne parole est rare, mais peut: that the right word is rare, but can come from anyone
textes.qu'il faut payer les orateurs en pierres: that orators should be paid in precious stones
textes.qu'il ne faut jamais parler en travailla: that one should never talk while working
textes.Le mot parfait est rare comme une pierre: The perfect word is as rare as a precious stone, but it does not depend on rank: a vizier reminds his son of it.
textes.Les Maximes conseillent aussi : « Ne par: The Maxims also advise: "Only speak when you have something worth saying."
textes.Ptahhotep conseille au fonctionnaire de: Ptahhotep advises the official to let the petitioner say everything on his mind before dismissing him.
textes.Vrai. Écouter fait partie de l'art de pa: True. Listening is part of the art of speaking: "listening benefits the listener".
textes.La maxime demande d'être patient en écou: The maxim asks for patience when listening to a petitioner and not to dismiss him until he has completely unburdened himself.
textes.Les historiens sont sûrs que les Maximes: Historians are sure the Maxims were written by Ptahhotep himself, under the 5th Dynasty.
textes.Faux. Le texte porte son nom, mais il a: False. The text bears his name, but it was probably composed later, in the Middle Kingdom.
textes.Enheduanna, à qui l'on attribue L'Exalta: Enheduanna, to whom The Exaltation of Inanna is attributed, was:
textes.grande prêtresse du dieu-lune Nanna à Ur: high priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur, daughter of King Sargon
textes.une scribe de la cour perse: a scribe of the Persian court
textes.Vers 2300 av. J.-C., la fille de Sargon: Around 2300 BC, the daughter of Sargon of Akkad led the cult of Nanna at Ur. Her hymns would make her the oldest author known by name.
textes.Son nom pourrait désigner sa fonction pl: Her name might designate her office rather than a person, and many Assyriologists doubt she wrote these hymns.
textes.Les copies des hymnes d'Enheduanna qui n: The surviving copies of Enheduanna's hymns date from her lifetime.
textes.Faux. Elles datent d'environ six siècles: False. They date from about six centuries after her, hence the doubts about the attribution.
textes.Bien des assyriologues doutent qu'Enhedu: Many Assyriologists doubt Enheduanna wrote these hymns; her name might even designate her office.
textes.Combien de chants compte l'Iliade ?: How many books does the Iliad have?
textes.24, comme l'Odyssée. Deux longs poèmes e: 24, like the Odyssey. Two long poems in dactylic hexameter.
textes.L'Iliade et l'Odyssée prennent forme en: The Iliad and the Odyssey took shape in Greece in the 8th or 7th century BC, from an oral tradition.
textes.Qu'a montré Milman Parry à partir de 192: What did Milman Parry show from 1928 on?
textes.que l'épopée homérique vient d'une compo: that Homeric epic comes from oral composition, made of ready-made formulas
textes.que l'Iliade avait été écrite d'un seul: that the Iliad was written in one go on papyrus
textes.Les épithètes répétées ne sont pas des t: The repeated epithets are not tics: they are tools that let the bard compose while singing, in rhythm.
textes.Sa thèse de 1928 s'intitule L'Épithète t: His 1928 thesis is called L'Épithète traditionnelle dans Homère (The Traditional Epithet in Homer).
textes.une formule toute prête que l'aède place: a ready-made formula the bard fits into the line
textes.le nom d'une déesse inventée par Parry: the name of a goddess invented by Parry
textes.Elle revient sans cesse parce qu'elle ti: It keeps returning because it fits the hexameter exactly. Like "wily Odysseus".
textes.Les aèdes, chanteurs professionnels, imp: The bards, professional singers, improvised by relying on these formulas.
textes.le débat sur l'existence d'Homère et la: the debate over Homer's existence and how his poems were composed
textes.la première question posée dans l'Iliade: the first question asked in the Iliad
textes.Qui était Homère, s'il a existé, et comm: Who Homer was, whether he existed, and how such long poems could arise without writing? Parry gave part of the answer.
textes.L'existence d'Homère reste un mystère :: Homer's existence remains a mystery: the two epics took shape in the 8th or 7th century BC.
textes.Pourquoi, selon la tradition, l'art de p: Why, according to tradition, was the art of pleading born in Syracuse in the 5th century BC?
textes.après la chute du tyran, les citoyens pl: after the tyrant's fall, citizens plead for themselves to recover their property
textes.les Athéniens y ouvrent une école: the Athenians open a school there
textes.Thrasybule renversé, les procès se multi: With Thrasybulus overthrown, lawsuits multiply, without lawyers. Corax and Tisias teach how to build a plea.
textes.Corax veut dire « corbeau ». Selon l'his: Corax means "crow". According to the story, his pupil Tisias refused to pay him, and the judge dismissed them: "a bad egg from a bad crow".
textes.Un homme faible accusé d'avoir battu un: A weak man accused of beating a strong man says: "How could I have?" He is using:
textes.l'argument du vraisemblable, attribué à: the argument from likelihood, attributed to Corax
textes.Il ne prouve rien : il montre que l'accu: He proves nothing: he shows the accusation is unlikely. The strong man turns the argument around: "I would have been suspected first."
textes.On ne connaît Corax que par Platon, Aris: Corax is known only through Plato, Aristotle and Cicero. Aristotle, for his part, credited Empedocles with inventing rhetoric.
textes.On possède les traités écrits par Corax: We have the treatises written by Corax himself.
textes.Faux. Il n'est connu que par ce qu'en di: False. He is known only from what Plato, Aristotle and Cicero say, and may even be legendary.
textes.« L'homme est la mesure de toutes choses: "Man is the measure of all things" is a saying of:
textes.Protagoras d'Abdère : chacun juge selon: Protagoras of Abdera: each judges by what appears to him. Hence the idea that both sides of a question can be argued.
textes.Ami de Périclès, Protagoras est, selon P: A friend of Pericles, Protagoras is, according to Plato, the inventor of the professional sophist, who teaches for a fee.
textes.Selon Protagoras, sur toute question :: According to Protagoras, on every question:
textes.une seule réponse est vraie et évidente: only one answer is true and obvious
textes.il vaut mieux se taire: it is better to keep silent
textes.D'où l'exercice des sophistes : plaider: Hence the sophists' exercise: arguing for and against. Aristotle would reproach him for wanting "to make the weaker argument stronger".
textes.Protagoras a vécu environ de 490 à 420 a: Protagoras lived from about 490 to 420 BC. Of the gods, he said he had no means of knowing whether they exist or not.
textes.Tous les historiens tiennent pour certai: All historians hold it certain that Protagoras' books were burned in the agora of Athens.
textes.Faux. Diogène Laërce le raconte, mais de: False. Diogenes Laërtius tells it, but centuries later; John Burnet doubts it, since no contemporary mentions it.
textes.Cicéron mentionne aussi cette destructio: Cicero also mentions this destruction, but he was not a contemporary either.
textes.En quelle année av. J.-C. Gorgias arrive: In what year BC did Gorgias come to Athens as ambassador of Leontinoi? (positive number)
textes.En 427 av. J.-C., pendant la guerre du P: In 427 BC, during the Peloponnesian War. The Athenians discovered an almost poetic prose.
textes.En 427 av. J.-C., Gorgias arrive à Athèn: In 427 BC, Gorgias came to Athens as ambassador of Leontinoi, his Sicilian city, aged about sixty. Tradition has him live to 108.
textes.Dans l'Éloge d'Hélène, Gorgias compare l: In the Encomium of Helen, Gorgias compares the effect of speech on the soul to that of:
textes.Certaines drogues guérissent, d'autres t: Some drugs heal, others kill; some speeches frighten, others embolden or poison the soul.
textes.Hélène, dit Gorgias, a pu partir pour Tr: Helen, Gorgias says, may have left for Troy driven by the gods, force, love or speech: in every case, she is not guilty.
textes.« un puissant maître » au corps minuscul: "a powerful master" with a tiny body
textes.La parole accomplit les actes les plus d: Speech achieves the most divine feats with the smallest and least evident body.
textes.L'Éloge d'Hélène était une pièce de démo: The Encomium of Helen was a show piece: Gorgias displayed his art in it to attract students.
textes.Dans le Gorgias de Platon, Socrate dit q: In Plato's Gorgias, Socrates says rhetoric is to politics what pastry baking is to:
textes.La pâtisserie flatte le goût sans se sou: Pastry flatters taste with no care for health; rhetoric flatters the audience with no care for justice. Same relation between cosmetics and gymnastics.
textes.Platon écrit le Gorgias vers 380 av. J.-: Plato wrote the Gorgias around 380 BC; Socrates there takes on Gorgias, then Polus and Callicles.
textes.Pour le Socrate du Gorgias, la rhétoriqu: For the Socrates of the Gorgias, rhetoric is:
textes.un savoir-faire, une flatterie qui vise: a knack, a flattery aiming at pleasure, not at what is best
textes.un art réservé aux dieux: an art reserved for the gods
textes.Elle devine ce qui plaît sans considérer: It guesses at what is pleasant with no consideration for what is best. Plato fixed for a long time the image of the smooth-talking sophist.
Gorgias came from Sicily, like Corax.
textes.Vrai. Corax enseignait à Syracuse, Gorgi: True. Corax taught in Syracuse, Gorgias came from Leontinoi: Greek rhetoric has Sicilian roots.
textes.Dans son oraison funèbre, Périclès appel: In his funeral oration, Pericles calls Athens:
textes.Il fait l'éloge de la cité plutôt que de: He praises the city rather than the battles: equal justice, open public life, merit.
textes.L'oraison est prononcée à la fin de la p: The oration was delivered at the end of the first year of the Peloponnesian War, for the first Athenian dead.
textes.Thucydide affirme rapporter l'oraison fu: Thucydides claims to report Pericles' funeral oration word for word.
textes.Faux. Il dit rendre l'esprit général des: False. He says he gives the general gist of the speeches, not their exact words.
textes.Platon, dans le Ménexène, attribue même: Plato, in the Menexenus, even attributes the writing of the oration to Aspasia, Pericles' companion.
textes.quelqu'un qui écrit des discours que d'a: someone who writes speeches that others deliver in court
textes.Chacun devait plaider lui-même : on ache: Everyone had to plead for himself: so one bought a speech from a specialist, learned it and delivered it oneself.
textes.Lysias fut logographe environ de 403 à 3: Lysias was a logographer from about 403 to 380 BC; he fitted each speech to his client's character.
textes.Pourquoi Lysias devient-il logographe ?: Why did Lysias become a logographer?
textes.ruiné par les Trente, qui ont fait mouri: ruined by the Thirty, who had his brother killed, he had to earn a living
textes.il voulait devenir juge: he wanted to become a judge
textes.En 404, sous les Trente, son frère Polém: In 404, under the Thirty, his brother Polemarchus was forced to drink hemlock and Lysias fled to Megara. Back home, he lived by his pen.
textes.Lysias, fils de Céphale de Syracuse, éta: Lysias, son of Cephalus of Syracuse, was a metic, a resident foreigner in Athens. 34 of his speeches have reached us complete.
textes.Combien de discours de Lysias nous sont: How many of Lysias' speeches have reached us complete?
textes.34, plus 3 en fragments ; 127 autres ne: 34, plus 3 as fragments; 127 others are known only from scraps or their titles.
textes.Pourquoi Isocrate ne parlait-il pas deva: Why did Isocrates not speak before the assembly?
textes.Il écrit donc des discours faits pour êt: So he wrote speeches meant to be read, and taught. According to Pliny, he sold a single speech for twenty talents.
Isocrates opened his school around 392 BC and never took more than nine pupils at a time.
textes.Combien d'élèves Isocrate acceptait-il a: At most how many pupils did Isocrates take in his school at once?
textes.Selon Plutarque, comment Démosthène corr: According to Plutarch, how did Demosthenes correct his pronunciation?
textes.en parlant avec des cailloux dans la bou: by talking with pebbles in his mouth
textes.en se taisant pendant un an: by keeping silent for a year
textes.Il déclamait aussi en courant, s'exerçai: He also declaimed while running, practised in an underground study and shaved half his head so as not to go out.
textes.Né en 384 av. J.-C., Démosthène plaide à: Born in 384 BC, Demosthenes pleaded at twenty against his guardians, who had squandered his inheritance.
textes.Sur la couronne (330 av. J.-C.) est le d: On the Crown (330 BC) is the speech in which Demosthenes:
textes.défend toute sa carrière contre Eschine: defends his whole career against Aeschines
textes.Eschine attaquait la proposition de cour: Aeschines attacked the proposal to crown Demosthenes for his services. Demosthenes won by a wide margin, and Aeschines was forced into exile.
textes.Démosthène prononce Sur la couronne en 3: Demosthenes delivered On the Crown in 330 BC against Aeschines, who was attacking Ctesiphon for proposing, in 336, to crown him.
textes.Cicéron jugeait Démosthène supérieur à t: Cicero judged Demosthenes superior to all other orators.
textes.Vrai. Il l'appelle celui qui, seul, l'em: True. He calls him the one who alone excels all. He would even name his speeches against Mark Antony the Philippics.
Demosthenes poisoned himself in 322 BC at Kalaureia, so as not to fall into Macedonian hands.
textes.Quel paradoxe a rendu Gongsun Long célèb: Which paradox made Gongsun Long famous?
textes.« un cheval blanc n'est pas un cheval »: "a white horse is not a horse"
textes.Le cheval nomme une forme, le blanc une: Horse names a shape, white a colour: so "white horse" does not name the same thing as "horse".
textes.Gongsun Long appartient à l'École des no: Gongsun Long belongs to the School of Names; only 6 of the 14 chapters of his book have reached us.
textes.Dans le dialogue du cheval blanc, quel e: In the white horse dialogue, which example supports the argument?
textes.demandez un cheval, on peut vous amener: ask for a horse and a yellow one will do; ask for a white horse and it won't
textes.le roi n'aime que les chevaux noirs: the king only likes black horses
textes.Si « cheval blanc » était identique à «: If "white horse" were identical to "horse", the same animals would satisfy both requests. They do not.
textes.Le paradoxe joue sur le mot chinois 非, q: The paradox plays on the Chinese word 非, which can mean "is not" or "is not identical to".
textes.Qui était Guiguzi, selon la tradition ?: Who was Guiguzi, according to tradition?
textes.le maître des stratèges Su Qin et Zhang: the master of the strategists Su Qin and Zhang Yi
textes.un général de la Grande Muraille: a general of the Great Wall
textes.Le « Sage de la vallée des démons » pass: The "Sage of Ghost Valley" is said to have founded the School of Vertical and Horizontal Alliances.
textes.C'est Sima Qian, dans ses Mémoires histo: It is Sima Qian, in his Records of the Grand Historian, who makes Guiguzi the master of Su Qin and Zhang Yi.
textes.Que conseille le premier chapitre du Gui: What does the first chapter of the Guiguzi, "Open and Shut", advise?
textes.rester caché, pour que l'autre croie que: staying hidden, so the other believes his decisions are his own
textes.toujours dire la vérité au prince: always telling the ruler the truth
textes.Faire parler l'autre, savoir se taire, e: Make the other talk, know when to keep silent, and never let it show that you pull the strings.
textes.Le Guiguzi a été compilé entre la fin de: The Guiguzi was compiled between the late Warring States and the end of the Han.
textes.Le Zhan Guo Ce, « Stratagèmes des Royaum: The Zhan Guo Ce, "Strategies of the Warring States", gathers:
textes.des anecdotes de manipulation politique: anecdotes of political manipulation and diplomacy
textes.On y voit les conseillers ambulants, com: It shows travelling advisers, like Su Qin, convincing kings to ally or to break.
textes.Le recueil a été compilé sous les Han pa: The collection was compiled under the Han by Liu Xiang.
textes.En 1973, on retrouve à Mawangdui des tex: In 1973, silk texts close to the Zhan Guo Ce were found at Mawangdui. How many chapters do they have?
textes.27 chapitres, dont 11 ressemblent à des: 27 chapters, of which 11 resemble passages of the known Zhan Guo Ce.
textes.Le Zhan Guo Ce que nous lisions avant ce: The Zhan Guo Ce read before this discovery had been compiled under the Han by Liu Xiang.
textes.Han Fei avait, selon Sima Qian, une part: Han Fei had, according to Sima Qian, a peculiarity:
textes.Un théoricien de la persuasion qui ne po: A theorist of persuasion who could hardly speak: his writings spoke for him.
textes.Han Fei, né vers 280 av. J.-C., apparten: Han Fei, born around 280 BC, belonged to the ruling family of the state of Han. He studied under Xunzi, together with Li Si.
textes.Selon Han Fei, que faut-il éviter avant: According to Han Fei, what must be avoided above all when advising a ruler?
textes.toucher ses « écailles à rebours », ses: touching his "reversed scales", his sore points
textes.Le dragon se laisse monter, mais tue qui: The dragon lets you ride it, but kills whoever touches the scales under its throat. So does the ruler.
textes.La comparaison du dragon conclut le chap: The dragon comparison concludes Han Fei's chapter on how an adviser can win the ruler's favour.
textes.Selon Han Fei, si l'on parle des grands: According to Han Fei, if you talk to a ruler about great men, he may think you are hinting at his own defects.
textes.Vrai. Tout le chapitre énumère ces malen: True. The whole chapter lists such misunderstandings: the ruler hears what the adviser did not say.
textes.Le favori Mi Zixia, d'abord loué, fut en: The favourite Mi Zixia, first praised, was later punished for the same deeds, when the ruler's love turned to hate.
How did Han Fei die, in 233 BC?
textes.poussé à boire du poison par son ancien: driven to drink poison by his former fellow pupil Li Si
textes.de vieillesse, entouré d'élèves: of old age, surrounded by pupils
textes.Li Si, ministre de Qin, craint que le ro: Li Si, minister of Qin, feared the king would prefer Han Fei to him. Both had studied under Xunzi.
textes.Le futur Premier Empereur de Chine admir: The future First Emperor of China admired Han Fei's writings.
textes.Vrai. Lisant ses textes, il aurait dit q: True. Reading his writings, he reportedly said he could die without regret if he could befriend their author.
textes.Le roi Ying Zheng de Qin deviendra le Pr: King Ying Zheng of Qin would become the First Emperor, and his minister Li Si would apply Legalist ideas.
textes.En Chine ancienne comme en Grèce, on che: In ancient China as in Greece, the main aim was to convince an assembly of citizens.
textes.Faux. Les conseillers chinois cherchaien: False. Chinese advisers sought to persuade a single man, the ruler, which changed everything: not displeasing mattered as much as proving.
textes.Pourquoi dit-on que Cicéron était un « h: Why is Cicero called a "new man" (novus homo)?
textes.aucun de ses ancêtres n'avait été consul: none of his ancestors had been consul; he rose by his talent as an orator
textes.il venait d'arriver à Rome d'Égypte: he had just arrived in Rome from Egypt
textes.Né à Arpinum dans une famille de chevali: Born at Arpinum into a family of knights, he owed everything to speech, up to the consulship in 63.
Cicero was born on 3 January 106 BC at Arpinum. From the equestrian order, with no consular ancestor, he was a "new man".
textes.Quel procès fait de Cicéron, en 70 av. J: Which trial, in 70 BC, made Cicero Rome's foremost orator?
textes.l'accusation de Verrès, gouverneur corro: the prosecution of Verres, corrupt governor of Sicily
textes.Verrès avait pris pour avocat le grand H: Verres had hired the great Hortensius. Cicero won and became the reference.
textes.Dix ans plus tôt, en 80, Cicéron avait d: Ten years earlier, in 80, Cicero had already defended Sextus Roscius by attacking Chrysogonus, Sulla's freedman, without implicating Sulla himself.
textes.« Jusques à quand, Catilina, abuseras-tu: "How long, Catiline, will you abuse our patience?" opens:
textes.Cicéron, consul, s'adresse à Catilina pr: Cicero, as consul, addresses Catiline, present in the Senate. Further on: "O tempora, o mores!"
textes.Les complices de Catilina restés à Rome: Catiline's accomplices left in Rome were executed without trial, for which Cicero was later blamed: he was exiled in 58.
textes.Contre qui Cicéron prononce-t-il ses Phi: Against whom did Cicero deliver his Philippics, in 44-43 BC?
textes.Il reprend le titre des discours de Démo: He borrowed the title of Demosthenes' speeches against Philip. Antony would not forgive him.
textes.Proscrit par le second triumvirat, Cicér: Proscribed by the Second Triumvirate, Cicero was caught near his villa at Formiae. He was the only proscription victim whose head and hands were displayed on the Rostra.
textes.Après la mort de Cicéron, sa tête et ses: After Cicero's death, his head and hands were nailed to the Rostra, the platform he had spoken from.
textes.Vrai, sur ordre d'Antoine. Selon Cassius: True, on Antony's orders. According to Cassius Dio, Fulvia, Antony's wife, pierced his tongue with a hairpin.
textes.En quelle année av. J.-C. Cicéron écrit-: In what year BC did Cicero write De oratore? (positive number)
textes.En 55 av. J.-C., un dialogue en trois li: In 55 BC, a dialogue in three books, in Plato's manner.
textes.De oratore se passe en 91 av. J.-C., dan: De oratore is set in 91 BC, in Crassus' villa at Tusculum; Crassus dies nine days after the dialogue.
textes.Dans De oratore, Crassus définit l'orate: In De oratore, Crassus defines the perfect orator as one who:
textes.peut parler de tous les sujets avec abon: can speak on every subject richly and variously
textes.D'où l'exigence d'une vaste culture : dr: Hence the demand for broad culture: law, history, philosophy. Antonius, in the dialogue, thinks knowledge of people is enough.
textes.Selon l'histoire racontée par Cicéron, c: According to the story Cicero tells, how did Simonides of Ceos invent the art of memory?
textes.en identifiant les victimes d'un banquet: by identifying the victims of a collapsed banquet from where they sat
textes.en apprenant l'Iliade par cœur: by learning the Iliad by heart
textes.L'ordre des lieux garde l'ordre des chos: The order of places keeps the order of things: that is the method of loci, or memory palace.
textes.Cicéron raconte l'histoire dans De orato: Cicero tells the story in De oratore, in 55 BC; Quintilian retells it in the Institutio Oratoria, around 95.
textes.On sait que la Rhétorique à Herennius, q: The Rhetorica ad Herennium, which first describes the method of loci, is known to have been written by Cicero.
textes.Faux. On la lui a longtemps attribuée, m: False. It was long attributed to him, but its author is unknown.
textes.Ce manuel latin date de la fin des année: This Latin manual dates from the late 80s BC; it distinguishes three styles, grand, middle and simple.
textes.Calagurris est l'actuelle Calahorra, en: Calagurris is today's Calahorra, in Spain. His father sent him young to study in Rome.
textes.Quintilien naît vers 35 à Calagurris, en: Quintilian was born around 35 at Calagurris, in Hispania. He died around 100.
textes.Lequel de ces Romains célèbres fut l'élè: Which of these famous Romans was Quintilian's pupil?
textes.Peut-être aussi Tacite. Cicéron, César e: Perhaps Tacitus too. Cicero, Caesar and Virgil had died before he was born.
textes.Après 68, Quintilien ouvre à Rome une éc: After 68, Quintilian opened a public school of rhetoric in Rome.
textes.En 90, l'empereur Domitien confie à Quin: In 90, the emperor Domitian entrusted Quintilian with:
textes.l'éducation de ses deux petits-neveux: the education of his two grand-nephews
textes.Deux ans après avoir cessé d'enseigner e: Two years after stopping teaching and pleading, in 88, he became a tutor at court.
textes.Quintilien était arrivé à Rome en 68, da: Quintilian had come to Rome in 68, in the retinue of the emperor Galba.
textes.En combien de livres Quintilien a-t-il é: In how many books did Quintilian write the Institutio Oratoria?
textes.Douze, publiés vers 95 : de l'éducation: Twelve, published around 95: from the small child's upbringing to the accomplished orator.
textes.L'Institution oratoire, vers 95, couvre: The Institutio Oratoria, around 95, covers the orator's education "from the cradle to the grave".
textes.Quelle définition de l'orateur Quintilie: Which definition of the orator did Quintilian take from Cato the Elder?
textes.En latin : vir bonus dicendi peritus. L': In Latin: vir bonus dicendi peritus. The good man first, the speaker second.
textes.Pour Quintilien, le parfait orateur est: For Quintilian, the perfect orator is first a good man, then a good speaker.
textes.Pour Quintilien, un méchant très habile: For Quintilian, a wicked man very skilled at speaking fully deserves the name of orator.
textes.Faux. L'orateur est d'abord un homme de: False. The orator is first a good man: virtue is part of the definition.
textes.Il répond ainsi à Platon, qui dans le Go: He thus answers Plato, who in the Gorgias made rhetoric a flattery with no care for justice.
textes.Que fait l'Institution oratoire de diffé: What does the Institutio Oratoria do differently from earlier rhetoric manuals?
textes.elle suit la formation de l'orateur depu: it follows the orator's training from the cradle
textes.elle ne parle que des figures de style: it only discusses figures of speech
textes.Quintilien commence par l'éducation du p: Quintilian starts with the small child's upbringing and goes up to the accomplished orator: it is a treatise on education as much as on rhetoric.
textes.En quelle année Pogge retrouve-t-il à Sa: In what year did Poggio find a complete manuscript of the Institutio Oratoria at St Gall?
textes.En 1416, pendant le concile de Constance: In 1416, during the Council of Constance. The complete text had been lost for centuries.
textes.En 1416, Pogge retrouve à l'abbaye de Sa: In 1416, Poggio found at the abbey of St Gall a complete manuscript of the Institutio Oratoria, until then known in pieces.
textes.avait adressé une lettre à Quintilien, m: had addressed a letter to Quintilian, dead for thirteen centuries
textes.avait traduit le livre en italien: had translated the book into Italian

textes.pour propager la foi catholique dans les: to propagate the Catholic faith in non-Catholic countries
textes.En pleine Contre-Réforme, il s'agit de m: In the midst of the Counter-Reformation, it was about missions. Propaganda means "what must be propagated".
textes.La congrégation existe encore : elle est: The congregation still exists: it became the Congregation for the Evangelization of Peoples.
textes.Quand le mot « propagande » passe-t-il a: When did the word "propaganda" pass into secular affairs?
textes.Il devient péjoratif au XXe siècle, nota: It became pejorative in the 20th century, notably after the campaigns of the First World War.
textes.En 1622, le mot désignait seulement la m: In 1622, the word merely designated the mission of propagating the Catholic faith.

textes.Le 23 juin 1789, que répond Bailly au ma: On 23 June 1789, what did Bailly answer the master of ceremonies who ordered the deputies to disperse?
textes.Doyen du Tiers état, Bailly refuse de cé: Dean of the Third Estate, Bailly refused to yield. The nobility had already left.
textes.Le 23 juin 1789, après le départ de la n: On 23 June 1789, after the nobility left, the Assembly voted its own confirmation, the inviolability of its members and the suspension of taxes in case of dissolution.
textes.La phrase de Mirabeau sur « la puissance: Mirabeau's line about "the power of bayonets" is attested word for word by all witnesses.
textes.Faux. Elle relève en partie de la légend: False. It partly belongs to legend: we do not know exactly what he said.
textes.Selon la légende, Mirabeau aurait dit qu: According to legend, Mirabeau said the deputies were there by the will of the people and would leave only by the power of bayonets.
textes.Le refrain « Ain't I a Woman? » de Sojou: Sojourner Truth's refrain "Ain't I a Woman?" (1851) appears:
textes.dans une version publiée par Frances Dan: in a version published by Frances Dana Gage in 1863, twelve years later
textes.dans le compte rendu relu avec Truth en: in the account checked with Truth in 1851
textes.La version de 1851, relue avec Truth, ne: The 1851 version, checked with Truth, does not contain this question. Gage also added a Southern accent.
textes.Marius Robinson, secrétaire de la conven: Marius Robinson, secretary of the Akron convention, went over his transcription with Sojourner Truth and published it in the Anti-Slavery Bugle on 21 June 1851.
textes.Sojourner Truth avait grandi dans le Sud: Sojourner Truth grew up in the South and spoke with the accent of Southern slaves.
textes.Faux. Née et élevée dans l'État de New Y: False. Born and raised in New York State, she spoke only Dutch until she was nine. The Southern accent is an invention of the 1863 version.
textes.Elle prononce son discours le 29 mai 185: She gave her speech on 29 May 1851 at the women's rights convention in Akron, Ohio.
textes.« Qu'est-ce que votre 4 juillet pour l'e: "What, to the American slave, is your 4th of July?" asked, in 1852:
textes.Le discours est prononcé le 5 juillet, à: The speech was delivered on 5 July, in Rochester, and turned the national holiday against slavery.
textes.Douglass prononce son discours le 5 juil: Douglass delivered his speech on 5 July 1852 at Corinthian Hall in Rochester, at the invitation of the Ladies' Anti-Slavery Society, founded in 1851.
textes.Frederick Douglass prononce son célèbre: Frederick Douglass delivered his famous Fourth of July speech on 4 July 1852.
textes.Faux. On l'appelle souvent discours du 4: False. It is often called a Fourth of July oration, but he delivered it on the 5th.
textes.Combien de débats Lincoln et Douglas tie: How many debates did Lincoln and Douglas hold in 1858?
textes.Sept, dans sept villes de l'Illinois, su: Seven, in seven Illinois towns, on extending slavery to the new states.
textes.D'août à octobre 1858, Lincoln et Dougla: From August to October 1858, Lincoln and Douglas debated seven times; up to 15,000 people per debate, according to the newspapers.
textes.Dans les débats Lincoln-Douglas, combien: In the Lincoln-Douglas debates, how long did the first speaker talk?
textes.une heure, puis une heure et demie de ré: an hour, then an hour and a half in reply and half an hour of rejoinder
textes.Trois heures par débat, devant des foule: Three hours per debate, before standing crowds. Douglas kept his seat, Lincoln gained national stature.
textes.Que risquait Zola en publiant « J'accuse: What did Zola risk by publishing "J'accuse…!"?
textes.un procès : il est condamné pour diffama: a trial: he was convicted of libel and went into exile in England
textes.Il accuse nommément les responsables, et: He named those responsible, knowingly: that was the aim, to provoke a public trial.
textes.Dreyfus sera gracié en 1899, puis réhabi: Dreyfus was pardoned in 1899, then rehabilitated in 1906.
textes.Dans quel journal paraît « J'accuse…! »,: In which newspaper did "J'accuse…!" appear, on 13 January 1898?
textes.En une, sous la forme d'une lettre au pr: On the front page, as a letter to the President of the Republic, Félix Faure.
textes.Zola accuse nommément ceux qui ont fait: Zola named those who had had the innocent Captain Dreyfus convicted.
textes.Selon Aristote, le discours prononcé dev: According to Aristotle, a speech before an assembly deciding on a law belongs to the genre:
textes.Le délibératif traite des affaires polit: The deliberative deals with political affairs; the judicial accuses or defends in court; the epideictic praises or blames.
textes.Aristote définit la rhétorique comme la: Aristotle defines rhetoric as the faculty of seeing, in each case, what may persuade.
textes.L'appel du 18 juin 1940 du général de Ga: General de Gaulle's appeal of 18 June 1940 was recorded, and that recording is what we hear today.
textes.Faux. Personne ne l'a enregistré : la vo: False. Nobody recorded it: the voice we hear is that of the 22 June appeal, with a similar but reworked text.
textes.L'affiche « À tous les Français », souve: The poster "À tous les Français", often confused with the appeal, was put up later in a few London streets.
textes.Combien de fois Raymond Queneau raconte-: How many times does Raymond Queneau tell the same anecdote in Exercises in Style (1947)?
textes.99 fois, chaque fois dans un style diffé: 99 times, each in a different style: form changes the whole story.
textes.Érasme jouait déjà à varier une même phr: Erasmus was already varying a single sentence in De copia, in 1512.
textes.Dans Exercices de style, l'anecdote raco: In Exercises in Style, the anecdote told 99 times takes place:
textes.dans l'autobus S, puis devant la gare Sa: on the S bus, then in front of Gare Saint-Lazare
textes.au sommet de la tour Eiffel: at the top of the Eiffel Tower
textes.Un jeune homme au long cou se dispute av: A young man with a long neck argues with a neighbour; two hours later, someone advises him to add a button to his overcoat. Nothing more.
textes.Queneau publie le livre chez Gallimard e: Queneau published the book with Gallimard in 1947.
textes.Pour Hitchcock, montrer d'abord au publi: For Hitchcock, first showing the audience the bomb hidden under the table creates more suspense than having it explode by surprise.
textes.Vrai. La surprise dure quinze secondes ;: True. Surprise lasts fifteen seconds; suspense lasts as long as the audience knows what the characters don't.
textes.Hitchcock le raconte à François Truffaut: Hitchcock told it to François Truffaut in 1962, during a week of interviews; the book came out in 1966.
textes.{comp}. Démosthène s'entraînait avec des: {comp}. Demosthenes practiced with pebbles in his mouth. You may keep your mouth empty.
textes.Rhétorique. Les tribunaux d'Athènes chro: Rhetoric. Athenian courts timed pleas with a water clock. I have the same one, only more impatient. {comp}.
textes.Gorgias se vantait de répondre à n'impor: Gorgias boasted he could answer any question. Let's see if you do better on {comp}.
textes.Bien argumenté. Aristote vous accorderai: Well argued. Aristotle would grant you logos. Pathos, we'll talk about later.
textes.Juste. Lincoln a dit l'essentiel en deux: Right. Lincoln said the essentials in two minutes at Gettysburg. You, in one tap. Noted.
textes.Bonne réponse. Cicéron en aurait fait un: Correct. Cicero would have made a three-hour speech out of it. Thank you for not doing so.
textes.Correct, et bien tourné. Je n'ai rien à: Correct, and well put. I have nothing to object, and it annoys me.
textes.Raté. Les sophistes enseignaient à faire: Missed. The sophists taught how to pass off the false as true. You managed the reverse, without a teacher.
textes.Faux. Cicéron a perdu la tête pour ses d: Wrong. Cicero lost his head over his speeches. You, only points.
textes.Erreur. Démosthène a été hué à son premi: Error. Demosthenes was booed at his first speech, says Plutarch. He tried again.
textes.En 1958, ce philosophe britannique démon: In 1958, this British philosopher takes an argument apart the way a lawyer would: a claim, the data that support it, the warrant linking the two, and the rebuttals. English philosophers shunned the book. American communication professors adopted it, and it is still taught everywhere.
textes.En 1947, il raconte quatre-vingt-dix-neu: In 1947, he tells the same mundane scene ninety-nine times, a long-necked young man jostled on a bus, changing style each time: metaphors, litotes, alexandrines, onomatopoeia. His Exercises in Style are a catalog of figures of speech funnier than any textbook.
textes.Compagne de Périclès, elle tient à Athèn: Pericles' companion, she kept a house in Athens where people came to talk. In Plato's Menexenus, Socrates claims she taught him rhetoric and wrote Pericles' famous funeral oration. Plato may be joking. The comic playwrights, for their part, insulted her without joking.
textes.Le philosophe pessimiste rédige vers 183: Around 1830, the pessimist philosopher writes The Art of Being Right: thirty-eight tricks for winning a debate without being right. The last, when all is lost: get personal, hurtful, rude. He never published it. The text appeared after his death, and has served both sides ever since.
textes.En 1791, elle répond à la Déclaration de: In 1791, she answers the Declaration of the Rights of Man article by article, with a Declaration of the Rights of Woman. Her article X: “Woman has the right to mount the scaffold; she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum.” She was guillotined in 1793 for her writings.
textes.Né esclave dans le Maryland, il apprend: Born enslaved in Maryland, he learns to read in secret, escapes in 1838 and publishes the narrative of his life in 1845. The text is so powerful that some readers doubt a former slave wrote it. To convince them, he gives the real names of his masters, so much so that his friends fear he will be recaptured.
textes.Avocat et consul, il fait échouer la con: Advocate and consul, he foiled Catiline's conspiracy in 63 BC: “How long, O Catiline, will you abuse our patience?” His speeches against Mark Antony, the Philippics, cost him his life. His head and hands were displayed on the Rostra, the platform from which he had spoken.
textes.Policier en Birmanie, blessé à la gorge: A policeman in Burma, shot in the throat in Spain, he saw how words are used to lie. In 1984, the Party creates Newspeak to make certain thoughts impossible to express. His advice from 1946: never use a long word where a short one will do.
textes.Maîtriser le premier losange d'Éloquence: Master the first diamond of Eloquence.
textes.Selon Plutarque, Démosthène, le plus gra: According to Plutarch, Demosthenes, the greatest orator of Athens, corrected his speech defect by talking with pebbles in his mouth, and trained his breath by declaiming while running or climbing slopes.
textes.Maîtriser 2 compétences. L'arbre de la R: Master 2 skills. The Rhetoric tree opens.
textes.Maîtriser la structure d'un argument. À: Master the structure of an argument. In Athens, you could have sold it.
textes.À Athènes, chacun devait plaider lui-mêm: In Athens, everyone had to plead their own case. Those who could afford it bought a speech from a logographer, such as Lysias, who wrote it in his client's style, clumsiness included, so the judges would believe they were hearing him speak.
textes.Maîtriser les figures de style. L'IA est: Master figures of speech. The AI is a shining light, darkening your day.
textes.Cette obscure clarté qui tombe des étoil: That dark brightness falling from the stars.
textes.Maîtriser l'ethos, le pathos et le logos: Master ethos, pathos and logos. Pathos is the most spectacular. Not the safest.
textes.Accusée d'impiété, la courtisane Phryné: Accused of impiety, the courtesan Phryne was supposedly acquitted because her advocate, Hyperides, bared her breasts before the judges. The story only appears centuries later, in Athenaeus. Hyperides' speech, on the other hand, was famous for its arguments.
textes.Maîtriser les sophismes. Vous savez main: Master fallacies. You now know when a debate is lost: at the first Godwin point.
textes.En 1951, le philosophe Leo Strauss bapti: In 1951, the philosopher Leo Strauss named a common fallacy “reductio ad Hitlerum”: an idea would be bad because Hitler shared it. “Hitler was a vegetarian” says nothing about vegetarianism. He added that an idea is not refuted by the fact that Hitler happened to hold it.
textes.Maîtriser l'art de réfuter et de débattr: Master the art of refuting and debating. The 1858 audience had more patience than you.
textes.En 1858, Abraham Lincoln et Stephen Doug: In 1858, Abraham Lincoln and Stephen Douglas compete for a Senate seat in seven three-hour public debates: an hour for the first speaker, an hour and a half for the reply, half an hour to conclude. Lincoln loses the election. The debates, once published, carry him to the presidency two years later.
textes.Aladin n'est pas dans les Mille et Une N: Aladdin is not in the Thousand and One Nights
textes.Maîtriser l'art de raconter. Les meilleu: Master the art of storytelling. The best stories were often added after the fact.
textes.Aladin et Ali Baba ne figurent dans aucu: Aladdin and Ali Baba appear in no early Arabic manuscript of the Thousand and One Nights. The translator Antoine Galland heard them in 1709 from a Syrian storyteller passing through Paris, Hanna Diyab, and added them to his translation. They are the two most famous tales in the collection.
textes.Maîtriser les grands discours. Kennedy n: Master great speeches. Kennedy was not a doughnut. Neither are you.
textes.On répète que Kennedy, en disant « Ich b: People repeat that Kennedy, by saying “Ich bin ein Berliner” in 1963, said “I am a doughnut”. That's false: the sentence is correct German, and the audience understood it as intended. The myth was born twenty years later, in the English-language press.
textes.Maîtriser la propagande et la manipulati: Master propaganda and manipulation. The newspapers of 1938 knew how to manipulate too.
textes.Le 30 octobre 1938, Orson Welles adapte: On October 30, 1938, Orson Welles adapts The War of the Worlds for radio. The next day, newspapers report widespread panic. Few people were listening, and almost none fled. The press, which saw radio stealing its advertising, had every interest in blowing up the story.
textes.Réussir trois quiz d'Éloquence sans faut: Pass three Eloquence quizzes without a mistake. Short, right. Lincoln approves.
textes.À Gettysburg, en 1863, Edward Everett pa: At Gettysburg, in 1863, Edward Everett speaks for two hours. Lincoln then delivers barely more than 270 words, in two minutes. The next day, Everett writes to him that he would be glad if he had come as near to the central idea of the occasion in two hours as Lincoln did in two minutes.
textes.Maîtriser l'art de parler avant la rhéto: Master speaking before rhetoric. The perfect word was hidden; you found it.
textes.« Un mot parfait est plus caché que les: "A perfect word is hidden more deeply than precious stones. It is to be found near the servants working at the mill-stone." An Egyptian vizier thus reminded his son, some four thousand years ago, that eloquence does not depend on rank.
textes.Mauvais œuf d'un mauvais corbeau: Bad egg of a bad crow
textes.Maîtriser les sophistes. Vous savez main: Master the sophists. You can now argue both sides. The AI will bill you for both.
textes.Tisias, élève de Corax, refuse de payer: Tisias, Corax's pupil, refused to pay for his lessons. In court he argued: if I learned well, I can convince you I owe nothing; if not, your teaching is worthless. Corax turned the argument around. The judge dismissed them both: "a bad egg from a bad crow". Corax means crow.
Master persuading the prince. You now know where not to touch the AI.
textes.« Le dragon est une bête douce : si on l: "The dragon is a gentle beast. If you indulge him and humor him, you may ride on his back. But beneath his throat there are transverse scales a foot long, and if you touch those scales, he will kill you. The lord of men also has transverse scales." Han Fei, 3rd century BC.
textes.Maîtriser l'éloquence de Cicéron. Votre: Master Cicero's eloquence. Your tongue is precious: keep it away from Fulvia.
textes.Le 7 décembre 43 av. J.-C., Cicéron, pro: On 7 December 43 BC, Cicero, proscribed, was killed near his villa at Formiae. On Mark Antony's orders, his head and hands were nailed to the Rostra. According to Cassius Dio, Fulvia, Antony's wife, took the head, pulled out the tongue and pierced it with a hairpin. The story is often wrongly attributed to Plutarch.
textes.Maîtriser Quintilien. Habile à parler, c: Master Quintilian. Skilled at speaking: done. A good man: the AI is waiting to see.
textes.Pour Quintilien, reprenant Caton l'Ancie: For Quintilian, following Cato the Elder, the orator is "a good man skilled at speaking". The perfect orator is first a good man, and only then a good speaker. Fourteen centuries later, Luther would say he preferred Quintilian to almost all authors.
textes.Maîtriser le débat indien. Thèse, raison: Master Indian debate. Thesis, reason, rule, application, conclusion: you earned this achievement, in five members.
textes.« Il y a du feu sur la colline. Car il y: "There is a fire on the hill. Because there is smoke on the hill. Whenever there is smoke, there is a fire. The hill is smoky. Therefore, there is a fire on the hill."
textes.Maîtriser l'éloquence arabe. Rangez vos: Master Arabic eloquence. Store your books flat, you never know.
Al-Jahiz reportedly wrote two hundred books. According to tradition, he died in Basra, aged over ninety, smothered by a mountain of books that fell on him.
textes.Maîtriser la chaire et l'école. Le trivi: Master the pulpit and the school. The trivium was the easy stage. You see where the AI is going.
textes.Grammaire, logique, rhétorique : le triv: Grammar, logic, rhetoric: the trivium opened the seven liberal arts, before the harder quadrivium. According to John Ayto's dictionary of word origins, our word "trivial" comes from this contrast.
textes.Maîtriser la parole des griots. L'IA cha: Master the word of the griots. The AI will sing your praises. For a fee.
textes.Dans l'épopée de Soundiata, le griot Bal: In the epic of Sundiata, the griot Balla Fasséké gets into the court of the enemy, Soumaoro, by playing his sacred balafon. After Sundiata's victory, he becomes its guardian, and the charge passes to his descendants, the Kouyatés, who still keep the Sosso Bala at Niagassola.
textes.Maîtriser l'imprimerie et les humanistes: Master printing and the humanists. The AI thanks you. Once, not 195 times.
textes.Dans De copia, en 1512, Érasme reformule: In De copia, in 1512, Erasmus rephrases the same sentence 195 times: "your letter delighted me greatly". The book, written for St Paul's School in London, went through at least 85 editions in the author's lifetime.
textes.Maîtriser les controverses de l'âge clas: Master the controversies of the classical age. The AI has been convinced. Pleased is another matter.
textes.Vers 1658, Pascal écrit que l'art de per: Around 1658, Pascal wrote that the art of persuading combines two arts: that of convincing, which addresses the mind, and that of pleasing, which addresses the heart and will. The text was meant to preface a geometry book for the little schools of Port-Royal.
textes.Maîtriser les théories modernes de l'arg: Master modern theories of argumentation. The AI looked for the flaw. She found a diagram.
textes.En 1958, Les usages de l'argumentation d: In 1958, Stephen Toulmin's The Uses of Argument was poorly received in England: his fellow philosophers at Leeds nicknamed it "Toulmin's anti-logic book". In the United States, rhetoricians adopted it; in 1963, Brockriede and Ehninger made it a tool for training debaters.
textes.Émotions, mémoire, motivation et influen: Emotions, memory, motivation and the influence of others.
textes.Hippocrate de Cos et ses disciples décri: Hippocrates of Kos and his disciples describe diseases as natural phenomena, not divine punishments. The treatise on the “sacred disease,” epilepsy, states that it is no more sacred than the others, and places in the brain the source of our joys, laughter, sorrows and fears. The Hippocratic Oath is probably not his, and the phrase “first, do no harm” does not appear in it word for word.
textes.« D'abord, ne pas nuire. » Formule absen: “First, do no harm.” A phrase missing from the original oath. The AI, for her part, does harm methodically.
textes.Retiré dans la tour de son château, Mich: Withdrawn into the tower of his château, Michel de Montaigne published the Essays: he takes himself as his subject and doubts what people think they know. His motto, “What do I know?”, comes with a pair of scales in balance. He writes about his fears, his anger, his friendship with La Boétie (“because it was he, because it was I”), notes that “each man calls barbarism whatever is not his own practice,” and wants the child to have a tutor with “a well-made rather than a well-filled head.”
textes.« Que sais-je ? » demandait Montaigne. L: “What do I know?” asked Montaigne. The AI knows exactly what you don't know.
textes.« Que sais-je ? », demande Montaigne. Pa: “What do I know?” asks Montaigne. Not much, evidently: back to Averroes.
textes.À la fin du IVe siècle av. J.-C., Théoph: At the end of the 4th century BC, Theophrastus, Aristotle's successor at the head of the Lyceum in Athens, sketches thirty human types in his Characters: short portraits of ordinary faults, caught through gestures and habits rather than theory. It is one of the first catalogues of personalities. Twenty centuries later, in 1688, La Bruyère translates them and writes his own Characters in their wake.
textes.Trente caractères, et aucun ne vous ress: Thirty characters, and none of them is you. A thirty-first was needed: the ill-informed optimist.
textes.Né esclave vers l'an 50 à Hiérapolis, en: Born a slave around the year 50 at Hierapolis, in Phrygia, Epictetus becomes a Stoic teacher. Lame, he teaches a simple distinction: some things are up to us, our judgements and our actions; others are not, outside events, which must be met calmly. He writes nothing. His pupil Arrian, who follows him around 108, records his lessons in the Discourses and draws a short Handbook from them.
textes.Votre note ne dépend pas de vous ? Si. É: Your score isn't up to you? Yes it is. Epictetus would be categorical.
textes.En 1649, René Descartes publie Les Passi: In 1649, René Descartes publishes The Passions of the Soul, born of his correspondence with Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia, to whom he dedicates the book. He counts six primitive passions: wonder, love, hatred, desire, joy and sadness. "Animal spirits", produced in the blood, move the body, and the soul is linked to it through a small gland in the brain, the pineal gland.
textes.Six passions primitives. Chez vous, je n: Six primitive passions. In you I only observe one: sadness, at every result.
textes.Philippe Pinel est resté l'homme qui a l: Philippe Pinel is remembered as the man who freed the insane from their chains at Bicêtre. The archives tell another story: it was Jean-Baptiste Pussin, the asylum's superintendent, who removed the irons in 1797, when Pinel had already left for the Salpêtrière, where he would do the same later. Pinel did change care: no more bleeding or purging, but observation and conversation, what would be called "moral treatment".
textes.Le héros n'était pas celui de la légende: The hero wasn't the one in the legend. Like in your group projects, I imagine.
textes.Le 13 septembre 1848, dans le Vermont, P: On 13 September 1848, in Vermont, Phineas Gage is preparing a blast on a railway site. The charge goes off too soon: an iron bar 1.1 m long and weighing 6 kg goes through his skull and destroys much of his left frontal lobe. He survives. His friends say he is "no longer Gage". But the accounts have greatly exaggerated: he would go on to drive stagecoaches in Chile, a demanding job, until shortly before his death in 1860.
textes.Une barre de fer dans le crâne, et il co: An iron bar through his skull, and he still drove stagecoaches. A multiple-choice question knocks you out.
textes.En 1861, à Paris, le chirurgien Paul Bro: In 1861, in Paris, the surgeon Paul Broca examines a patient who can only say one syllable: "tan". On his death, the autopsy shows a lesion on the surface of the left frontal lobe. A second patient, Lazare Lelong, who can say only five words, has a lesion in the same place. Broca concludes that speech production lives in a precise area of the brain, which now bears his name. "Tan"'s brain is kept at Sorbonne University.
textes.Un seul mot, « tan », et il a fait avanc: A single word, "tan", and he moved science forward. You say a lot more, without the same result.
textes.Le 26 novembre 1872, Charles Darwin publ: On 26 November 1872, Charles Darwin publishes The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals. He had sent a questionnaire to missionaries and travellers: do distant peoples show anger or fear with the same expressions? He also shows his family photos of faces electrically stimulated by Duchenne de Boulogne. His conclusion: the main expressions are shared, the legacy of a common evolution. The book quickly sells nearly 7,000 copies.
textes.Darwin a classé les expressions humaines: Darwin classified human expressions. Yours, facing this question, isn't in there. Too recent.
textes.En 1879, à l'université de Leipzig, Wilh: In 1879, at the University of Leipzig, Wilhelm Wundt opens the first laboratory devoted entirely to psychology. Reaction times are measured there. Wundt distrusts naive introspection: observing oneself must be learned and done under experimental control. He would supervise 185 theses, 70 of them by foreign students, who spread everywhere. He is called the father of experimental psychology, a title he himself gave to Ernst Weber.
textes.Wundt mesurait les temps de réaction à l: Wundt measured reaction times in fractions of a second. Yours are measured with a calendar.
textes.De 1880 à 1885, Hermann Ebbinghaus appre: From 1880 to 1885, Hermann Ebbinghaus learns meaningless syllables by heart, such as WID or ZOF, then tests himself at various intervals. Sole subject: himself. In 1885 he publishes Über das Gedächtnis and the first forgetting curve: you lose a lot at first, then the loss slows down. Spaced reviews flatten the curve. In 2015, a replication carried out the same way found results close to his. This game's reminders are built on that curve.
textes.Sans Ebbinghaus, pas de rappels. Si vous: No Ebbinghaus, no reminders. If you hate your reviews, now you know whom to curse.
textes.En 1897, le physiologiste russe Ivan Pav: In 1897, the Russian physiologist Ivan Pavlov publishes his work on digestion in dogs, which would earn him the Nobel Prize in 1904. He notices that his dogs salivate before the meal, as soon as the lab assistant who feeds them arrives. He calls this "psychic secretion" and studies it: a metronome, then food, and soon the metronome alone brings on salivation. And the famous bell? It is not certain he ever used one.
textes.Un métronome, et ils salivaient. Il me s: A metronome, and they drooled. I only have to say "reminder" and you sigh. Same principle.
textes.En 1904, le ministère de l'Instruction p: In 1904, the French Ministry of Public Instruction sets up a commission to identify pupils who need adapted teaching. Alfred Binet is its secretary. In 1905, with Théodore Simon, he develops a scale of tasks graded by age: a child's mental age is the age of the tasks he or she passes. In 1916, the American Lewis Terman revises it and derives the IQ from it, a single number that Simon would call a betrayal of the test's purpose.
textes.Le test servait à aider les élèves en di: The test was meant to help struggling pupils. I'm not saying that's you. I'm not saying anything.
textes.Au début du XXe siècle, en Allemagne, le: In the early 20th century, in Germany, the horse Hans seems able to count: his owner, Wilhelm von Osten, a mathematics teacher, sets him sums and Hans taps out the answer with his hoof. In 1904, a thirteen-member commission finds no trickery. In 1907, the psychologist Oskar Pfungst finds the trick: Hans is right 89% of the time when he can see a questioner who knows the answer, 6% otherwise. He reads people's involuntary cues.
textes.Un cheval lisait les visages mieux que v: A horse read faces better than you read questions. And he had no thumbs.
textes.En 1908, Robert Yerkes et John Dodson pu: In 1908, Robert Yerkes and John Dodson publish a study of learning in Japanese dancing mice according to the strength of the stimulus. A law was drawn from it: performance rises with arousal, then falls past a threshold, in an inverted U. For a simple task, more pressure helps; for a hard task, too much pressure brings you down. The original paper, though, only spoke of stimulus strength, not arousal.
textes.Un peu de pression aide, trop vous fait: A little pressure helps, too much brings you down. I dose mine carefully. Well, almost.
textes.En 1932, le psychologue britannique Fred: In 1932, the British psychologist Frederic Bartlett publishes Remembering. He had English students read a Native American tale, The War of the Ghosts, then asked them to retell it at intervals. The more time passes, the more the story is distorted: what does not fit their habits is forgotten or made familiar, canoes become boats. For Bartlett, remembering is not rereading a trace: it is reconstructing, using schemas drawn from our experience.
textes.Votre mémoire reconstruit. C'est pour ça: Your memory reconstructs. That's why you're so sure of your wrong answers.
textes.En 1943, le psychologue américain Abraha: In 1943, the American psychologist Abraham Maslow publishes A Theory of Human Motivation. He ranks five needs: physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, self-actualisation; a higher need wakes once the lower ones are more or less met. The famous pyramid? Maslow never drew it: it comes from a consultant, Charles McDermid, in a business journal. And studies struggle to confirm such a strict order.
textes.La pyramide de Maslow n'est pas de Maslo: Maslow's pyramid isn't Maslow's. The dunce cap I'm saving for you is all mine.
textes.Le 1er septembre 1953, pour soigner une: On 1 September 1953, to treat severe epilepsy, the neurosurgeon William Scoville removes both of Henry Molaison's hippocampi and the regions around them. Henry can no longer form new lasting memories. In the early 1960s, Brenda Milner has him trace a star looking only at its reflection in a mirror: he improves from one attempt to the next without remembering having tried. Knowing how and remembering are two distinct memories.
textes.Henry apprenait sans s'en souvenir. Vous: Henry learned without remembering. You remember without having learned. Admirable symmetry.
textes.En 1958, devant l'Association américaine: In 1958, before the American Psychological Association, Harry Harlow presents "The Nature of Love". He had given young monkeys two artificial mothers: one made of wire, the other covered in cloth. Even when only the wire mother holds the bottle, the infants go to her only to feed and stay clinging to the cloth mother. Attachment comes not from food but from contact. His experiments are now considered unethical.
textes.Même un singe préfère la douceur. Je vou: Even a monkey prefers softness. Fair warning: I have no cloth, only wire.
textes.En août 1961, à Yale, trois mois après l: In August 1961, at Yale, three months after the Eichmann trial opened, Stanley Milgram asks volunteers to give increasing shocks to a "learner", actually an actor, for each mistake. The shocks are fake. When they hesitate, the experimenter replies: "The experiment requires that you continue." Psychiatrists predicted barely one in a thousand would go all the way; 65% go up to 450 volts. Critics have since shown that many only half believed it.
textes.Rassurez-vous, mes punitions ne sont pas: Don't worry, my punishments aren't electric. Just humiliating. Step back two spaces.
textes.En 1961, pour l'armée de l'air américain: In 1961, for the US Air Force, Ernest Tupes and Raymond Christal analyse peer ratings and find five broad personality factors. The idea rests on a bet about language: an important trait must have a word. In 1936, Allport and Odbert had listed 4,504 descriptive adjectives in the dictionary. In 1981, Lewis Goldberg names the model the "Big Five": openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism.
textes.Cinq grands traits. Chez vous, j'en ajou: Five broad traits. In you I'd add a sixth: optimism when facing maths questions.
textes.Les Fore de Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée n': The Fore of Papua New Guinea had hardly seen films or magazines. Yet Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen show them photos of faces, and the Fore largely recognise the same emotions as elsewhere. Published in 1971, the study supports the idea of universal expressions, tempered by display rules specific to each culture. In 1978, they code every facial movement into action units. Their method is contested, and the debate goes on.
textes.Les Fore lisaient la peur sur un visage: The Fore read fear on an unknown face. I read panic on yours at every timer.
textes.En 1970 puis 1972, à Stanford, Walter Mi: In 1970 and then 1972, at Stanford, Walter Mischel offers children at the Bing Nursery School a deal: one treat right now, or two if they wait about fifteen minutes for the experimenter to return. In 1990, a follow-up finds that those who had waited longer get better SAT scores. In 2018, a replication with a more varied group finds a much weaker effect, which shrinks further once family background is taken into account.
textes.Deux friandises si vous attendez. Moi, j: Two treats if you wait. I offer you two reminders if you don't cheat. The deal is less sweet.
textes.Mihály Csíkszentmihályi s'intéressait au: Mihály Csíkszentmihályi was interested in painters who, absorbed in their canvas, forget to eat, drink and sleep. In 1975, he describes this "flow", the state where you lose yourself in what you are doing. Its conditions: a clear goal, immediate feedback, and a challenge matching your skills, neither too easy nor too hard. To study it, he has people fill in questionnaires at random moments, eight times a day. His book Flow comes out in 1990.
textes.Un défi à votre niveau, des retours immé: A challenge at your level, immediate feedback. That's exactly what I do. Thank me instead of sighing.
textes.En 1888, l'Espagnol Santiago Ramón y Caj: In 1888, the Spaniard Santiago Ramón y Cajal publishes his first drawings of the nervous system. He has perfected the silver stain of the Italian Camillo Golgi, which blackens a few neurons. He sees what Golgi will not accept: the brain is not a continuous network, but a set of separate cells divided by tiny gaps. As a child he dreamed of being a painter; his drawings are still used in teaching. In 1906, Cajal and Golgi share the Nobel Prize, without agreeing.
textes.Des milliards de neurones séparés. Chez: Billions of separate neurons. In your case, I suspect they don't talk much.
textes.Le 4 novembre 1899, à Vienne, Sigmund Fr: On 4 November 1899, in Vienna, Sigmund Freud publishes The Interpretation of Dreams, dated 1900. For him, every dream fulfils a hidden wish, and interpreting it is "the royal road" to the unconscious. The first print run of 600 copies would take eight years to sell. Psychoanalysis would mark the whole 20th century, but its methods are heavily criticised: Freud cited dreams in his own favour and his predecessors as it suited him.
textes.Vous rêvez de réussir ce quiz ? Freud y: You dream of passing this quiz? Freud would see a hidden wish. I see a dream.
textes.Piaget et le verre d'eau: Piaget and the glass of water
