In 1911, Binet revised the test without Simon, with five tasks per age, and died the same year. For him as for Simon, intelligence is malleable: the test is there to help, not to condemn.
textes.1905, trente épreuves ; 1908, l'âge ment: 1905, thirty tasks; 1908, mental age; a malleable intelligence, to be helped.
textes.En 1912, l'Allemand William Stern propos: In 1912, the German William Stern proposed dividing mental age by real age and multiplying by 100: the Intelligenzquotient, the IQ. Simon saw it as a betrayal of the test's purpose. In 1916, Lewis Terman, at Stanford, revised the scale and made it the most used test in the United States for decades. During the First World War, 1.75 million American soldiers took written tests.
textes.Les tests modernes ne calculent plus un: Modern tests no longer compute a quotient: they place each person on a curve with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15, where about two people in three are between 85 and 115. And raw scores rise by about three points per decade: the Flynn effect. In 1981, Stephen Jay Gould denounced in The Mismeasure of Man the idea of summing up intelligence in a single number.
textes.Stern (1912) : QI = âge mental ÷ âge rée: Stern (1912): IQ = mental age ÷ real age × 100. Today: mean 100, standard deviation 15; Flynn effect.
textes.Le stress de Selye, l'adaptation hédoniq: Selye's stress, hedonic adaptation, sleep, and Csíkszentmihályi's flow: what wears us down and what makes us happy.
textes.Trois façons de faire avec une émotion :: Three ways to handle an emotion: name it, reappraise it, suppress it
textes.Les deux faces de l'empathie, et l'écout: The two sides of empathy, and active listening that rephrases to check
textes.Salovey et Mayer 1990 · Goleman 1995 : i: Salovey and Mayer 1990 · Goleman 1995: emotional intelligence

textes.Ebbinghaus veut mesurer la mémoire comme: Ebbinghaus wants to measure memory the way a physicist measures heat. So that the meaning of words won't help him, he invents 2,300 nonsense syllables, like DAX or BOK, and learns them himself in lists, to the beat of a metronome. He records how many repetitions he needs to relearn a list after a few minutes, hours or days. Result: forgetting is very fast at first, then slows down; this is the forgetting curve. He also shows that reviews spaced out over time are far more effective than massed reviews. For years, he was the only subject of his experiments.

textes.Le psychologue Abraham Maslow propose qu: The psychologist Abraham Maslow proposes that our needs are organized by priority: first physiological needs, eating, sleeping, then safety, belonging and love, esteem, and finally self-actualization. Later research qualified the strict order of needs, but the idea remains very influential.

textes.Vers 45, le philosophe stoïcien Sénèque: Around 45, the Stoic philosopher Seneca wrote for his elder brother Novatus a treatise in three books: "You have asked me, Novatus, to write on how anger can be mitigated." The first part explains what anger is; the second, from the middle of book II, gives remedies. For Seneca, a passion is a false belief about the value of things. He pursues two aims: preventing anger from arising, and doing no wrong when angry. He often cites the fits of rage of the emperor Caligula, who died in 41, and takes as his adversary Theophrastus, Aristotle's pupil. In book III, he decides: one must not control anger, but destroy it entirely.

textes.Le Dhammapada est un recueil de 423 vers: The Dhammapada is a collection of 423 verses in Pali, arranged in 26 chapters. It belongs to the Khuddaka Nikāya, one of the divisions of the Pali canon of Theravāda Buddhism. Its source may go back to the 3rd century BC, according to the scholar Glenn Wallis. More than half of its verses are found elsewhere in the canon. The first chapter opens thus: "Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, their quality is made by mind." A commentary attributed to Buddhaghosa, in the 4th or 5th century, tells 305 stories that place each verse. There are also versions in Gandhari and Sanskrit.

textes.Trente portraits très courts de types hu: Thirty very short portraits of human types, caught in the life of Athens at the end of the 4th century BC. Each opens with a one-sentence definition, then lines up gestures: the flatterer who laughs at his patron's dull jokes and assures him the whole city admires him; the superstitious man who sprinkles himself with water before starting his day; the coward, the miser, the chatterbox, the man who learns late in life. There is neither moral nor theory: Theophrastus looks and describes. The translators Bennett and Hammond think it was probably written in 319 BC. textes.Le Manuel, ou Enchiridion, est un petit: The Handbook, or Enchiridion, is a small book of 53 chapters that Arrian drew, in the early 2nd century, from the lessons of his master Epictetus. It is dated around 125. It opens with a distinction: some things depend on us, our judgements, desires and choices; others do not, the body, reputation, events. Everything else follows. In chapter 5, the most famous sentence: what upsets people is not things themselves but their judgements about things. The book is meant as a practical reminder, to keep at hand. It enjoyed its greatest vogue between 1550 and 1750, with Neostoicism.

textes.Écrit par Abu Zayd al-Balkhi, qui vécut: Written by Abu Zayd al-Balkhi, who lived from 850 to 934, this treatise, Masalih al-Abdan wa al-Anfus, deals with the body and then the soul: its second part is the work on the soul. The author reproaches physicians for forgetting their patients' minds. In it he classifies emotional disorders into four families, fear, anger, sadness and obsession, distinguishes three kinds of depression and proposes for each a treatment through words and reflection. Against phobia, he recommends gradual exposure to what one dreads. He draws on the Qur'an and the hadiths, and links mental health to spiritual health. He is counted among the first to attribute both psychological and physiological causes to illnesses of the mind.

textes.Publié en 1575 par Juan Huarte de San Ju: Published in 1575 by Juan Huarte de San Juan, a physician born around 1529 at Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, in Lower Navarre, the Examen de ingenios para las ciencias starts from a simple idea: each person has a talent of his own, and should practise the trade that matches it. This talent depends on temperament, according to the old theory of humours: memory, for example, was thought to depend on moisture and understanding on dryness. Children must therefore be studied very young to find where they excel. First banned by the Inquisition, the book reappeared expurgated after the author's death. It went through sixty editions up to 1800 and translations into French, Italian, English, Latin, German and Dutch.

textes.Achevé en 1649 et dédié à la princesse É: Completed in 1649 and dedicated to Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia, this treatise grew out of the letters exchanged since 1643, in which she questioned him about happiness, morals and the union of soul and body. In three parts and 212 short articles, Descartes first explains the body's machine: animal spirits, produced in the blood, move the limbs, and the soul is attached to the body by the pineal gland. Then he takes stock of the passions: six primitive ones, wonder, love, hatred, desire, joy and sadness, of which all the others are made. He concludes that the passions are good in themselves, that one need only avoid their excess, and that one can learn to govern them.

textes.Publié en 1801, trois ans après sa Nosog: Published in 1801, three years after his Nosographie philosophique, the Medico-philosophical Treatise on Mental Alienation, or Mania, gathers what Philippe Pinel learned at Bicêtre and then at the Salpêtrière. In it he sorts madness into four types, melancholia, mania, dementia and idiotism, and defends moral treatment: observing patients, talking to them, keeping them busy, instead of chaining, bleeding or purging them. textes.En 1860, à Leipzig, Gustav Fechner publi: In 1860, in Leipzig, Gustav Fechner published his Elemente der Psychophysik in two volumes. In it he sought an exact mathematical relation between mind and body. He started from Ernst Weber's experiments: we do not perceive an absolute difference, but a ratio; it takes about 108 g to tell a weight from 100 g. Fechner gave his name to this Weber's law, and drew his own from it: sensation grows as the logarithm of stimulus intensity, because the stimulus must increase in geometric progression for sensation to rise steadily. The book's title named the discipline: psychophysics, the measurement of sensations.

textes.En 1948, le psychologue comportementalis: In 1948, the behaviourist psychologist B. F. Skinner published a novel. The narrator, Professor Burris, accompanies two young veterans to a rural community founded by T. E. Frazier, where nearly a thousand people live. Everything rests on behavioural engineering: from birth, education shapes cooperative relationships and erases the competitive spirit. People work about four hours a day; each task earns credits, and the least pleasant earn more. A board of six planners governs. Burris's colleague, Professor Castle, suspects Frazier of being a despot. The novel caused controversy because it rejects free will: it is the environment that shapes behaviour.

textes.Publié le 4 novembre 1899 à Leipzig et V: Published on 4 November 1899 in Leipzig and Vienna by Franz Deuticke, but dated 1900, this book defends a thesis: every dream is the fulfilment of a wish. This wish is censored and repressed; during sleep, the unconscious condenses and displaces it, so that the manifest content, the one we remember, hides a latent content that must be interpreted. Freud's first great example is one of his own dreams, Irma's injection, from the summer of 1895, in which he sees the wish to be cleared of a fault towards a patient. The first printing, 600 copies, took eight years to sell; seven more editions followed in his lifetime. A. A. Brill gave the authorised English translation in 1913.

textes.En 1981, le paléontologue Stephen Jay Go: In 1981, the palaeontologist Stephen Jay Gould attacked biological determinism: the idea that social and economic differences between groups stem from inborn differences. His main target is the assumption that worth can be assigned to individuals and groups by measuring intelligence as a single quantity. He saw two errors in it: reification, which turns an abstract concept into a thing, and ranking, which orders complex variation on a single ascending scale. He took on IQ, the g factor, and Samuel Morton's skull measurements. A revised edition, in 1996, added two chapters against The Bell Curve. The book won awards, but was also sharply criticised by psychologists who accused it of misrepresenting Binet or Terman.

textes.D'où sanguin, flegmatique, colérique et: Hence sanguine, phlegmatic, choleric and melancholic (“black bile” in Greek). The theory is wrong, the words stayed.
textes.La phrénologie de Franz Joseph Gall prét: Franz Joseph Gall's phrenology claimed to read character:
textes.dans les bosses du crâne: in the bumps of the skull
textes.dans les lignes de la main: in the lines of the hand
textes.Elle nous a laissé l'expression « avoir: It left French with the expression “avoir la bosse des maths”, having a bump for math.
textes.Selon les études de jumeaux, les traits: According to twin studies, personality traits are heritable to about:
textes.Le reste tient surtout aux expériences p: The rest is mostly due to each person's own experiences, more than to the shared family. Twins raised together are no more alike than twins raised apart.
textes.L'erreur fondamentale d'attribution cons: The fundamental attribution error consists in:
textes.expliquer le comportement d'autrui par s: explaining others' behavior by their character rather than the situation
textes.Il vous coupe la route : c'est un chauff: He cuts you off: he's a reckless driver. You cut someone off: you were in a hurry (Ross, 1977).
textes.Parmi les Big Five, la conscienciosité e: Among the Big Five, conscientiousness is the trait most linked to academic success.
textes.Organisation, persévérance et fiabilité: Organization, perseverance and reliability predict results almost as well as intelligence (Poropat, 2009).
textes.Hans Selye a popularisé le mot « stress: Hans Selye popularized the word “stress” by describing:
textes.un syndrome d'adaptation en trois phases: an adaptation syndrome in three phases: alarm, resistance, exhaustion
textes.Sa lettre à Nature, en 1936, décrit des: His letter to Nature, in 1936, describes rats subjected to all kinds of harm. He borrowed the word from materials physics.
textes.Quelle hormone des glandes surrénales es: Which adrenal hormone is nicknamed the “stress hormone”?
textes.Utile à court terme pour mobiliser l'éne: Useful in the short term to mobilize energy. Chronically high, it weakens immunity and memory.
textes.La loi de Yerkes et Dodson (1908) dit qu: The Yerkes-Dodson law (1908) says that performance:
textes.augmente avec l'activation jusqu'à un po: rises with arousal up to a point, then falls
textes.baisse dès qu'il y a du stress: drops as soon as there is stress
textes.Une courbe en cloche : un peu de trac ai: A bell curve: a little stage fright helps, a lot paralyzes. The authors established it on mice.
textes.Selon l'étude d'Harvard sur le développe: According to the Harvard Study of Adult Development, running since 1938, the best predictor of a long, happy life is:
textes.Robert Waldinger, son quatrième directeu: Robert Waldinger, its fourth director: “Good relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period.”
textes.Après un grand gain ou une grande perte,: After a big gain or a big loss, happiness tends to return close to its usual level.
textes.C'est l'adaptation hédonique. Brickman (: This is hedonic adaptation. Brickman (1978) compared lottery winners with people who had become paraplegic. The return is not always complete.
textes.La psychologie positive a été lancée en: Positive psychology was launched in 1998 by:
textes.Devenu président de l'Association améric: Having become president of the American Psychological Association, he proposed studying what goes right as well.
textes.cesser d'essayer après avoir appris qu'o: giving up after learning that you control nothing
textes.oublier ce qu'on sait faire: forgetting what you know how to do
textes.Découverte dans des expériences sur des: Discovered in experiments on dogs, it fed into the understanding of depression.
textes.Combien d'heures de sommeil par nuit son: What is the minimum recommended number of hours of sleep per night for an adult?
textes.Les recommandations vont de 7 à 9 heures: Recommendations range from 7 to 9 hours. Regularly sleeping less than 6 hours is linked to many health risks.
textes.L'activité physique régulière, face à l': Regular physical activity, against anxiety and mild depression:
textes.n'agit que par effet placebo: only works through the placebo effect
textes.Plusieurs méta-analyses la placent à un: Several meta-analyses put it at a level close to psychotherapy for mild to moderate forms.
textes.La pleine conscience a été introduite en: Mindfulness was brought into medicine to reduce stress by:
textes.Jon Kabat-Zinn, avec son programme MBSR: Jon Kabat-Zinn, with his MBSR program in 1979
textes.Huit semaines d'exercices de méditation,: Eight weeks of secularized meditation exercises, for patients with chronic pain.
textes.Psychiatre dans une clinique gratuite de: A psychiatrist at a free clinic in New York, he observed it in volunteers, and in himself. The WHO recognized it in 2019 as an “occupational phenomenon”.
textes.Écrire sur ses émotions difficiles quelq: Writing about your difficult emotions for a few days in a row can improve health.
textes.Le protocole d'écriture expressive de Ja: James Pennebaker's expressive writing protocol (1986) showed fewer visits to the doctor. The effects are real but modest.
textes.Darwin défendait déjà en 1872 l'idée d'é: Darwin already argued in 1872 that emotions are universal. Paul Ekman tested the idea with Wallace Friesen among the Fore of Papua New Guinea, then completed his Facial Action Coding System (FACS) in 1978. The hero of the TV series Lie to Me is based on him.
textes.Karl Friedrich Burdach nomme l'amygdale: Karl Friedrich Burdach named the amygdala in 1822. In 1939, Heinrich Klüver and Paul Bucy observed that monkeys deprived of this region lost their fear. Patient S. M., whose two amygdalae were destroyed by Urbach–Wiethe disease, feels almost no fear.
textes.Paul Ekman et Wallace Friesen publient e: Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen published their study of the Fore of Papua New Guinea, an isolated people, in 1971: they recognised the same basic expressions as Westerners.
textes.Le philosophe allemand Theodor Lipps emp: German philosopher Theodor Lipps used the word Einfühlung, "feeling into", in 1903. Psychologist Edward Titchener rendered it in English as empathy in 1909, from the Greek empatheia.
textes.L'expression apparaît peut-être dès 1964: The phrase may first appear in 1964 in Michael Beldoch's work. Peter Salovey and John Mayer defined it in 1990, and journalist Daniel Goleman turned it into a bestseller in 1995. The scientific validity of these measures is still criticised.
textes.Le physiologiste américain Walter Cannon: American physiologist Walter Cannon described this response in 1914 and wrote of "fighting or flight" in 1915. He showed the role of adrenaline, released by the adrenal glands.
textes.En 2007, Matthew Lieberman et son équipe: In 2007, Matthew Lieberman and colleagues showed that naming what you feel lowers amygdala activity. Talk therapies have used it for more than a century.
textes.Elaine Hatfield, John Cacioppo et Richar: Elaine Hatfield, John Cacioppo and Richard Rapson devoted a book to emotional contagion in 1993. In 2014, a Facebook and Cornell University study that altered users' news feeds without their knowledge drew strong criticism.
textes.Le psychologue James Gross propose en 19: Psychologist James Gross proposed his process model of emotion regulation in 1998. Reappraisal is classed in it among the adaptive strategies.
textes.Dans le modèle de James Gross (1998), la: In James Gross's model (1998), expressive suppression is classed among the maladaptive strategies, unlike reappraisal.
textes.L'équipe de Giacomo Rizzolatti, à Parme,: Giacomo Rizzolatti's team in Parma discovered them in the 1980s-1990s in the macaque's area F5: neurons that fire both when the monkey grasps an object and when it sees someone do it (di Pellegrino et al., 1992). Their role in human empathy remains poorly established.
textes.Dans Über das Gedächtnis (1885), Hermann: In Über das Gedächtnis (1885), Hermann Ebbinghaus used himself as the subject, learning lists of nonsense syllables drawn from 2,300 of them. From this he derived the forgetting curve.
textes.L'article de George Miller paraît en 195: George Miller's paper appeared in 1956 in Psychological Review and is among the most cited in psychology. Nelson Cowan has since proposed a lower limit of about 4 chunks.
textes.C'est Hermann Ebbinghaus qui découvre l': It was Hermann Ebbinghaus who discovered the spacing effect, by studying himself in Über das Gedächtnis (1885).
textes.L'anatomiste Giulio Cesare Aranzi la com: Anatomist Giulio Cesare Aranzi compared it in 1587 to a silkworm, then to a seahorse, which gave it its name. In 1971, John O'Keefe and Jonathan Dostrovsky found "place cells" in it.
textes.Le chirurgien William Scoville l'opère l: Surgeon William Scoville operated on him on 1 September 1953 in Hartford to treat his epilepsy. Scoville and Brenda Milner reported the case in 1957. Henry Molaison could no longer retain anything new, yet he learned mirror drawing without remembering having practised.
Henry Molaison died on 2 December 2008. On 4 December 2009, Jacopo Annese's team cut his brain into 2,401 slices to study it.
textes.En 1974, avec John Palmer, Elizabeth Lof: In 1974, with John Palmer, Elizabeth Loftus showed that a crash video was judged faster depending on the question's verb: 34 mph for "hit", 41 for "smashed". She has testified as an expert in more than 300 court cases.
Cicero tells, in De Oratore (55 BC), how the poet Simonides identified the dead of a collapsed banquet hall by where each had sat. The method is described around 90 BC in the Rhetorica ad Herennium, and memory champions still use it.
textes.En 1924, John Jenkins et Karl Dallenbach: In 1924, John Jenkins and Karl Dallenbach found that people remember a list better after sleeping than after the same time spent awake.
textes.William James le décrit dès 1890. En 196: William James described it as early as 1890. In 1966, Roger Brown and David McNeill induced it in the laboratory at Harvard. According to Bennett Schwartz (1999), 45 of 51 languages have an idiom for it.
textes.Des études montrent qu'un poisson rouge: Studies show goldfish keep memories for at least three months. In 1994, at the University of Plymouth, goldfish learned to push a lever to get food. The show MythBusters also debunked the legend.
textes.Le terme d'effet de position sérielle vi: The term serial position effect comes from Hermann Ebbinghaus. In 1962, Bennet Murdock plotted its U-shaped curve: the start and end of a list are remembered better than the middle.
textes.Edward Deci et Richard Ryan bâtissent le: Edward Deci and Richard Ryan built their self-determination theory from their mid-1980s book. In 1971, Deci paid $1 per solved puzzle (the Soma puzzle) to measure the urge to keep going without reward.
textes.Edward Deci et Richard Ryan posent ces t: Edward Deci and Richard Ryan set out these three needs, autonomy, competence and relatedness, in their theory from the mid-1980s.
textes.En 1971, Edward Deci montre que des étud: In 1971, Edward Deci showed that students paid to solve puzzles came back to them less of their own accord afterwards than those who received nothing.
textes.Abraham Maslow expose sa hiérarchie des: Abraham Maslow set out his hierarchy of needs in 1943 in Psychological Review. He never drew a pyramid: it is due to consultant Charles McDermid, in the journal Business Horizons.
textes.Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi part de l'observ: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi started from watching painters, so absorbed they forgot hunger and fatigue. He described flow in Beyond Boredom and Anxiety (1975), then in a popular book in 1990.
textes.Edwin Locke lance la théorie de la fixat: Edwin Locke launched goal-setting theory in 1968. With Gary Latham, he summarised it in 1990 and again in 2002, from about 400 studies.
textes.La première expérience a lieu en 1970 à: The first experiment took place in 1970 at Stanford's Bing Nursery School. A 1990 follow-up linked waiting to better SAT scores, but a 2018 replication by Tyler Watts and colleagues found much smaller effects.
textes.Le mot vient du latin procrastinare, de: The word comes from the Latin procrastinare, from cras, "tomorrow". Psychologist Piers Steel defined it in 2007 as voluntarily delaying an intended course of action despite expecting to be worse off.
textes.Bluma Zeigarnik publie en 1927 dans Psyc: Bluma Zeigarnik published in 1927 in Psychologische Forschung, after Kurt Lewin noticed that a waiter remembered orders only until they were paid. A 2025 meta-analysis found no memory advantage for unfinished tasks.
textes.L'idée vient des recherches de Carol Dwe: The idea comes from Carol Dweck's research at Stanford. Large classroom trials have been disappointing: the Education Endowment Foundation's in 2019, then a 2024 study, found no gain.
textes.En 2009, Phillippa Lally suit des volont: In 2009, Phillippa Lally followed volunteers: on average it took them 66 days for an action to become automatic, from 18 to 254 depending on the case. William James already said we are "bundles of habits".
textes.Solomon Asch mène ses expériences en 195: Solomon Asch ran his experiments in 1951 at Swarthmore College. 74% of participants went along with the group's wrong answer at least once; with a single ally in the room, they gave in only 5% of the time.
textes.Stanley Milgram commence en août 1961, t: Stanley Milgram began in August 1961, three months after the trial of Adolf Eichmann opened in Jerusalem: he wanted to understand how ordinary people obey atrocious orders. He published in 1963.
textes.Dans la version de base, 65 % des partic: In the baseline version, 65% of participants went up to 450 volts. Jerry Burger in 2009 found similar rates, halting after the 150-volt switch; Gina Perry, in 2012, reported a troubling mismatch between the published descriptions and what actually happened.
textes.L'idée naît du meurtre de Kitty Genovese: The idea was born from the murder of Kitty Genovese in New York on 13 March 1964, whose story of neighbours who stayed passive was exaggerated: The New York Times itself acknowledged it in 2016. In 2019, Richard Philpot showed from street videos that someone intervened in over 90% of conflicts.
textes.Edward Thorndike nomme l'effet en 1920 :: Edward Thorndike named the effect in 1920: officers rated their soldiers good or bad at everything at once. In 1972, Karen Dion and colleagues showed that people credit attractive faces with more qualities.
textes.Leon Festinger publie sa théorie en 1957: Leon Festinger published his theory in 1957. With James Carlsmith, he showed that students paid $1 to praise a boring task ended up finding it more enjoyable than those paid $20.
textes.En 1966, Jonathan Freedman et Scott Fras: In 1966, Jonathan Freedman and Scott Fraser asked residents to accept a large sign in their yard: 76% said yes after a small prior request, against 17% without.
textes.En 1971, Dennis Regan montre que des par: In 1971, Dennis Regan showed that participants given a soft drink later bought more raffle tickets. Sociologist Phillip Kunz sent greeting cards to strangers: many sent one back.
textes.En 1975, Stephen Worchel et ses collègue: In 1975, Stephen Worchel and colleagues offered cookies from a jar: those from a jar holding only 2 were rated better than those from a jar holding 10.
textes.Tout part du mémoire de master de James: It all started with James Stoner's master's thesis at MIT in 1961, on the "risky shift" of groups. Serge Moscovici and Marisa Zavalloni generalised the effect in 1969: the group pushes in the direction it already leaned.
textes.William Whyte forge le mot groupthink en: William Whyte coined the word groupthink in 1952 in Fortune magazine. Irving Janis studied it through fiascos such as the Bay of Pigs invasion; the decision to launch the Challenger shuttle is another example often cited.
textes.En août 1971, 24 étudiants jouent gardie: In August 1971, 24 students played guards and prisoners; the experiment, planned for two weeks, was stopped on day 6 after Christina Maslach intervened. In 2018, Thibault Le Texier argued in Histoire d'un mensonge that the guards' behaviour was caused by Zimbardo's instructions.
textes.Le chiffre de 86 milliards vient de Suza: The figure of 86 billion comes from Suzana Herculano-Houzel: in 2005 she developed a method that dissolves the brain into a "soup" of cell nuclei that can be counted.
textes.Le mythe se répand en 1936, dans la préf: The myth spread in 1936, in Lowell Thomas's foreword to Dale Carnegie's book, which attributed the figure to William James. It is wrongly attributed to Einstein. Brain imaging shows that every region is active.
textes.Le 13 septembre 1848, à Cavendish (Vermo: On 13 September 1848, in Cavendish, Vermont, an iron bar 1.1 m long and weighing 6 kg went through the skull of this railroad foreman. According to his doctor John Harlow, he was "no longer Gage". Yet he ended up a stagecoach driver in Chile and died on 21 May 1860.
textes.Paul Broca examine en 1861 le cerveau de: In 1861, Paul Broca examined the brain of Louis Victor Leborgne, nicknamed "Tan", the only word he could say: a lesion of the left frontal lobe. Physician Marc Dax had made a similar observation a generation earlier.
textes.Santiago Ramón y Cajal colore les neuron: Santiago Ramón y Cajal stained neurons with Camillo Golgi's method, though Golgi believed in a continuous network. They shared the Nobel Prize in 1906, and Cajal's drawings are still used in textbooks.
textes.Le mythe vient d'une lecture abusive des: The myth comes from an overstretched reading of Roger Sperry and Michael Gazzaniga's 1960s studies of split-brain patients. In 2013, a University of Utah study found no "dominant side" in individuals.
textes.William James parle de plasticité dès 18: William James spoke of plasticity as early as 1890, and Pole Jerzy Konorski was the first to write "neural plasticity". Paul Bach-y-Rita showed that people can learn to "see" through touch.
textes.Eleanor Maguire a observé chez les chauf: Eleanor Maguire observed changes in the hippocampus of London taxi drivers, the region for memory of places.
textes.Seiji Ogawa découvre le signal BOLD en 1: Seiji Ogawa discovered the BOLD signal in 1990 at Bell Labs. The idea is old: Angelo Mosso already weighed blood flow to the brain, and Charles Roy and Charles Sherrington linked activity and blood flow in 1890. In 2009, a dead salmon "responded" in a badly analysed scan.
textes.Le neurochirurgien Wilder Penfield opère: Neurosurgeon Wilder Penfield operated on awake patients under local anaesthesia, a technique learned in Germany in 1928. By stimulating their cortex, he mapped the body's "little man", the homunculus. He founded the Montreal Neurological Institute in 1934.
textes.Cervelet veut dire « petit cerveau ». Ga: Cerebellum means "little brain". Galen already described it; Luigi Rolando in 1809, then Pierre Flourens showed its role in movement. It holds more neurons than all the rest of the brain.
textes.Chez Binet, à Paris, Jean Piaget corrige: At Binet's in Paris, Jean Piaget marked intelligence tests and became interested in children's mistakes. He then closely observed his own three children, and founded the International Centre for Genetic Epistemology in Geneva in 1955.
textes.Jean Piaget tire ses quatre stades en bo: Jean Piaget drew his four stages largely from observing his own three children.
textes.Piaget décrit « l'erreur A-non-B » : le: Piaget described the "A-not-B error": the baby looks for the toy where it found it before, not where it saw it hidden. In 1991, Renée Baillargeon and Julie DeVos showed that a baby of three and a half months is already surprised when a hidden object vanishes.
textes.En 1985, Simon Baron-Cohen, Alan Leslie: In 1985, Simon Baron-Cohen, Alan Leslie and Uta Frith ran the test: 85% of non-autistic children passed (23 of 27), against 20% of autistic children (4 of 20).
textes.Lev Vygotski introduit cette notion dans: Lev Vygotsky introduced this idea in the last three years of his life, before his death in 1934. The word "scaffolding", often linked to it, came later from Jerome Bruner, David Wood and Gail Ross.
textes.Harry Harlow présente ses résultats en 1: Harry Harlow presented his results in 1958 in "The Nature of Love": baby monkeys preferred the cloth mother to the wire mother that gave milk. These experiments are now considered unethical.
textes.Le psychiatre John Bowlby pose la théori: Psychiatrist John Bowlby set out the theory, and Mary Ainsworth devised the "Strange Situation" in the 1970s, observing a baby's reaction when its mother leaves and comes back.
textes.Selon Piaget, la conservation s'acquiert: According to Piaget, conservation is acquired around age 7. But when a "naughty teddy" messes up the row, in James McGarrigle and Margaret Donaldson's experiment, younger children succeed far more often.
textes.Janet Werker et Richard Tees le montrent: Janet Werker and Richard Tees showed it: at 6-8 months, babies tell apart the sounds of a foreign language better than at 8-10 months, when their ear has already tuned to the language they hear.
textes.En 1993, Frances Rauscher fait écouter M: In 1993, Frances Rauscher played Mozart to 36 students (not babies): a slight gain on a spatial task, lasting about fifteen minutes. Georgia governor Zell Miller nonetheless proposed in 1998 to give every newborn a classical music CD. Meta-analyses by Chabris (1999) and Pietschnig (2010) found no notable effect.
textes.Eleanor Gibson et Richard Walk testent 3: Eleanor Gibson and Richard Walk tested 36 babies aged 6 to 14 months; 27 of them crawled to their mother on the shallow side. More recent work indicates that this caution is not innate: it comes with experience.
textes.Francis Galton propose dès 1884 de cherc: Francis Galton proposed as early as 1884 looking for traits in the words of the language. In 1936, Gordon Allport and Henry Odbert listed 4,504 adjectives. Ernest Tupes and Raymond Christal found five factors in 1961, and Lewis Goldberg named them the "Big Five" in 1981.
textes.Katharine Briggs et sa fille Isabel Myer: Katharine Briggs and her daughter Isabel Myers, with no training in psychology, drew on Jung (1921) and began during the Second World War; the manual came out in 1962. Between 39 and 76% of people get a different type when retaking it five weeks later.
textes.Le névrosisme fait partie des cinq facte: Neuroticism is one of the five factors found by Ernest Tupes and Raymond Christal in 1961, which Lewis Goldberg named the "Big Five" in 1981.
textes.Pour Hans Eysenck, l'introverti a un cer: For Hans Eysenck, the introvert has an already highly aroused brain and seeks less stimulation. In 2012, Susan Cain's book Quiet popularised the defence of introverts.
textes.Carl Jung les introduit dans Psychologis: Carl Jung introduced them in Psychologische Typen in 1921, translated into English in 1923.
textes.Delroy Paulhus et Kevin Williams nomment: Delroy Paulhus and Kevin Williams named the dark triad in 2002. Machiavellianism was already measured with Richard Christie and Florence Geis's MACH-IV scale (1970). Sadism is sometimes added: the "dark tetrad".
textes.La théorie des quatre humeurs vient d'Hi: The theory of the four humours comes from Hippocrates; Galen drew from it the four temperaments: sanguine, phlegmatic, choleric and melancholic. Kant still used them in 1798.
textes.Franz Joseph Gall lance sa « cranioscopi: Franz Joseph Gall launched his "cranioscopy" around 1796; his collaborator Johann Spurzheim popularised the word "phrenology". Pierre Flourens's experiments helped discredit it by the 1840s.
textes.À partir de 1979, Thomas Bouchard étudie: From 1979, Thomas Bouchard studied identical twins raised apart in Minneapolis: they are about 50% alike in personality.
textes.Lee Ross nomme cette erreur en 1977, d'a: Lee Ross named this error in 1977, based on Edward Jones and Victor Harris's experiment (1967): even knowing a writer had been assigned to argue for Fidel Castro, readers credited the writer with that opinion.
textes.Le modèle des Big Five vient de Tupes et: The Big Five model comes from Tupes and Christal (1961) and Goldberg (1981); of the five traits, conscientiousness best predicts exam success.
textes.En 1936, Hans Selye publie « A Syndrome: In 1936, Hans Selye published "A Syndrome Produced by Diverse Nocuous Agents": he observed that rats exposed to cold, drugs or injury all reacted the same way, in three phases. He later distinguished good stress (eustress) from bad (distress).
textes.Robert Yerkes et John Dodson publient en: Robert Yerkes and John Dodson published in 1908 in the Journal of Comparative Neurology and Psychology, from experiments on dancing mice. The paper was cited only ten times in fifty years before becoming famous.
textes.L'étude commence en 1938 à la faculté de: The study began in 1938 at Harvard Medical School, funded by William Thomas Grant, with 268 students. George Vaillant directed it for more than thirty years; Robert Waldinger took over. One of its conclusions: success depends on warmth of relationships, not on intelligence.
textes.Philip Brickman et Donald Campbell parle: Philip Brickman and Donald Campbell spoke of the "hedonic treadmill" in 1971. In 1978, Brickman, Dan Coates and Ronnie Janoff-Bulman compared 22 lottery winners and 29 paraplegics: the winners were no happier than before, and the paraplegics expected to get back to their level within a couple of years.
textes.Martin Seligman en fait le thème de sa p: Martin Seligman made it the theme of his term as president of the American Psychological Association in 1998, feeling the field focused too much on illness. The phrase dates back at least to 1954, the title of a chapter by Maslow.
textes.En 1967, à l'université de Pennsylvanie,: In 1967, at the University of Pennsylvania, dogs that had no way to stop shocks later lay down in a box they could have escaped with one jump. In 2016, Steven Maier and Seligman turned the theory around: by default the brain assumes it has no control, and it is control that is learned.
textes.Le record est détenu par Randy Gardner,: The record belongs to Randy Gardner, who stayed awake 264 hours, 11 days, without stimulants. The US National Sleep Foundation recommends that adults aim for 7 hours a night.
textes.Jon Kabat-Zinn crée son programme de réd: Jon Kabat-Zinn created his stress reduction programme in 1979 at the University of Massachusetts Medical School. It lasts eight weeks; its roots are in Zen Buddhism, but the programme is secular.
textes.Le psychologue Herbert Freudenberger s'o: Psychologist Herbert Freudenberger observed himself and his fellow volunteers at a free clinic for drug addicts, in "Staff Burn-Out" in 1974. Christina Maslach published her inventory in 1981, and the WHO recognised it in 2019 as an occupational phenomenon, not a medical condition.
textes.En 1986, James Pennebaker et Sandra Beal: In 1986, James Pennebaker and Sandra Beall had students write 15 minutes a day, 4 days in a row, about their deepest thoughts on a trauma. Over the following months, they visited the doctor significantly less than those who wrote about neutral topics.
textes.Selon Aristote, d'où naît la colère ?: According to Aristotle, where does anger come from?
textes.Du sentiment d'avoir été rabaissé: From the feeling of having been belittled
textes.D'un excès de bile jaune: From an excess of yellow bile
textes.De la volonté des dieux: From the will of the gods
textes.On s'irrite contre qui nous insulte, ou: We are angered by whoever insults us, or insults what we value. Aristotle analysed it in the Rhetoric, so that the speaker could arouse or calm it.
textes.Dans le livre II de la Rhétorique, Arist: In book II of the Rhetoric, Aristotle arranged emotions in opposing pairs; anger arises from the feeling of having been belittled.
textes.Avec quelle émotion Aristote met-il la c: With which emotion does Aristotle pair anger, in the Rhetoric?
textes.Il range les émotions par paires opposée: He arranged emotions in opposing pairs: anger and calmness, friendliness and enmity. They serve pathos, one of the three means of persuasion along with ethos and logos.
textes.Pour Sénèque, il suffit de modérer la co: For Seneca, it is enough to moderate anger: in the right dose, it is useful.
textes.Faux. « Il ne faut pas contrôler la colè: False. "We shouldn't control anger, but destroy it entirely," he wrote in book III. For the Stoic, it is a false belief about the value of things.
textes.Sénèque, De la colère (vers 45), dédié à: Seneca, On Anger (around 45), dedicated to his brother Novatus: "We shouldn't control anger, but destroy it entirely."
textes.Combien d'agrégats (skandhas) composent: How many aggregates (skandhas) make up a person, according to the Buddha?
textes.Forme, sensation, perception, formations: Form, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness. None is a "self": this is the doctrine of non-self.
textes.Les cinq agrégats : forme, sensation, pe: The five aggregates: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness; none is a self.
textes.Quel animal représente la haine au centr: Which animal stands for hatred at the centre of the wheel of life?
textes.Le coq figure l'avidité, le serpent la h: The rooster stands for greed, the snake for hatred, the pig for ignorance: the three poisons that turn the wheel.
textes.Les trois poisons, désir, haine et ignor: The three poisons, desire, hatred and ignorance, are painted at the centre of the wheel of life as a rooster, a snake and a pig.
textes.Quels sont les trois « feux » que l'ense: Which three "fires" does the Buddha's teaching seek to put out?
textes.Leur extinction est la délivrance. Les t: Their extinction is liberation. The texts also call them the three poisons.
textes.Selon le Bouddha, la conscience est le v: According to the Buddha, consciousness is the true "self" hidden behind the other four aggregates.
textes.Faux. La conscience est un agrégat comme: False. Consciousness is an aggregate like the others, and none is a self: "this is not my self".
textes.À quoi un vieux texte bouddhique compare: What does an old Buddhist text compare form and feelings to?
textes.À une montagne et à un fleuve: To a mountain and a river
textes.À un roi et à ses ministres: To a king and his ministers
textes.À une graine et à un arbre: To a seed and a tree
textes.Toute forme est comparable à l'écume, to: All form is comparable to foam, all feelings to bubbles; then come the mirage, the plantain trunk and the illusion.
textes.Quels sont les quatre fondements de l'at: What are the four foundations of mindfulness in the Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta?
textes.Ce discours, le dixième du Majjhima Nikā: This discourse, the tenth of the Majjhima Nikāya, is the foundation of modern vipassana meditation.
textes.Le Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta enseigne quatre fo: The Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta teaches four foundations of mindfulness: body, feelings, mind, phenomena.
textes.Dans le discours de la flèche, qu'est-ce: In the discourse on the arrow, what is the "second arrow"?
textes.La douleur de l'esprit ajoutée à celle d: The pain of the mind added to that of the body
textes.Le disciple instruit sent la douleur du: The instructed disciple feels the pain of the body but does not add a second one: he receives only one arrow.
textes.Dans le discours de la flèche, l'homme n: In the discourse on the arrow, the untaught man receives a second arrow, the pain of the mind.
textes.Combien de semaines dure le cours de réd: How many weeks does the stress reduction course founded by Jon Kabat-Zinn last?
textes.Huit semaines de méditation, d'attention: Eight weeks of meditation, body awareness and yoga, plus a day-long retreat. The programme was born in 1979 at the University of Massachusetts.
textes.En 1979, Jon Kabat-Zinn fonde la cliniqu: In 1979, Jon Kabat-Zinn founded the University of Massachusetts stress reduction clinic: a secular eight-week course.
textes.Combien de versets compte le Dhammapada: How many verses does the Pali Dhammapada have?
textes.423 versets en 26 chapitres. Le premier: 423 verses in 26 chapters. The first says: "Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief."
textes.Le Dhammapada compte 423 versets en 26 c: The Dhammapada has 423 verses in 26 chapters and opens with "Mind precedes thoughts".
textes.Le programme de pleine conscience de Kab: Kabat-Zinn's mindfulness programme is secular, even though it draws on Buddhist meditations.
textes.Vrai. Il emprunte au zen, au yoga et à l: True. It borrows from Zen, yoga and vipassana, but requires no belief. Studies find it has a moderate effect on anxiety and pain.
textes.Combien de types humains Théophraste déc: How many human types does Theophrastus describe in his Characters?
textes.Trente portraits brefs : le flatteur, le: Thirty brief sketches: the flatterer, the chatterbox, the coward, the superstitious man, the miser… La Bruyère would translate them in 1688.
textes.Les Caractères de Théophraste décrivent: Theophrastus's Characters describe thirty moral types; it is the first known attempt at systematic character writing.
textes.De qui Théophraste a-t-il été l'élève, p: Whose pupil, then successor at the head of the Lyceum, was Theophrastus?
textes.C'est Aristote qui l'aurait surnommé Thé: It was Aristotle who supposedly nicknamed him Theophrastus; his name was Tyrtamus. Aristotle left him his library.
textes.Théophraste, successeur d'Aristote au Ly: Theophrastus, Aristotle's successor at the Lyceum, reportedly had more than 2,000 students; Diogenes Laërtius credits him with 227 titles.
textes.« Théophraste » serait un surnom donné p: "Theophrastus" was reportedly a nickname given by Aristotle, for the grace of his conversation.
textes.Une peur rampante des puissances invisib: A crouching fear of unseen powers
textes.Un excès de piété envers les dieux: An excess of piety towards the gods
textes.Son superstitieux s'asperge d'eau avant: His superstitious man sprinkles himself with water before starting his day and stops if a weasel crosses his path.
textes.Dans la traduction de Bennett et Hammond: In Bennett and Hammond's translation, superstition is "a crouching fear of unseen powers"; the flatterer says "Behold! how the people gaze at you!".
textes.Que glisse le flatteur de Théophraste à: What does Theophrastus's flatterer whisper to the man he walks with?
textes.« Regarde comme les gens te dévisagent !: "Behold! how the people gaze at you!"
textes.Pour Théophraste, la flatterie est une c: For Theophrastus, flattery is a cringing sort of conduct that serves the flatterer's interest.
textes.Chaque caractère de Théophraste s'ouvre: Each of Theophrastus's characters opens with a short definition, followed by concrete gestures.
textes.Vrai. « La loquacité est un bavardage in: True. "Garrulity is incessant heedless talk", then come the scenes where the chatterbox strikes.
textes.Quel écrivain français traduit Théophras: Which French writer translated Theophrastus in 1688 and published his own Characters after them?
textes.Ses Caractères sont surtout des satires: His Characters are mostly satires of thinly disguised contemporaries.
textes.En 1688, La Bruyère traduit les Caractèr: In 1688, La Bruyère translated Theophrastus's Characters and published his own after them.
textes.Combien de titres Diogène Laërce attribu: How many titles does Diogenes Laërtius attribute to Theophrastus?
textes.227 titres, presque tous perdus. Il en r: 227 titles, almost all lost. What remains includes his books on plants, which make him the "father of botany", and the Characters.
textes.La préface des Caractères, où Théophrast: The preface of the Characters, in which Theophrastus says he is 99, is probably authentic.
textes.Faux. Elle passe pour un faux. Les sourc: False. It is regarded as a forgery. Ancient sources disagree on his age: 85 according to Diogenes Laërtius, 107 according to Jerome's Chronicle.
textes.La préface des Caractères, où Théophrast: The preface of the Characters, where Theophrastus writes in his 99th year, is probably spurious; Jerome has him live to 107.
textes.Quelle romancière anglaise publie en 187: Which English novelist published Impressions inspired by Theophrastus in 1879?
textes.Impressions of Theophrastus Such, en 187: Impressions of Theophrastus Such, in 1879. Before her, Joseph Hall in 1608 and Thomas Overbury had imitated the genre.
textes.George Eliot s'inspire des Caractères po: George Eliot drew on the Characters for Impressions of Theophrastus Such (1879).
textes.Selon le chapitre 5 du Manuel, qu'est-ce: According to chapter 5 of the Handbook, what upsets people?
textes.C'est la phrase la plus citée d'Épictète: It is Epictetus's most quoted sentence: to change one's judgement is to change one's emotion. Albert Ellis would take it up in the 20th century.
textes.Manuel, chapitre 5 : ce qui trouble les: Handbook, chapter 5: what upsets people is not things themselves but their judgements about things.
textes.Que fut Épictète avant d'être philosophe: What was Epictetus before he was a philosopher?
textes.L'esclave d'un secrétaire de Néron: The slave of a secretary of Nero
textes.Son maître, Épaphrodite, était un riche: His master, Epaphroditus, was a wealthy freedman in Nero's service. Epictetus was freed after the emperor's death in 68.
textes.À Rome, Épictète est l'esclave d'Épaphro: In Rome, Epictetus was the slave of Epaphroditus, a wealthy freedman and Nero's secretary.
textes.Épictète n'a rien écrit. Arrien, vers 10: Epictetus wrote nothing. Arrian, around 108, noted his lessons almost word for word: these are the Discourses, from which he drew the Handbook.
textes.Épictète naît esclave vers 50 à Hiérapol: Epictetus was born a slave around 50 at Hierapolis; around 93, Domitian banished philosophers, and he taught at Nicopolis.
textes.Pour Épictète, notre réputation fait par: For Epictetus, our reputation is among the things that depend on us.
textes.Faux. Nos jugements, nos désirs et nos c: False. Our judgements, desires and choices depend on us; the body, reputation and events do not.
textes.Le Manuel d'Épictète, compilé par Arrien: Epictetus's Handbook, compiled by Arrian, has 53 chapters; it opens with what depends on us and what does not.
textes.Combien de chapitres compte le Manuel d': How many chapters does Epictetus's Handbook have?
textes.53 courts chapitres, d'un paragraphe ou: 53 short chapters, of a paragraph or two each. This division dates from Johann Schweighäuser's edition, in 1798.
textes.Le Manuel compte 53 courts chapitres, se: The Handbook has 53 short chapters, following Schweighäuser's division (1798).
textes.Où Épictète fonde-t-il son école après l: Where did Epictetus found his school after philosophers were expelled from Rome?
textes.Vers 93, Domitien chasse tous les philos: Around 93, Domitian drove all philosophers out of Rome. It was at Nicopolis that Arrian came to hear him.
textes.Comment Épictète appelle-t-il la faculté: What does Epictetus call the faculty of choice, the only thing entirely ours?
textes.La prohairesis, notre volonté ou notre c: Prohairesis, our will or choice. Making good use of our impressions is what makes happiness.
textes.Dans les Entretiens, la prohairesis, vol: In the Discourses, prohairesis, will or choice, is the only thing fully within our control.
textes.Dans le schéma d'Albert Ellis, que désig: In Albert Ellis's scheme, what does the letter B stand for?
textes.A, l'événement ; B, la croyance ; C, la: A, the event; B, the belief; C, the emotional consequence. Ellis said this principle had been discovered by the Stoics.
textes.Albert Ellis fonde au milieu des années: Albert Ellis founded in the mid-1950s a therapy that quotes Epictetus; scheme A (event), B (belief), C (emotional consequence).
textes.Des moines grecs du Moyen Âge ont adapté: Greek monks in the Middle Ages adapted Epictetus's Handbook into a rule of monastic life.
textes.Vrai. Trois adaptations chrétiennes exis: True. Three Christian adaptations exist, from the 10th to the 14th century; Socrates sometimes becomes Saint Paul in them.
textes.Trois adaptations chrétiennes grecques d: Three Greek Christian adaptations of the Handbook (10th, 11th, 14th centuries) served as a monastic rule; Socrates is sometimes replaced by Paul.
textes.Quel empereur romain cite les Entretiens: Which Roman emperor quotes Epictetus's Discourses in his Meditations?
textes.L'empereur stoïcien lit l'ancien esclave: The Stoic emperor read the former slave. Irony: it was another emperor, Domitian, who had driven Epictetus out of Rome.
textes.Marc Aurèle, influencé par Épictète, le: Marcus Aurelius, influenced by Epictetus, quotes him in his Meditations.
textes.Quel philosophe al-Balkhi a-t-il suivi l: Which philosopher did al-Balkhi follow during his stay in Iraq?
textes.Il passe environ huit ans en Irak, vers: He spent about eight years in Iraq, around the time of al-Kindi's death, before settling for good in Balkh.
textes.Al-Balkhi (850-934) range les troubles é: Al-Balkhi (850-934) sorted emotional disorders into four families: fear and anxiety, anger, sadness and depression, obsession.
textes.En combien de familles al-Balkhi range-t: Into how many families did al-Balkhi sort emotional disorders?
textes.Quatre : la peur et l'angoisse, la colèr: Four: fear and anxiety, anger and aggression, sadness and depression, obsession.
textes.Que conseille al-Balkhi contre la phobie: What did al-Balkhi advise against phobia?
textes.S'exposer peu à peu à ce qui fait peur: Exposing oneself gradually to what is feared
textes.Exposé de façon répétée, on s'habitue et: Exposed repeatedly, one grows used to it and the fear fades. Modern exposure therapies rest on the same idea.
textes.Contre la phobie (fazaa'), al-Balkhi con: Against phobia (fazaa'), al-Balkhi advised gradual, repeated exposure to what is feared.
textes.D'où vient « l'essentiel de la terreur »: Where does "most of the terror" come from, according to a saying al-Balkhi quoted?
textes.D'où son conseil : s'informer, et voir d: Hence his advice: to get informed, and see realistically what the object of worry really is.
textes.Pour al-Balkhi, une âme malade peut rend: For al-Balkhi, a sick soul can make the body ill, and a sick body weakens the soul.
textes.Vrai. Il reproche aux médecins de soigne: True. He reproached physicians for treating the body while forgetting the mind. Health depends on the balance between the two.
textes.Pour al-Balkhi, la santé dépend de l'âme: For al-Balkhi, health depends on soul and body intertwined: if one falls ill, the other suffers.
textes.Combien de sortes de dépression al-Balkh: How many kinds of depression did al-Balkhi distinguish by origin: ordinary, from the body, or in reaction to an event?
textes.Trois : la tristesse ordinaire, la dépre: Three: ordinary sadness, depression from within the body, and reactive depression, from outside.
textes.Al-Balkhi distingue une tristesse normal: Al-Balkhi distinguished normal sadness, endogenous depression and reactive depression.
textes.À quoi al-Balkhi compare-t-il les pensée: What did al-Balkhi compare the positive thoughts one should keep in reserve to?
textes.On garde de quoi soigner une blessure av: One keeps what is needed to treat a wound before the accident; likewise, thoughts ready before the crisis.
textes.Al-Balkhi recommande de garder pensées e: Al-Balkhi recommended keeping positive thoughts and feelings ready for crises, like first-aid supplies.
textes.Qu'introduit l'hôpital al-Mansuri du Cai: What did the al-Mansuri hospital in Cairo, completed in 1284, introduce to treat mental patients?
textes.Dans les bimaristans, nul ne devait être: In the bimaristans, no one was to be turned away, not even the mentally ill; in Aleppo, the Arghun hospital relied on light, air, running water and music.
textes.À l'hôpital al-Mansuri du Caire, achevé: At the al-Mansuri hospital in Cairo, completed in 1284, mental patients were also treated and music was introduced as therapy.
textes.Le mot bimaristan vient du persan et sig: The word bimaristan comes from Persian and means roughly "place of the sick".
textes.Vrai. Il vient du moyen-persan wēmārestā: True. It comes from the Middle Persian wēmārestān: wēmār, the sick person, and -stān, the place.
textes.Bimarestan vient du moyen-persan wēmāres: Bimarestan comes from the Middle Persian wēmārestān: wēmār, sick person, and -stan, place.
textes.Quel psychiatre a réintroduit en 1969 la: Which psychiatrist reintroduced in 1969 al-Balkhi's technique of treating an ill by its opposite?
textes.Al-Balkhi l'appelait al-ilaj bi al-did ;: Al-Balkhi called it al-ilaj bi al-did; Wolpe spoke of reciprocal inhibition.
textes.Al-Balkhi introduit l'inhibition récipro: Al-Balkhi introduced reciprocal inhibition (al-ilaj bi al-did), reintroduced by Joseph Wolpe in 1969.
textes.À quel âge Montaigne se retire-t-il dans: At what age did Montaigne withdraw to the tower of his château, in 1571?
textes.Né en 1533, il a 38 ans en 1571. Il s'in: Born in 1533, he was 38 in 1571. He settled in his library of about 1,500 books and began the Essays.
textes.En 1571, à 38 ans, Montaigne se retire d: In 1571, at 38, Montaigne withdrew to the tower of his château, with about 1,500 volumes.
textes.Quelle langue le père de Montaigne lui f: Which language did Montaigne's father have him speak as his first language?
textes.Et pour lui épargner un réveil brutal, u: And to spare him a harsh awakening, a musician woke him every morning.
textes.Le père de Montaigne lui fait parler lat: Montaigne's father had him speak Latin as his first language, and had him woken by a musician.
textes.Combien de chapitres comptent les Essais: How many chapters do Montaigne's Essays have?
textes.107 chapitres de longueur très inégale,: 107 chapters of very unequal length, in three books: two in 1580, the third in 1588.
textes.Les Essais ont trois livres et 107 chapi: The Essays have three books and 107 chapters; first edition in 1580, book III in 1588.
textes.Montaigne prévient son lecteur qu'il est: Montaigne warns his reader that he himself is the matter of his book.
textes.Vrai. Ses contemporains jugent cela comp: True. His contemporaries found it self-indulgent; yet it is one of the first great self-observations.
textes.« Je suis moi-même la matière de mon liv: "I am myself the matter of my book": Montaigne takes himself as his subject.
textes.Lequel de ces titres n'est pas un chapit: Which of these titles is not a chapter of the Essays?
textes.L'inconscient attendra Freud. Montaigne: The unconscious would wait for Freud. Montaigne wrote Of Sadness, Of Fear, Of Idleness, Of Imagination, Of Friendship.
textes.Les Essais comptent trois livres et 107: The Essays have three books and 107 chapters; among the titles, Of Sadness, Of Fear, Of Idleness, Of Imagination.
textes.Que se passe-t-il pour Montaigne vers 15: What happened to Montaigne around 1570 that inspired an observation of the approach of death?
textes.Il est renversé de cheval et perd connai: He was knocked off his horse and lost consciousness
textes.Il est blessé en duel: He was wounded in a duel
A companion at full gallop crashed into him. He was "for more than two full hours taken for dead".
textes.Vers 1570, un compagnon au galop renvers: Around 1570, a galloping companion knocked Montaigne off his horse; he lost consciousness and thought himself dead.
textes.Selon Juan Huarte (1575), que faut-il fa: According to Juan Huarte (1575), what should be done to guide each person well?
textes.Repérer tôt le talent propre de chaque e: Spot each child's own talent early
textes.Chaque personne a un talent unique, lié: Each person has a single talent, tied to his temperament; he should choose the trade that suits it. He has been made an ancestor of vocational guidance.
textes.En 1575, Juan Huarte publie l'Examen des: In 1575, Juan Huarte published the Examination of Men's Wits: one talent per person, tied to temperament, and a trade to suit it.
textes.Combien d'éditions l'Examen des esprits: How many editions did Huarte's Examination of Men's Wits go through between 1575 and 1800?
textes.Soixante éditions, en six langues europé: Sixty editions, in six European languages, despite a ban by the Inquisition. In 1983, Spain made him the patron of its psychology.
textes.L'Examen de ingenios connaît soixante éd: The Examen de ingenios went through sixty editions from 1575 to 1800; in 1983, Huarte became patron of Spanish psychology.
textes.Quel philosophe allemand a écrit qu'un t: Which German philosopher wrote that such a man, by writing, had increased the joy of living on Earth?
textes.Nietzsche admirait Montaigne. Pascal, lu: Nietzsche admired Montaigne. Pascal, for his part, owed him much of his scepticism.
textes.Nietzsche : « qu'un tel homme ait écrit: Nietzsche: "That such a man wrote has truly augmented the joy of living on this Earth."
textes.Montaigne se présente comme un philosoph: Montaigne presents himself as a philosopher building a complete system.
textes.Faux. « Je ne suis pas philosophe », écr: False. "I am not a philosopher," he wrote. He tried, doubted and corrected himself: more than three thousand corrections after 1588.
textes.Montaigne refuse le titre de philosophe: Montaigne refused the title of philosopher; after 1588, he made more than three thousand corrections of detail.
textes.Combien de passions primitives Descartes: How many primitive passions does Descartes count?
textes.Six : l'admiration, l'amour, la haine, l: Six: wonder, love, hatred, desire, joy and sadness. All the others are composed of them.
textes.Les Passions de l'âme (1649) comptent tr: The Passions of the Soul (1649) have three parts and 212 articles; six primitive passions: wonder, love, hatred, desire, joy, sadness.
textes.Laquelle de ces passions ne figure pas p: Which of these passions is not among Descartes's six primitive passions?
textes.La peur n'est pas primitive pour Descart: Fear is not primitive for Descartes: it is composed of the first six. Ekman, three centuries later, would put it among his basic emotions.
textes.Qui pose à Descartes, en 1643, la questi: Who asked Descartes in 1643 how the soul can move the body?
textes.Le philosophe Jaegwon Kim y voit le prem: The philosopher Jaegwon Kim sees in it the first causal argument for physicalism. Descartes would dedicate the Passions of the Soul to her.
textes.En 1643, Élisabeth de Bohême demande à D: In 1643, Elisabeth of Bohemia asked Descartes how an immaterial soul can move the body.
textes.Combien d'articles comptent Les Passions: How many articles do The Passions of the Soul have?
textes.212 courts articles, en trois parties, a: 212 short articles, in three parts, completed in 1649 and dedicated to Elisabeth.
textes.Pour Descartes, les passions sont mauvai: For Descartes, the passions are bad by nature and must be suppressed.
textes.Faux. À l'article 211, il les déclare bo: False. In article 211, he declares them good by nature: one avoids only their misuse or excess.
textes.Article 211 : les passions sont intrinsè: Article 211: the passions are intrinsically good; only their misuse or excess is to be avoided.
textes.Selon Descartes, où sont produits les «: According to Descartes, where are the "animal spirits" that move the body produced?
textes.Produits dans le sang, ils circulent dan: Produced in the blood, they flow through the nerves and move the body in all the ways it is capable of (article 10).
textes.Article 10 : les esprits animaux, produi: Article 10: the animal spirits, produced in the blood, move the body in all the ways it is capable of.
textes.Quelle est la taille de la glande pinéal: What is the size of the pineal gland, where Descartes placed the principal seat of the soul?
textes.Celle d'un grain de riz: That of a grain of rice
textes.De 5 à 8 mm. Elle produit la mélatonine,: 5 to 8 mm. It produces melatonin, which regulates sleep. Galen took it for a mere support for the tissues.
textes.La glande pinéale, grosse comme un grain: The pineal gland, the size of a grain of rice, produces melatonin; Descartes made it the principal seat of the soul.
textes.Quelle hormone produit la glande pinéale: Which hormone does the pineal gland produce?
textes.Elle règle les cycles du sommeil, au ryt: It regulates sleep cycles, following day and night. Nothing to do with the soul, then.
textes.Descartes pensait que même les âmes les: Descartes thought that even the weakest souls could learn to master their passions.
textes.Vrai. Article 50 : avec assez d'industri: True. Article 50: with enough effort to train and guide them, they would acquire absolute mastery over their passions.
textes.Article 50 : même les âmes les plus faib: Article 50: even the weakest souls could acquire absolute mastery over their passions.
textes.Quel ouvrage Descartes dédie-t-il à Élis: Which work did Descartes dedicate to Elisabeth in 1644, before The Passions of the Soul?
textes.Élisabeth deviendra plus tard abbesse de: Elisabeth later became abbess of Herford, in 1667, and governed a community of about 7,000 people.
textes.Descartes dédie à Élisabeth ses Principe: Descartes dedicated his Principles of Philosophy (1644) to Elisabeth; she became abbess of Herford in 1667.
textes.Qui a retiré les fers des malades de Bic: Who removed the irons from the Bicêtre patients in 1797?
textes.Pinel était déjà parti à la Salpêtrière,: Pinel had already left for the Salpêtrière, where he would remove the chains three years later. The legend kept his name.
textes.En 1797, à Bicêtre, Pussin retire les fe: In 1797, at Bicêtre, Pussin removed the patients' irons after Pinel had left; Pinel removed the chains at the Salpêtrière three years later.
textes.En combien de types Pinel range-t-il les: Into how many types did Pinel sort mental disorders?
Melancholia, mania, dementia and idiotism. He thus simplified William Cullen's "neuroses".
textes.Pinel ramène les névroses de Cullen à qu: Pinel reduced Cullen's neuroses to four types: melancholia, mania, dementia and idiotism.
textes.On soigne par la parole, l'observation e: Treatment came through words, observation and a humane setting, rather than bloodletting and purges.
textes.Pour Pinel, « moral » signifie émotionne: For Pinel, "moral" meant emotional or psychological, not ethical.
textes.Qui fonde le Retreat d'York en 1796 ?: Who founded the York Retreat in 1796?
textes.Une trentaine de patients, du repos, de: About thirty patients, rest, conversation and manual work. He was responding to the death of a Quaker woman in an asylum in 1790.
textes.Le traitement moral : une approche humai: Moral treatment: a humane, psychological approach; Tuke founded the York Retreat in 1796, Chiarugi banned chains in Florence in 1785-1788.
textes.La scène de Pinel libérant seul les fous: The scene of Pinel alone freeing the insane from their chains is partly a legend.
textes.Vrai. C'est Pussin qui ôte les fers de B: True. It was Pussin who removed the irons at Bicêtre in 1797, after Pinel had left.
textes.Quel drame personnel a tourné Pinel vers: What personal tragedy turned Pinel towards the study of madness?
textes.Le suicide d'un ami devenu maniaque: The suicide of a friend who had become manic
textes.Cet ami souffrait de « mélancolie nerveu: This friend suffered from "nervous melancholy", which degenerated into mania.
textes.Un ami de Pinel, atteint de mélancolie n: A friend of Pinel's, suffering from nervous melancholy, sank into mania and killed himself: this tragedy motivated Pinel.
textes.Où Pinel est-il médecin-chef à partir de: Where was Pinel chief physician from 1795 until his death?
textes.Il y fait venir Pussin en 1802, et y ôte: He had Pussin transferred there in 1802, and removed the patients' chains there, three years after Bicêtre.
textes.En Grande-Bretagne, la population moyenn: In Britain, the average asylum population rose from 166 patients in 1827 to 1,221 in 1930. By roughly what factor did it multiply? (one decimal)
textes.Facteur = population d'arrivée ÷ populat: Factor = final population ÷ initial population = 1,221 ÷ 166 ≈ 7.4. This is the definition of a ratio, with no discoverer. In asylums seven times bigger, moral treatment turned into routine.
textes.La population moyenne des asiles britann: The average British asylum population rose from 166 in 1827 to 1,221 in 1930; moral treatment turned into routine.
textes.Quel médecin bannit les chaînes à l'hôpi: Which physician banned chains at the Santa Dorotea hospital in Florence between 1785 and 1788?
textes.Sous le grand-duc Pierre-Léopold, avant: Under Grand Duke Pietro Leopoldo, even before Pussin and Pinel. He extended the rule to St Boniface hospital from 1788.
textes.Après Pinel, les asiles du XIXe siècle r: After Pinel, 19th-century asylums stayed small and moral treatment spread there without difficulty.
textes.Faux. Les asiles deviennent immenses et: False. Asylums became huge and overcrowded; moral treatment turned into routine there. In America, Dorothea Dix had 32 state hospitals opened.
textes.À la fin du XIXe siècle, les asiles sont: By the late 19th century, asylums were overcrowded and moral treatment had become routine; Dorothea Dix helped establish 32 state hospitals.
textes.Dans quel livre de Darwin L'Expression d: In which Darwin book was The Expression of the Emotions first meant to be just a chapter?
textes.Darwin finit La Filiation le 15 janvier: Darwin finished The Descent on 15 January 1871 and began The Expression two days later.
textes.L'Expression des émotions paraît chez Jo: The Expression of the Emotions was published by John Murray on 26 November 1872 and quickly sold almost 7,000 copies.
textes.Selon Darwin, quelle est « la plus singu: According to Darwin, what is "the most peculiar and the most human of all expressions"?
It is the subject of his chapter 13.
textes.Au chapitre 13, Darwin appelle le rougis: In chapter 13, Darwin called blushing "the most peculiar and the most human of all expressions".
textes.Comment Duchenne de Boulogne provoquait-: How did Duchenne de Boulogne provoke expressions on his models' faces?
textes.Il appliquait un courant par des pointes: He applied a current through metal probes and photographed the result. His main model: an old toothless man.
textes.Duchenne de Boulogne provoque des expres: Duchenne de Boulogne provoked expressions with electricity and showed that the true smile also works the eye muscles.
textes.Le « sourire de Duchenne », celui de la: The "Duchenne smile", that of real joy, works the eye muscles as well as those of the mouth.
textes.Vrai. Un sourire de politesse ne bouge q: True. A polite smile moves only the mouth; sincere joy also creases the eyes.
textes.En quelle année Darwin publie-t-il L'Exp: In what year did Darwin publish The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals?
textes.Le 26 novembre 1872, chez John Murray. L: On 26 November 1872, by John Murray. The book has never been out of print since.
textes.Comment Darwin recueille-t-il des observ: How did Darwin gather observations about the expressions of distant peoples?
textes.Par un questionnaire envoyé à des corres: Through a questionnaire sent to correspondents
textes.En voyageant lui-même sur cinq continent: By travelling himself across five continents
textes.Il le fait circuler dès 1867, d'abord à: He circulated it from 1867, first by hand, then printed.
textes.Darwin fait circuler en 1867 un question: Darwin circulated a handwritten questionnaire in 1867, then a printed version in late 1867 or early 1868.
textes.Lequel de ces principes n'est pas l'un d: Which of these is not one of Darwin's three principles of expression?
textes.L'action directe du système nerveux: Direct action of the nervous system
textes.Pour Darwin, l'essentiel des expressions: For Darwin, most expressions are inherited, not learned from parents: hence their similarity from one people to another.
textes.Les chapitres 1 à 3 posent trois princip: Chapters 1 to 3 set out three principles: serviceable associated habits, antithesis, action of the nervous system.
textes.Qui Darwin observe-t-il de près pour étu: Whom did Darwin watch closely to study a baby's expressions?
textes.Un bébé orang-outan du zoo: A baby orangutan at the zoo
textes.Ses notes sur William paraîtront en 1877: His notes on William appeared in 1877 in the journal Mind, as "A Biographical Sketch of an Infant".
textes.Darwin observe son fils William Erasmus: Darwin observed his son William Erasmus; "A Biographical Sketch of an Infant" appeared in Mind in 1877.
textes.Qu'achèvent Paul Ekman et Wallace Friese: What did Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen complete in 1978?
textes.Un système de codage des mouvements du v: A coding system for facial movements
textes.Chaque mouvement observable du visage y: Each observable movement of the face is an "action unit". Ekman later advised the series Lie to Me.
textes.Ekman et Friesen achèvent en 1978 le sys: Ekman and Friesen completed the Facial Action Coding System (FACS) in 1978.
textes.L'éditeur de Darwin trouvait que les pho: Darwin's publisher thought the book's photographs would be costly.
textes.Vrai. Il prévint qu'elles feraient « un: True. He warned they would "make a hole in the profits". The book nevertheless sold almost 7,000 copies.
textes.L'éditeur de Darwin avertit que les phot: Darwin's publisher warned that the photographs would "make a hole in the profits".
textes.En quelle année Wundt ouvre-t-il à Leipz: In what year did Wundt open the first psychology laboratory in Leipzig?
textes.En 1879. Wundt y dirigera 185 thèses. Il: In 1879. Wundt would supervise 185 theses there. Yet he called Ernst Weber, rather than himself, the father of experimental psychology.
textes.Wundt ouvre en 1879 à Leipzig le premier: Wundt opened in 1879 in Leipzig the first laboratory devoted entirely to psychology; he supervised 185 theses there, 70 by foreigners.
textes.De quel grand physicien Wundt fut-il l'a: Which great physicist was Wundt assistant to at Heidelberg, from 1858?
textes.Il y était chargé des travaux pratiques: He was in charge of the physiology laboratory course. Helmholtz too was interested in reaction times.
textes.En 1858, Wundt devient l'assistant de He: In 1858, Wundt became Helmholtz's assistant, in charge of the physiology laboratory course at Heidelberg.
textes.Selon Weber, on distingue un poids de 10: According to Weber, a 100 g weight can be told from another if it differs by about 8%. What minimal difference is needed for a 500 g weight?
textes.Loi de Weber : ΔI = k × I, où ΔI est la: Weber's law: ΔI = k × I, where ΔI is the smallest perceived difference, I the reference weight and k the Weber fraction. Here k = 8 ÷ 100 = 0.08 and ΔI = 0.08 × 500 = 40 g. Ernst Weber established it in 1834; Gustav Fechner gave it its name.
textes.Weber : on distingue au mieux deux poids: Weber: one best distinguishes two weights that differ by 8 to 10%; for 100 g, one needs at least 108 g.
textes.Chez Donders, discriminer prend 0,047 s: In Donders's work, discriminating takes 0.047 s and choosing 0.036 s more. How many milliseconds longer does method b (discriminating then choosing) take than the simple method a?
textes.Méthode de soustraction : (b − a) = (c −: Subtraction method: (b − a) = (c − a) + (b − c), where each difference measures one step. Here 0.047 + 0.036 = 0.083 s, i.e. 83 ms. Franciscus Donders published these measurements in 1868.
textes.Donders (1868) : la méthode c prend 0,04: Donders (1868): method c takes 0.047 s longer than a (discriminating), method b 0.036 s longer than c (choosing).
textes.Comment Gustav Fechner s'est-il abîmé le: How did Gustav Fechner damage his eyes, in 1839?
textes.En regardant le Soleil à travers des ver: By looking at the Sun through coloured glasses
textes.En observant une éclipse au télescope: By watching an eclipse through a telescope
textes.Il étudiait les images rémanentes. Il du: He was studying afterimages. He had to resign his chair, and turned to the relation between mind and body.
textes.En 1839, Fechner s'abîme les yeux en étu: In 1839, Fechner damaged his eyes studying afterimages, looking at the Sun through coloured glasses.
textes.Selon la loi de Fechner, comment la sens: According to Fechner's law, how does sensation vary with stimulus intensity?
textes.Pour que la sensation monte d'un cran à: For sensation to rise by one step each time, the stimulus must be multiplied, not increased by the same amount.
textes.Fechner publie en 1860 les Éléments de p: Fechner published the Elements of Psychophysics in 1860; sensation grows as the logarithm of the stimulus.
textes.Combien de thèses Wundt a-t-il dirigées: How many doctoral theses did Wundt supervise between 1875 and 1919?
textes.185, dont 70 d'étudiants étrangers, comm: 185, 70 of them by foreign students, such as Cattell, Hall or Titchener.
textes.Wundt faisait confiance à l'introspectio: Wundt trusted the spontaneous introspection of any volunteer.
textes.Faux. Il rejetait l'introspection naïve: False. He rejected naive introspection: self-observation had to be learned and carried out under strict experimental control.
textes.Wundt rejette l'introspection naïve : l': Wundt rejected naive introspection: self-observation must be trained and kept under strict experimental control.
textes.Chez de jeunes adultes, à quoi réagit-on: In young adults, what does one react to fastest, on average?
textes.Environ 160 ms pour un son, 190 ms pour: About 160 ms for a sound, 190 ms for a light. A response faster than 100 ms is often an anticipation.
textes.Chez les étudiants, le temps de réaction: In college-age individuals, mean simple reaction time is about 160 ms for a sound and 190 ms for a light.
textes.Selon quelles dimensions Wundt décrit-il: Along which dimensions did Wundt describe feelings?
textes.Trois dimensions : c'est sa théorie trid: Three dimensions: his tridimensional theory of feeling.
textes.Wundt décrit l'émotion en trois dimensio: Wundt described emotion in three dimensions: pleasant-unpleasant, tense-relaxed, excited-depressed.
textes.Pour quels travaux Pavlov reçoit-il le p: For what work did Pavlov receive the Nobel Prize in 1904?
textes.Le Nobel salue la digestion, pas le réfl: The Nobel honoured digestion, not the conditioned reflex. Pavlov was the first Russian to receive a Nobel Prize.
textes.Pavlov reçoit le Nobel 1904 pour ses tra: Pavlov received the 1904 Nobel for his work on digestion, the first Russian laureate; his writings cite metronomes, whistles, tuning forks, shocks; the bell is disputed.
textes.Il est certain que Pavlov utilisait une: It is certain that Pavlov used a bell to condition his dogs.
textes.Faux. Ses écrits parlent de métronomes,: False. His writings mention metronomes, whistles, tuning forks and electric shocks; the bell remains disputed.
textes.Comment Pavlov appelait-il la salivation: What did Pavlov call his dogs' salivation before food arrived?
textes.C'est ce phénomène gênant pour ses mesur: It was this phenomenon, a nuisance for his digestion measurements, that he decided to study for its own sake. He published in 1897.
textes.Conditionnement classique : un stimulus: Classical conditioning: a neutral stimulus paired with food triggers salivation on its own; extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalisation.
textes.Dans l'expérience de Pavlov, qu'est-ce q: In Pavlov's experiment, what is the food?
textes.Elle fait saliver sans apprentissage. Le: It causes salivation without learning. The metronome becomes a conditioned stimulus by repeatedly announcing the meal.
textes.Qu'arrive-t-il quand le stimulus conditi: What happens when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented without food?
textes.La réponse s'éteint, sans que l'apprenti: The response dies out, without the learning being erased
textes.C'est l'extinction. Après un repos, la r: This is extinction. After a rest, the response can return, weaker: spontaneous recovery.
textes.De quoi le petit Albert a-t-il appris à: What was little Albert taught to fear in 1920?
textes.Chaque fois qu'il touchait le rat, on fr: Each time he touched the rat, a steel bar was struck behind him. The fear spread to a rabbit, a dog, a fur coat.
textes.En 1920, Watson et Rayner conditionnent: In 1920, Watson and Rayner conditioned "Albert" to fear a white rat by striking a steel bar; the fear spread to a rabbit, a dog, fur.
textes.La peur d'Albert s'est étendue à d'autre: Albert's fear spread to other furry things, such as a rabbit or a Santa Claus mask.
textes.Vrai. C'est la généralisation : un stimu: True. This is generalisation: a similar stimulus triggers the same response. But not everything with hair.
textes.Selon le manifeste de Watson (1913), que: According to Watson's manifesto (1913), what should psychology be?
