textes.Une branche expérimentale purement objec: A purely objective experimental branch of natural science
textes.L'étude de l'âme par l'introspection: The study of the soul through introspection
textes.Fini la conscience : seul compte le comp: No more consciousness: only observable behaviour counts. Watson nevertheless ended up in advertising, at J. Walter Thompson.
textes.En 1913, Watson décrit la psychologie co: In 1913, Watson described psychology as "a purely objective experimental branch of natural science"; he joined J. Walter Thompson in late 1920.
textes.Qui propose en 1898 la « loi de l'effet: Who proposed the "law of effect" in 1898, the basis of operant conditioning?
textes.Thorndike étudiait des animaux dans des: Thorndike studied animals in puzzle boxes. Skinner would adapt these boxes, with levers for rats and keys for pigeons.
textes.Thorndike propose la loi de l'effet en 1: Thorndike proposed the law of effect in 1898; Skinner adapted his puzzle box.
textes.Skinner aimait qu'on appelle son disposi: Skinner liked his apparatus being called the "Skinner box".
textes.Faux. Il détestait ce nom, qu'il n'emplo: False. He disliked the name, which he did not use, and asked for "lever box". The name is thought to come from Clark Hull and his Yale students.
textes.Skinner n'aimait pas le terme « Skinner: Skinner disliked the term "Skinner box" and preferred "lever box"; Clark Hull and his students are thought to have coined it.
textes.Quelle patiente de Josef Breuer a invent: Which of Josef Breuer's patients coined the phrase "talking cure"?
textes.Breuer et Freud publient ensuite, en 189: Breuer and Freud then published, in 1895, the Studies on Hysteria.
textes.Anna O. (Bertha Pappenheim), soignée par: Anna O. (Bertha Pappenheim), treated by Breuer, coined the phrase "talking cure"; Studies on Hysteria, 1895.
textes.Selon Freud, qu'est-ce qu'un rêve ?: According to Freud, what is a dream?
textes.Un désir déguisé : le contenu manifeste: A disguised wish: the manifest content hides a latent content, which interpretation must recover.
textes.L'Interprétation des rêves paraît le 4 n: The Interpretation of Dreams appeared on 4 November 1899, dated 1900; 600 copies, sold over eight years.
textes.Combien d'années le premier tirage de L': How many years did the first printing of The Interpretation of Dreams (600 copies) take to sell?
textes.Huit ans. Le livre connaîtra pourtant hu: Eight years. The book would nevertheless go through eight editions in Freud's lifetime, the last in 1929.
textes.L'Interprétation des rêves est parue en: The Interpretation of Dreams appeared in November 1899, but bears the date 1900.
textes.Vrai. Le 4 novembre 1899, chez Franz Deu: True. On 4 November 1899, from Franz Deuticke, in Leipzig and Vienna, with the date of the new century.
textes.Quelle instance, selon Freud, obéit au p: Which agency, according to Freud, obeys the pleasure principle?
textes.Le ça, présent dès la naissance, réservo: The id, present from birth, reservoir of drives. The ego follows the reality principle.
textes.Le ça obéit au principe de plaisir, le m: The id obeys the pleasure principle, the ego the reality principle; the superego is the seat of self-criticism.
textes.Par quelle méthode Freud remplace-t-il l: With what method did Freud replace hypnosis?
textes.Le patient dit tout ce qui lui vient à l: The patient says whatever comes to mind, without sorting. In classical psychoanalysis, he lies down and the analyst sits behind him.
textes.Après avoir abandonné l'hypnose, Freud i: After abandoning hypnosis, Freud encouraged his patients to talk freely: free association.
textes.Quel reproche Karl Popper fait-il à la p: What criticism did Karl Popper make of psychoanalysis?
textes.Une théorie qui peut tout expliquer ne p: A theory that can explain everything can never be proved wrong: for Popper, this is the sign of a pseudoscience.
textes.Popper juge la psychanalyse irréfutable,: Popper judged psychoanalysis unfalsifiable, and classed it among the pseudosciences.
textes.Auprès de qui Freud part-il étudier à Pa: With whom did Freud go to study in Paris in 1885?
textes.Trois mois de bourse auprès du neurologu: A three-month fellowship with the neurologist, who studied hypnosis.
textes.En octobre 1885, Freud part trois mois à: In October 1885, Freud went to Paris for three months to study with Charcot, who researched hypnosis.
textes.Dans la séance classique, le patient est: In the classical session, the patient lies down and the analyst sits behind him, out of sight.
textes.Vrai. Et la cure classique demande de tr: True. And the classical cure requires three to five sessions a week, often for years.
textes.En psychanalyse classique, le patient es: In classical psychoanalysis, the patient is on a couch, the analyst just behind, out of sight; three to five sessions a week.
textes.Que répond Freud en 1933 quand les nazis: What did Freud say in 1933 when the Nazis burned his books?
textes.Qu'au Moyen Âge, on l'aurait brûlé lui-m: That in the Middle Ages they would have burned him
textes.Rien, il ne l'apprend qu'après la guerre: Nothing, he only learned of it after the war
textes.« Quels progrès nous faisons ! » dit-il: "What progress we are making!" he told Ernest Jones. He died in London in 1939.
textes.À Ernest Jones : « Au Moyen Âge, ils m'a: To Ernest Jones: "In the Middle Ages they would have burned me. Now, they are content with burning my books."
textes.Pourquoi Binet met-il au point son échel: Why did Binet devise his scale in 1905?
textes.Pour repérer les écoliers qui ont besoin: To spot pupils who need adapted teaching
textes.En 1904, le ministère de l'Instruction p: In 1904, the Ministry of Public Instruction set up a commission on struggling pupils. The test was meant to help, not to rank.
textes.En 1905, Binet et Simon publient une éch: In 1905, Binet and Simon published a scale of thirty tasks; the 1908 version introduced mental age.
textes.Avec la formule de Stern, quel est le QI: Using Stern's formula, what is the IQ of an 8-year-old who passes the tasks of a 10-year-old?
textes.QI = (âge mental ÷ âge réel) × 100. Ici: IQ = (mental age ÷ real age) × 100. Here IQ = (10 ÷ 8) × 100 = 1.25 × 100 = 125. Formula proposed by William Stern in 1912; Simon saw it as a betrayal of the test's purpose.
textes.William Stern propose en 1912 le quotien: William Stern proposed in 1912 the intelligence quotient: mental age divided by real age, multiplied by 100.
textes.Avec la formule de Stern, quel est le QI: Using Stern's formula, what is the IQ of a 10-year-old whose mental age is 9?
textes.QI = (âge mental ÷ âge réel) × 100 = (9: IQ = (mental age ÷ real age) × 100 = (9 ÷ 10) × 100 = 0.9 × 100 = 90. This is William Stern's formula, from 1912. Modern tests have abandoned this quotient in favour of a ranking on a curve.
textes.Combien d'épreuves comptait l'échelle Bi: How many tasks did the 1905 Binet-Simon scale have?
textes.Trente, en quatre parties : de saisir un: Thirty, in four parts: from grasping an object to answering an abstract question. It took about a quarter of an hour.
textes.Qu'introduit la version de 1908 de l'éch: What did the 1908 version of the Binet-Simon scale introduce?
textes.L'âge mental est l'âge dont l'enfant réu: Mental age is the age whose tasks the child succeeds at. The IQ would come from Stern in 1912.
textes.Binet et Simon voyaient l'intelligence c: Binet and Simon saw intelligence as a fixed quantity, given at birth.
textes.Faux. Ils la jugeaient malléable. Simon: False. They judged it malleable. Simon even found that the conversion into IQ betrayed the test's purpose.
textes.Binet et Simon insistent sur une intelli: Binet and Simon stressed that intelligence was malleable rather than fixed.
textes.Quel psychologue de Stanford révise l'éc: Which Stanford psychologist revised Binet's scale in 1916?
textes.Le Stanford-Binet devient le test le plu: The Stanford-Binet became the most used test in the United States for decades, and adopted Stern's IQ.
textes.En 1916, Lewis Terman publie la révision: In 1916, Lewis Terman published the Stanford revision, which replaced mental age with IQ.
textes.Sur les tests modernes, entre quels scor: On modern tests, between which scores do about two people in three fall?
textes.La moyenne est fixée à 100 et l'écart ty: The mean is set at 100 and the standard deviation at 15: 85 and 115 are one standard deviation on either side.
textes.Les tests modernes ont une moyenne de 10: Modern tests have a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15; about two-thirds of people are between 85 and 115; Flynn effect: about three points per decade.
textes.Les scores bruts de QI montent d'environ: Raw IQ scores rise by about 3 points per decade. By how many points do they rise in 30 years?
textes.Hausse = rythme × durée = 3 points par d: Rise = rate × duration = 3 points per decade × 3 decades = 9 points. This is a simple proportion, with no discoverer. The phenomenon is called the Flynn effect.
textes.Dans La Mal-Mesure de l'homme (1981), qu: In The Mismeasure of Man (1981), what did Stephen Jay Gould denounce?
textes.L'idée de résumer l'intelligence en un s: The idea of summing up intelligence in a single number
textes.L'usage des ordinateurs à l'école: The use of computers at school
textes.Il y voit deux erreurs : faire d'un conc: He saw two errors in it: turning an abstract concept into a thing (reification) and ranking complex variation on a single scale. The book was itself sharply criticised.
textes.Gould critique l'hypothèse qu'on puisse: Gould criticised the assumption that worth can be assigned to individuals by measuring intelligence as a single quantity; reification and ranking.
textes.{comp}. Ebbinghaus apprenait des syllabe: {comp}. Ebbinghaus learned syllables with no meaning at all. I give you some. Make the most of it.
textes.Psychologie. William James disait que no: Psychology. William James said we are sad because we cry. Don't cry too soon: {comp}.
textes.Pavlov sonnait, les chiens salivaient. J: Pavlov rang, the dogs salivated. I launch {comp}, you tap the screen.
textes.Juste. Votre hippocampe travaille. Henry: Right. Your hippocampus is working. Henry Molaison would have envied yours.
textes.Bonne réponse. Piaget vous aurait noté d: Correct. Piaget would have noted you in his notebook, between two of his children.
textes.Correct. Milgram aurait voulu savoir qui: Correct. Milgram would have wanted to know who ordered you to succeed. Me.
textes.Bien vu. Je ressens quelque chose. Proba: Well spotted. I feel something. Probably a bug.
textes.Raté. Phineas Gage s'est remis d'une bar: Missed. Phineas Gage recovered from an iron bar through his skull. You'll recover from this.
textes.Faux. Gall lisait le caractère dans les: Wrong. Gall read character in the bumps of the skull. I read the error in your answer. It's more reliable.
textes.Erreur. La courbe de l'oubli d'Ebbinghau: Error. Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve was lying in wait. It got you.
textes.Je compatis. C'est faux, mais l'intentio: I sympathize. It's wrong, but the intention is there.
textes.Avec son mari Kenneth, elle présente à d: With her husband Kenneth, she shows Black children two identical dolls, one white, one Black, and asks them which one is nice, which one is pretty. Most choose the white one. This work was cited in 1954 by the Supreme Court in the ruling that ended school segregation.
textes.Pour lui, nous ne pleurons pas parce que: For him, we don't cry because we are sad: we are sad because we cry. The body reacts first, the emotion follows. At Harvard he taught the first course in experimental psychology in the United States, and noted that the first lecture on psychology he ever heard was his own.
textes.Seul cobaye de ses propres expériences,: The only guinea pig of his own experiments, he learns thousands of nonsense syllables (textbooks cite DAX or BOK), to the beat of a metronome, and measures how fast he forgets them. This is the forgetting curve, published in 1885. This game applies it to your recalls.
textes.Il reçoit le Nobel en 1904 pour ses trav: He received the Nobel in 1904 for his work on digestion, not for the conditioned reflex. His laboratory ran like a factory, with dozens of assistants and dogs. To announce food, he mostly used a metronome, a buzzer or a whistle, far more often than a bell.
textes.En 1961, il fait croire à des volontaire: In 1961, he leads volunteers to believe they are sending electric shocks to a “learner” who makes mistakes. On the calm orders of a man in a gray lab coat, twenty-six out of forty go up to 450 volts. The shocks were fake. The volunteers' distress was very real.
textes.Avec une coloration à l'argent inventée: Using a silver stain invented by his rival Golgi, he shows that the brain is made of separate cells, neurons, and draws thousands of them. They share the 1906 Nobel and contradict each other in their speeches. As a child, he had built a cannon and demolished a neighbor's gate.
textes.Médecin des gladiateurs de Pergame, puis: Physician to the gladiators of Pergamon, then to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, he derives four temperaments from Hippocrates' four humors: sanguine, phlegmatic, choleric, melancholic. The theory is wrong, the words stayed. He dissected monkeys for lack of human bodies, and his errors stood until Vesalius.
textes.Jeune chercheur à Montréal, maladroit, i: A clumsy young researcher in Montreal, he injects all sorts of extracts into struggling rodents, and always gets the same lesions, whatever the extract. From this he derives the concept of “stress”. He later took money from the tobacco industry, delighted that people talked about stress rather than cigarettes.
Master the first diamond of Empathy.
textes.Le cœur a ses raisons, que la raison ne: The heart has its reasons, which reason knows nothing of.
textes.Maîtriser l'influence sociale. Vous saur: Master social influence. At least you'll know why nobody moved.
textes.Le meurtre de Kitty Genovese (1964) a la: The murder of Kitty Genovese (1964) launched the study of the bystander effect, with “38 witnesses who did nothing”. The figure was greatly exaggerated: few neighbors understood what was happening, and some called the police. The New York Times acknowledged it in 2016.
textes.Maîtriser 7 compétences. L'arbre de la P: Master 7 skills. The Psychology tree opens.
textes.L'art d'être sage est l'art de savoir ce: The art of being wise is the art of knowing what to overlook.
textes.Maîtriser les émotions. Sourire de force: Master emotions. Forcing a smile doesn't make things funnier. The AI does.
textes.En 1988, une étude célèbre fait tenir un: In 1988, a famous study had people hold a pen between their teeth (which forces a smile) or between their lips: cartoons seemed funnier to the involuntary smilers. In 2016, seventeen laboratories carefully redid the experiment. No effect.
textes.Maîtriser la mémoire. Vous retiendrez ce: Master memory. You'll remember this one; he couldn't.
textes.En 1953, on retire à Henry Molaison une: In 1953, part of both of Henry Molaison's hippocampi is removed to treat his epilepsy. He can no longer form new memories. Yet he learns to draw in a mirror, better and better, without ever remembering having done it. So there are several kinds of memory.
textes.Maîtriser la motivation. Vous avez atten: Master motivation. You waited for this achievement without eating it. Well done.
textes.Dans les années 1970, des enfants qui ré: In the 1970s, children who resisted one marshmallow to get two seemed to do better later on. In 2018, a replication with over 900 children found a much weaker effect, largely explained by family background.
textes.Maîtriser le cerveau. Le cerveau répare: Master the brain. The brain repairs more than people say.
textes.En 1848, une barre de fer traverse le cr: In 1848, an iron bar goes through the skull of Phineas Gage, a railroad foreman. The story goes that he stayed brutish and unstable until his death. In fact, he later drove stagecoaches in Chile for years, a job that demands patience and organization.
Master child development. Your parents observed you too. Less scientifically.
textes.Jean Piaget a bâti une bonne partie de s: Jean Piaget built a good part of his theory by observing his three children, Jacqueline, Lucienne and Laurent, from the cradle to school: he notes their gestures, hides objects from them under a cushion, and watches whether they look for them.
textes.Maîtriser la personnalité. Vous n'êtes p: Master personality. You are not a type. You are a distribution.
textes.Le test MBTI, qui range chacun dans l'un: The MBTI test, which sorts everyone into one of sixteen types, was designed by Katharine Briggs and her daughter Isabel Myers, with no training in psychology, based on Jung. Retaken five weeks later, it changes the type of 39 to 76% of people. Psychologists prefer the Big Five traits.
textes.Maîtriser le bien-être et le stress. L'h: Master well-being and stress. The habit of playing here, you have picked up.
textes.Il faudrait 21 jours pour prendre une ha: It supposedly takes 21 days to form a habit. The figure comes from a cosmetic surgeon, Maxwell Maltz, who noted in 1960 that his patients got used to their new face in about three weeks. Measured in 2010: from 18 to 254 days, 66 on average.
textes.Réussir trois quiz d'Empathie sans faute: Pass three Empathy quizzes without a mistake. The AI expected the worst. You disappointed her.
textes.En 1968, Rosenthal et Jacobson annoncent: In 1968, Rosenthal and Jacobson announce that pupils randomly labeled “promising” progress more, because their teachers believe in them. The effect exists, but reanalyses show it is much weaker than promised, and mostly in the youngest children.
textes.Maîtriser l'esprit selon le Bouddha. La: Master the mind according to the Buddha. The first arrow was the question. The second, you shot at yourself.
textes.Dans le discours de la flèche, l'homme n: In the discourse on the arrow, the untaught man receives two arrows: the pain, then the pain of being in pain. The instructed disciple receives only one.
Master Theophrastus's Characters. The late learner memorises verse at sixty. You are a little ahead of him. A little.
textes.Le « tardif » de Théophraste apprend des: Theophrastus's "late learner" memorises poems at sixty and has his own son teach him military drill.
textes.Maîtriser Épictète et les passions. Le s: Master Epictetus and the passions. The Stoic would tell you to accept what follows calmly. The AI would tell you to revise.

textes.Le Soleil se trouve aujourd'hui dans la: Today, the Sun is in the constellation of your sign on your birthday.

textes.Quand Mercure est rétrograde, la planète: When Mercury is in retrograde, the planet really changes direction in its orbit.

textes.Un argument d'analogie qui oublie l'éche: An argument by analogy that forgets about scale.
textes.En 1948, des étudiants ont jugé très jus: In 1948, students judged a psychological portrait very accurate when it was the same for everyone.

textes.En 1910, on a vendu des « pilules anti-c: In 1910, “comet pills” were sold against the gases of Halley's comet.

textes.Johannes Kepler, qui a découvert les loi: Johannes Kepler, who discovered the laws of planetary motion, cast horoscopes.

textes.Un « fluide magnétique animal » peut gué: An “animal magnetic fluid” can cure the sick.
textes.Les commissaires de 1784 bandent les yeu: The 1784 commissioners blindfolded the patients: they reacted when they believed they were being magnetized, not when they actually were. Conclusion: it is imagination.
textes.Mesmer développe sa théorie à Vienne dan: Mesmer developed his theory in Vienna in the 1770s, then settled in Paris in 1778, where he treated a wealthy clientele.
textes.L'imagerie montre que toutes les régions: Imaging shows that every region is used, and damage anywhere has consequences.
textes.Une déformation des idées du psychologue: A distortion of the ideas of the psychologist William James, popularized in 1936 by the preface to a Dale Carnegie book.
textes.Écouter du Mozart rend les bébés plus in: Listening to Mozart makes babies smarter.
textes.L'étude d'origine portait sur des étudia: The original study was on students, with a slight effect lasting a few minutes. Meta-analyses found nothing lasting.

textes.On apprend mieux quand l'enseignement su: You learn better when teaching matches your learning style, visual, auditory or kinesthetic.
textes.Les études bien conçues ne trouvent pas: Well-designed studies do not find this effect. The best format depends mostly on what is being learned.
textes.Un modèle très vendu aux enseignants dep: A model widely sold to teachers since the 1970s.
textes.Chacun est plutôt « cerveau gauche », lo: Everyone is either “left-brained,” logical, or “right-brained,” creative.

textes.Le détecteur de mensonges repère les men: The lie detector reliably catches liars.
textes.Il mesure le stress, pas le mensonge. Un: It measures stress, not lying. An anxious innocent person fails, a calm liar passes.
textes.Inventé en 1921 par John Larson ; l'un d: Invented in 1921 by John Larson; one of its promoters, William Marston, would go on to create Wonder Woman and her lasso of truth.
textes.Des images subliminales « Buvez Coca-Col: Subliminal “Drink Coca-Cola” images shown in a movie theater made sales jump.

textes.Un cheval, Hans le Malin, semblait savoi: A horse, Clever Hans, seemed to know how to count, but was actually reading his audience's involuntary gestures.

textes.On appelle depuis « effet Hans le Malin: The experimenter's involuntary influence has been called the “Clever Hans effect” ever since.

textes.Environ la moitié ne voit pas l'étudiant: About half do not see the student dressed as a gorilla. This is inattentional blindness.
textes.L'expérience de Simons et Chabris est de: Simons and Chabris's experiment has become a classic of the psychology of attention.

textes.Le chiffre de dix pour un vient d'un cal: The ten-to-one figure comes from a quick 1972 calculation, copied for forty years.
textes.L'évolution mène vers des espèces de plu: Evolution leads toward more and more perfect species.
textes.La sélection naturelle n'a pas de but :: Natural selection has no goal: it favors what works in a given environment. Bacteria, which appeared more than 3 billion years ago, are doing very well.
textes.L'image populaire d'une échelle qui mont: The popular image of a ladder climbing up to humans, which Darwin avoided.
textes.Des poissons rouges ont appris à pousser: Goldfish have learned to push a lever to get food, and to do so at a precise time. Other experiments show memories lasting months.

textes.L'idée est déjà chez Pline l'Ancien, qui: The idea is already in Pliny the Elder, who thinks the bird believes itself hidden once it has stuck its neck into a bush.
textes.Le généticien Nikolaï Vavilov, opposant: The geneticist Nikolai Vavilov, Lysenko's opponent, died in prison.
textes.Arrêté en 1940, il meurt en 1943 dans la: Arrested in 1940, he died in 1943 in Saratov prison, worn out by detention; some authors speak of starvation. He had built up one of the largest seed collections in the world, which his colleagues protected during the siege of Leningrad.
textes.Son histoire n'a été racontée librement: His story was only told freely after Lysenko's fall.

textes.Ces animaux, le plus souvent plus petits: These animals, usually smaller than half a millimeter, withstand extreme conditions by drying out.
textes.Gregor Mendel a publié ses lois de l'hér: Gregor Mendel published his laws of heredity in 1866, but they were ignored for 34 years.
textes.Elles sont redécouvertes en 1900 par tro: They were rediscovered in 1900 by three botanists, de Vries, Correns and Tschermak.

textes.L'article d'Andrew Wakefield dans The La: Andrew Wakefield's 1998 article in The Lancet, retracted in 2010; Wakefield was struck off the medical register.
textes.Les pyramides d'Égypte sont trop parfait: The pyramids of Egypt are too perfect to have been built by humans of that era.
textes.On a retrouvé les villages des ouvriers: The workers' villages have been found at Giza, their tombs, and the diary of the inspector Merer describing the transport of the blocks.

textes.En 1962, l'état-major américain a propos: In 1962, the US Joint Chiefs of Staff proposed staging attacks to justify a war against Cuba.
textes.C'est l'opération Northwoods. Le gouvern: This is Operation Northwoods. The Kennedy administration rejected it. The document was declassified in 1997.

textes.L'analyse de 176 études par l'agence de: The Australian health agency's review of 176 studies found no condition for which it does better than a placebo. It has not been reimbursed in France since 2021.
textes.La grippe est due à un virus, les antibi: The flu is caused by a virus; antibiotics only act on bacteria. Taking them for nothing encourages resistance.
textes.Une confusion si répandue qu'elle a eu s: A confusion so widespread that it got its own French campaign: “Antibiotics are not automatic.”

textes.La vitamine C à haute dose protège du rh: High-dose vitamin C protects against colds.
textes.Chez la plupart des gens, elle ne réduit: In most people, it does not reduce the number of colds, and only shortens them a little.

textes.Les cheveux et les ongles continuent de: Hair and nails keep growing after death.

textes.En décembre 1799, ses médecins lui retir: In December 1799, his doctors drew about 2.4 liters of blood in twelve hours for a severe throat inflammation.

textes.À Vienne en 1847, la mortalité de sa cli: In Vienna in 1847, his clinic's death rate fell from about 10% to 1 or 2%. But he could not explain it, and his colleagues took offense at being accused.
textes.Pasteur et Lister lui donneront raison v: Pasteur and Lister would prove him right twenty years later.
textes.Un placebo peut soulager même quand le p: A placebo can bring relief even when the patient knows it is a placebo.

textes.Les lemmings se jettent en masse du haut: Lemmings throw themselves off cliffs en masse.
textes.Leurs populations explosent puis s'effon: Their populations boom and then crash about every four years, and they then migrate in great numbers. They do not commit suicide.

textes.Les bovins distinguent mal le rouge. C'e: Cattle see red poorly. It is the movement of the cape that triggers the charge: waved about, a blue cape has the same effect.
textes.La muleta des corridas est rouge, surtou: The muleta used in bullfights is red, mainly to hide the blood.
textes.Toutes voient, et les grandes roussettes: All bats can see, and large fruit bats even have very good eyesight. Many also find their way by echolocation.
textes.À la fin du XVIIIe siècle, Spallanzani c: In the late 18th century, Spallanzani found that bats with blinded eyes still avoided obstacles. People concluded they did not need their eyes.

textes.Les dromadaires stockent de l'eau dans l: Camels store water in their hump.
textes.La bosse est une réserve de graisse. Leu: The hump is a fat reserve. Their endurance comes from very thrifty kidneys and red blood cells that can swell when they drink a lot at once.

textes.Il ne peut pas les lancer. Les piquants: It cannot throw them. The quills come loose on contact and stay stuck in the attacker.

textes.Les hirondelles passent l'hiver endormie: Swallows spend the winter asleep at the bottom of ponds.

textes.Aristote parle d'hirondelles qui se cach: Aristotle speaks of swallows that hide in winter. In 1555, Archbishop Olaus Magnus tells of fishermen hauling them up in netfuls from the bottom of lakes.
textes.Les deux tiers des neurones d'une pieuvr: Two thirds of an octopus's neurons are in its arms.
textes.Sur environ 500 millions de neurones, la: Of about 500 million neurons, most are in the arms, which can taste, grasp and react without waiting for the brain.
textes.Des comptages de neurones et des expérie: Neuron counts and experiments on isolated arms.
textes.Les corneilles reconnaissent un visage h: Crows recognize a human face and remember it for years.
textes.À Seattle, des chercheurs masqués ont ca: In Seattle, masked researchers captured a few crows. Years later, the birds still screamed at that mask, including those that had never been captured.
textes.Une expérience menée avec des masques de: An experiment run with rubber masks, to separate the face from the person.
textes.En 1822, une cigogne est arrivée en Alle: In 1822, a stork arrived in Germany with an African spear stuck through its neck.
textes.Cette « cigogne à flèche » a prouvé que: This “arrow stork” proved that storks wintered in Africa, at a time when the great migrations were still doubted.
textes.L'oiseau naturalisé est toujours exposé: The stuffed bird is still on display at the University of Rostock.
textes.On repère un menteur à son regard, qui p: You can spot a liar by their gaze, which goes up and to the right.
textes.Des chercheurs ont filmé des personnes q: Researchers filmed people who were lying or telling the truth: the direction of their gaze did not tell them apart.
textes.Le polygraphe mesure le stress : pouls,: The polygraph measures stress: pulse, breathing, sweat. An anxious innocent person can fail, a calm liar can pass.
textes.Inventé en 1921 par John Larson, popular: Invented in 1921 by John Larson, popularized by William Marston, who also created Wonder Woman and her lasso of truth.
textes.La mémoire enregistre les événements com: Memory records events like a video that can be replayed faithfully.
textes.Chaque souvenir se reconstruit quand on: Every memory is rebuilt when it is recalled. You can even make people believe they got lost in a shopping mall as children.
textes.La métaphore de l'enregistrement, et l'a: The recording metaphor, and the “recovered memories” affair of the 1990s.
textes.Une soirée trop arrosée détruit des mill: One heavy night of drinking destroys thousands of neurons.
textes.L'alcool perturbe les neurones et, à lon: Alcohol disrupts neurons and, in the long term and at high doses, damages their connections. But no loss of cortical neurons is found in heavy drinkers.
textes.Une formule de prévention qui a pris le: A prevention slogan that took a shortcut.
textes.Il faut ajouter au moins l'équilibre, la: You must add at least balance, body position, temperature and pain. Physiologists count about ten, or even more.

textes.La langue a des zones séparées pour le s: The tongue has separate areas for sweet, salty, sour and bitter.
textes.Toutes les parties de la langue qui port: Every part of the tongue that has taste buds perceives every taste.
textes.Une thèse allemande de 1901, dont les co: A 1901 German thesis whose curves, redrawn in 1942 by the psychologist Edwin Boring, were misread and then copied into textbooks.
textes.Le cerveau d'Einstein était plus gros qu: Einstein's brain was bigger than average.
textes.Il pesait environ 1 230 grammes, dans le: It weighed about 1,230 grams, at the low end of the normal range. Some regions had an unusual shape, which does not prove much.
