textes.Un ordinateur ne manipule au fond que de: Deep down, a computer only handles 0s and 1s.
textes.Textes, images et sons sont tous codés e: Text, images and sound are all encoded in binary.
textes.En décembre 1733, le Français Charles du: In December 1733, Frenchman Charles du Fay concluded that there are two kinds of electricity, which he called "vitreous" and "resinous": our positive and negative charges.
textes.C'est Benjamin Franklin qui nomme les ch: It was Benjamin Franklin who named charges positive and negative, in the 18th century, without knowing which case was a surplus. The electron was only named in 1891 by George Johnstone Stoney, and J. J. Thomson showed in 1897 that it is a particle.
textes.En 1729, l'Anglais Stephen Gray montre q: In 1729, Englishman Stephen Gray showed that electricity travels along a hemp thread but not along silk, which he used to insulate it. For his "flying boy", he hung a child from silk cords and electrified him.
textes.Stephen Gray est le premier à étudier la: Stephen Gray was the first to study conduction systematically, around 1729: he showed that metals carry electricity. His colleague John Desaguliers coined the words "conductor" and "insulator".
textes.Les règles des circuits en série et en d: The rules for series and parallel circuits were first described in 1845 by German physicist Gustav Kirchhoff.
textes.Gustav Kirchhoff énonce en 1845 les lois: Gustav Kirchhoff set out in 1845 the laws that say how current divides between the branches of a circuit.
textes.Ingénieur militaire, Charles-Augustin de: A military engineer, Charles-Augustin de Coulomb supervised the building of Fort Bourbon in Martinique. In 1785, with his torsion balance, he showed that the force between two charges falls off as the square of the distance. The unit was named after him in 1880.
textes.En 1600, le médecin anglais William Gilb: In 1600, English physician William Gilbert coined the Latin word electricus from the Greek word for amber.
textes.Le physicien Louis Breguet recommande de: Physicist Louis Breguet recommended thinner wires to protect telegraph stations from lightning: they melt first. Thomas Edison patented a fuse in 1890 for his network, and circuit breakers replaced it in new homes from the 1950s.
textes.Tout part d'une dispute : dans les année: It all began with a dispute: in the 1780s, Luigi Galvani saw a frog's leg twitch in contact with two metals. Volta thought the electricity came from the metals, not the animal, and described his pile in a letter to the Royal Society on 20 March 1800. That same year, it was used to split water.
textes.Henry Cavendish avait trouvé la même loi: Henry Cavendish had found the same law in 1781, measuring current by the strength of the shock he took through his own body; he published nothing, and Maxwell revealed his results in 1879.
textes.Le livre d'Ohm est très mal reçu : un cr: Ohm's book was very badly received: a critic called it "a web of naked fancies" and the Minister of Education judged that a professor preaching such heresies was unworthy to teach science. The law only won acceptance in the 1840s.
textes.L'ampère porte le nom d'André-Marie Ampè: The ampere is named after André-Marie Ampère (1775-1836). It became an international unit in 1881, at the International Exposition of Electricity; since 2019, it has been defined from the elementary charge.
textes.Le mot « volt » est inventé en 1861 par: The word "volt" was coined in 1861 by Latimer Clark and Charles Bright, in honour of Volta. The 1881 International Electrical Congress adopted it as the unit of voltage.
textes.En 1899, la compagnie d'électricité de B: In 1899, Berlin's electricity company switched to 220 V, a model taken up across Europe, while the United Kingdom chose 240 V. A 1983 standard set 230 V for all, phased in from 1987.
textes.Le nom de watt, en hommage à James Watt,: The name watt, in honour of James Watt, was proposed in August 1882 by engineer William Siemens before the British Association. It was officially adopted at the 1908 London international conference.
textes.La formule P = U × I s'appuie sur l'inte: The formula P = U × I relies on current, for which Ampère introduced the symbol I in 1820.
textes.Humphry Davy fait briller une lame de pl: Humphry Davy made a platinum strip glow as early as 1802, with no practical result. Joseph Swan showed his lamp to 700 people on 3 February 1879, and Thomas Edison succeeded in his first test on 22 October 1879: thirteen and a half hours. A filament bulb turns less than 5% of its energy into light.
textes.En 1884, une ligne de 34 km en courant a: In 1884, a 34 km alternating-current line was built for the Turin exhibition. In 1891, the Lauffen-Frankfurt line carried three-phase current at 15,000 volts over about 175 km.
textes.James Prescott Joule étudie cet échauffe: James Prescott Joule studied this heating in 1841. In countries of the former USSR, it is called the Joule-Lenz law.
textes.Le 20 décembre 1951, le réacteur expérim: On 20 December 1951, the experimental reactor EBR-I in Idaho produced the first nuclear electricity. The Obninsk plant in the USSR was the first connected to the grid, on 27 June 1954.
textes.Heinrich Hertz observe l'effet en 1887 :: Heinrich Hertz observed the effect in 1887: ultraviolet light made his sparks easier. Einstein explained it in 1905 with packets of light. Robert Millikan, who found the idea "quite unthinkable", confirmed his law in 1914.
textes.Le joule est proposé en 1882 par William: The joule was proposed in 1882 by William Siemens and officially adopted on 31 August 1889, at the second International Electrical Congress.
textes.Vers 1269, Pierre de Maricourt écrit sa: Around 1269, Peter Peregrinus of Maricourt wrote his Letter on the Magnet: the oldest surviving text to speak of poles and show that like poles repel.
textes.En 1600, dans De Magnete, William Gilber: In 1600, in De Magnete, William Gilbert, physician to Elizabeth I, experimented on a small magnetised Earth, the terrella, and concluded that the Earth is itself a magnet.
textes.Le récit d'une découverte faite par hasa: The story of a chance discovery in the middle of a lecture is a myth: Ørsted had been looking for this link since 1818. His discovery at once launched Ampère's work. Ørsted also isolated aluminium in 1824.
textes.Le 29 août 1831, Faraday enroule deux fi: On 29 August 1831, Faraday wound two wires around an iron ring: connecting one, he saw a brief "wave of electricity" in the other. American Joseph Henry made the same discovery on his own in 1832.
textes.Le pôle magnétique nord est atteint pour: The north magnetic pole was first reached on 1 June 1831 by James Clark Ross. It moves: about 55 km a year in 2019, from Canada towards Siberia.
textes.William Sturgeon invente l'électroaimant: William Sturgeon invented the electromagnet in 1824: 18 turns of bare copper wire on a horseshoe that lifted 9 pounds. Joseph Henry improved it from 1830 with silk-insulated wire; its first major use was the telegraph.
textes.Faraday et le Français Hippolyte Pixii f: Faraday and Frenchman Hippolyte Pixii ran the first generators in the 1830s. The word "alternator" appeared in the late 1870s, when Yablochkov's arc lamps worked better on alternating current.
textes.Le 3 septembre 1821, Faraday fait tourne: On 3 September 1821, Faraday made a wire dipped in mercury rotate around a magnet. Moritz von Jacobi built the first truly useful motor in 1834, which in 1838 drove a boat with 14 people across a wide river.
textes.En 1855, Weber et Kohlrausch mesurent un: In 1855, Weber and Kohlrausch measured an electrical velocity of about 310,000 km/s, very close to the speed of light. Maxwell published his equations in 1865: twenty equations originally, which Oliver Heaviside rewrote in today's compact form.
textes.Le Norvégien Kristian Birkeland envoie u: Norwegian Kristian Birkeland aimed an electron beam at a magnetised sphere: the electrons gathered towards the poles in rings of light. From this he drew his theory of the aurora, confirmed only in 1967 by a space probe.
textes.Pierre Curie se demandait dès 1894 si un: Pierre Curie wondered as early as 1894 whether a single magnetic pole could exist, and Paul Dirac developed its theory in 1931. On 14 February 1982, Blas Cabrera recorded a signal nicknamed the "Valentine's Day monopole", never reproduced. None has ever been observed.
textes.Les premiers brevets datent de 1906 (Art: The first patents date from 1906 (Arthur Berry, in the UK) and 1909. Frigidaire toured demonstration hobs in the mid-1950s without selling them; Westinghouse sold its own from 1973 to 1975.
textes.Maxwell comprend dès 1861, dans On Physi: Maxwell understood as early as 1861, in On Physical Lines of Force, that light is an electromagnetic wave. In 1865, he published A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field.
textes.Hertz mène ses expériences de 1886 à 188: Hertz carried out his experiments from 1886 to 1889 in Karlsruhe and confirmed the waves predicted by Maxwell. Asked about applications, he replied: "Nothing, I guess." He died in 1894, aged 36; the unit of frequency bears his name.
textes.En 1800, William Herschel place un therm: In 1800, William Herschel placed a thermometer beyond the red end of a spectrum of sunlight: it warmed up. A year later, Johann Ritter discovered on the other side, beyond violet, rays that darken silver chloride.
textes.Le Français Paul Villard découvre les ra: Frenchman Paul Villard discovered gamma rays in 1900 while studying radium. Ernest Rutherford named them in 1903, and showed with Edward Andrade in 1914 that their wavelength is shorter than that of X-rays.
textes.Percy Spencer n'avait pas fini l'école p: Percy Spencer had not finished grammar school and taught himself in the Navy. Others had seen a candy bar melt near a radar; he looked into it, popping corn and bursting an egg. The first commercial oven, in 1947, stood about 6 feet tall and weighed 750 pounds.
textes.Le 8 novembre 1895, à Würzburg, Röntgen: On 8 November 1895, in Würzburg, Röntgen saw a screen glow near a discharge tube. He called the rays "X", the letter for the unknown. Six weeks later, he imaged the hand of his wife Anna Bertha, who exclaimed: "I have seen my death!"
textes.Newton est le premier à employer le mot: Newton was the first to use the word "spectrum" in 1671 for light split by a prism; he first counted six colours and later added indigo. Thomas Young was the first to measure the wavelengths of colours, in 1802.
textes.Le 12 décembre 1901, Marconi écoute à Si: On 12 December 1901, Marconi listened at Signal Hill, Newfoundland, with a kite-borne antenna, for a signal sent from Poldhu about 3,500 km away. No automatic record was made, and historians doubt he really received it. He shared the 1909 Nobel Prize with Ferdinand Braun.
textes.En 1985, l'autorité américaine des téléc: In 1985, the US communications regulator opened the 2.4 GHz band to unlicensed use. NCR and AT&T created the precursor of Wi-Fi in 1991 in the Netherlands, for cash registers; the 802.11 standard came out in 1997. The name Wi-Fi was coined by a branding agency in 1999.
textes.On croyait la lumière portée par un « ét: Light was thought to be carried by an "aether". In 1887, in Cleveland, Albert Michelson and Edward Morley tried to measure the aether wind and found nothing: it has been called the most famous failed experiment in history.
textes.En 1801, Johann Ritter découvre au-delà: In 1801, Johann Ritter discovered invisible rays beyond violet that darken silver chloride; they were long called "chemical rays". Their effect on DNA was only established in 1960.
textes.En janvier 1935, le ministère britanniqu: In January 1935, the British Air Ministry asked whether a "death ray" was possible. Arnold Wilkins calculated that it was not, but suggested locating aircraft by radio: on 26 February 1935, at Daventry, a bomber was detected. In 1956, Robert Watson-Watt was stopped for speeding by a radar gun.
textes.Le 23 décembre 1947, Walter Brattain fai: On 23 December 1947, Walter Brattain demonstrated a germanium point-contact transistor that amplified speech. Julius Lilienfeld had filed a patent on the principle as early as 1925 in Canada, and Germans Mataré and Welker independently invented the "transistron" in 1948.
textes.Karl Ferdinand Braun découvre en 1874 qu: Karl Ferdinand Braun discovered in 1874 that a contact between a metal and a mineral lets current through in one direction only. John Ambrose Fleming patented the first vacuum diode on 16 November 1904, and William Eccles coined the word "diode" in 1919, from the Greek for "two paths".
textes.Henry Joseph Round, des laboratoires Mar: Henry Joseph Round, of the Marconi labs, saw a carborundum crystal emit light under voltage in 1906; Soviet inventor Oleg Losev built an LED in 1927. The first white LEDs went on sale in autumn 1996.
textes.L'ancêtre du condensateur est la bouteil: The ancestor of the capacitor is the Leyden jar, discovered on 11 October 1745 by Ewald von Kleist and then by Musschenbroek in Leiden. Abbé Nollet sent its discharge through 180 royal guards before Louis XV, and Franklin spoke of an "electrical battery" in 1749.
textes.William Shockley installe son laboratoir: William Shockley set up his laboratory in Mountain View in 1956 and preferred silicon to germanium. Journalist Don Hoefler popularised the phrase "Silicon Valley" on 11 January 1971, in the weekly Electronic News.
textes.En 1833, Faraday remarque que le sulfure: In 1833, Faraday noticed that silver sulfide conducts better when heated, unlike metals. The word Halbleiter, "semiconductor", appeared in 1910 in Josef Weiss's thesis.
textes.Nouvel employé de Texas Instruments, Jac: As a new Texas Instruments employee, Jack Kilby had no summer vacation in 1958: he spent it on the problem. On 12 September 1958, he showed his germanium circuit to management. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2000.
textes.Le premier microprocesseur, l'Intel 4004: The first microprocessor, the Intel 4004, came out on 15 November 1971 with 2,300 transistors. It had been ordered by Japan's Busicom for its calculators.
textes.L'ENIAC, construit à l'université de Pen: ENIAC, built at the University of Pennsylvania by John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert, was unveiled on 14 February 1946. It weighed 27 tonnes; several tubes burned out almost every day. Six women did most of its programming, long unrecognised.
textes.Dès 1903, l'Allemand Albert Hanson décri: As early as 1903, German Albert Hanson described flat conductors laminated to an insulating board. Austrian Paul Eisler invented the printed circuit around 1936 for a radio set; the United States used it on a large scale around 1943 for proximity fuzes.
textes.Willard Boyle et George Smith inventent: Willard Boyle and George Smith invented the CCD sensor in 1969 at Bell Labs, while looking for a new kind of memory. In 1975, Steven Sasson at Kodak built the first digital still camera from it, at 100 × 100 pixels. Boyle and Smith received the Nobel Prize in 2009.
textes.Vers 1893, AEG en Allemagne choisit le 5: Around 1893, AEG in Germany chose 50 Hz and Westinghouse in the United States 60 Hz, hence the world's two frequencies today.
textes.Pour discréditer l'alternatif, Harold Br: To discredit alternating current, Harold Brown electrocuted dogs in 1888 in public demonstrations, secretly linked to Edison's company. On 6 August 1890, the first electric chair execution, of William Kemmler, used alternating current: the first jolt did not kill him.
textes.Faraday enroule dès 1831 deux bobines su: Faraday wound two coils on an iron ring as early as 1831. Lucien Gaulard and John Gibbs showed a transformer in London in 1882 and in Turin in 1884; in 1885, Ganz engineers in Budapest patented the closed core, the basis of today's transformers.
textes.En 1890, la première ligne à haute tensi: In 1890, the first high-voltage alternating-current line linked Willamette Falls to Portland, Oregon. In 1891, the Lauffen-Frankfurt line ran about 175 km at 15,000 volts.
textes.Héron d'Alexandrie décrit déjà une roue: Hero of Alexandria already described a wind-driven wheel, and the windmills of Sistan in Iran were turning from the 7th century. In July 1887, Scotsman James Blyth lit his holiday home with the first electric wind turbine.
textes.Les cellules restent une curiosité jusqu: Cells remained a curiosity until 1954: Calvin Fuller, Daryl Chapin and Gerald Pearson presented the first practical cell at Bell Labs. The Vanguard I satellite carried some as early as 1958.
textes.Après le choc pétrolier de 1973, le Prem: After the 1973 oil crisis, Prime Minister Pierre Messmer announced a vast nuclear programme on 6 March 1974. France built 56 reactors in fifteen years; the very first had been commissioned at Marcoule from 1956.
textes.En 1878, à Cragside, en Angleterre, Will: In 1878, at Cragside in England, William Armstrong set up the first hydroelectric scheme, for a single arc lamp in his art gallery. Edison's first hydroelectric station started on 30 September 1882 in Appleton, Wisconsin.
textes.Stanley Whittingham invente le principe: Stanley Whittingham invented the principle at Exxon in 1974, but metallic lithium caught fire; John Goodenough and Koichi Mizushima found a better cathode in 1980, and Akira Yoshino the anode in 1985. Sony sold the first batteries in 1991.
textes.La première station de pompage date de 1: The first pumped-storage plant dates from 1907, in Switzerland, near Schaffhausen. In 2020, such plants accounted for about 95% of the world's electricity storage installations.
textes.La centrale de Pearl Street, à Manhattan: Pearl Street Station, in Manhattan, started on 4 September 1882 and supplied 400 lamps for 82 customers, in direct current at 110 volts. It burned down in 1890 and ran until 1895.
textes.Bien avant Leibniz, les trigrammes du Yi: Long before Leibniz, the trigrams of the Chinese I Ching (9th century BC) resemble binary numbers, and India's Pingala described metre with short and long syllables. Leibniz wrote his first text on binary in 1679.
textes.Le mot byte est inventé en juin 1956 par: The word byte was coined in June 1956 by Werner Buchholz at IBM, for the Stretch computer: he respelled bite as byte so it would not be confused with bit. The word "octet" unambiguously means 8 bits.
textes.George Boole, autodidacte qui enseigne d: George Boole, self-taught and teaching from age 16, published his algebraic logic in 1847 and then in The Laws of Thought in 1854. It is this algebra that Shannon applied to circuits.
textes.Babbage décrit sa machine en 1837 et ne: Babbage described his machine in 1837 and did not finish it, for lack of money and after a conflict with his engineer. His son Henry built a small part that, in 1910, calculated a list of multiples of pi... a wrong one. In 1991, London's Science Museum built his Difference Engine No. 2, which works.
textes.Le mot bug est bien plus ancien : Thomas: The word bug is much older: Thomas Edison used it in a letter of 13 November 1878 for an invention's little faults. The log book with the moth is kept at the National Museum of American History in Washington.
textes.Gordon Moore l'écrit en 1965 dans la rev: Gordon Moore wrote it in 1965 in Electronics magazine, under the title "Cramming more components onto integrated circuits". Caltech professor Carver Mead later popularised the name "Moore's law". The pace has slowed since around 2010.
textes.Le rapport de John von Neumann de 1945 s: John von Neumann's 1945 report built on the work of Eckert and Mauchly, but circulated under his name alone, which angered them. The first stored program ran on 21 June 1948, on the Manchester "Baby".
textes.La première vraie mémoire vive est le tu: The first true random-access memory was the Williams tube, which ran the Manchester "Baby"'s first program on 21 June 1948. Robert Dennard invented the one-transistor cell at IBM in 1966, and Intel sold the first such chip in 1970.
textes.Le mot bit, contraction de binary digit,: The word bit, short for binary digit, comes from a Bell Labs memo by John Tukey dated 9 January 1947. Claude Shannon took it up in his founding 1948 paper.
textes.Conçu par l'ingénieur des postes Tommy F: Designed by Post Office engineer Tommy Flowers, Colossus broke the German Lorenz cipher: the first message fell on 5 February 1944, and the Mark 2 was ready on 1 June 1944, just before D-Day. After the war, Flowers was ordered to burn the plans.
textes.Le mot « logiciel » est formé en 1969 pa: The word "logiciel" was formed in 1969 by the Délégation à l'informatique, in charge of the Plan Calcul, from "logique" and "matériel". The Académie française adopted it in 1972.
textes.En 1937, Claude Shannon montre dans son: In 1937, Claude Shannon showed in his MIT master's thesis that Boolean algebra and binary arithmetic can drive relays and switches: the basis of digital circuits.
textes.Une pile de Volta à l'eau salée donne en: A salt-water voltaic pile gives about 0.76 V per cell. What voltage do 6 stacked cells give, in volts?
textes.En série, les tensions s'additionnent :: In series, voltages add up: U = n × u = 6 × 0.76 = 4.56 V. This is the loop rule, stated by Gustav Kirchhoff in 1845: around a loop, the voltages balance out.
textes.Chaque cellule à saumure produit environ: Each brine cell produces about 0.76 V; a pile of six gives 4.56 V.

textes.Le cuivre peut être remplacé par de l'ar: Silver can replace the copper. It was later understood that the salt water takes part in the chemical reactions.

textes.En 1810. Le volt, unité de tension, port: In 1810. The volt, the unit of voltage, now bears his name.

textes.Une tension trop forte, jusqu'à 2 000 vo: Too high a voltage, up to 2,000 volts, damaged the insulation

textes.Quel instrument de William Thomson, le f: Which instrument of William Thomson, the future Lord Kelvin, helped read the cable's faint signals?
textes.Un instrument extrêmement sensible. Avec: An extremely sensitive instrument. With it, the 1866 cable carried 8 words a minute.
textes.Le galvanomètre à miroir de Thomson, trè: Thomson's very sensitive mirror galvanometer detected faint signals.
textes.Quel service le télégraphe transcontinen: Which service did the American transcontinental telegraph put an end to in 1861?

textes.Vers 47, à quoi le médecin romain Scribo: Around AD 47, what did the Roman physician Scribonius Largus use the torpedo for?

textes.En 1800, qu'a vu Alexander von Humboldt: In 1800, what did Alexander von Humboldt see in South America?
textes.Des chevaux poussés dans une mare pour é: Horses driven into a pond to exhaust the electric eels

textes.En 1800, Humboldt voit des pêcheurs pous: In 1800, Humboldt saw fishermen drive horses into the water to exhaust the electric eels.
textes.Combien d'espèces de poissons électrique: About how many species of electric fish are known?
textes.Quelque 350 espèces : torpilles, poisson: Some 350 species: torpedoes, catfish, electric eels, elephantfish… Many emit only weak signals to find their way.
textes.On compte quelque 350 espèces de poisson: There are some 350 species of electric fish; the electric organ evolved eight times.
textes.L'organe électrique n'est apparu qu'une: The electric organ appeared only once in the evolution of fish.
textes.Faux. Il est apparu huit fois, de façon: False. It appeared eight times, independently; four of these organs are powerful enough to deliver a shock.
textes.Sur quel objet égyptien voit-on déjà le: On which Egyptian object does the electric catfish already appear, around 3100 BC?
textes.Le poisson-chat électrique vit dans le N: The electric catfish lives in the Nile. The Egyptians painted it on their walls; in Arabic it would be called ra'ad, "thunder".

textes.Que veut dire ra'ad, le nom arabe du poi: What does ra'ad, the Arabic name of the electric catfish, mean?
textes.Au XIIe siècle, Abd al-Latif al-Baghdadi: In the 12th century, Abd al-Latif al-Baghdadi described its properties. The fish strikes like lightning, hence its name.
textes.En 1839, quel savant étudie une anguille: In 1839, which scientist studied an electric eel from Surinam?

textes.En 1839, Faraday étudie une anguille éle: In 1839, Faraday studied an electric eel from Surinam and confirmed that its discharges are electrical.
textes.De quel mot grec vient « électricité » ?: From which Greek word does "electricity" come?
textes.L'ambre frotté attire les brins de paill: Rubbed amber attracts bits of straw. In 1600, William Gilbert drew from it the Latin adjective electricus; the English electricity appeared in 1646.
textes.Le mot grec êlektron, l'ambre, a donné «: The Greek word ēlektron, amber, gave "electric" and "electricity".
textes.Thalès pensait que l'ambre frotté devena: Thales thought that rubbed amber became magnetic.
textes.Vrai, d'après des auteurs tardifs. Il co: True, according to later authors. He confused the two effects; it was static electricity.
textes.Thalès, vers 600 av. J.-C., attribuait à: Thales, around 600 BC, wrongly attributed the attraction of rubbed amber to magnetism.
textes.Les plus vieux morceaux ont environ 320: The oldest pieces are about 320 million years old; trapped insects are sometimes found in it.
textes.L'ambre est une résine d'arbre fossilisé: Amber is fossilised tree resin; the oldest pieces are about 320 million years old.
textes.Selon Aristote, pourquoi Thalès donnait-: According to Aristotle, why did Thales give the lodestone a soul?
textes.Parce qu'elle tombe du ciel: Because it falls from the sky
textes.Pour Thalès, « tout est plein de dieux »: For Thales, "all things are full of gods": what causes movement is alive, and what is alive has a soul.
textes.Selon Aristote, Thalès pensait que la pi: According to Aristotle, Thales thought the lodestone had a soul because it attracts iron.
textes.La foudre en serait la cause : en frappa: Lightning is thought to be the cause: striking the ground, it aligns the ore's magnetic domains. It is found mostly near the surface.
textes.La pierre d'aimant est de la magnétite a: Lodestone is naturally magnetised magnetite, probably by lightning.
textes.La pierre d'aimant aurait été aimantée p: Lodestone is thought to have been magnetised by lightning.
textes.Vrai, c'est la théorie principale ; elle: True, it is the leading theory; it explains why it is found near the surface.
textes.Quel est le plus ancien texte chinois qu: What is the oldest Chinese text that mentions magnetism?
textes.Puis, au IIe siècle av. J.-C., le Lüshi: Then, in the 2nd century BC, the Lüshi Chunqiu noted that the lodestone "makes iron come".
textes.Le Guiguzi, au IVe siècle av. J.-C., est: The Guiguzi, in the 4th century BC, is the oldest Chinese mention of magnetism.
textes.Comment Pline l'Ancien dit-il que les Sy: What does Pliny the Elder say Syrian women called amber?
textes.Parce qu'il attire les feuilles et la pa: Because it attracts leaves and straw. They made spindle whorls of it, the weights of spinning spindles.
textes.Pline rapporte qu'en Syrie l'ambre s'app: Pliny reports that in Syria amber was called harpax, because it attracts leaves and straw.
textes.Qui distingue, en 1550, peut-être pour l: Who distinguished in 1550, perhaps for the first time, the attraction of amber from that of the magnet?
textes.Dans son De subtilitate, le médecin et m: In his De subtilitate, the Italian physician and mathematician separated these two forces that Thales had confused.
textes.Cardan, dans De subtilitate (1550), dist: Cardano, in De subtilitate (1550), perhaps first distinguished electrical and magnetic forces.
textes.Le mot anglais electricity apparaît en 1: The English word electricity first appeared in 1646 in the work of:
textes.Dans sa Pseudodoxia Epidemica, un invent: In his Pseudodoxia Epidemica, an inventory of popular errors. Gilbert had coined the Latin electricus in 1600.
textes.Le premier usage du mot electricity est: The first use of the word electricity is ascribed to Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica, 1646.
textes.En 1088, comment Shen Kuo dit-il qu'on s: In 1088, how does Shen Kuo say the magnetised needle is hung?
textes.Les géomanciens frottent l'aiguille sur: Geomancers rub the needle on a lodestone then hang it up: it is the first incontestable mention of a magnetised needle.
textes.En 1088, Shen Kuo donne la première ment: In 1088, Shen Kuo gave the first incontestable mention of a magnetised needle.
textes.Sous quelle dynastie chinoise vivait She: Under which Chinese dynasty did Shen Kuo live?
textes.Né en 1031 à Hangzhou, il dirige le bure: Born in 1031 in Hangzhou, he headed the bureau of astronomy and the Hanlin Academy, before completing his Essays in 1088.
textes.Shen Kuo (1031-1095), savant et homme d': Shen Kuo (1031-1095), scholar and statesman of the Northern Song.
textes.Shen Kuo a remarqué que l'aiguille ne po: Shen Kuo noticed that the needle does not point exactly to true north or south.
textes.Vrai : il note un léger écart vers l'est: True: he noted a slight deviation to the east. It is magnetic declination, which varies with place and year.
textes.Shen Kuo note un léger écart de l'aiguil: Shen Kuo noted a slight deviation of the needle to the east: magnetic declination.
textes.Où trouve-t-on le premier usage attesté: Where is the first attested use of the compass at sea found?
textes.Dans ses Propos de table de Pingzhou : «: In his Pingzhou Table Talks: "in dark weather they look at the south-pointing needle".
textes.Zhu Yu, entre 1111 et 1117, atteste le p: Zhu Yu, between 1111 and 1117, attests the first use of the compass at sea.

textes.Vers 70-80, Wang Chong décrit une cuillè: Around 70-80, Wang Chong described a spoon that comes to rest pointing south.
textes.Que décrit le traité militaire Wujing Zo: What does the military treatise Wujing Zongyao describe, around 1044?
textes.Un poisson de fer qui flotte et montre l: An iron fish that floats and points south
textes.Le fer a été aimanté en le chauffant pui: The iron was magnetised by heating it then letting it cool: thermoremanence. It was used in the darkness of night.
textes.Le Wujing Zongyao (1040-1044) décrit un: The Wujing Zongyao (1040-1044) describes an iron fish magnetised by heat, floating on water.
textes.Vers quelle année l'Europe mentionne-t-e: Around what year does Europe first mention the compass, in Alexander Neckam?
textes.Un siècle après Shen Kuo. Neckam écrit q: A century after Shen Kuo. Neckam wrote that sailors touch the magnet with a needle, which starts to whirl.
textes.Alexander Neckam, De naturis rerum, vers: Alexander Neckam, De naturis rerum, around 1190: first European mention of the sailors' needle.
textes.Où se trouve la première mention de la b: Where is the first mention of the compass in the Muslim world, in 1232?
textes.Dans un recueil de contes persan: In a Persian book of tales
textes.Le Jawami ul-Hikayat. En 1282, au Caire,: The Jawami ul-Hikayat. In 1282, in Cairo, Baylak al-Qibjaqi would also describe a floating iron fish seen on a voyage to Alexandria.
textes.La plus ancienne mention de la boussole: The earliest reference to a compass in the Muslim world is in a Persian talebook of 1232.
textes.À quoi a d'abord servi la boussole en Ch: What was the compass first used for in China?
textes.À la géomancie, pour orienter tombes et: Geomancy, to orient tombs and houses

textes.En 1088, dans son jardin du « torrent de: In 1088, in his "Dream Brook" garden. A century before any European mention of the compass.
textes.Shen Kuo achève ses Écrits en 1088, dans: Shen Kuo completed his Essays in 1088, at his Dream Brook estate.
textes.En quelle année Pierre de Maricourt date: In what year did Peter of Maricourt date his Letter on the Magnet?

textes.Pôles semblables se repoussent, pôles co: Like poles repel, unlike poles attract: it is the first time a surviving text explains it.

textes.La lettre est adressée à Sygerus de Fouc: The letter is addressed to Sygerus of Foucaucourt, a Picard soldier.
textes.Toutes les copies de la lettre disent qu: All copies of the letter say it was written at the siege of Lucera.

textes.Une seule des 39 copies de la lettre la: Only one of the 39 copies of the letter places it at the siege of Lucera.
textes.Quelles boussoles décrit Pierre de Maric: Which compasses does Peter of Maricourt describe?

textes.Une boussole solaire et une boussole lun: A solar compass and a lunar compass

textes.La lettre décrit une boussole flottante: The letter describes a floating compass and a dry pivoted compass.
textes.Pour Pierre de Maricourt, vers quoi l'ai: For Peter of Maricourt, towards what does the magnet turn?
textes.Vers les pôles du ciel: Towards the poles of the sky
textes.Il se trompe : en 1600, William Gilbert: He was wrong: in 1600, William Gilbert would understand that it is the Earth that is a magnet.

textes.Où la Lettre sur l'aimant est-elle impri: Where was the Letter on the Magnet first printed, in 1558?
textes.Par Achilles Gasser. En 1562, Jean Taisn: By Achilles Gasser. In 1562, Jean Taisnier copied it without credit.
textes.Première édition imprimée : Augsbourg, 1: First printed edition: Augsburg, 1558, by Achilles Gasser.
textes.Quel savant reconnaît en 1600 sa dette e: Which scholar acknowledged his debt to Peter of Maricourt in 1600?

textes.Selon Pierre de Maricourt, on peut inver: According to Peter of Maricourt, the magnetisation of an already magnetised piece of iron can be reversed.

textes.Comment Gilbert appelle-t-il sa boule ta: What did Gilbert call his ball carved from lodestone?

textes.Gilbert montre avec sa terrella que la T: Gilbert showed with his terrella that the Earth is a magnet.
textes.Quel mot latin Gilbert forge-t-il d'aprè: Which Latin word did Gilbert coin from the Greek ēlektron?
textes.Electricus, « comme l'ambre ». Le mot an: Electricus, "like amber". The English word electricity followed in 1646, in Thomas Browne.
textes.Gilbert forge le latin electricus, « com: Gilbert coined the Latin electricus, "like amber", from the Greek ēlektron.
textes.Une aiguille sur pivot qui tourne vers u: A pivoted needle that turns towards a rubbed object
textes.C'est le premier instrument de mesure él: It is the first electrical measuring instrument. The needle, of any metal, responds to rubbed amber.
textes.Le versorium de Gilbert est considéré co: Gilbert's versorium is regarded as the first electrical measuring instrument.
textes.Gilbert a montré que seul l'ambre devien: Gilbert showed that only amber becomes electric when rubbed.

textes.Gilbert jugeait électricité et magnétism: Gilbert judged electricity and magnetism different; Ørsted and Maxwell showed the opposite.
textes.Il la soigne jusqu'à sa mort en 1603, et: He treated her until her death in 1603, and James I reappointed him. Gilbert himself died the same year.
textes.Gilbert est médecin d'Élisabeth Ire de 1: Gilbert was physician to Elizabeth I from 1601 until her death in 1603.
textes.Selon De Magnete, comment varie l'inclin: According to De Magnete, how does a magnetised needle's dip vary?
textes.À plat à l'équateur, elle plonge de plus: Flat at the equator, it plunges more and more towards the poles
textes.Elle plonge à l'équateur et reste à plat: It plunges at the equator and stays flat at the poles
textes.Elle change avec les saisons seulement: It changes only with the seasons
textes.Gilbert décrit même un instrument pour l: Gilbert even described an instrument to measure it. That is what the needle does on the terrella, and on the Earth.
textes.L'inclinaison est nulle à l'équateur et: Dip is zero at the equator and increases towards the poles; Gilbert described an instrument to measure it.
textes.Dans quelle langue De Magnete est-il écr: In which language is De Magnete written?
textes.La langue savante de l'époque. Il n'est: The scholarly language of the time. It was translated into English only in 1893, by Paul Fleury Mottelay.
textes.De Magnete est écrit en latin ; traducti: De Magnete is written in Latin; English translation by Mottelay in 1893.
textes.De Magnete prend aussi parti pour la rot: De Magnete also argues for the Earth's rotation.
textes.Vrai. Le dernier livre défend la rotatio: True. The last book defends the Earth's rotation and the Copernican system, twenty years before Galileo's troubles.
textes.De Magnete traite de la rotation terrest: De Magnete deals with the Earth's rotation and supports the Copernican system.
textes.Qui fait le premier, en octobre 1745, l': Who first did, in October 1745, the experiment of the bottle that keeps electricity?
textes.Un clerc allemand, avec une bouteille d': A German cleric, with a bottle of alcohol pierced by a nail. Musschenbroek and Cunaeus got there independently at Leiden.
textes.La bouteille de Leyde, inventée en 1745-: The Leyden jar, invented in 1745-1746, is the first capacitor.
textes.Qui donne son nom à la bouteille de Leyd: Who gave the Leyden jar its name?
textes.Nollet la nomme d'après Leyde, où travai: Nollet named it after Leiden, where Musschenbroek worked, and made it a court show.
textes.Nollet fait passer la décharge d'une bou: Nollet sent a jar's discharge through 180 guards before Louis XV.
textes.À travers combien de gardes du roi Nolle: Through how many royal guards did Nollet send the discharge before Louis XV?
textes.180 gardes se tenant par la main. Il rec: 180 guards holding hands. He then did it again with monks, about 200, in 1746.
textes.Dans une bouteille de Leyde, où la charg: In a Leyden jar, where is the charge stored, according to Franklin?
textes.Le verre isolant sépare deux armatures d: The insulating glass separates two metal coatings: that is the principle of every capacitor.
textes.Franklin conclut que la charge est stock: Franklin concluded that the charge was stored in the glass, not the water.
textes.La bouteille de Leyde est un ancêtre du: The Leyden jar is an ancestor of the capacitor.
textes.Vrai : deux conducteurs, les feuilles de: True: two conductors, the metal foils, separated by an insulator, the glass.
textes.Qu'a montré Stephen Gray en 1729 ?: What did Stephen Gray show in 1729?
textes.Que l'électricité peut voyager le long d: That electricity can travel along a thread
textes.Que la Terre est un aimant: That the Earth is a magnet
textes.Avec Granville Wheler, il la fait courir: With Granville Wheler, he sent it along 800 feet of thread. Hence the distinction between conductors and insulators.
textes.En 1729, Stephen Gray montre que l'élect: In 1729, Stephen Gray showed that electricity is conducted through metals and along a thread.
textes.Quelle récompense Stephen Gray reçoit-il: Which award did Stephen Gray receive first, in 1731?
textes.La toute première médaille Copley de la: The very first Copley Medal of the Royal Society, for his work on conduction and insulation.
textes.Gray reçoit la première médaille Copley: Gray received the first Copley Medal in 1731.
textes.Comment du Fay appelle-t-il en 1733 les: What did du Fay call the two kinds of electricity in 1733?
textes.Deux fluides qui se neutralisent quand o: Two fluids that neutralise each other when combined. Franklin would rename them positive and negative.
textes.Du Fay, en 1733, distingue deux électric: Du Fay, in 1733, distinguished two electricities, vitreous and resinous.
textes.Environ combien de moines Nollet relie-t: About how many monks did Nollet link in 1746 to measure the speed of electricity?
textes.Environ 200, sur un cercle d'un mille de: About 200, in a circle a mile round: they all reacted almost at once.
textes.En 1746, Nollet relie environ 200 moines: In 1746, Nollet linked about 200 monks in a circle about a mile round.
textes.Musschenbroek et Cunaeus ont compris qu': Musschenbroek and Cunaeus understood that the bottle had to be held in the hand while charging.
textes.Vrai. Plus tard, William Watson garnira: True. Later, William Watson lined the jar with metal foil inside and out, and dropped the water.
textes.Qui fait voler le cerf-volant avec Frank: Who flew the kite with Franklin in June 1752?
textes.Une clé de métal est attachée à la ficel: A metal key is tied to the string, and Franklin holds a silk cord that insulates him.
textes.En juin 1752, Franklin et son fils Willi: In June 1752, Franklin and his son William flew a kite fitted with a key and charged a Leyden jar.
textes.Le cerf-volant de Franklin a été frappé: Franklin's kite was struck by lightning.
textes.Faux. La charge a été induite par un nua: False. The charge was induced by a nearby charged cloud. A real lightning strike would probably have killed him.
textes.Le cerf-volant de Franklin n'a pas été f: Franklin's kite was not struck by lightning; the charge was induced by a nearby cloud.
textes.Qui réussit le premier, en mai 1752 en F: Who first succeeded, in May 1752 in France, with the rod experiment proposed by Franklin?
textes.À Marly-la-Ville, un mois avant le cerf-: At Marly-la-Ville, a month before the Philadelphia kite.
textes.Dalibard réalise une expérience de la ti: Dalibard performed a rod experiment at Marly-la-Ville in May 1752.
textes.Quels noms Franklin donne-t-il aux deux: What names did Franklin give the two kinds of charge?
textes.Avant lui, on parlait d'électricité vitr: Before him, people spoke of vitreous and resinous electricity. For Franklin, it is one fluid, in excess or in deficit.
textes.Franklin est le premier à nommer positiv: Franklin was the first to name the two kinds of charge positive and negative.
textes.Franklin a découvert le principe de cons: Franklin discovered the principle of conservation of charge.
textes.Vrai : on ne crée pas de charge, on la d: True: charge is not created, it is moved; what one body gains, another loses.
textes.Qui meurt en 1753 à Saint-Pétersbourg en: Who died in 1753 in Saint Petersburg while repeating the lightning experiment?
textes.En août 1753, apparemment frappé par une: In August 1753, apparently struck by ball lightning. Franklin's experiment was no game.
textes.Georg Wilhelm Richmann est tué à Saint-P: Georg Wilhelm Richmann was killed in Saint Petersburg in August 1753.
textes.Sur quels bâtiments pose-t-on des parato: On which buildings were lightning rods installed in 1752?
textes.L'Académie de Philadelphie et le Capitol: The Academy of Philadelphia and the Pennsylvania State House
textes.Après des essais sur la maison de Frankl: After trials on Franklin's house. The point connected to the ground conducts lightning harmlessly.
textes.En 1752, des paratonnerres sont installé: In 1752, lightning rods were installed on the Academy of Philadelphia and the Pennsylvania State House.
textes.En quelle année la Royal Society décerne: In what year did the Royal Society award Franklin the Copley Medal?
textes.En 1753. Elle l'élit membre en 1756, hon: In 1753. It elected him a fellow in 1756, a rare honour for an 18th-century American.
textes.Franklin reçoit la médaille Copley en 17: Franklin received the Copley Medal in 1753 and became a fellow of the Royal Society in 1756.
textes.D'où vient le récit détaillé de l'expéri: Where does the detailed account of the kite experiment come from?
textes.D'une lettre de William Franklin: From a letter by William Franklin
textes.Franklin n'a publié qu'une courte lettre: Franklin published only a short letter in the Pennsylvania Gazette, on 19 October 1752, without saying in what circumstances he had done it.
textes.Le récit de Priestley paraît en 1767 ; l: Priestley's account appeared in 1767; Franklin's letter in the Pennsylvania Gazette dates from 19 October 1752.
textes.À qui Franklin écrit-il les lettres qui: To whom did Franklin write the letters that became the 1751 book?
textes.Collinson les transmet à la Royal Societ: Collinson passed them on to the Royal Society. The book, Experiments and Observations on Electricity, went through five editions.
textes.Experiments and Observations on Electric: Experiments and Observations on Electricity (1751) gathers Franklin's letters to Peter Collinson.
textes.Deux charges se repoussent avec une forc: Two charges repel with a force of 36 N. The distance between them is tripled. What is the new force, in newtons?
textes.Loi de Coulomb : F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r². S: Coulomb's law: F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r². If r is multiplied by 3, r² is multiplied by 3 × 3 = 9, so F is divided by 9: F = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 N. Charles-Augustin Coulomb published this law in 1785, measured with his torsion balance.
textes.La force électrique varie comme l'invers: The electric force varies as the inverse square of the distance (Coulomb, 1785).
textes.Deux charges s'attirent avec une force d: Two charges attract with a force of 5 N. One of the two charges is doubled, without changing the distance. What is the new force, in newtons?
textes.Loi de Coulomb : F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r². L: Coulomb's law: F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r². The force is proportional to the product of the charges: if q₁ doubles, F doubles. F = 5 × 2 = 10 N. Law published by Coulomb in 1785.
textes.Avec F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r² et k = 9 × 10⁹: With F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r² and k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C², what force, in newtons, acts between two charges of 1 microcoulomb (10⁻⁶ C) placed 1 m apart?
textes.Loi de Coulomb : F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r² =: Coulomb's law: F = k × q₁ × q₂ ÷ r² = 9 × 10⁹ × 10⁻⁶ × 10⁻⁶ ÷ 1² = 9 × 10⁻³ = 0.009 N. Less than a hundredth of a newton: hence Coulomb's very sensitive torsion balance (1785).
textes.La constante de Coulomb vaut k = 1/(4π ε: Coulomb's constant is k = 1/(4π ε₀) ≈ 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C², with ε₀ ≈ 8.854 × 10⁻¹² F/m.
textes.Quel instrument Coulomb invente-t-il pou: What instrument did Coulomb invent to measure the electric force?
textes.Une barre suspendue à un fil fin : l'ang: A bar hung from a thin wire: the angle by which the wire twists measures the force between two charged balls.
textes.Coulomb utilise une balance de torsion d: Coulomb used a torsion balance of his own invention, designed for very weak forces.
textes.Où Coulomb a-t-il passé huit ans à const: Where did Coulomb spend eight years building a fort?
textes.Le fort Bourbon, de 1764 à 1772. Il étai: Fort Bourbon, from 1764 to 1772. He was a military engineer before being a physicist.
textes.Coulomb a dirigé la construction du fort: Coulomb directed the building of Fort Bourbon in Martinique from 1764 to 1772.
textes.Comme la gravitation, la force électriqu: Like gravitation, the electric force only attracts.
textes.Faux. Les deux forces suivent l'inverse: False. Both forces follow the inverse square, but the electric force attracts or repels depending on the signs of the charges.
textes.La gravitation attire toujours ; la forc: Gravitation always attracts; the electrostatic force can attract or repel.
textes.Qui avait trouvé l'inverse du carré avan: Who had found the inverse square before Coulomb, without ever publishing it?
textes.Au début des années 1770. Priestley l'av: In the early 1770s. Priestley had conjectured it in 1767, Robison roughly measured it in 1769.
textes.Cavendish a établi la même relation au d: Cavendish worked out the same relationship in the early 1770s without publishing it.
textes.En quelle unité mesure-t-on une charge é: In what unit is electric charge measured?
The unit was named after Coulomb in 1880. An electron carries a charge of about 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulomb.
textes.Le coulomb, unité SI de charge électriqu: The coulomb, SI unit of electric charge, was named after Coulomb in 1880.
textes.Depuis 2019, la charge de l'électron est: Since 2019, the charge of the electron is a value fixed exactly by definition.
textes.Vrai : e = 1,602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C exactem: True: e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C exactly. Before, it was a measured quantity; Millikan had measured it in 1909.
textes.Depuis la révision du SI de 2019, e vaut: Since the 2019 SI revision, e is exactly 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
textes.Sur quel monument le nom de Coulomb est-: On which monument is Coulomb's name engraved, among 72 scientists?
textes.Gustave Eiffel y a fait graver 72 noms d: Gustave Eiffel had 72 names of French scientists and engineers engraved on it.
textes.Le nom de Coulomb est l'un des 72 noms g: Coulomb's name is one of the 72 names inscribed on the Eiffel Tower.
textes.Comment Thomson appelle-t-il d'abord les: What did Thomson first call the particles he discovered in 1897?
textes.Le nom d'électron, proposé par Stoney en: The name electron, proposed by Stoney in 1891, would eventually prevail.
textes.Le 30 avril 1897, Thomson annonce que le: On 30 April 1897, Thomson announced that cathode rays are particles more than a thousand times lighter than hydrogen.
textes.D'où vient le mot « électron » ?: Where does the word "electron" come from?
textes.Du grec pour l'ambre, comme électricité: From the Greek for amber, like electricity
textes.George Stoney le propose en 1891 pour l': George Stoney proposed it in 1891 for the unit of electric charge, combining "electric" and "ion".
textes.Stoney propose « électron » en 1891 ; le: Stoney proposed "electron" in 1891; the word derives from the Greek for amber.
textes.Environ combien de fois un électron est-: About how many times lighter than a proton is an electron?
textes.Environ 1 836 fois. Thomson, en 1897, l': About 1,836 times. Thomson, in 1897, already estimated it at more than a thousand times lighter than a hydrogen atom.
textes.La masse de l'électron vaut environ 1/18: The electron's mass is about 1/1836 of the proton's.
textes.En 1937, le fils de J. J. Thomson a reçu: In 1937, J. J. Thomson's son received the Nobel for showing that the electron behaves like a wave.
textes.Vrai : George Paget Thomson, pour la dif: True: George Paget Thomson, for electron diffraction. The father showed a particle, the son a wave.
textes.George Paget Thomson partage le Nobel de: George Paget Thomson shared the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physics for electron diffraction.
textes.Dans quelle ville Jagadish Chandra Bose: In which city did Jagadish Chandra Bose give his microwave demonstration in 1895?
textes.Au Town Hall : les ondes traversent deux: At the Town Hall: the waves crossed two walls over 23 metres, rang a bell and ignited gunpowder.
textes.En 1895, Bose envoie des micro-ondes à t: In 1895, Bose sent microwaves through two walls, in Calcutta, to ring a bell.
textes.Bose a été le premier à détecter des ond: Bose was the first to detect radio waves with a semiconductor junction.
textes.Vrai. Il travaillait avec des ondes d'en: True. He worked with waves of about 5 millimetres, up to 60 GHz, and declined to patent most of his work.
textes.Bose est le premier à utiliser une jonct: Bose was the first to use a semiconductor junction to detect radio waves.
textes.Quelle lettre Marconi dit-il avoir reçue: Which letter did Marconi say he received across the Atlantic on 12 December 1901?
textes.Envoyée de Poldhu, en Cornouailles, et r: Sent from Poldhu, Cornwall, and received at Signal Hill, Newfoundland. Without a recording, the reception remains debated.
textes.Le 12 décembre 1901, Marconi dit recevoi: On 12 December 1901, Marconi said he received at Signal Hill the letter S sent from Poldhu.
textes.Avec qui Marconi partage-t-il le prix No: With whom did Marconi share the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1909?
textes.Pour leurs contributions à la télégraphi: For their contributions to wireless telegraphy. Hertz had died in 1894.
textes.Marconi partage le Nobel de physique 190: Marconi shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics with Ferdinand Braun, for wireless telegraphy.
textes.Que fait la valve de Fleming, brevetée e: What does Fleming's valve, patented in 1904, do?
textes.Elle ne laisse passer le courant que dan: It lets current through in one direction only
textes.C'est la première diode à tube à vide, u: It is the first vacuum-tube diode, used as a radio detector. In 1906, de Forest added a grid: the audion amplifies.
textes.La valve de Fleming (16 novembre 1904) e: Fleming's valve (16 November 1904) is the first thermionic diode; De Forest's audion (1906) amplifies.
textes.Quel hommage les émetteurs radio du mond: What tribute did the world's radio transmitters pay Marconi at his death, in 1937?
textes.À 18 heures, le jour de ses funérailles: At 6 pm, on the day of his funeral: the airwaves fell silent for the man who had put them to work.
textes.Les émetteurs du monde observent deux mi: Transmitters around the world observed two minutes of silence on the day of Marconi's funeral.
textes.À quelle température, en kelvins, la rés: At what temperature, in kelvins, did mercury's resistance vanish in 1911?
textes.Vers 4,2 K, soit environ −269 °C. Pour y: At about 4.2 K, some −269 °C. Getting there required liquid helium, which Kamerlingh Onnes had been the first to obtain in 1908.
textes.Le 8 avril 1911, Kamerlingh Onnes voit l: On 8 April 1911, Kamerlingh Onnes saw mercury's resistance vanish at 4.2 K.
textes.Dans quelle ville Kamerlingh Onnes décou: In which city did Kamerlingh Onnes discover superconductivity?
textes.Dans le laboratoire du froid qu'il y a f: In the cryogenics laboratory he founded there in 1904. Leiden had already given its name to the jar of 1745.
textes.Un supraconducteur a une résistance élec: A superconductor has exactly zero electrical resistance.
textes.Vrai. Dans une boucle supraconductrice,: True. In a superconducting loop, a current can flow without a power source: a Belgian gravimeter kept its currents for about 28 years.
textes.Sous sa température critique, un supraco: Below its critical temperature, a superconductor has exactly zero resistance; a current can flow indefinitely.
textes.Que découvrent Meissner et Ochsenfeld en: What did Meissner and Ochsenfeld discover in 1933?
textes.Qu'un supraconducteur chasse le champ ma: That a superconductor expels magnetic fields
textes.C'est l'effet Meissner. L'explication co: This is the Meissner effect. The full explanation would wait for BCS theory, in 1957.
textes.En 1933, Meissner et Ochsenfeld montrent: In 1933, Meissner and Ochsenfeld showed that superconductors expel applied magnetic fields.
textes.Selon la théorie BCS de 1957, comment le: According to the 1957 BCS theory, how do electrons cross a superconductor?
textes.Bardeen, Cooper et Schrieffer reçoivent: Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer received the Nobel in 1972. It was Bardeen's second, after the transistor.
textes.La théorie BCS (1957) décrit le courant: BCS theory (1957) describes the current as a flow of bound electron pairs, Cooper pairs; Nobel 1972.
textes.À quelle température, en kelvins, l'azot: At what temperature, in kelvins, does liquid nitrogen boil?
textes.77 K, environ −196 °C. Depuis 1987, des: 77 K, about −196 °C. Since 1987, ceramics have been superconducting above it, at about 92 K: they can be cooled with a cheap liquid.
textes.La céramique à l'yttrium (YBCO) est supr: The yttrium ceramic (YBCO) is superconducting at about 92 K, above liquid nitrogen's 77 K.
textes.Quelle est la couleur de la lumière du p: What colour was the light of the first laser, in 1960?
textes.Un cristal de rubis éclairé par une lamp: A ruby crystal lit by a flash lamp emits at 694 nanometres, in the red.
textes.Le 16 mai 1960, Maiman fait fonctionner: On 16 May 1960, Maiman operated the first laser, a ruby one, at Hughes laboratories.
textes.Que signifie l'acronyme laser ?: What does the acronym laser stand for?
textes.Amplification de lumière par émission st: Light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation
textes.Lumière artificielle à source électrique: Light artificially sourced from red electricity
textes.Lampe à rayon émis sans réflexion: Lamp with ray emitted without reflection
textes.Lentille amplifiant la source d'énergie: Lens amplifying the source of radiant energy
textes.Light amplification by stimulated emissi: Gordon Gould wrote the word in a notebook in 1957 and published it in 1959.
textes.LASER : light amplification by stimulate: LASER: light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation; Gould published the acronym in 1959.
textes.Qui pose dès 1917 la théorie de l'émissi: Who laid down in 1917 the theory of stimulated emission, the basis of the laser?
textes.Quarante-trois ans avant le premier lase: Forty-three years before the first laser. Townes's maser, in 1953, first applied it to microwaves.
textes.Les travaux d'Einstein de 1917 posent la: Einstein's 1917 work laid the theoretical foundation of stimulated emission.
textes.Comment surnomme-t-on le laser à sa nais: What was the laser nicknamed at its birth?
textes.Les applications sont venues ensuite : l: The applications came later: supermarket barcodes in 1974, compact disc players in 1982.
textes.{comp}. Franklin envoyait un cerf-volant: {comp}. Franklin flew a kite into a storm, or so he said. I'm sending you a question. It's less dangerous.
textes.Électricité. Faraday a quitté l'école à: Electricity. Faraday left school at 13 and discovered induction. You have no excuse left: {comp}.
textes.Volta empilait le zinc et le cuivre. J'e: Volta stacked zinc and copper. I stack questions: {comp}.
textes.Juste. Le courant passe entre nous. Ohm: Right. There's a current between us. Ohm would measure a very low resistance.
textes.Bonne réponse. Tesla dirait qu'il l'avai: Correct. Tesla would say he found it before you. He said that about everything.
textes.Correct. Faraday aurait fait une confére: Correct. Faraday would have given a Christmas lecture about you, for the children.
textes.Étincelant. Ne vous habituez pas à la lu: Sparkling. Don't get used to the light.
textes.Raté. Galvani croyait à l'électricité an: Missed. Galvani believed in animal electricity. You believe in your answer. Same result.
textes.Faux. Edison a essayé des milliers de ma: Wrong. Edison tried thousands of materials before the right filament. You're allowed a few more tries.
textes.Erreur. Franklin s'est assommé en voulan: Error. Franklin knocked himself out trying to electrocute a turkey. You knocked yourself out all on your own.
textes.Court-circuit. Je coupe le courant à vot: Short circuit. I'm cutting the power to your pride.
textes.Fils de forgeron, apprenti relieur, il a: A blacksmith's son, apprenticed to a bookbinder, he learned science by reading the books he bound. He discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831. To a minister who asked what electricity was good for: “One day, sir, you may tax it.” The retort is probably made up.
textes.Fille de Byron, elle écrit en 1843 le pr: Byron's daughter, she wrote the first published program in 1843, for Babbage's Analytical Engine, and foresaw that a machine might compose music. Her mother had raised her on mathematics to protect her from the “madness” she attributed to her father.
textes.Haut fonctionnaire de la dynastie Song,: A high official of the Song dynasty, he noted in 1088 that a magnetized needle does not point exactly north: the first known description of magnetic declination. He also described Bi Sheng's movable-type printing and the formation of fossils.
textes.En 1921, sur le bateau du retour, il se: In 1921, on the ship home, he wonders why the sea is blue. In Calcutta, he discovers that a small part of the light scattered by molecules changes color: the Raman effect. Nobel Prize 1930; he had booked his trip to Stockholm months before the announcement.
textes.Professeur de lycée à Cologne, il publie: A secondary-school teacher in Cologne, he published his law in 1827 after months of measurements. In Germany, the reception was cold; he left his post. It took the Royal Society of London awarding him the Copley Medal in 1841 for his country to take him seriously.
textes.Coinventeur du transistor en 1947, il es: Co-inventor of the transistor in 1947, he is the only person to have received the Nobel Prize in physics twice. In 1956, he brought only one of his three children to Stockholm. The King of Sweden chided him; he promised to come back with all of them. In 1972, he did, with all three.
textes.Son moteur à courant alternatif l'emport: His alternating-current motor beat Edison's direct current in the “war of the currents”: our grids come from it. He also promised wireless power and a death ray, never built. He died alone and in debt in a New York hotel room, where he looked after pigeons.
textes.Maîtriser la puissance électrique. Comme: Master electric power. Like Edison, you didn't invent everything.
textes.Edison n'a pas inventé l'ampoule. Humphr: Edison did not invent the light bulb. Humphry Davy, Warren de la Rue and Joseph Swan came before him. His contribution, in 1879, was a long-lasting carbon filament and above all the whole system to produce and distribute the current.
textes.Maîtriser les charges et les circuits. A: Master charges and circuits. No frogs were harmed. This time.
textes.Dans les années 1780, Luigi Galvani voit: In the 1780s, Luigi Galvani sees frogs' legs twitch on contact with two metals. He believes in an “animal electricity”. Volta disagrees and, to prove it, invents the battery.
textes.Maîtriser la loi d'Ohm. Vous l'avez mieu: Master Ohm's law. You received it better than his contemporaries.
textes.Georg Ohm publie sa loi en 1827. Elle es: Georg Ohm published his law in 1827. It got a cold reception in Germany, and Ohm had to leave his teaching post. Recognition came from London, with the Royal Society's Copley Medal in 1841.
textes.Maîtriser le magnétisme. Le nord n'est p: Master magnetism. North isn't quite the same anymore.
textes.En 1820, Hans Christian Ørsted remarque: In 1820, Hans Christian Ørsted notices that a wire carrying a current deflects a magnetized needle. Electricity and magnetism would never again be two separate disciplines.
textes.Maîtriser le premier losange d'Étincelle: Master the first diamond of Spark.
textes.L'expérience du cerf-volant de Franklin: Franklin's kite experiment (1752) is only known in detail through an account published fifteen years later by Joseph Priestley. In 1753, Georg Richmann, who was reproducing this kind of experiment in Saint Petersburg, was killed by lightning.
textes.Maîtriser 6 compétences. L'arbre de l'Él: Master 6 skills. The Electricity tree opens.
textes.En 1825, Michael Faraday lance à la Roya: In 1825, Michael Faraday launched Christmas lectures for children at the Royal Institution. He gave nineteen series himself. They have been held every year since, except during World War II.
Master electromagnetic waves. Don't stand in front of the magnetron.
textes.En 1945, l'ingénieur Percy Spencer trava: In 1945, engineer Percy Spencer is working on radar magnetrons at Raytheon and notices that a chocolate bar has melted in his pocket. He tries corn, which pops. The first microwave oven, in 1947, is almost two meters tall and weighs 340 kilos.
textes.Maîtriser l'électronique. Le mot « bug »: Master electronics. The word “bug” is older than computing.
textes.Le 9 septembre 1947, l'équipe du calcula: On September 9, 1947, the team of the Harvard Mark II calculator taped into its log a moth found in a relay: “First actual case of bug being found”. The joke works because the word already existed: Edison spoke of “bugs” in his inventions as early as 1878.
textes.Maîtriser le réseau et les énergies. La: Master the grid and energy. The war of the currents has enough real horrors.
textes.On attribue à Edison l'électrocution de: Edison is credited with electrocuting the elephant Topsy to discredit alternating current. It happened in 1903 at Coney Island, ten years after the war of the currents ended, and Edison had nothing to do with it. His company merely filmed the scene.
Master from transistor to computer. You surely have more than five at home.
textes.« Je pense qu'il y a un marché mondial p: “I think there is a world market for maybe five computers.” The line is attributed to Thomas Watson, head of IBM, in 1943. Nobody has ever found it in a document from the time. The most famous failed predictions are often made up.
textes.Réussir trois quiz d'Étincelle sans faut: Pass three Spark quizzes without a mistake. You're right. The current, though, flows backwards.
textes.Vers 1747, Benjamin Franklin nomme « pos: Around 1747, Benjamin Franklin named the two kinds of electricity “positive” and “negative”, guessing which way the fluid flows. He had a fifty-fifty chance and got it wrong: electrons, discovered in 1897, go the other way. Conventional current keeps his choice.
textes.Maîtriser Kirchhoff et les circuits. Tou: Master Kirchhoff and circuits. Everything that goes in comes out. Except your credits: they come to me.
textes.Gustav Kirchhoff était encore étudiant,: Gustav Kirchhoff was still a student, in 1845, when he formulated his two circuit laws, for an exercise in Franz Neumann's seminar at Königsberg. The work became his thesis.
textes.Maîtriser le télégraphe. Seize heures po: Master the telegraph. Sixteen hours for 98 words: you read faster than the 1858 cable. Barely.
textes.En 1858, le message de la reine Victoria: In 1858, Queen Victoria's message to President Buchanan, 98 words, took 16 hours to cross the Atlantic. Three weeks later, the cable died, fried by 2,000 volts. The 1866 one would carry 8 words a minute.
textes.Maîtriser les poissons électriques. Sans: Master electric fish. Without dipping a hand in. The AI has never had a hand.
textes.En 1800, Alexander von Humboldt accompag: In 1800, Alexander von Humboldt went with indigenous fishermen in South America. To catch electric eels, they drove about thirty horses into a pond: the fish attacked and wore themselves out. Two horses, stunned, drowned; the tired eels were caught with harpoons.
Master amber and lodestone. Thales gave pebbles a soul; the AI grants you one, provisionally.
textes.Selon Aristote, Thalès disait que « tout: According to Aristotle, Thales said that "all things are full of gods": the lodestone has a soul, since it makes iron move. The same Thales is also said, by later authors, to have rubbed amber to attract straw.
textes.Maîtriser la boussole chinoise. Elle mon: Master the Chinese compass. It points south. You had it all upside down too.
In China, the compass "points south". Around 1044, the Wujing Zongyao describes an iron fish floated on a bowl of water; it was magnetised by heating it and letting it cool in the right direction.
textes.Maîtriser Pierre de Maricourt. Sa roue d: Master Peter of Maricourt. His wheel was supposed to turn forever. So is your progress, apparently.
textes.Dans sa Lettre sur l'aimant de 1269, Pie: In his Letter on the Magnet of 1269, Peter of Maricourt proposed a toothed wheel that a magnet would turn forever, by attracting then repelling its teeth. It never turned.
textes.Maîtriser Gilbert et le De Magnete. Vous: Master Gilbert and De Magnete. You hold the Earth in your hand. Don't drop it.
textes.La terrella de Gilbert est une boule tai: Gilbert's terrella is a ball carved from lodestone. A needle placed on it behaves like a compass on Earth: it stays flat at the equator and plunges towards the poles. Hence his conclusion of 1600: the Earth is a magnet.
textes.Maîtriser la bouteille de Leyde. 180 gar: Master the Leyden jar. 180 guards jumped before you. You just clicked.
textes.Devant Louis XV, l'abbé Nollet fait pass: Before Louis XV, Abbé Nollet sent the discharge of a Leyden jar through 180 royal guards holding hands. Then he did it again with monks, even more of them.
textes.Maîtriser Franklin et la foudre. Vous av: Master Franklin and lightning. You survived the experiment. Richmann did not.
textes.En août 1753, à Saint-Pétersbourg, Georg: In August 1753, in Saint Petersburg, Georg Wilhelm Richmann repeated the lightning experiment and died, apparently struck by ball lightning. Franklin had never seen his kite struck: the charge came from a nearby cloud.
textes.Maîtriser Coulomb et sa balance. Il a co: Master Coulomb and his balance. He built a fort before weighing charges. You just weighed your words.
textes.Avant d'être physicien, Coulomb est offi: Before being a physicist, Coulomb was a military engineer. Sent to Martinique, he directed the building of the new Fort Bourbon, a project that kept him there from 1764 to 1772. His law of electricity came only in 1785.
textes.Maîtriser l'électron et la radio. Pour u: Master the electron and radio. For once, the AI is quiet. Enjoy it, it won't last two minutes.
textes.À la mort de Guglielmo Marconi, en 1937,: At Guglielmo Marconi's death, in 1937, radio transmitters around the world observed two minutes of silence, at 6 pm, on the day of his funeral.
textes.Maîtriser les supraconducteurs et le las: Master superconductors and the laser. You are a solution. The AI is still looking for the problem.
textes.Le premier laser, en 1960, fut surnommé: The first laser, in 1960, was nicknamed "a solution looking for a problem". The problems came: barcodes in 1974, compact discs in 1982.
textes.L'os d'Ishango, trouvé en 1950 au Congo,: The Ishango bone, found in 1950 in the Congo, is a bone covered in notches arranged in groups, so worked that no one can tell which animal it came from. Some read prime numbers or a lunar calendar in it; others, more cautious, a simple counting tool. Dated to about 20,000 years ago, it is kept in Brussels and is among the oldest known mathematical objects.
textes.Des encoches sur un os. Les premiers mat: Notches on a bone. The first mathematicians had no blackboard, but they already had skeptics to dispute their results.
textes.Pythagore n'a probablement pas démontré: Pythagoras probably did not prove the theorem that bears his name: the Babylonians knew the relation a millennium earlier, as the Plimpton 322 tablet shows, and no writing by Pythagoras has come down to us. His school mixed mathematics, music and strange rules, such as the ban on eating beans. It left an idea that has crossed the centuries: the world can be described by numbers.
textes.Le théorème de Pythagore n'est pas de Py: The Pythagorean theorem isn't by Pythagoras. The AI isn't quite an intelligence. Everyone has their labels.
textes.À Alexandrie, Euclide rassemble la géomé: In Alexandria, Euclid gathered the geometry of his time in the Elements: 13 books, definitions, five postulates and hundreds of theorems proven step by step. It is one of the most copied and printed books in history. To King Ptolemy, who asked for a shorter path, he supposedly replied: “There is no royal road to geometry.”
textes.Pas de voie royale en géométrie, ni sur: No royal road to geometry, nor on this board. The AI sees to it.
textes.Les Éléments ont servi de manuel pendant: The Elements served as a textbook for more than two thousand years. People still study them. Your turn.
textes.Le mathématicien indien Brahmagupta donn: In 628, the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta gave rules for calculating with zero and negative numbers: a debt minus zero is a debt, zero minus zero is zero. Zero already existed as a placeholder among the Babylonians and the Maya, but he made it a number like any other. Yet he got zero divided by zero wrong, saying it equals zero.
textes.Zéro devient un nombre. L'IA connaît des: Zero becomes a number. The AI knows quizzes that made it their favorite score.
textes.Brahmagupta fixe les règles du zéro, mai: Brahmagupta set the rules for zero, but stated 0 ÷ 0 = 0. One calculation error, two squares back.
textes.À la Maison de la sagesse de Bagdad, al-: At the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, al-Khwarizmi wrote a treatise on solving equations by “al-jabr,” restoration, which gave us the word algebra. His name, Latinized as Algoritmi, gave us “algorithm.” His books also introduced Europe to the Indian numerals, which have since been called, wrongly, Arabic numerals.
textes.Les algorithmes portent le nom d'un math: Algorithms are named after a mathematician from Baghdad. The AI is made of algorithms. She'll let you draw the connection.
textes.Leonardo de Pise, dit Fibonacci, publie: Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci, published the Liber abaci: in it he explained to European merchants the Hindu-Arabic numerals and written calculation, far more practical than Roman numerals. He is mostly remembered for a little problem about rabbits that gives the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13… Indian mathematicians had known it for centuries.
textes.Calculez avec MCMXXIV, puis avec 1924. V: Calculate with MCMXXIV, then with 1924. You'll understand the shortcut.
textes.Le chevalier de Méré, joueur, demande à: The Chevalier de Méré, a gambler, asked Blaise Pascal how to divide the stakes of an interrupted game. Pascal discussed it by letter with Pierre de Fermat in the summer of 1654: their correspondence laid the foundations of probability theory. At 18, Pascal had also built a calculating machine, the Pascaline, to help his father collect taxes.
textes.Les probabilités sont nées d'une partie: Probability was born from a game of dice. Your chances of passing the next quiz can be calculated. The AI has calculated them.
textes.Pascal et Fermat posent les bases du cal: Pascal and Fermat laid the foundations of probability to fairly divide the stakes of an interrupted game. This time, the split falls your way.
textes.Alan Turing imagine une machine abstrait: Alan Turing imagined an abstract machine that reads and writes symbols on a tape: it can carry out any calculation. It is the theoretical model of all our computers. During the war, he helped break the Enigma code at Bletchley Park. Convicted in 1952 of “gross indecency” because of his relationship with a man, he died in 1954; the United Kingdom granted him a posthumous pardon in 2013.
textes.Turing a inventé l'ordinateur sur le pap: Turing invented the computer on paper, then wondered whether a machine could think. The AI reserves her answer.
textes.Vers 1800 av. J.-C., probablement à Lars: Around 1800 BC, probably in Larsa, in Mesopotamia, a scribe inscribes on a clay tablet a table of 15 rows in base 60. It contains Pythagorean triples: whole numbers like 3, 4 and 5, sides of a right triangle, more than a thousand years before Pythagoras. Bought around 1922 by the New York publisher George Plimpton, it is at Columbia University. What was it for? Specialists still debate it.
textes.Mille ans avant Pythagore, un scribe con: A thousand years before Pythagoras, a scribe already knew his triangles. You, a thousand years after, let's check.
textes.Vers 1550 av. J.-C., à Thèbes, le scribe: Around 1550 BC, in Thebes, the scribe Ahmes copies an older mathematics manual. The papyrus opens with a table writing the fractions 2/n as sums of fractions with numerator 1, the Egyptian way. Then come problems of sharing loaves, pyramid slopes, areas. For the area of a disc, Ahmes in effect takes 256/81 for π, about 3.16. Alexander Rhind buys it in Luxor in 1858; it is now in the British Museum.
textes.3,16 pour π, il y a trente-cinq siècles: 3.16 for π, thirty-five centuries ago: less than one percent off. Do better in the next quiz.
textes.Vers 250 av. J.-C., dans La Mesure du ce: Around 250 BC, in Measurement of a Circle, Archimedes traps the circle between two regular 96-sided polygons, one inside, one outside. The circle's perimeter must lie between the two. From this he gets bounds: π is greater than 223/71 and less than 22/7, that is between 3.1408 and 3.1429. His method, which approaches a curve with ever finer figures, foreshadows calculus.
textes.Archimède a dessiné deux fois 96 côtés p: Archimedes drew 96 sides twice for one answer. You need only one answer. A right one.
textes.Au IIIe siècle, à Alexandrie, Diophante: In the 3rd century, in Alexandria, Diophantus writes the Arithmetica in thirteen books: number problems solved with equations. He invents abbreviations for the unknown and its powers, a first step towards algebraic notation. Six books survive in Greek; four more, in Arabic, were only found in 1968. Bachet's Latin edition of 1621 made him read all over Europe, right into Fermat's margin.
textes.Diophante a inventé une abréviation pour: Diophantus invented an abbreviation for the unknown. Here, the unknown is your next answer.
textes.En 1539, le mathématicien Tartaglia conf: In 1539, the mathematician Tartaglia tells Gerolamo Cardano his method for solving certain cubic equations, on condition that he keep it secret. Cardano then learns that Scipione del Ferro had found it first, and publishes everything in 1545 in the Ars Magna, with his student Ferrari's method for the fourth degree. In it, for the first time, appear square roots of negative numbers, which Cardano judges as subtle as they are useless.
textes.Des nombres aussi subtils qu'inutiles, d: Numbers as subtle as they are useless, said Cardano. Today they are used everywhere. Beware of your final judgements.
textes.En 1614, l'Écossais John Napier publie l: In 1614, the Scot John Napier publishes the Description of the Wonderful Rule of Logarithms: 57 pages of explanation and 90 pages of tables. Thanks to them, long hand calculations become much faster. He had already invented his bones, numbered rods to make multiplication easier. In 1615, Henry Briggs visits him; Napier hands him the computation of new tables, which will become base-10 logarithms.
textes.Napier a passé des années à calculer pou: Napier spent years calculating so others could calculate less. You calculate less without having done anything.
textes.Vers 1637, Pierre de Fermat, magistrat à: Around 1637, Pierre de Fermat, a magistrate in Toulouse, annotates his copy of Diophantus's Arithmetica. He states that no cube is the sum of two cubes, and more generally that no power beyond the square is the sum of two like powers. He claims a marvellous proof, but the margin is too narrow to contain it. His son publishes the note in 1670. It took until Andrew Wiles, in 1994: 358 years.
textes.J'ai une démonstration merveilleuse de v: I have a marvellous proof of your delay, but this square is too small. Go back two.
textes.À Königsberg, la rivière Pregel entoure: In Königsberg, the river Pregel surrounds two islands linked to the banks by seven bridges. Can you take a walk crossing each bridge once and only once? In 1736, Leonhard Euler forgets the map and keeps only the essentials: land masses linked by bridges. He shows that such a walk requires zero or two land masses touched by an odd number of bridges. Königsberg has four: it is impossible. This is the first theorem of graph theory.
textes.Euler a résolu le problème en effaçant l: Euler solved the problem by erasing the map. Erase your preconceptions, that works too.
textes.L'Anglais Thomas Bayes meurt en 1761 san: The Englishman Thomas Bayes dies in 1761 without having published his work on probability. His friend Richard Price finds it among his papers, completes it and has it published in 1763 in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society. The essay shows how to revise a probability in the light of a new observation, starting from an initial estimate. This reasoning, since called Bayes's theorem, is used today in medicine, law and artificial intelligence.
textes.Bayes révisait ses probabilités à chaque: Bayes revised his probabilities with each new observation. After your last answer, I'm revising mine.
textes.En 1854, l'Anglais George Boole publie A: In 1854, the Englishman George Boole publishes An Investigation of the Laws of Thought. In it he treats logic like algebra: Aristotle's propositions become equations, which one solves. He justifies his system with a rule of calculation on the numbers 0 and 1 alone. His successors, such as Jevons, Peirce or Schröder, will draw from it the algebra that bears his name, that of the circuits of our computers, where everything comes down to true or false.
textes.Chez Boole, tout est vrai ou faux. Votre: With Boole, everything is true or false. Your last answer was 0.
