textes.Cette tablette d'argile, achetée par Geo: This clay tablet, bought by George Plimpton around 1922, holds a table of numbers satisfying a² + b² = c², a millennium before Pythagoras.
textes.François Viète publie un calcul où les l: François Viète publishes a calculus in which letters replace numbers.
textes.Son Introduction à l'art analytique note: His Introduction to the Analytic Art writes unknowns as vowels and known quantities as consonants. Viète, an adviser to Henri IV, also cracked Spanish secret codes: Philip II accused him of sorcery before the pope.
textes.Publication posthume de l'essai de Thoma: Posthumous publication of Thomas Bayes's essay.
textes.Le pasteur Thomas Bayes n'a jamais publi: The minister Thomas Bayes never published his theorem: his friend Richard Price found it among his papers and had it published two years after his death.
textes.Lobatchevski publie une géométrie où les: Lobachevsky publishes a geometry in which parallel lines behave differently.
textes.Bolyai fait la même découverte de son cô: Bolyai makes the same discovery on his own. Gauss had thought of it without publishing, for fear of “the clamor of the Boeotians”, as he wrote.
textes.George Boole, autodidacte, réduit le rai: George Boole, self-taught, reduces reasoning to calculations on 0 and 1. Claude Shannon would use it in 1937 to design electrical circuits.
textes.Florence Nightingale montre en graphique: Florence Nightingale shows in charts that soldiers die mostly of preventable diseases.
textes.Ses diagrammes polaires, présentés au go: Her polar area diagrams, presented to the British government, helped reform hygiene in military hospitals. She was the first woman elected to the Royal Statistical Society, in 1858.
textes.Georg Cantor montre qu'on ne peut pas nu: Georg Cantor shows that the real numbers cannot all be numbered.
textes.Son travail choque une partie des mathém: His work shocked some mathematicians, including Kronecker. Hilbert would later say: “No one shall expel us from the paradise that Cantor has created for us.”
textes.Francis Galton retrouve la corrélation e: Francis Galton rediscovers correlation by comparing heights and forearm lengths.
textes.Cousin de Darwin, Galton invente aussi l: A cousin of Darwin, Galton also invented the questionnaire, fingerprints in criminology and, unfortunately, the word “eugenics”.
textes.Dans une grotte d'Afrique australe, quel: In a cave in southern Africa, someone notches a baboon fibula.
textes.Entre 42 000 et 43 000 ans d'âge : bâton: Between 42,000 and 43,000 years old: tally stick or ritual object, it is one of the oldest notched objects known.
textes.Un scribe égyptien calcule le volume d'u: An Egyptian scribe calculates the volume of a truncated pyramid, and gets it right.
textes.25 problèmes ; le 14e donne 56 pour une: 25 problems; the 14th gives 56 for a truncated pyramid of 4, 2 and 6. Bought in Thebes in 1892 or 1893, it is in the Pushkin Museum.
textes.À Constantinople, Heiberg reconnaît des: In Constantinople, Heiberg recognises texts by Archimedes beneath a 13th-century prayer book.
textes.Il en tire La Méthode, seule copie connu: From it he recovered The Method, the only known copy. The manuscript, sold again in 1998, gave up the rest of its secrets under X-rays.
textes.Liu Hui commente les Neuf chapitres et c: Liu Hui comments on the Nine Chapters and calculates π with a 3,072-sided polygon.
textes.Il obtient 3,14159, mieux qu'Archimède e: He obtains 3.14159, better than Archimedes and Ptolemy, and attaches a manual for measuring what cannot be reached.
textes.Un paysan trouve près de Mardan un manus: A peasant near Mardan finds a mathematical manuscript in which a dot marks zero.
textes.Conservé à la Bodléienne d'Oxford, il a: Kept in Oxford's Bodleian Library, it was carbon-dated in 2017 with gaps of several centuries between folios; Oxford revised those dates in 2024.
textes.Bombelli donne les règles pour calculer: Bombelli gives the rules for calculating with roots of negative numbers.
textes.« Plus de moins par plus de moins fait m: "Plus of minus by plus of minus makes minus": complex numbers get their rules, and Bombelli solves equations where Cardano had given up.
textes.Henry Briggs fait le voyage jusqu'à Édim: Henry Briggs travels to Edinburgh to meet the inventor of logarithms.
textes.Ils s'accordent sur une nouvelle échelle: They agree on a new scale; Briggs would compute base-10 logarithms, to 14 decimals.
textes.La Royal Society donne raison à Newton c: The Royal Society finds for Newton against Leibniz, in a report written by Newton.
textes.Leibniz n'a pas été entendu et ne découv: Leibniz was not heard and only discovered the text in autumn 1714. Historians today judge the two discoveries independent.
textes.Appel et Haken démontrent par ordinateur: Appel and Haken prove by computer that any map can be coloured with four colours.
textes.1 834 configurations, plus de mille heur: 1,834 configurations, over a thousand hours of computing: Guthrie's question, asked in 1852, is settled by a machine.
textes.Gödel annonce l'incomplétude le 7 septem: Gödel announces incompleteness on 7 September; the next day, Hilbert proclaims "We shall know".
textes.Deux jours, une ville, deux visions des: Two days, one city, two visions of mathematics. Gödel's announcement went almost unnoticed; Hilbert's phrase ended up on his tombstone.
textes.Six siècles après sa mort, Léonard de Pi: Six centuries after his death, Leonardo of Pisa becomes "Fibonacci" in the writing of Guglielmo Libri.
textes.Le surnom abrège filius Bonacci, « fils: The nickname shortens filius Bonacci, "son of Bonacci". In his lifetime he was called Leonardo of Pisa, or Leonardo Bigollo, the traveller.
textes.À Venise, Erhard Ratdolt imprime pour la: In Venice, Erhard Ratdolt prints Euclid's Elements for the first time.
textes.D'après la version latine de Campanus. O: From Campanus's Latin version. It is estimated that only the Bible has had more editions since.
textes.Dans sa Summa, Luca Pacioli donne une as: In his Summa, Luca Pacioli gives a merchant's trick: 72 divided by the interest rate gives the time to double the stake.
textes.À 6 % par an, l'argent double en 72 ÷ 6: At 6% a year, money doubles in about 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years. Pacioli does not explain it: the rule is probably older than him.
textes.À Samarcande, Omar Khayyam commence son: In Samarkand, Omar Khayyam begins his Treatise on Algebra.
textes.Il classe quatorze types d'équations du: He classified fourteen types of third-degree equations and solved them by intersecting conic sections. The poet of the Quatrains was also a mathematician.
textes.Un rouleau de près de cinq mètres, copié: A scroll nearly five meters long, copied by the scribe Ahmes from an older text. It gathers eighty-seven solved problems, like a workbook: sharing loaves among ten men, computing the volume of a granary, the slope of a pyramid. The Egyptians wrote their fractions as sums of fractions with numerator one, and the papyrus provides tables to handle them. For the area of a disk, it removes one ninth from the diameter and squares the rest, which amounts to taking pi as about 3.16. No proofs: recipes, checked on examples.
textes.C'est l'un des plus anciens manuels de m: It is one of the oldest mathematics textbooks to have come down to us.
textes.Ahmès l'a intitulé, sans fausse modestie: Ahmes titled it, with no false modesty, “correct method of reckoning, for grasping the meaning of things and knowing everything”. The Scotsman Rhind bought it in Luxor in 1858.
textes.Connaître tous les secrets, en quatre-vi: Knowing all secrets, in eighty-four exercises. I give you fewer, and you already find it a lot.
textes.anglais, trad. de l'égyptien par A. B. C: English, translated from Egyptian by A. B. Chace
textes.Treize livres pour bâtir toute la géomét: Thirteen books to build all of geometry from almost nothing: a few definitions (a point, a line), five postulates accepted without proof, and common notions such as “the whole is greater than the part”. From there, Euclid proves hundreds of propositions step by step: the Pythagorean theorem, the construction of regular polygons, the infinitude of prime numbers. Each result rests on the previous ones, like the floors of a building. The fifth postulate, the one about parallels, intrigued mathematicians for two thousand years; by replacing it, they invented non-Euclidean geometries in the 19th century.
textes.Il a fixé pour des siècles ce que veut d: It set for centuries what it means to “prove”.
textes.Abraham Lincoln raconte avoir étudié, et: Abraham Lincoln said he studied, and nearly mastered, the first six books after his term in Congress.
textes.Treize livres, et pas une phrase de trop: Thirteen books, and not one sentence too many. The AI sees in it a model your answers could follow.

textes.Archimède s'adresse au roi Gélon de Syra: Archimedes addresses King Gelon of Syracuse. Some people think, he says, that the grains of sand are too many to be counted. He sets out to show the opposite: how many grains would it take to fill the whole Universe? The Greeks have no word for very large numbers, and the largest they name is the myriad, ten thousand. So Archimedes invents a system of nested orders of magnitude, which foreshadows our powers of ten. His answer: at most ten to the power of sixty-three grains. A huge number, but finite.
textes.Il montre qu'un nombre immense n'est pas: It shows that an immense number is not infinite, and gives a method for writing very large numbers.
textes.Pour estimer la taille de l'Univers, Arc: To estimate the size of the Universe, Archimedes cites Aristarchus's hypothesis: the Earth revolves around the Sun. This passage is one of the few testimonies of it that remain.
textes.Dix puissance soixante-trois grains de s: Ten to the sixty-third grains of sand. I recounted: one is missing. It's in your shoe.
textes.Première phrase, adressée au roi de Syra: First sentence, addressed to the king of Syracuse
textes.Coupez un cône avec un plan : selon l'in: Cut a cone with a plane: depending on the tilt, you get a circle, an ellipse, a parabola or a hyperbola. Apollonius studies these curves in eight books, further than all his predecessors. He is the one who gives them their names, and he obtains them all from a single double cone, by varying the angle of the cut. He proves hundreds of their properties: tangents, foci, diameters. For centuries, these curves remain a game for geometers. Then Kepler discovers that the planets follow ellipses, and Galileo that projectiles follow parabolas.
textes.Ces courbes sans usage apparent sont dev: These curves with no apparent use became the shape of orbits and trajectories.
textes.Le huitième livre ne nous est pas parven: The eighth book has not come down to us. In 1710, the astronomer Edmond Halley, of comet fame, published a reconstruction of it, based on clues left by the commentators.
textes.Dix-huit siècles avant que quelqu'un s'e: Eighteen centuries before anyone used them. Mathematicians' patience reassures me about yours.
textes.Diophante pose et résout des problèmes d: Diophantus poses and solves number problems: find two numbers whose sum and sum of squares are given, split a square into two squares. He looks for whole or fractional solutions, and uses abbreviations for the unknown and its powers: a first step toward algebraic notation. Of thirteen books, six have come down to us in Greek; four more were found in 1968 in an Arabic translation. Equations for which whole-number solutions are sought are now called “Diophantine”.
textes.Il a fait de l'arithmétique un art de ré: He turned arithmetic into the art of solving equations, and inspired Fermat.
textes.Pierre de Fermat a écrit dans la marge d: Pierre de Fermat wrote in the margin of his copy that he had a marvelous proof, but that the margin was too narrow. It took until Andrew Wiles, in 1994.

textes.Al-Khwarizmi écrit à Bagdad un manuel pr: Al-Khwarizmi writes in Baghdad a practical handbook for solving problems of inheritance, trade or land surveying. He reduces all quadratic equations to six standard forms, and gives a step-by-step recipe for each. Al-jabr, “completion”, means moving a term to the other side of the equation; al-muqabala, “balancing”, means removing the same quantity from both sides. He uses no symbols: everything is written in words, and justified by geometric figures. Negative numbers are not yet accepted as solutions.
textes.Il a fait de l'algèbre une discipline à: He made algebra a discipline of its own and gave it its name.
textes.Le mot « algorithme » vient de la forme: The word “algorithm” comes from the Latin form of his name, Algoritmi.
textes.Des équations écrites tout en mots. L'IA: Equations written entirely in words. The AI measures how lucky you are to have “x”.
textes.Al-Kindi, savant de la Maison de la sage: Al-Kindi, a scholar of the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, describes how to break a message enciphered by substitution, where each letter is replaced by another. His method: count the letters. In a long Arabic text, some letters come up much more often than others. You just count the symbols of the enciphered message, match the most frequent one with the most frequent letter of the language, and so on. This is frequency analysis, which would leave every simple cipher vulnerable for a thousand years.

textes.Les Égyptiens écrivaient leurs fractions: The Egyptians wrote their fractions as sums of distinct fractions with numerator 1. The Rhind papyrus, copied by the scribe Ahmes, gives whole tables of them.
textes.Les plus anciennes tables de multiplicat: The oldest known multiplication tables are Babylonian, about 4,000 years old, but in base 60. The oldest in base 10 is Chinese: 21 bamboo slips dated to about 305 BC.
textes.Comparer des fractions en décimal, l'Eur: Europe learned to compare fractions in decimals in 1585 with The Tenth, a 35-page booklet by the Fleming Simon Stevin. Al-Uqlidisi was already using decimal fractions in 952.
textes.La multiplication ne passe avant l'addit: Multiplication has only come before addition since the algebraic notation of the 17th century. In the 1920s, historian Florian Cajori noted that mathematicians still disagreed about multiplication and division.
textes.La méthode pour trouver le PGCD figure d: The method for finding the GCD appears in Euclid's Elements, around 300 BC: it is one of the oldest algorithms still in use. It was probably known to Eudoxus as early as 375 BC.
textes.La « preuve par neuf » repose sur cette: "Casting out nines" relies on this property. The oldest text using it to check a calculation is Indian, around 950; Avicenna described it around 1020 as the "Hindu method".
textes.Euclide démontre vers 300 avant notre èr: Euclid proved around 300 BC that there are infinitely many primes, in Book IX of the Elements: "prime numbers are more than any assigned multitude of prime numbers".
textes.Dans la Chine des Han, on calculait avec: In Han China, people calculated with red rods for positive numbers and black rods for negative ones. In Europe, Michael Stifel still called them "absurd numbers" in 1544.
textes.Le mot « exposant » est forgé par Michae: The word "exponent" was coined by Michael Stifel in 1544, and it was Descartes who, in 1637 in La Géométrie, first wrote powers small and raised, as in 2⁵.
textes.La barre de fraction horizontale apparaî: The horizontal fraction bar first appears in the work of al-Hassar, a mathematician from Fez, around 1200. Indian mathematicians already wrote the numerator above the denominator, but without a bar.
textes.Le signe % vient de l'italien per cento,: The % sign comes from the Italian per cento, "for a hundred". Around 1425, a scribe shortened it to "pc" with a small loop, which by 1650 had become the fraction-like sign we know.
textes.C'est en étudiant les intérêts composés,: It was by studying compound interest, successive increases that multiply instead of adding up, that Jacob Bernoulli discovered the number e, about 2.718, in 1683.
textes.Les Romains calculaient déjà en centième: The Romans already calculated in hundredths: Emperor Augustus levied a 1% tax on goods sold at auction, the centesima rerum venalium. By the 17th century, interest rates were routinely quoted in hundredths.
textes.La règle de trois était connue des mathé: The rule of three was known to Chinese mathematicians before the 2nd century AD, in The Nine Chapters. Europe only took it up much later; it was sometimes called the "golden rule".
textes.La carte de Cassini, au 1/86 400, est la: The Cassini map, at 1:86,400, was the first map of a whole country based on triangulation. Four generations of Cassinis worked on it for more than sixty years, in the 18th century.
textes.La TVA est une invention française : le: VAT is a French invention: senior civil servant Maurice Lauré devised it in 1954. It then spread to much of the world.
textes.La théorie des proportions vient d'Eudox: The theory of proportion comes from Eudoxus of Cnidus, in the 4th century BC: he defined when two ratios are equal. Euclid took it up in Book V of the Elements.
textes.Les plus anciens dés connus viennent peu: The oldest known dice may come from the Burnt City, in Iran, around 2800-2500 BC, found with a backgammon-like game. At Mohenjo-daro, one die already has opposite faces adding up to 7.
textes.Le 18 août 1913, au casino de Monte-Carl: On 18 August 1913, at the Monte Carlo casino, the ball landed on black 26 times in a row. Players bet on red, convinced it "had" to come up, and lost millions of francs.
textes.En 1654, le chevalier de Méré soumet à P: In 1654, the Chevalier de Méré put gambling problems to Pascal. The correspondence between Pascal and Fermat that followed founded probability theory.
textes.Vers 1564, le médecin et joueur Jérôme C: Around 1564, physician and gambler Gerolamo Cardano wrote The Book on Games of Chance, which counts dice outcomes: the first systematic treatment of probability. It was only published in 1663.
textes.En 1990, Marilyn vos Savant donne la bon: In 1990, Marilyn vos Savant gave the right answer in Parade magazine. She received about 10,000 letters telling her she was wrong, nearly 1,000 of them from PhDs; even Paul Erdős was only convinced by a simulation.
textes.Dans leurs lettres de 1654, Pascal et Fe: In their 1654 letters, Pascal and Fermat realised that stakes must be divided according to the rounds still to be won, not those already won. Huygens drew from this, in 1657, the first systematic treatise on probability.
textes.Le paradoxe des anniversaires est attrib: The birthday paradox is credited to mathematician Harold Davenport, around 1927, who did not publish it. Richard von Mises published the first version in 1939.
textes.L'urne est un classique depuis Jacques B: The urn has been a classic since Jacob Bernoulli: in Ars Conjectandi (1713), he sought to infer the proportion of pebbles of each colour in an urn from the draws.
textes.En 1989, les statisticiens Persi Diaconi: In 1989, statisticians Persi Diaconis and Frederick Mosteller formulated the "law of truly large numbers": with enough trials, a very unlikely event is almost sure to happen.
textes.Huygens découvre les jeux de hasard lors: Huygens discovered games of chance during a stay in Paris in 1655, where he heard of Pascal's and Fermat's work. His 1657 treatise was translated into Latin and published by his teacher Frans van Schooten.
textes.Le théorème de Bayes porte le nom du pas: Bayes' theorem is named after the minister Thomas Bayes, but his essay was only published in 1763, after his death, by his friend Richard Price. Laplace found the same result independently.
textes.Aristote décrit déjà ce piège dans les R: Aristotle already described this trap in the Sophistical Refutations, in the 4th century BC, as the fallacy "connected with the consequent": snow and the swan are both white, but they are not the same thing.
textes.Le premier à décrire explicitement ce ra: The first to describe this reasoning explicitly, "if A then B; not B; therefore not A", was Theophrastus, Aristotle's pupil. Today it is called modus tollens.
textes.Aristote distingue déjà, dans De l'inter: Aristotle already distinguished, in On Interpretation, "every man is white" from its contradictory "not every man is white". Boethius later drew the famous square of opposition from it.
textes.George Boole, mathématicien autodidacte,: George Boole, a self-taught mathematician, put logic into equations in 1847 and then in 1854 in The Laws of Thought. In 1937, Claude Shannon showed that this algebra could be used to design circuits: the basis of computers.
textes.Aristote définit le syllogisme dans les: Aristotle defined the syllogism in the Prior Analytics, around 350 BC. His logic dominated Western thought for centuries; in the Middle Ages, this very argument was memorised under the name "Barbara".
textes.Augustus De Morgan énonce ces lois en 18: Augustus De Morgan stated these laws in 1847 in his Formal Logic. But Aristotle had made a similar remark, and William of Ockham was already writing them out in words in the 14th century.
textes.Cette définition de « si… alors » vient: This definition of "if... then" comes from Philo the Dialectician, around 300 BC: a conditional is false only if the antecedent is true and the consequent false. It is the one used in modern logic.
textes.Les logiciens du Moyen Âge donnaient un: Medieval logicians gave a name to each valid form of syllogism, whose vowels encoded the type of proposition: Barbara, Celarent, Darii... A way to learn them by heart.
textes.Wittgenstein popularise les tables de vé: Wittgenstein popularised truth tables in the Tractatus, published in 1921, and Emil Post proposed them the same year. But Charles Sanders Peirce was already drawing them in manuscripts from 1883-1884.
textes.L'exemple le plus célèbre est la preuve: The most famous example is the proof that √2 is not a fraction, which Aristotle already alludes to. According to legend, Hippasus of Metapontum was killed for revealing this discovery.
textes.Les Romains croyaient que les cygnes noi: The Romans believed black swans did not exist: the poet Juvenal speaks of a bird "as rare as a black swan". In 1697, explorer Willem de Vlamingh saw some in Australia.
textes.La phrase d'Épiménide, vers 600 avant no: Epimenides' line, around 600 BC, is quoted in the Epistle to Titus without any problem being seen in it. Only with Bertrand Russell, in 1908, was it presented as "the oldest contradiction of the kind".
textes.Le papyrus Rhind, vers 1550 avant notre: The Rhind papyrus, around 1550 BC, already contains first-degree equations, the "aha" problems: for example x + x/3 + x/4 = 2. It was bought near Luxor in 1858 by Alexander Rhind.
textes.Le traité d'al-Khwârizmî est traduit en: Al-Khwarizmi's treatise was translated into Latin by Robert of Chester in 1145. It remained a textbook in European universities until the 16th century, even though everything in it is written in words, with no symbols at all.
textes.Diophante d'Alexandrie, au IIIe siècle,: Diophantus of Alexandria, in the 3rd century, was one of the first to use a symbol for the unknown. It was in the margin of a 1621 edition of his Arithmetica that Fermat wrote his famous "last theorem".
textes.Le mot « imaginaire » pour ces nombres v: The word "imaginary" for these numbers comes from Descartes, and it was Euler who introduced the letter i. Electrical engineers often write j, because for them i means current.
textes.Le chapitre 8 des Neuf Chapitres, livre: Chapter 8 of The Nine Chapters, a Chinese book compiled between the 10th and 2nd centuries BC, solves systems with up to five unknowns. Its method, fangcheng, is what we now call Gaussian elimination.
textes.Avocat et conseiller d'Henri IV, Viète c: A lawyer and adviser to Henry IV, Viète broke a Spanish secret code of more than 500 characters in 1590. The King of Spain accused him of using magical powers.
textes.Dès 2000 avant notre ère, des tablettes: As early as 2000 BC, Babylonian tablets solved problems about the areas of rectangles with a method equivalent to our formula. Brahmagupta gave the first explicit solution in 628.
textes.Le signe = est inventé en 1557 par le Ga: The = sign was invented in 1557 by the Welshman Robert Recorde, who chose two parallel lines because "noe 2 thynges can be moare equalle". It did not appear in print again until 1618.
textes.Niccolò Fontana doit son surnom de Tarta: Niccolò Fontana owed his nickname Tartaglia, "the stammerer", to a sabre blow from a French soldier he received as a child during the sack of Brescia in 1512, which left him with a speech impediment.
textes.L'idée de médiane apparaît déjà dans le: The idea of the median already appears in the Talmud in the 6th century, to settle diverging appraisals. The word "median" was fixed by Francis Galton in 1881, after he had tried "middle-most value" and "medium".
textes.En 1668, un auteur signant « D. B. » exp: In 1668, an author signing "D. B." explained in the Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions how he took the mean of five measurements of magnetic variation.
textes.L'expression « écart type » est employée: The term "standard deviation" was first used in writing by Karl Pearson in 1894. Before him, Gauss spoke of "mean error".
textes.Le mot « mode » en statistique vient aus: The word "mode" in statistics also comes from Karl Pearson, in 1895: he found it "convenient" for the value of maximum frequency.
textes.Abraham de Moivre découvre la courbe en: Abraham de Moivre discovered the bell curve in 1733, approximating the outcomes of coin tosses. Gauss and Laplace developed it around 1809-1823; the name "normal" was popularised by Pearson in the late 19th century.
textes.Quetelet n'avait pas conçu son indice co: Quetelet had not designed his index as a medical tool. It was in 1972 that physiologist Ancel Keys renamed it "body mass index".
textes.Les intervalles de confiance, qui donnen: Confidence intervals, which give an estimate its margin of error, were theorised by the Pole Jerzy Neyman, in a 1934 paper and then a full account in 1937.
textes.Le Literary Digest avait interrogé ses l: The Literary Digest had polled its readers, car owners and telephone users, wealthier than average. Roosevelt won every state but two, and the magazine folded in 1938.
textes.En 1859, Florence Nightingale devient la: In 1859, Florence Nightingale became the first female member of the Royal Statistical Society. She called her circular diagrams "coxcombs".
textes.C'est la proposition 32 du livre I des É: It is Proposition 32 of Book I of Euclid's Elements, already known to the Pythagoreans. In the 1820s, Gauss reportedly measured a triangle formed by three mountain peaks to check whether space really followed this rule.
textes.Archimède démontre vers 260 avant notre: Archimedes proved around 260 BC, in Measurement of a Circle, that the area of a disc equals that of a right triangle whose base is the circumference and whose height is the radius: that is πr².
textes.La première table trigonométrique connue: The first known trigonometric table is due to the Greek astronomer Hipparchus, in the 2nd century BC: a table of chords, in steps of 7.5°. He is nicknamed the "father of trigonometry".
textes.« Sinus » vient d'une erreur de lecture: "Sine" comes from a misreading: the Sanskrit jyā, "bowstring", was transcribed jība in Arabic, read as jayb, "fold", and translated into Latin as sinus in the 12th century. The word "cosine" dates from 1620.
textes.Le théorème qui relie cet excès d'angles: The theorem linking this angle excess to the triangle's area is named after Albert Girard. Thomas Harriot had proved it as early as 1603, without publishing it.
textes.Doubler le volume d'un cube est l'un des: Doubling the volume of a cube is one of the great Greek problems, linked by legend to an oracle consulted against a plague on Delos. Pierre Wantzel proved in 1837 that it cannot be done with ruler and compass.
textes.Thalès de Milet est né vers 625 avant no: Thales of Miletus was born around 625 BC. According to Plutarch, his shadow method pleased the pharaoh Amasis; some historians doubt, however, that such anecdotes have any value.
textes.Le symbole π est utilisé pour la premièr: The symbol π was first used in 1706 by the Welshman William Jones, then popularised by Euler. A Babylonian tablet from 1900-1600 BC already used 3.125.
textes.Archimède est tué en 212 avant notre ère: Archimedes was killed in 212 BC by a Roman soldier when Syracuse fell, despite General Marcellus's order to spare him. The famous "do not disturb my circles" appears in no ancient source.
textes.Le lien entre sommets, arêtes et faces (: The link between vertices, edges and faces (8 - 12 + 6 = 2 for the cube) was stated by Euler in 1758. Francesco Maurolico had noted it as early as 1537 for the Platonic solids, in an unpublished manuscript.
textes.Gauss avait trouvé les idées de la géomé: Gauss had found the ideas of non-Euclidean geometry around 1813, but never published them. A century earlier, in 1733, Saccheri had brushed against it while believing he was proving Euclid's postulate.
textes.Archimède utilise une somme de ce genre: Archimedes used a sum of this kind in the 3rd century BC to calculate the area under a parabola. Euclid had already given the sum of a finite geometric sequence, in Book IX of the Elements.
textes.Galilée remarque dès 1638, dans ses Deux: Galileo noted as early as 1638, in his Two New Sciences, that there are as many squares as whole numbers. He concluded that "more", "less" and "equal" do not apply to infinity: Cantor would show otherwise.
textes.Zénon d'Élée, vers 490-430 avant notre è: Zeno of Elea, around 490-430 BC, wanted to defend his teacher Parmenides, for whom motion is an illusion. His texts are lost: we know his paradoxes through Aristotle's Physics.
textes.Son ancien professeur Leopold Kronecker: His former professor Leopold Kronecker called Cantor a "corrupter of youth". David Hilbert defended him: "No one shall expel us from the paradise that Cantor has created."
textes.Le Liber abaci de 1202 sert surtout à fa: The 1202 Liber abaci mainly served to introduce Hindu-Arabic numerals and place value to Europe. The sequence existed before Fibonacci: it only owes him its name.
textes.Euclide appelait ce nombre le partage en: Euclid called this number the division in "extreme and mean ratio", and Luca Pacioli the "divine proportion". The link with the Fibonacci sequence was noticed by Simon Jacob, then by Kepler.
textes.La preuve d'Oresme, vers 1350, tombe dan: Oresme's proof, around 1350, fell into obscurity. Pietro Mengoli redid it in 1650, and Jacob Bernoulli published another in 1689, crediting it to his brother Johann.
textes.David Hilbert présente son hôtel dans un: David Hilbert presented his hotel in a 1924-1925 lecture, "On the Infinite". It was George Gamow's book One Two Three... Infinity, in 1947, that made it famous.
textes.Le problème 79 du papyrus Rhind, vers 15: Problem 79 of the Rhind papyrus, around 1550 BC, is already a geometric sequence: 7 houses, 49 cats, 343 mice, 2,401 spelt plants, 16,807 measures of grain.
textes.Wallis n'a jamais expliqué pourquoi il a: Wallis never explained why he chose this sign. One hypothesis links it to an old Roman way of writing 1,000, CIↃ; another to the Greek letter omega.
textes.Euler justifie déjà que 0,999… = 1 dans: Euler already justified that 0.999... = 1 in his Elements of Algebra, in 1770. The rigorous definitions of real numbers that settle the question arrived in 1872.
textes.Newton développe ses « fluxions » dès 16: Newton developed his "fluxions" from 1666 but published nothing; Leibniz published first, in 1684. The Royal Society report that ruled in Newton's favour, in 1712, was written by Newton himself.
textes.Quel âge a l'os de Lebombo, l'un des plu: How old is the Lebombo bone, one of the oldest known notched bones?
textes.Vingt-quatre datations au carbone 14 le: Twenty-four radiocarbon dates place it between 42,000 and 43,000 years. It is a baboon fibula about 8 cm long.
textes.L'os de Lebombo, un péroné de babouin en: The Lebombo bone, a notched baboon fibula, is 42,000 to 43,000 years old.
textes.L'os d'Ishango prouve que des hommes con: The Ishango bone proves that people knew prime numbers 20,000 years ago.
textes.Faux. Une colonne ressemble aux premiers: False. One column looks like the primes between 10 and 20 (11, 13, 17, 19), but it may be a coincidence; another bone from the same layer shows nothing of the kind.
textes.Pour beaucoup d'historiens, la notion de: For many historians, the notion of a prime number does not appear before about 500 BC.
textes.Combien d'entailles compte l'os d'Ishang: How many notches does the Ishango bone have?
textes.168 entailles, rangées en trois colonnes: 168 notches, arranged in three columns called M, G and D. Columns G and D each total 60, column M totals 48.
textes.L'os d'Ishango porte 168 entailles en tr: The Ishango bone bears 168 notches in three columns; it was found in 1950 in the Congo.
textes.Où a-t-on trouvé l'os d'Ishango ?: Where was the Ishango bone found?
textes.Au Congo, au bord de la Semliki: In the Congo, by the Semliki River
textes.En Chine, au bord du fleuve Jaune: In China, by the Yellow River
textes.En 1950, Jean de Heinzelin le trouve prè: In 1950, Jean de Heinzelin found it near Ishango, in what was then the Belgian Congo. It is now in Brussels.
textes.Selon Alexander Marshack, l'os d'Ishango: According to Alexander Marshack, the Ishango bone would be:
textes.Marshack remarque que deux colonnes font: Marshack noted that two columns total 60 and the third 48, and saw six lunar months in it. His critics say he looked for a pattern without testing the hypothesis.
textes.Marshack a proposé un calendrier lunaire: Marshack proposed a six-month lunar calendar; critics find that he merely searched for a pattern.
textes.L'os d'Ishango est le plus ancien os ent: The Ishango bone is the oldest known notched bone.
textes.Faux. L'os de Lebombo, en Afrique austra: False. The Lebombo bone, in southern Africa, is over 40,000 years old, twice as old.
textes.L'os de Lebombo et l'os du loup sont plu: The Lebombo bone and the Wolf bone are older than the Ishango bone.
textes.Dans la ville d'Uruk, vers 3200 av. J.-C: In the city of Uruk, around 3200 BC, what were clay tablets first used for?
textes.À compter l'orge, les moutons et la bièr: To count barley, sheep and beer
textes.Les plus anciennes tablettes sont des co: The oldest tablets are accounts: sacks of barley, head of cattle, rations. Laws and myths came later.
textes.À Uruk, vers 3200 av. J.-C., les premièr: At Uruk, around 3200 BC, the first tablets were used for accounting.
textes.Le plus ancien nom de personne connu ser: The oldest known personal name may be Kushim's. Who was he?
textes.Un comptable, au bas d'un reçu d'orge: An accountant, at the bottom of a barley receipt
textes.Kushim signe des tablettes de comptes d': Kushim signed tablets of barley accounts at Uruk. The first name in history may be an accountant's.
textes.Kushim, comptable d'Uruk, est peut-être: Kushim, an accountant of Uruk, may be the oldest known personal name.
textes.Pour Denise Schmandt-Besserat, l'écritur: For Denise Schmandt-Besserat, writing was born from accounting for harvests and exchanges.
textes.Vrai. Avant l'écriture, de petits jetons: True. Before writing, small clay tokens served as counters. The idea is widely accepted, even if some of her conclusions are disputed.
textes.Denise Schmandt-Besserat a publié sa thé: Denise Schmandt-Besserat published her token theory from 1977, then Before Writing in 1992.
textes.Que servaient à compter, selon Schmandt-: According to Schmandt-Besserat, what did the small clay tokens of the 4th millennium BC count?
textes.Chaque jeton représentait une quantité d: Each token stood for a quantity of a product. Managing ever larger stocks is said to have pushed people to think more abstractly.
textes.Une rangée d'encoches sur un os prouve q: A row of notches on a bone proves that people knew how to add.
textes.Faux. Les encoches peuvent être décorati: False. Notches can be decorative or ritual; its discoverer thinks those of Lebombo were made during rituals.
textes.Peter Beaumont pense que les entailles d: Peter Beaumont thinks the Lebombo notches were made during rituals; the tally stick remains a conjecture.
textes.Que tient l'os d'Ishango à l'un de ses b: What does the Ishango bone hold at one of its ends?
textes.Un éclat de quartz y est fixé, peut-être: A piece of quartz is fixed to it, perhaps for engraving. The bone is so worked that it is no longer possible to tell which animal it came from.
textes.L'os mesure une dizaine de centimètres e: The bone is about ten centimetres long and bears a piece of quartz at its end.
textes.Dans quelle base comptaient les scribes: In what base did the Babylonian scribes count?
textes.La base 60. Nos 60 minutes, 60 secondes: Base 60. Our 60 minutes, 60 seconds and 360 degrees are its heirs.
textes.La base 60 des Babyloniens nous a laissé: The Babylonians' base 60 left us the 60 minutes of the hour and the 360 degrees of the circle.
textes.Combien 60 a-t-il de diviseurs, en compt: How many divisors does 60 have, counting 1 and 60?
textes.1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30 et: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30 and 60: twelve divisors. That is what makes sharing so convenient in base 60.
textes.60 est un nombre très composé : il a bea: 60 is a highly composite number: it has many divisors, which makes fractions easier.
textes.Les Babyloniens avaient dès le départ un: The Babylonians had a zero digit from the start.
textes.Faux. Ils n'avaient ni chiffre ni notion: False. They had neither a digit nor a notion of zero; later, a sign marks an empty place, but only in the middle of a number.
textes.Les textes babyloniens tardifs utilisent: Late Babylonian texts use an empty-place sign, but only in medial positions.
textes.Combien de signes différents utilisent l: How many different signs did the Babylonians use to write their digits?
textes.Deux : un pour l'unité, un pour la dizai: Two: one for the unit, one for ten
textes.Un clou pour 1, un chevron pour 10 : en: A nail for 1, a chevron for 10: by repeating them, all the digits from 1 to 59 can be written.
textes.Les Babyloniens écrivaient leurs 59 chif: The Babylonians wrote their 59 digits with two signs: one for the unit, one for ten.
textes.Chez les Babyloniens, la valeur d'un chi: Among the Babylonians, the value of a digit depends on its place in the number.
textes.Vrai. C'est une vraie numération de posi: True. It is a true positional system, like ours, unlike Egyptian or Roman numerals.
textes.La numération babylonienne est une vraie: Babylonian notation is a true place-value system, unlike Egyptian or Roman.
textes.En base 60, le nombre écrit « 1 ; 30 » (: In base 60, the number written "1;30" (one unit, then 30 sixtieths) is worth how much in decimal notation?
textes.1 + 30/60 = 1 + 0,5 = 1,5. C'est la même: 1 + 30/60 = 1 + 0.5 = 1.5. It is the same idea as our hours: 1 h 30 = 1.5 hours.
textes.En base 60, les places après l'unité val: In base 60, the places after the unit are sixtieths, like our minutes in the hour.
textes.Que montre la petite tablette YBC 7289 ?: What does the small tablet YBC 7289 show?
textes.Un carré, ses diagonales et une valeur d: A square, its diagonals and a value of √2
textes.Le côté vaut 30 ; sur la diagonale, √2 ≈: The side is 30; on the diagonal, √2 ≈ 1;24,51,10 and the product 42;25,35. It is a pupil's rough work.
textes.La tablette YBC 7289 donne √2 avec envir: Tablet YBC 7289 gives √2 to about six correct decimal digits.
textes.Avec combien de chiffres décimaux exacts: To how many correct decimal digits does tablet YBC 7289 give √2?
textes.1,41421296 contre 1,41421356 : l'erreur: 1.41421296 against 1.41421356: the error is less than one part in two million. It is the best accuracy known from antiquity.
textes.La tablette YBC 7289 était probablement: Tablet YBC 7289 was probably a pupil's work.
textes.Vrai. Petite et ronde, elle se tenait da: True. Small and round, it was held in the palm of the hand for rough work.
textes.Sa forme de tablette ronde à tenir dans: Its round, hand-held tablet shape suggests a pupil's exercise.
textes.La tablette Plimpton 322 contient un tab: Tablet Plimpton 322 contains a table related to:
textes.Chaque ligne correspond à des nombres co: Each row corresponds to numbers like 3, 4, 5, sides of a right triangle, more than a thousand years before Pythagoras.
textes.Plimpton 322, vers 1800 av. J.-C., compt: Plimpton 322, around 1800 BC, has four columns and fifteen rows; it probably comes from Larsa.
textes.Pour l'historienne Eleanor Robson, Plimp: For the historian Eleanor Robson, Plimpton 322 was probably:
textes.Un aide-mémoire de professeur pour fabri: A teacher's aid for making up exercises
textes.Robson juge la lecture trigonométrique a: Robson finds the trigonometric reading anachronistic: the Babylonians did not measure angles. She sees rather parameters for creating problems.
textes.Eleanor Robson pense que l'auteur était: Eleanor Robson thinks the author was a scribe of Larsa, probably a teacher, and the tablet a set of exercises.
textes.En base 60, l'inverse de 7 s'écrit avec: In base 60, the reciprocal of 7 is written with a finite number of digits.
textes.Faux. Seuls les nombres dont les facteur: False. Only numbers whose prime factors are 2, 3 or 5 have a finite reciprocal in base 60; for 7, 11 or 13, scribes gave approximate values.
textes.Les inverses de 7, 11 ou 13 n'ont pas d': The reciprocals of 7, 11 or 13 have no finite form in base 60: scribes approximated them.
textes.Comment s'appelle le scribe qui a recopi: What was the name of the scribe who copied the Rhind papyrus?
textes.« Le scribe Ahmès écrit cette copie » :: "The scribe Ahmose writes this copy": he signs it himself. Rhind is the Scot who bought it in 1858.
textes.Le papyrus porte la mention « Le scribe: The papyrus bears the words "The scribe Ahmose writes this copy".
textes.Combien de problèmes compte le papyrus R: How many problems does the Rhind papyrus contain?
textes.91 problèmes : numérotés de 1 à 87, plus: 91 problems: numbered 1 to 87, plus four "B" problems. Sharing, areas, volumes, slopes of pyramids.
textes.Le papyrus Rhind compte 91 problèmes ; A: The Rhind papyrus has 91 problems; Ahmes copied it around 1550 BC.
textes.Une somme de fractions de numérateur 1,: A sum of distinct fractions with numerator 1: 1/3 + 1/15 = 5/15 + 1/15 = 6/15 = 2/5. Repeating 1/5 + 1/5 was not allowed.
textes.Le papyrus Rhind s'ouvre sur une table d: The Rhind papyrus opens with a table of 2/n for odd n from 3 to 101.
textes.Dans une fraction égyptienne, on peut ré: In an Egyptian fraction, the same fraction can be repeated, as in 1/5 + 1/5.
textes.Faux. Les fractions de numérateur 1 doiv: False. The fractions with numerator 1 must all be different; that is why the Rhind papyrus needs a table of 2/n.
textes.Une fraction égyptienne est une somme fi: An Egyptian fraction is a finite sum of distinct unit fractions.
textes.Cinq pains à partager entre huit personn: Five loaves to share among eight people: what does each get, the Egyptian way?
textes.Chacun doit recevoir 5/8. Or 1/2 + 1/8 =: Each must receive 5/8. Now 1/2 + 1/8 = 4/8 + 1/8 = 5/8: a half and an eighth, two different fractions with numerator 1.
textes.Partager 5 parts entre 8 convives donne: Sharing 5 items among 8 diners gives each a half plus an eighth.
textes.La recette égyptienne de l'aire d'un dis: The Egyptian recipe for the area of a disc amounts to taking π as about:
textes.Aire = (8/9 × d)². Avec la formule moder: Area = (8/9 × d)². With the modern formula π × (d/2)², we find π = 4 × 64/81 = 256/81 ≈ 3.16, within 1% of the true value.
textes.La recette égyptienne de l'aire du disqu: The Egyptian recipe for the area of a disc amounts to π ≈ 256/81, within 1%.
textes.Avec la recette d'Ahmès, aire = (8/9 × d: With Ahmes's recipe, area = (8/9 × d)², what is the area of a round field 9 metres across, in m²?
textes.(8/9 × d)² avec d = 9 : 8/9 × 9 = 8, et: (8/9 × d)² with d = 9: 8/9 × 9 = 8, and 8² = 64 m². The modern formula π × (d/2)² gives 3.1416 × 4.5² ≈ 63.6 m². The recipe is Ahmes's, problem 48 of the Rhind papyrus.
textes.Le problème 79 du papyrus Rhind aligne 7: Problem 79 of the Rhind papyrus lists 7 houses, 49 cats, 343 mice: each number is seven times the previous one.
textes.Vrai. La suite continue avec 2 401 épis: True. The sequence continues with 2,401 ears and 16,807 measures of grain: a geometric progression with ratio 7.
textes.Le problème 79 décrit sept maisons, 49 c: Problem 79 describes seven houses, 49 cats, 343 mice, 2,401 spelt plants and 16,807 heqats.
textes.Quel volume le papyrus de Moscou trouve-: What volume does the Moscow papyrus find for its truncated pyramid (4 at the bottom, 2 at the top, height 6)?
textes.V = h/3 × (a² + ab + b²) = 6/3 × (16 + 8: V = h/3 × (a² + ab + b²) = 6/3 × (16 + 8 + 4) = 2 × 28 = 56. The scribe of the Moscow papyrus follows exactly these steps around 1850 BC; it is the oldest known trace of this formula.
textes.Le problème 14 du papyrus de Moscou calc: Problem 14 of the Moscow papyrus computes the volume of a truncated pyramid: 56.
textes.Où est conservé le papyrus Rhind ?: Where is the Rhind papyrus kept?
textes.Alexander Rhind l'achète à Louxor en 185: Alexander Rhind bought it in Luxor in 1858; the British Museum acquired it in 1865. Fragments are in the Brooklyn Museum.
textes.Rhind achète le papyrus à Louxor en 1858: Rhind bought the papyrus in Luxor in 1858; the British Museum acquired it in 1865.
textes.Ahmès a inventé lui-même les problèmes d: Ahmes invented the problems of the Rhind papyrus himself.
textes.Faux. Il recopie un texte plus ancien, d: False. He was copying an older text, from the reign of Amenemhat III, now lost.
textes.Le papyrus est la copie d'un texte plus: The papyrus is a copy of an older text, linked to the reign of Amenemhat III.
textes.En 1202, qui décrit une méthode pour écr: In 1202, who described a method for writing any fraction as a sum of fractions with numerator 1?
textes.Dans le Liber abaci, Fibonacci prend à c: In the Liber abaci, Fibonacci takes at each step the largest fraction with numerator 1 that fits in what is left. The method always works, but sometimes gives very large denominators.
textes.La méthode gloutonne de Fibonacci, dans: Fibonacci's greedy method, in the 1202 Liber abaci, always gives a finite expansion.
textes.Combien de côtés ont les polygones avec: How many sides do the polygons Archimedes used to bound π have?
textes.Il part de l'hexagone et double quatre f: He started from the hexagon and doubled four times: 6, 12, 24, 48, 96. The perimeters of the two polygons trap that of the circle.
textes.Archimède encadre π entre 223/71 et 22/7: Archimedes bounded π between 223/71 and 22/7 with 96-sided polygons.
textes.Archimède a prouvé que π vaut exactement: Archimedes proved that π equals exactly 22/7.
textes.Faux. 22/7 est sa borne haute : π est pl: False. 22/7 is his upper bound: π is less than 22/7 and greater than 223/71.
textes.Quelle fraction du volume du cylindre qu: What fraction of the volume of its enclosing cylinder does a sphere occupy?
textes.Cylindre : π r² × 2r = 2π r³. Sphère : 4: Cylinder: π r² × 2r = 2π r³. Sphere: 4/3 π r³. The ratio is (4/3)/2 = 2/3. Archimedes was so proud of it that he wanted it on his tomb.
textes.La sphère a les deux tiers du volume et: The sphere has two thirds of the volume and surface of the enclosing cylinder; Archimedes had it carved on his tomb.
textes.Un cylindre enferme exactement une sphèr: A cylinder exactly encloses a sphere and holds 30 litres. How many litres does the sphere hold?
textes.Volume de la sphère = 2/3 × volume du cy: Volume of the sphere = 2/3 × volume of the cylinder = 2/3 × 30 = 20 litres. The 2/3 ratio was proved by Archimedes in On the Sphere and Cylinder.
textes.Les derniers mots « Ne dérange pas mes c: The last words "Do not disturb my circles" are reported by ancient historians.
textes.Faux. Aucune source antique ne les cite: False. No ancient source quotes them; in Valerius Maximus, Archimedes merely protects his drawings with his hands.
textes.La célèbre phrase n'apparaît dans aucune: The famous line appears in no ancient source; Valerius Maximus shows him protecting the dust with his hands.
textes.Qui retrouva la tombe d'Archimède, grâce: Who found Archimedes' tomb, thanks to the carved sphere and cylinder?
textes.Cicéron la découvre envahie de broussail: Cicero found it overgrown near the Agrigentine gate, in Syracuse.
textes.Cicéron, questeur en Sicile, trouva la t: Cicero, quaestor in Sicily, found the overgrown tomb, adorned with a sphere and a cylinder.
textes.Un parchemin gratté puis réécrit: A parchment scraped and written over
textes.En 1229, les pages d'un manuscrit d'Arch: In 1229, the pages of an Archimedes manuscript were scraped and washed to write a prayer book over them.
textes.Le palimpseste d'Archimède, gratté en 12: The Archimedes Palimpsest, scraped in 1229, was recognised by Heiberg in 1906.
textes.Quel texte d'Archimède n'existe que dans: Which text by Archimedes exists only in the palimpsest?
textes.La Méthode, où il explique comment il «: The Method, where he explains how he "weighed" figures to guess his results before proving them.
textes.Le palimpseste est la seule source connu: The palimpsest is the only known source of The Method of Mechanical Theorems.
textes.Pour combien de millions de dollars le p: For how many million dollars was the Archimedes Palimpsest sold in 1998?
textes.2 millions de dollars, à New York, à un: $2 million, in New York, to an anonymous American buyer, after a court case over its ownership.
textes.Le palimpseste fut acheté 2 millions de: The palimpsest was bought for $2 million by an anonymous American buyer in 1998.
textes.Dans L'Arénaire, combien de grains de sa: In The Sand Reckoner, how many grains of sand does Archimedes estimate are needed to fill the universe?
textes.Pour écrire un si grand nombre, il inven: To write such a large number, he invented a system based on powers of the myriad, 10,000.
textes.Archimède estime à 8 × 10⁶³ le nombre de: Archimedes estimated 8 × 10⁶³ grains of sand to fill the universe.
textes.Comment les calculateurs chinois disting: How did Chinese calculators distinguish positive numbers from negative ones?
textes.Ils ne connaissaient pas les négatifs: They did not know negative numbers
textes.Des baguettes de deux couleurs, posées s: Rods of two colours, laid on a counting board. The Nine Chapters give the rules for adding and subtracting them.
textes.George Sarton signale l'usage de baguett: George Sarton mentions the use of red and black rods for positive and negative numbers.
textes.La méthode fangcheng des Neuf chapitres: The fangcheng method of the Nine Chapters corresponds to what we call:
textes.Des systèmes d'équations résolus en sous: Systems of equations solved by subtracting columns of a table: the method credited to Gauss, more than sixteen centuries later.
textes.La méthode fangcheng des Neuf chapitres: The fangcheng method of the Nine Chapters is what is now called Gaussian elimination.
textes.Combien d'inconnues compte l'exemple le: How many unknowns does the most complex example of the fangcheng chapter have?
textes.Cinq inconnues, résolues avec des baguet: Five unknowns, solved with rods on a counting board.
textes.Au plus tard en quelle année le texte de: By what year at the latest was the text of the Nine Chapters fixed?
textes.Le Livre des Han postérieurs le mentionn: The Book of the Later Han mentions it: it was fixed by 93 AD at the latest, after centuries of writing.
textes.Les Neuf chapitres ont été rédigés sur d: The Nine Chapters were written over centuries and fixed by 93 AD at the latest.
textes.Que fait le chapitre 7 des Neuf chapitre: What does chapter 7 of the Nine Chapters, "Excess and deficit", do?
textes.Il résout des problèmes par la règle de: It solves problems by the rule of false position
textes.On essaie deux réponses fausses, l'une t: Two wrong answers are tried, one too large, the other too small, and the right one is deduced: the rule of false position.
textes.Le chapitre « Excès et déficit » utilise: The "Excess and deficit" chapter uses what the West would call the rule of false position.
textes.Avec combien de côtés Liu Hui pousse-t-i: How many sides does Liu Hui push his polygon to in order to calculate π?
textes.3 072 côtés, après un polygone à 192 côt: 3,072 sides, after a 192-sided polygon. He obtained 3.14159, better than Archimedes and Ptolemy.
textes.Liu Hui commente les Neuf chapitres en 2: Liu Hui commented on the Nine Chapters in 263 and computed π with a 3,072-sided polygon.
textes.Quelle fraction Zu Chongzhi appelle-t-il: Which fraction did Zu Chongzhi call "the close ratio" for π?
textes.355/113 = 3,1415929…, juste à sept décim: 355/113 = 3.1415929…, correct to nearly seven decimals. 22/7 was his "approximate ratio".
textes.Zu Chongzhi place π entre 3,1415926 et 3: Zu Chongzhi placed π between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927 and proposed 355/113.
textes.Pendant combien de temps l'encadrement d: For how long did Zu Chongzhi's bounds on π remain the most accurate in the world?
textes.Entre 3,1415926 et 3,1415927 : personne: Between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927: nobody did better for over nine centuries.
textes.Liu Hui a calculé le volume de la sphère: Liu Hui calculated the volume of the sphere.
textes.Faux. Il avoue ne pas y arriver et le la: False. He admitted he could not manage it and left it "to a future mathematician". Zu Chongzhi and his son would complete the work.
textes.Liu Hui n'a pas su calculer le volume de: Liu Hui could not compute the volume of the sphere and left it to a future mathematician.
textes.Le chapitre 9 des Neuf chapitres, gougu,: Chapter 9 of the Nine Chapters, gougu, deals with:
textes.Gougu, « base et hauteur » : l'équivalen: Gougu, "base and altitude": the Chinese counterpart of Pythagoras' theorem, with for example the 3-4-5 triangle.
textes.Le chapitre gougu est la version chinois: The gougu chapter is the Chinese version of Pythagoras' theorem; it cites the 3-4-5 triple.
textes.Avant Liu Hui, on prenait souvent π égal: Before Liu Hui, π was often taken as 3 in China.
textes.Vrai. Liu Hui montre que c'est trop peu,: True. Liu Hui showed it was too little, and with his polygons obtained 3.14159.
textes.Avant Liu Hui, il était courant de suppo: Before Liu Hui, it was common to assume π = 3.
textes.Que mesure le Manuel mathématique de l'î: What does Liu Hui's Sea Island Mathematical Manual measure?
textes.Des hauteurs et des distances qu'on ne p: Heights and distances that cannot be reached
textes.Avec des perches et des barres posées à: With poles and bars set at right angles, the height of a tower or a distant island is calculated.
textes.Le Haidao suanjing, en 263, mesure haute: The Haidao suanjing, in 263, measures pagoda heights and distances with poles and bars at right angles.
textes.En quelle année Brahmagupta compose-t-il: In what year did Brahmagupta compose the treatise that made zero a number?
textes.En 628, à 30 ans : le Brahmasphutasiddha: In 628, aged 30: the Brahmasphutasiddhanta, the oldest known text treating zero as a number in its own right.
textes.En 628, le Brahmasphutasiddhanta traite: In 628, the Brahmasphutasiddhanta treated zero as a number in its own right.
textes.Pour Brahmagupta, combien fait zéro divi: For Brahmagupta, what is zero divided by zero?
textes.Il écrit que zéro divisé par zéro fait z: He wrote that zero divided by zero is zero. Today, this division is undefined.
textes.Brahmagupta écrit que zéro divisé par zé: Brahmagupta wrote that zero divided by zero is zero (verse 18.34).
textes.Selon Brahmagupta, le produit de deux no: According to Brahmagupta, the product of two negative numbers is positive.
textes.Vrai. Ses règles, en 628, sont celles qu: True. His rules, in 628, are those we still apply: −3 × −4 = 12.
textes.Brahmagupta énonce que le produit de deu: Brahmagupta states that the product of two negatives is positive.
textes.Quelle valeur de π Aryabhata donne-t-il: What value of π did Aryabhata give in 499?
textes.Un cercle de diamètre 20 000 a une circo: A circle of diameter 20,000 has a circumference that "can be approached" by 62,832: 62,832 ÷ 20,000 = 3.1416.
textes.Aryabhata donne π ≈ 62 832/20 000 = 3,14: Aryabhata gave π ≈ 62,832/20,000 = 3.1416 in the Aryabhatiya, in 499.
textes.Quel âge Aryabhata dit-il avoir en 499,: What age does Aryabhata say he was in 499, the year of his treatise?
textes.23 ans, d'où l'on déduit sa naissance en: 23, from which his birth in 476 is deduced.
textes.L'Aryabhatiya indique qu'Aryabhata avait: The Aryabhatiya states that Aryabhata was 23 in 499.
textes.Aryabhata affirmait que la Terre tourne: Aryabhata stated that the Earth rotates on its axis every day.
textes.Vrai. Pour lui, c'est ce qui explique le: True. For him, it explains the apparent motion of the stars.
textes.Aryabhata dit que la Terre tourne sur so: Aryabhata said the Earth rotates on its axis daily, hence the stars' apparent motion.
textes.Comment le manuscrit de Bakhshali note-t: How does the Bakhshali manuscript write zero?
textes.Un point marque la place vide dans ses n: A dot marks the empty place in its numbers. The manuscript, found in 1881 in present-day Pakistan, is in Oxford's Bodleian Library.
textes.Le manuscrit de Bakhshali, trouvé en 188: The Bakhshali manuscript, found in 1881, writes zero as a dot.
textes.La datation du manuscrit de Bakhshali es: The dating of the Bakhshali manuscript is definitively settled.
textes.Faux. En 2017, trois feuillets ont donné: False. In 2017, three folios gave very different dates, from the 3rd to the 10th century; Oxford revised the whole in 2024, to between 799 and 1102.
textes.Dans quelle région de l'Inde Madhava fon: In what region of India did Madhava found his school, around 1400?
textes.L'école d'astronomie et de mathématiques: The Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics, in south-western India.
textes.Madhava, au Kerala, vers 1400, obtient 1: Madhava, in Kerala, around 1400, obtained 11 decimals of π by an infinite series.
textes.Combien de décimales exactes de π Madhav: How many correct decimals of π did Madhava obtain?
textes.11 décimales, avec 21 termes d'une série: 11 decimals, with 21 terms of a faster series and correction terms.
textes.Les séries de Madhava sont prouvées avoi: Madhava's series are proven to have reached Europe before Gregory and Leibniz.
textes.Faux. Rien ne prouve que les séries du K: False. Nothing proves the Kerala series reached Europe before the 19th century; the discoveries seem independent.
textes.Il n'existe aucune preuve directe que le: There is no direct evidence that the Kerala series reached Europe before the 19th century.
textes.Pourquoi appelle-t-on nos chiffres « ara: Why are our numerals called "Arabic" when they come from India?
textes.Parce que l'Europe les a reçus par le mo: Because Europe received them through the Arab world
textes.Parce qu'ils ont été inventés à Bagdad: Because they were invented in Baghdad
textes.Les livres d'al-Khwarizmi, à Bagdad, pui: Al-Khwarizmi's books, in Baghdad, then Fibonacci's Liber abaci made them known to Europe, which took them for Arabic.
textes.Les livres d'al-Khwarizmi ont fait conna: Al-Khwarizmi's books made Indian numerals known to Europe, which wrongly calls them Arabic numerals.
textes.En 1512, un soldat français lui tranche: In 1512, a French soldier slashed his jaw and palate with a sabre: he was left with a speech impediment.
textes.Tartaglia doit son surnom, « le bègue »,: Tartaglia owed his nickname, "the stammerer", to a sabre blow received in 1512 at the sack of Brescia.
textes.Sous quelle forme Tartaglia transmet-il: In what form did Tartaglia pass his method on to Cardano?
textes.Il lui donne les solutions de trois form: He gave him the solutions of three forms of third-degree equations, in verse, against a promise not to publish them.
textes.Tartaglia a transmis ses solutions de tr: Tartaglia passed on his solutions to three forms of the cubic in verse.
textes.Qui avait trouvé la formule du troisième: Who had found the third-degree formula before Tartaglia?
textes.C'est en découvrant les papiers de del F: It was on discovering del Ferro's papers that Cardano felt free to publish.
textes.L'Ars Magna de Cardan paraît en 1545, av: Cardano's Ars Magna appeared in 1545, with the third and fourth degrees.
textes.Quel élève de Cardan résout les équation: Which pupil of Cardano solved fourth-degree equations?
textes.Sa méthode passe par une équation auxili: His method goes through an auxiliary third-degree equation, hence its dependence on Tartaglia's.
textes.Cardan cherche deux nombres de somme 10: Cardano looks for two numbers with sum 10 and product 40. With 5 + √−15 and 5 − √−15, what is the product 5² − (√−15)², that is 25 − (−15)?
textes.(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² ; ici 5² − (√−1: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²; here 5² − (√−15)² = 25 − (−15) = 25 + 15 = 40. The sum is indeed 5 + 5 = 10. The identity is old; the use of √−15 is Cardano's, in the Ars Magna.
textes.Dans l'Ars Magna, Cardan trouve 5 + √−15: In the Ars Magna, Cardano found 5 + √−15 and 5 − √−15, which he judged as subtle as useless.
textes.Comment Cardan juge-t-il ses racines de: How did Cardano judge his roots of negative numbers?
textes.Aussi subtiles qu'inutiles: As subtle as they are useless
textes.Il les trouve « sophistiques » et inutil: He found them "sophistic" and useless. It took Bombelli, then centuries, to make them full numbers.
textes.Comment Bombelli appelle-t-il le nombre: What did Bombelli call the number we write i?
textes.« Plus de moins » pour i, « moins de moi: "Plus of minus" for i, "minus of minus" for −i. And "plus of minus by plus of minus makes minus": i × i = −1.
textes.En 1572, Bombelli donne les règles de ca: In 1572, Bombelli gave the rules for calculating with complex numbers.
textes.Pour Bombelli, « plus de moins par plus: For Bombelli, "plus of minus by plus of minus makes minus", that is i × i = −1.
textes.Vrai. C'est la règle fondamentale des no: True. It is the fundamental rule of complex numbers, set out in L'Algebra in 1572.
textes.Cardan est l'auteur du premier traité sy: Cardano wrote the first systematic treatise on probability.
textes.Vrai. Joueur invétéré, il écrit vers 156: True. An inveterate gambler, he wrote the Book on Games of Chance around 1564, published only in 1663, with a chapter on cheating.
textes.Le Liber de ludo aleae, écrit vers 1564: The Liber de ludo aleae, written around 1564 and published in 1663, is the first systematic treatment of probability.
textes.En quelle année Napier publie-t-il les l: In what year did Napier publish logarithms?
textes.En 1614, la Mirifici Logarithmorum Canon: In 1614, the Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio, in Latin.
textes.La Descriptio de Napier, en 1614, compte: Napier's Descriptio, in 1614, has about 57 pages of explanation and 90 pages of tables.
textes.Avec des logarithmes en base 10, log 100: With base-10 logarithms, log 100 = 2 and log 1,000 = 3. What is log(100 × 1,000)?
textes.log(a × b) = log a + log b : log(100 × 1: log(a × b) = log a + log b: log(100 × 1,000) = 2 + 3 = 5, and 10⁵ = 100,000. This property is the one John Napier exploited in 1614; base 10 was Henry Briggs's choice.
textes.Henry Briggs rend visite à Napier en 161: Henry Briggs visited Napier in 1615 and then computed base-10 logarithms to 14 decimals.
textes.Les logarithmes transforment une multipl: Logarithms turn a multiplication into an addition.
textes.Vrai. C'est tout leur intérêt : avec une: True. That is their whole point: with a table, multiplying large numbers amounts to adding their logarithms.
textes.Les logarithmes simplifient les longues: Logarithms simplify long multiplications, divisions and root extractions.
textes.Qui a calculé les premiers logarithmes e: Who computed the first base-10 logarithms?
textes.Après sa visite à Napier en 1615, Briggs: After his visit to Napier in 1615, Briggs computed base-10 logarithms, to 14 decimals.
textes.À combien de décimales Briggs calcule-t-: To how many decimals did Briggs compute his base-10 logarithms?
textes.À quoi servaient d'abord les tables de N: What were Napier's tables first used for?
textes.À la trigonométrie sphérique, pour l'ast: Spherical trigonometry, for astronomy and navigation
textes.Le deuxième livre de la Descriptio appli: The second book of the Descriptio applies logarithms to trigonometry, essential for finding one's way on the celestial sphere or at sea.
textes.Les tables de Napier étaient surtout uti: Napier's tables were especially useful in spherical trigonometry, central to astronomy and navigation.
textes.Des réglettes portant des tables de mult: Rods bearing multiplication tables, described in the Rabdology, published in 1617 after his death.
textes.Napier inventa des réglettes numérotées: Napier invented numbering rods for multiplying, described in the 1617 Rabdology.
textes.Napier passait pour magicien auprès de s: Napier was taken for a magician by his contemporaries.
textes.Vrai. On disait qu'il gardait une araign: True. People said he kept a black spider in a box and that his black cockerel was a familiar spirit.
textes.Napier était souvent perçu comme un magi: Napier was often perceived as a magician; people credited him with a black spider and a cockerel familiar.
textes.Quel signe Napier introduit-il dans l'éc: What sign did Napier introduce into the writing of decimal numbers?
textes.Le point qui sépare la partie entière: The point separating the whole part
textes.Il améliore la notation de Simon Stevin: He improved Simon Stevin's notation with a point, our decimal point.
textes.Napier a amélioré la notation décimale d: Napier improved Stevin's decimal notation by introducing the point.
textes.Les logarithmes ont été le principal fac: Logarithms were the largest single factor in the general adoption of decimal arithmetic.
textes.Vrai. Pour utiliser les tables, il falla: True. To use the tables, numbers had to be written as decimals.
textes.Le développement des logarithmes est con: The development of logarithms is credited as the largest single factor in the general adoption of decimal arithmetic.
textes.Comment Napier démasqua-t-il un voleur p: How did Napier unmask a thief among his servants?
textes.Avec un coq couvert de suie, dans une pi: With a soot-covered cockerel, in a dark room
textes.En leur faisant passer un examen: By making them sit an exam
textes.Il annonce que son coq chantera si le vo: He announced that his cockerel would crow if the thief touched it. He had covered it in soot: the servant with clean hands, who dared not touch it, was the culprit.
textes.Napier fait caresser son coq couvert de: Napier had his soot-covered cockerel stroked in the dark, then inspected his servants' hands.
textes.Qui a publié le premier une méthode de c: Who first published a method of calculus, in 1684?
textes.Leibniz publie la Nova methodus en 1684: Leibniz published the Nova methodus in 1684; Newton, who had found it earlier, did not publish until 1704.
textes.Newton invente ses fluxions en 1666 ; Le: Newton invented his fluxions in 1666; Leibniz published first in 1684.
textes.Quel âge a Newton en 1666, quand il inve: How old was Newton in 1666, when he invented his method of fluxions?
textes.23 ans. Il garde pourtant sa méthode pou: 23. Yet he kept his method to himself for decades.
textes.Quel symbole Leibniz invente-t-il pour l: What symbol did Leibniz invent for the integral?
textes.Le S allongé de « summa », la somme : un: The elongated S of "summa", the sum: an integral is a sum of infinitely many small pieces.
textes.Leibniz introduit la notation dy/dx et l: Leibniz introduced the dy/dx notation and the ∫ sign for the integral.
textes.Le rapport de la Royal Society qui a don: The Royal Society report that found for Newton was drafted under his control.
textes.Vrai. Newton, président de la Royal Soci: True. Newton, president of the Royal Society, engineered the 1713 Commercium epistolicum. Leibniz was not even consulted.
textes.Le rapport de la Royal Society de 1713 s: The 1713 Royal Society report on the quarrel was engineered by Newton himself.
textes.Que pensent aujourd'hui les historiens d: What do historians think today of the Newton-Leibniz quarrel?
textes.Le consensus moderne est que les deux ho: The modern consensus is that the two men developed their ideas independently.
textes.Le consensus moderne : les deux hommes o: The modern consensus: the two men developed their ideas independently.
textes.Quel est le premier manuel de calcul dif: What is the first textbook of differential calculus, published in 1696?
textes.Publié sans nom d'auteur par le marquis: Published anonymously by the Marquis de L'Hôpital, it deals only with differential calculus.
textes.En 1696, l'Analyse des infiniment petits: In 1696, L'Hôpital's Analyse des infiniment petits was the first textbook of differential calculus.
textes.Qui est sans doute le véritable auteur d: Who is probably the real author of "L'Hôpital's rule"?
textes.L'Hôpital payait Bernoulli 300 livres pa: L'Hôpital paid Bernoulli 300 francs a year and had the right to use his discoveries as he saw fit.
textes.L'Hôpital versait à Jean Bernoulli 300 f: L'Hôpital paid Johann Bernoulli 300 francs a year; the rule is attributed to Bernoulli.
textes.Qui accuse publiquement Leibniz de plagi: Who publicly accused Leibniz of plagiarism in 1699?
textes.Le Suisse Fatio de Duillier, proche de N: The Swiss Fatio de Duillier, close to Newton, started the quarrel in 1699.
textes.En 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accus: In 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier publicly accused Leibniz of plagiarising Newton.
textes.Combien de ponts reliaient les terres de: How many bridges linked the land masses of Königsberg in Euler's time?
textes.Sept ponts, reliant deux îles et deux ri: Seven bridges, linking two islands and two banks of the Pregel.
textes.Euler montre en 1736 qu'on ne peut pas t: Euler showed in 1736 that the seven bridges of Königsberg cannot each be crossed once.
textes.Pour passer une fois et une seule sur ch: To cross each bridge once and only once, at most how many land masses may be touched by an odd number of bridges?
textes.Deux, le départ et l'arrivée: Two, the start and the end
textes.Chaque fois qu'on entre dans une terre,: Every time you enter a land mass, you leave it: bridges come in pairs, except at the start and the end. Königsberg had four odd ones.
textes.Euler a résolu le problème des ponts en: Euler solved the bridge problem by carefully measuring their lengths.
textes.Faux. Il oublie les distances et ne gard: False. He forgot distances and kept only the land masses and their links: that is the very idea of a graph.
textes.Euler réduit la ville à des terres (nœud: Euler reduced the city to land masses (nodes) and bridges (edges), discarding everything else.
textes.Kaliningrad, en Russie. Il reste cinq po: Kaliningrad, in Russia. Five bridges remain at the original sites, and Euler's walk has become possible there, from one island to the other.
textes.Königsberg est devenue Kaliningrad ; ave: Königsberg became Kaliningrad; with five bridges left, an Eulerian path exists, from one island to the other.
textes.Un cube a 8 sommets, 12 arêtes et 6 face: A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 faces. What is vertices − edges + faces?
textes.S − A + F = 8 − 12 + 6 = 2. La formule S: V − E + F = 8 − 12 + 6 = 2. The formula V − E + F = 2 holds for every convex polyhedron; Euler published it in 1758.
textes.Pour tout polyèdre convexe, sommets − ar: For any convex polyhedron, vertices − edges + faces = 2; Euler stated it in 1758.
textes.Un tétraèdre a 4 sommets et 4 faces. Com: A tetrahedron has 4 vertices and 4 faces. How many edges does it have, according to V − E + F = 2?
textes.S − A + F = 2 donne A = S + F − 2 = 4 +: V − E + F = 2 gives E = V + F − 2 = 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 edges. The formula is Euler's, in 1758.
textes.Qui a noté la formule S − A + F = 2 pour: Who noted the formula V − E + F = 2 for the Platonic solids as early as 1537, without publishing it?
textes.Le Sicilien Maurolico l'écrit dans un ma: The Sicilian Maurolico wrote it in a manuscript that stayed unpublished; Euler stated it for all polyhedra in 1758.
textes.La formule a été énoncée pour les solide: The formula was stated for the Platonic solids in 1537 by Maurolico, in an unpublished manuscript.
textes.Combien de couleurs suffisent pour color: How many colours suffice to colour any map so that no two neighbouring countries share one?
textes.Quatre. Remarqué par Francis Guthrie en: Four. Noticed by Francis Guthrie in 1852 on a map of the counties of England, proved in 1976.
textes.Appel et Haken démontrent le théorème de: Appel and Haken proved the four colour theorem in 1976 with a computer.
textes.La démonstration d'Alfred Kempe, en 1879: Alfred Kempe's 1879 proof was accepted for eleven years before an error was found in it.
textes.Vrai. Percy Heawood trouve la faille en: True. Percy Heawood found the flaw in 1890.
textes.La preuve de Kempe, en 1879, a été large: Kempe's 1879 proof was widely accepted until Heawood found the error in 1890.
textes.Pourquoi la preuve d'Appel et Haken, en: Why was Appel and Haken's 1976 proof controversial?
textes.Elle reposait sur un ordinateur, impossi: It relied on a computer, impossible to check by hand
textes.1 834 configurations vérifiées en plus d: 1,834 configurations checked in over a thousand hours of computing: many doubted such a demonstration was really a proof.
textes.À combien de configurations Appel et Hak: To how many configurations did Appel and Haken reduce the four colour problem?
textes.Que regardait Francis Guthrie quand il a: What was Francis Guthrie looking at when he noticed that four colours were enough?
textes.Une carte des comtés d'Angleterre: A map of the counties of England
textes.En 1852, en coloriant les comtés anglais: In 1852, colouring the English counties, he posed the question that would take more than a century to answer.
textes.Quel postulat d'Euclide les géométries n: Which of Euclid's postulates do non-Euclidean geometries challenge?
textes.Celui qui dit que tous les angles droits: The one saying all right angles are equal
textes.Le cinquième, celui des parallèles. En l: The fifth, the parallel postulate. By denying it, Lobachevsky and Bolyai obtained geometries just as consistent.
textes.Lobatchevski publie en 1829 une géométri: Lobachevsky published in 1829 a geometry denying Euclid's parallel postulate.
textes.Dans la géométrie de Lobatchevski, la so: In Lobachevsky's geometry, the sum of a triangle's angles is:
textes.Moins de 180°. Sur une sphère, à l'inver: Less than 180°. On a sphere, conversely, it exceeds 180°.
textes.Saccheri, en 1733, a découvert la géomét: Saccheri, in 1733, discovered non-Euclidean geometry without realising it.
textes.Vrai. Il croyait prouver qu'elle était a: True. He thought he was proving it absurd, and in fact established its first results.
textes.Saccheri croyait avoir montré la géométr: Saccheri believed he had shown hyperbolic geometry impossible; he had in fact discovered it.
textes.Gauss avait développé ces idées sans les: Gauss had developed these ideas without publishing them; it was he who gave them this name.
textes.C'est Gauss qui a forgé l'expression « g: It was Gauss who coined the term "non-Euclidean geometry".
textes.Où paraît la géométrie de János Bolyai,: Where did János Bolyai's geometry appear, in 1832?
textes.En appendice du manuel de son père: As an appendix to his father's textbook
textes.En appendice du Tentamen, le manuel de m: As an appendix to the Tentamen, the mathematics textbook of his father Farkas Bolyai.
textes.Le travail de Bolyai paraît en 1832 en a: Bolyai's work appeared in 1832 as an appendix to his father's Tentamen.
textes.« À partir de rien, j'ai créé un étrange: "Out of nothing I have created a strange new universe." Who wrote that?
textes.Galois, la veille de sa mort: Galois, the night before his death
textes.En 1823, Bolyai annonce ainsi à son père: In 1823, Bolyai thus announced his new geometry to his father.
textes.Bolyai écrit en 1823 à son père : « à pa: Bolyai wrote to his father in 1823: "out of nothing I have created a strange new universe".
textes.Combien d'officiers János Bolyai affront: How many officers did János Bolyai fight in duels, one after the other?
textes.Treize, en jouant du violon entre deux d: Thirteen, playing his violin between bouts. He disarmed or wounded them all.
textes.Défié par treize officiers, Bolyai les c: Challenged by thirteen officers, Bolyai fought each in turn, playing the violin between bouts.
textes.À quel âge Évariste Galois meurt-il ?: At what age did Évariste Galois die?
textes.À 20 ans, le 31 mai 1832, au lendemain d: At 20, on 31 May 1832, the day after a duel whose causes remain unclear.
textes.Galois meurt le 31 mai 1832, à 20 ans, a: Galois died on 31 May 1832, aged 20, the day after a duel.
textes.Quelle notion mathématique Galois laisse: What mathematical notion did Galois leave behind?
textes.Il emploie le mot « groupe » dans un sen: He used the word "group" in a sense close to the modern one; his ideas founded Galois theory.
textes.Galois fut l'un des premiers à employer: Galois was among the first to use the word "group" in a sense close to its modern technical meaning.
textes.Galois a été le premier à prouver que le: Galois was the first to prove that fifth-degree equations cannot in general be solved by radicals.
textes.Faux. Abel l'avait prouvé en 1824 ; Galo: False. Abel had proved it in 1824; Galois gave a new proof, which explains why.
textes.Abel avait prouvé l'insolubilité de la q: Abel had proved the insolvability of the quintic in 1824; Galois gave a new proof.
textes.Comment Poisson juge-t-il le mémoire de: How did Poisson judge Galois's memoir, in 1831?
textes.Poisson le trouve incompréhensible, tout: Poisson found it incomprehensible, while urging him to publish his complete work.
textes.En 1831, Poisson déclare le travail de G: In 1831, Poisson declared Galois's work "incomprehensible" but urged him to publish.
textes.« Nous devons savoir. Nous saurons. » Qu: "We must know. We shall know." Who said this, engraved on his tombstone?
textes.Hilbert, à Königsberg, le 8 septembre 19: Hilbert, in Königsberg, on 8 September 1930. The day before, at the same congress, Gödel announced it was not possible.
textes.Hilbert proclame « Nous devons savoir. N: Hilbert proclaimed "We must know. We shall know." at Königsberg on 8 September 1930.
textes.Que dit le premier théorème d'incomplétu: What does Gödel's first incompleteness theorem say?
textes.Un système cohérent capable d'arithmétiq: A consistent system capable of arithmetic contains statements it can neither prove nor disprove
textes.Tout système cohérent assez riche pour l: Any consistent system rich enough for arithmetic is incomplete: undecidable statements remain within it.
textes.Gödel publie ses théorèmes d'incomplétud: Gödel published his incompleteness theorems in 1931.
textes.Selon le second théorème de Gödel, un sy: According to Gödel's second theorem, a consistent system capable of arithmetic can prove its own consistency.
textes.Faux. C'est justement ce qu'il ne peut p: False. That is precisely what it cannot do, hence the blow to Hilbert's programme.
