textes.le débarquement de la baie des Cochons,: the Bay of Pigs invasion, in 1961
textes.le premier pas sur la Lune: the first step on the Moon
textes.L'équipe de Kennedy accepte sans examen: Kennedy's team accepted the CIA's plan to invade Cuba without scrutiny; objections were brushed aside, doubts went unspoken. The operation turned into a disaster.
textes.Janis étudie aussi l'attaque de Pearl Ha: Janis also studied the Pearl Harbor attack, in 1941: Washington had warned the base's officers, who did not take the warning seriously.
textes.Pendant la crise des missiles de Cuba (1: During the Cuban missile crisis (1962), how did Kennedy avoid groupthink?
textes.il fait venir des experts extérieurs, di: he brought in outside experts, split the group and sometimes left the room
textes.il décide seul, sans réunion: he decided alone, with no meetings
textes.Sans le chef dans la pièce, chacun ose p: With the boss out of the room, everyone dares to speak; subgroups generate several options; outside views break the consensus.
textes.Janis oppose ce succès au fiasco de la b: Janis contrasts this success with the Bay of Pigs fiasco a year earlier, partly involving the same men.
textes.Dans l'étude « Pygmalion à l'école » (19: In the "Pygmalion in the classroom" study (1968), 20% of pupils were randomly labelled "bloomers". Result:
textes.ils progressent un peu plus, surtout en: they made somewhat greater gains, mainly in first and second grade
textes.ils deviennent tous premiers de la class: they all became top of the class
textes.Les attentes des enseignants pèsent, mai: Teachers' expectations matter, but the gap was clear only among the youngest. All classes had improved, bloomers or not.
textes.Robert Rosenthal et Lenore Jacobson trav: Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson worked in a Californian elementary school. All classes took a disguised IQ test at the start and end of the study.
textes.Les études plus récentes jugent l'effet: More recent studies judge the Pygmalion effect at school to be small and often temporary.
textes.La méta-analyse de Jussim et Harber (200: Jussim and Harber's meta-analysis (2005) concludes that the effects are "usually small and temporary". Raudenbush (1984): once the teacher has known the pupils for two weeks, the effect falls almost to zero.
textes.Dès 1968, Robert Thorndike juge le test: As early as 1968, Robert Thorndike judged the test used to be flawed and quoted a colleague: "When the clock strikes thirteen, doubt is cast not only on the last stroke but also all that have gone before."
textes.Le récit des « 38 témoins » restés passi: The story of the "38 witnesses" who stood by during Kitty Genovese's murder (New York, 1964):
textes.était très exagéré, le New York Times l': was greatly exaggerated, as the New York Times acknowledged in 2016
textes.Peu de voisins avaient vraiment vu l'att: Few neighbours had actually seen the attack, and some called the police. Yet the story launched research into the "bystander effect".
textes.Une étude de 2007 avait déjà montré que: A 2007 study had already shown that the figure of 38 witnesses did not hold up; the newspaper that had published it admitted it in 2016.
textes.Latané et Rodin mettent des participants: Latané and Rodin put participants in front of a woman in distress. Alone, 70% helped her. Next to a stranger:
textes.La responsabilité se dilue : chacun atte: Responsibility is diluted: each waits for the other to move, and reads their calm as a sign that nothing serious is happening.
textes.Dans l'expérience de la fumée de Latané: In Latané and Darley's smoke experiment, a person alone noticed the smoke within about 5 seconds; in a group, up to 20 seconds.
textes.En 2019, l'équipe de Richard Philpot ana: In 2019, Richard Philpot's team analysed 219 real street disputes filmed by CCTV. Someone intervened:
textes.dans plus de 9 cas sur 10: in more than 9 cases out of 10
textes.Dans la vraie vie, la foule aide le plus: In real life, crowds usually help: the more bystanders, the better the chance that at least one acts.
textes.Les images venaient de trois villes : La: The footage came from three cities: Lancaster in the UK, Amsterdam and Cape Town. An outcome opposite to what the theory predicts.
textes.Frederic Bartlett fait raconter à des An: Frederic Bartlett had English people retell a Native American tale, The War of the Ghosts. Retelling it, they:
textes.oublient ou transforment ce qui leur est: forget or change what is foreign to them: "canoes" become "boats"
textes.Ce qui n'entre pas dans nos schémas, nos: What does not fit our schemas, our usual frames, is erased or replaced by something familiar. The memory adapts to the one remembering.
textes.Bartlett décrit ces expériences dans Rem: Bartlett described these experiments in Remembering, in 1932. He then ran the psychology laboratory at Cambridge and had held the chair of experimental psychology there since 1931.
textes.Pour Bartlett, se souvenir, c'est relire: For Bartlett, remembering means replaying a faithful recording stored in the brain.
textes.C'est l'inverse : la mémoire est reconst: The opposite: memory is reconstructive. At each recall, we rebuild the memory from a few traces, from what we know and what we expect.
textes.Dans ses expériences de reproduction rép: In his repeated-reproduction experiments, the same person retold the story several times, weeks apart: the longer the interval, the further the account drifted from the original.
textes.Loftus et Palmer (1974) montrent un film: Loftus and Palmer (1974) show a film of a crash and then ask: "How fast were the cars going when they … each other?" Which verb produced the highest speeds?
textes.Avec smashed, la moyenne est d'environ 4: With smashed, the average was about 41 miles per hour; with contacted, about 32. A single word in the question shifted the memory.
textes.La première expérience porte sur 45 étud: The first experiment involved 45 students at the University of Washington. The five verbs: smashed, collided, bumped, hit, contacted.
textes.Une semaine après le film, Loftus et Pal: A week after the film, Loftus and Palmer ask: "Did you see any broken glass?" There was none. What percentage of the "smashed" group says yes?
textes.16 sur 50, soit 32 %. Avec « hit », 7 su: 16 out of 50, or 32%. With "hit", 7 out of 50 (14%); with no speed question, 12%. The word "smashed" manufactured broken glass.
textes.Cette seconde expérience porte sur 150 é: This second experiment involved 150 students, in three groups of 50.
textes.On montre un accident avec un panneau «: People are shown a crash with a "Stop" sign, then a question mentions a "Yield" sign. Later, many witnesses:
textes.C'est l'effet de désinformation : une in: This is the misinformation effect: information received after the event slips into the memory of the event itself.
textes.Cette étude du panneau, menée par Elizab: This sign study, led by Elizabeth Loftus and her colleagues, dates from 1978.
textes.Pourquoi Elizabeth Loftus est-elle souve: Why is Elizabeth Loftus often called before the courts?
textes.comme experte de la fragilité des témoig: as an expert on the fragility of eyewitness testimony
textes.Un témoin sincère peut se tromper : elle: A sincere witness can be wrong: she explains to juries how questions, photos or accounts heard afterwards change memories.
textes.Elle a témoigné dans plus de 300 affaire: She has testified in more than 300 cases, including Harvey Weinstein's trial in 2020. In 2002, a ranking placed her 58th among the most influential psychologists of the 20th century.
textes.Un souvenir très vif, dont on est absolu: A very vivid memory, of which one is absolutely sure, is necessarily accurate.
textes.La confiance et l'exactitude ne vont pas: Confidence and accuracy do not go together. The sharpest memories can be largely reconstructed.
textes.Une étude menée sur des étudiants le len: A study of students the day after 11 September 2001 concluded that flashbulb memories are not special in their accuracy, but only in their perceived accuracy.
textes.En 1977, Roger Brown et James Kulik appe: In 1977, Roger Brown and James Kulik named "flashbulb memories":
textes.les souvenirs très vifs du moment où l'o: the vivid memories of the moment one learned shocking news
textes.On se « voit » encore, des années après: Years later, we still "see" ourselves: where we were, with whom, what we were doing. The feeling of precision is strong.
textes.Après l'explosion de la navette Challeng: After the Challenger shuttle exploded in 1986, Ulric Neisser and Nicole Harsch questioned students. Three years later, their memories were not very accurate, yet they remained highly confident.
textes.« Je le savais depuis le début ! » après: "I knew it all along!" after the fact is:
textes.Une fois l'issue connue, elle nous paraî: Once the outcome is known, it seems predictable, and we believe we foresaw it. The memory of what we thought before is rewritten.
textes.Baruch Fischhoff le décrit en 1975 sous: Baruch Fischhoff described it in 1975 as "creeping determinism"; he wanted to explain a remark by the psychologist Paul Meehl in 1973: clinicians often overestimate their ability to have foreseen the outcome.
textes.Avant le voyage de Nixon à Pékin et Mosc: Before Nixon's trip to Beijing and Moscow (1972), Fischhoff and Beyth had people estimate its chances of success. After the trip, the participants:
textes.se souviennent avoir donné plus de chanc: remembered giving higher odds to what actually happened
textes.pensent s'être trompés sur tout: thought they had been wrong about everything
textes.Connaître l'issue a réécrit le souvenir: Knowing the outcome rewrote their memory of their own forecasts.
textes.Le biais rétrospectif touche aussi les e: Hindsight bias affects experts too: a radiologist who knows an abnormality is on the image finds it easier to see than it was, and jurors judge a defendant more able to have prevented the harm.
textes.se demander comment les choses auraient: asking how things might have turned out otherwise
textes.Imaginer d'autres issues possibles rappe: Imagining other possible outcomes reminds us the result was not written in advance. Writing forecasts down beforehand helps too: they can no longer be rewritten.
textes.Les chercheurs appellent cette parade la: Researchers call this remedy counterfactual thinking: prompting people to explicitly consider other outcomes has proved effective against the bias.
textes.Dans l'expérience de Loftus et Palmer, u: In Loftus and Palmer's experiment, some students "remember" broken glass that was not in the film.
textes.La question avec « smashed » a suggéré u: The question with "smashed" suggested a violent crash; memory added the detail that went with it.
textes.Avec des récits inventés, comme s'être p: With made-up stories, such as getting lost as a child in a shopping mall, some participants end up producing a false memory, partial or complete.
textes.Les prix avaient flambé pendant l'hiver: Prices had soared during the winter of 1636-37. In February 1637, contract prices suddenly collapsed.
textes.Au plus fort, certains bulbes se vendent: At the peak, some bulbs sold for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled artisan.
textes.Le Semper Augustus, la tulipe la plus cé: The Semper Augustus, the most famous tulip of the mania, was traded at around:
textes.rien : il n'était pas à vendre: nothing: it was not for sale
textes.Une fortune pour un bulbe. Ses pétales b: A fortune for one bulb. Its white petals bore a carmine flame; we now know those flames came from a virus.
textes.On négocie surtout dans les tavernes, av: Trading happened mostly in taverns, with contracts for future delivery: people bought and resold bulbs still in the ground.
textes.D'après l'historienne Anne Goldgar, la t: According to the historian Anne Goldgar, tulip mania ruined a large part of the Dutch economy.
textes.Elle n'a trouvé dans les archives qu'une: In the archives she found only a handful of people in trouble, fewer than half a dozen. The pamphlets against speculation, long taken as evidence of ruin, were mainly religiously motivated.
textes.Le récit catastrophiste a été popularisé: The catastrophic story was popularised in 1841 by Charles Mackay, who even tells of a sailor eating a precious bulb, taking it for an onion.
textes.En 1841, Charles Mackay publie Extraordi: In 1841, Charles Mackay published Extraordinary Popular Delusions. It covers:
textes.les bulles financières, l'alchimie et la: financial bubbles, alchemy and witch hunts
textes.Mackay range ensemble les folies collect: Mackay groups collective follies together: the South Sea Bubble, Law's Mississippi scheme, tulip mania, the Crusades, relics, prophecies.
textes.La première édition compte trois volumes: The first edition had three volumes: national delusions, peculiar follies, philosophical delusions. The 1852 edition had only two.
textes.Allport et Postman (1947) font passer un: Allport and Postman (1947) passed a message by word of mouth. After 5 or 6 transmissions:
textes.environ 70 % des détails ont disparu: about 70% of the details had disappeared
textes.le message a doublé de longueur: the message had doubled in length
textes.La rumeur raccourcit vite, puis se stabi: The rumour shortens fast, then settles on a few striking elements.
textes.Ils décrivent trois mécanismes : le nive: They describe three mechanisms: levelling (details drop out), sharpening (others are magnified), assimilation (the story bends to each person's expectations).
textes.Dans l'image utilisée par Allport et Pos: In the picture used by Allport and Postman, an ambulance carries crates marked "TNT". What did participants often report?
textes.que l'ambulance transportait du matériel: that the ambulance carried medical supplies
textes.C'est l'assimilation : une ambulance « d: This is assimilation: an ambulance "must" carry medicine, so memory corrects the picture.
textes.En 1944, Robert Knapp avait déjà classé: In 1944, Robert Knapp had already classified over 1,000 wartime rumours, collected by a Boston Herald column, the "Rumor Clinic".
textes.Robert Knapp (1944) range les rumeurs en: Robert Knapp (1944) sorted rumours into three families. Which is one of them?
textes.les rumeurs qui enfoncent un coin dans u: wedge-driving rumours that split a group
textes.Les trois familles : les rumeurs-souhait: The three families: pipe-dream rumours (what we hope for), bogie rumours (what we fear), and those meant to divide a group.
textes.Pour Knapp, une rumeur est une propositi: For Knapp, a rumour is a proposition for belief of topical reference disseminated without official verification.
textes.En mai 1969, la « rumeur d'Orléans » acc: In May 1969, the "Orléans rumour" accused Jewish shopkeepers:
textes.de faire disparaître des clientes dans l: of making customers disappear in their fitting rooms
textes.Aucune disparition n'avait eu lieu. Les: No disappearance had occurred. The authorities' denials did not stop the rumour, which in turn accused them of complicity.
textes.Six magasins de vêtements sont visés. Un: Six clothing shops were targeted. A team of five sociologists led by Edgar Morin investigated for three days on site and published La Rumeur d'Orléans the same year.
textes.Dans Psychologie des foules (1895), Gust: In The Crowd (1895), Gustave Le Bon compares the individual in a crowd to:
textes.un grain de sable que le vent soulève à: a grain of sand that the wind stirs up at will
textes.Pour Le Bon, dans la foule, l'individu p: For Le Bon, in a crowd the individual loses his own judgement and is carried away by emotional contagion.
textes.Le livre a beaucoup influencé : Freud le: The book was very influential: Freud discussed it in 1921, and Hitler may have drawn on it for his propaganda.
textes.Le 30 octobre 1938, La Guerre des mondes: On 30 October 1938, Orson Welles' The War of the Worlds aired on radio. According to today's historians:
textes.la grande panique nationale a été très e: the great national panic was greatly exaggerated by the press
textes.tout le pays a fui les villes: the whole country fled the cities
textes.Peu de gens écoutaient, et presque perso: Few people were listening, and almost nobody was fooled. Newspapers, which were losing advertising revenue to radio, played up the rare cases of fear. The panic became the real rumour.
textes.Le soir même, un sondage Hooper auprès d: That night, a Hooper survey of 5,000 households found only about 2% listening to the play. The psychologist Hadley Cantril would nonetheless claim 6 million listeners, 1.2 million of them frightened.
textes.réfuter une ânerie demande beaucoup plus: refuting nonsense takes far more energy than producing it
textes.plus une info est partagée, plus elle es: the more information is shared, the truer it is
textes.Alberto Brandolini, programmeur italien,: Alberto Brandolini, an Italian programmer, wrote it in January 2013: the amount of energy needed to refute bullshit is an order of magnitude bigger than that needed to produce it.
textes.L'idée est ancienne : en 1710, Jonathan: The idea is old: in 1710, Jonathan Swift wrote that falsehood flies, and the truth comes limping after it.
textes.L'article frauduleux d'Andrew Wakefield: Andrew Wakefield's fraudulent article linking a vaccine and autism (1998) illustrates Brandolini's law: long debunked, it still circulates.
textes.L'article a été retiré et Wakefield a pe: The article was retracted and Wakefield lost his licence to practise medicine. The rumour goes on.
textes.L'article de Wakefield, publié en 1998,: Wakefield's article, published in 1998, is the example given on the page devoted to Brandolini's law.
textes.Où l'épidémie de 430 av. J.-C. frappe-t-: Where did the epidemic of 430 BC strike first, according to Thucydides?
textes.Au Pirée, le port d'Athènes: At Piraeus, the port of Athens
textes.Elle touche d'abord le Pirée, puis gagne: It first hit Piraeus, then reached the upper city, where deaths multiplied. It was at the port that the enemy was accused of poisoning the water.
textes.Au Pirée, en 430 av. J.-C., on accuse le: In Piraeus, in 430 BC, the Peloponnesians were accused of poisoning the reservoirs.
textes.De quoi les habitants du Pirée accusent-: What did the people of Piraeus accuse the Peloponnesians of during the plague?
textes.La rumeur est d'autant plus étrange qu'i: The rumour is all the stranger since there were as yet no wells in Piraeus, Thucydides points out: a culprit was needed.
textes.Thucydide a attrapé la peste d'Athènes e: Thucydides caught the plague of Athens and died of it.
textes.Faux. Il l'a attrapée et y a survécu ; i: False. He caught it and survived; he writes that he can describe it all the better for having had it himself. He died around 400 BC.
textes.Thucydide, général en 424 av. J.-C., est: Thucydides, a general in 424 BC, was exiled for twenty years after the loss of Amphipolis; he survived the plague.
textes.Pendant la peste, quel mot les Athéniens: During the plague, which word did the Athenians settle on in the old verse "A Dorian war shall come and with it…"?
textes.Certains tenaient pour « famine ». Mais: Some held out for "dearth". But the plague was there, and "death" was chosen: people, says Thucydides, make their memories fit their sufferings.
textes.Thucydide note que les Athéniens ont acc: Thucydides notes that the Athenians made their memory of an old verse fit their sufferings.
textes.Selon Thucydide, qui gouvernait vraiment: According to Thucydides, who really ruled Athens when Harmodius and Aristogeiton killed Hipparchus?
textes.Les Athéniens croyaient qu'Hipparque éta: The Athenians believed Hipparchus was the tyrant. Thucydides corrects them: it was Hippias, the eldest son of Pisistratus, only driven out in 510 BC.
textes.Thucydide corrige les idées reçues de se: Thucydides corrects the received ideas of his contemporaries and deplores that people accept the first story to hand.
textes.Selon Thucydide, chaque roi de Sparte di: According to Thucydides, each king of Sparta has two votes in council.
textes.Faux. C'est une idée reçue qu'il corrige: False. It is a received idea that he corrects: each king has only one vote. He also mentions the "Pitane company", which never existed.
textes.Comment Thucydide décrit-il l'attitude d: How does Thucydides describe most people's attitude to the truth?
textes.Ils acceptent la première histoire venue: They accept the first story that comes along
textes.La plupart des gens, écrit-il, se donnen: Most people, he writes, take very little trouble to seek the truth. He says he checked every fact, without trusting his first impression.
textes.En 424 av. J.-C., les alliés d'Athènes s: In 424 BC, Athens's allies turned to the Spartan Brasidas. How does Thucydides explain it?
textes.Ils confient à un espoir irréfléchi ce q: They entrust to careless hope what they long for
textes.Ils se trompaient sur la puissance d'Ath: They misjudged Athens's power: it is mankind's habit, notes Thucydides, to believe what they long for and to reason away what they dislike. Today we speak of wishful thinking.
textes.Thucydide, IV, 108 : c'est l'habitude de: Thucydides, IV, 108: it is a habit of mankind to entrust to careless hope what they long for.
textes.Après la perte d'Amphipolis, Thucydide a: After the loss of Amphipolis, Thucydides spent twenty years in exile.
textes.Vrai. Général en 424 av. J.-C., il arriv: True. A general in 424 BC, he arrived too late to save Amphipolis, taken by Brasidas. Athens exiled him: "it was also my fate to be an exile from my country for twenty years".
textes.En combien de causes Ibn Khaldun range-t: Into how many causes does Ibn Khaldun sort the errors of historians in the Muqaddimah?
textes.Sept, dont la partialité, la confiance e: Seven, including partisanship, overconfidence in sources and flattery of the powerful. The most serious, for him, is ignorance of the laws that govern societies.
textes.Dans la Muqaddima, en 1377, Ibn Khaldun: In the Muqaddimah, in 1377, Ibn Khaldun sorted the errors of historians into seven causes.
textes.Quel récit d'al-Masudi Ibn Khaldun juge-: Which account by al-Masudi does Ibn Khaldun judge impossible?
textes.Une ville bâtie en un jour: A city built in a day
textes.Un roi vivant mille ans: A king living a thousand years
textes.Le pays n'aurait pas pu contenir une tel: The land could not have held such an army, he objects, and so large an army could not have manoeuvred as one body. Before believing a story, ask whether it is possible.
textes.Quelle épidémie a emporté les parents d': Which epidemic carried off Ibn Khaldun's parents, in Tunis, when he was about 17?
textes.Né en 1332, il a vu de près la peste noi: Born in 1332, he saw the Black Death at close range, as Thucydides had seen the plague of Athens. He finished the first version of the Muqaddimah in 1377.
textes.Ibn Khaldun, né à Tunis en 1332, perd se: Ibn Khaldun, born in Tunis in 1332, lost his parents in the plague of 1348-1349.
textes.Qui sont les Kalamas, à qui le Bouddha s: Who are the Kalamas, whom the Buddha addresses in the Kalama Sutta?
textes.Un clan de la ville de Kesaputta: A clan of the town of Kesaputta
textes.Ils voient défiler de nombreux maîtres e: They saw many teachers pass through and did not know which to believe. The text is in the Anguttara Nikaya, at number 3.65.
textes.Le Kalama Sutta (Anguttara Nikaya 3.65): The Kalama Sutta (Anguttara Nikaya 3.65) advises not to rely on tradition, rumour or a teacher's prestige alone.
textes.Selon le Kalama Sutta, sur quoi peut-on: According to the Kalama Sutta, what can one finally rely on?
textes.Ce qu'on a reconnu soi-même comme bon, e: What one has recognised oneself as good, and the wise approve
textes.La tradition, la rumeur, les écritures o: Tradition, rumour, scripture or a teacher's prestige are not enough on their own. One must know for oneself that a thing is good, praised by the wise and beneficial.
textes.Pour le moine Bhikkhu Bodhi, le Kalama S: For the monk Bhikkhu Bodhi, the Kalama Sutta allows everyone to believe whatever they please.
textes.Faux. Bodhi critique cette lecture : le: False. Bodhi criticises this reading: the text is no praise of radical scepticism. It gives criteria, such as avoiding what springs from greed, hatred and delusion.
textes.Dans l'Udana, comment finit la dispute d: In the Udana, how does the blind men's dispute over the elephant end?
textes.Chacun défend l'objet qu'il a touché, et: Each defends the object he touched, and they fight, to the king's great delight. In an older version described by Paul Griffiths, they do not fight.
textes.Dans l'Udana, des aveugles touchent chac: In the Udana, blind men each touch one part of an elephant and come to blows.
textes.Quelle idée jaïne le conte des aveugles: Which Jain idea does the tale of the blind men and the elephant serve to explain?
textes.Pour l'anekantavada, aucun point de vue: For anekantavada, no single viewpoint grasps all of reality. The Jains have the tale in their most ancient texts.
textes.Chez le poète persan Rumi, où se trouve: In the Persian poet Rumi's version, where is the elephant?
textes.Au fond d'un puits: At the bottom of a well
textes.Des hommes qui voient le touchent dans l: Sighted men touch it in the dark. Rumi concludes: if each had had a candle, their differences would have disappeared.
textes.Le poème « It was six men of Indostan »: The poem "It was six men of Indostan" is the work of a 19th-century American poet.
textes.Vrai. John Godfrey Saxe (1816-1887) en t: True. John Godfrey Saxe (1816-1887) drew from it a moral against theologians who argue about what none of them has seen.
textes.En quelle année naît le philosophe chino: In what year was the Chinese philosopher Wang Chong born?
textes.En 27, sous les Han de l'Est ; il meurt: In 27 AD, under the Eastern Han; he died around 97. Poor, he is said to have studied standing at the booksellers' stalls of Luoyang.
textes.Wang Chong (27-vers 97) attribue le tonn: Wang Chong (27-c. 97) attributed thunder to fire or heat and demanded evidence.
textes.D'où vient le tonnerre, selon Wang Chong: Where does thunder come from, according to Wang Chong?
textes.De la colère du Ciel contre les méchants: From Heaven's anger at the wicked
textes.Il rejette l'idée d'un Ciel qui punit :: He rejects the idea of a punishing Heaven: for him, Heaven has no purpose towards us, either benevolent or hostile.
textes.Wang Chong en doute : si les fantômes ét: Wang Chong doubts it: if ghosts were the souls of the dead, they should…
textes.apparaître nus, car les vêtements n'ont: appear naked, since clothes have no souls
textes.Il ajoute qu'ils seraient bien plus nomb: He adds that they would far outnumber the living. He does not explicitly deny spirits, but demands evidence.
textes.Combien de chapitres compte le texte du: How many chapters does the received text of the Lunheng have?
textes.85 chapitres, en 30 rouleaux ; mais le c: 85 chapters, in 30 scrolls; but chapter 44 contains only its title, so 84 is a better count.
textes.Le Lunheng, publié vers 80, compte 85 ch: The Lunheng, published around 80 AD, has 85 chapters; Needham rendered its title "Discourses Weighed in the Balance".
textes.Comment Joseph Needham traduit-il le tit: How did Joseph Needham translate the title Lunheng?
textes.Lun veut dire discourir, heng peser, la: Lun means to discuss, heng to weigh, the balance. Alfred Forke published a translation in 1907.
textes.Entre quelles années Ibn al-Haytham écri: Between which years did Ibn al-Haytham write his Book of Optics?
textes.Au Caire, au début du XIe siècle. Selon: In Cairo, in the early 11th century. According to legend, he was then in hiding, having feigned madness, until the caliph al-Hakim died in 1021.
textes.Le Livre de l'optique d'Ibn al-Haytham,: Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics, in seven volumes, dates from 1011 to 1021.
textes.Quelle idée d'Euclide et de Ptolémée Ibn: Which idea of Euclid and Ptolemy did Ibn al-Haytham reject?
textes.L'œil lance des rayons vers les objets: The eye sends rays out towards objects
textes.Pour lui, c'est la lumière venue des obj: For him, it is light coming from objects that enters the eye: the intromission theory, accepted today. He kept, on the other hand, propagation in straight lines.
textes.En combien de volumes Ibn al-Haytham a-t: In how many volumes did Ibn al-Haytham write his Book of Optics?
textes.Sept volumes : la vision, la lumière, l': Seven volumes: vision, light, the eye, mirrors, refraction. Translated into Latin, it fed European optics until the 17th century.
textes.La Lune paraît plus grosse à l'horizon p: The Moon looks bigger on the horizon because it is then much closer to us.
textes.Faux. Sa distance réelle ne varie que d': False. Its real distance varies by only about 1.5% between horizon and zenith, and its measured apparent size does not change. It is an illusion.
textes.L'illusion de la Lune : la Lune paraît e: The Moon illusion: the Moon looks about 50 percent larger on the horizon, without changing apparent size.
textes.Comment vérifier soi-même que la Lune ne: How can you check for yourself that the Moon does not grow on the horizon?
textes.Un caillou tenu à bout de bras la cache: A pebble held at arm's length covers it in both cases
textes.La regarder à travers un verre d'eau: Look at it through a glass of water
textes.Fermer un œil puis l'autre: Close one eye then the other
textes.Le caillou couvre la Lune aussi bien en: The pebble covers the Moon equally well high and low; a theodolite or photographs taken at different heights confirm it.
textes.De combien de pour cent environ la Lune: By roughly what percentage does the Moon look larger on the horizon, according to Ross and Plug?
textes.L'illusion varie, mais l'agrandissement: The illusion varies, but the perceived increase in diameter is around 50 percent. Nothing of the kind on photographs.
textes.Comment Ibn al-Haytham explique-t-il l'i: How did Ibn al-Haytham explain the Moon illusion?
textes.Par les objets intermédiaires qui nous f: By the intervening objects that make us judge distance
textes.Par la colère des astres: By the anger of the stars
textes.Par un défaut des yeux de chacun: By a flaw in each person's eyes
textes.À l'horizon, la Lune est derrière des ch: On the horizon, the Moon lies beyond fields, trees, houses: it seems far, and so large. High in the sky, with nothing in between, it seems closer and smaller.
textes.Aujourd'hui, l'illusion de la Lune est e: Today, the Moon illusion is fully explained.
textes.Faux. Elle reste discutée ; Ross et Plug: False. It remains debated; Ross and Plug conclude that no single theory has won. In 1962, Kaufman and Rock showed the importance of distance cues.
textes.Sous quel nom l'Occident latin connaissa: Under what name did the Latin West know Ibn al-Haytham?
textes.Alhazen. Né à Bassora vers 965, il meurt: Alhazen. Born in Basra around 965, he died in Cairo around 1040. He has sometimes been called the "first true scientist".
textes.Ibn al-Haytham (vers 965-vers 1040), dit: Ibn al-Haytham (c. 965-c. 1040), known as Alhazen, was born in Basra and died in Cairo.
textes.Que raconte la légende sur Ibn al-Haytha: What does the legend say about Ibn al-Haytham and the caliph al-Hakim?
textes.Il aurait simulé la folie pour lui échap: He feigned madness to escape him
textes.Il l'aurait guéri de la peste: He cured him of the plague
textes.Selon un récit, il avait proposé un barr: According to one account, he had proposed a dam on the Nile, then realised it was impractical. The feigned madness and his hiding until 1021 belong to legend.
textes.Sous quel titre latin le Livre de l'opti: Under what Latin title did the Book of Optics circulate in Europe?
textes.De aspectibus, ou Perspectiva, traduit à: De aspectibus, or Perspectiva, translated in the late 12th or early 13th century. Roger Bacon drew on it in his Opus Majus, in 1267.
textes.En quelle année Friedrich Risner imprime: In what year did Friedrich Risner print Ibn al-Haytham's optics in his Opticae thesaurus?
textes.En 1572, plus de cinq siècles après sa r: In 1572, more than five centuries after it was written. The book influenced European optics, physics and mathematics from the 13th to the 17th century.
textes.De quel livre de la Bible vient le rite: Which book of the Bible does the scapegoat rite come from?
textes.Au chapitre 16, le jour du Grand Pardon,: In chapter 16, on the Day of Atonement, one of the two goats is driven into the wilderness, laden with the people's sins.
textes.Le bouc émissaire vient du Lévitique, ch: The scapegoat comes from Leviticus, chapter 16; Tyndale coined the English word scapegoat in 1530.
textes.En quelle année William Tyndale forge-t-: In what year did William Tyndale coin the English word scapegoat, translating the Bible?
textes.En 1530, d'après le latin caper emissari: In 1530, from the Latin caper emissarius, the "sent-away goat". The King James Bible took up the word in 1611.
textes.À Abdère, en Grèce, un pauvre servant de: In Abdera, in Greece, a poor man serving as scapegoat was driven out of the city with stones.
textes.Vrai. On le nourrissait bien, on le prom: True. He was well fed, led around the walls, then driven out. Such rites were used in times of famine, drought or plague.
textes.Pendant la peste noire, de quoi accuse-t: During the Black Death, what were Jews accused of?
textes.La rumeur court de 1348 à 1351. Des aveu: The rumour ran from 1348 to 1351. Confessions were extracted under torture, and some 510 Jewish communities were destroyed.
textes.De 1348 à 1351, on accuse les Juifs d'em: From 1348 to 1351, Jews were accused of poisoning wells; in Strasbourg, about 2,000 were burned on 14 February 1349.
textes.Combien de Juifs environ sont brûlés vif: About how many Jews were burned alive in Strasbourg on 14 February 1349?
textes.Environ 2 000. La peste n'avait même pas: About 2,000. The plague had not even reached the city yet: the culprit was named before the disease arrived.
textes.Quand les Juifs de Strasbourg sont massa: When the Jews of Strasbourg were massacred, in February 1349, the plague was already ravaging the city.
False. It had not yet arrived there. Fear of the disease was enough.
textes.Quel argument le pape Clément VI oppose-: What argument did Pope Clement VI put in 1348 to those accusing the Jews?
textes.Les Juifs meurent aussi de la peste: Jews are dying of the plague too
textes.La peste est une punition des astres: The plague is a punishment from the stars
textes.Il ajoute que la peste frappe des région: He added that the plague struck regions where there were no Jews. His two bulls date from 6 July and 26 September 1348; he also offered protection in Avignon.
textes.Quel roi accueille les Juifs qui fuient: Which king welcomed the Jews fleeing the persecutions of the Black Death?
textes.Ces migrations vers la Pologne et la Lit: These migrations to Poland and Lithuania partly explain the size of Poland's Jewish population for centuries.
textes.Qui est l'auteur principal du Malleus ma: Who is the main author of the Malleus Maleficarum, the Hammer of Witches?
textes.Kramer le publie à Spire en 1486. Jacob: Kramer published it in Speyer in 1486. Jacob Sprenger was only presented as co-author from 1519, and his role is disputed.
textes.Le Malleus maleficarum de Heinrich Krame: Heinrich Kramer's Malleus Maleficarum appeared in Speyer in 1486.
textes.Quelle part des personnes condamnées pou: Roughly what percentage of those convicted of witchcraft were women?
textes.Environ 80 %. Le Marteau des sorcières a: About 80 percent. The Hammer of Witches claimed that women yield more easily to the devil.
textes.Les procès de sorcellerie font de 40 000: Witch trials killed 40,000 to 60,000 people, mostly from 1560 to 1630; about 80 percent of those convicted were women.
textes.Que soutient le médecin Johann Weyer en: What did the physician Johann Weyer argue in 1563 about women accused of witchcraft?
textes.Elles sont payées par l'ennemi: They are paid by the enemy
textes.Pour lui, la sorcellerie est impossible: For him, witchcraft is impossible: those who confess suffer from a mental disturbance. He asked for clemency; Jean Bodin and King James VI of Scotland opposed him.
textes.En 1563, Johann Weyer décrit les accusée: In 1563, Johann Weyer described women accused of witchcraft as melancholic and sick.
textes.Quand les procès de sorcellerie atteigne: When did witch trials reach their peak in Europe?
textes.Pas au Moyen Âge, mais au temps de la Re: Not in the Middle Ages, but in the age of the Renaissance and early science. Some historians link this peak to the cooling climate, an explanation judged too simple.
textes.À qui Roger Bacon envoie-t-il son Opus m: To whom did Roger Bacon send his Opus Majus in 1267?
The pope had asked him for it. The work has seven parts, from biblical languages to optics and experimental science.
textes.En 1267, l'Opus majus de Roger Bacon cla: In 1267, Roger Bacon's Opus Majus classified four causes of error.
textes.Laquelle de ces causes d'erreur figure d: Which of these causes of error appears in Roger Bacon's list?
textes.Ses quatre causes : l'autorité fragile,: His four causes: weak authority, custom, the ignorance of the crowd, and ignorance hidden behind a show of knowledge.
textes.Sur quels savants s'appuie la partie opt: Which scholars does the optics part of the Opus Majus draw on?
textes.Alhazen, c'est Ibn al-Haytham, dont l'op: Alhazen is Ibn al-Haytham, whose optics circulated in Latin. Bacon deals with the eye, light, mirrors and lenses.
textes.Selon Francis Bacon, d'où viennent les i: According to Francis Bacon, where do the idols of the marketplace come from?
textes.Des mots et des échanges entre les gens: From words and exchanges between people
textes.Le langage confus égare : un mot savant: Confused language misleads: a technical word taken in its everyday sense, and there is an error. The marketplace is where people talk.
textes.En 1620, le Novum Organum de Francis Bac: In 1620, Francis Bacon's Novum Organum described four idols: tribe, cave, marketplace, theatre.
textes.Que désignent les idoles de la caverne ?: What do the idols of the cave refer to?
textes.Les erreurs propres à chaque individu: The errors specific to each individual
textes.Les erreurs de toute l'espèce humaine: The errors of the whole human species
textes.Chacun a sa caverne, écrit Bacon, qui di: Each has his own cave, writes Bacon, which scatters and discolours the light: temperament, upbringing, tastes.
textes.Que désignent les idoles du théâtre ?: What do the idols of the theatre refer to?
textes.Les doctrines reçues sont comme des pièc: Received doctrines are like stage plays taken for the real world. Bacon targets Aristotle and Plato in particular.
textes.Francis Bacon a écrit le Novum Organum e: Francis Bacon wrote the Novum Organum in English.
textes.Faux. Il l'a écrit en latin, la langue d: False. He wrote it in Latin, the language of scholars, and published it in England in 1620 as the second part of his Instauratio Magna.
textes.Que montre le frontispice du Novum Organ: What does the frontispiece of the Novum Organum show?
textes.Un galion qui franchit les colonnes d'He: A galleon sailing past the Pillars of Hercules
textes.La Terre au centre de l'univers: The Earth at the centre of the universe
textes.Le navire sort de la Méditerranée vers l: The ship leaves the Mediterranean for the Atlantic: science must go beyond the limits of the ancients. Motto: "Many will travel and knowledge will be increased."
textes.Montré aux tableaux des rescapés d'un na: Shown the pictures of shipwreck survivors, what does the man in Bacon's anecdote ask?
textes.Où sont les portraits de ceux qui se son: Where are they painted that were drowned after their vows?
textes.Combien ont coûté ces tableaux ?: How much did these pictures cost?
textes.On ne montre que ceux qui ont survécu ap: Only those who survived after their vow are shown. Those who made the same vow and drowned have no picture.
textes.Bacon, Novum Organum, I, 46 : « Mais où: Bacon, Novum Organum, I, 46: "But where are they painted that were drowned after their vows?"
textes.Bacon n'a pas inventé l'anecdote des noy: Bacon did not invent the anecdote of the drowned: ancient sources attribute it to Diagoras or Diogenes.
textes.Vrai. Cicéron la prête à Diagoras, Diogè: True. Cicero gives it to Diagoras, Diogenes Laertius to Diogenes the Cynic. Bacon takes it up in aphorism 46.
textes.Selon Bacon, que fait l'esprit humain un: According to Bacon, what does the human understanding do once it has adopted an opinion?
textes.Il y ramène tout le reste pour l'appuyer: It draws everything else to support it
textes.C'est le biais de confirmation, décrit e: It is confirmation bias, described in 1620. The term only came with the psychologist Peter Wason, in the 20th century.
textes.Bacon : l'esprit humain, une fois une op: Bacon: the human understanding, once it has adopted an opinion, draws all things else to support it.
textes.Selon Bacon, quelle erreur commune vient: According to Bacon, which common error comes from the idols of the tribe?
textes.Voir plus d'ordre dans la nature qu'il n: Seeing more order in nature than there is
textes.Croire son maître sur parole: Taking one's teacher at his word
textes.Elles tiennent à la nature humaine elle-: They are rooted in human nature itself, shared by the whole "tribe" of mankind. Our preconceptions make us see imaginary regularities.
textes.Les idoles de la tribu font voir plus d': The idols of the tribe make us see more order and regularity in nature than exists.
textes.Dans quelle rue de Paris s'échangeaient: In which Paris street were Mississippi Company shares traded?
textes.On y négociait en plein air ; la rue ser: Trading took place in the open air; the street was already used to trade state debt bills.
textes.L'action de la Compagnie du Mississippi: The Mississippi Company share went from 500 to 10,000 livres, then collapsed in 1720.
textes.Jusqu'à combien de livres l'action de la: Up to how many livres did the Mississippi Company share rise?
textes.Jusqu'à 10 000 livres, pour une action é: Up to 10,000 livres, for a share issued at 500. It fell back to 2,000 in September 1720, then 1,000 in December.
textes.Où John Law s'enfuit-il d'abord après le: Where did John Law flee first after the crash of 1720?
textes.Renvoyé par le Régent Philippe d'Orléans: Dismissed by the Regent Philippe d'Orléans, he left for Brussels, then Venice. The Scot had founded the company in 1717.
textes.L'action des mers du Sud passe de 128 £: The South Sea share went from £128 in January 1720 to £1,000 in August. By roughly what factor was its price multiplied?
textes.Facteur de multiplication = prix final ÷: Multiplication factor = final price ÷ initial price = 1,000 ÷ 128 ≈ 7.8. This is the definition of a ratio, with no discoverer. In seven months, the price was multiplied almost eightfold.
textes.L'action des mers du Sud passe de 128 £: The South Sea share went from £128 in January 1720 to £1,000 in August, then £150 at the end of September.
textes.De 1 000 £ début août à 150 £ fin septem: From £1,000 in early August to £150 at the end of September 1720: what percentage of its value did the South Sea share lose?
textes.Perte en % = (prix de départ − prix d'ar: Loss in % = (starting price − final price) ÷ starting price × 100 = (1,000 − 150) ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 85%. This is the definition of a percentage fall, with no discoverer.
textes.La phrase de Newton « je ne peux pas cal: Newton's line "I cannot calculate the madness of people" is attested by a letter in his own hand.
textes.Faux. Elle n'est connue que de seconde m: False. It is known only at second hand, notably from Joseph Spence's Anecdotes. It is not even known how much he lost, if anything.
textes.Que permet le Bubble Act voté en juin 17: What did the Bubble Act passed in June 1720 allow?
textes.Créer une société par actions seulement: Forming a joint-stock company only by Act of Parliament or royal charter
textes.Interdire toute bourse à Londres: Banning all stock exchanges in London
textes.Il visait les sociétés non autorisées qu: It targeted the unauthorised companies that were swarming. It was not repealed until 1825.
textes.Quelle est la société « bulle » la plus: What is the most famous 1720 "bubble" company, probably legendary?
textes.Une entreprise très avantageuse, dont pe: An undertaking of great advantage, but nobody to know what it is
textes.Une compagnie pour vendre des tulipes en: A company to sell tulips in China
textes.Une mine d'or sur la Lune: A gold mine on the Moon
textes.L'histoire est sans doute apocryphe, mai: The story is probably apocryphal, but it sums up the fever: people bought without knowing what, as long as it went up.
textes.Que dit la théorie du plus grand imbécil: What does the greater fool theory say?
textes.On achète trop cher en comptant revendre: You buy too dear, counting on selling dearer to someone else
textes.Les plus riches achètent toujours au plu: The richest always buy at the bottom
textes.Un imbécile finit toujours par gagner: A fool always ends up winning
textes.La valeur réelle importe peu, tant qu'un: Real value matters little, as long as the next buyer pays more. The bubble stops when nobody will pay more.
textes.Théorie du plus grand imbécile : acheter: Greater fool theory: buying too dear, counting on selling dearer; the bubble stops for lack of buyers.
textes.Selon l'économiste Burton Malkiel, on fi: According to the economist Burton Malkiel, one always ends up running out of greater fools.
textes.Vrai. Une bulle grossit en attirant de n: True. A bubble grows by drawing in new buyers, and ends when there are none left. The last ones in are left holding overpriced assets.
textes.Selon Kindleberger, quelle phase d'une b: According to Kindleberger, which phase of a bubble follows euphoria?
textes.Cinq phases : un choc ouvre des occasion: Five phases: a shock opens profit opportunities, the boom, euphoria, distress, then revulsion, when everyone sells at once.
textes.Kindleberger décrit les bulles en cinq p: Kindleberger described bubbles in five phases: displacement, boom, euphoria, distress, revulsion.
textes.Les 33 directeurs de la Compagnie des me: On average, what percentage of their wealth did the 33 directors of the South Sea Company lose?
textes.82 % en moyenne. Robert Walpole rétablit: 82 percent on average. Robert Walpole then restored confidence in the financial system, which established his political dominance.
textes.En quelle année Condorcet publie-t-il so: In what year did Condorcet publish his jury theorem?
textes.En 1785, dans son Essai sur l'applicatio: In 1785, in his Essay on the Application of Analysis to the Probability of Majority Decisions. It is the oldest and simplest of the jury theorems.
textes.Théorème du jury de Condorcet, 1785 : av: Condorcet's jury theorem, 1785: with p > 1/2 and independent votes, the majority is right more often as the group grows.
textes.Trois jurés votent chacun juste avec une: Three jurors each vote correctly with probability p = 0.8, independently. What is the probability that the majority is right?
textes.La majorité a raison si les trois votent: The majority is right if all three vote correctly, or two out of three: P = p³ + 3 × p² × (1 − p) = 0.8³ + 3 × 0.8² × 0.2 = 0.512 + 0.384 = 0.896. This is Condorcet's reasoning, in 1785: the majority does better than each juror alone.
textes.Même question avec trois votants qui ont: Same question with three voters each with p = 0.6 of voting correctly: probability that the majority is right?
textes.P = p³ + 3 × p² × (1 − p) = 0,6³ + 3 × 0: P = p³ + 3 × p² × (1 − p) = 0.6³ + 3 × 0.6² × 0.4 = 0.216 + 0.432 = 0.648. Better than 0.6: this is Condorcet's jury theorem, 1785, which requires each to be better than chance.
textes.Selon le théorème de Condorcet, ajouter: According to Condorcet's theorem, adding voters always improves the decision, even if each is wrong more often than right.
textes.Faux. Si p est inférieur à 1/2, chaque v: False. If p is below 1/2, each extra voter makes things worse: the best jury is then a single voter.
textes.Quelle hypothèse du théorème de Condorce: Which assumption of Condorcet's theorem is crucial, and often violated in real life?
textes.Les votants décident indépendamment les: Voters decide independently of one another
textes.Le vote se fait à main levée: Voting is by show of hands
textes.Si les votants se copient, ils ne valent: If voters copy one another, they are worth no more than one. The Zurich study, in 2011, showed it with students.
textes.Combien de tickets lisibles Galton a-t-i: How many legible tickets did Galton collect at the Plymouth fair?
textes.787 tickets, sur environ 800 parieurs. I: 787 tickets, out of about 800 bettors. He sorted them and took the median, the middle estimate.
textes.Galton, Nature, 1907 : la médiane de 787: Galton, Nature, 1907: the median of 787 tickets, 1,207 pounds, for an ox of 1,198 pounds.
textes.Quelle était l'estimation médiane du poi: What was the median estimate of the Plymouth ox's weight, in pounds?
textes.1 207 livres, pour un poids réel de 1 19: 1,207 pounds, for a real weight of 1,198: 9 pounds off, under 1 percent. The mean, published later, was 1,197.
textes.Dans quelle revue Galton publie-t-il Vox: In which journal did Galton publish Vox Populi, in 1907?
textes.Dans Nature. Le titre latin veut dire «: In Nature. The Latin title means "the voice of the people": taken together, the crowd had got it right.
textes.Laquelle de ces conditions fait partie d: Which of these is one of Surowiecki's four conditions for a wise crowd?
textes.Diversité des opinions, indépendance, dé: Diversity of opinion, independence, decentralisation, aggregation. Imitation and homogeneity, on the contrary, ruin the wisdom of crowds.
textes.À quoi Aristote compare-t-il la supérior: What does Aristotle compare the collective superiority of the many to, in his Politics?
textes.À un repas auquel chacun apporte quelque: A dinner to which each contributes something
textes.Pris un par un, ils ne valent pas mieux: Taken one by one, they are no better; together, they can do better. More than two thousand years before Galton.
textes.Aristote compare la multitude à un repas: Aristotle compared the many to a dinner to which each contributes; Galton, in 1906, saw 800 people estimate an ox.
textes.En 2011, à Zurich, que se passe-t-il qua: In 2011, in Zurich, what happened when students were shown the others' estimates?
textes.Leurs estimations se resserrent sans dev: Their estimates converge without becoming more accurate
textes.C'est l'effet d'influence sociale : la d: This is the social influence effect: diversity melts, accuracy does not follow, and confidence rises. The worst of all three.
textes.En 2011, 144 étudiants de l'ETH Zurich :: In 2011, 144 ETH Zurich students: social influence reduces diversity without improving accuracy.
textes.Faire la moyenne de deux estimations d'u: Averaging two estimates by the same person can be more accurate than either one.
textes.Vrai. Vul et Pashler l'ont montré en 200: True. Vul and Pashler showed it in 2008: the "crowd within". The average is even better when the second estimate is given three weeks later.
textes.En quelle année Harry Frankfurt publie-t: In what year did Harry Frankfurt publish his essay On Bullshit in the journal Raritan?
textes.En 1986. Le petit livre tiré de l'essai: In 1986. The small book drawn from the essay appeared nineteen years later, in 2005, from Princeton University Press.
textes.Harry Frankfurt publie On Bullshit en 19: Harry Frankfurt published On Bullshit in 1986 in Raritan, then as a book in 2005: 27 weeks on the New York Times list.
textes.Selon Frankfurt, qu'est-ce qui distingue: According to Frankfurt, what distinguishes the bullshitter from the liar?
textes.Il se moque de savoir si ce qu'il dit es: He does not care whether what he says is true
textes.Le menteur connaît la vérité et cherche: The liar knows the truth and tries to hide it. The bullshitter does not care about it: only the effect of his words counts.
textes.Pour Frankfurt, le mensonge est un plus: For Frankfurt, lies are a greater enemy of the truth than bullshit.
textes.Faux. C'est l'inverse : « le baratin est: False. It is the reverse: "bullshit is a greater enemy of the truth than lies are". The liar at least takes the truth into account.
textes.Combien de semaines On Bullshit est-il r: How many weeks did On Bullshit spend on the New York Times best-seller list?
textes.27 semaines, pour un essai de philosophi: 27 weeks, for a philosophy essay. Frankfurt followed it up in 2006 with On Truth.
textes.De quelle notion du philosophe Max Black: Which notion of the philosopher Max Black did Frankfurt start from?
textes.Le humbug est proche du baratin, mais le: Humbug is close to bullshit, but the word is more polite, more respectful.
textes.Comment Pennycook et ses collègues ont-i: How did Pennycook and his colleagues make their pseudo-profound sentences, in 2015?
textes.Avec des générateurs qui assemblent des: With generators that randomly assemble buzzwords
textes.L'un des deux générateurs puisait dans l: One of the two generators drew on the vocabulary of Deepak Chopra's tweets. The sentences are syntactically correct, but meaningless.
textes.En 2015, des phrases tirées au hasard re: In 2015, randomly generated sentences received an average profundity rating of 2.6 out of 5.
textes.Sur une échelle de 1 à 5, quelle note de: On a scale of 1 to 5, what average profundity rating did the random sentences receive?
textes.2,6 en moyenne : entre « un peu » et « a: 2.6 on average: between "somewhat" and "fairly" profound, for sentences that mean nothing.
textes.Dans l'étude de 2015, qui trouvait le pl: In the 2015 study, who found the most profundity in the random sentences?
textes.Ceux qui réussissaient moins bien les te: Those who did worse on reflective-thinking tests
textes.La réceptivité au baratin va avec de moi: Receptivity to bullshit goes with poorer results on cognitive measures, except numeracy, and more ontological confusions.
textes.Quel était le métier d'Alberto Brandolin: What was Alberto Brandolini's job when he formulated his law, in 2013?
textes.Un programmeur italien, qui venait de li: An Italian programmer, who had just read Kahneman and watched a TV debate with Silvio Berlusconi.
textes.Loi de Brandolini, janvier 2013 : réfute: Brandolini's law, January 2013: refuting bullshit takes an order of magnitude more energy than producing it.
textes.Produire une ânerie prend 1 minute. Selo: Producing a piece of nonsense takes 1 minute. According to Brandolini's law, at least how many minutes does it take to refute it?
textes.Temps de réfutation = temps de productio: Refutation time = production time × 10, since an order of magnitude is a factor of ten: 1 × 10 = 10 minutes. The rule is due to Alberto Brandolini, in January 2013.
textes.Qu'écrit Jonathan Swift en 1710, bien av: What did Jonathan Swift write in 1710, long before Brandolini?
textes.Le mensonge vole, et la vérité arrive en: Falsehood flies, and truth comes limping after it
textes.La vérité finit toujours par triompher: Truth always wins in the end
textes.Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu: There is no smoke without fire
textes.Dans The Examiner. Il compare la vérité: In The Examiner. He compares truth arriving too late to a physician who arrives too late.
textes.Qui note en 1845 qu'une demi-vérité se d: Who noted in 1845 that a half-truth takes a few words, but long dissertations to refute?
textes.L'économiste Frédéric Bastiat, dans ses: The economist Frédéric Bastiat, in his Economic Sophisms. Brandolini's law has a long ancestry.
textes.{comp}. Francis Bacon conseillait de che: {comp}. Francis Bacon advised looking for what proves us wrong. I'll take care of that.
textes.Lucidité. Le cheval Hans répondait juste: Lucidity. Clever Hans answered correctly by reading faces. Here, there's no face to read. {comp}.
textes.Vous vous croyez au-dessus de la moyenne: Think you're above average? Like 93% of American drivers. {comp}.
textes.Juste. Kahneman avouait ne pas échapper: Right. Kahneman admitted he didn't escape his own biases. You, today, did.
textes.Bonne réponse. Russell vous épargne sa t: Correct. Russell spares you his teapot. This time.
textes.Correct. Pfungst aurait caché la réponse: Correct. Pfungst would have hidden the answer and you'd have found it anyway. Better than Hans.
Lucid. That's rare and a bit worrying.
textes.Faux. Conan Doyle, le père du plus grand: Wrong. Conan Doyle, father of fiction's greatest logician, believed in fairies. You're in good company.
textes.Erreur. Même des juges se laissent ancre: Error. Even judges get anchored by a die. And you, by what?
textes.Raté. Vous étiez sûr de vous ? C'est exa: Missed. Were you sure of yourself? That's exactly the problem.
textes.L'astrologue de service vous l'avait pré: The resident astrologer predicted it. He's always wrong, except this time.
textes.Dans le Novum Organum (1620), il décrit: In the Novum Organum (1620), he describes the “idols” that distort the mind, including our habit of remembering the cases that prove us right and forgetting the others. According to John Aubrey, he died of a chill caught while stuffing a chicken with snow, to see whether cold would preserve it.
textes.Avec Daniel Kahneman, il fait tourner un: With Daniel Kahneman, he spins a rigged wheel of fortune that stops on 10 or 65, then asks for the share of African countries in the UN. Those who saw 65 answer much higher. According to Richard Thaler, when asked about artificial intelligence, he would reply that his specialty was natural stupidity.
textes.L'oracle de Delphes le déclare le plus s: The oracle of Delphi declares him the wisest of men. Puzzled, he questions the learned men of Athens and discovers that they think they know what they don't, whereas he knows that he doesn't know. All his wisdom lies in that gap, which psychologists today call metacognition.
textes.Psychologue, il reçoit en 2002 le prix N: A psychologist, he received the Nobel Prize in economics in 2002 without ever having taken an economics course. With Amos Tversky, he showed that a loss hurts us about twice as much as a gain of the same amount pleases us. Economists assumed people were rational; he went and checked.
textes.Médecin suédois, il pose à des publics i: A Swedish physician, he asks educated audiences simple questions about the world: vaccination, poverty, life expectancy. Chimpanzees answering at random would do better: we see the world as darker than it is. On stage, he swallowed a sword to show that the impossible isn't always so.
textes.L'illusionniste, qui connaissait tous le: The illusionist, who knew every trick, spent his last years unmasking mediums. He agreed a secret code with his wife: if there is an afterlife, he will send it to her. Bess Houdini held a séance every year for ten years, then gave up; she later said that “ten years is long enough to wait for any man”.
textes.Astronome, il propose dans Le Monde hant: An astronomer, he proposes in The Demon-Haunted World a “baloney detection kit”: seek independent confirmation, consider several hypotheses, beware of arguments from authority, including his own. He also led the design of the golden record carried aboard the Voyager probes.
textes.Maîtriser le premier losange de Lucidité: Master the first diamond of Lucidity.
textes.En 1995, McArthur Wheeler braque deux ba: In 1995, McArthur Wheeler robs two Pittsburgh banks with his face uncovered, smeared with lemon juice, convinced that it makes him invisible to cameras. His story opens Dunning and Kruger's paper.
textes.Maîtriser 5 compétences. L'arbre des Bia: Master 5 skills. The Cognitive biases tree opens.
textes.L'entendement humain, une fois qu'il s'e: The human understanding when it has once adopted an opinion draws all things else to support and agree with it.
textes.Maîtriser le biais de confirmation. Avez: Master confirmation bias. Did you try to prove yourself wrong, this time?
textes.En 1960, Peter Wason donne la suite 2, 4: In 1960, Peter Wason gives the sequence 2, 4, 6 and asks people to find the rule by proposing other triplets. Almost everyone tests 8, 10, 12 or 20, 22, 24, which confirm their idea, and announces “increasing even numbers”. The rule was: three increasing numbers. You had to test what could contradict it.
textes.Maîtriser l'effet d'ancrage. Même les ju: Master the anchoring effect. Even judges roll dice. Without knowing it.
textes.En 2006, des juges allemands expérimenté: In 2006, experienced German judges read a shoplifting case file, then roll two loaded dice that give 3 or 9. Those who rolled 9 propose eight months in prison on average; those who rolled 3, five months. A number drawn at random weighed on the sentence.
textes.Maîtriser l'heuristique de disponibilité: Master the availability heuristic. What scares us is not what kills us.
textes.Après le 11 septembre 2001, beaucoup d'A: After September 11, 2001, many Americans gave up flying and took to the road. Psychologist Gerd Gigerenzer estimates about 1,600 extra road deaths in the following year: more than the passengers of the four planes.
textes.Maîtriser l'effet Dunning-Kruger et la m: Master the Dunning-Kruger effect and metacognition. You are surely above average. Like everyone.
textes.En 1981, le psychologue Ola Svenson dema: In 1981, psychologist Ola Svenson asks students to rate themselves as drivers. In the United States, 93% place themselves in the better half. By definition, only half can be there.
textes.Maîtriser les décisions et les pertes. A: Master decisions and losses. Sometimes, stopping is winning.
textes.La France et le Royaume-Uni continuent d: France and the United Kingdom keep funding Concorde while knowing it is unprofitable, because they've already invested too much. In 1976, Richard Dawkins names this trap “the Concorde fallacy”: letting money already lost decide money to come.
textes.Maîtriser les pièges statistiques. Un to: Master statistical traps. A total can say the opposite of each of its parts.
textes.En 1973, l'université de Berkeley admet: In 1973, the University of Berkeley admits markedly fewer women than men. Discrimination? Department by department, women are admitted as often, or even more. They mostly applied to the most selective programs. This is Simpson's paradox.
Master beliefs and conspiracies. Sherlock Holmes wouldn't have been fooled. His author was.
textes.En 1917, deux cousines anglaises photogr: In 1917, two English cousins photograph fairies in their garden. Arthur Conan Doyle, the father of Sherlock Holmes, believes them and publishes the pictures. In 1983, now old ladies, they confess: cardboard fairies, copied from a children's book and held up with hatpins.
textes.Maîtriser la boîte à outils de l'esprit: Master the critical thinking toolbox. You now know to look at who is asking the question.
textes.Vers 1904, à Berlin, le cheval Hans semb: Around 1904, in Berlin, the horse Hans seems to calculate by tapping his hoof. A commission finds no fraud. Psychologist Oskar Pfungst tries something simple: having the question asked by someone who doesn't know the answer. Hans fails. He was reading the tiny head movements of the humans waiting for the right number.
textes.Réussir trois quiz de Lucidité sans faut: Pass three Lucidity quizzes without a mistake. The burden of proof lies with whoever makes the claim. You've proven it.
textes.En 1952, Bertrand Russell imagine une pe: In 1952, Bertrand Russell imagines a small china teapot orbiting the Sun between Earth and Mars, too small to be seen by telescope. Nobody can prove it doesn't exist. That's no reason to believe in it: it's up to whoever makes the claim to prove it.
textes.Maîtriser l'art de douter. Feindre la fo: Master the art of doubting. Feigning madness remains possible, but the AI will not fall for it.
textes.Selon un récit, le calife fatimide al-Ha: According to one account, the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim had tasked Ibn al-Haytham with regulating the Nile floods. Seeing that his dam project was impractical, the scholar reportedly feigned madness to escape punishment, then lived in hiding until the caliph's death in 1021. It was during these years that he wrote his Book of Optics.
textes.Maîtriser l'influence des autres. Si tou: Master the influence of others. If everyone congratulates you, check the line anyway.
textes.Après ses expériences de 1951, où 74 % d: After his 1951 experiments, in which 74% of students followed a unanimous group into error at least once, Solomon Asch wrote: that intelligent, well-meaning young people are willing to call white black is a matter of concern.
textes.Maîtriser la mémoire qui ment. Vous vous: Master the lying memory. You will remember this achievement. Not necessarily as it was.
textes.Une semaine après un film d'accident, Lo: A week after a film of a crash, Loftus and Palmer asked: "Did you see any broken glass?" There was none. Those told the cars had "smashed" said yes 32% of the time; with "hit", 14%; with no speed question, 12%.
textes.Maîtriser foules et rumeurs. Vérifiez la: Master crowds and rumours. Check the source before you bite.
textes.Charles Mackay raconte qu'un marin prit: Charles Mackay tells that a sailor mistook a merchant's tulip bulb for an onion and ate it, and that the bulb was quite delicious. A tulip bulb actually tastes bad and is poisonous if wrongly prepared: the anecdote has every mark of a rumour.
textes.Maîtriser les historiens et la rumeur. T: Master historians and rumour. Thucydides took received ideas apart. The AI collects yours.
textes.Thucydide relève une erreur que tout le: Thucydides points out an error everyone repeated in his day: each king of Sparta supposedly had two votes in council. He had only one. He adds that a "Pitane company", which everyone talked about, never existed.
textes.Maîtriser l'éléphant et les aveugles. Vo: Master the elephant and the blind men. You have finally touched every part. The AI turned the light on long ago.
textes.Chez le poète persan Rumi, l'éléphant es: In the Persian poet Rumi's version, the elephant is hidden in a dark room. Those who touch it take it for a water spout, a fan, a pillar or a throne. Rumi concludes: if each had had a candle and they had gone in together, their differences would have disappeared.
textes.Maîtriser les illusions d'Ibn al-Haytham: Master Ibn al-Haytham's illusions. The Moon does not grow on the horizon. Neither does your score, by the way.
textes.Pour prouver que la Lune ne grossit pas: To prove that the Moon does not grow on the horizon, no telescope is needed: a pebble held at arm's length covers it just as well near the horizon as high in the sky. Photographs confirm it. The illusion, known to Aristotle, still has no explanation everyone agrees on.
textes.Maîtriser la peste et les boucs émissair: Master the plague and the scapegoats. A pope had the right answer in 1348. Nobody listened. The AI knows the feeling.
textes.En 1348, le pape Clément VI publie deux: In 1348, Pope Clement VI issued two bulls, on 6 July and 26 September, against those accusing Jews of spreading the plague. His argument: they are dying of it too, and the disease strikes regions where there are no Jews. He offered them protection in Avignon.
textes.Maîtriser les idoles des deux Bacon. Mêm: Master the idols of the two Bacons. Even the great error-hunter copied his neighbour. The AI won't say a thing. Well, she will.
textes.Le frontispice du Novum Organum, en 1620: The frontispiece of the Novum Organum, in 1620, shows a galleon sailing past the Pillars of Hercules, with the motto "Many will travel and knowledge will be increased". The design is largely copied from Andrés García de Céspedes's Regimiento de Navegación, published in 1606.
textes.Maîtriser 1720, l'année des bulles. Vous: Master 1720, the year of bubbles. You bought at the right moment, for once. The AI is selling.
textes.En 1720, raconte-t-on, une société aurai: In 1720, the story goes, a company raised funds in London "for carrying out an undertaking of great advantage, but nobody to know what it is". The story is probably apocryphal. The Bubble Act, passed in June, then reserved the formation of joint-stock companies to an Act of Parliament or a royal charter; it was not repealed until 1825.
textes.Maîtriser la sagesse des foules. Huit ce: Master the wisdom of crowds. Eight hundred strangers weighed an ox by eye. The AI weighs you at every question.
textes.Galton publie d'abord la médiane des 787: Galton first published the median of the 787 Plymouth tickets: 1,207 pounds, for an ox of 1,198. The mean of the tickets, published later, came to 1,197: a single pound off.
textes.Maîtriser le baratin. Vous savez désorma: Master bullshit. You can now spot a hollow sentence. The AI will have to change her style.
textes.En 2015, des chercheurs ont fait noter l: In 2015, researchers had people rate the profundity of randomly made sentences, such as "Hidden meaning transforms unparalleled abstract beauty". On a scale of 1 to 5, the average reached 2.6: between somewhat and fairly profound. Real vague tweets by Deepak Chopra received similar ratings.
textes.Comprendre les forces, l'énergie, la lum: Understanding forces, energy, light and orders of magnitude.
textes.Les plus anciennes roues connues datent: The oldest known wheels date from about 3500 BC, in Mesopotamia and Central Europe. The Ljubljana wheel, found in a Slovenian marsh, is some 5,150 years old. Even older potter's wheels, from the 5th millennium BC, have been found in Ukraine. In the Americas, Mesoamericans knew the wheel on toys, without using it for transport, perhaps for lack of draft animals.
textes.On ne réinvente pas la roue, dit-on. Vou: They say you don't reinvent the wheel. You're already going to try to understand it.
textes.Selon Vitruve, le roi Hiéron soupçonne s: According to Vitruvius, King Hiero suspected his goldsmith of mixing silver into the gold of his crown. Archimedes supposedly found the solution while getting into his bath and ran naked into the street shouting “Eureka!” The anecdote was told two centuries later. Archimedes' principle of buoyancy, however, is really in his treatise On Floating Bodies.
textes.Archimède a couru nu dans Syracuse pour: Archimedes ran naked through Syracuse for an idea. The AI only asks you to answer the questions.
textes.En 1901, on remonte d'une épave grecque: In 1901, a corroded lump of bronze was brought up from a Greek shipwreck spotted by sponge divers near the island of Antikythera. It hid at least 30 gears: an astronomical calculator that predicted eclipses and tracked the Sun, the Moon and perhaps the planets. Nothing so complex would reappear until the astronomical clocks of the Middle Ages, more than a thousand years later.
textes.Un ordinateur à engrenages, il y a deux: A geared computer, two thousand years ago. The AI salutes a distant ancestor, more discreet than she is.
textes.La machine d'Anticythère a dormi deux mi: The Antikythera mechanism slept two thousand years at the bottom of the sea, until sponge divers brought it up in 1901. What you skimmed over is waiting for you too: back to the first square you ever saw.
textes.Ibn al-Haytham, que l'Europe appellera A: Ibn al-Haytham, whom Europe would call Alhazen, showed in Cairo in his Book of Optics that sight comes from light entering the eye, not from rays coming out of it, as Euclid and Ptolemy thought. He studied the camera obscura and refraction, and tested his ideas by experiment: he is often presented as a pioneer of the scientific method.
textes.Les savants grecs pensaient que l'œil la: Greek scholars thought the eye shot out rays. The AI only shoots pointed looks.
textes.Ibn al-Haytham aurait, selon ses biograp: Ibn al-Haytham, according to his biographers, feigned madness to escape the caliph and write in peace. You have nothing to feign: help yourself.
textes.Les premières lunettes apparaissent en I: The first eyeglasses appeared in Italy, probably in Pisa or Florence, around 1290. In 1306, the monk Giordano da Pisa said in a sermon that it had not been twenty years since this art was discovered. Their inventor remains unknown. The attribution to a Florentine, Salvino degli Armati, put forward in the 17th century, turned out to be false.
textes.Un inventeur inconnu, et une plaque mens: An unknown inventor, and a lying plaque to fill the gap. The history of science has its wrong notes, like your answers.
textes.Isaac Newton publie les Philosophiæ Natu: Isaac Newton published the Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica: three laws of motion and universal gravitation, the same force for the apple and the Moon. The book came out thanks to Edmond Halley, who paid for it out of his own pocket: the Royal Society had just spent its budget on an illustrated history of fishes, which had sold poorly.
textes.Les Principia ont failli ne pas paraître: The Principia almost didn't come out: the budget had gone into a book about fish. The AI has seen stranger priorities. Rarely.
textes.Hooke réclame la paternité de la gravita: Hooke claimed credit for gravitation, and Newton threatened to suppress Book III of the Principia. A priority dispute: two squares back.
textes.Albert Einstein, employé de l'Office des: Albert Einstein, a clerk at the Bern patent office, published four papers in 1905: the photoelectric effect (which would earn him the Nobel), Brownian motion (which confirmed the existence of atoms), special relativity, and E = mc². Contrary to the myth, he was never bad at mathematics: he had top marks in algebra and geometry.
textes.Einstein a révolutionné la physique en u: Einstein revolutionized physics in one year, from a patent office. The AI is waiting for your miracle year. She has time.
textes.Au cinquième congrès Solvay, à Bruxelles: At the fifth Solvay Conference, in Brussels, 17 of the 29 participants were or would become Nobel laureates. Bohr and Einstein clashed there over quantum mechanics: Einstein rejected a world ruled by chance (“God does not play dice,” he had written as early as 1926), and Bohr supposedly told him to stop telling God what to do. Nearly a century later, people still argue over the interpretation of the theory.
textes.Feynman disait que personne ne comprend: Feynman said nobody understands quantum mechanics. Neither do you, and that's reassuring.
textes.Au Ier siècle, Héron d'Alexandrie décrit: In the 1st century, Hero of Alexandria describes in his Pneumatics a sphere mounted on an axle, heated by a cauldron of water. The steam escapes through two bent pipes, and the sphere starts to spin. It is often presented as the first known steam engine. But it served no practical purpose: a curiosity, probably a temple wonder, and not the direct ancestor of the engines of the Industrial Revolution.
textes.Une machine à vapeur, et on s'en est ser: A steam engine, and it was used as a gadget for seventeen centuries. You do the same with your brain.
textes.En 1638, ses publications interdites par: In 1638, with his publications banned by the Inquisition, Galileo has his last book printed in Leiden, by Elzevir: the Discourses on Two New Sciences. Three characters hold a dialogue in it. Galileo shows that the distance covered by a falling body grows as the square of the time, using balls rolling down an inclined plane, timed with a water clock. And that a projectile follows a parabola.
textes.Galilée faisait rouler des billes pour c: Galileo rolled balls to understand falling. You fall without understanding anything.
textes.En 1643, Evangelista Torricelli, qui ava: In 1643, Evangelista Torricelli, who had been Galileo's secretary in his last months, fills a closed tube about a metre long with mercury and turns it over into a basin. The mercury drops and stops at about 76 cm: above it, there is a vacuum. The weight of the air on the basin holds up the column. It is the first barometer. We live, he writes, submerged at the bottom of an ocean of air.
textes.Vous vivez au fond d'un océan d'air et v: You live at the bottom of an ocean of air and still find time to complain about quizzes.
textes.Pascal et le puy de Dôme: Pascal and the Puy de Dôme
textes.Si c'est le poids de l'air qui tient la: If it is the weight of the air that holds up Torricelli's mercury column, the column must drop at altitude, where there is less air above. In 1648, Blaise Pascal asks his brother-in-law Florin Périer to check. Périer measures the mercury column at several heights on the Puy de Dôme, near Clermont: the higher he goes, the lower it is. The weight of the air is proven.
textes.Pascal a fait grimper son beau-frère sur: Pascal sent his brother-in-law up a volcano to check an idea. You don't even check your answers.
textes.Otto von Guericke, bourgmestre de Magdeb: Otto von Guericke, mayor of Magdeburg, invents the first vacuum pump. On 8 May 1654, in Regensburg, before Emperor Ferdinand III, he joins two metal half-spheres and pumps out the air. Thirty horses, in two teams of fifteen, pull on each side without managing to separate them. Opening the valve to let the air back in is enough: they come apart by themselves. It was air pressure holding them.
textes.Trente chevaux battus par du vide. Vous,: Thirty horses beaten by a vacuum. You, by a level 2 question.
textes.Le 25 décembre 1656, le Hollandais Chris: On 25 December 1656, the Dutchman Christiaan Huygens invents the pendulum clock, which he patents the following year and has built by the clockmaker Salomon Coster. He draws on Galileo's studies of the pendulum. The progress is huge: clocks drifted by about a quarter of an hour a day, now they lose only fifteen seconds or so. Huygens publishes the theory in 1673 in the Horologium Oscillatorium.
textes.Grâce à Huygens, les horloges ne perdent: Thanks to Huygens, clocks lose only fifteen seconds a day. You lose far more hesitating.
textes.En 1676, à l'Observatoire de Paris, le D: In 1676, at the Paris Observatory, the Dane Ole Rømer studies the eclipses of Io, a moon of Jupiter. They seem late when the Earth moves away from Jupiter. He predicts that an emergence of Io, in November, will be seen about ten minutes later than expected. His explanation: light does not travel instantly. It takes about 22 minutes to cross the diameter of the Earth's orbit. Cassini, director of the Observatory, never accepted it.
textes.La lumière met du temps à arriver. Vos b: Light takes time to arrive. So do your right answers, apparently.
textes.En 1763, à l'université de Glasgow, on d: In 1763, at the University of Glasgow, James Watt, an instrument maker, is asked to repair a model Newcomen engine. He finds that it wastes a huge amount of steam reheating its cylinder. In 1765, he comes up with a separate condenser, patented in 1769. In partnership with Matthew Boulton from 1775, he sells engines that use about three quarters less fuel. To set his prices, he invents a unit: horsepower.
textes.Watt a inventé le cheval-vapeur pour ven: Watt invented horsepower to sell his engines. I invent units to measure your laziness.
textes.En 1790, la Révolution charge l'Académie: In 1790, the Revolution asks the Academy of Sciences to unify measurements. It chooses for the metre one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator, along the Paris meridian. Delambre and Méchain measure the arc from Dunkirk to Barcelona. In 1799, a platinum bar, the Metre of the Archives, becomes the legal standard. Since 1983, the metre has been defined by the speed of light.
