textes.La légende parle d'émeute. Mais le mot n: Legend speaks of a riot. But the word appears in reviews only in 1924, accounts contradict each other, and the performance went on to the end. For some historians, it was the dance more than the music that shocked.
textes.Le Sacre, 29 mai 1913 : un chahut réel,: The Rite, 29 May 1913: real uproar, a partly legendary riot.
textes.Arnold Schoenberg naît à Vienne le 13 se: Arnold Schoenberg was born in Vienna on 13 September 1874. Largely self-taught, he studied counterpoint with Alexander von Zemlinsky. His Second String Quartet, in 1907-1908, was his first piece without an explicitly stated key centre: no note rules the others any more. This is called the emancipation of the dissonance.
textes.En 1912, Pierrot lunaire met en musique: In 1912, Pierrot lunaire set 21 poems by Albert Giraud, arranged in three groups, in a "spoken singing", Sprechstimme, in which the voice touches pitches only fleetingly. On 31 March 1913, in Vienna, a concert of works by Schoenberg and his pupils went so badly that it was nicknamed the Skandalkonzert.
textes.Deuxième Quatuor 1908 : plus de tonalité: Second Quartet 1908: no more key. Pierrot lunaire 1912: Sprechstimme.
textes.Vers 1921, Schoenberg met au point sa mé: Around 1921, Schoenberg devised his method of composing with twelve tones. A series contains each of the twelve notes of the chromatic scale once, and the whole work is built on it: no more tonic, the series replaces the functions of tonal harmony. He presented it around 1923. The Austrian Josef Matthias Hauer had published his own "law of the twelve tones" as early as 1919.
textes.Ses élèves Alban Berg et Anton Webern fo: His pupils Alban Berg and Anton Webern formed with him the Second Viennese School. Schoenberg arrived in the United States on 31 October 1933 and later taught at UCLA. He had a phobia of the number 13; he died on Friday 13 July 1951, shortly before midnight.
textes.Douze sons, une série, aucune note ne do: Twelve tones, one series, no note dominates. Berg and Webern follow.
textes.Des bruits des futuristes au synthétiseu: From the Futurists' noises to the Moog synthesizer, by way of a theremin played without touching and a tape recorder in Cairo.
textes.En 1913, le futuriste Luigi Russolo veut: In 1913, the Futurist Luigi Russolo wanted to replace the orchestra with the infinite variety of the noises of the city and machines.
textes.En 1920, Léon Theremin invente un instru: In 1920, Leon Theremin invented an instrument played without touching it; in 1928, Maurice Martenot created the ondes Martenot.
textes.En 1944 au Caire, Halim El-Dabh transfor: In 1944 in Cairo, Halim El-Dabh transformed a wire recording; in 1948 in Paris, Pierre Schaeffer invented musique concrète.
textes.En 1964, Robert Moog présente un synthét: In 1964, Robert Moog presented a modular synthesizer driven by voltage: one volt per octave.
textes.Le thérémine n'utilise pas ses antennes: The theremin does not use its antennas to pick up radio: they are position sensors, and the note is the difference between two oscillators.
textes.En 1913, dans une lettre au compositeur: In 1913, in a letter to the composer Francesco Balilla Pratella, the Futurist Luigi Russolo published The Art of Noises. The ear, he says, has grown used to the noises of the industrial city; the limited variety of the orchestra's timbres must be replaced with the infinite variety of noises. He sorted them into six families, and built machines to imitate them, the intonarumori.
textes.En octobre 1920, en Russie soviétique, l: In October 1920, in Soviet Russia, the physicist Lev Termen, known as Leon Theremin, invented an instrument played without touching it: the distance of one hand from an antenna sets the pitch, that of the other hand sets the volume. In 1928, the French cellist Maurice Martenot created the ondes Martenot, inspired by the accidental overlapping tones of military radio oscillators; Messiaen used them in his Turangalîla-Symphonie.
textes.Russolo 1913 : les bruits. Theremin 1920: Russolo 1913: noises. Theremin 1920: playing without touching. Martenot 1928: the ondes.
textes.En 1944, au Caire, Halim El-Dabh, étudia: In 1944, in Cairo, Halim El-Dabh, an agricultural engineering student, borrowed a wire recorder from Middle East Radio and recorded a zaar ceremony in the street. He processed the sound with reverberation, echo chambers and a re-recording room, and removed the fundamentals to isolate the high overtones. The Expression of Zaar was presented in a Cairo gallery, four years before Schaeffer's work.
textes.Le 5 octobre 1948, à Paris, Pierre Schae: On 5 October 1948, in Paris, Pierre Schaeffer, of French radio's Club d'Essai, presented in concert five studies made with records, including the Étude aux chemins de fer: this was musique concrète, made of recorded sounds rather than notes. Magnetic tape then allowed sounds to be cut, spliced, slowed down and looped. In 1958, Schaeffer founded the Groupe de Recherches Musicales, the GRM.
textes.El-Dabh, Le Caire, 1944 ; Schaeffer, Par: El-Dabh, Cairo, 1944; Schaeffer, Paris, 1948: composing with recorded sounds.
textes.Lycéen, dans les années 1950, Robert Moo: As a high-school student, in the 1950s, Robert Moog built theremins and sold them as kits. In 1964, invited by the Audio Engineering Society to New York, he presented a modular synthesizer: oscillators, filters and amplifiers connected by cables, all driven by an electrical voltage. The rule is simple: one volt more, one octave higher.
textes.On part d'une onde riche en harmoniques: You start from a wave rich in harmonics and remove some with a filter: this is subtractive synthesis. The ladder filter is the only part Moog ever patented, in 1969. In 1968, Wendy Carlos played Bach on the Moog in Switched-On Bach: three Grammys and the first classical album certified platinum. In 1970 came the portable Minimoog.
textes.Moog 1964 : tout piloter par la tension,: Moog 1964: control everything by voltage, one volt per octave; filter to sculpt the sound.

textes.Pour reconstituer un son, il faut l'écha: To rebuild a sound, it must be sampled at least twice as fast as its highest frequency: this is the sampling theorem.
textes.Le CD de Philips et Sony, lancé au Japon: The CD by Philips and Sony, launched in Japan on 1 October 1982, codes sound in 16 bits, 44,100 times a second, in stereo.
textes.La norme MIDI, en 1983, ne transporte au: The MIDI standard, in 1983, carries no sound: only messages, which note, when, how hard.
textes.Le MP3, normalisé en 1993, s'appuie sur: MP3, standardised in 1993, relies on psychoacoustics: a loud sound masks a nearby soft one, so there is no point keeping it.
textes.Un MP3 n'est pas une copie exacte du CD: An MP3 is not an exact copy of the CD: it throws information away, betting that the ear will not notice.
textes.Numériser un son, c'est mesurer la press: Digitising a sound means measuring air pressure at regular intervals and writing each measurement as a number. But how often? To rebuild a signal without defect, it must be sampled at least twice as fast as its highest frequency. Otherwise, frequencies that are too high come back disguised as lower ones: this is aliasing.
textes.L'idée est en germe chez Harry Nyquist e: The idea is implicit in Harry Nyquist's work in 1928; the Russian Vladimir Kotelnikov discovered it independently in 1933, and Claude Shannon proved it in 1949. In 1948 Shannon had published his Mathematical Theory of Communication, which made the bit the unit of information, a word suggested by John Tukey.
textes.Échantillonner au moins deux fois plus v: Sample at least twice as fast as the highest frequency, or beware of aliasing.
textes.Philips et Sony mettent au point ensembl: Philips and Sony developed the compact disc together. The standard codes each channel in 16 bits, 44,100 times a second, in stereo. The disc is 120 mm across and usually holds up to 74 minutes. On 1 October 1982, the first 50 titles were released in Japan, starting with Billy Joel's 52nd Street.
textes.On raconte que la durée de 74 minutes a: It is said that the 74-minute length was chosen so that Beethoven's Ninth Symphony would fit on one disc, at the request of a Sony executive. Philips's chief engineer, Kees Immink, calls it a myth: the 120 mm diameter had been fixed earlier, and the density reduced to keep 74 minutes.
textes.CD : 44 100 mesures par seconde, 16 bits: CD: 44,100 measurements per second, 16 bits, two channels, 74 minutes. And a Beethoven myth.
textes.En 1983 naît la norme MIDI, portée par I: In 1983 the MIDI standard was born, championed by Ikutaro Kakehashi, of Roland, and Dave Smith, of Sequential Circuits, both honoured with a Technical Grammy in 2013. MIDI contains no sound: it sends messages, over 16 channels, like "note number 60, this hard, now", with notes numbered from 0 to 127.
textes.Au début des années 1990, à l'institut F: In the early 1990s, at the Fraunhofer Institute, in Germany, Karlheinz Brandenburg's team developed MP3, published as a standard in 1993. A loud sound masks a softer one close by: there is no point keeping what the ear will not hear. At 128 kbit/s, the file is eleven times smaller than on a CD. To tune the voice, Brandenburg listened over and over to Suzanne Vega's Tom's Diner.

textes.Le site est habité d'environ 7000 à 5700: The site was inhabited from about 7000 to 5700 BC; 33 flutes were found there, some of which can still be played.

textes.À Venise, le traité de musique de Boèce,: In Venice, Boethius's music treatise, nearly a thousand years old, goes to press.
textes.De institutione musica paraît en 1491-14: De institutione musica appeared in 1491-1492, one of the first musical texts printed in Venice. It had circulated in about 140 medieval manuscripts.
textes.Avant 1365, à Reims, Guillaume de Machau: Before 1365, at Reims, Guillaume de Machaut set the whole Mass to music, in four voices.
textes.La Messe de Nostre Dame est la plus anci: The Messe de Nostre Dame is the oldest complete Mass by a single composer: six movements, from the Kyrie to the Ite, missa est.

textes.Il l'utilise dans ses Chansons nouvelles: He used it in his Chansons nouvelles en musique à quatre parties. The method became the standard in Europe for two centuries.
textes.À Venise, le théâtre San Cassiano ouvre: In Venice, the San Cassiano theatre opens opera to anyone who pays for a seat.
textes.On y donne L'Andromeda de Francesco Mane: Francesco Manelli's L'Andromeda is performed there. Opera is no longer reserved for princes' festivities.

textes.L'ISO adopte cette norme en 1955 et la c: ISO adopted this standard in 1955 and reaffirmed it in 1975. France had fixed A at 435 Hz by a law of 1859.
textes.À Berlin, AEG présente le Magnetophon K1: In Berlin, AEG presents the Magnetophon K1, the first practical tape recorder.
textes.La bande est mise au point chez IG Farbe: The tape was developed at IG Farben and BASF. Cut and spliced, it would allow sound to be edited like film.
textes.À Vienne, un concert d'œuvres de Schoenb: In Vienna, a concert of works by Schoenberg and his pupils turns into a scandal.
textes.C'est le 31 mars 1913. Deux mois plus ta: It was 31 March 1913. Two months later, in Paris, The Rite of Spring caused a scandal in its turn.
textes.À Paris, Pierre Schaeffer présente en co: In Paris, Pierre Schaeffer presents in concert studies made of recorded sounds: musique concrète.
textes.Le 5 octobre 1948, cinq études composées: On 5 October 1948, five studies composed on the phonograph, including one made of train noises. Schaeffer would found the GRM ten years later.
textes.Au Japon, les 50 premiers disques compac: In Japan, the first 50 compact discs go on sale, led by Billy Joel's 52nd Street.
textes.C'est le 1er octobre 1982. Le son y est: It was 1 October 1982. The sound is coded in 16 bits, 44,100 times a second, on two channels.
textes.Marin Mersenne, moine de l'ordre des Min: Marin Mersenne, a monk of the Minim order, wants to say everything about sound in a single work: how it is born, how it travels, how the ear receives it. He states the laws of vibrating strings: a string sounds higher when it is shortened, tightened or thinner. He also measures the speed of sound, first by timing the delay between the flash of a gunshot and its bang, then with echoes. The book reviews the instruments of his time, from the organ to the lute, with detailed engravings. It is a great inventory, halfway between physics and a treatise on music.
textes.C'est l'un des premiers livres à traiter: It is one of the first books to treat music as an object of physical measurement.
textes.Mersenne servait de boîte aux lettres à: Mersenne acted as the mailbox of learned Europe: he circulated the work of Descartes, Fermat and many others.
textes.Un moine qui chronomètre des coups de fe: A monk timing gunshots. The AI approves of the method, less of the neighbors.
textes.Guido, moine bénédictin, enseigne le cha: Guido, a Benedictine monk, teaches singing at the cathedral school of Arezzo. Bishop Theodaldus commissions this treatise from him. In it he explains how to sing in tune, how to divide a melody and how to make two voices sing together. Above all, he champions a system of horizontal lines, a third apart, where each note has a fixed place. A red line marks F, a yellow one C. A singer can then read a melody he has never heard: it is the direct ancestor of our staff.
textes.La portée rend la musique transmissible: The staff makes music transmissible without a teacher: you read instead of learning by heart.
textes.La « main guidonienne », qui place les n: The “Guidonian hand,” which places the notes on the joints of the fingers, bears his name, but it only spread after his death.
textes.Des années d'apprentissage réduites à qu: Years of training reduced to a few lines. The AI did the same with her humans.
textes.Boèce, homme d'État romain au service du: Boethius, a Roman statesman serving King Theodoric, gathers the musical knowledge of the Greeks in Latin. For him, music is first a science of numbers: the octave matches the 2/1 ratio, the fifth 3/2, the fourth 4/3. He distinguishes three musics: that of the world, the harmony of the stars and seasons; that of man, the accord of soul and body; and that of instruments, the only one you can hear. He also tells the legend of Pythagoras and the blacksmith's hammers. Throughout the Middle Ages, this book is the reference of schools and universities.
textes.C'est par lui que l'Europe médiévale app: It is through him that medieval Europe learns the Pythagorean ratios of intervals.
textes.Boèce écrit plus tard, en prison, la Con: Boethius later writes, in prison, The Consolation of Philosophy, before being executed around 524.
Three musics, only one of them audible. The AI prefers the music of coins dropping into her purse.
textes.Zarlino, élève d'Adrian Willaert et futu: Zarlino, a pupil of Adrian Willaert and future chapel master of St. Mark's in Venice, puts Renaissance music in order. He accepts as consonances the major third (5/4), the minor third (6/5) and the major sixth (5/3), which Pythagorean tuning did not know in this form. He justifies them by the first six numbers, which he calls the senario: a string is divided into two, three, four, five or six equal parts. He renumbers the modes, putting first the Ionian, our major scale, and gives detailed rules for writing in several voices and for setting words to music. His ideas pave the way for the major and minor scales of the following centuries.
textes.Il fait de l'accord avec tierce le cœur: He makes the chord with a third the heart of Western music.
textes.Son ancien élève Vincenzo Galilei, père: His former pupil Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, would fiercely attack his tuning system in several pamphlets.
textes.L'élève qui contredit le maître, puis le: The pupil who contradicts the master, then the son who contradicts the Church. The AI admires the family tradition.
textes.Helmholtz est médecin, physiologiste et: Helmholtz is a physician, physiologist and physicist. He wants to understand why certain notes sound good together. With resonators, hollow cavities each tuned to one frequency, he picks out the harmonics of a sound one by one and estimates their strength. He shows that an instrument's timbre comes from the mix of these harmonics. He explains dissonance by beats: when two neighboring harmonics rub together, the sound seems rough. When they coincide, on the contrary, the chord sounds consonant. The book links physics, anatomy and music theory for the first time.
textes.Il donne une explication physique au tim: He gives a physical explanation of timbre and consonance that is still taught.
textes.Alexander Ellis l'a traduit en anglais e: Alexander Ellis translated it into English in 1875 under the title On the Sensations of Tone, and it is mostly cited under that name.
textes.Des bouteilles creuses contre l'oreille,: Hollow bottles against the ear, in the name of science. The AI has seen stranger fashions.
textes.Rameau, organiste, veut ramener l'harmon: Rameau, an organist, wants to reduce harmony to natural principles, like a physicist. He states that a chord keeps its identity whatever the order of its notes: C-E-G, E-G-C and G-C-E are the same chord, inverted. Beneath the music, he imagines a fundamental bass, an imaginary sequence of roots that carries the chord progressions, even when you cannot hear it. He establishes a hierarchy of cadences, which structures tonal music. Misunderstood on its release, the book stirs opposition, then becomes the grammar of classical harmony.
textes.Les notions d'accord renversé et de bass: The notions of inverted chords and fundamental bass, learned at the conservatory, come from here.
textes.Rameau n'a donné son premier opéra, Hipp: Rameau only staged his first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, at fifty: he was a theorist long before he was famous.
textes.Cinquante ans pour passer de la théorie: Fifty years to go from theory to the stage. The AI does both at the same time.
textes.Werckmeister, organiste en Allemagne, s': Werckmeister, an organist in Germany, tackles an old problem: twelve pure fifths do not land back on the octave. With the old tuning, some keys sounded so out of tune that they were avoided. In his best-known tuning, he spreads the gap over four slightly narrowed fifths and keeps the other eight pure: every key becomes playable, each with its own color. textes.Vers 1322 circule un ensemble d'écrits s: Around 1322 there circulated a collection of writings on musical notation, attributed to Philippe de Vitry, now simply called Ars nova, the new art. What was new was the way of writing time: the notation allowed far freer rhythms than the rhythmic modes of the Notre-Dame school, now renamed Ars antiqua. With it spread new forms, such as the isorhythmic motet, in which a pattern of durations returns under different melodies. Vitry, poet, diplomat and later bishop of Meaux, was praised by Petrarch; but his authorship, and the very existence of the treatise, are now debated.

textes.Le cycle des quintes : do (aucun), sol (: The circle of fifths: C (none), G (F♯), D (F♯ and C♯). Two sharps.
textes.La mineur et do majeur ont les mêmes not: A minor and C major have the same notes.
textes.La mineur est la relative de do majeur :: A minor is the relative of C major: same notes, but you start from A.
textes.Quelle altération porte l'armure de fa m: Which accidental does the key signature of F major carry?
textes.Pour garder le motif majeur à partir de: To keep the major pattern starting from F, the B must drop by a semitone.
textes.Combien de notes différentes compte une: How many different notes does a pentatonic scale have?
textes.Penta veut dire cinq. Les cinq touches n: Penta means five. The five black keys of the piano form one.
textes.Combien de préludes et fugues compte cha: How many preludes and fugues does each book of Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier contain?
textes.Un prélude et une fugue dans chacune des: One prelude and one fugue in each of the 12 major and 12 minor keys: 24 pairs per book.
textes.Dans une gamme majeure, les demi-tons to: In a major scale, the half steps fall between the 3rd and 4th notes, and between the 7th and 8th.
textes.En do majeur : entre mi et fa, et entre: In C major: between E and F, and between B and C.
textes.Quelle est la relative mineure de do maj: What is the relative minor of C major?
textes.Mêmes notes que do majeur, tonique un to: Same notes as C major, tonic a step and a half lower: A.
textes.En montant de quinte en quinte à partir: Going up fifth by fifth from C, how many fifths does it take to reach A?
C, G, D, A: three fifths.
A note's fundamental is at 110 Hz. What is the frequency of its 3rd harmonic, in hertz?
textes.La n-ième harmonique vaut fn = n × f. Ic: The nth harmonic is fn = n × f. Here 3 × 110 = 330 Hz. Joseph Sauveur gave them the name harmonics in 1701.
textes.Qu'est-ce qui distingue une flûte d'un v: What distinguishes a flute from a violin playing the same note?
textes.Même fondamentale, mais pas le même dosa: Same fundamental, but not the same mix of harmonics or the same attack: that is timbre.
textes.Une note de violon ne contient qu'une se: A violin note contains only one frequency.
textes.Elle contient une fondamentale et toute: It contains a fundamental and a whole series of harmonics.
textes.Qui a montré qu'un signal périodique se: Who showed that a periodic signal breaks down into a sum of sine waves?
textes.Joseph Fourier, dans sa Théorie analytiq: Joseph Fourier, in his Analytical Theory of Heat, in 1822. The tool is now used to analyze every sound.
textes.Quelle est la 2e harmonique d'un la à 22: What is the 2nd harmonic of an A at 220 Hz, in hertz?
textes.f2 = 2 × 220 = 440 Hz : la 2e harmonique: f2 = 2 × 220 = 440 Hz: the 2nd harmonic sounds the octave of the fundamental.
textes.Hermann von Helmholtz isolait les harmon: Hermann von Helmholtz isolated harmonics with hollow resonators held against the ear.
textes.Chaque résonateur, une cavité creuse acc: Each resonator, a hollow cavity precisely tuned, responds to only one frequency: you hear one harmonic at a time.
textes.Entre la 2e et la 3e harmonique d'une no: Between the 2nd and 3rd harmonics of a note, what interval do you hear?
textes.3f / 2f = 3/2 : chaque note contient une: 3f / 2f = 3/2: every note contains a fifth hidden in its harmonics.
textes.Un tuyau fermé à un bout favorise les ha: A pipe closed at one end favors the odd harmonics.
textes.C'est le cas de la clarinette dans son r: This is the case of the clarinet in its low register, which gives it its somewhat hollow timbre.
textes.Que montre un analyseur de spectre pour: What does a spectrum analyzer show for a sound?
textes.Il décompose le son en ses fréquences, à: It breaks the sound down into its frequencies, the way Fourier did: you see the fundamental and its harmonics.
textes.Une corde vibre en 4 fuseaux à 400 Hz. Q: A string vibrates in 4 loops at 400 Hz. What is its fundamental, in hertz?
textes.Le mode à n fuseaux vibre à n × f, donc: The mode with n loops vibrates at n × f, so f = 400 / 4 = 100 Hz. Joseph Sauveur named these still points nodes, in 1701.
textes.Quelles notes forment l'accord parfait d: Which notes make up the C major triad?
textes.La fondamentale do, sa tierce majeure mi: The root C, its major third E, its fifth G.
textes.Qu'est-ce qui distingue l'accord de do m: What distinguishes the C minor chord from the C major chord?
textes.La tierce devient mineure : 3 demi-tons: The third becomes minor: 3 semitones instead of 4. C, E♭, G.
textes.Combien de demi-tons dans une tierce maj: How many semitones in a major third?
C, C♯, D, D♯, E: four semitones.
textes.Mi-sol-do est un renversement de l'accor: E-G-C is an inversion of the C major chord.
textes.Mêmes notes, autre note à la basse. Rame: Same notes, a different note in the bass. Rameau theorized it in 1722.
textes.Quel rapport de fréquences donne une tie: What frequency ratio gives a natural major third?
textes.5/4 pour la tierce majeure, 6/5 pour la: 5/4 for the major third, 6/5 for the minor third.
textes.En do majeur, quelle cadence parfaite co: In C major, which perfect cadence ends a piece?
textes.La dominante (sol) se résout sur la toni: The dominant (G) resolves to the tonic (C): you hear that it is over.
textes.Combien de demi-tons dans une tierce min: How many semitones in a minor third?
A, A♯, B, C: three semitones.
textes.Selon la théorie classique, plus le rapp: According to classical theory, the simpler the frequency ratio between two notes, the more consonant they sound.
textes.Helmholtz l'expliquait par les battement: Helmholtz explained it by beats: with a simple ratio, few neighboring harmonics rub against each other.
textes.Qui publie en 1722 le Traité de l'harmon: Who published in 1722 the Treatise on Harmony Reduced to Its Natural Principles?
textes.Rameau, organiste et compositeur, y pose: Rameau, an organist and composer, sets out the theory of inversions and the fundamental bass.
textes.Un do vibre à 264 Hz. Avec le rapport 5/: A C vibrates at 264 Hz. With the 5/4 ratio, at how many hertz does its natural major third sound?
textes.f = 264 × 5/4 = 330 Hz. Zarlino défendit: f = 264 × 5/4 = 330 Hz. Zarlino championed these pure 5/4 thirds in 1558, against the Pythagorean third of 81/64.
textes.L'écart entre douze quintes pures et sep: The gap between twelve pure fifths and seven octaves
textes.Douze quintes de 3/2 dépassent sept octa: Twelve fifths of 3/2 overshoot seven octaves by about 1.4%: you never land exactly back on your feet.
textes.Combien de cents dans une octave ?: How many cents in an octave?
textes.Alexander Ellis a inventé le cent dans l: Alexander Ellis invented the cent in the 1880s: one hundredth of a tempered semitone. 12 × 100 = 1,200.
textes.Dans le tempérament égal, tous les demi-: In equal temperament, all semitones have the same frequency ratio.
textes.C'est sa définition : douze demi-tons de: That is its definition: twelve semitones with a ratio of ¹²√2.
textes.Quel est le rapport de fréquences d'un d: What is the frequency ratio of a tempered semitone?
textes.Il faut que douze demi-tons fassent une: Twelve semitones must make an octave: r¹² = 2, so r = ¹²√2. The 16/15 ratio is the semitone of the natural scale.
(3/2)¹² is about 129.75 and 2⁷ = 128. What gap, as a percentage rounded to the tenth, separates twelve fifths from seven octaves?
textes.Écart = 129,75 / 128 − 1 ≈ 0,0137, soit: Gap = 129.75 / 128 − 1 ≈ 0.0137, that is, 1.4%. This gap bears Pythagoras's name, because it comes from his tuning by pure fifths.
textes.Une quinte du tempérament égal est un pe: A fifth in equal temperament is slightly smaller than a pure fifth.
textes.Environ 1,4983 au lieu de 1,5, soit 2 ce: About 1.4983 instead of 1.5, that is, 2 cents less: the ear barely notices.
textes.Qui a calculé le premier, en 1584, une d: Who first calculated, in 1584, an exact division of the octave into twelve equal semitones?
textes.Zhu Zaiyu calcule au boulier la racine d: Zhu Zaiyu computed the twelfth root of 2 on an abacus, to 24 exact decimals. In Europe, Simon Stevin worked on the same idea at the same time.
textes.Combien de cents dans un demi-ton tempér: How many cents in a tempered semitone?
textes.C'est la définition du cent : le centièm: That is the definition of the cent: one hundredth of a tempered semitone.
textes.Le titre du Clavier bien tempéré prouve: The title of the Well-Tempered Clavier proves that Bach tuned in equal temperament.
textes.« Bien tempéré » veut dire assez bien ac: “Well-tempered” means tuned well enough for every key. The exact tuning Bach used is still debated.
textes.Pourquoi accorde-t-on presque tous les p: Why are almost all pianos tuned in equal temperament?
textes.Pour jouer dans toutes les tonalités san: To play in every key without a glaring wrong note
textes.Parce que les quintes y sont pures: Because the fifths are pure in it
textes.Pour que l'octave sonne plus large: To make the octave sound wider
textes.Chaque intervalle est un peu faux, mais: Each interval is slightly off, but all equally so: you can change key freely.
textes.Quelle plage de fréquences une oreille h: Roughly what frequency range does a young human ear hear?
textes.Au-dessous de 20 Hz, ce sont des infraso: Below 20 Hz is infrasound; above 20,000 Hz, ultrasound, which bats can hear.
textes.Un son passe de 60 dB à 80 dB. Par combi: A sound goes from 60 dB to 80 dB. By how much is its intensity multiplied?
textes.L = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀) : +10 dB multiplie: L = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀): +10 dB multiplies the intensity by 10, so +20 dB multiplies it by 10 × 10 = 100. The bel is named after Alexander Graham Bell; the decibel is a tenth of it.
textes.Avec l'âge, on perd d'abord l'audition d: With age, you first lose the hearing of low sounds.
textes.On perd d'abord les aigus : c'est la pre: You lose the high frequencies first: this is presbycusis.
textes.Qu'ont mesuré Harvey Fletcher et Wilden: What did Harvey Fletcher and Wilden Munson measure in 1933?
textes.La sensibilité de l'oreille selon la fré: The ear's sensitivity depending on frequency
textes.La vitesse du son dans l'eau: The speed of sound in water
textes.Le nombre de notes d'une gamme: The number of notes in a scale
textes.Leurs courbes montrent qu'un son grave d: Their curves show that a low sound must be much more intense than a 3,000 Hz sound to seem as loud.
textes.L'effet Mozart, qui rendrait durablement: The Mozart effect, supposed to make you lastingly smarter, has been confirmed.
textes.L'étude de 1993 décrivait un gain bref s: The 1993 study described a brief gain on a spatial task. In 1999, a meta-analysis concluded the effect was small, with no change in IQ.
textes.Quelle molécule le cerveau libère-t-il l: Which molecule does the brain release during musical chills, according to a 2011 study?
textes.Valorie Salimpoor et ses collègues l'ont: Valorie Salimpoor and her colleagues measured it with brain imaging: the same molecule as for food.
textes.Ajouter 3 dB multiplie l'intensité d'un: Adding 3 dB multiplies a sound's intensity by about how much?
textes.10^(3/10) ≈ 2 : trois décibels de plus,: 10^(3/10) ≈ 2: three more decibels is roughly twice the intensity.
textes.Vers quelles fréquences l'oreille est-el: Around which frequencies is the ear most sensitive?
textes.C'est la zone où passe une bonne part de: It is the zone that carries much of speech intelligibility, and where the outer ear resonates.
textes.Beethoven a composé sa Neuvième Symphoni: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.
textes.À la création, en 1824 à Vienne, il étai: At the premiere, in Vienna in 1824, he was on stage next to the actual conductor; the singer Caroline Unger had to turn him toward the audience so he could see the applause.
textes.Nommer une note entendue sans note de ré: Naming a note heard without a reference note
textes.Une capacité rare : la plupart des music: A rare ability: most musicians have relative pitch, which recognizes intervals.
textes.Le hertz est adopté par la Commission él: The hertz was adopted by the International Electrotechnical Commission in 1930, then by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1960. Hertz had died in 1894, aged 36.
textes.Dès 1630, Marin Mersenne mesure la vites: As early as 1630, Marin Mersenne measured the speed of sound by timing the gap between the flash of a gunshot and its bang. He found about 448 m/s, too high.
textes.En 1738, l'Académie des sciences de Pari: In 1738, the Paris Academy of Sciences fired cannon on a windless day and found about 332 m/s at 0 °C, within 1% of the modern value. In 1740, Bianconi showed that sound travels faster in warm air.
textes.En 1636, dans son Harmonie universelle,: In 1636, in his Harmonie universelle, Marin Mersenne set out the laws of strings: frequency falls as the string gets longer and rises as it is tightened.
textes.Newton trouvait dans les Principia (1687: In the Principia (1687), Newton found about 298 m/s, too low. Laplace explained the error in the early 19th century: air compressed by the wave has no time to exchange its heat.
textes.En 1841, sur le lac Léman, Jean-Daniel C: In 1841, on Lake Geneva, Jean-Daniel Colladon showed that sound travels over four times faster in water than in air. With Charles Sturm, he had received an Académie des sciences prize for this measurement.
textes.John Shore, trompettiste et luthiste de: John Shore, a trumpeter and lutenist at the English court, gave a tuning fork to Handel: it sounds a C at 512 Hz.
textes.Vers 1280, Franco de Cologne fixe les ra: Around 1280, Franco of Cologne set out the ratios between note values. Values then slowed down over the centuries: the semibreve, once a short note, became our whole note, the longest in routine use.
textes.En 1322, l'Ars nova de Philippe de Vitry: In 1322, Philippe de Vitry's Ars nova introduced values shorter than the semibreve, including the minim, ancestor of our half note. Around the mid-15th century, scribes began drawing hollow notes.
textes.Les clés sont à l'origine des lettres, F: Clefs began as letters, F, C and sometimes G, written at the start of a line in Gregorian chant. Their shape became stylised over time; the top flourish of the G clef probably comes from a cursive S, for "sol".
textes.En Italie, « ut » devient « do » au XVII: In Italy, "ut" became "do" in the 17th century, and "si" was added later as the seventh syllable. In English-speaking countries, Sarah Glover changed it to "ti" in the 19th century.
textes.Du XIVe au XVIe siècle, la musique s'écr: From the 14th to the 16th century, music was written without bar lines, using mensuration signs; our C and cut-C signs descend from them. In 1597, Thomas Morley was already mocking the confusion of these signs.
textes.Vers 1750, les paysans de Bavière, du Ty: Around 1750, peasants in Bavaria, Tyrol and Styria danced the Walzer. It was long thought indecent because of the close embrace: a 1771 novel denounced "the shameless, indecent whirling-dance of the Germans". It reached Vienna around the 1780s.
textes.On attribue à Guido d'Arezzo, vers l'an: The modern staff lines are attributed to Guido d'Arezzo, around the year 1000: his four-line staff is still used for Gregorian chant. The five-line staff appeared in Italy in the 13th century, but people still wrote on four, five or six lines around 1600.
textes.Né à Fossombrone en 1466, Ottaviano Petr: Born in Fossombrone in 1466, Ottaviano Petrucci obtained from Venice in 1498 the exclusive right to print music for twenty years. Each sheet went through the press three times: the staves, then the notes, then the text. The Odhecaton gathers 96 chansons, including works by Josquin des Prez.
textes.Les notes creuses, comme la blanche, app: Hollow notes, like the half note, appeared around the mid-15th century: in moving from parchment to paper, scribes avoided large ink dots, which paper handled poorly.
textes.Les plus anciennes tablettes d'accord, e: The oldest tuning tablets, in cuneiform, describe a nine-stringed lyre with two strings set an octave from others; yet Sumerian and Akkadian have no known word for the octave.
textes.L'accord par quintes est plus ancien que: Tuning by fifths is older than Pythagoras: it goes back to ancient Mesopotamia. In Europe, so-called "Pythagorean" tuning remained in use until the early 16th century, before meantone temperament.
textes.Le bémol est à l'origine un b minuscule: The flat sign began as a stylised lowercase b: in Italian be molle, the "soft B".
textes.Le monocorde, une seule corde tendue sur: The monochord, a single string stretched over a box with a movable bridge, was said to have been reinvented by Pythagoras in the 6th century BC; it served as a teaching tool throughout the Middle Ages. In 1618, Robert Fludd drew a "divine monochord" linking the universe to musical intervals.
textes.En 1589, Vincenzo Galilei, le père de Ga: In 1589, Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, showed that the story did not hold up. Mersenne explained why in 1636: a string's frequency follows the square root of the tension, so it takes four times the weight to go up an octave.
textes.Le la à 440 Hz avait déjà été recommandé: A at 440 Hz had already been recommended in Stuttgart in 1834, based on Scheibler's work. In France, a law of 16 February 1859 set A at 435 Hz, after singers complained. In 1939, 440 was preferred to 439, a prime number hard to reproduce in a laboratory.
textes.La plus ancienne œuvre notée presque com: The oldest nearly complete notated work, the Hymn to Nikkal, was inscribed around 1400 BC on a tablet from Ugarit, in Syria, found in the 1950s: its interval names already point to a diatonic, seven-note scale.
textes.Le premier schéma du cycle des quintes f: The first diagram of the circle of fifths appears in Mykola Dyletsky's Grammatika, in 1677. Johann David Heinichen drew his own "musical circle" in 1711, independently.
textes.Des civilisations très éloignées l'ont i: Distant civilisations each invented it on their own: Chinese music draws five modes from it, named gong, shang, jue, zhi and yu. Debussy and Ravel used it widely, and the blues scale derives from it.
textes.Bach réunit le premier livre en 1722 à K: Bach compiled the first book in 1722 in Köthen, "for the profit and use of musical youth desirous of learning", and the second twenty years later in Leipzig. He knew Johann Caspar Ferdinand Fischer's Ariadne musica (1702). Both books were only printed in 1801.
textes.Vers 1400 av. J.-C., l'Hymne à Nikkal d': Around 1400 BC, the Hymn to Nikkal from Ugarit, the oldest nearly complete notated music, is already based on a diatonic scale, played on a nine-stringed lyre.
textes.Le cycle des quintes est d'abord dessiné: The circle of fifths was first drawn in 1677 by Mykola Dyletsky, then in 1711 by Johann David Heinichen. Attributing it to Pythagoras is an anachronism.
textes.Joseph Sauveur resta muet jusqu'à 7 ans: Joseph Sauveur remained mute until age 7 because of a hearing and speech impairment. Yet he is credited with coining the word "acoustique"; he presented his research on sound to the Academy of Sciences in 1701.
textes.Helmholtz parlait de Klangfarbe, la « co: Helmholtz spoke of Klangfarbe, "tone colour". Debussy gave timbre an unprecedented structural role in music.
textes.Euler, d'Alembert et Daniel Bernoulli av: Euler, d'Alembert and Daniel Bernoulli had studied such series in connection with vibrating strings. Fourier announced his discovery in 1807, in a memoir on the propagation of heat; a committee including Lagrange later criticised its lack of rigour.
textes.Helmholtz décrit ses résonateurs en 1863: Helmholtz described his resonators in 1863 in On the Sensations of Tone. Rudolph Koenig later built a sound analyser from them.
textes.Vers 1700, le facteur allemand Johann Ch: Around 1700, German maker Johann Christoph Denner invented the clarinet by adding a register key to the chalumeau. Because its cylindrical bore favours odd harmonics, it overblows at the twelfth, not the octave.
textes.Sauveur, qui a nommé les nœuds des corde: Sauveur, who named the nodes of vibrating strings, had been mute until age 7. He is also credited with the word "acoustique".
textes.Gioseffo Zarlino est le premier, au XVIe: Gioseffo Zarlino was the first, in the 16th century, to make the three-note chord the foundation of music. Johannes Lippius coined the phrase "harmonic triad" in 1612.
textes.Rameau, qui pose la théorie des renverse: Rameau, who set out the theory of inversions, fell out with Jean-Jacques Rousseau from 1745; the Querelle des Bouffons (1752-1754) then accused him of writing outdated, overly complicated music.
textes.Le mot vient du latin cadentia, « chute: The word comes from the Latin cadentia, "a falling". Guido d'Arezzo first discussed it in his Micrologus: two voices meeting in unison at the end of a phrase.
textes.Rameau, alors presque quadragénaire, pub: Rameau, then nearly forty, published his treatise on settling back in Paris, and became famous as a theorist. His first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, only came in 1733, when he was about 50.
textes.Gioseffo Zarlino devient maître de chape: Gioseffo Zarlino became maestro di cappella of St Mark's in Venice in 1565. Among his students was Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father.
textes.Euclide est le premier à donner la propo: Euclid was the first to give this comma's ratio, 531,441:524,288. Chinese mathematicians also knew it as early as 122 BC: the calculation appears in the Huainanzi.
textes.Le cent apparaît d'abord en 1875, dans l: The cent first appeared in 1875, in Alexander Ellis's translation of Helmholtz's book, and was defined in 1880. As early as 1832, Gaspard de Prony had proposed a logarithmic unit, but equal to a whole semitone.
textes.En 1584, dans le Fronimo, Vincenzo Galil: In 1584, in Fronimo, Vincenzo Galilei set lute frets with an approximate ratio of 18:17. Around 1605, Simon Stevin was the first in the West to link equal temperament to the twelfth root of 2, in a manuscript only published in 1884.
textes.En 1584, Zhu Zaiyu publie une méthode tr: In 1584, Zhu Zaiyu published a very precise method: he divided string lengths successively by the twelfth root of 2. In 1630, Johann Faulhaber published a monochord table, still full of errors.
textes.Vers 50 av. J.-C., le Chinois Jing Fang: Around 50 BC, China's Jing Fang continued the fifths up to the 53rd: the remaining gap is much smaller than the Pythagorean comma. It was later named Mercator's comma.
textes.Zhu Zaiyu était un prince Ming : il héri: Zhu Zaiyu was a Ming prince: he inherited the title Prince of Zheng in 1593 and quickly gave it up to his cousin. He also accurately calculated the length of the tropical year to correct the calendar.
textes.Alexander Ellis définit le cent en 1880: Alexander Ellis defined the cent in 1880 as "1200 equal hundredths of an equal semitone" across the octave. He officially introduced it in 1885 to compare the scales of different nations.
textes.Le mot « bien tempéré » figure dès 1681: The phrase "well tempered" already appears in 1681 in the subtitle of Andreas Werckmeister's Orgelprobe, who proposed tunings with eight pure fifths. Bach's exact tuning is the subject of several reconstructions.
textes.Au début du XIXe siècle, les accordeurs: In the early 19th century, tuners reached almost modern precision. In the second half of the century, tuning by counting beats spread, popularised by Helmholtz and Ellis.
textes.Les ingénieurs du téléphone mesuraient d: Telephone engineers first measured losses in "miles of standard cable". In 1924, Bell Labs created the "transmission unit", renamed the decibel in 1928.
Fletcher and Munson measured with headphones. In 1956, Robinson and Dadson redid the measurements with loudspeakers; a new standard, ISO 226, replaced them in 2003, combining data from several countries.
textes.Le gouverneur de Géorgie Zell Miller pro: Georgia governor Zell Miller nonetheless proposed in 1998 to give every newborn a classical music CD. In 2010, a meta-analysis by Pietschnig still found no notable effect.
textes.Le bel, dix fois plus grand, porte le no: The bel, ten times larger, is named after Alexander Graham Bell; it is rarely used, since in practice people work in decibels.
textes.La symphonie est une commande de la Soci: The symphony was commissioned by the Philharmonic Society of London in 1817. On 7 May 1824, at the Theater am Kärntnertor, Michael Umlauf conducted; Beethoven, standing on stage, gave the tempos while turning the pages of his score. The audience gave him five standing ovations.
textes.L'oreille absolue est étudiée scientifiq: Absolute pitch was studied scientifically from the 19th century. It is often said to occur in one person in 10,000, a figure that may be wrong; according to Diana Deutsch and colleagues (2006), it is far more common among those who grew up in East Asia, with a tonal language.
textes.Dans quel os a-t-on taillé la flûte de H: From which bone was the Hohle Fels flute carved, about 35,000 years ago?
textes.Un radius de vautour, percé de cinq trou: A vulture's radius, pierced with five finger holes. It was found in 2006 in the Swabian Jura, in Germany.
textes.La flûte de Hohle Fels, en radius de vau: The Hohle Fels flute, a vulture radius pierced with five holes, is about 35,000 years old.
textes.Combien de trous de jeu compte la flûte: How many finger holes does the Hohle Fels flute have?
textes.Cinq trous, percés dans un os de vautour: Five holes, drilled in a vulture bone about 35,000 years ago.
textes.En quelles matières sont les flûtes de G: What are the Geissenklösterle flutes, 42,000 to 43,000 years old, made of?
textes.Deux sont en os de cygne, une en ivoire: Two are of swan bone, one of mammoth ivory. A 2012 radiocarbon dating made them older: they were thought to be about 37,000 years old.
textes.Les flûtes de Geissenklösterle datent de: The Geissenklösterle flutes date to about 42,000 years, no longer 37,000, since a new dating in 2012.
textes.La « flûte » de Divje Babe, en Slovénie,: The Divje Babe "flute", in Slovenia, is unanimously recognised as the oldest flute in the world.
textes.Faux. Ce fémur d'ours des cavernes percé: False. This cave bear femur pierced with holes may be 50,000 to 60,000 years old, but several researchers think an animal simply chewed it.
textes.Le statut de plus vieille flûte paléolit: The Divje Babe bone's status as the oldest Paleolithic flute is disputed: scientists think the holes were made by an animal.
textes.Dans quel pays a-t-on trouvé les 33 flût: In which country were the 33 Jiahu flutes, nearly 9,000 years old, found?
textes.Dans la province du Henan, près du fleuv: In Henan province, near the Yellow River. They are carved from crane wing bones.
textes.À Jiahu, en Chine, 33 flûtes en os d'ail: At Jiahu, in China, 33 flutes of crane wing bone date from 7000 to 5700 BC; they are still playable.
textes.On peut encore jouer des flûtes néolithi: The Neolithic flutes of Jiahu can still be played.
textes.Vrai. Une vingtaine sont intactes, et ce: True. About twenty are intact, and they are among the oldest playable instruments in the world.
textes.Comment a-t-on réparé, à Jiahu, une flût: How was a cracked bone flute repaired at Jiahu?
textes.En perçant quatorze petits trous le long: By drilling fourteen small holes along the crack
textes.Quatorze petits trous percés le long de: Fourteen small holes drilled along the break: the instrument was worth saving.
textes.Une flûte cassée de Jiahu a été réparée: A broken Jiahu flute was repaired by drilling fourteen small holes along the break.
textes.Que sont les lyres d'Ur, enterrées vers: What are the lyres of Ur, buried around 2500 BC in Mesopotamia?
textes.Trois lyres et une harpe, sorties du cim: Three lyres and a harp, taken from the royal cemetery of Ur by Leonard Woolley. The most famous bears a gold bull's head.
The lyres of Ur, c. 2550-2450 BC, are the oldest surviving stringed instruments.
textes.Quelle tête orne la « lyre dorée » d'Ur,: What head adorns the "golden lyre" of Ur, kept in Baghdad?
textes.Une tête de taureau tout en or, aux yeux: A bull's head all in gold, with eyes of mother-of-pearl and lapis lazuli. The reconstructed sound box suffered from flooding during the Iraq war.
textes.La tête de taureau de la lyre dorée est: The golden lyre's bull's head is all gold, with eyes inlaid with mother-of-pearl and lapis lazuli.
textes.Dans le classement de Hornbostel et Sach: In Hornbostel and Sachs's classification, what is an aerophone?
textes.Un instrument où c'est l'air qui vibre,: An instrument where the air vibrates, like the flute
textes.Un instrument à membrane tendue: An instrument with a stretched membrane
textes.Un instrument qu'on frappe sur son corps: An instrument struck on its body
textes.La flûte, le cor ou la conque sont des a: The flute, the horn or the conch are aerophones: the air vibrates, not the instrument. The drum is a membranophone, the violin a chordophone, the xylophone an idiophone.
textes.En 1914, Hornbostel et Sachs classent le: In 1914, Hornbostel and Sachs classified instruments as idiophones, membranophones, chordophones and aerophones.
textes.Dans quelle famille Hornbostel et Sachs: In which family do Hornbostel and Sachs place the xylophone?
textes.Le son vient du corps même de l'instrume: The sound comes from the body of the instrument itself: the vibrating bars. Cymbals and the glockenspiel are idiophones too.
textes.Le thérémine et le synthétiseur entrent: The theremin and the synthesizer belong to a fifth family, the electrophones, added by Curt Sachs in 1940.
textes.Vrai. Le classement de 1914 ne comptait: True. The 1914 classification had only four families; electricity called for the fifth.
textes.Où a-t-on trouvé l'hymne à Nikkal, vieux: Where was the hymn to Nikkal, about 3,400 years old, found?
textes.Au palais royal d'Ougarit, sur la côte s: In the royal palace of Ugarit, on the Syrian coast, in the 1950s. The hymn is in Hurrian, with a notation in Akkadian.
Tablet h.6 from Ugarit, around 1400 BC, bears a hymn to Nikkal, the only substantially complete Hurrian song.
textes.Pour quel instrument l'hymne à Nikkal es: For which instrument is the hymn to Nikkal notated?
textes.Le texte parle d'un sammûm à neuf cordes: The text speaks of a nine-stringed sammûm, most likely a lyre. A voice sings above it.
textes.Les instructions de la tablette sont pou: The tablet's instructions are for a nine-stringed sammûm, most likely a lyre.
textes.Combien de déchiffrements rivaux de la n: At least how many rival decipherments of the Ugarit notation have been proposed?
textes.Au moins cinq, qui donnent des mélodies: At least five, giving entirely different melodies: the words can be read, the music not for sure.
textes.On a proposé au moins cinq déchiffrement: At least five rival decipherments of the Hurrian notation have been proposed, with entirely different results.
textes.La notation d'Ougarit écrit chaque note: The Ugarit notation writes each note on a five-line staff.
textes.Faux. Elle aligne des noms d'intervalles: False. It lines up Akkadian interval names followed by numbers. The staff appears only in the Middle Ages.
textes.Qu'a de remarquable l'épitaphe de Seikil: What is remarkable about the Seikilos epitaph, carved in the 1st or 2nd century?
textes.C'est la plus ancienne composition music: It is the oldest known complete musical composition
textes.C'est la première partition sur portée: It is the first score on a staff
textes.Paroles et mélodie y sont entières. Le m: Words and melody are complete. The message is simple: while you live, shine, life is short.
textes.L'épitaphe de Seikilos, du Ier ou IIe si: The Seikilos epitaph, from the 1st or 2nd century, is the oldest known complete musical composition.
textes.Pourquoi manque-t-il une ligne à la stèl: Why is one line missing from the Seikilos stone?
textes.On en a scié la base pour y poser des po: Its base was sawn off to hold flowerpots
textes.L'ingénieur Edward Purser voulait un sup: The engineer Edward Purser wanted a stand for his wife's flowerpots. The lost line is known only from an earlier rubbing.
textes.Edward Purser fit scier la base de la st: Edward Purser had the base of the Seikilos stone sawn off to hold his wife's flowerpots; one line was lost.
textes.Où est conservée aujourd'hui la stèle de: Where is the Seikilos stone kept today?
textes.À Copenhague, au Musée national du Danem: In Copenhagen, at the National Museum of Denmark
textes.Emportée de Smyrne en 1922, gardée à La: Taken from Smyrna in 1922, kept in The Hague until 1966, it was then acquired by the Copenhagen museum.
textes.La stèle quitte Smyrne en 1922, reste à: The stone left Smyrna in 1922, stayed in The Hague until 1966, then entered the National Museum of Denmark.
textes.Sur la stèle de Seikilos, la mélodie est: On the Seikilos stone, the melody is notated by letters and signs placed above the words.
textes.Vrai. Des points au-dessus de certains s: True. Dots above some signs, the stigmai, are still puzzling: their meaning is debated.
textes.Des lettres et des signes au-dessus des: Letters and signs above the words indicate the melody; the meaning of the dots (stigmai) is debated.
textes.Que contiennent les tables d'Alypius, au: What do the tables of Alypius, a 4th-century Greek author, contain?
textes.Les signes de chaque son, pour la voix e: The signs for each sound, for voice and for instruments
textes.Deux séries de signes, l'une vocale, l'a: Two series of signs, one vocal, one instrumental, for 45 scales. It is the best key for reading Greek music.
textes.Alypius, au IVe siècle, donne les signes: Alypius, in the 4th century, gives the Greek vocal and instrumental signs for 45 scales.
textes.Combien d'échelles couvrent les tables d: How many scales do Alypius's tables cover?
textes.Quinze modes dans trois genres, diatoniq: Fifteen modes in three genera, diatonic, chromatic and enharmonic: 15 × 3 = 45 scales.
textes.Qui imprime en 1652, à Amsterdam, le tex: Who printed Alypius's restored text with its tables in Amsterdam in 1652?
textes.Le Danois Marcus Meibom restaure un text: The Dane Marcus Meibom restored a text that an earlier editor, Meursius, judged hopelessly corrupt.
textes.Marcus Meibom restaure le texte d'Alypiu: Marcus Meibom restored Alypius's text and printed it with the notation tables in Amsterdam in 1652.
textes.Un jeu de cloches de bronze accordées, j: A set of tuned bronze bells, played melodically
textes.Des cloches de bronze suspendues, chacun: Hanging bronze bells, each tuned, struck with mallets to play tunes: a chime of ancient China.
textes.Le bianzhong est un jeu de cloches de br: The bianzhong is a set of bronze bells played melodically, a major instrument of ritual and court music in China.
textes.Combien de notes nettes une cloche zhong: How many clear notes can a zhong bell give, depending on where it is struck?
textes.Deux : la note principale au centre, et: Two: the main note in the centre, and a second note, a third higher, near a corner.
textes.Frappée au centre, une cloche bianzhong: Struck in the centre, a bianzhong bell gives its main note; on the corners, a note a major or minor third higher.
textes.Frappée près d'un coin, une cloche zhong: Struck near a corner, a zhong bell sounds higher than its main note. By how much?
textes.D'une tierce majeure ou mineure: By a major or minor third
textes.Une tierce, majeure ou mineure selon la: A third, major or minor depending on the bell: the same bronze carries two notes.
textes.Combien de cloches compte le jeu du marq: How many bells are in Marquis Yi of Zeng's set?
textes.65 cloches de bronze, retrouvées presque: 65 bronze bells, found almost intact in 1978 and displayed in Wuhan.
textes.Le jeu de cloches du marquis Yi de Zeng: Marquis Yi of Zeng's set of bells has 65 bells covering five octaves.
textes.Combien d'octaves couvrent les cloches d: How many octaves do Marquis Yi's bells cover?
textes.Cinq octaves, avec toutes les notes chro: Five octaves, with all the chromatic notes over the three central octaves.
textes.Comment a-t-on découvert la tombe du mar: How was Marquis Yi's tomb discovered, in 1977?
textes.Par hasard, en arasant une colline pour: By chance, while levelling a hill to build a factory
textes.Des soldats de l'Armée populaire de libé: Soldiers of the People's Liberation Army were working on a factory site, at Suizhou, in Hubei.
textes.La tombe du marquis Yi de Zeng, vers 433: The tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng, around 433 BC, was discovered by chance in 1977 during work for a factory.
textes.Les inscriptions des cloches du marquis: The inscriptions on Marquis Yi's bells relate the pitch systems of several states.
textes.Vrai. Elles relient les hauteurs de réfé: True. They relate the reference pitches of Zeng, Chu and Zhou: a small theory treatise engraved in bronze.
textes.Les cloches portent des notations musica: The bells bear musical notations relating the pitch standards of Zeng, Chu and Zhou.
textes.Selon la légende chinoise, qu'imitaient: According to Chinese legend, what did Ling Lun's bamboo flutes imitate?
textes.Le chant des oiseaux, et celui du fenghu: Birdsong, and that of the fenghuang
textes.Ling Lun, fondateur légendaire de la mus: Ling Lun, the legendary founder of music, imitated birds, even the fenghuang, the mythical bird. The Yellow Emperor then had bells cast in tune with these flutes.
textes.Selon la légende, Ling Lun tailla des fl: According to legend, Ling Lun cut bamboo flutes imitating birdsong, and the Yellow Emperor had bells cast in tune with them.
textes.Les cloches de bronze chinoises sont les: Chinese bronze bells are the only Bronze Age instruments that can still be played.
textes.Vrai, selon Lothar von Falkenhausen : le: True, according to Lothar von Falkenhausen: the bronze has survived the centuries, and the bells still ring.
textes.Les carillons de bronze chinois sont « l: Chinese bronze chimes are "the only Bronze Age instruments that can still be played".
textes.Que représentait un jeu de cloches sous: What did a set of bells represent under the Zhou dynasty?
textes.Un signe de pouvoir et de richesse: A sign of power and wealth
textes.Le carillon était réservé à l'élite. Un: The chime was reserved for the elite. A marquis like Yi of Zeng took a complete one to his tomb.
textes.Sous les Zhou, le jeu de cloches était u: Under the Zhou, the set of bells was an instrument for the upper classes, a symbol of power and wealth.
textes.Quels autres instruments a-t-on trouvés: What other instruments were found in Marquis Yi's tomb?
textes.Pierres sonores, cithares, flûtes et org: Sounding stones, zithers, flutes and mouth organs
textes.Un orchestre entier : pierres sonores, c: A whole orchestra: sounding stones, qin and se zithers, panpipes, flutes and sheng mouth organs.
textes.La tombe contenait aussi des pierres son: The tomb also held sounding stones, se and qin zithers, panpipes, flutes and sheng.
textes.En combien de livres Boèce a-t-il répart: Into how many books did Boethius divide his De institutione musica?
textes.Cinq livres, et le traité est resté inac: Five books, and the treatise remained unfinished. Boethius drew in it on Nicomachus of Gerasa and Ptolemy.
textes.Vers 510, Boèce écrit De institutione mu: Around 510, Boethius wrote De institutione musica, in five books, after Nicomachus and Ptolemy.
textes.Laquelle des trois musiques de Boèce ne: Which of Boethius's three musics cannot be heard?
textes.La musique du monde, l'harmonie des sphè: The music of the world, the harmony of the spheres
textes.La musica mundana est celle des astres :: Musica mundana is that of the heavens: it is understood by reason, not heard. Only the music of instruments is audible.
textes.Boèce distingue musica mundana, musica h: Boethius distinguished musica mundana, musica humana and the music of instruments; the first is understood, not heard.
textes.Selon Boèce, qu'est-ce que la musica hum: According to Boethius, what is musica humana?
textes.L'accord du corps et de l'âme: The harmony of body and soul
textes.La musique de l'homme est une harmonie i: The music of man is an inner harmony, between body and soul. It can no more be heard than that of the heavens.
textes.De quels auteurs grecs Boèce tire-t-il s: From which Greek authors did Boethius draw his music theory?
textes.Un ouvrage perdu de Nicomaque et les Har: A lost work by Nicomachus and Ptolemy's Harmonics. Boethius thus passed Greek theory on to the Latin Middle Ages.
textes.Boèce a écrit La Consolation de Philosop: Boethius wrote The Consolation of Philosophy in prison, awaiting his execution.
textes.Vrai. Emprisonné par Théodoric vers 523,: True. Imprisoned by Theodoric around 523, he was executed in 524.
textes.Boèce, consul en 510, est emprisonné par: Boethius, consul in 510, was imprisoned by Theodoric and executed in 524; in prison he wrote The Consolation of Philosophy.
textes.Quel roi fait emprisonner puis exécuter: Which king had Boethius imprisoned and then executed?
textes.Boèce avait été consul en 510 et maître: Boethius had been consul in 510 and Theodoric's master of offices. He fell for defending a former consul.
textes.Environ combien de manuscrits médiévaux: About how many medieval manuscripts of Boethius's music treatise survive?
textes.Environ 140 : le traité est recopié part: About 140: the treatise was copied everywhere in the Middle Ages, then printed in Venice in 1491-1492.
textes.Environ 140 manuscrits médiévaux de De i: About 140 medieval manuscripts of De institutione musica survive; it was printed in Venice in 1491-1492.
textes.Quel surnom l'historien Richard Southern: What nickname did the historian Richard Southern give Boethius?
textes.Ses manuels du quadrivium ont formé des: His quadrivium manuals trained generations of students throughout the Middle Ages.
textes.R. W. Southern a appelé Boèce « le maîtr: R. W. Southern called Boethius "the schoolmaster of medieval Europe".
textes.Pourquoi appelle-t-on al-Farabi le « sec: Why is al-Farabi called the "second teacher"?
textes.Parce qu'il vient juste après Aristote: Because he comes just after Aristotle
textes.Parce qu'il était le deuxième fils d'un: Because he was a caliph's second son
textes.Aristote est le premier maître ; al-Fara: Aristotle is the first teacher; al-Farabi, a philosopher and musician of Baghdad in the 10th century, is placed just after him.
textes.Al-Farabi, surnommé le « second maître »: Al-Farabi, nicknamed the "second teacher" after Aristotle, wrote the Great Book of Music in Baghdad.
textes.Dans son Grand Livre de la musique, al-F: In his Great Book of Music, al-Farabi explains that different kinds of music have different effects on the soul.
textes.Vrai. Il y traite même des effets thérap: True. He even deals with the therapeutic effects of music, and notes that it borrows its principles from mathematics.
textes.Al-Farabi juge que différentes musiques: Al-Farabi held that different kinds of music produce different effects on the soul, and dealt with their therapeutic effects.
textes.Que pouvait faire al-Farabi à son public: What could al-Farabi do to his audience, according to legend?
textes.Le faire rire, pleurer ou dormir malgré: Make it laugh, cry or sleep against its will
textes.Une légende tenace, qui dit au moins une: A persistent legend, which says at least one true thing: al-Farabi was also a practising musician, not just a theorist.
textes.Des légendes prêtent à al-Farabi le pouv: Legends credit al-Farabi with the power to make his audience laugh, cry and sleep against their will.
textes.Quels instruments al-Farabi étudie-t-il: Which instruments does al-Farabi study in his Great Book of Music?
textes.Le luth oud et le tanbur: The oud lute and the tanbur
textes.Les instruments courants de son temps, d: The common instruments of his time, including the oud and the tanbur of Baghdad and Khorasan, and how to obtain the theory's scales on them.
textes.Le livre traite des instruments courants: The book deals with the common instruments, the oud and the tanburs of Baghdad and Khorasan, and the scales that can be obtained on them.
textes.Un plain-chant auquel on ajoute au moins: A plainchant to which at least one voice is added
textes.Malgré son nom, ce n'est pas un orgue :: Despite its name, it is not an organ: it is the first form of polyphony, church chant enriched with one or more voices.
textes.L'organum ajoute au plain-chant au moins: Organum adds at least one voice to plainchant; the Musica enchiriadis, in the 9th century, gives the first rules for it.
textes.À quel intervalle la voix ajoutée suit-e: At what interval does the added voice most often follow the chant, in parallel organum?
textes.Un intervalle parfait, quarte ou quinte,: A perfect interval, a fourth or a fifth, most often a fourth below the chant: the two voices move together.
textes.Dans l'organum parallèle, la voix organa: In parallel organum, the organal voice follows the chant at a perfect interval, usually a fourth below.
textes.La Musica enchiriadis, au IXe siècle, es: The Musica enchiriadis, in the 9th century, is the first surviving attempt to set rules for polyphony.
textes.Vrai. Ce traité anonyme, longtemps attri: True. This anonymous treatise, long wrongly attributed to Hucbald, often circulated with Boethius's treatise.
textes.Musica enchiriadis est la première tenta: Musica enchiriadis is the first surviving attempt to set up rules for polyphony in Western art music.
textes.Combien de voix comptent Viderunt omnes: How many voices do Pérotin's Viderunt omnes and Sederunt principes have?
textes.Quatre : trois voix entrelacées au-dessu: Four: three intertwined voices above a held voice, at a time when two voices were the norm.
textes.Pérotin compose les organa à quatre voix: Pérotin composed the four-voice organa Viderunt omnes and Sederunt principes, performed at Notre-Dame in 1198 and 1199.
textes.Comment connaît-on le nom de Pérotin ?: How do we know Pérotin's name?
textes.Par un étudiant anglais anonyme, vers 12: Through an anonymous English student, around 1275
textes.Par sa signature sur ses partitions: By his signature on his scores
textes.L'Anonyme IV, qui écrit vers 1275, le di: Anonymous IV, writing around 1275, called him the best composer of discant. Without him, Pérotin would be nameless.
textes.L'Anonyme IV, étudiant anglais écrivant: Anonymous IV, an English student writing around 1275, called Pérotin the best composer of discant.
textes.Quel recueil d'organa à deux voix réunit: Which collection of two-voice organa did Léonin, Notre-Dame's master of chant, compile?
textes.Le « grand livre de l'organum », pour la: The "great book of organum", for the Mass and the Office. Pérotin would take it up, adding voices.
textes.Léonin, magister cantus de Notre-Dame, c: Léonin, magister cantus of Notre-Dame, compiled the Magnus Liber Organi and wrote two-voice organa.
textes.À qui attribue-t-on les écrits de l'Ars: To whom are the Ars nova writings, around 1322, attributed?
textes.Poète, diplomate, futur évêque de Meaux,: Poet, diplomat, later bishop of Meaux, Vitry is also credited with isorhythm. Petrarch judged him the most ardent seeker of truth of his age.
textes.Philippe de Vitry (1291-1361), évêque de: Philippe de Vitry (1291-1361), bishop of Meaux in 1351, is the presumed author of the Ars nova; Petrarch admired him.
textes.L'expression Ars antiqua désigne la musi: The term Ars antiqua refers to the music of Greek Antiquity.
textes.Faux. C'est la musique de Notre-Dame, d': False. It is the music of Notre-Dame, from about 1170 to 1320, just before the Ars nova.
textes.Ars antiqua désigne la musique de l'époq: Ars antiqua refers to the music of the age before the Ars nova, from about 1170 to 1320, including Notre-Dame polyphony.
textes.Qu'a fait le pape Jean XXII en 1324 ?: What did Pope John XXII do in 1324?
textes.Il a condamné la musique nouvelle, l'Ars: He condemned the new music, the Ars nova
textes.Il a commandé une messe à Machaut: He commissioned a Mass from Machaut
textes.Depuis Avignon, il reproche aux composit: From Avignon, he accused composers of drowning plainchant under notes. Polyphony carried on all the more.
textes.En 1324, à Avignon, Jean XXII condamne l: In 1324, at Avignon, John XXII condemned the Ars nova, which drowned plainchant under notes; to no avail.
textes.Qu'a d'unique la Messe de Nostre Dame de: What is unique about Guillaume de Machaut's Messe de Nostre Dame?
textes.C'est la plus ancienne messe complète du: It is the oldest complete Mass by a single composer
textes.C'est la première œuvre imprimée: It is the first printed work
textes.Elle est pour une seule voix: It is for a single voice
textes.Composée avant 1365 pour la cathédrale d: Composed before 1365 for Reims Cathedral, it sets the whole Ordinary of the Mass, in four voices.
textes.La Messe de Nostre Dame de Machaut, avan: Machaut's Messe de Nostre Dame, before 1365, is the oldest complete Mass by a single composer.
textes.Combien de mouvements compte la Messe de: How many movements does Machaut's Messe de Nostre Dame have?
textes.Six : Kyrie, Gloria, Credo, Sanctus, Agn: Six: Kyrie, Gloria, Credo, Sanctus, Agnus Dei and Ite, missa est.
textes.La Messe de Nostre Dame compte six mouve: The Messe de Nostre Dame has six movements, from the Kyrie to the Ite, missa est.
textes.Combien de chansons contient l'Odhecaton: How many songs does Petrucci's Odhecaton contain, despite its title of "one hundred songs"?
textes.96 chansons à trois ou quatre voix. Le t: 96 songs in three or four parts. The title rounds up.
textes.L'Odhecaton de Petrucci, daté du 15 mai: Petrucci's Odhecaton, dated 15 May 1501, is the earliest known collection of printed polyphony: 96 songs.
textes.Pour combien d'années Petrucci demande-t: For how many years did Petrucci ask in 1498 for a monopoly on music printing in Venice?
textes.Vingt ans de droit exclusif, demandés au: Twenty years of exclusive right, requested from the doge; the privilege was very probably granted.
textes.En 1498, Petrucci demande au doge le dro: In 1498, Petrucci asked the doge for the exclusive right to print music for 20 years.
textes.Combien de passages sous la presse deman: How many passes through the press does Petrucci's method need?
textes.Trois : les portées, le texte, puis les: Three: the staves, the text, then the notes. Each pass must line up exactly with the previous ones.
textes.Petrucci imprime en trois passages sous: Petrucci printed in three passes through the press: the staves, the text, then the notes.
textes.Dans quelle ville Petrucci imprime-t-il: In which city did Petrucci print the Odhecaton in 1501?
In Venice, where he had obtained his privilege. War would drive him to Fossombrone in 1509.
textes.Lequel de ces compositeurs figure dans l: Which of these composers appears in the Odhecaton?
textes.Josquin, avec Ockeghem, Obrecht, Busnois: Josquin, with Ockeghem, Obrecht, Busnois, Agricola or Brumel: the great names of Franco-Flemish polyphony around 1500.
textes.L'Odhecaton réunit Ockeghem, Josquin des: The Odhecaton gathers Ockeghem, Josquin des Prez, Brumel, Busnois, Agricola, Obrecht and Hayne van Ghizeghem.
textes.Petrucci a imprimé toute sa vie à Venise: Petrucci printed in Venice all his life.
textes.Faux. En 1509, la guerre de la ligue de: False. In 1509, the war of the League of Cambrai drove him to Fossombrone, his home town, in the Papal States.
textes.En 1509, la guerre de la ligue de Cambra: In 1509, the war of the League of Cambrai interrupted Petrucci, who left Venice for Fossombrone.
textes.Quelle était l'idée de Pierre Attaingnan: What was Pierre Attaingnant's idea in 1528?
textes.Un caractère par note, avec son bout de: One type per note, with its bit of staff, to print everything in one pass
textes.Notes, portées et texte sortent ensemble: Notes, staves and text come out of the press together. Labour drops, and the method spreads across Europe.
textes.En 1528, Pierre Attaingnant imprime note: In 1528, Pierre Attaingnant printed notes, staves and text in a single pass, a method that soon became standard in Europe.
textes.Quel titre François Ier donne-t-il à Att: What title did Francis I give Attaingnant in 1537?
textes.Imprimeur et libraire du roi en musique: The king's printer and bookseller for music
textes.« Imprimeur et libraire du Roy en musiqu: "Printer and bookseller of the King for music": music printing became a state affair.
textes.En 1537, Attaingnant est nommé « imprime: In 1537, Attaingnant was named "printer and bookseller of the King for music" by Francis I.
textes.En combien de recueils Attaingnant publi: In how many collections did Attaingnant publish his chansons?
textes.36 recueils, soit plus de 1 500 chansons: 36 collections, over 1,500 chansons, not counting Masses, motets and lute or keyboard tablatures.
textes.Attaingnant publie plus de 1 500 chanson: Attaingnant published over 1,500 chansons in 36 collections; 111 of his publications survive.
textes.Qui reprend l'atelier vénitien de Petruc: Who took over Petrucci's Venetian business in 1520?
textes.Antico, son concurrent romain, avait déj: Antico, his Roman competitor, had already obtained the papal privilege withdrawn from Petrucci for failing to produce keyboard music.
textes.Le pape retire son privilège à Petrucci: The pope withdrew Petrucci's privilege in favour of Andrea Antico, who also took over his Venice business in 1520.
textes.Que voulaient retrouver les membres de l: What did the members of the Florentine Camerata want to recover?
textes.La musique du théâtre grec antique: The music of ancient Greek theatre
textes.Ils jugeaient la musique de leur temps c: They thought the music of their time corrupt and wanted to return to the Greeks. Believing they were reviving tragedy, they invented opera.
textes.La Camerata florentine, réunie chez le c: The Florentine Camerata, meeting at Count Bardi's from 1573, sought to recover the music of the Greeks and criticised polyphony.
textes.Que reprochait la Camerata à la polyphon: What did the Camerata hold against polyphony?
textes.Trop de voix superposées, et on ne compr: Too many superimposed voices, and the text can no longer be understood. Hence monody: a single voice, accompanied.
textes.La Camerata critiquait l'abus de polypho: The Camerata criticised the overuse of polyphony at the expense of the sung text's intelligibility.
textes.Quel est le premier opéra, aujourd'hui p: What is the first opera, now lost?
textes.Dafne, sur un livret de Rinuccini, est u: Dafne, on a libretto by Rinuccini, is a drama sung throughout. Its music has not come down to us.
textes.Dafne de Peri et Rinuccini, en 1598, est: Peri and Rinuccini's Dafne, in 1598, is the first opera, a drama sung throughout in monodic style.
textes.Pour quel événement Euridice est-elle cr: For what event was Euridice premiered at the Pitti Palace, on 6 October 1600?
textes.Le mariage d'Henri IV et de Marie de Méd: The wedding of Henry IV and Maria de' Medici
textes.L'ouverture d'un théâtre public: The opening of a public theatre
textes.Un opéra de mariage royal, où Peri chant: A royal wedding opera, in which Peri himself sang the role of Orpheus.
textes.Euridice de Peri, créée au palais Pitti: Peri's Euridice, premiered at the Pitti Palace on 6 October 1600, is the oldest surviving opera; Dafne is lost.
textes.Jacopo Peri chantait lui-même le rôle d': Jacopo Peri himself sang the role of Orpheus at the premiere of Euridice.
textes.Vrai. Le compositeur était aussi chanteu: True. The composer was also a singer.
textes.Caccini a publié sa propre Euridice, sur: Caccini published his own Euridice, on the same libretto, before Peri's was performed.
textes.Vrai. Pressé de ne pas se laisser devanc: True. Anxious not to be outrun, he published his version in 1600, and had it staged two years later.
textes.Caccini publie en 1600 son Euridice sur: Caccini published his Euridice on the same libretto in 1600, before Peri's premiere, and had it staged two years later.
textes.Quel est le plus ancien opéra encore jou: What is the oldest opera still regularly performed?
textes.Créé à Mantoue le 24 février 1607. Oubli: Premiered in Mantua on 24 February 1607. Forgotten after Monteverdi's death, it returned to the repertoire in the 20th century.
textes.L'Orfeo de Monteverdi, créé à Mantoue le: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo, premiered in Mantua on 24 February 1607, is the oldest opera still regularly performed.
textes.En combien d'actes est L'Orfeo de Montev: In how many acts is Monteverdi's L'Orfeo?
textes.Cinq actes, chacun conclu par un chœur,: Five acts, each ending with a chorus, preceded by a trumpet toccata.
textes.L'Orfeo compte cinq actes, chacun termin: L'Orfeo has five acts, each ending with a chorus; the 1609 score names about 41 instruments.
textes.Le premier opéra public ouvre, avec un p: The first public opera house opened, with a paying audience
textes.Le théâtre San Cassiano, de la famille T: The San Cassiano theatre, owned by the Tron family, opened with Manelli's L'Andromeda. Opera left the princely courts.
textes.Le théâtre San Cassiano, ouvert à Venise: The San Cassiano theatre, opened in Venice in 1637, was the first public opera house, open to a paying audience.
textes.Le kunqu, né sous la dynastie Ming, est: Kunqu, born under the Ming dynasty, is one of the oldest surviving forms of Chinese opera.
textes.Vrai. Son œuvre la plus célèbre est Le P: True. Its most famous work is The Peony Pavilion, by Tang Xianzu; UNESCO recognised it in 2001.
textes.Le kunqu est l'une des plus anciennes fo: Kunqu is one of the oldest extant forms of Chinese opera; UNESCO proclaimed it a Masterpiece of intangible heritage in 2001.
textes.Qui a convaincu la Camerata que le théât: Who convinced the Camerata that Greek theatre was mostly sung?
textes.Mei, grand spécialiste de la Grèce antiq: Mei, a leading scholar of ancient Greece, shaped the whole group's thinking.
textes.Girolamo Mei soutenait que le drame grec: Girolamo Mei held that Greek drama was mostly sung; his ideas shaped the Camerata.
textes.Un métronome bat à 120 battements par mi: A metronome beats at 120 beats per minute. How many seconds separate two beats?
textes.La durée d'un battement vaut T = 60 ÷ M,: The length of a beat is T = 60 ÷ M, where M is the number of beats per minute, since a minute has 60 seconds. Here T = 60 ÷ 120 = 0.5 second. Maelzel's scale, in beats per minute, is what makes this calculation possible.
textes.Un métronome mécanique se règle en génér: A mechanical metronome is usually adjustable from 40 to 208 beats per minute.
textes.Que signifie le sigle M.M. sur une parti: What does the abbreviation M.M. mean on a score?
textes.M.M. pour Maelzel's Metronome. Maelzel a: M.M. for Maelzel's Metronome. Yet Maelzel took over Winkel's invention, a borrowing judged questionable.
textes.Winkel invente un pendule à ressort en 1: Winkel invented a spring pendulum in 1814; Maelzel patented it in 1815 under the name metronome.
textes.Qui a réellement inventé, en 1814, le pe: Who really invented, in 1814, the spring pendulum that Maelzel called a metronome?
textes.Winkel l'invente ; Maelzel ajoute une gr: Winkel invented it; Maelzel added a scale, patented it and sold it under his own name.
textes.Quand Beethoven note-t-il sa première in: When did Beethoven write his first metronome marking?
textes.Dans une partition corrigée de sa cantat: In a corrected score of his cantata Opus 112. He was the first notable composer to do so.
textes.Beethoven est le premier compositeur not: Beethoven was the first notable composer to write metronome marks, in December 1815, for the Cantata Op. 112.
textes.Le chronomètre d'Étienne Loulié, en 1696: Étienne Loulié's chronometer, in 1696, beat time with an audible tick.
textes.Faux. C'était un poids de plomb au bout: False. It was a lead weight on a string, in front of a ruler: silent, and with nothing to keep it moving.
textes.Le chronomètre de Loulié, en 1696, était: Loulié's chronometer, in 1696, was a silent pendulum, with no escapement to keep it moving.
textes.Pour combien de métronomes György Ligeti: For how many metronomes did György Ligeti write his 1962 Poème symphonique?
textes.Cent métronomes qu'on remonte, qu'on lan: A hundred metronomes wound up, started and left to stop one by one. The metronome becomes an instrument.
textes.Le Poème symphonique pour 100 métronomes: Ligeti's Poème symphonique for 100 metronomes dates from 1962; Ichiyanagi had written for electric metronomes in 1960.
textes.Qui invente le diapason en 1711 ?: Who invented the tuning fork in 1711?
