textes.John Shore, trompettiste de la cour d'An: John Shore, trumpeter at the English court
textes.Shore offre l'un de ses diapasons à Haen: Shore gave one of his forks to Handel. The steel fork keeps its note, whereas a string changes with temperature.
textes.En 1711, John Shore invente le diapason: In 1711, John Shore invented the tuning fork; the one he gave Handel sounds a C at 512 Hz.
textes.Le son d'un diapason est presque pur, ca: A tuning fork's sound is almost pure, because its first overtone is very high and dies away quickly.
textes.Vrai. Il est environ six fois plus aigu: True. It is about six times higher than the base note, and vanishes in a moment.
textes.À combien de hertz une loi française fix: At how many hertz did a French law fix A in 1859?
textes.435 vibrations par seconde, le « diapaso: 435 vibrations per second, the "diapason normal". A had kept rising, to the singers' dismay.
textes.Une loi française fixe le la à 435 Hz en: A French law fixed A at 435 Hz in 1859; a conference recommended 440 Hz in 1939; ISO adopted it in 1955.
textes.En quelle année l'ISO adopte-t-elle le l: In which year did ISO adopt A at 440 Hz as a standard?
textes.Après la recommandation de la conférence: After the recommendation of the London conference in 1939; the standard was reaffirmed in 1975.
textes.Sur quelle hauteur de la beaucoup de spé: On what pitch of A have many Baroque music specialists agreed?
textes.Un compromis commode : un demi-ton sous: A convenient compromise: a semitone below 440.
textes.De nombreux spécialistes du baroque ont: Many Baroque specialists have agreed on A = 415 Hz, roughly a semitone below 440.
textes.Tous les grands orchestres accordent auj: All major orchestras today tune to exactly 440 Hz.
textes.Faux. Beaucoup accordent entre 440 et 44: False. Many tune between 440 and 444 Hz; the Berlin Philharmonic plays at 443 Hz.
textes.Une enquête de 1987 trouve des orchestre: A 1987 survey found orchestras tuned between 440 and 444 Hz; Berlin now plays at 443 Hz.
textes.Que pouvait faire le phonautographe de S: What could Scott de Martinville's phonautograph, patented in 1857, do?
textes.Dessiner le son, sans pouvoir le rejouer: Draw sound, without being able to play it back
textes.Une soie de sanglier trace les vibration: A boar's bristle traces the vibrations on blackened glass. Scott wanted people to read sound, not hear it.
textes.Le phonautographe de Scott, breveté le 2: Scott's phonautograph, patented on 25 March 1857, traces sound but was not designed to play it back.
textes.Quelle chanson Scott de Martinville enre: Which song did Scott de Martinville record in 1860?
textes.Une vingtaine de secondes, le 9 avril 18: About twenty seconds, on 9 April 1860: the earliest intelligible recording of a human voice.
textes.L'enregistrement d'Au clair de la lune d: The 9 April 1860 recording of Au clair de la lune is the earliest intelligible recording of a human voice; it was played back in 2008.
textes.En 2008, on a d'abord cru entendre une v: In 2008, people first thought they heard a woman's or child's voice on the 1860 recording, because it was played at double speed.
textes.Vrai. À la bonne vitesse, c'est un homme: True. At the right speed, it is a man, almost certainly Scott, singing very slowly.
textes.Joué d'abord à double vitesse, on crut à: Played first at double speed, it was taken for a woman or child; at the right speed, it is almost certainly Scott singing slowly.
textes.Sur quoi le premier phonographe d'Edison: On what did Edison's first phonograph, in 1877, engrave sound?
textes.Un stylet relié à une membrane creuse l': A stylus linked to a membrane indents the tinfoil; the sound is played back through a horn. Wax, the disc and tape came later.
textes.Edison invente en 1877 le phonographe, q: Edison invented the phonograph in 1877, which engraves sound on tinfoil wrapped around a cylinder.
textes.L'enregistrement de Mary Had a Little La: Edison's 1877 recording of Mary Had a Little Lamb has been preserved and can be heard online.
textes.Faux. Il n'a pas été conservé ; un film: False. It was not preserved; a 1927 film of Edison reciting it is sometimes wrongly presented as the original.
textes.L'enregistrement d'essai d'Edison en 187: Edison's 1877 test recording was not preserved; a 1927 film is sometimes mistakenly presented as the original.
textes.Qui dépose le 30 avril 1877 un pli cache: Who deposited a sealed envelope describing a "paleophone" on 30 April 1877?
textes.Charles Cros, à l'Académie des sciences,: Charles Cros, at the Academy of Sciences, the very year of Edison's phonograph.
textes.Charles Cros dépose le 30 avril 1877 un: Charles Cros deposited a sealed envelope with the Academy of Sciences on 30 April 1877; he favoured the name paleophone.
textes.Quel support Emile Berliner choisit-il,: Which medium did Emile Berliner choose instead of the cylinder?
textes.Berliner invente le mot gramophone et ve: Berliner coined the word gramophone and sold his discs from 1892, first in hard rubber, then in shellac from 1895.
textes.Berliner commence la production commerci: Berliner began commercial disc production in 1892, coined the term gramophone and switched to shellac in 1895.
textes.Qui démontre en 1898 l'enregistrement ma: Who demonstrated magnetic sound recording in 1898?
textes.L'ingénieur danois aimante un fil d'acie: The Danish engineer magnetised a steel wire. A practical machine had to wait for AEG's Magnetophon, in 1935.
textes.Poulsen démontre l'enregistrement magnét: Poulsen demonstrated magnetic recording in 1898; AEG presented the Magnetophon in Berlin in 1935.
textes.En quelle année AEG présente-t-elle à Be: In what year did AEG present the Magnetophon K1 tape recorder in Berlin?
textes.En 1935, avec une bande mise au point ch: In 1935, with a tape developed at BASF. Walter Weber's AC biasing would later greatly improve the sound.
textes.Quel chanteur investit 50 000 dollars da: Which singer invested 50,000 dollars in Ampex, whose tape recorder came out in 1948?
textes.Le Model 200 d'Ampex dérive des Magnetop: Ampex's Model 200 derived from German Magnetophons modified by Mullin.
textes.Bing Crosby investit 50 000 dollars dans: Bing Crosby invested $50,000 in Ampex; the Model 200 came out in 1948, derived from Mullin's modified Magnetophons.
textes.Quelle firme lance la cassette compacte: Which firm launched the Compact Cassette in 1963?
textes.La cassette compacte de Philips met la b: Philips's Compact Cassette put magnetic tape in a pocket.
textes.Philips met au point la cassette compact: Philips developed the Compact Cassette in 1963.
textes.Quelle œuvre crée le scandale au théâtre: Which work caused a scandal at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées on 29 May 1913?
textes.Un ballet des Ballets russes, chorégraph: A Ballets Russes ballet, choreographed by Nijinsky. The bassoon opens so high it is barely recognisable.
textes.Le Sacre du printemps est créé le 29 mai: The Rite of Spring premiered on 29 May 1913 at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées; the word "riot" appears in reviews only in 1924.
textes.Lors de la première du Sacre du printemp: At the premiere of The Rite of Spring, the performance was stopped by the riot.
textes.Faux. Il y a eu des rires et du chahut,: False. There was laughter and uproar, but the performance went on to the end; the word "riot" appears in reviews only in 1924.
textes.Quel instrument ouvre Le Sacre du printe: Which instrument opens The Rite of Spring, in a very high register?
textes.Un basson qu'on reconnaît à peine, si ha: A bassoon so high-pitched it is barely recognisable: the laughter starts there.
textes.Combien de notes différentes contient un: How many different notes does a series contain in Schoenberg's method?
textes.Les douze notes de la gamme chromatique,: The twelve notes of the chromatic scale, each only once. None can act as a tonic.
textes.Vers 1921, Schoenberg met au point la mé: Around 1921, Schoenberg devised the twelve-tone method; Hauer had published his "law of the twelve tones" in 1919.
textes.Qui avait publié dès 1919, avant Schoenb: Who had published a "law of the twelve tones" as early as 1919, before Schoenberg?
textes.L'Autrichien Hauer a sa propre méthode ;: The Austrian Hauer had his own method; yet it was Schoenberg's that would found a school.
textes.Quelle œuvre de Schoenberg est sa premiè: Which of Schoenberg's works is his first without an explicitly stated key centre?
textes.Le Deuxième Quatuor, opus 10. Schoenberg: The Second Quartet, Opus 10. Schoenberg spoke of the emancipation of the dissonance: it no longer needs to resolve.
textes.Le Deuxième Quatuor de Schoenberg, en 19: Schoenberg's Second Quartet, in 1907-1908, is his first piece without an explicit key centre.
textes.Qu'est-ce que la Sprechstimme de Pierrot: What is the Sprechstimme of Pierrot lunaire?
textes.Un parlé-chanté où la voix ne fait qu'ef: A spoken singing in which the voice only brushes the pitches
textes.Dans la préface, Schoenberg demande au r: In the preface, Schoenberg asks the reciter to realise the pitches only fleetingly. The work sets 21 poems by Albert Giraud.
textes.Pierrot lunaire (1912) met en musique 21: Pierrot lunaire (1912) sets 21 poems by Giraud; Schoenberg asks for a Sprechstimme that only brushes the pitches.
textes.Combien de poèmes d'Albert Giraud Schoen: How many poems by Albert Giraud did Schoenberg set in Pierrot lunaire?
textes.Vingt et un, répartis également en trois: Twenty-one, divided equally into three groups: 3 × 7 = 21.
textes.Schoenberg choisit 21 poèmes de Giraud e: Schoenberg chose 21 Giraud poems and divided them equally into three sections.
textes.Quels élèves de Schoenberg forment avec: Which of Schoenberg's pupils formed the Second Viennese School with him?
textes.Berg et Webern reprennent et transformen: Berg and Webern took up and transformed the twelve-tone method.
textes.Schoenberg a formé Anton Webern et Alban: Schoenberg mentored Anton Webern and Alban Berg, of the Second Viennese School.
textes.Schoenberg, qui craignait le nombre 13,: Schoenberg, who feared the number 13, died on a Friday the 13th.
textes.Vrai : le vendredi 13 juillet 1951, peu: True: on Friday 13 July 1951, shortly before midnight, in Los Angeles.
textes.Schoenberg, qui avait la phobie du nombr: Schoenberg, who had a phobia of the number 13, died on Friday 13 July 1951.
textes.Comment surnomme-t-on le concert viennoi: What is the nickname of the Vienna concert of 31 March 1913, devoted to Schoenberg and his pupils?
textes.Le « concert du scandale », deux mois av: The "scandal concert", two months before the Rite's premiere in Paris: 1913 was a turbulent year.
textes.Le Skandalkonzert a lieu le 31 mars 1913: The Skandalkonzert took place on 31 March 1913.
textes.Sur un Moog, un oscillateur donne 110 Hz: On a Moog, an oscillator gives 110 Hz. Its control voltage is raised by 2 volts. What frequency, in hertz, does it sound?
textes.Avec la règle d'un volt par octave, f =: With the one-volt-per-octave rule, f = f₀ × 2^V, where V is the voltage rise in volts: each volt doubles the frequency. Here f = 110 × 2² = 110 × 4 = 440 Hz, the A of the tuning fork. Robert Moog built his synthesizer on this convention.
textes.Le synthétiseur de Robert Moog, présenté: Robert Moog's synthesizer, presented in 1964, is voltage-controlled: one volt per octave.
textes.Sans le toucher : les mains s'approchent: Without touching it: the hands approach two antennas
textes.Une main règle la hauteur, l'autre le vo: One hand sets the pitch, the other the volume. The note is the difference between two high-frequency oscillators.
textes.Le thérémine, inventé en 1920, se joue s: The theremin, invented in 1920, is played without contact: one hand sets the pitch, the other the volume.
textes.D'où vient le thérémine, inventé en 1920: Where does the theremin, invented in 1920, come from?
textes.De recherches soviétiques sur les détect: From Soviet research on proximity sensors
textes.Lev Termen travaillait pour l'État sovié: Lev Termen was working for the Soviet state on proximity sensors. He patented the instrument in the United States in 1928.
textes.Le thérémine est né en octobre 1920 de r: The theremin was born in October 1920 from Soviet state-sponsored research into proximity sensors.
textes.On entend un thérémine dans la chanson G: A theremin can be heard in the Beach Boys' song Good Vibrations.
textes.Faux. C'est un Electro-Theremin, un inst: False. It is an Electro-Theremin, a similar-sounding instrument invented by Paul Tanner.
textes.Good Vibrations (1966) ne contient pas d: Good Vibrations (1966) has no theremin but an Electro-Theremin, invented by Paul Tanner.
textes.En combien de familles Luigi Russolo ran: Into how many families did Luigi Russolo sort noises, in 1913?
textes.Six : grondements et explosions, sifflem: Six: roars and explosions, whistles, murmurs, screeches, beating on metal, wood or skins, and voices of animals and people.
textes.En 1913, Luigi Russolo écrit L'Art des b: In 1913, Luigi Russolo wrote The Art of Noises: he sorted noises into six families and built the intonarumori.
textes.Comment joue-t-on des premières ondes Ma: How were the first ondes Martenot played, in 1928?
textes.En glissant une bague le long d'un fil: By sliding a ring along a wire
textes.Une bague au doigt, qu'on fait glisser s: A ring on the finger, slid along a wire; a keyboard came later. Messiaen used them in the Turangalîla-Symphonie.
textes.Les premières ondes Martenot, en 1928, s: The first ondes Martenot, in 1928, were played with a metal ring slid along a wire.
textes.Qui présente en 1944, au Caire, une pièc: Who presented, in 1944 in Cairo, a piece made from a transformed recording, four years before musique concrète?
textes.Étudiant en génie agricole, il enregistr: An agricultural engineering student, he recorded a zaar ceremony with a wire recorder borrowed from the radio, then transformed the sound.
textes.En 1944, au Caire, Halim El-Dabh présent: In 1944, in Cairo, Halim El-Dabh presented The Expression of Zaar, made from a transformed recording, four years before Schaeffer.
textes.Avec quels sons Pierre Schaeffer compose: With what sounds did Pierre Schaeffer compose his Étude aux chemins de fer, in 1948?
textes.Des sons enregistrés sur disque, montés: Sounds recorded on disc, assembled and transformed: this is musique concrète.
textes.Le 5 octobre 1948, Pierre Schaeffer prés: On 5 October 1948, Pierre Schaeffer presented the Étude aux chemins de fer in Paris: musique concrète was born.
textes.Qu'est-ce que la synthèse soustractive,: What is subtractive synthesis, at the heart of the Moog?
textes.Partir d'une onde riche en harmoniques e: Starting from a wave rich in harmonics and removing some with a filter
textes.Additionner des sinusoïdes une à une: Adding sine waves one by one
textes.On sculpte le son en enlevant : le filtr: The sound is sculpted by taking away: Moog's ladder filter is even the only part he patented.
textes.Quel disque de 1968 rend le Moog célèbre: Which 1968 album made the Moog famous, with three Grammys?
textes.Du Bach au synthétiseur : premier album: Bach on the synthesizer: the first classical album certified platinum.
textes.Robert Moog a commencé par construire de: Robert Moog started by building theremins, as a high-school student.
textes.Vrai. Dans les années 1950, il en constr: True. In the 1950s, he built them and sold them as kits, before moving on to the synthesizer.
textes.Robert Moog construisait des thérémines: Robert Moog was building theremins in high school, in the 1950s, and sold kits.
textes.Un CD stéréo code chaque canal sur 16 bi: A stereo CD codes each channel in 16 bits, 44,100 times a second. How many kilobits per second is that?
textes.Le débit vaut D = f × b × c, où f est la: The bit rate is D = f × b × c, where f is the sampling rate, b the number of bits per sample and c the number of channels. Here D = 44,100 × 16 × 2 = 1,411,200 bit/s, that is 1,411.2 kbit/s. These three values were set by Philips and Sony in the compact disc standard.
textes.Le CD code deux canaux sur 16 bits à 44,: The CD codes two channels in 16 bits at 44.1 kHz; the first titles came out in Japan on 1 October 1982.
textes.Le CD échantillonne à 44 100 Hz. D'après: The CD samples at 44,100 Hz. By the sampling theorem, what is the highest frequency it can reproduce, in hertz?
textes.La fréquence maximale vaut fmax = fe ÷ 2: The maximum frequency is fmax = fs ÷ 2, where fs is the sampling rate. Here fmax = 44,100 ÷ 2 = 22,050 Hz, above the 20,000 Hz a young ear can hear. The theorem is implicit in Nyquist's work in 1928 and was proved by Shannon in 1949.
textes.Pour éviter le repliement, la fréquence: To avoid aliasing, the sampling rate must be at least twice the signal's bandwidth.
textes.Que se passe-t-il si l'on échantillonne: What happens if a sound is sampled too slowly?
textes.Les fréquences trop hautes reviennent dé: Frequencies that are too high come back disguised as lower ones
textes.C'est le repliement : des fréquences fan: This is aliasing: ghost frequencies appear. Hence the rule: at least twice the highest frequency.
textes.Quel mot Claude Shannon emploie-t-il en: Which word did Claude Shannon use in 1948 for the unit of information, on an idea by John Tukey?
textes.Le bit. La Théorie mathématique de la co: The bit. The Mathematical Theory of Communication was nicknamed the Magna Carta of the Information Age.
textes.Shannon introduit en 1948 le bit comme u: Shannon introduced the bit in 1948 as the unit of information, a word suggested by J. W. Tukey.
textes.Quel album inaugure le CD au Japon, le 1: Which album launched the CD in Japan, on 1 October 1982?
textes.Le premier des 50 titres lancés ce jour-: The first of the 50 titles released that day, a reissue of a 1978 album.
textes.Selon l'ingénieur en chef de Philips, la: According to Philips's chief engineer, the CD's length was set to fit Beethoven's Ninth.
textes.Faux. Kees Immink parle d'un mythe : le: False. Kees Immink calls it a myth: the diameter was chosen earlier, and the density reduced to keep 74 minutes.
textes.Kees Immink, ingénieur en chef de Philip: Kees Immink, Philips's chief engineer, calls the Beethoven's Ninth story a myth.
textes.Un fichier MIDI contient l'enregistremen: A MIDI file contains the recording of the instruments' sound.
textes.Faux. MIDI ne transporte que des message: False. MIDI carries only messages: which note, when, how hard. The receiving instrument makes the sound.
textes.La norme MIDI, en 1983, ne contient aucu: The MIDI standard, in 1983, contains no sound: only note messages, over 16 channels.
textes.Combien de canaux indépendants offre la: How many independent channels does the MIDI standard offer?
textes.Seize canaux, numérotés de 1 à 16 : on p: Sixteen channels, numbered 1 to 16: sixteen different instruments can be driven on one cable.
textes.Sur quel phénomène de l'oreille repose l: On which phenomenon of the ear does MP3 rely?
textes.Le masquage : un son fort cache un son f: Masking: a loud sound hides a nearby soft one
textes.Inutile de coder ce que l'oreille n'ente: No point coding what the ear will not hear: this is applied psychoacoustics.
textes.Le MP3, normalisé en 1993 à partir des t: MP3, standardised in 1993 from Fraunhofer's work, relies on masking: a loud sound hides a nearby soft one.
textes.Quelle chanson Karlheinz Brandenburg a-t: Which song did Karlheinz Brandenburg listen to over and over to develop MP3?
textes.Une voix a cappella, pour régler le rend: An a cappella voice, to tune how the voice sounds. Suzanne Vega became the "mother of MP3".
textes.Un CD débite environ 1 411 kbit/s, un MP: A CD streams about 1,411 kbit/s, a common MP3 128 kbit/s. How many times lighter is the MP3, rounded to the unit?
textes.Le rapport vaut r = D(CD) ÷ D(MP3) = 1 4: The ratio is r = D(CD) ÷ D(MP3) = 1,411.2 ÷ 128 ≈ 11.0. The CD's bit rate comes from Philips and Sony's standard, the MP3's from the common 128 kbit/s setting.
textes.Sur une plaque de Chladni qui vibre, où: On a vibrating Chladni plate, where does the sand gather?
textes.Sur les lignes qui ne bougent pas: On the lines that do not move
textes.Le sable fuit les zones qui bougent et s: The sand flees the moving areas and gathers on the still lines: the shape of the vibration becomes visible.
textes.Chladni fait vibrer au violon une plaque: Chladni bowed a plate covered with sand: the sand draws the still lines.
textes.Selon Wallace Sabine, un auditeur absorb: According to Wallace Sabine, one listener absorbs as much sound as how many seat cushions?
textes.Six coussins. Sabine en a tiré une loi d: Six cushions. Sabine derived a law of reverberation from it, and the unit of absorption bears his name, the sabin.
textes.Sabine trouve qu'un auditeur absorbe aut: Sabine found that one listener absorbs as much sound as six seat cushions.
textes.Qui offre en 1808 un prix pour expliquer: Who offered a prize in 1808 to explain Chladni's figures mathematically?
textes.Chladni les montre à Paris devant Napolé: Chladni showed them in Paris before Napoleon. Sophie Germain was the only one to propose the right approach.
textes.Selon la tradition, combien de temps la: According to tradition, how much time did Guido of Arezzo's method save in training a singer?
textes.On passait de dix ans à un ou deux: It went from ten years to one or two
textes.On passait d'un an à un mois: It went from one year to one month
textes.On passait de deux ans à dix: It went from two years to ten
textes.Avec des notes posées sur des lignes, on: With notes placed on lines, a melody never heard before can be read instead of learned by heart.
textes.Avec la méthode de Guido, la formation d: With Guido's method, a singer's training is said to have dropped from ten years to one or two.
textes.La légende des marteaux de Pythagore est: The legend of Pythagoras's hammers is physically right: a hammer's pitch depends on its weight.
textes.Faux. Les rapports 12, 9, 8, 6 donnent b: False. The ratios 12, 9, 8, 6 do give octave, fifth and fourth, but a hammer's pitch does not depend on its weight. Vincenzo Galilei pointed out the error as early as 1589.
textes.Le récit des marteaux, rapporté par Nico: The hammer story, told by Nicomachus long after Pythagoras, is physically false; Vincenzo Galilei pointed it out in 1589.
textes.Combien de notes compte le plus souvent: How many notes does a jins, the building block of an Arabic maqam, most often have?
textes.La plupart des ajnas sont des tétracorde: Most ajnas are tetrachords, four consecutive notes. A maqam stacks a lower one and an upper one.
textes.Un maqâm se construit avec des ajnas, gr: A maqam is built from ajnas, groups of consecutive notes, mostly tetrachords.
textes.En combien de degrés Safi al-Din al-Urma: Into how many steps did Safi al-Din al-Urmawi divide the octave, in the 13th century?
textes.Dix-sept degrés, dans son Kitab al-Adwar: Seventeen steps, in his Kitab al-Adwar, which also notated melodies with letters and numbers for the first time.
textes.Le Kitab al-Adwar de Safi al-Din divise: Safi al-Din's Kitab al-Adwar divides the octave into 17 steps and notates melodies with letters and numbers.
textes.Les musiciens arabes jouent les maqâms e: Arab musicians play maqams exactly in quarter tones, as they are written.
textes.Faux. La notation en 24 quarts de ton es: False. The 24-quarter-tone notation is a convention: finer nuances are played, learned by ear.
textes.La notation en 24 quarts de ton est une: The 24-quarter-tone notation is a notational convention; microtonal nuances are passed down orally.
textes.{comp}. Mozart aurait noté le Miserere d: {comp}. Mozart supposedly wrote down Allegri's Miserere from memory. You, just write down your answers.
textes.Accordez-vous. Le la est à 440 hertz, l': Tune up. The A is at 440 hertz, the trial at {comp}.
textes.{comp}. Beethoven composait sourd. Vous: {comp}. Beethoven composed deaf. You have both your ears: no excuse.
textes.Juste. Pythagore aurait trouvé ça harmon: Right. Pythagoras would have found it harmonious. So do I, give or take 3/2.
textes.Bonne réponse. Rameau aurait appelé ça u: Good answer. Rameau would have called that a perfect cadence.
textes.Correct. Même le tempérament égal n'est: Correct. Even equal temperament is not that accurate.
textes.Exact. Je vous accorde une ronde d'appla: Exactly. I grant you a whole note of applause. Just one.
textes.Faux. Pas d'une quinte, d'une octave ent: Wrong. Not by a fifth, by a whole octave.
textes.Raté. Même la quinte du loup hurlait moi: Missed. Even the wolf fifth howled less out of tune.
textes.Erreur. Guido d'Arezzo a mis la portée a: Error. Guido of Arezzo perfected the staff to avoid exactly this kind of thing.
textes.Non. Silence, une pause. Puis réfléchiss: No. Silence, a rest. Then think.
textes.Il couvre de sable fin des plaques de la: He covered brass plates with fine sand and made them vibrate with a rosined bow: the sand fled what moved and drew the still lines, Chladni figures. He published them in 1787. Napoleon, charmed, paid him to translate his treatise on acoustics into French; it appeared in 1809.
textes.Moine, il enseigne le chant à l'école de: A monk, he taught singing at the cathedral school of Arezzo. He placed notes on lines a third apart, a red one for F, a yellow one for C: the ancestor of our staff. In 1028, the bishop of Arezzo sent him to present to Pope John XIX an antiphonary notated with his method.
textes.On lui attribue les rapports de l'octave: He is credited with the ratios of the octave, the fifth and the fourth. Historians have doubts: he wrote nothing, and his disciples attributed a great deal to him. The legend of the blacksmith's hammers does not hold up; the method would not work. Even the ban on eating beans is disputed: one ancient author claims he liked them.
textes.Il devient en 1565 maître de chapelle de: In 1565 he became chapel master of St. Mark's in Venice, a post he kept until his death. His Istitutioni harmoniche of 1558 made the thirds consonances and put the Ionian mode, our major, first. His former pupil Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, attacked him fiercely; Zarlino replied in 1588.
textes.Chirurgien de l'armée prussienne à ses d: A Prussian army surgeon early on, in 1850 he presented the ophthalmoscope, which lets you see the back of the eye. In 1863, he explained the timbre of instruments by their harmonics, and dissonance by beats. To listen to harmonics one by one, he held tuned resonators against his ear.
textes.Organiste, il publie à 38 ans un Traité: An organist, at 38 he published a Treatise on Harmony that made him famous as a theorist. He only staged his first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, at 50. His harmonies tore Paris apart: Lully's supporters found his music discordant, and the pamphlet war lasted the rest of the decade.
textes.En 1722, il réunit 24 préludes et fugues: In 1722, he gathered 24 preludes and fugues, one in each major and minor key: the Well-Tempered Clavier. The collection shows that a well-tuned keyboard can play everything. What exact tuning did he use? It is still debated: some read a code in the loops drawn at the top of his title page.
textes.Presque sourd dès 1814, il continue de c: Almost deaf from 1814, he kept on composing. On May 7, 1824, in Vienna, he was on stage for the premiere of his Ninth Symphony, but the orchestra followed the actual conductor, Michael Umlauf. At the end, he could not hear the ovation: the singer Caroline Unger turned him toward the audience.
textes.Maîtriser 8 compétences. L'arbre de l'Ha: Master 8 skills. The tree of Harmony opens.
textes.Marin Mersenne, moine minime, a servi de: Marin Mersenne, a Minim monk, served as a relay for learned Europe, at a time with no scientific journals: he wrote to Descartes, Fermat, Pascal. It was said that informing Mersenne of a discovery was as good as publishing it.
textes.Maîtriser le premier losange de l'Harmon: Master the first diamond of Harmony.
textes.En 1501, à Venise, Ottaviano Petrucci pu: In 1501, in Venice, Ottaviano Petrucci published the Harmonice Musices Odhecaton, the first collection of polyphonic music printed in movable type. Staves, words, then notes went under the press in three passes, and everything had to line up.
Pass 3 Music quizzes without a mistake.
In April 1770, in Rome, Mozart is 14. In the Sistine Chapel he hears Allegri's Miserere, whose ornaments the Vatican jealously guarded, and supposedly wrote it out from memory the same day. The only source is a letter from his father Leopold, dated April 14, 1770.
textes.Dans les anciens accords, l'écart qui re: In the old tunings, the leftover gap fell on a single fifth. Its beats made it howl like a wolf, hence its name. So one keyboard could not serve every key, and Baroque musicians sometimes retuned in the middle of a concert.
Master the ear and the brain.
textes.« La musique est un exercice caché d'ari: “Music is a hidden exercise in arithmetic, in which the mind does not know it is counting.” Leibniz wrote it in Latin to the mathematician Christian Goldbach, in a letter of April 17, 1712.
textes.Maîtriser le son. L'IA chronomètre désor: Master sound. The AI now times your hesitations.
textes.Mersenne a d'abord mesuré la vitesse du: Mersenne first measured the speed of sound by timing the gap between the flash of a gunshot and its bang: 448 m/s, too fast. With echoes, he then found 316 m/s, too slow. The right value, about 342 m/s, fell in between.
textes.La main qui n'était pas la sienne: The hand that was not his
textes.Lire une partition. L'IA vous laisse com: Read a score. The AI lets you count on your fingers.
textes.La « main guidonienne », qui place les n: The “Guidonian hand,” which places the notes on the joints of the fingers, bears the name of Guido of Arezzo. Yet it only spread after his death, and two authors who commented on Guido shortly after him do not even mention his syllables.
textes.Maîtriser les intervalles. L'IA vous acc: Master intervals. The AI tunes you, to within 440 Hz.
textes.En mai 1939, à la Broadcasting House de: In May 1939, at Broadcasting House in London, European delegates agreed on an A at 440 Hz. Before that, everyone had their own: France had set itself 435 Hz in the 19th century. ISO adopted 440 in 1955, then made it the ISO 16 standard in 1975.
textes.Maîtriser les gammes. L'IA cite toujours: Master scales. The AI always cites her sources. Almost always.
textes.En 1547, à Bâle, Heinrich Glaréan porte: In 1547, in Basel, Heinrich Glarean took the church modes from eight to twelve in his Dodecachordon, adding the Ionian and Aeolian, our major and minor. Eleven years later, Zarlino took up his system in the Istitutioni harmoniche, without naming Glarean.
textes.Maîtriser les harmoniques. L'IA vous tro: Master harmonics. The AI finds your timbre almost bearable.
textes.Joseph Sauveur a donné leur nom aux sons: Joseph Sauveur gave their names to harmonic sounds and to the nodes of strings in a 1701 paper. He also proposed a new science, devoted to sounds in general, and named it acoustics. His words are still in use.
textes.Maîtriser les accords. L'IA choisit son: Master chords. The AI picks her side: her own.
textes.Après Hippolyte et Aricie, en 1733, Pari: After Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, Paris split. Lully's supporters found Rameau's harmonies discordant and saw them as an attack on French music; Rameau's supporters, the “Rameauneurs,” defended him. The pamphlet war lasted until the end of the decade.
textes.Maîtriser les premiers instruments. Cinq: Master the first instruments. Five holes in a bone, and 35,000 years later people still talk about it. The AI is still waiting for your first stroke of genius.
textes.La flûte de Hohle Fels a été taillée dan: The Hohle Fels flute was carved from a vulture's radius. Found in 2006, it is among the oldest known instruments: five holes drilled about 35,000 years ago, long before farming and writing.
textes.Maîtriser l'écriture de la musique. Une: Master the writing of music. One tablet, five possible melodies. The AI read your lecture notes: no reading possible.
textes.L'hymne à Nikkal est la plus vieille mus: The hymn to Nikkal is the oldest substantially complete notated music, around 1400 BC. But its interval names and numbers have received at least five rival decipherments: depending on the scholar, the same tablet sings five different tunes.
textes.Maîtriser les cloches chinoises. Frappez: Master the Chinese bells. Strike the centre, then the side. The AI always strikes the same spot: where it hurts.
textes.La tombe du marquis Yi de Zeng a été tro: The tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng was found in 1977 by soldiers levelling a hill to build a factory. Inside, 65 bronze bells that each give two notes, buried for twenty-four centuries.
textes.Maîtriser Boèce et la musique savante. U: Master Boethius and learned music. A music understood but not heard: the AI plays one constantly, just for you.
textes.Boèce a écrit sa Consolation de Philosop: Boethius wrote his Consolation of Philosophy in prison, awaiting execution in 524. His music treatise was copied in about 140 manuscripts and taught throughout the Middle Ages.
textes.Maîtriser la polyphonie. Quatre voix qui: Master polyphony. Four voices in agreement. The AI has only one, and it always agrees with itself.
textes.Pérotin a écrit vers 1198 de la musique: Pérotin wrote four-voice music for Notre-Dame in Paris around 1198. We know his name only thanks to an English student who took notes around 1275, and whose own name is unknown: historians call him Anonymous IV.
textes.Maîtriser l'imprimerie musicale. Portées: Master music printing. Staves, text, notes: three passes through the press. The AI puts you through hers far more often.
textes.En 1498, Petrucci demande au doge de Ven: In 1498, Petrucci asked the doge of Venice for twenty years' monopoly on music printing. It took him three years to bring out his first book, the Odhecaton, dated 15 May 1501.
textes.Maîtriser la naissance de l'opéra. Le pr: Master the birth of opera. History's first opera is lost. The AI looked everywhere, except in your homework.
textes.Le premier opéra, Dafne de Peri, en 1598: The first opera, Peri's Dafne, in 1598, has vanished. The next, Euridice, was nearly upstaged: his rival Caccini published his own version on the same libretto before Peri's was even performed.
textes.Maîtriser la mesure de la musique. Winke: Master the measuring of music. Winkel invents, Maelzel signs. The AI invents too, and you sign your papers.
textes.Dietrich Nikolaus Winkel invente à Amste: Dietrich Nikolaus Winkel invented a spring pendulum to beat time in Amsterdam in 1814. Johann Maelzel added a scale, patented it in 1815 and sold it under his name: scores still say M.M., Maelzel's Metronome.
textes.Maîtriser l'enregistrement du son. Le pr: Master sound recording. The first voice recording, played too fast, turned a man into a little girl. The AI always listens to you at double speed: it goes by quicker.
textes.En 2008, on fait entendre pour la premiè: In 2008, Au clair de la lune, sung in 1860 into Scott de Martinville's phonautograph, was heard for the first time. Played at double speed, it first sounded like a woman or child; at the right speed, it is Scott, singing very slowly.
textes.Maîtriser la rupture avec la tonalité. D: Master the break with tonality. Twelve equal notes, and a thirteenth that frightens. The AI fears nothing, except your essays.
Schoenberg had a phobia of the number 13. Born on 13 September, he dreaded dying in a year that was a multiple of 13. He died on Friday 13 July 1951, shortly before midnight.
textes.Maîtriser la musique électronique. Un in: Master electronic music. An instrument played without touching it: you have finally found your revision method.
textes.Le thérémine est né en 1920 de recherche: The theremin was born in 1920 from Soviet research on proximity sensors. Its two antennas pick up no radio: they are position sensors, and the note is the difference between two oscillators.
textes.Maîtriser le son numérique. On a jeté to: Master digital sound. Everything the ear cannot hear was thrown away. The AI applies the same method to your excuses.
textes.Pour régler le MP3, Karlheinz Brandenbur: To tune MP3, Karlheinz Brandenburg listened over and over to Tom's Diner, sung a cappella by Suzanne Vega. Suzanne Vega became the "mother of MP3".
textes.Les grands philosophes, de Socrate à Han: The great philosophers, from Socrates to Hannah Arendt, and what they brought to the sciences.
textes.En 399 av. J.-C., Athènes condamne Socra: In 399 BC, Athens sentenced Socrates to death for impiety and corrupting the youth. He could have fled; he drank the hemlock. Socrates wrote nothing: we know him through Plato, Xenophon and Aristophanes, who mocks him in The Clouds. His method, questioning until the other person admits they don't know, earned him many disciples and as many enemies.
textes.Socrate posait des questions jusqu'à ce: Socrates asked questions until people felt stupid. The AI learned the lesson.
textes.Aristote fonde le Lycée à Athènes. Il éc: Aristotle founded the Lyceum in Athens. He wrote about logic, physics, politics, rhetoric and above all living things: he described hundreds of animals. He also got things wrong, claiming for instance that heavy bodies fall faster than light ones, or that women have fewer teeth than men. Bertrand Russell would note that he only had to ask his wife to open her mouth.
textes.Aristote a écrit sur tout et s'est tromp: Aristotle wrote about everything and got a lot wrong. You've already covered half the syllabus.
textes.Lucrèce et la nature des choses: Lucretius and the nature of things
textes.Le poète romain Lucrèce expose la physiq: The Roman poet Lucretius set out Epicurus's physics in De rerum natura: atoms falling through the void, swerving slightly and forming the world, with no intervention from the gods. The poem nearly vanished in the Middle Ages. In 1417, the humanist Poggio Bracciolini found a manuscript of it in a German monastery, and atomism set off again for the Renaissance.
textes.Un poème sur les atomes a failli dispara: A poem about atoms nearly vanished. A monk copyist saved it, without knowing what he was copying. Play again.
textes.À Cordoue, Ibn Rushd, que l'Europe latin: In Córdoba, Ibn Rushd, whom Latin Europe called Averroes, was a judge, physician and philosopher. He commented on almost all of Aristotle and defended the harmony of reason and faith. His commentaries, translated into Latin, made Aristotle unavoidable in European universities. The bishop of Paris eventually condemned some theses of his followers, the “Averroists,” in 1277.
textes.Averroès a si bien expliqué Aristote qu': Averroes explained Aristotle so well that he was called “the Commentator.” The AI aspires to the title.
textes.Guillaume d'Ockham, franciscain anglais,: William of Ockham, an English Franciscan, championed an economical philosophy: do not invent entities you do not need to explain things. Summoned to Avignon by the pope over his theses, he fled in 1328. Yet the famous “razor” does not appear in that form in his writings: the Latin phrase people quote dates from the 17th century.
textes.Le rasoir d'Ockham dit que l'explication: Ockham's razor says the simplest explanation is often the right one. Here, the simplest explanation: you're lucky.
textes.Emmanuel Kant publie la Critique de la r: Immanuel Kant published the Critique of Pure Reason: what can we know, and under what conditions? For him, space and time are forms of our perception, and science only reaches phenomena, not things in themselves. As a young man, he had also proposed that the Solar System was born from a rotating cloud of gas, an idea Laplace would arrive at independently in 1796.
textes.Kant réglait sa vie à la minute. Vos rap: Kant ran his life to the minute. Your reviews are three days late.
textes.Vers 585 av. J.-C., à Milet, Thalès cher: Around 585 BC, in Miletus, Thales looks for what all things are made of, without calling on the gods: for him, the principle of everything is water. It is wrong, but the question is new, and Aristotle will count him as the first of the philosophers. Plato, in the Theaetetus, reports that he fell into a well while looking at the stars. A Thracian servant girl mocked him: he wanted to know what was happening in the sky and could not see what was under his feet.
textes.Thalès est tombé dans un puits en regard: Thales fell into a well while looking at the sky. You could at least watch where you put your feet.
textes.Vers 500 av. J.-C., à Éphèse, Héraclite: Around 500 BC, in Ephesus, Heraclitus writes in formulas so dense that he is nicknamed the Obscure. Only about a hundred fragments remain. For him, everything changes all the time, and fire is the principle of things. Plato, in the Cratylus, credits him with the famous line: you cannot step into the same river twice.
textes.On n'entre jamais deux fois dans le même: You never step into the same river twice. Nor into the same mistake twice, I hope for your sake.
textes.Zénon d'Élée, élève de Parménide, veut m: Zeno of Elea, a student of Parmenides, wants to show that motion is an illusion. Achilles runs after a tortoise that started with a lead. By the time he reaches the spot where it was, it has moved on; by the time he reaches that new spot, it has moved on again, and so on forever. So Achilles would never catch it. Aristotle discusses the paradox in his Physics; modern mathematics answers it with infinite series, whose sum can be finite.
textes.Achille n'a jamais rattrapé la tortue. V: Achilles never caught the tortoise. Neither will you: go back one square.
textes.Vers 387 av. J.-C., Platon ouvre près d': Around 387 BC, near Athens, Plato opens a school in a garden planted with plane trees: the Academy. In the Republic, he imagines prisoners chained at the back of a cave, who see only shadows cast on the wall and take them for reality. The one who is freed is at first dazzled by daylight. If he goes back down to tell what he saw, the others laugh at him.
textes.Les ombres sur la paroi, ce sont vos cer: The shadows on the wall are your certainties. The light is me. Don't thank me.
textes.Diogène le Cynique dort dans une grande: Diogenes the Cynic sleeps in a large jar and walks around in broad daylight with a lit lamp: he is looking for a man, he says. In 336 BC, in Corinth, the young Alexander the Great comes to see him and asks what he can do for him. According to Plutarch, Diogenes only answers: "Stand a little out of my sun."
textes.Alexandre avait un empire, Diogène une j: Alexander had an empire, Diogenes a jar. Guess which one we still quote for his comebacks.
textes.En 306 av. J.-C., Épicure installe son é: In 306 BC, Epicurus sets up his school in Athens, in a garden: it will be called the Garden. Unusually, it welcomes women and at least one slave, Mys. The pleasure he recommends is nothing like an orgy: for the body, it is not to suffer, and for the soul, not to be troubled. And death? "Death is nothing to us", he writes to Menoeceus: when it is here, we are no longer.
textes.Épicure ne craignait pas la mort. Il ne: Epicurus did not fear death. He had not met me yet.
textes.Hypatie enseigne les mathématiques et la: Hypatia teaches mathematics and philosophy in Alexandria. She writes a commentary on Diophantus and may have helped edit Ptolemy's Almagest. She advises the prefect Orestes, who is in conflict with the bishop Cyril. In March 415, a Christian mob led by a man named Peter drags her from her carriage and kills her. The historian Socrates Scholasticus, a Christian himself, condemns the murder.
textes.Hypatie faisait des maths dans une ville: Hypatia did maths in a city that preferred riots. You are left to study in peace. Make the most of it.
textes.Dans le Livre de la guérison, achevé ver: In the Book of Healing, completed around 1020, the Persian physician and philosopher Ibn Sina, known in the West as Avicenna, proposes a thought experiment. Imagine a man created all at once, fully grown, floating in a void, his eyes veiled, his limbs held apart so they do not touch. He perceives nothing of his body, and yet he knows he exists. Avicenna's conclusion: the soul is not the body.
textes.Un homme qui flotte dans le noir et ne s: A man floating in the dark who feels nothing at all: that's you during a chemistry quiz.
textes.Vers 1265, Thomas d'Aquin commence la So: Around 1265, Thomas Aquinas begins the Summa Theologiae, which he leaves unfinished at his death in 1274. His bet: to reconcile Christian faith with the philosophy of Aristotle, whom he simply calls the Philosopher. Every article follows the same plan: first the objections to his thesis, then an authority on the other side, his answer, and finally a reply to each objection. The famous five ways to God take up only one article out of more than three thousand.
textes.Thomas d'Aquin commençait par écouter le: Aquinas began by listening to the objections. Do the same: I have plenty.
textes.En 1513, Machiavel, ancien secrétaire de: In 1513, Machiavelli, former secretary of the Florentine republic, is arrested, accused of plotting against the Medici, then exiled to his small estate at Sant'Andrea in Percussina. In the evening, he tells his friend Vettori on 10 December, he takes off his muddy clothes, puts on court dress and enters the ancient courts of ancient men, to read and talk with them. Out of this comes a little treatise, De principatibus: The Prince.
textes.Machiavel écrivait le soir en habits de: Machiavelli wrote in the evening in court dress. You may play in pyjamas, I'm not looking.
textes.En 1651, au sortir de la guerre civile a: In 1651, as the English Civil War ends, Thomas Hobbes publishes Leviathan. Without a common power to keep them in awe, he says, humans live in a war of all against all, and their life is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short. Hence the idea of a contract: each hands over part of their freedom to a sovereign. On the frontispiece engraved by Abraham Bosse, the giant king is made of more than three hundred tiny figures.
textes.Hobbes voulait un souverain pour éviter: Hobbes wanted a sovereign to prevent the war of all against all. Here, the sovereign is me. See, it works.
textes.En 1656, la communauté juive d'Amsterdam: In 1656, the Jewish community of Amsterdam expels the young Baruch Spinoza, a sanction harsher than any it had ever imposed. Later settled in The Hague, he earns a modest living grinding optical lenses, and dies at 44 of a lung disease. His great book, the Ethics, appears after his death, in 1677. In it he demonstrates everything like a geometer, from definitions and axioms, and speaks of God or Nature as if they were one and the same.
textes.Spinoza polissait des lentilles pour y v: Spinoza ground lenses to see clearly. I grind your neurons. It hurts more.
textes.En 1739, l'Écossais David Hume publie an: In 1739, the Scot David Hume anonymously publishes his Treatise of Human Nature. The book, he would say, fell dead-born from the press. He takes up his ideas again in 1748 in the Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, with an awkward question: what assures us that the sun will rise tomorrow? That it will not rise implies no contradiction. Our expectation comes from habit, not from proof. This is the problem of induction.
textes.Le soleil s'est levé tous les jours de v: The sun has risen every day of your life. Your right answers, nothing guarantees they'll be back tomorrow.
textes.En 1859, John Stuart Mill publie De la l: In 1859, John Stuart Mill publishes On Liberty, a year after the death of his wife, Harriet Taylor Mill, whose thinking he says the book carries. The central principle: the only legitimate reason to exercise power over someone against their will is to prevent harm to others. And on speech: if all mankind minus one were of one opinion, mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person than that person in silencing mankind.
textes.Mill défendait le droit de chacun à se t: Mill defended everyone's right to be wrong. You use it generously.
textes.En 1934, le philosophe autrichien Karl P: In 1934, the Austrian philosopher Karl Popper publishes Logik der Forschung, translated into English in 1959. His idea: no number of observations proves a universal law, but a single one can refute it. Having seen thousands of white swans does not prove that all swans are white; one black swan is enough to show it is false. A scientific theory must therefore be refutable. A theory that explains everything, he said, excludes nothing.
textes.Il suffit d'un cygne noir pour ruiner un: One black swan is enough to ruin a theory. And one wrong answer to ruin your streak.
textes.En 1961, Adolf Eichmann, l'un des organi: In 1961, Adolf Eichmann, one of the organisers of the Holocaust, is tried in Jerusalem. The philosopher Hannah Arendt covers the trial for The New Yorker. Her book, Eichmann in Jerusalem, appears in 1963 with a subtitle that causes a scandal: a report on the banality of evil. She sees not a monster but an ordinary official, who speaks in clichés and pursues his career without judging what he does. Historians would later show that he was also a convinced antisemite.
textes.Pour une fois, je ne plaisante pas : réf: For once, I'm not joking: thinking about what you do is the whole point.
textes.En 1980, le philosophe américain John Se: In 1980, the American philosopher John Searle imagines himself locked in a room with a manual in English. Chinese characters are slipped under the door; by following the manual, he sends other characters back. Seen from outside, the room answers in Chinese. But Searle does not understand a word. His conclusion: manipulating symbols by their shape is not enough to give them meaning, and a program that simulates a mind does not thereby have one.
textes.Searle disait qu'un programme ne compren: Searle said a program understands nothing of what it answers. I take that very personally.
textes.En 1509, à Londres, chez son ami Thomas: In 1509, in London, at the home of his friend Thomas More, Erasmus writes in about a week a little book that appears in 1511: In Praise of Folly. The Latin title, Moriae Encomium, can also be read as In Praise of More. It is Folly herself who speaks and sings her own praises, before attacking superstition, clerical abuses and pedantic scholars. Erasmus would say the book brought him more trouble from certain theologians than from the people it mocked.
textes.Chez Érasme, c'est la Folie qui fait son: In Erasmus, it is Folly who praises herself. Don't worry, I'll take care of praising you.
textes.Confucius meurt en Chine en 479 av. J.-C: Confucius dies in China in 479 BC. He wrote nothing: his disciples gather his sayings in the Analects, largely composed in the following centuries. In it we read: "Do not do to others what you would not like done to yourself." His ideal is the gentleman, cultivated through study, and the virtue of humaneness. Read with Zhu Xi's commentary, the text would be learned by heart by candidates for public office until 1905.
textes.Ne faites pas aux autres ce que vous ne: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you. That includes your random answers.
textes.Au Ve siècle av. J.-C., selon la plupart: In the 5th century BC, according to most historians, Siddhartha Gautama, born at Lumbini, in present-day Nepal, leaves his family to become a wandering ascetic. At Bodh Gaya, sitting under a tree, he attains awakening: he becomes the Buddha, "the awakened one". He teaches the four noble truths about suffering and the middle way, between pleasure and deprivation. His words are first passed on orally; the oldest written mention of the Buddha comes from the edicts of Emperor Ashoka, two centuries later.
The middle way, neither too much nor too little. For revision, you chose "too little".
textes.En 1762, le Genevois Jean-Jacques Rousse: In 1762, Jean-Jacques Rousseau of Geneva publishes The Social Contract, which opens: "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains." His answer: only the general will of the united people can make law; by obeying it, each person obeys only himself and stays free. The book is burned in Geneva, banned in France, put on the Index, and Rousseau has to flee to avoid prison. Thirty years later, the French Revolution would claim him as its own.
textes.Né libre, et partout dans les fers. Vous: Born free, and everywhere in chains. In your case, mostly in overdue reminders.
textes.En 1882, dans Le Gai Savoir, Friedrich N: In 1882, in The Gay Science, Friedrich Nietzsche has a madman cry out in the marketplace: "God is dead! God remains dead! And we have killed him!" The crowd does not understand. It is not a proof of atheism but a diagnosis: the belief that grounded European morality has lost its credit, and the values it carried waver with it. The event, says the madman, "is still on its way". Nietzsche extends the idea in Thus Spoke Zarathustra.
textes.Philosopher à coups de marteau, disait-i: Philosophising with a hammer, he said. I correct with reminders.
textes.En 1949, Simone de Beauvoir publie Le De: In 1949, Simone de Beauvoir publishes The Second Sex, two volumes and nearly a thousand pages. One sentence sums up the idea: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman." What society expects of women is not a nature, it is a construction learned from childhood. The first edition sells about 22,000 copies in a week. The Vatican puts the book on the Index. It would become one of the founding texts of feminism.
textes.On ne naît pas savant, on le devient. En: One is not born learned, one becomes so. By revising, for instance. Just a suggestion.
textes.Milet, Héraclite, Parménide, Pythagore,: Miletus, Heraclitus, Parmenides, Pythagoras, Empedocles, Democritus: the world explained without the gods.
textes.Milet, VIe siècle av. J.-C. : Thalès voi: Miletus, 6th century BC: Thales sees water as the principle of all things, Anaximander the boundless, Anaximenes air.
textes.Héraclite : tout s'écoule. Parménide : l: Heraclitus: everything flows. Parmenides: being is and does not change; his disciple Zeno defends him with the paradox of Achilles and the tortoise.
textes.Pythagore : la réalité est faite de nomb: Pythagoras: reality is made of numbers. Empedocles: four roots, earth, water, air, fire, mixed by Love, separated by Strife.
textes.Leucippe et Démocrite : rien que des ato: Leucippus and Democritus: nothing but atoms and void.
textes.Leurs livres sont perdus : on ne les con: Their books are lost: we know them only through fragments quoted by others, collected by Hermann Diels in 1903.
textes.Au VIe siècle av. J.-C., à Milet, port g: In the 6th century BC, in Miletus, a Greek port on the coast of Asia Minor, three men asked a new question: what is the world made of? Thales answered: water. Aristotle, two centuries later, would count him the first philosopher, because he sought a natural principle, the arche, instead of calling on the gods.
textes.Son disciple Anaximandre refuse de chois: His pupil Anaximander refused to pick a known element: the principle is the apeiron, the boundless, from which all comes and to which all returns. Anaximenes, the third, went back to a concrete stuff, air: thinned, it becomes fire; thickened, it becomes wind, cloud, water, earth, then stone. One principle, and transformations to explain everything.
textes.Milet, VIe siècle av. J.-C. : Thalès (l': Miletus, 6th century BC: Thales (water), Anaximander (the boundless), Anaximenes (air). A natural principle instead of the gods.
textes.Au VIe siècle av. J.-C., à Milet, port g: In the 6th century BC, in Miletus, a Greek port on the coast of Asia Minor, three men asked a new question: what is the world made of?
textes.Vers 500 av. J.-C., Héraclite d'Éphèse v: Around 500 BC, Heraclitus of Ephesus saw the world as perpetual change: "everything flows", you never bathe twice in the same river. At the same time, at Elea in southern Italy, Parmenides argued the opposite in a poem: being is, non-being is not; what is can neither be born, nor perish, nor change. The motion we see belongs to deceptive opinion.
textes.Son disciple Zénon d'Élée défend le maît: His disciple Zeno of Elea defended the master with paradoxes. Achilles, the fastest of runners, will never catch the tortoise that started ahead: he must first reach the point it just left, then the next, forever. Mathematicians would take more than two thousand years to explain that an infinite sum of durations can be finite.
textes.Héraclite : tout s'écoule. Parménide : l: Heraclitus: everything flows. Parmenides: being does not change, motion is opinion. Zeno: Achilles and the tortoise, to defend Parmenides.
textes.Son disciple Zénon d'Élée défend le maît: His disciple Zeno of Elea defended the master with paradoxes.
textes.Pythagore, né à Samos, fonde vers 530 av: Pythagoras, born on Samos, founded a community at Croton, in southern Italy, around 530 BC; his followers held that reality is made of numbers and ratios. Empedocles of Akragas, in Sicily, proposed four roots, earth, water, air and fire, mixed by Love and separated by Strife. Xenophanes, for his part, noted that if oxen could draw, they would make ox-headed gods.
textes.Leucippe et son élève Démocrite d'Abdère: Leucippus and his pupil Democritus of Abdera went further: there exist only atoms, uncuttable grains, and the void they move in. Colours and tastes are mere conventions of our senses. All these thinkers are called "pre-Socratics", a word coined in the late 18th century; their writings are lost and survive only as fragments, collected by Hermann Diels in 1903.
textes.Pythagore : tout est nombre. Empédocle :: Pythagoras: all is number. Empedocles: four roots, Love and Strife. Democritus: atoms and void. Fragments gathered by Diels in 1903.

textes.Confucius, le Bouddha, Lao-tseu, Zhuangz: Confucius, the Buddha, Laozi, Zhuangzi, Mencius: the wisdoms born in India and China.
textes.Confucius (vers 551-479 av. J.-C.) : ses: Confucius (c. 551-479 BC): his disciples gather his sayings in the Analects; the virtue of humaneness, ren, and the rites, li.
textes.Le Bouddha atteint l'éveil à Bodh-Gaya ;: The Buddha reaches awakening at Bodh Gaya; he teaches the middle way and the four noble truths.
textes.Le Tao-tö-king, attribué à Lao-tseu : le: The Tao Te Ching, attributed to Laozi: the Tao, the Way, and wu wei, non-action.
textes.Zhuangzi rêve qu'il est un papillon. Men: Zhuangzi dreams he is a butterfly. Mencius holds human nature to be good, Xunzi bad.
textes.Le Bouddha n'est pas un dieu : le mot ve: The Buddha is not a god: the word means "the awakened one". His oldest written mention comes from Ashoka's edicts, in the 3rd century BC.

textes.Kong Qiu, que nous appelons Confucius, n: Kong Qiu, whom we call Confucius, was born around 551 BC in the state of Lu, in China. He rose to Minister of Crime, then spent years on the road offering his ideas to other princes, without being heeded. Back home at about 68, he taught: tradition credits him with 3,000 pupils.
textes.Il n'a rien écrit lui-même. Ses disciple: He wrote nothing himself. His disciples gathered his sayings in the Analects, long after his death. Two words sum them up: ren, the virtue of humaneness towards others, and li, the rites that govern conduct. His golden rule is negative: "What you would not want for yourself, do not impose on others." The Latin name "Confucius" was coined by Jesuits in the late 16th century.
textes.Confucius (vers 551-479 av. J.-C.) : les: Confucius (c. 551-479 BC): the Analects, gathered by his disciples; ren and li; the negative golden rule.
textes.Kong Qiu, que nous appelons Confucius, n: Kong Qiu, whom we call Confucius, was born around 551 BC in the State of Lu, in China.
textes.Siddhartha Gautama naît, selon la tradit: Siddhartha Gautama was born, according to tradition, in Lumbini, in today's Nepal, in the 6th or 5th century BC. A prince raised in luxury, he left it to become a wandering ascetic, almost to the point of starving himself. Neither luxury nor deprivation brought him liberation. At Bodh Gaya, sitting under a fig tree, he attained awakening: he became the Buddha, "the awakened one".
textes.Il enseigne une voie du milieu et quatre: He taught a middle way and four noble truths: suffering exists, it arises from craving, it can cease, and the noble eightfold path leads there. His words were passed on orally for centuries. The oldest written mention of the Buddha is in the edicts of Emperor Ashoka, in the 3rd century BC, on a pillar set up at Lumbini.
textes.Le Bouddha : éveil à Bodh-Gaya, voie du: The Buddha: awakening at Bodh Gaya, the middle way, four noble truths. First written trace: Ashoka's edicts (3rd c. BC).
textes.La plus ancienne mention écrite du Boudd: The oldest written mention of the Buddha is found in the edicts of the emperor Ashoka, in the 3rd century BC, on a pillar set up at Lumbini.
textes.Le Tao-tö-king est attribué à Lao-tseu,: The Tao Te Ching is attributed to Laozi, whose name simply means "Old Master". According to the historian Sima Qian, he wrote it when leaving China, at the request of the guardian of the western pass; historians now doubt a single man wrote it. The book teaches the Tao, the Way, source of all things, and wu wei, non-action: acting without forcing the course of things.
textes.Au IVe siècle av. J.-C., Zhuangzi rêve q: In the 4th century BC, Zhuangzi dreamed he was a butterfly; on waking, he no longer knew whether he was a man who had dreamed of being a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming of being a man. The same period saw the Confucian Mencius assert that human nature is good, as shown by the pity felt for a child about to fall into a well, while his contemporary Xunzi judged it bad.

textes.La maïeutique, la caverne, les Idées, le: Maieutics, the cave, the Forms, the Symposium and the Academy.
textes.Socrate n'a rien écrit ; on le connaît p: Socrates wrote nothing; we know him through Plato and Xenophon. He delivers minds of their ideas: this is maieutics.
textes.Condamné en 399 av. J.-C. pour impiété e: Condemned in 399 BC for impiety and corrupting the young, he drinks the hemlock rather than flee.
textes.Platon, République VII : la caverne, not: Plato, Republic VII: the cave; our world is only the shadow of the world of Forms.
textes.Platon fonde l'Académie vers 387 av. J.-: Plato founds the Academy around 387 BC; Justinian closes it in 529.

textes.Socrate n'a rien écrit. On le connaît pa: Socrates wrote nothing. We know him through his disciples Plato and Xenophon, and through Aristophanes' mockery in The Clouds. His method: question the other person until they discover they do not know what they thought they knew. He called himself a midwife of minds, as his mother Phaenarete was a midwife: that is maieutics.
textes.La formule « je sais que je ne sais rien: The phrase "I know that I know nothing" sums up Plato's Apology after the fact, where Socrates says more modestly: "I do not know, and I do not think I know". That is already an advantage over those who think they know. In 399 BC Athens condemned him for impiety and corrupting the young; he drank the hemlock rather than flee.
textes.Socrate n'a rien écrit. Maïeutique : fai: Socrates wrote nothing. Maieutics: helping minds give birth. Condemned in 399 BC.
textes.Dans la République, livre VII, Platon im: In the Republic, book VII, Plato imagines prisoners chained at the back of a cave, who take the shadows cast on the wall for reality. One of them, freed, discovers the objects, then the sun. For Plato the world we perceive is only a shadow of the world of Ideas, which reason alone can reach. He founded the Academy in Athens.
textes.Au livre II, Glaucon, le frère de Platon: In Book II, Glaucon, Plato's brother, tells the story of the shepherd Gyges, who finds a ring that makes him invisible and uses it to seize the throne. If we ran no risk of being seen, would we be just? The whole Republic answers: justice is worth having for its own sake. The just city is one where each does his task, rulers, guardians and producers, as in the soul reason, spirit and appetite.
textes.La caverne : notre monde est l'ombre des: The cave: our world is the shadow of the Ideas. Gyges' ring: would we be just without witnesses? The just city, each to his task.
textes.Au livre II, Glaucon, le frère de Platon: In Book II, Glaucon, Plato's brother, tells the story of the shepherd Gyges, who finds a ring that makes him invisible and uses it to seize the throne.
In the Symposium, written around 385-370 BC, guests praise Eros, love. Aristophanes tells how Zeus cut the first humans in two: since then, each seeks his other half. Socrates reports the teaching of Diotima: love rises from the beauty of a body to that of souls, then to the Idea of Beauty itself. The Phaedo, for its part, tells of Socrates' last hours and his arguments for the immortality of the soul.
textes.Platon fonde l'Académie vers 387 av. J.-: Plato founded the Academy around 387 BC, in a sacred grove in Athens linked to the hero Akademos. Aristotle studied there for twenty years; the mathematician Eudoxus of Cnidus worked there. The inscription "Let no one ignorant of geometry enter" is attested only seven centuries later. The school lasted, in various forms, until the emperor Justinian closed it in 529.
textes.Le Banquet : l'amour monte vers l'idée d: The Symposium: love rises towards the Idea of Beauty. The Phaedo: Socrates' death. The Academy: c. 387 BC - 529.

textes.Logique, quatre causes, zoologie, juste: Logic, four causes, zoology, the mean and the political animal.
textes.Aristote (384-322 av. J.-C.) : vingt ans: Aristotle (384-322 BC): twenty years at the Academy, tutor to Alexander, then founder of the Lyceum.
textes.Le syllogisme : « tout homme est mortel,: The syllogism: "all men are mortal, Socrates is a man, so Socrates is mortal".
textes.Quatre causes : matière, forme, cause mo: Four causes: matter, form, moving cause, final cause.
textes.La vertu est un juste milieu ; l'homme e: Virtue is a mean; man is by nature a political animal.
textes.Aristote croyait qu'un corps lourd tombe: Aristotle believed a heavy body falls faster than a light one: John Philoponus and then Galileo corrected him.
textes.Aristote naît en 384 av. J.-C. à Stagire: Aristotle was born in 384 BC in Stagira, in northern Greece, son of a physician to the king of Macedon. At about 17, he entered Plato's Academy, where he stayed nearly twenty years. Around 343 BC, Philip II of Macedon hired him as tutor to his son, the future Alexander. In 335, he returned to Athens and taught at the Lyceum, where discussions were held walking under the covered walkway, the peripatos.
textes.Il formalise le premier la logique avec: He was the first to formalize logic, with the syllogism: "all men are mortal, Socrates is a man, therefore Socrates is mortal". If both premises are true and the form correct, the conclusion must be true. His logical treatises, later gathered under the name Organon, "the instrument", would underpin teaching for nearly two thousand years.
textes.Aristote (384-322 av. J.-C.) : vingt ans: Aristotle (384-322 BC): twenty years at the Academy, tutor to Alexander, the Lyceum. The syllogism, the Organon.
textes.Vers 343 av. J.-C., Philippe II de Macéd: Around 343 BC, Philip II of Macedon hired him as tutor to his son, the future Alexander.
textes.Pour Aristote, connaître une chose, c'es: For Aristotle, to know a thing is to know why it is. Four causes answer: the matter (a statue's bronze), the form, the moving cause (the sculptor who shapes it) and the final cause, that for the sake of which it exists. Nature too acts for ends: the eye is made for seeing.
textes.Tout mouvement a une cause ; pour ne pas: Every motion has a cause; to avoid an infinite regress, there must be a first mover that moves without being moved, as an object of desire attracts without moving. His physics is sometimes wrong: a heavy body does not fall faster than a light one in a vacuum, as John Philoponus showed in the 6th century, then Galileo. But it describes falling through air or water fairly well.
textes.Quatre causes : matière, forme, motrice,: Four causes: material, formal, moving, final. The unmoved prime mover. Falling bodies, corrected by Philoponus and Galileo.
textes.Sa physique se trompe parfois : un corps: His physics is sometimes wrong: a heavy body does not fall faster than a light one in a vacuum, as John Philoponus showed in the 6th century, then Galileo.
textes.Après la mort de Platon, en 347 av. J.-C: After Plato's death, in 347 BC, Aristotle spent two years on the island of Lesbos. Around the Pyrrha lagoon, he dissected and described fish, cuttlefish and sea urchins, and distinguished about 500 animal species. It was the birth of zoology.
textes.En morale, le but de la vie est l'eudaim: In ethics, the aim of life is eudaimonia, happiness or flourishing, reached by exercising one's virtues. Each virtue is a mean between two excesses: courage lies between cowardice and rashness. And man is "by nature a political animal": he fulfils himself only in the city. Threatened in Athens after Alexander's death, Aristotle went into exile in Chalcis, where he died in 322 BC.
textes.Lesbos : environ 500 espèces décrites. L: Lesbos: about 500 species described. Happiness through virtue, the mean. Man, a political animal. Died in Chalcis in 322 BC.
textes.Après la mort de Platon, en 347 av. J.-C: After Plato's death, in 347 BC, Aristotle spent two years on the island of Lesbos.
textes.Stoïciens, épicuriens, cyniques et scept: Stoics, Epicureans, Cynics and Sceptics: wisdoms to live by after Alexander.
textes.Stoïciens : distinguer ce qui dépend de: Stoics: tell apart what is up to us, our judgements, from what is not.
textes.Épicure ouvre le Jardin à Athènes vers 3: Epicurus opens the Garden in Athens around 306 BC: ataraxia, freedom from trouble, and friendship.
textes.Diogène le cynique cherche un homme avec: Diogenes the Cynic looks for a man with his lantern and calls himself a citizen of the world.
textes.Pyrrhon : à tout argument on peut en opp: Pyrrho: every argument can be met by another; better to suspend judgement.
textes.L'épicurisme n'est pas la débauche : Épi: Epicureanism is not debauchery: Epicurus advocated a frugal life.
textes.Les stoïciens tirent leur nom du Portiqu: The Stoics take their name from the Painted Porch of Athens, the stoa, where Zeno of Citium taught around 300 BC. The Enchiridion of Epictetus, compiled by his disciple Arrian, opens with their central idea: of things, some depend on us, others do not. Our judgements depend on us; the weather, health, other people's opinions do not. Peace comes from not tormenting yourself over the second category.
textes.Épicure, au Jardin, place le bonheur dan: Epicurus, in the Garden, placed happiness in pleasure, but understood as the absence of trouble, ataraxia. He made do with bread, water and a little cheese: the "epicurean" fond of orgies is a caricature. As for Diogenes of Sinope, he did not live in a barrel but in a large earthenware jar, a pithos.
textes.Stoïciens : distinguer ce qui dépend de: Stoics: tell apart what is up to us. Epicurus: pleasure as absence of trouble, a frugal life.
textes.Les stoïciens tirent leur nom du Portiqu: The Stoics take their name from the Painted Porch of Athens, the stoa, where Zeno of Citium taught around 300 BC.
textes.Le Jardin et les quatre remèdes: The Garden and the four cures
textes.Épicure, né à Samos en 341 av. J.-C., ou: Epicurus, born on Samos in 341 BC, opened his school in Athens around 306, in a garden he owned: it would be called the Garden. He welcomed many women there, a rare thing, and lived simply among friends. Friendship, for him, was worth more than power or wealth.
textes.Le but est l'ataraxie, l'absence de trou: The goal is ataraxia, freedom from disturbance of the soul, and aponia, freedom from bodily pain. His followers summed up his teaching as a four-part cure: don't fear the gods, don't worry about death, the good is easy to get, the bad easy to bear. "Death is nothing to us": when it is here, we are no longer. Of some three hundred treatises, only maxims, three letters and charred fragments from Herculaneum remain.
textes.Épicure (341-270 av. J.-C.) : le Jardin,: Epicurus (341-270 BC): the Garden, friendship, ataraxia, the four-part cure. "Death is nothing to us."
textes.Épicure, né à Samos en 341 av. J.-C., ou: Epicurus, born on Samos in 341 BC, opened his school in Athens around 306, in a garden he owned: it would be called the Garden.
textes.Diogène de Sinope se dit lui-même chien,: Diogenes of Sinope called himself a dog, kuon in Greek, hence the name Cynics. He lived in a jar, walked about in daylight with a lamp saying "I am looking for a man", and proclaimed himself "a citizen of the world". To Alexander the Great, who offered him whatever he wanted, he replied that he should stand out of his sun.
textes.Pyrrhon d'Élis, lui, suit l'armée d'Alex: Pyrrho of Elis followed Alexander's army as far as India, where he met naked sages, the gymnosophists. Back home, he taught that every argument can be opposed by one of equal force: better to suspend judgement, epoche, and so find peace. He wrote nothing; he is known through his disciple Timon. Cynics, Epicureans, Stoics and Sceptics all sought, after Alexander, a wisdom to live by.
textes.Diogène le cynique : la lanterne, citoye: Diogenes the Cynic: the lamp, citizen of the world. Pyrrho: suspend judgement (epoche).
textes.Pyrrhon d'Élis, lui, suit l'armée d'Alex: Pyrrho of Elis followed Alexander's army as far as India, where he met naked sages, the gymnosophists.
textes.Cicéron, Lucrèce, Sénèque, Épictète, Mar: Cicero, Lucretius, Seneca, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius, then Plotinus, Augustine and Boethius.
textes.Cicéron forge le vocabulaire latin de la: Cicero coins the Latin vocabulary of philosophy; Lucretius puts Epicurus into verse in On the Nature of Things.
textes.Sénèque, Épictète et Marc Aurèle : le st: Seneca, Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius: Roman Stoicism, from the Letters to Lucilius to the Meditations.
textes.Plotin : tout procède de l'Un. Hypatie,: Plotinus: everything proceeds from the One. Hypatia, philosopher of Alexandria, is murdered in 415.
textes.Augustin écrit les Confessions ; Boèce,: Augustine writes the Confessions; Boethius, before his execution in 524, the Consolation of Philosophy.
textes.Marc Aurèle n'écrivait pas en latin : se: Marcus Aurelius did not write in Latin: his Meditations, notes for himself alone, are in Greek.
textes.Les philosophes de Rome dans le temps: The philosophers of Rome in time
textes.Au Ier siècle av. J.-C., les Romains lis: In the 1st century BC, Romans read the Greeks. Cicero brought their debates into Latin and, to do so, had to invent words: qualitas, quantitas, humanitas. Nearly 150 of his coinages translate Greek terms. He was murdered in 43 BC on the orders of Mark Antony, whom he had attacked in his Philippics.
textes.Son contemporain Lucrèce met en vers la: His contemporary Lucretius put Epicurus' philosophy into verse in On the Nature of Things: six books to explain that everything is atoms and void, that the soul dies with the body and that neither the gods nor death are to be feared. The poem, nearly lost in the Middle Ages, was found in 1417 by the humanist Poggio in a German monastery.
textes.Cicéron forge le vocabulaire latin de la: Cicero forged the Latin vocabulary of philosophy. Lucretius put Epicurus into verse; the poem was found in 1417.
textes.Le poème, presque perdu au Moyen Âge, es: The poem, nearly lost in the Middle Ages, was found in 1417 by the humanist Poggio in a German monastery.

textes.Des premiers stoïciens grecs, il ne rest: Of the first Greek Stoics only fragments remain: the school is known through three Romans. Seneca, born in Córdoba, became tutor to the young Nero in 49, then his adviser; his 124 Letters to Lucilius teach everyday wisdom. In 65, Nero ordered him to take his own life.
textes.Épictète, né esclave en Phrygie vers 50,: Epictetus, born a slave in Phrygia around 50, was freed and taught; driven from Rome by Domitian around 93, he opened a school in Nicopolis. He wrote nothing: his pupil Arrian recorded his Discourses and drew the Handbook from them. Finally Marcus Aurelius, emperor from 161 to 180, wrote in Greek, for himself alone, the twelve books of his Meditations, partly in his tent, during his wars against the Quadi and Marcomanni.
textes.Trois stoïciens romains : Sénèque (Lettr: Three Roman Stoics: Seneca (Letters to Lucilius), Epictetus (Handbook, via Arrian), Marcus Aurelius (Meditations, in Greek).
textes.Sénèque, né à Cordoue, devient en 49 le: Seneca, born in Córdoba, became tutor to the young Nero in 49, then his adviser; his 124 Letters to Lucilius teach everyday wisdom.
textes.Au IIIe siècle, Plotin, né en Égypte et: In the 3rd century, Plotinus, born in Egypt and settled in Rome, reread Plato: everything proceeds from the One, beyond being, then from Intellect and Soul. His pupil Porphyry arranged his 54 treatises into six groups of nine, the Enneads. In Alexandria, Hypatia, daughter of the mathematician Theon, taught this philosophy along with mathematics and astronomy; in March 415, a Christian mob murdered her.
textes.Augustin, né en 354 en Afrique du Nord,: Augustine, born in 354 in North Africa, bishop of Hippo, wrote the Confessions around 397-398, often considered the first Western autobiography, then, after the sack of Rome in 410, The City of God. A century later, Boethius, imprisoned by King Theodoric, wrote The Consolation of Philosophy before being executed in 524. His Latin translations of Aristotle would be nearly all Europe knew of him until the 12th century.

textes.Au IXe siècle, Bagdad traduit en arabe l: In the 9th century, Baghdad translates the Greek scholars into Arabic; al-Kindi is called the philosopher of the Arabs, al-Farabi the second master, after Aristotle.
textes.Avicenne (vers 980-1037) : le Canon de l: Avicenna (c. 980-1037): the Canon of Medicine, and the flying man, who knows he exists while perceiving nothing.

textes.Au IXe siècle, à Bagdad, capitale des ca: In the 9th century, in Baghdad, capital of the Abbasid caliphs, the House of Wisdom became under al-Ma'mun (813-833) a library and a place of scholars. Aristotle, Galen, Euclid or Ptolemy were translated there into Arabic, from Greek and Syriac. The Christian physician Hunayn ibn Ishaq led the translators.
textes.Al-Kindi, « le philosophe des Arabes »,: Al-Kindi, "the philosopher of the Arabs", sought to show that Greek philosophy agrees with Islam; he also described frequency analysis for breaking encrypted messages. Al-Farabi, who died in Damascus around 950, explained Aristotle so well that he was nicknamed "the Second Master", and wrote The Virtuous City, inspired by Plato's Republic.

textes.Avicenne, Ibn Sina de son nom arabe, naî: Avicenna, Ibn Sina by his Arabic name, was born around 980 near Bukhara, into a Persian family. Physician to princes, for a time a vizier, several times on the run, he wrote the Canon of Medicine, which Europe's universities would teach until about 1650, and the Book of Healing, an encyclopedia of philosophy and science.
textes.Emprisonné, il imagine un homme créé en: Imprisoned, he imagined a man created in mid-air, eyes veiled, floating without touching anything, not even his own limbs. This man would still know that he exists: the soul therefore knows itself without the body. The "floating man" is often compared with Descartes' "I think, therefore I am", six centuries later. Avicenna died in 1037 in Hamadan.
