textes.Au XIIe siècle, à Cordoue, Ibn Rushd, qu: In the 12th century, in Córdoba, Ibn Rushd, whom the Latins called Averroes, commented on Aristotle's work so carefully that he was nicknamed simply "the Commentator". He defended the agreement of reason and faith. His commentaries passed Aristotle on to Latin Europe.
textes.Vers 1180, il répond à al-Ghazali, qui a: Around 1180, he answered al-Ghazali, who had attacked Avicenna and al-Farabi in The Incoherence of the Philosophers, with The Incoherence of the Incoherence. Also born in Córdoba, the Jewish philosopher Maimonides wrote around 1190, in Judeo-Arabic, the Guide for the Perplexed to reconcile the Bible and Aristotle. Later, in North Africa, Ibn Khaldun would describe history as a cycle of rise and decline of dynasties.

textes.Anselme : Dieu est « ce dont on ne peut: Anselm: God is "that than which nothing greater can be conceived", the ontological argument.

textes.Thomas d'Aquin, la Somme théologique : A: Thomas Aquinas, the Summa Theologica: Aristotle as an ally of theology, five ways to God.

textes.Au Moyen Âge, les savants savaient la Te: In the Middle Ages, scholars knew the Earth was round: the medieval flat Earth is a 19th-century myth.
textes.La scolastique est la philosophie des éc: Scholasticism is the philosophy of the medieval schools, then of the universities. Its method: read the authorities, set out arguments for and against, decide by reason. In 1077-1078, the monk Anselm, future archbishop of Canterbury, wrote the Proslogion, first titled "Faith seeking understanding". God there is "that than which nothing greater can be conceived": if he existed only in the mind, a greater one could be conceived; so he exists. The monk Gaunilo answered with the parody of a perfect island.
textes.Au siècle suivant, Pierre Abélard, profe: In the next century, Peter Abelard, a star lecturer in Paris, lined up in Sic et Non quotations from authorities that contradict each other: reason must decide. His affair with his pupil Héloïse ended badly: the young woman's uncle had him castrated. On the dispute over universals, he sought a path between realists and nominalists.

textes.Thomas d'Aquin, dominicain italien né ve: Thomas Aquinas, an Italian Dominican born around 1225, was so silent that his fellows called him the "dumb ox". He taught twice at the University of Paris and made Aristotle an ally of theology in his Summa Theologica, written from 1266 to 1273 and left unfinished. In it he offers five ways to God, the first taking up Aristotle's prime mover. He is also credited with the principle of double effect: an action aiming at a good may be allowed even if it brings about a foreseen but unintended harm.
textes.Aristote inquiète pourtant l'Église. En: Aristotle nonetheless worried the Church. In 1277, the bishop of Paris, Étienne Tempier, condemned 219 theses, often drawn from Aristotle and Averroes, such as the eternity of the world. The historian Pierre Duhem would see in it the birth of modern science, freed from Aristotle; today's historians qualify this. Thomas, who died in 1274, was declared a saint in 1323.

textes.Le rasoir d'Ockham conseille, entre deux: Ockham's razor advises preferring, between two explanations, the more economical: do not multiply entities beyond necessity. The exact phrase does not appear as such in William of Ockham, a 14th-century English Franciscan, but the idea is his. It has become a scientific reflex: the simplest hypothesis first.
textes.Ockham est aussi un champion de la quere: Ockham was also a champion in the dispute over universals. Does "the horse" exist somewhere, in addition to particular horses? Realists say yes; nominalists, Ockham among them, answer that it is only a convenient name. And no, medieval scholars did not think the Earth was flat: Bede or Sacrobosco knew it was round. That myth dates mainly from the 19th century.
textes.Rasoir d'Ockham : l'explication la plus: Ockham's razor: the most economical explanation first. Universals: realists versus nominalists. A round Earth in the Middle Ages.

textes.Machiavel écrit Le Prince en 1513 ; il n: Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513; it only came out in 1532, five years after his death. He describes power as it is exercised, not as it should be: a prince must sometimes know how to do wrong. The phrase "the end justifies the means" does not appear as such. At the same time Erasmus published In Praise of Folly (1511) and Thomas More coined the word Utopia (1516), from the Greek for "nowhere".
textes.Montaigne publie en 1580, à Bordeaux, la: Montaigne published the first edition of the Essays in 1580, in Bordeaux, and kept adding to them until his death in 1592. His motto, "What do I know?", was engraved in 1576 on a medal with a pair of scales: weigh, doubt, take oneself as the subject of study. His friend La Boétie had written the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude: "Resolve to serve no more, and you are free."

textes.Au XVe siècle, Florence redécouvre Plato: In the 15th century, Florence rediscovered Plato. In 1462, Cosimo de' Medici entrusted Greek manuscripts to the young Marsilio Ficino, who produced the first complete Latin translation of the dialogues, printed in 1484, and led the Platonic Academy of Florence. It was Ficino who coined, in 1476, the phrase "Platonic love".
textes.En 1486, Pic de la Mirandole, 23 ans, pr: In 1486, Pico della Mirandola, aged 23, offered to defend in Rome 900 theses blending Plato, Aristotle, Hermeticism and Kabbalah. His Oration on the Dignity of Man, the "manifesto of the Renaissance", makes man a being with no fixed place, free to rise or fall. Pope Innocent VIII had the theses condemned: the first printed book banned by the Church. Pico died at 31, probably poisoned with arsenic.

textes.Érasme, chanoine né vers 1466 à Rotterda: Erasmus, a canon born around 1466 in Rotterdam or Gouda, is the most famous of the humanists. He wrote In Praise of Folly at his friend Thomas More's home in London, and in 1516 published the New Testament in Greek, with a new Latin translation: one must go back to the sources rather than the commentaries.
textes.En France, Étienne de La Boétie écrit ve: In France, Étienne de La Boétie wrote around 1548, aged 18, the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude: tyrants hold power only through the consent of those they oppress. In 1558, he met Montaigne; he died five years later, aged 32. Montaigne, in the essay "Of Friendship", gives up explaining the bond: "Because it was he, because it was I."

textes.Descartes décide de rejeter tout ce dont: Descartes decides to reject everything that can be doubted: the senses that deceive, dreams that resemble waking life, and even mathematics, in case an evil demon is deceiving him. One thing alone resists: while he doubts, he thinks, so he exists. "I think, therefore I am" appears in French in the Discourse on Method in 1637; the Latin "cogito, ergo sum" comes from the Principles, in 1644.
textes.La même année 1637, dans La Géométrie, i: That same year, 1637, in La Géométrie, he linked algebra and geometry through coordinates: the "Cartesian" frame is named after him. His contemporary Pascal proposed a wager: believing in God costs little if you are wrong and gains infinitely if you are right, an expected-value argument published in the Pensées in 1670.

textes.En face, les empiristes anglais. Pour Jo: Facing them, the British empiricists. For John Locke, in the Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1690), the mind at birth is a blank page: all our ideas come from experience. No innate ideas.
textes.David Hume pousse plus loin. On ne voit: David Hume went further. We never see the cause itself, only one thing that usually follows another. The sun has always risen, but nothing logically guarantees it will rise tomorrow: that is the problem of induction. We generalise out of habit, not proof. Kant would say that Hume woke him from his "dogmatic slumber".

textes.En 1620, Francis Bacon publie le Novum O: In 1620, Francis Bacon published the Novum Organum, a "new instrument" answering Aristotle's Organon: start from observations to rise to laws, and beware the "idols" that distort judgement. In April 1651, during the English Civil War, Thomas Hobbes published Leviathan: without a State, life would be "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short". So each gives up his right to govern himself to a sovereign, on condition that the others do the same.
textes.À Amsterdam, le jeune Baruch Spinoza est: In Amsterdam, the young Baruch Spinoza was expelled from his Jewish community in 1656; he lived by grinding lenses. For him, "God, or Nature": God is one with the universe. His Ethics, demonstrated like a geometry treatise, appeared after his death, in 1677. Leibniz, finally, argued in the Theodicy (1710) that we live in the best of all possible worlds, which Voltaire would mock.

textes.En 1784, dans « Qu'est-ce que les Lumièr: In 1784, in "What is Enlightenment?", Kant gave the age its motto: "Sapere aude!", dare to use your own understanding. Enlightenment means leaving the tutelage in which one keeps oneself. The philosopher of Königsberg was thought so regular that, according to legend, his neighbours set their watches by his walk.
textes.En France, Diderot et d'Alembert dirigen: In France Diderot and d'Alembert edited the Encyclopédie: 17 volumes of text from 1751 to 1765, plus 11 of plates. Rousseau, in The Social Contract (1762), wanted law to express the general will. And the line "I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it" is not Voltaire's: it is Evelyn Beatrice Hall's, summing up his thought in 1906.

textes.En 1748, Montesquieu publie sans nom d'a: In 1748, Montesquieu published anonymously, in Geneva, The Spirit of the Laws. To avoid despotism, the power to make laws, the power to execute them and the power to judge must be given to different bodies, each limiting the others. The Church put the book on the Index in 1751; the founders of the United States drew on it.
textes.Le tremblement de terre de Lisbonne, en: The Lisbon earthquake of 1755 shook optimism. In January 1759 Voltaire published Candide, in which Dr Pangloss repeats, under an avalanche of misfortunes, that all is for the best in the best of worlds: Leibniz is the target. The novel ends with advice: "We must cultivate our garden."

textes.Émilie du Châtelet, mathématicienne et p: Émilie du Châtelet, a mathematician and physicist, translated and annotated Newton's Principia; she finished her work shortly before her death, in 1749, and her version, published in full in 1759, remains the only complete French translation. She worked with Voltaire at the château of Cirey. Diderot, for his part, spent a few months in the keep of Vincennes in 1749 for his Letter on the Blind, before running the Encyclopédie.
textes.En 1781, à Königsberg, Emmanuel Kant pub: In 1781, in Königsberg, Immanuel Kant published the Critique of Pure Reason. Hume, he said, had woken him from his "dogmatic slumber". His "Copernican revolution" turns the question around: it is not our knowledge that conforms to objects, but objects that conform to the forms of our mind. Reason knows the world of experience, but goes astray when it claims to prove God or the soul.

textes.« Dieu est mort » n'est pas une célébrat: “God is dead” isn't a celebration for Nietzsche: it's the observation of a crisis of values.
textes.« Dieu est mort » apparaît dans Le Gai S: "God is dead" appears in The Gay Science in 1882, notably in the scene of the madman who announces it in the marketplace. It is not a victory cry: it is an anxious diagnosis. If the West no longer believes in God, on what can it ground its values? Nietzsche calls for all of them to be re-evaluated.
textes.On l'a récupéré à contresens. Nietzsche: He has been hijacked against his meaning. Nietzsche despised antisemitism and German nationalism. His sister Elisabeth, married to an antisemite, falsified his manuscripts after his death to make him a thinker for the regime she admired.

textes.En 1934, à Vienne, Karl Popper publie Lo: In 1934, in Vienna, Karl Popper published Logik der Forschung. For him a theory is scientific if it can be refuted by an observation. A thousand white swans do not prove that all swans are white; a single black swan proves the opposite. A theory that explains everything, whatever happens, explains nothing.
textes.En 1962, Thomas Kuhn décrit autre chose: In 1962 Thomas Kuhn described something else in The Structure of Scientific Revolutions: normal science works within a shared framework, a paradigm, and does not abandon it at the first anomaly. When anomalies pile up, a revolution replaces the whole framework, like Copernicus replacing Ptolemy.

textes.« L'existence précède l'essence », résum: "Existence precedes essence", Sartre summed up in 1946 in Existentialism is a Humanism: humans have no nature fixed in advance, they define themselves by their acts and bear the responsibility. In 1949 Simone de Beauvoir wrote in The Second Sex: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman." Sartre would refuse the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1964, so as not to be turned into an institution.
textes.Camus, lui, part de l'absurde : le monde: Camus started from the absurd: the world does not answer our need for meaning. The Myth of Sisyphus (1942) ends: one must imagine Sisyphus happy. And in 1963 Hannah Arendt, sent to the Eichmann trial, spoke of the "banality of evil": the man who organised the deportations was not a monster but an ordinary bureaucrat who did not think.

textes.L'utilitarisme ne dit pas « la fin justi: Utilitarianism doesn't say “the end justifies the means”: it also counts the means among the consequences.
textes.Pour l'utilitarisme de Jeremy Bentham, p: For the utilitarianism of Jeremy Bentham, then John Stuart Mill, the right action is the one that produces the most total well-being, for everyone it affects. Acts are judged by their consequences. Bentham even had his body preserved, still on display at University College London. Careful: utilitarianism does not say "the end justifies the means", it counts the means among the consequences too.
textes.En 1972, Peter Singer pousse la logique: In 1972 Peter Singer pushed the logic: you would save a child drowning in a pond at the cost of your shoes; why not a child on the other side of the world, for the same price? In 1975 he also popularised the word "speciesism", proposed by Richard Ryder in 1970. Robert Nozick objected in 1974 with his experience machine: would you plug your brain into a simulated perfect life? Most people refuse.

textes.Kant répond autrement. En 1785, dans les: Kant answered differently. In 1785, in the Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, he formulated the categorical imperative: act only according to the maxim that you can will to become a universal law. If everyone lied whenever it suited them, words would be worth nothing, and lying itself would become impossible.
textes.Kant va jusqu'au bout : en 1797, réponda: Kant went all the way: in 1797, replying to Benjamin Constant, he argued that it is forbidden to lie even to a murderer who asks where your friend is hiding. Few Kantians follow him that far. But the central idea remains: some actions are forbidden whatever the consequences, and a person must never be treated merely as a means.
textes.Kant (1785) : agir selon une maxime univ: Kant (1785): act on a maxim that can be universalised. Some acts are forbidden, whatever the consequences.
textes.En 1967, Philippa Foot pose le dilemme d: In 1967 Philippa Foot posed the trolley problem: a runaway trolley will kill five people; by switching it, it will kill only one. Do you do it? Most say yes. Judith Jarvis Thomson then invented variants, including the footbridge: pushing a man onto the track to stop the trolley. Same toll, one life for five, and yet almost everyone refuses. Our intuitions are not purely utilitarian.
textes.En 2018, l'expérience Moral Machine du M: In 2018 MIT's Moral Machine experiment gathered nearly 40 million decisions in 233 countries and territories on self-driving car dilemmas; preferences vary across cultures. Virtue ethics, inherited from Aristotle, shifts the question: not "what should I do?" but "what person should I become?". textes.Pour Thomas Hobbes, dans le Léviathan (1: For Thomas Hobbes, in Leviathan (1651), without a State there is a war of every man against every man, and life would be "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short". To escape it, everyone hands their liberty to an all-powerful sovereign. For John Locke, on the contrary, power exists only to protect natural rights, life, liberty, property; a tyrannical power may be overthrown.
textes.Rousseau, en 1762, veut que le peuple so: Rousseau, in 1762, wanted the sovereign people to obey only the laws it had given itself: law expresses the general will. Much earlier, Plato entrusted the ideal city to philosopher-kings, wary of the democracy that had condemned Socrates. And Aristotle saw man as a political animal: whoever lives outside the city is "either a beast or a god".
textes.Hobbes (1651) : la sécurité contre la li: Hobbes (1651): security in exchange for liberty. Locke: protecting natural rights. Rousseau (1762): the general will.
textes.En 1748, dans De l'esprit des lois, Mont: In 1748, in The Spirit of the Laws, Montesquieu wrote: "To prevent the abuse of power, things must be so arranged that power checks power." Hence the separation of the legislature, which makes laws, from the executive, which applies them, and the judiciary, which judges. He did not start from nothing: he drew on Locke and on what he observed in England.
Even in a democracy the danger remains. Tocqueville, in Democracy in America, feared the tyranny of the majority, which can oppress as surely as a king, and more discreetly. John Stuart Mill replied in 1859 with On Liberty: the only legitimate reason to limit someone's liberty is to prevent harm to others. Over himself, the individual is sovereign.

textes.En 1971, dans Théorie de la justice, Joh: In 1971, in A Theory of Justice, John Rawls proposed an experiment: choose a society's rules behind a veil of ignorance, without knowing what place you will have in it. You might be born poor, ill or in a minority. Rawls thought you would then choose equal liberties for all, and accept inequalities only if they also benefit the worst off.
textes.D'autres pensent l'État par la force ou: Others think of the State in terms of force or resistance. For Max Weber, in 1919, the State is what successfully claims the monopoly of legitimate physical violence. Henry David Thoreau, jailed for a night in 1846 for refusing to pay tax, theorised civil disobedience, which Gandhi and Martin Luther King would read. And Karl Popper, in 1945, stated the paradox of tolerance: unlimited tolerance towards the intolerant ends up destroying tolerance.

textes.Pour Descartes, l'esprit, res cogitans,: For Descartes the mind, res cogitans, and the body, res extensa, are two different substances. It remains to explain how they communicate. He proposed the pineal gland, chosen because it is single at the centre of the brain rather than paired. We now know that it mainly secretes melatonin, the sleep hormone.
textes.En 1949, dans La Notion d'esprit, Gilber: In 1949, in The Concept of Mind, Gilbert Ryle mocked this dualism: he called it the "ghost in the machine", a philosopher's myth. For materialism, the mind is what the brain does. For functionalism, it is defined by what it does, not by what it is made of: a well-organised machine could then have a mind. Alyca follows the debate with interest.

A judge converses in writing with a human and a machine; if they cannot tell them apart, by what right deny the machine the word "think"?
textes.En 1980, John Searle répond avec la cham: In 1980 John Searle replied with the Chinese room. A man shut in a room receives questions in Chinese and, using a rule book, sends back perfect answers without understanding a word. Manipulating symbols according to rules would therefore not be enough to understand. Passing the Turing test would not prove consciousness. Alyca finds the example a little personal.

textes.En 1974, Thomas Nagel demande : quel eff: In 1974 Thomas Nagel asked: what is it like to be a bat? You can know everything about echolocation without knowing what it is like to live it. These subjective feelings, the red of your red, are called qualia. In 1982 Frank Jackson imagined Mary, a scientist who knows everything about colour but has lived in a black and white room: the day she sees a tomato, does she learn something?

And in 1983 Benjamin Libet measured brain activity, the readiness potential, that precedes the felt decision to move by about a third of a second. Its interpretation regarding free will remains hotly debated.

textes.Une dinde est nourrie chaque matin à 9 h: A turkey is fed every morning at 9 o'clock. Day after day it concludes that it always will be. It has its throat cut on Christmas Eve. This is the popular version of an example by Bertrand Russell, who spoke of a chicken, in 1912 in The Problems of Philosophy. It illustrates Hume's problem of induction: no accumulation of observations logically guarantees the next one.
textes.Dans les années 1920 et 1930, le cercle: In the 1920s and 1930s the Vienna Circle, with Carnap, Schlick and Neurath, wanted a science based on experience and judged metaphysics meaningless, neither true nor false. Popper countered with falsifiability. And Norwood Russell Hanson pointed out in 1958 that observation is not neutral: do Tycho Brahe and Kepler, watching the sunrise, see the same thing?
textes.Induction : des milliers d'observations: Induction: thousands of observations do not prove the next one (Hume, Russell's chicken). Observation depends on what you know.
textes.La thèse de Duhem-Quine dit qu'on ne tes: The Duhem-Quine thesis says you never test a hypothesis alone, but together with a whole web of auxiliary hypotheses: if the experiment fails, the fault may lie with the hypothesis, the instrument or a side theory. Which to sacrifice? In 1846 Uranus was not following its predicted orbit. Rather than throw out Newton's mechanics, Le Verrier assumed an unknown planet. Johann Galle found it less than a degree from the predicted position: Neptune.
textes.Le Verrier recommence pour expliquer les: Le Verrier tried again to explain Mercury's anomalies and predicted Vulcan. It did not exist: general relativity was needed. Imre Lakatos drew a rule from this: a research programme is "progressive" when it predicts unexpected things that turn out true, and "degenerates" when it only patches up its failures after the fact.
textes.Duhem-Quine : on teste un réseau, pas un: Duhem-Quine: you test a web, not a lone hypothesis. Neptune (1846): a successful rescue. Vulcan: the theory had to change.
textes.En 2015, l'Open Science Collaboration te: In 2015 the Open Science Collaboration tried to reproduce 100 psychology studies published in good journals. It found a significant result for only about 36 % of them. That is not necessarily fraud: often an effect too weak, a sample too small, or analyses chosen after seeing the data. The replication crisis has pushed researchers to preregister studies.
textes.La relecture a ses failles. En 1996, le: Peer review has its flaws. Scientific realism replies with Putnam's no-miracles argument: if our theories were not roughly true, their success would be a miracle.

textes.Héraclite d'Éphèse, actif vers 500 av. J: Heraclitus of Ephesus, active around 500 BC, was nicknamed "the Obscure" for his riddling style. According to Diogenes Laërtius, he deposited his only book in the Temple of Artemis; only fragments quoted by others survive.
textes.Zénon était un marchand chypriote. Après: Zeno was a Cypriot merchant. After a shipwreck, he read Xenophon's Memorabilia about Socrates in an Athens bookshop, and was sent to study with the Cynic Crates.
textes.Épicure fonde le Jardin à Athènes vers 3: Epicurus founded the Garden in Athens around 306 BC; the school welcomed many women, such as Themista and Leontion. His followers carved on their graves "I was not, I was, I am not, I do not care".
textes.Fils du médecin du roi Amyntas de Macédo: Son of King Amyntas of Macedon's physician, Aristotle taught Alexander at Mieza, in the gardens of the Nymphs near Pella. In 322 BC, accused of impiety, he left Athens "so as not to let the Athenians sin twice against philosophy", a nod to Socrates.
textes.Accusé par Mélétos, Anytos et Lycon, Soc: Accused by Meletus, Anytus and Lycon, Socrates was found guilty by 280 votes to 221. He first proposed, provocatively, to be fed at public expense in the Prytaneum, like a benefactor.
textes.Diogène et son père auraient été chassés: Diogenes and his father were said to have been driven from Sinope for debasing the currency. When Alexander asked what he wanted, he told him to stand out of his sun; when Plato defined man as a "featherless biped", he brought him a plucked cock.
textes.Les Premiers Analytiques datent d'enviro: The Prior Analytics date from around 350 BC. Aristotle's logic dominated for more than two thousand years: Kant still judged it "completed" in 1800, before Boole (1854) and then Frege (1879) went beyond it.
textes.Né à Cordoue en 1126, Averroès est juge: Born in Córdoba in 1126, Averroes was a judge and physician at the Almohad court. In 1195, his books were burned and he was exiled to Lucena. Dante placed him in Limbo, and Raphael painted him in The School of Athens.
textes.L'idée est bien plus ancienne qu'Ockham: The idea is much older than Ockham: Aristotle, Ptolemy and Robert Grosseteste already preferred the simplest explanation. textes.Ses frères l'enlèvent et le gardent pris: His brothers kidnapped him and held him prisoner for nearly a year to stop him joining the Dominicans. His fellow students called him "the dumb ox". In December 1273, after a mystical experience, he stopped writing: it all seemed "like straw" to him. He was canonised in 1323.

textes.Machiavel l'écrit en 1513, quelques mois: Machiavelli wrote it in 1513, a few months after being arrested, tortured and banished by the returning Medici, and yet dedicated it to Lorenzo de' Medici. The book came out after his death, in 1532, and the Church placed it on the Index in 1559.
textes.Élevé en latin comme langue maternelle,: Raised with Latin as his first language, Montaigne withdrew in 1571, at 38, to the tower of his château, which he dedicated by an inscription to "his freedom, tranquility and leisure". He was nonetheless mayor of Bordeaux from 1581 to 1585.
textes.Érasme l'écrit en 1509 chez son ami Thom: Erasmus wrote it in 1509 at his friend Thomas More's house in London. The Latin title, Moriae Encomium, is a pun: it can also be read "In Praise of More". Hans Holbein the Younger illustrated a copy.
textes.Écrite en latin, Utopia paraît en 1516 e: Written in Latin, Utopia came out in 1516 and was only translated into English in 1551. More also played on eu-topos, "the good place". On his island, property is held in common and people work about six hours a day.
textes.Né à Tunis en 1332, Ibn Khaldoun écrit l: Born in Tunis in 1332, Ibn Khaldun wrote the Muqaddimah over more than three years, sheltered by a Berber tribe. He met the conqueror Timur outside Damascus. Historian Arnold Toynbee called it "the greatest work of its kind".
textes.Le débat part d'une question laissée ouv: The debate began with a question Porphyry left open in the 3rd century: do genera and species exist in things or only in the mind? Boethius passed it on to the Middle Ages by translating his Isagoge; Roscelin answered that universals are mere vocal sounds.
textes.Bruno est détenu sept ans à Rome ; le ca: Bruno was held for seven years in Rome; Cardinal Bellarmine demanded that he recant, in vain. To his judges he reportedly said: "Perhaps you pronounce this sentence against me with greater fear than I receive it." His statue was unveiled at the site of the pyre on 9 June 1889.
textes.L'édition de 1580 ne compte que deux liv: The 1580 edition had only two books; that of 1588 added the third. Montaigne then annotated a copy by hand, the "Bordeaux Copy", kept at the city's municipal library.
textes.Saint Augustin avait déjà répondu aux sc: Saint Augustine had already answered the sceptics, in the early 5th century in The City of God: "If I am mistaken, I exist." Avicenna also proposed the "floating man" thought experiment, about self-awareness without any perception.
textes.Pierre de Fermat découvre la même idée d: Pierre de Fermat discovered the same idea independently, without publishing it, and Nicole Oresme was already using similar constructions in the 14th century. The two perpendicular axes only took hold after La Géométrie was translated into Latin in 1649.
textes.Les Pensées sont un recueil, publié aprè: The Pensées are a collection, published after his death, of notes Pascal had never published: that is where the wager first appears in writing.
textes.Le 27 juillet 1656, la communauté juive: On 27 July 1656, Amsterdam's Jewish community issued against Spinoza, aged 23, the harshest ban in its history, never lifted. He lived by grinding lenses and died in The Hague in 1677, aged 44; his friends then published his works.
textes.L'image est ancienne : Aristote compare: The image is old: Aristotle already compared the mind to a tablet with nothing written on it. In the 12th century, Ibn Tufail's novel Hayy ibn Yaqdhan follows a child who learns everything alone on an island; its 1671 Latin translation influenced Locke.
textes.Sextus Empiricus soulevait déjà la diffi: Sextus Empiricus already raised the difficulty in antiquity. Hume formulated it in 1739 in his Treatise of Human Nature, then in 1748: for him, it is habit, not reason, that makes us expect tomorrow.
textes.Evelyn Beatrice Hall écrit cette phrase: Evelyn Beatrice Hall wrote the sentence in The Friends of Voltaire, in the chapter on Helvétius, to illustrate Voltaire's attitude. It is still often attributed to him.
textes.Kant ne quitte guère Königsberg que pour: Kant hardly left Königsberg except to tutor in nearby towns, from 1748 to 1754. After long years of silence, he published the Critique of Pure Reason in 1781, at about 57.
textes.La formule vient du poète latin Horace,: The phrase comes from the Latin poet Horace, around 20 BC, in a letter to Lollius: "He who has begun is half done; dare to know; begin!" Melanchthon quoted it in 1518 in Wittenberg, and Foucault took up Kant's text in 1984.
textes.Le livre est interdit en France, mis à l: The book was banned in France, put on the Index and burned in Geneva; Rousseau had to flee to avoid prison. Voltaire, who criticised it, protested: to burn a book of argument is to admit you lack the wit to answer it.
textes.Le projet devait au départ traduire la C: The project was first meant to translate Englishman Ephraim Chambers's Cyclopaedia (1728). Suspended in 1752, then stripped of its privilege in 1759, the work went on in secret. The Chevalier de Jaucourt alone wrote about a quarter of the articles.
textes.En 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accus: In 1699, Nicolas Fatio de Duillier accused Leibniz of plagiarising Newton. The 1713 Royal Society report that sided with Newton was written by Newton himself. Yet it is Leibniz's notation, dy/dx, that prevailed.
textes.Popper oppose les théories qui font des: Popper contrasted theories making risky predictions with psychoanalysis and Marxism, whose followers explained away any fact after the event. His example: no list of white swans proves they all are, but a single black swan refutes the idea.
textes.Kuhn prend pour exemple le passage de l': Kuhn's example is the shift from Ptolemy's astronomy to Copernicus's, in 1543. Kant had already spoken in 1787 of a "revolution in the way of thinking".
textes.En 1885, sa sœur Elisabeth épouse Bernha: In 1885, his sister Elisabeth married Bernhard Förster, a nationalist and antisemite; Nietzsche did not attend the wedding. They founded the colony of Nueva Germania in Paraguay. Later she compiled The Will to Power, and Hitler attended her funeral in 1935. Recent work, however, questions the idea of deliberate falsification.
textes.Le Deuxième Sexe se serait vendu à envir: The Second Sex reportedly sold about 22,000 copies in its first week. The Vatican put it on the Index, where it remained until the Index was abolished in 1966. The first English translation, in 1953, cut whole passages.
textes.Eichmann est enlevé en Argentine par des: Eichmann was seized in Argentina by Israeli agents in 1960, tried in 1961 and executed in 1962. Arendt covered the trial for The New Yorker, where her report appeared in five articles. The book sparked fierce controversy, notably with Gershom Scholem.
textes.Russell trouve le paradoxe en mai 1901 e: Russell found the paradox in May 1901 while looking for a flaw in a proof by Cantor. Frege replied on 22 June 1902 and added an appendix to his book: nothing worse can befall a scientific writer than to see one of the foundations of his edifice shaken. Zermelo had found it around 1899, without publishing it.
textes.Sartre avait écrit le 14 octobre 1964 à: Sartre had written to the Nobel Institute on 14 October 1964 asking to be removed from the list. A prisoner of war in 1940, he had written his first play in a camp in Trier. On 19 April 1980, 50,000 Parisians followed his coffin.
textes.Sartre prononce cette conférence le 29 o: Sartre gave this lecture on 29 October 1945 at the Club Maintenant in Paris, before a packed hall. The text came out in 1946, and Sartre later regretted publishing it.
textes.Camus commence l'essai en 1940, pendant: Camus began the essay in 1940, during the fall of France. He starts from what he calls the only philosophical question that matters: must one kill oneself after recognising life's absurdity? His answer is no.
textes.Wittgenstein prend ses notes comme solda: Wittgenstein took his notes as a soldier in the First World War and finished the book on leave in summer 1918. The 1922 English edition had an introduction by Bertrand Russell. At the time he thought he had solved all of philosophy's problems.
textes.Élu au Collège de France fin 1969 à une: Elected to the Collège de France in late 1969 to a chair in the "history of systems of thought", Foucault co-founded the Prison Information Group in February 1971. He died of AIDS on 25 June 1984; his partner Daniel Defert then founded the AIDES charity.
textes.Le livre paraît chez l'éditeur Julius Sp: The book was published by Julius Springer with the date 1935 printed on it. Popper himself rewrote it in English: The Logic of Scientific Discovery came out in 1959.
textes.Philippa Foot imagine son tramway en réf: Philippa Foot devised her trolley while thinking about debates on abortion and the doctrine of double effect. A version already existed in 1905 in a questionnaire by Frank Chapman Sharp, and it was Judith Jarvis Thomson who named it the "trolley problem" in 1976.
textes.Bentham meurt le 6 juin 1832. Selon son: Bentham died on 6 June 1832. Following his will, his body was dissected and then preserved by Thomas Southwood Smith, dressed in his clothes; his real head, judged too macabre, was replaced with a wax one. In 2020, he was placed at the entrance of UCL's new Student Centre.
textes.Dans le même livre de 1785, Kant donne u: In the same 1785 book, Kant gave another formula: treat humanity, in yourself and in others, always also as an end and never merely as a means.
textes.L'éthique des vertus revient au premier: Virtue ethics came back to the fore with Elizabeth Anscombe's article "Modern Moral Philosophy" in 1958, then with Alasdair MacIntyre's After Virtue in 1981. The four cardinal virtues are already in Plato's Republic.
textes.L'idée est plus ancienne qu'Aristote : «: The idea is older than Aristotle: "Nothing in excess" was carved on the front of the temple at Delphi. It is also found in China in Confucius's way of the mean, and in the Buddha's "Middle Way".
textes.Singer écrit cet essai en 1971 face à la: Singer wrote this essay in 1971 in response to the starvation of refugees during the Bangladesh Liberation War. William MacAskill came across it in a seminar and later helped found the effective altruism movement.
textes.Richard Ryder lance le mot dans une broc: Richard Ryder launched the word in a privately printed pamphlet in Oxford in 1970, protesting against animal experimentation. He wrote: "Since Darwin, scientists have agreed that there is no 'magical' essential difference between humans and other animals."
textes.Une forme négative de la règle figure dé: A negative form of the rule already appears on an Egyptian papyrus from the Late Period (664-323 BC): "That which you hate to be done to you, do not do to another." It is also found in Hillel the Elder, in the Talmud, and in the Mahabharata.
textes.Le premier raisonnement connu de ce type: The first known reasoning of this kind is in the Summa Theologica, on self-defence: Thomas Aquinas allows that one may kill an attacker if one aims to defend oneself, not to kill.
textes.En 2010, Felipe De Brigard renverse l'ex: In 2010, Felipe De Brigard turned the experiment around: of students told they were already plugged in, 54% wanted to disconnect, but only 13% if told their real life was that of a maximum-security prisoner. He saw it mostly as status quo bias.
textes.Le site est lancé en 2016 par l'équipe d: The site was launched in 2016 by Iyad Rahwan's team at the MIT Media Lab. The results outline three broad cultural clusters: for example, East Asian countries spare the young less often than others.
textes.Hobbes écrit le Léviathan pendant la gue: Hobbes wrote Leviathan during the English Civil War. Historian Hugh Trevor-Roper summed it up: "The axiom, fear; the method, logic; the conclusion, despotism."
textes.Montesquieu publie le livre anonymement: Montesquieu published the book anonymously in Geneva, after about ten years of work; the Church put it on the Index in 1751. He describes the English system at length, and the work inspired the framers of the US Constitution.
textes.L'économiste William Vickrey avait décri: Economist William Vickrey had described the same thought experiment as early as 1945, and John Harsanyi formalised it in 1955, but to defend utilitarianism. Rawls coined the phrases "original position" and "veil of ignorance".
textes.Pour écrire Les Politiques, Aristote fai: To write the Politics, Aristotle had 158 constitutions of Greek cities collected to compare their strengths and weaknesses. The text may come partly from students' notes taken at the Lyceum.
textes.En 1831, Tocqueville part avec Gustave d: In 1831, Tocqueville left with Gustave de Beaumont to study American prisons for the French government. They stayed about nine months and used the trip to observe the whole of society. The book came out in two parts, in 1835 and 1840.
textes.Mill conçoit l'essai en 1854 avec sa fem: Mill conceived the essay in 1854 with his wife Harriet Taylor, and they rewrote it together. She died suddenly in 1858; Mill published it the following year without changing it, to "consecrate it to her memory", calling it their joint production.
textes.Marx écrit ces notes à Bruxelles en 1845: Marx wrote these notes in Brussels in 1845 and did not publish them. Engels edited them and published them in 1888; the original text only appeared in 1924.
textes.Montaigne affirmait que son ami l'avait: Montaigne claimed his friend wrote it at 16 or 18, but the text more likely dates from 1552-1553, when La Boétie was 22. It circulated in copies and was only printed in 1576, after his death; the Huguenots took it up.
textes.Popper le formule dans une note de La So: Popper set it out in a note to The Open Society and Its Enemies: "Unlimited tolerance must lead to the disappearance of tolerance." He linked it to a "paradox of freedom" noted by Plato. Rawls, in 1971, called for tolerating the intolerant except when the free society's survival is at stake.
textes.Platon tente l'expérience en vrai : en 3: Plato tried it for real: in 367 BC, his disciple Dion invited him to Syracuse to advise the young tyrant Dionysius II. The pupil resisted, and nothing came of it. Later, the emperor Marcus Aurelius was seen as a philosopher king.
textes.Weber donne cette conférence le 28 janvi: Weber gave this lecture on 28 January 1919 in Munich, to a students' association, in the midst of the German Revolution. An extended version came out in July 1919.
textes.Thoreau refuse de payer l'impôt pour pro: Thoreau refused to pay the tax to protest against slavery and the war with Mexico. He made it into a lecture in 1848, then the essay Resistance to Civil Government in 1849.
textes.C'est la princesse Élisabeth de Bohême q: It was Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia who raised the awkward question, in a letter of 20 June 1643: how can an unextended soul move a body? Their correspondence lasted until Descartes's death in 1650.
textes.Galien la décrit le premier au IIe siècl: Galen first described it in the 2nd century, naming it konarion, "little cone". Descartes made it the "principal seat of the soul" in The Passions of the Soul (1649). Its hormone, melatonin, was only isolated in 1958 by Aaron Lerner at Yale.
textes.Leibniz imaginait déjà un cerveau agrand: Leibniz already imagined a brain enlarged to the size of a mill, where one would only see parts pushing each other. In 1961, a short story by Soviet writer Anatoly Dneprov had a whole stadium of people, who knew no Portuguese, simulate a translation program.
textes.Turing prédisait qu'autour de l'an 2000,: Turing predicted that around the year 2000, an average interrogator would have no more than a 70% chance of identifying the machine after five minutes. In 1966, the ELIZA program, which mimicked a psychotherapist, already fooled some users.
textes.L'article de Thomas Nagel paraît en octo: Thomas Nagel's article appeared in October 1974 in The Philosophical Review. Daniel Dennett noted that in 1950, B. A. Farrell had already raised a similar question in the journal Mind.
textes.Chalmers lance l'expression en 1994, dan: Chalmers launched the phrase in 1994, in a talk at the consciousness conference in Tucson, Arizona, before his 1995 article. Leibniz and Thomas Huxley had put forward similar arguments.
textes.Charles Sanders Peirce introduit le mot: Charles Sanders Peirce introduced the word quale in 1866, and C. I. Lewis used it in its modern sense in 1929. The "inverted spectrum" question comes from John Locke, in 1689.
textes.En 1925, C. D. Broad imaginait déjà un a: In 1925, C. D. Broad already imagined an archangel who knew everything about the structure of ammonia yet could not predict its smell. Jackson eventually changed his mind: in 2023 he said he no longer accepts his own argument.
textes.Hans Kornhuber et Lüder Deecke avaient d: Hans Kornhuber and Lüder Deecke had discovered this "readiness potential" in 1965. Libet also noted that the movement could still be cancelled: he spoke of "free won't". In 2012, Aaron Schurger and colleagues saw it rather as spontaneous fluctuations in neural activity.
textes.Selon Plutarque, les Athéniens gardèrent: According to Plutarch, the Athenians kept the ship until the time of Demetrius of Phalerum. In the 17th century, Thomas Hobbes made the puzzle harder: what if a second ship were rebuilt from the old planks taken out?
textes.Hilary Putnam en propose la première ver: Hilary Putnam proposed the first version in the 1960s, comparing the mind to a Turing machine. By the mid-1970s he himself began to question it, and Ned Block countered in 1980 with a "brain" made of the whole population of China.
textes.Le scénario vient de Gilbert Harman en 1: The scenario comes from Gilbert Harman in 1973. Putnam took it up in 1981 to argue that the sentence "I am a brain in a vat" refutes itself. Zhuangzi's butterfly dream already raises a similar question.
textes.Russell racontait l'histoire d'un poulet: Russell told the story of a chicken fed every day by the man who, one fine morning, wrings its neck. Hume had posed the problem in 1739; in 1955, Nelson Goodman invented a variant with the predicate "grue".
textes.Le manifeste du cercle paraît en 1929. M: The circle's manifesto appeared in 1929. Moritz Schlick was murdered in 1936 by a former student, and Nazi Germany's annexation of Austria in 1938 ended the circle in Vienna.
textes.Pierre Duhem limitait cette idée à la ph: Pierre Duhem limited this idea to physics. Quine extended it to all knowledge, including logic and mathematics, in "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", before partly backing down on logic.
textes.Le livre devait être un débat avec Imre: The book was meant to be a debate with Imre Lakatos, who would defend scientific reason while Feyerabend attacked it; Lakatos died suddenly in 1974. Feyerabend explained that "anything goes" is not his principle, but the terrified exclamation of a rationalist who takes a closer look at history.
textes.Les médecins hippocratiques voulaient dé: Hippocratic physicians already wanted to distinguish their reasoning from mythical accounts. In 1983, Larry Laudan judged that philosophy had failed to draw this line and proposed speaking instead of reliable or unreliable knowledge.
textes.Né Imre Lipsitz en Hongrie en 1922, Laka: Born Imre Lipsitz in Hungary in 1922, Lakatos changed his name to escape the Nazis, spent three years in prison under the communist regime, then fled in 1956. A professor at the London School of Economics, he died suddenly in 1974. His motto: philosophy of science without history of science is empty.
textes.Galilée avait déjà vu Neptune fin 1612 e: Galileo had already seen Neptune in late 1612 and early 1613, but took it for a star. Galle received Le Verrier's letter on the morning of 23 September 1846 and found the planet that very night, with Heinrich d'Arrest. Englishman John Couch Adams had made a similar calculation, hence a priority dispute.
textes.Cette idée est surtout associée à Hanson: This idea is mainly associated with Hanson, Kuhn and Feyerabend, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Pierre Duhem had probably already put it forward, at least implicitly, some fifty years earlier.
textes.L'article s'intitule « Transgresser les: The article was titled "Transgressing the Boundaries: Towards a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity" and appeared in a special issue on the "Science Wars". Sokal revealed the hoax about three weeks later in the magazine Lingua Franca. In 2018, the "grievance studies" affair replayed it.
textes.Les projets Many Labs du Center for Open: The Many Labs projects of the Center for Open Science followed: 186 researchers from 60 labs re-tested 28 psychology findings, and half failed to replicate, despite large samples.
textes.Le nom latin experimentum crucis est ens: The Latin name experimentum crucis was later coined by Robert Hooke, and Newton used it in the Opticks for the prism experiment showing that white light is made of different rays.
textes.Pour Anaximandre de Milet, le principe d: For Anaximander of Miletus, the principle of all things is:
textes.Anaximandre, disciple de Thalès, ne choi: Anaximander, Thales' pupil, picks no known element: the principle is the apeiron, a boundless, undefined stuff from which everything comes.
textes.Thalès, Anaximandre et Anaximène viennen: Thales, Anaximander and Anaximenes all came from Miletus, in Ionia, in the 6th century BC: the Milesian school. Each looked for the arche, the single principle of the world, without calling on the gods.
textes.Anaximène, le troisième penseur de Milet: Anaximenes, the third thinker of Miletus, derives everything from:
textes.Pour Anaximène, l'air raréfié devient fe: For Anaximenes, thinned air becomes fire; thickened, it becomes wind, cloud, water, then earth and stone. One principle, two motions.
textes.Les textes des Milésiens sont perdus : o: The Milesians' writings are lost: they are known only through quotations by later authors, Aristotle and his successors. Scholars speak of "fragments" and "testimonies".
textes.Dans son poème De la nature, Parménide o: In his poem On Nature, Parmenides contrasts:
textes.la voie de la vérité et la voie de l'opi: the way of truth and the way of opinion
textes.Pour Parménide, l'être est, le non-être: For Parmenides, being is and non-being is not: what is can neither come to be nor change. The motion and change our senses show belong to deceptive opinion.
textes.Le poème de Parménide, écrit en vers ver: Parmenides' poem, written in verse around the early 5th century BC, opens with a proem in which a goddess guides the narrator. Only a few pieces of the way of opinion survive.
textes.Zénon d'Élée invente le paradoxe d'Achil: Zeno of Elea invents the paradox of Achilles and the tortoise to:
textes.défendre son maître Parménide : le mouve: defend his master Parmenides: motion would be an illusion
textes.montrer qu'Achille est trop lent: show that Achilles is too slow
textes.Achille doit d'abord atteindre le point: Achilles must first reach the point the tortoise started from; it has already moved on, and so on forever. Zeno wanted to show that our senses deceive us about motion, as Parmenides held.
Zeno's writings (c. 490-430 BC) are lost. Nine of his paradoxes reached us because Aristotle quotes them to refute them in his Physics.
textes.Pour Leucippe et Démocrite, le monde est: For Leucippus and Democritus, the world is made of:
textes.« Atome » vient du grec atomos, « inséca: "Atom" comes from the Greek atomos, "uncuttable". For the atomists, only indivisible grains moving through the void truly exist; tastes and colours are mere conventions of our senses.
textes.Démocrite, né à Abdère en Thrace vers 46: Democritus, born in Abdera in Thrace around 460 BC, took up the idea of his teacher Leucippus. He was nicknamed "the laughing philosopher" for the weight he gave to cheerfulness.
textes.Empédocle explique tout ce qui existe pa: Empedocles explains everything with four roots, earth, water, air and fire, mixed and separated by:
textes.L'Amour (Philotès) unit les éléments, la: Love (Philotes) unites the elements, Strife (Neikos) separates them.
textes.Selon Diogène Laërce, Empédocle d'Agrige: According to Diogenes Laertius, Empedocles of Akragas threw himself into Etna so people would think he had become a god; the volcano supposedly spat back one of his bronze sandals, exposing the trick.
textes.Les penseurs grecs d'avant Socrate se dé: The Greek thinkers before Socrates called themselves "pre-Socratics".
textes.Le mot est moderne : il range ces penseu: The word is modern: it ranks these thinkers in relation to Socrates, whom not all of them knew, since some were his contemporaries. They rather called themselves "physicists", inquirers into nature.
textes.Le philosophe allemand Johann August Ebe: The German philosopher Johann August Eberhard first used the phrase "pre-Socratic philosophy" in the late 18th century; Hermann Diels made it standard in 1903 with his collection Die Fragmente der Vorsokratiker.
textes.En quelle année Hermann Diels publie-t-i: In what year did Hermann Diels publish Die Fragmente der Vorsokratiker, the standard collection of the pre-Socratics?
textes.En 1903. Le recueil donne un numéro à ch: In 1903. The collection gives each thinker a number and files accounts of his life and views under A, fragments of his own words under B. Scholars still cite the pre-Socratics this way.
textes.Walther Kranz révise ensuite le recueil,: Walther Kranz later revised the collection, hence the abbreviation DK, for Diels-Kranz: his fifth edition, published in 1934-1937, gives the numbering used today.
textes.Xénophane de Colophon remarque que si le: Xenophanes of Colophon notes that if oxen, horses or lions could draw, they would picture the gods:
textes.Xénophane critique les dieux d'Homère et: Xenophanes criticizes the gods of Homer and Hesiod, made in the image of men: everyone pictures the gods in their own likeness.
textes.Xénophane, né à Colophon en Ionie vers 5: Xenophanes, born in Colophon in Ionia around 570 BC, is said to have lived past 90 as a wandering poet. His critique makes him one of the first to see religious beliefs as a human projection.
textes.Pythagore fonde sa communauté de discipl: Pythagoras founds his community of disciples in:
textes.Né à Samos, Pythagore s'installe à Croto: Born on Samos, Pythagoras settled in Croton, in Magna Graecia. His followers held that reality is made of numbers and their ratios.
textes.Pythagore n'a laissé aucun écrit ; ce qu: Pythagoras left no writings; what is credited to him often comes from his disciples, so it is hard to separate his own thought from that of the Pythagorean school.
textes.Les paroles de Confucius nous sont parve: Confucius' sayings have come down to us in:
textes.les Entretiens, rassemblés par ses disci: the Analects, compiled by his disciples
textes.un traité qu'il a écrit en prison: a treatise he wrote in prison
textes.des inscriptions sur bronze de son vivan: bronze inscriptions made in his lifetime
textes.Les Entretiens (Lunyu) sont des recueils: The Analects (Lunyu) are collections of short dialogues and maxims, put together by his disciples, then by their disciples, long after his death.
textes.Selon le Shiji de Sima Qian, Confucius a: According to Sima Qian's Shiji, Confucius had 3,000 pupils, 72 or 77 of them particularly accomplished.
textes.par des missionnaires jésuites, à la fin: by Jesuit missionaries, in the late 16th century
It Latinizes Kong Fuzi, "Master Kong". In China he is rather called Kongzi. His personal name was Kong Qiu.
textes.Le jésuite italien Matteo Ricci, arrivé: The Italian Jesuit Matteo Ricci, who reached Macau in 1582, was with the Chinese scholar Xu Guangqi the first to translate some of the Confucian classics into Latin.
textes.Confucius enseigne : « Ce que tu ne voud: Confucius teaches: "What you would not want for yourself, do not impose on others."
textes.C'est une forme négative de la règle d'o: It is a negative form of the golden rule, quoted twice in the Analects. It rests on reciprocity (shu) and on ren, the virtue of humaneness towards others.
textes.Confucius a été haut fonctionnaire dans: Confucius served as a high official in the state of Lu, rising to Minister of Crime, before spending years on the road offering his ideas to other princes, without being heeded.
textes.Selon la tradition, en quelle année avan: According to tradition, in what year BC was Confucius born? (answer without the minus sign)
textes.Vers 551 av. J.-C., dans l'État de Lu, l: Around 551 BC, in the state of Lu, today's Qufu area in Shandong. He died around 479.
textes.Ces dates en font un contemporain du Bou: These dates make him a contemporary of the Buddha, and about eighty years older than Socrates.
textes.Selon la tradition, Siddhartha Gautama a: According to tradition, Siddhartha Gautama attains awakening, becoming the Buddha, while meditating:
textes.sous un figuier, à Bodh-Gaya: under a fig tree, at Bodh Gaya
textes.sur les rives du Gange, à Bénarès: on the banks of the Ganges, at Benares
textes.L'arbre, un figuier des pagodes (Ficus r: The tree, a sacred fig (Ficus religiosa), is called the Bodhi tree, the tree "of awakening". Buddha means "the awakened one".
textes.Le Bouddha aurait ensuite donné son prem: The Buddha is then said to have given his first sermon at the Deer Park in Sarnath, near Benares, and to have died at about 80 in Kushinagar.
textes.La « voie du milieu » enseignée par le B: The "middle way" taught by the Buddha runs between:
textes.Le jeune Siddhartha a connu le luxe d'un: Young Siddhartha knew the luxury of a palace, then years of harsh asceticism. Neither leads to awakening: a path between the two is needed.
textes.Ses enseignements se sont transmis orale: His teachings were passed on orally for centuries, in Indian dialects, before being written down; the oldest written mention of the Buddha is in the edicts of Emperor Ashoka, in the 3rd century BC.
textes.La première des quatre nobles vérités du: The first of the Buddha's four noble truths is about:
textes.l'existence d'un dieu créateur: the existence of a creator god
textes.Les quatre vérités : la souffrance exist: The four truths: suffering exists; it has a cause, craving; it can cease; and a path leads there, the noble eightfold path.
textes.Siddhartha Gautama serait né à Lumbini,: Siddhartha Gautama is said to have been born in Lumbini, in today's Nepal, in the 6th or 5th century BC; his exact dates remain uncertain.
textes.La plus ancienne trace écrite du Bouddha: The oldest written trace of the Buddha is:
textes.une inscription de l'empereur Ashoka, au: an inscription by Emperor Ashoka, in the 3rd century BC
textes.un livre écrit de sa main: a book in his own hand
textes.Sur le pilier de Lumbini, Ashoka fait gr: On the Lumbini pillar, Ashoka had it carved that he came to worship at this spot "because the Buddha Shakyamuni was born here".
textes.Ashoka, qui règne sur presque tout le so: Ashoka, who ruled most of the Indian subcontinent around 268-232 BC, turned to Buddhism after the slaughter of his war on Kalinga. His edicts are the oldest datable texts of India.
textes.Le Tao-tö-king, attribué à Lao-tseu, rec: The Tao Te Ching, attributed to Laozi, recommends wu wei, that is:
textes.le non-agir : agir sans forcer le cours: non-action: acting without forcing the course of things
textes.Le Tao, la Voie, est la source de toute: The Tao, the Way, is the source of all things. The sage imitates it: he acts like water, which does not fight and yet wears down stone.
textes.Selon l'historien Sima Qian, Lao-tseu, q: According to the historian Sima Qian, Laozi, leaving China for the west, wrote the book at the request of the guardian of the pass, Yinxi. Historians now doubt he existed; his name simply means "Old Master".
textes.Zhuangzi raconte qu'il a rêvé être un pa: Zhuangzi tells how he dreamed he was a butterfly. On waking, he wonders:
textes.s'il est un homme qui a rêvé d'être papi: whether he is a man who dreamed of being a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming of being a man
textes.Le rêve du papillon illustre la « transf: The butterfly dream illustrates the "transformation of things": the boundaries between beings, and between dreaming and waking, are less clear than we think.
textes.Zhuang Zhou vécut au IVe siècle av. J.-C: Zhuang Zhou lived in the 4th century BC; the book that bears his name is, with the Tao Te Ching, one of the two founding texts of Taoism.
textes.Mencius, disciple de la lignée de Confuc: Mencius, in the line of Confucius, holds that human nature is:
textes.bonne, et que la société la gâte: good, and that society spoils it
textes.mauvaise, et que l'éducation la redresse: bad, and that education straightens it
textes.ni bonne ni mauvaise, une page blanche: neither good nor bad, a blank page
textes.Pour Mencius, chacun porte des germes de: For Mencius, everyone carries seeds of goodness, like the pity that seizes us at the sight of a child about to fall into a well. His near-contemporary Xunzi held on the contrary that human nature is bad.
textes.Mencius (vers 371-289 av. J.-C.) est app: Mencius (c. 371-289 BC) is called the "Second Sage" in China. In a famous story, his mother moved three times to raise him in a good neighbourhood.
textes.Confucius et le Bouddha ont vécu à peu p: Confucius and the Buddha lived at roughly the same time, in the 6th and 5th centuries BC.
textes.Confucius vit vers 551-479 av. J.-C. ; l: Confucius lived around 551-479 BC; the Buddha in the 6th or 5th century BC. At the same time, in Greece, Heraclitus and Parmenides were thinking about being and change.
textes.En 1949, le philosophe Karl Jaspers appe: In 1949, the philosopher Karl Jaspers called these centuries, when the great wisdoms of China, India, Persia and Greece emerged without contact with one another, the "Axial Age".
textes.Selon l'accusation, Socrate était coupab: According to the indictment, Socrates was guilty of:
textes.On lui reproche de ne pas reconnaître le: He was charged with not recognizing the city's gods, introducing new ones and corrupting the young men who listened to him.
textes.Le jury, tiré au sort, comptait probable: The jury, chosen by lot, probably numbered 501 citizens. Xenophon, another disciple, also wrote an Apology of Socrates and the Memorabilia about his master.
textes.Dans la République, l'anneau de Gygès, q: In the Republic, the ring of Gyges, which makes its wearer invisible, is used to ask:
textes.serait-on juste si personne ne pouvait n: would we be just if no one could see us?
textes.Le berger Gygès trouve un anneau qui le: The shepherd Gyges finds a ring that makes him invisible; he uses it to seduce the queen, kill the king and seize the throne. If we did not fear being seen, would we stay honest?
textes.C'est Glaucon, le frère aîné de Platon,: It is Glaucon, Plato's elder brother, who tells the story in Book II of the Republic. The whole rest of the dialogue tries to answer him: is justice worth having for its own sake?
textes.Le Banquet de Platon est un concours de: Plato's Symposium is a contest of speeches in praise of:
textes.Aristophane y raconte que les humains, c: In it, Aristophanes tells how humans, cut in two by Zeus, seek their lost half. Socrates reports the lessons of the wise woman Diotima: love rises from a beautiful body to the Idea of Beauty.
The Symposium dates from about 385-370 BC. The phrase "Platonic love" is not Plato's: it comes from Marsilio Ficino, in Florence, in 1476.
textes.Le jour de sa mort, Socrate discute avec: On the day of his death, Socrates discusses the immortality of the soul with his friends, then drinks the hemlock. It is also the dialogue where the theory of Forms first appears.
textes.Le récit est fait par Phédon d'Élis, tém: The account is given by Phaedo of Elis, who witnessed the scene, to Echecrates of Phlius. Plato never presents himself as a witness: apart from the Apology, nothing suggests he heard the conversations he relates.
textes.du bois sacré d'Akadêmos, à Athènes, où: the sacred grove of Akademos, in Athens, where Plato taught
textes.Platon fonde son école vers 387 av. J.-C: Plato founded his school around 387 BC in an olive grove sacred to Athena, linked to the legendary hero Akademos. The word went around the world.
textes.L'Académie a fonctionné, sous diverses f: The Academy ran, in various forms, until the emperor Justinian closed it in 529, more than nine centuries later. Aristotle studied there for twenty years.
textes.Les Grecs de l'époque de Platon ont vu g: Greeks of Plato's time saw carved at the entrance of the Academy: "Let no one ignorant of geometry enter".
textes.Rien ne le prouve. Cette inscription n'e: Nothing proves it. The inscription is reported only by commentators writing some seven hundred years after the school's founding: it is a nice legend.
textes.Des mathématiciens fréquentaient pourtan: Mathematicians did frequent the Academy, though: Theaetetus took part in the gatherings it grew out of, and Eudoxus of Cnidus, who arrived around 385, was the first to study planetary motion.
textes.Dans la cité idéale de la République, Pl: In the ideal city of the Republic, Plato entrusts the city's defence, alongside the rulers, to:
textes.La cité compte trois groupes : les dirig: The city has three groups: rulers, guardians and producers. Each matches a part of the soul: reason, spirit, appetite.
textes.Platon a tenté de mettre ses idées en pr: Plato tried to put his ideas into practice in Syracuse, which he first visited around 385 BC, under the tyrant Dionysius. The Sicilian stays would end badly.
textes.Né entre 428 et 423 av. J.-C., Platon me: Born between 428 and 423 BC, Plato died in 348 or 347, aged over 75. His nephew Speusippus succeeded him at the head of the Academy, not Aristotle.
textes.On pense que toute son œuvre écrite nous: His complete written work is believed to have survived, a rare thing for an ancient author. Its arrangement goes back to Thrasyllus of Mendes, in the 1st century AD.
textes.Aristote est surnommé « le Stagirite » p: Aristotle is nicknamed "the Stagirite" because he was born:
textes.Né en 384 av. J.-C. à Stagire, en Grèce: Born in 384 BC in Stagira, in northern Greece, son of Nicomachus, physician to King Amyntas of Macedon, he came to Athens at about 17 or 18.
textes.Il passe près de vingt ans à l'Académie: He spent nearly twenty years at Plato's Academy, until the master's death, when he was about 37.
textes.le péripatos, la galerie couverte du Lyc: the peripatos, the covered walkway of the Lyceum
textes.Peripatos désigne la colonnade, la prome: Peripatos means the colonnade, the covered walk of the Lyceum. Legend has it that Aristotle taught while walking, hence the image of the philosopher who thinks as he strolls.
Aristotle returned to Athens in 335 BC and taught at the Lyceum for twelve years. On Alexander's death, in 323, he left Athens, hostile to the Macedonians, and died the following year in Chalcis, on Euboea.
textes.Pour une statue, Aristote appelle « caus: For a statue, Aristotle calls the "final cause":
textes.ce en vue de quoi elle est faite: that for the sake of which it is made
textes.le bronze dont elle est faite: the bronze it is made of
textes.Quatre causes répondent à « pourquoi ? »: Four causes answer "why?": the matter (the bronze), the form, the moving cause (the sculptor) and the end, what the thing exists for.
textes.La théorie des quatre causes est exposée: The theory of the four causes is set out in Book II of the Physics. The final cause, which modern science would banish from physics, is still debated in biology.
textes.meut tout sans être mû lui-même: moves everything without being moved itself
textes.Il faut un premier moteur pour éviter un: A first mover is needed to avoid an infinite chain of causes. It does not act by pushing: it attracts, like an object of desire or of thought.
textes.Le moteur immobile inspirera au Moyen Âg: The unmoved mover would inspire, in the Middle Ages, Islamic philosophers such as Avicenna and Averroes, Jewish thinkers such as Maimonides, and Thomas Aquinas, who took it up in his five ways to God.
textes.Aristote pensait qu'un corps lourd tombe: Aristotle thought a heavy body falls faster than a light one.
textes.C'est vrai dans l'air ou dans l'eau, où: It holds in air or water, where he reasoned, but is false in a vacuum. John Philoponus in the 6th century, then Galileo in the 17th, would challenge it.
textes.Le physicien Carlo Rovelli a défendu en: The physicist Carlo Rovelli argued in 2015 that Aristotle's physics is correct within its domain: objects falling through a fluid under Earth's gravity.
textes.Pour Aristote, le but de toute vie humai: For Aristotle, the aim of every human life, the highest good, is:
textes.Tout ce que nous faisons vise une fin ;: Everything we do aims at an end; the ultimate end, wanted for its own sake, is eudaimonia, reached by exercising one's virtues over a whole life.
The Nicomachean Ethics has ten books. Its title probably refers to Nicomachus, Aristotle's son, who may have edited it; his grandfather bore the same name.
textes.« L'homme est par nature un animal polit: "Man is by nature a political animal", writes Aristotle. He means that man:
textes.ne s'accomplit que dans la vie en cité: only fulfils himself through life in a city
textes.est fait pour gouverner les animaux: is made to rule over animals
textes.Pour Aristote, la cité (polis) est la pl: For Aristotle, the city (polis) is the highest of human communities: only there does man fully realize his nature, beyond the family and the village.
textes.Pour écrire la Politique, Aristote et se: To write the Politics, Aristotle and his students gathered the constitutions of 158 Greek cities; only Athens' has been found, on a papyrus published in 1891.
textes.Pour observer les animaux marins, Aristo: To observe sea creatures, Aristotle spends two years:
textes.sur l'île de Lesbos, autour de la lagune: on the island of Lesbos, around the Pyrrha lagoon
textes.en Égypte, au bord du Nil: in Egypt, on the banks of the Nile
textes.Il y dissèque et décrit poissons, seiche: There he dissected and described fish, cuttlefish and sea urchins. He distinguished about 500 animal species and classified them: the first great work of zoology.
textes.Après la mort de Platon, en 347 av. J.-C: After Plato's death, in 347 BC, Aristotle left Athens. It was during these years away from the city that he studied the wildlife of Lesbos, before becoming Alexander's tutor in 343.
textes.En quelle année avant notre ère meurt Ar: In what year BC did Aristotle die? (answer without the minus sign)
textes.En 322 av. J.-C., à Chalcis, un an après: In 322 BC, in Chalcis, a year after Alexander. He had left Athens, it was said, so as not to let the Athenians "sin twice against philosophy".
textes.Ses manuscrits, cachés pour les protéger: His papers, hidden for safekeeping, were later bought by the collector Apellicon. Around 40 BC, Andronicus of Rhodes gathered his logical treatises into a six-book set: the Organon.
textes.Le mot « cynique » vient du grec kuôn, q: The word "cynic" comes from the Greek kuon, meaning:
textes.Diogène se disait lui-même chien : il re: Diogenes called himself a dog: he fawned on those who gave him something and barked at those who gave nothing. The Cynics lived without shame, according to nature, scorning conventions.
textes.Diogène, né à Sinope sur la mer Noire ve: Diogenes, born in Sinope on the Black Sea around 413-403 BC, had been exiled from it after an affair of debased coinage.
textes.Diogène se promenait en plein jour avec: Diogenes walked about in broad daylight with a lit lamp. He said:
textes.Il cherchait un homme digne de ce nom, u: He was looking for a man worthy of the name, a wise man, in the crowd of the marketplace. Diogenes' lamp remains the image of the philosopher judging his contemporaries.
textes.À qui lui demandait d'où il venait, Diog: Asked where he came from, Diogenes replied: "I am a citizen of the world." It is one of the oldest statements of cosmopolitanism.
textes.Épicure fonde son école à Athènes vers 3: Epicurus founds his school in Athens around 306 BC. It is called:
textes.Les cours se tenaient dans un jardin qu': Lessons were held in a garden he owned, roughly midway between the Stoa and the Academy. Life there was simple, among friends: Epicurus put friendship above power and wealth.
textes.Fait rare à l'époque, le Jardin accueill: Unusually for the time, the Garden welcomed many women among its students. Epicurus had been born on Samos in 341 BC.
textes.Le tetrapharmakos, le « quadruple remède: The tetrapharmakos, the Epicureans' "four-part cure", teaches in particular:
textes.que la mort n'est rien à craindre: that death is nothing to fear
textes.qu'il faut jeûner quatre jours: that one should fast for four days
textes.qu'il faut prier quatre dieux: that one should pray to four gods
textes.Les quatre remèdes : ne pas craindre les: The four cures: don't fear the gods, don't worry about death, the good is easy to get, the bad easy to bear. "Death is nothing to us", said Epicurus: when it is here, we are no more.
textes.Le quadruple remède résume les quatre pr: The four-part cure sums up Epicurus' first four Principal Doctrines. It reached us through his follower Philodemus of Gadara, on a charred papyrus found at Herculaneum.
textes.Le but des épicuriens comme des sceptiqu: The goal of the Epicureans as of the Sceptics is ataraxia, that is:
textes.l'absence de trouble de l'âme: freedom from disturbance of the soul
textes.Ataraxia veut dire « absence de trouble: Ataraxia means "absence of disturbance". The Epicureans pair it with aponia, the absence of bodily pain. For the Sceptics, suspending judgement leads to it.
textes.On appelle hellénistique la période qui: The Hellenistic period runs from the death of Alexander the Great, in 323 BC, to the battle of Actium, in 31 BC. Three schools dominated it: Stoics, Epicureans and Sceptics.
textes.Pyrrhon d'Élis, le premier des sceptique: Pyrrho of Elis, the first of the Sceptics, recommends, faced with conflicting opinions:
textes.Pour chaque argument, on peut en trouver: For each argument, another of equal force can be found. Rather than decide, the Sceptic suspends judgement, and finds peace in doing so.
textes.Pyrrhon (vers 360-270 av. J.-C.) suivit: Pyrrho (c. 360-270 BC) followed Alexander's army as far as India, where he met the "gymnosophists", naked sages. He wrote nothing: he is known through his disciple Timon of Phlius.
textes.Zénon de Kition serait venu à la philoso: Zeno of Citium is said to have come to philosophy after a shipwreck.
textes.Selon Diogène Laërce, marchand venu de C: According to Diogenes Laertius, a merchant from Cyprus, he was shipwrecked near Piraeus; in Athens, he read Xenophon's Memorabilia at a bookseller's and asked where to find a man like Socrates. He was pointed to the Cynic Crates.
textes.Zénon (vers 334-262 av. J.-C.) enseigne: Zeno (c. 334-262 BC) taught around 300 under the Painted Porch of Athens. For him, the good life is a virtuous life, in agreement with nature.
textes.Quand Alexandre le Grand demande à Diogè: When Alexander the Great asks Diogenes what he wants, he replies:
textes.Diogène prenait le soleil quand le roi l: Diogenes was sunbathing when the most powerful king in the world came to offer him whatever he wished. He only asked him to move aside a little.
textes.Selon Plutarque, Alexandre aurait dit en: According to Plutarch, Alexander then told his courtiers, who were mocking the philosopher: "If I were not Alexander, I would be Diogenes."
textes.En quelle année avant notre ère meurt Ép: In what year BC did Epicurus die? (answer without the minus sign)
textes.En 270 av. J.-C., à Athènes, à 71 ans en: In 270 BC, in Athens, aged about 71. Born in 341, he taught for some thirty years at the Garden.
textes.D'Épicure, qui aurait écrit quelque troi: Of Epicurus, who reportedly wrote some three hundred treatises, little remains beyond the Principal Doctrines, three letters preserved by Diogenes Laertius and fragments of his major work, On Nature, found at Herculaneum.
textes.Dans De la nature des choses, Lucrèce ex: In On the Nature of Things, Lucretius sets out in Latin verse the philosophy of:
textes.En six livres, Lucrèce explique que tout: In six books, Lucretius explains that everything is made of atoms and void, that the soul dies with the body and so neither the gods nor death are to be feared.
textes.Le poème a failli se perdre au Moyen Âge: The poem was nearly lost in the Middle Ages: the humanist Poggio found it in 1417 in a German monastery. Cicero, Lucretius' contemporary, already praised its "flashes of genius".
textes.Cicéron a beaucoup compté pour la philos: Cicero mattered greatly for philosophy because he:
textes.a fait passer la philosophie grecque en: brought Greek philosophy into Latin, inventing words
textes.Pour traduire les notions grecques, Cicé: To translate Greek notions, Cicero coined Latin words such as qualitas (quality), quantitas (quantity) or humanitas. Nearly 150 of his creations translate Greek terms.
textes.Orateur et homme politique, Cicéron est: Orator and statesman, Cicero was killed on 7 December 43 BC on Mark Antony's orders, after delivering the Philippics against him.
textes.Sénèque, philosophe stoïcien, fut le pré: Seneca, a Stoic philosopher, was tutor and then adviser to the emperor:
textes.Précepteur du jeune Néron à partir de 49: Tutor to the young Nero from 49, Seneca advised him during the first years of his reign, before withdrawing.
textes.En 65, Néron lui ordonne de se donner la: In 65, Nero ordered him to take his own life, accusing him of a part in the Pisonian conspiracy; many historians doubt it. Born in Córdoba, Seneca left 124 Letters to Lucilius.
textes.Marc Aurèle a écrit ses Pensées en latin: Marcus Aurelius wrote his Meditations in Latin, to publish them in his lifetime.
textes.Il les a écrites en grec, pour lui-même: He wrote them in Greek, for himself: they are private notes, hence their Greek title, "To Himself". The emperor urges himself to judge calmly what is not up to him.
textes.Marc Aurèle règne de 161 à 180. Une part: Marcus Aurelius reigned from 161 to 180. Part of the twelve books was written on campaign: the first is marked "among the Quadi, on the Granua", in today's Slovakia.
textes.Épictète, l'un des maîtres du stoïcisme,: Epictetus, one of the masters of Stoicism, had first been:
textes.Né esclave vers 50 à Hiérapolis, en Phry: Born a slave around 50 in Hierapolis, Phrygia, Epictetus was freed and taught philosophy. He wrote nothing: his pupil Arrian recorded his Discourses and drew the Handbook from them.
textes.Vers 93, l'empereur Domitien chasse les: Around 93, the emperor Domitian banished philosophers from Rome; Epictetus then opened a school in Nicopolis, in Epirus. He was lame, from birth or because of a brutal master, depending on the source.
textes.Pour Plotin, fondateur du néoplatonisme,: For Plotinus, founder of Neoplatonism, everything proceeds from:
textes.de l'Un, principe au-delà de tout: the One, a principle beyond everything
textes.Trois principes s'emboîtent : l'Un, l'In: Three principles fit together: the One, Intellect and Soul. The One lies beyond being itself; the sage seeks to rise back to it.
textes.Né en Égypte romaine vers 204, Plotin en: Born in Roman Egypt around 204, Plotinus taught in Rome from the age of 40. His pupil Porphyry arranged his 54 treatises into six groups of nine: the Enneads, from the Greek ennea, "nine".
textes.Hypatie, philosophe et mathématicienne d: Hypatia, philosopher and mathematician of Alexandria, dies in 415:
textes.tuée par une foule de chrétiens: killed by a mob of Christians
textes.dans l'incendie de la bibliothèque: in the fire of the Library
textes.de vieillesse, dans son école: of old age, in her school
textes.En mars 415, une foule menée par un lect: In March 415, a mob led by a lector named Peter murdered her: rumour accused her of preventing the reconciliation of the prefect Orestes with Bishop Cyril.
textes.Fille du mathématicien Théon d'Alexandri: Daughter of the mathematician Theon of Alexandria, Hypatia commented on Diophantus' Arithmetica and Apollonius' Conics. She had Christians among her pupils, such as the future bishop Synesius.
textes.En quelle année Hypatie est-elle assassi: In what year was Hypatia murdered in Alexandria?
textes.En 415, en mars. Sa mort a fait d'elle,: In 415, in March. Her death made her, for later centuries, a "martyr for philosophy".
textes.Elle enseignait à Alexandrie la philosop: She taught Neoplatonic philosophy, mathematics and astronomy in Alexandria; she may also have helped edit Ptolemy's Almagest.
textes.Les Confessions d'Augustin, écrites vers: Augustine's Confessions, written around 397-398, are often considered:
textes.Augustin y raconte sa jeunesse, ses faut: Augustine recounts his youth, his sins and his conversion to Christianity, addressing God. Book XI also meditates on the nature of time.
textes.Né en 354 à Thagaste, dans l'actuelle Al: Born in 354 in Thagaste, in today's Algeria, Augustine became bishop of Hippo. After the Visigoths sacked Rome in 410, he wrote The City of God to console Christians.
textes.Boèce écrit La Consolation de Philosophi: Boethius writes The Consolation of Philosophy:
textes.au sommet de sa gloire de consul: at the height of his glory as consul
textes.dans un monastère, à la fin d'une longue: in a monastery, at the end of a long life
