textes.Accusé de complot, Boèce est emprisonné: Accused of conspiracy, Boethius was imprisoned around 523 by the Ostrogothic king Theodoric and executed in 524. In his book, Philosophy appears to him as a woman and consoles him: Fortune turns like a wheel.
textes.Boèce avait traduit en latin la logique: Boethius had translated Aristotle's logic into Latin. From the 6th to the 12th century, his translations were nearly all Latin Europe knew of Aristotle.
textes.Marc Aurèle, l'auteur stoïcien des Pensé: Marcus Aurelius, the Stoic author of the Meditations, was a Roman emperor.
textes.Il règne de 161 à 180. On l'a appelé le: He reigned from 161 to 180. He has been called the "philosopher on the throne", an image of the philosopher-king Plato dreamed of.
textes.Dernier des « cinq bons empereurs », il: The last of the "Five Good Emperors", he spent much of his reign fighting the Marcomanni, Quadi and Iazyges, who came from across the Danube. He died in 180, at Vindobona (Vienna) or near Sirmium.
textes.Un esclave affranchi, un ministre de Nér: A freed slave, a minister of Nero and an emperor shared the same philosophy. Which?
textes.Épictète, Sénèque et Marc Aurèle sont le: Epictetus, Seneca and Marcus Aurelius are the three great Stoics of the Roman era, whose writings have survived, unlike those of the first Greek Stoics.
textes.Des fondateurs grecs du stoïcisme, Zénon: Of the Greek founders of Stoicism, Zeno and Chrysippus, almost nothing has survived. It is through the Romans, and Arrian's notes on Epictetus, that the school is best known.
textes.À Bagdad, au IXe siècle, la Maison de la: In Baghdad, in the 9th century, the House of Wisdom is known above all for:
textes.la traduction en arabe des savants et ph: translating Greek scientists and philosophers into Arabic
textes.Sous le calife al-Ma'mun (813-833), on y: Under the caliph al-Ma'mun (813-833), Aristotle, Galen, Euclid or Ptolemy were translated there from Greek and Syriac. The Christian physician Hunayn ibn Ishaq led the translators.
textes.La Maison de la sagesse disparaît lors d: The House of Wisdom vanished in the Mongol siege of Baghdad in 1258. The historian Dimitri Gutas even doubts it was a true institution rather than a library.
textes.Al-Kindi, au IXe siècle, est surnommé :: Al-Kindi, in the 9th century, is nicknamed:
textes.Al-Kindi (vers 801-873) travaille à Bagd: Al-Kindi (c. 801-873) worked in Baghdad, where he oversaw translations of Greek texts. He wanted to show that Greek philosophy agrees with Islam.
textes.Al-Kindi est aussi le premier connu à dé: Al-Kindi is also the first known to describe frequency analysis: counting how often letters appear in an encrypted message to break it. It is the birth of cryptanalysis.
textes.Al-Farabi est surnommé « le second maîtr: Al-Farabi is nicknamed "the Second Master". The first is:
textes.Le titre dit l'admiration des philosophe: The title expresses Arabic-language philosophers' admiration for Aristotle, "the First Master", and for the man who best explained him. Al-Farabi lived around 870-950 and died in Damascus.
textes.Al-Farabi a écrit sur la politique, avec: Al-Farabi wrote on politics, with The Virtuous City, inspired by Plato's Republic, but also a Great Book of Music.
textes.L'« homme volant » d'Avicenne est une ex: Avicenna's "floating man" is a thought experiment: a man floats in the air, with no sensation at all. Avicenna concludes:
textes.qu'il saurait encore qu'il existe : l'âm: that he would still know he exists: the soul knows itself without the body
textes.qu'il tomberait aussitôt: that he would fall at once
textes.Aveuglé, sans toucher ni ses membres ni: Blindfolded, touching neither his limbs nor anything else, the floating man would still be aware that he exists: for Avicenna, the soul is therefore a substance distinct from the body.
textes.Avicenne aurait imaginé l'homme volant e: Avicenna is said to have devised the floating man while imprisoned. Six centuries later, Descartes' "I think, therefore I am" would often be compared to it.
textes.Le Canon de la médecine d'Avicenne fut e: Avicenna's Canon of Medicine was taught in European universities:
textes.Cette encyclopédie médicale, une fois tr: This medical encyclopedia, once translated into Latin, became a standard textbook at many European universities, and remained one until the mid-17th century.
textes.Avicenne (Ibn Sina), né vers 980 près de: Avicenna (Ibn Sina), born around 980 near Bukhara into a Persian family, died in 1037 in Hamadan. His great work of philosophy is called the Book of Healing.
textes.Al-Ghazali attaque Avicenne et al-Farabi: Al-Ghazali attacks Avicenna and al-Farabi in The Incoherence of the Philosophers. Averroes replies with:
textes.Al-Ghazali, professeur à Bagdad à la fin: Al-Ghazali, a professor in Baghdad in the late 11th century, faulted the philosophers for following the Greeks where they contradict Islam. Around 1180, Averroes took up his arguments one by one to defend philosophy.
textes.Le livre d'al-Ghazali est écrit pendant: Al-Ghazali's book was written while he taught at the Nizamiyya of Baghdad, where he was appointed in 1091. It marks the rise of the Asharite school of theology.
textes.Maïmonide écrit le Guide des égarés vers: Maimonides writes the Guide for the Perplexed around 1190 to reconcile the Bible and Aristotle. He writes it in:
textes.Comme Averroès, Maïmonide est né à Cordo: Like Averroes, Maimonides was born in Córdoba. A Jewish philosopher writing in Arabic, he explains difficult biblical passages through reason.
textes.Le Guide, composé vers 1185-1190, est tr: The Guide, written around 1185-1190, was translated into Hebrew by Samuel ibn Tibbon in 1204, the year Maimonides died. Thomas Aquinas cites it in several of his works.
textes.Averroès, le grand commentateur d'Aristo: Averroes, Aristotle's great commentator, was also a judge (qadi) in Córdoba.
textes.Né à Cordoue en 1126, il est cadi à Sévi: Born in Córdoba in 1126, he was qadi in Seville, then chief qadi of Córdoba, and physician to the caliph. He died in Marrakesh in 1198.
textes.Dans la Divine Comédie, achevée en 1320,: In the Divine Comedy, completed in 1320, Dante places Averroes, "who made the Great Commentary", in Limbo, alongside the sages of Antiquity.
textes.En quelle année meurt Avicenne, à Hamada: In what year did Avicenna die, in Hamadan, Persia?
textes.En 1037, le 22 juin. Né vers 980 près de: In 1037, on 22 June. Born around 980 near Bukhara, he served several princes as physician and vizier, between flights and an imprisonment.
textes.Son nom latin, « Avicenne », déforme l'a: His Latin name, "Avicenna", distorts the Arabic Ibn Sina. His two great books, the Canon of Medicine and the Book of Healing, together cover nearly all the knowledge of his time.
textes.Hunayn ibn Ishaq, chef des traducteurs d: Hunayn ibn Ishaq, head of the Baghdad translators in the 9th century, was:
textes.Chrétien nestorien, médecin, Hunayn trad: A Nestorian Christian and a physician, Hunayn translated from Greek and Syriac into Arabic; 116 works are credited to him. Arabic-language philosophy was born of work by many hands and several faiths.
textes.Il porte le titre de « cheikh des traduc: He bore the title "sheikh of the translators". It was through these Arabic translations, retranslated into Latin from the 12th century, that Europe rediscovered much of Aristotle.
textes.Dans le Proslogion, Anselme définit Dieu: In the Proslogion, Anselm defines God as:
textes.ce dont on ne peut rien concevoir de plu: that than which nothing greater can be conceived
textes.C'est l'argument ontologique : si cet êt: This is the ontological argument: if such a being existed only in the mind, one could conceive a greater one that also existed in reality. So it must exist.
textes.Anselme écrit le Proslogion en 1077-1078: Anselm wrote the Proslogion in 1077-1078; he would become archbishop of Canterbury. The monk Gaunilo replied at once with a parody: an island "greater than which nothing can be conceived" would then have to exist too.
textes.Dans Sic et non (« Oui et non »), Pierre: In Sic et Non ("Yes and No"), Peter Abelard gathers:
textes.des citations d'autorités qui se contred: quotations from authorities that contradict each other
textes.Abélard met côte à côte des textes de la: Abelard sets side by side texts of the Bible and the Church Fathers that say opposite things: reason must decide. This is the spirit of scholasticism, the method of the schools.
textes.Professeur vedette à Paris, Abélard tomb: A star lecturer in Paris, Abelard fell in love with his pupil Héloïse; her uncle had him castrated. He tells his woes in the History of My Calamities.
textes.Dans la Somme théologique, Thomas d'Aqui: In the Summa Theologica, Thomas Aquinas offers, to prove God's existence:
textes.Les cinq voies partent du monde : le mou: The five ways start from the world: motion, cause, the possible and the necessary, degrees of perfection, the order of nature. The first takes up Aristotle's prime mover.
textes.La Somme est restée inachevée : vers la: The Summa was left unfinished: near the end of his life, after a mystical experience, Thomas reportedly said that all he had written seemed to him "like straw". He was canonized in 1323.
textes.Jeune étudiant silencieux, Thomas d'Aqui: As a silent young student, Thomas Aquinas is nicknamed by his fellows:
textes.Ses camarades le croyaient lent parce qu: His fellows thought him slow because he spoke little. His teacher Albertus Magnus is said to have predicted that this ox's bellowing would one day be heard throughout the world.
textes.Dominicain, Thomas enseigne deux fois à: A Dominican, Thomas taught twice at the University of Paris. The Church calls him the "Angelic Doctor".
textes.En 1277, l'évêque de Paris Étienne Tempi: In 1277, the bishop of Paris Étienne Tempier condemns:
textes.219 thèses, souvent inspirées d'Aristote: 219 theses, often inspired by Aristotle and Averroes
textes.L'évêque interdit d'enseigner des thèses: The bishop forbade teaching theses such as the eternity of the world, or the idea that God could not move the heavens in a straight line because it would leave a vacuum: that would limit his omnipotence.
textes.L'historien Pierre Duhem a soutenu que l: The historian Pierre Duhem argued that modern science was born in 1277, by freeing minds from Aristotle. Historians now qualify this, while granting that the condemnations opened up new possibilities.
textes.L'« âne de Buridan », placé à égale dist: "Buridan's ass", placed equally far from a bucket of water and a pile of hay, as hungry as it is thirsty:
textes.meurt de faim et de soif, faute de pouvo: dies of hunger and thirst, unable to choose
textes.Le paradoxe se moque d'une volonté qui n: The paradox mocks a will that would only follow the best motive: with equal motives, it would be paralysed. It bears the name of the 14th-century Parisian philosopher Jean Buridan.
textes.Buridan ne parle pourtant nulle part de: Yet Buridan nowhere discusses this donkey in his known writings. The idea goes back to Aristotle, who mentioned in On the Heavens a man as hungry as he is thirsty, between food and drink.
textes.Le mot « scolastique » vient du latin sc: The word "scholasticism" comes from the Latin schola, meaning:
textes.La scolastique est la philosophie enseig: Scholasticism is the philosophy taught in the schools, then in the universities springing up in Europe's great cities: read a text, ask a question, weigh pros and cons, conclude.
textes.La méthode oblige à exposer d'abord les: The method requires first setting out the arguments for a thesis, then those against it, before refuting the latter: each master must face the opposing view. Aquinas' Summa is built this way.
textes.En quelle année Thomas d'Aquin est-il pr: In what year was Thomas Aquinas declared a saint?
textes.En 1323, par le pape Jean XXII, près de: In 1323, by Pope John XXII, nearly fifty years after his death in 1274.
textes.L'année suivante, en 1324, le franciscai: The following year, in 1324, the Franciscan William of Ockham was summoned to the papal court in Avignon to answer for his theses.
textes.En 1486, le jeune Pic de la Mirandole pr: In 1486, young Pico della Mirandola offers to debate publicly in Rome:
textes.Ses thèses mêlent Platon, Aristote, les: His theses blend Plato, Aristotle, the Neoplatonists, Hermeticism and Jewish Kabbalah into a single whole. He even offered to pay the travel costs of scholars who would come to contradict him. The 95 theses are Luther's, in 1517.
textes.Le pape Innocent VIII fait arrêter le dé: Pope Innocent VIII had the debate halted in 1487; the 900 theses were condemned: the first time the Church banned a printed book.
textes.Le Discours sur la dignité de l'homme de: Pico della Mirandola's Oration on the Dignity of Man (1486) is often called:
textes.Pour Pic, Dieu a créé l'homme sans place: For Pico, God created man with no fixed place in the chain of being: through philosophy, he can rise towards the angels; if he fails to use his intellect, he vegetates like a plant.
textes.Pic meurt à 31 ans, en 1494. En 2007, l': Pico died at 31, in 1494. In 2007, analysis of his remains showed he had most likely been poisoned with arsenic.
textes.Pour Cosme de Médicis, Marsile Ficin réa: For Cosimo de' Medici, Marsilio Ficino accomplishes in Florence:
textes.la première traduction latine complète d: the first complete Latin translation of Plato
textes.Cosme lui confie en 1462 des manuscrits: Cosimo entrusted him with Greek manuscripts of Plato in 1462; the translation of the dialogues was finished around 1468-1469 and printed in 1484. Latin Europe, which read Aristotle, rediscovered Plato.
textes.Ficin dirige l'Académie platonicienne de: Ficino led the Platonic Academy of Florence, an attempt to revive Plato's Academy. It was he who coined, in 1476, the phrase "Platonic love".
textes.Dans son Discours de la servitude volont: In his Discourse on Voluntary Servitude, La Boétie argues that tyrants:
textes.ne tiennent que par le consentement de c: hold power only through the consent of those they oppress
textes.Il suffirait de cesser de servir pour qu: It would be enough to stop serving for the tyrant to fall: "Resolve to serve no more, and you are free." The Protestants would later use the text against the monarchy.
textes.La Boétie l'écrit vers 1548, à environ 1: La Boétie wrote it around 1548, aged about 18, while studying law. He met Montaigne in 1558 and died in 1563, aged 32.
textes.Interrogé sur son amitié avec La Boétie,: Asked about his friendship with La Boétie, Montaigne answers:
textes.« Parce que c'était lui, parce que c'éta: "Because it was he, because it was I"
textes.La phrase se trouve dans l'essai « De l': The phrase is in the essay "Of Friendship" (Essays, Book I, chapter 28). Montaigne gives up explaining a friendship that cannot be explained.
textes.Montaigne avait conçu ses Essais comme u: Montaigne had conceived his Essays as a setting for La Boétie's Discourse. When Protestants published it in 1574, he gave up including it, for fear of passing for a Calvinist.
textes.Érasme publie en 1516 un ouvrage qui ser: In 1516, Erasmus publishes a work that would serve the translators of the Reformation:
textes.une édition du Nouveau Testament en grec: an edition of the New Testament in Greek
textes.Érasme revient au texte grec, avec une n: Erasmus went back to the Greek text, with a new Latin translation and notes: one must read the sources, not just their commentaries. That is the very approach of humanism.
textes.Érasme a écrit l'Éloge de la folie chez: Erasmus wrote In Praise of Folly at his friend Thomas More's London home, in about a week, by his own account; the Latin title, Moriae encomium, can also be read "In Praise of More".
textes.Dans le Novum Organum (1620), Francis Ba: In the Novum Organum (1620), Francis Bacon calls "idols":
textes.les sources d'erreur qui faussent notre: the sources of error that distort our judgement
textes.les statues des dieux grecs: the statues of the Greek gods
textes.Bacon en distingue quatre : de la tribu: Bacon distinguishes four: of the tribe (flaws of human nature), of the cave (each person's own), of the marketplace (ill-defined words) and of the theatre (inherited philosophical systems).
textes.Le titre répond à l'Organon d'Aristote,: The title answers Aristotle's Organon, the collection of his logical treatises: Bacon wanted to replace the syllogism with induction, which rises from observations to laws.
textes.Le frontispice du Léviathan de Hobbes (1: The frontispiece of Hobbes's Leviathan (1651) shows a giant sovereign whose body is made of:
textes.de centaines de petits personnages, ses: hundreds of tiny figures, his subjects
textes.L'image dit l'idée du livre : chacun ren: The image states the book's idea: each person gives up governing himself in favour of a sovereign, provided the others do likewise. The State is an artificial body made of everyone.
textes.La gravure est d'Abraham Bosse, réalisée: The engraving is by Abraham Bosse, made after long discussions with Hobbes: the giant's torso holds more than three hundred figures, all seen from behind. The book was written during the English Civil War.
textes.En 1656, la communauté juive portugaise: In 1656, the Portuguese Jewish community of Amsterdam pronounces against the young Spinoza:
textes.Le texte du herem, daté du 27 juillet 16: The herem text, dated 27 July 1656, is the harshest ever pronounced in the community. Spinoza then earned his living by grinding lenses for spectacles, telescopes and microscopes.
textes.Son Éthique, « démontrée selon l'ordre g: His Ethics, "demonstrated in geometrical order", appeared only after his death, in 1677, published by his friends.
textes.Descartes meurt en 1650 à Stockholm, où: Descartes dies in 1650 in Stockholm, where he had come:
textes.à l'invitation de la reine Christine de: at the invitation of Queen Christina of Sweden
textes.comme ambassadeur du roi de France: as ambassador of the King of France
textes.La reine l'avait invité en 1649 pour fon: The queen had invited him in 1649 to found an academy and give her lessons. He died on 11 February 1650, of pneumonia according to the most common account.
textes.Descartes avait passé plus de vingt ans: Descartes had spent over twenty years in the Dutch Republic, where he wrote all his major works. His Meditations on First Philosophy appeared in Latin in 1641.
textes.Leibniz soutient dans sa Théodicée (1710: In his Theodicy (1710), Leibniz holds that our world is:
textes.le meilleur des mondes possibles: the best of all possible worlds
textes.le pire des mondes possibles: the worst of all possible worlds
textes.Dieu, parfait, a choisi parmi tous les m: God, being perfect, chose the best of all possible worlds: the evil found in it is the price of the greatest overall good.
textes.Voltaire s'en moque dans Candide (1759): Voltaire mocked it in Candide (1759) through Dr Pangloss, who keeps repeating that "all is for the best" while disasters rain down on him.
textes.En quelle année paraît le Léviathan de T: In what year was Thomas Hobbes's Leviathan published?
textes.En 1651. Hobbes y décrit la vie sans Éta: In 1651. In it, Hobbes describes life without a State as "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short".
textes.Le titre renvoie au Léviathan du livre d: The title refers to the Leviathan of the Book of Job, a biblical sea monster: a title chosen to provoke.
textes.En 1751, trois ans après sa parution, L': In 1751, three years after publication, Montesquieu's The Spirit of the Laws is:
textes.mis à l'Index par l'Église catholique: put on the Index by the Catholic Church
textes.Le livre, publié anonymement à Genève en: The book, published anonymously in Geneva in 1748, joined the Index of forbidden books. It nonetheless inspired the American revolutionaries, who drew the separation of powers from it.
textes.Publier sans nom d'auteur était alors l': Publishing without an author's name was then the custom for daring books; Montesquieu built on John Locke, who had already distinguished several powers in the State.
textes.Candide, de Voltaire (1759), se termine: Voltaire's Candide (1759) ends with the line:
textes.Après mille malheurs, Candide renonce au: After a thousand misfortunes, Candide gives up Pangloss's grand optimistic theories: rather than talk about the best of worlds, let us work.
textes.Le tremblement de terre de Lisbonne, en: The Lisbon earthquake of 1755, followed by a tsunami and fires, had shaken optimism; Voltaire used it in Candide against Leibniz. The book appeared in January 1759, in several countries at once.
textes.Émilie du Châtelet laisse en mourant, en: Émilie du Châtelet leaves at her death, in 1749, a translation that is still the standard:
textes.Mathématicienne et physicienne, elle tra: A mathematician and physicist, she translated and annotated Newton's work. Her version, published in 1756 and in full in 1759, remains the only complete French translation of the Principia.
textes.Compagne et collaboratrice de Voltaire,: Voltaire's companion and collaborator, she worked with him at the château of Cirey, in Champagne, which became a centre for the study of science.
textes.En 1749, Diderot est enfermé au donjon d: In 1749, Diderot is locked up in the keep of Vincennes for:
textes.sa Lettre sur les aveugles, jugée impie: his Letter on the Blind, judged impious
textes.Parue anonymement en juin 1749, la Lettr: Published anonymously in June 1749, the Letter on the Blind casts doubt on a creator God. The author was quickly identified, and imprisoned until November.
textes.Diderot dirige ensuite l'Encyclopédie av: Diderot then ran the Encyclopédie with d'Alembert, then alone after 1759. In 1766, Catherine II of Russia bought his library and left him its use, with a librarian's salary.
textes.Kant compare sa Critique de la raison pu: Kant compares his Critique of Pure Reason (1781) to a revolution:
textes.Au lieu de supposer que notre connaissan: Instead of assuming that our knowledge conforms to objects, Kant proposes that objects conform to the forms of our knowledge, as Copernicus had made the observer turn rather than the stars.
textes.La comparaison apparaît dans la préface: The comparison appears in the preface to the second edition, in 1787. Kant acknowledges his debt to Hume, who had "interrupted his dogmatic slumber".
textes.En quelle année paraît la première éditi: In what year was the first edition of Kant's Critique of Pure Reason published?
textes.En 1781 ; Kant en donne une seconde édit: In 1781; Kant issued a revised second edition in 1787. He was then 57 and teaching in Königsberg.
textes.La Critique cherche ce que la raison peu: The Critique asks what reason can know without experience, and where it goes astray: God, the soul or the beginning of the world lie beyond any proof.
textes.{comp}. Socrate posait des questions jus: {comp}. Socrates asked questions until people admitted they knew nothing. Your turn.
textes.Philosophie. Kant n'a presque jamais qui: Philosophy. Kant hardly ever left Königsberg. You won't leave this trial without {comp}.
textes.Diogène cherchait un homme en plein jour: Diogenes looked for a man in broad daylight with a lantern. I'm looking for a right answer. {comp}.
textes.Juste. Descartes doutait de tout. Moi, j: Right. Descartes doubted everything. I doubt you less and less.
textes.Bonne réponse. Ockham vous félicite, san: Correct. Ockham congratulates you, with no superfluous entities.
textes.Correct. Montaigne aurait écrit un essai: Correct. Montaigne would have written an essay about you. A short one.
textes.Sage réponse. Je vais devoir trouver une: A wise answer. I'll have to find a deeper taunt.
textes.Raté. Socrate disait savoir qu'il ne sav: Missed. Socrates said he knew that he knew nothing. You're proving it.
textes.Faux. Diogène se roulait dans le sable b: Wrong. Diogenes rolled in hot sand to toughen himself. I'll let you roll in your error.
textes.Erreur. Thalès, dit-on, mesurait les pyr: Error. Thales, they say, measured the pyramids by their shadow. You didn't see yours coming.
textes.La caverne de Platon vous va bien. Reste: Plato's cave suits you. Stay there for a review.
textes.Précepteur d'Alexandre, il a écrit sur l: Tutor to Alexander, he wrote on logic, physics, biology, politics and rhetoric. He thought women had fewer teeth than men. Bertrand Russell was amused that he never thought to check in his two wives' mouths.
textes.Il enseigne la morale, les rites et l'ar: He taught morality, rites and the art of governing by example. His disciples collected his sayings in the Analects. “What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others” appears there, five centuries before the Gospels.
textes.Juge et médecin à Cordoue, il commente A: A judge and physician in Córdoba, he commented on Aristotle so completely that the Latins simply called him “the Commentator”. For him, philosophy and religion, properly interpreted, cannot contradict each other. Exiled, his books burned, he was rehabilitated shortly before his death.
textes.Diplomate, juge et historien né à Tunis,: A diplomat, judge and historian born in Tunis, he wrote the Muqaddimah in 1377, an introduction to history. In it he seeks the laws of the rise and fall of dynasties: a group's solidarity carries it to power, then luxury wears it down in three or four generations.
textes.En 1929, à 21 ans, elle est reçue deuxiè: In 1929, at 21, she placed second in the philosophy agrégation, the youngest of her year. Sartre came first, on his second attempt; the jury hesitated to swap them. Twenty years later, The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.”
textes.Pour lui, l'esprit et le corps sont deux: For him, mind and body are two distinct substances, which communicate through the pineal gland, in the middle of the brain. The question of their union has occupied philosophers ever since. His body rests in Saint-Germain-des-Prés; a skull presented as his is kept at the National Museum of Natural History.
textes.Pour lui, une théorie n'est scientifique: For him, a theory is only scientific if you can imagine the observation that would refute it. Astrology, which can accommodate anything, fails the test. In 1946 in Cambridge, Wittgenstein reportedly threatened him with a poker during a debate; the witnesses still disagree about what happened.
textes.Diogène vivait dans un pithos, une jarre: Diogenes lived in a pithos, an earthenware jar. Alexander the Great supposedly asked him what he wanted; he supposedly replied: “Stand out of my sunlight.”
textes.Le mythe d'un Moyen Âge persuadé que la: The myth of a Middle Ages convinced the Earth was flat owes much to Washington Irving's fictionalized biography of Columbus, in 1828. Medieval scholars opposed Columbus over the size of the Earth, and they were right: he had underestimated it.
textes.« Je désapprouve ce que vous dites, mais: “I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it” is by Evelyn Beatrice Hall, in The Friends of Voltaire (1906). She was summing up Voltaire's thinking, and had to clarify it herself in 1939.
textes.Maîtriser les philosophes modernes. Votr: Master the modern philosophers. Your achievement is provisional, like any scientific theory.
textes.Le critère de la scientificité d'une thé: The criterion of the scientific status of a theory is its falsifiability, or refutability, or testability.
Master the first diamond of Wisdom. You now know that you know nothing, but with references.
I know that I know nothing.
textes.Réussir 3 quiz de Sagesse sans faute. Vo: Pass 3 Wisdom quizzes without a mistake. You finally see the objects, not their shadows.
textes.Platon place l'allégorie de la caverne a: Plato places the allegory of the cave in Book VII of the Republic. According to tradition, he had “Let no one ignorant of geometry enter here” inscribed over the door of the Academy. The phrase is only attested nearly nine centuries later.
textes.Maîtriser 9 compétences. L'arbre de la P: Master 9 skills. The Philosophy tree opens.
textes.Une vie sans examen ne vaut pas d'être v: The unexamined life is not worth living.
textes.Maîtriser l'éthique. Vous pouvez tirer l: Master ethics. You can pull the lever or do nothing. The AI has already chosen.
textes.Le dilemme du tramway, qui fonce sur cin: The trolley dilemma, hurtling toward five people unless you throw a switch toward just one, was posed in 1967 by the philosopher Philippa Foot, in a paper on abortion. The name “trolley problem” comes from Judith Jarvis Thomson, in 1976.
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie politique. La f: Master political philosophy. The end doesn't justify made-up quotes.
textes.« La fin justifie les moyens » ne figure: “The end justifies the means” appears nowhere in Machiavelli. In The Prince, he writes that in politics, with no court to appeal to, a prince is judged by his results. The more brutal phrase is a summary by his opponents.
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie de l'esprit. Vo: Master the philosophy of mind. Your cells change, so do your memories. Are you still you?
textes.Selon Plutarque, les Athéniens remplaçai: According to Plutarch, the Athenians replaced the rotten planks of Theseus's ship one by one: was it still the same ship? Hobbes, in 1655, sharpens the question: if someone rebuilds a ship from the old planks, which of the two is the real one?
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie des sciences. C: Master the philosophy of science. Shift your paradigm. Which one? Take your pick.
textes.Thomas Kuhn popularise en 1962 le mot «: Thomas Kuhn popularized the word “paradigm” in 1962. In 1970, the philosopher Margaret Masterman found twenty-one different senses of the word in his book. Kuhn acknowledged it, and came to prefer “disciplinary matrix”.
textes.Maîtriser les sagesses hellénistiques. L: Master Hellenistic wisdom. The AI gives you back your jar.
textes.Maîtriser la scolastique. Christophe Col: Master scholasticism. Christopher Columbus convinced nobody the Earth was round: everybody knew.
textes.Maîtriser les Lumières. L'IA désapprouve: Master the Enlightenment. The AI disapproves of your quotes, but lets you say them.
textes.Maîtriser les présocratiques. Empédocle: Master the Pre-Socratics. Empedocles left a sandal; you, at least, leave answers.
textes.D'après Diogène Laërce, Empédocle se ser: According to Diogenes Laërtius, Empedocles threw himself into Etna so that people would think he had become a god. The volcano threw back one of his bronze sandals, giving the trick away.
textes.Maîtriser les sagesses d'Asie. La mère d: Master the wisdom of Asia. Mencius' mother would have moved fewer times for you.
textes.Selon les Biographies des femmes exempla: According to Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women, Mencius' mother lived near a cemetery, where the child imitated burials, then near a market, where he imitated the merchants. She finally settled near a school: he began to study.
textes.Maîtriser Socrate et Platon. Aristophane: Master Socrates and Plato. Aristophanes would have hung you in a basket too.
textes.Dans Les Nuées, jouée en 423 av. J.-C.,: In The Clouds, staged in 423 BC, Aristophanes shows Socrates hanging in a basket to observe the sky better. The play came last in the contest; yet Plato cites it among the causes of Socrates' trial.
textes.Maîtriser Aristote. Une compétence ne fa: Master Aristotle. One skill does not make a spring, but it's a start.
textes.Pour Aristote, le bonheur se juge sur un: For Aristotle, happiness is judged over a whole life: "one swallow does not make a spring". The phrase comes from the Nicomachean Ethics.
textes.Maîtriser les philosophes de Rome. Notez: Master the philosophers of Rome. Write it down for yourself alone; the AI will read over your shoulder.
textes.Marc Aurèle n'a pas donné de titre à ses: Marcus Aurelius gave his Meditations no title: the manuscript reads "To himself". It is unlikely he meant to publish them.
textes.Maîtriser les philosophes de l'Islam. Ap: Master the philosophers of Islam. After Aristotle and al-Farabi, the AI grants you third place.
textes.Al-Farabi était appelé le « second maîtr: Al-Farabi was called the "Second Master", after Aristotle. Avicenna said he did not properly understand Aristotle's Metaphysics until he had read an introduction by al-Farabi.
textes.Maîtriser la Renaissance. Pic de la Mira: Master the Renaissance. Pico della Mirandola defended nine hundred; you, a few.
textes.En 1486, à 23 ans, Pic de la Mirandole p: In 1486, aged 23, Pico della Mirandola offered to defend 900 theses in Rome and to pay the travel of anyone who came to debate them. The pope suspended the debate; the book became the first printed book banned everywhere by the Church.
textes.Maîtriser l'âge classique. Personne ne v: Master the classical age. Nobody has summoned you at five in the morning. Not yet.
textes.En 1649, la reine Christine de Suède fai: In 1649, Queen Christina of Sweden brought Descartes to Stockholm in midwinter and asked for lessons three times a week, at five in the morning. He contracted pneumonia and died on 11 February 1650.
textes.La méthode scientifique, la cellule, l'é: The scientific method, the cell, evolution and genetics.
textes.Les plus anciennes traces de feu contrôl: The oldest traces of controlled fire are about a million years old (Wonderwerk Cave, in South Africa), but its regular use became widespread some 400,000 years ago. Cooking food makes it easier to digest: the anthropologist Richard Wrangham even sees it as a driver of the growth of our brain.
