Genetics was born, thirty-five years late.
textes.Dominant, récessif et le tableau des qua: Dominant, recessive and the four-square table
textes.Dominant : s'exprime avec une seule copi: Dominant: shows with one copy; recessive: with two. Aa × Aa → a quarter aa. Dominant ≠ common.
textes.Un gène existe en plusieurs versions, le: A gene comes in several versions, alleles. The dominant allele, written A, shows as soon as it is present; the recessive allele, a, only in two copies. A person who is Aa therefore carries the recessive trait without showing it, and can pass it on: it sometimes stays hidden for several generations.
textes.A avec T, G avec C. Double hélice : Wats: A with T, G with C. Double helix: Watson and Crick (1953), thanks to Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51.
textes.L'ADN s'écrit avec quatre lettres, les b: DNA is written with four letters, the bases A, T, G and C, and these letters always pair the same way: A with T, G with C. One strand is therefore enough to rebuild the other, and that is how the cell copies its DNA. The human genome has about 3 billion base pairs, and only about 20,000 protein-coding genes, far fewer than the 100,000 expected.
textes.En 1953, James Watson et Francis Crick p: In 1953 James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix structure. They relied on Photo 51, an X-ray diffraction image taken in Rosalind Franklin's laboratory, without her knowledge. She died in 1958 and did not share the 1962 Nobel Prize. Today the CRISPR-Cas9 tool can correct this writing at a precise spot.
textes.Circulation en circuit fermé (Harvey, 16: Closed-circuit circulation (Harvey, 1628). Right heart → lungs; left heart → body. Blood is never blue.
textes.Pendant quatorze siècles, on a suivi Gal: For fourteen centuries people followed Galen: the liver made blood from food, and the body used it up. In 1628 William Harvey did a simple calculation, with deliberately low estimates: in one day the heart pumps far more than the body's weight. The liver cannot produce that. Blood must therefore go round in a closed circuit.
textes.Le cœur est une double pompe. La partie: The heart is a double pump. The right side sends blood to the lungs, the pulmonary circulation, where it picks up oxygen in about 70 m² of alveoli. The left side sends it round the whole body, the systemic circulation. And blood is never blue: it is dark red in the veins; it is the skin that makes them look blue.
textes.Bouche → estomac → intestin grêle (absor: Mouth → stomach → small intestine (absorption). Bile from the liver for fats. Kidneys: 180 L filtered a day.
textes.La digestion commence dans la bouche, où: Digestion begins in the mouth, where saliva already attacks starch. The stomach churns and acidifies. The liver makes bile, stored in the gallbladder, which helps digest fats. Most absorption then takes place in the small intestine, whose folded wall offers a very large surface.
textes.Les reins font le tri : ils filtrent env: The kidneys do the sorting: they filter about 180 litres of blood a day and pass only a small part of it as urine. The pancreas produces insulin, which lets sugar into the cells; its discovery in 1921 by Banting and Best transformed the lives of diabetics.
textes.Vésale (1543) corrige Galien en disséqua: Vesalius (1543) corrects Galen by dissecting humans. 206 adult bones, 4.5 to 6 L of blood. The 10 % myth is false.
textes.Galien avait surtout disséqué des animau: Galen had mostly dissected animals, notably macaques, and drawn from them a human anatomy full of mistakes that nobody dared contradict. In 1543 Andreas Vesalius published the Fabrica, illustrated with magnificent plates. He dissected human bodies, which was rare, and corrected Galen on many points: the lower jaw is a single bone, not two; the wall between the ventricles has no hole.
textes.Quelques chiffres de ce corps enfin rega: A few figures from this body finally looked at: 206 bones in an adult, about 300 in a newborn, which fuse as it grows; 4.5 to 6 litres of blood; a heart that beats 60 to 100 times a minute at rest. And no, we do not use only 10 % of our brain: imaging shows every area is used.
textes.Bactéries et virus, deux ennemis différe: Bacteria and viruses, two different enemies
textes.Bactérie = cellule vivante ; virus = par: Bacterium = living cell; virus = cell parasite. Antibiotics: bacteria only (Fleming, 1928).
textes.Une bactérie est une cellule vivante, qu: A bacterium is a living cell that feeds and divides on its own. A virus is just a genetic message in a shell: it has to get into a cell and hijack its machinery to copy itself. That difference decides the treatment.
textes.Les antibiotiques attaquent des mécanism: Antibiotics attack mechanisms specific to bacteria; against a virus, a cold or flu, they do nothing. In September 1928 Alexander Fleming came back from holiday and found a culture dish overrun by a mould, Penicillium, around which the bacteria had died: that was penicillin. In his Nobel lecture in 1945 he was already warning: misused, it would make microbes resistant.
textes.Vaccin = entraînement du système immunit: Vaccine = training the immune system, which keeps a memory (Jenner, 1796). Smallpox eradicated in 1980.
textes.En 1796, Edward Jenner inocule à un garç: In 1796 Edward Jenner inoculated a boy, James Phipps, with pus from cowpox, a mild disease of cows, then exposed him to smallpox: he did not fall ill. The word vaccine comes from this, from the Latin vacca, cow. Before him, people practised variolation, a risky inoculation with smallpox itself.
textes.Le principe : présenter au système immun: The principle: show the immune system a fragment or a harmless version of the microbe. It makes antibodies and keeps a memory, which lets it react fast at the real encounter. When enough people are immune, the microbe stops circulating and protects those who cannot be vaccinated. Smallpox, declared eradicated by the WHO in 1980, remains the only human disease beaten this way.
textes.Les antibiotiques sélectionnent les bact: Antibiotics select resistant bacteria. No antibiotic against a virus.
textes.Une bactérie se divise parfois toutes le: A bacterium sometimes divides every twenty minutes. In an infection there are billions, and a few carry by chance a mutation that makes them resistant to an antibiotic. The treatment kills the others; the resistant ones survive and multiply. That is natural selection, before our eyes.
textes.Producteurs → consommateurs → décomposeu: Producers → consumers → decomposers. About 10 % of the energy passes from one link to the next (Lindeman, 1942).
textes.Une chaîne alimentaire part des producte: A food chain starts with the producers, plants and algae, which build their matter from light, water and CO₂. Then come the consumers, herbivores then carnivores, and finally the decomposers, fungi and bacteria, which return dead matter to the soil. Without them the cycles would stop.
textes.À chaque maillon, la plus grande partie: At each link, most of the energy is lost, mainly through respiration: roughly only 10 % passes to the next level. This 10 % rule comes from Raymond Lindeman, in 1942. That is why it takes a lot of grass to feed a few gazelles, and a lot of gazelles for one lion: large predators are bound to be rare.
textes.La matière se recycle, l'énergie vient d: Matter is recycled; energy comes from the Sun and dissipates. Natural greenhouse effect, strengthened by our emissions (Arrhenius, 1896).
textes.La matière circule en cycles : le carbon: Matter moves in cycles: carbon goes from the air to plants, animals, soil, oceans, and back. Water evaporates, falls, runs off. Energy does not go round: it arrives from the Sun and ends up dissipated as heat.
textes.L'effet de serre est naturel et vital :: The greenhouse effect is natural and vital: without it the Earth would be frozen. But the CO₂ we emit reinforces it. Svante Arrhenius calculated its effect as early as 1896. The oceans absorb about a quarter of our CO₂ emissions, which acidifies them, and overheated corals expel the algae that feed them: they bleach.
textes.L'espèce qui tient tout: The species that holds it all
textes.Espèce clé de voûte : son retrait boulev: Keystone species: removing it upsets the ecosystem (Paine, 1969). Yellowstone wolves, 1995: trophic cascade.
textes.Certaines espèces pèsent bien plus que l: Some species weigh far more than their numbers. In the 1960s, on the coast of Washington State, the ecologist Robert Paine removed the starfish Pisaster from a stretch of shore: mussels, freed from their predator, took over everything, and the rock pools went from 15 species to 8 in three years. In 1969 he coined the term keystone species.
textes.Le loup de Yellowstone, réintroduit en 1: The Yellowstone wolf, reintroduced in 1995, is the famous example: by keeping elk in check, it is said to have let willows and aspens grow back along the rivers. That is a trophic cascade, although its real extent is still debated. Conversely, an invasive species, like the rabbit in Australia, can throw everything off balance.
textes.PCR : chauffer, refroidir, recopier ; ch: PCR: heat, cool, copy; each cycle doubles the DNA (30 cycles ≈ 1 billion). Mullis, 1983.
textes.La PCR copie un fragment d'ADN des milli: PCR copies a piece of DNA billions of times. Each cycle heats the DNA to around 95 °C to separate its two strands, cools it so that small primers attach, then lets an enzyme rebuild the missing strands at around 72 °C. Each cycle doubles the number of copies: after 30 cycles, a single molecule has produced over a billion.
textes.L'astuce : une enzyme qui résiste à la c: The trick: a heat-resistant enzyme, Taq polymerase, taken from a hot-spring bacterium, Thermus aquaticus, notably from Yellowstone. Kary Mullis invented the method in 1983 and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. Diagnostic tests, criminal investigations, ancient DNA: it is everywhere.
textes.CRISPR-Cas9 : un ARN guide mène Cas9 cou: CRISPR-Cas9: a guide RNA leads Cas9 to cut DNA at a precise spot (Charpentier and Doudna, 2012; Nobel 2020).
textes.Les bactéries gardent en mémoire des mor: Bacteria keep pieces of DNA from viruses that have attacked them, so they can recognise and cut them up at the next attack. In 2012 Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna turned this system into a tool: a guide RNA leads the Cas9 enzyme to a chosen sequence, where it cuts the DNA.
textes.C'est un ciseau programmable, bien plus: It is programmable scissors, far simpler and cheaper than earlier methods. They received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020. This is not biologists' first ethical debate: as early as 1975, at Asilomar, they imposed a moratorium on themselves for the first genetic manipulations.
textes.Le vaccin qui donne une recette: The vaccine that hands over a recipe
textes.Vaccin à ARN : une recette de protéine,: mRNA vaccine: a protein recipe, read outside the nucleus, broken down within days. Does not alter DNA (Karikó and Weissman, Nobel 2023).
textes.Un vaccin à ARN messager ne contient pas: An mRNA vaccine does not contain the virus, but the recipe for one of its proteins. Cells read this message, make the protein, and the immune system learns to recognise it. The RNA stays outside the nucleus, where the DNA is, and breaks down within a few days: it does not alter the genome.
textes.Cette technique n'est pas née avec la co: This technique was not born with covid-19. Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman found in the 2000s how to make injected RNA less inflammatory; they received the Nobel Prize in 2023. Another milestone: since 1982, insulin for diabetics has been produced by genetically modified bacteria, no longer extracted from animal pancreases.
textes.Un malade prend un remède et guérit. Le: A patient takes a remedy and gets better. Did the remedy work? Impossible to say: they might have recovered on their own. To find out, you compare two similar groups, drawn by lot: one gets the treatment, the other a placebo, a pill with no active ingredient. Only the difference between the two counts. The ancestor of these trials dates from 20 May 1747: aboard HMS Salisbury, the Scottish doctor James Lind split twelve sailors with scurvy across six treatments. The two given oranges and lemons were almost recovered by the end of the month.
textes.En double aveugle, ni les patients ni le: In a double-blind trial, neither patients nor doctors know who receives what, so that their expectations do not skew the result. Random allocation took hold with the British streptomycin trial against tuberculosis, published in 1948, where the statistician Austin Bradford Hill had it adopted. And a result only really counts when other teams find it again: that is reproducibility. Even a peer-reviewed article can be corrected or retracted later.
textes.Le noyau garde l'ADN, la recette de tout: The nucleus keeps the DNA, the recipe for every protein. To make a protein, the cell copies the gene it needs into messenger RNA, which leaves the nucleus. Ribosomes read this message three letters at a time and assemble the amino acids in the right order. This one-way flow, from DNA to RNA to protein, was called the "central dogma" of molecular biology by Francis Crick in 1958; he returned to it in 1970 in Nature.
textes.Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck pensait que les: Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck thought organs change through use and that those changes are passed on: the giraffe would have lengthened its neck by stretching it, and bequeathed it to its young. He set it out in 1809 in his Zoological Philosophy, one of the first scientific theories of evolution. That is wrong: a muscular blacksmith does not have more muscular children. What you acquire in your life is not written into your genes.
textes.Deux parents Aa : chacun transmet A ou a: Two Aa parents: each passes on A or a, at random. The table gives AA, Aa, aA and aa. This grid bears the name of the English geneticist Reginald Punnett, who devised it around 1905, shortly after Mendel's work was rediscovered in 1900. On average one child in four is aa and shows the recessive trait. Careful: dominant does not mean common. Polydactyly, having extra fingers, is dominant and yet rare.
textes.D'où les règles : ne pas prendre d'antib: Hence the rules: do not take antibiotics against a virus, and finish the prescribed course, so as not to let the toughest bacteria survive. Alexander Fleming, who had discovered penicillin in 1928, was already warning in 1945, in his Nobel lecture: he feared that "the ignorant man" would underdose himself. Fever is not the enemy: it hinders the growth of some microbes and activates the defences.
textes.L'ancêtre de ces essais date du 20 mai 1: The ancestor of these trials dates from 20 May 1747: aboard HMS Salisbury, the Scottish doctor James Lind split twelve sailors with scurvy across six treatments.
textes.Le tirage au sort, lui, s'impose avec l': Random allocation took hold with the British streptomycin trial against tuberculosis, published in 1948, where the statistician Austin Bradford Hill had it adopted.
textes.En 1847, à l'hôpital général de Vienne,: In 1847, at the Vienna General Hospital, Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women delivered by doctors died of childbed fever far more often than those delivered by midwives.
textes.En 1665, Robert Hooke regarde une fine t: In 1665 Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of cork under the microscope and saw little chambers: he called them cells.
textes.Tiktaalik, découvert en 2004, montre une: Tiktaalik, discovered in 2004, shows a transitional form between fish and four-legged animals.
textes.De 1856 à 1863, dans le jardin de son ab: From 1856 to 1863, in the garden of his abbey in Brno, the monk Gregor Mendel crossed about 28,000 plants, mostly peas.
textes.En 1900, trois botanistes, Hugo de Vries: In 1900 three botanists, Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak, rediscovered his laws independently.
textes.En 1953, James Watson et Francis Crick p: In 1953 James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix structure.
textes.En 1628, William Harvey fait un calcul s: In 1628 William Harvey did a simple calculation, with deliberately low estimates: in one day the heart pumps far more than the body's weight.
textes.En 1543, André Vésale publie la Fabrica,: In 1543 Andreas Vesalius published the Fabrica, illustrated with magnificent plates.
textes.En septembre 1928, Alexander Fleming rev: In September 1928 Alexander Fleming came back from holiday and found a culture dish overrun by a mould, Penicillium, around which the bacteria had died: that was penicillin.
textes.En 1796, Edward Jenner inocule à un garç: In 1796 Edward Jenner inoculated a boy, James Phipps, with pus from cowpox, a mild disease of cows, then exposed him to smallpox: he did not fall ill.
textes.La variole, déclarée éradiquée par l'OMS: Smallpox, declared eradicated by the WHO in 1980, remains the only human disease beaten this way.
textes.Alexander Fleming, qui avait découvert l: Alexander Fleming, who had discovered penicillin in 1928, was already warning in 1945, in his Nobel lecture: he feared that "the ignorant man" would underdose himself.
textes.Cette règle des 10 % vient de Raymond Li: This 10 % rule comes from Raymond Lindeman, in 1942.
textes.Dans les années 1960, sur la côte de l'É: In the 1960s, on the coast of Washington State, the ecologist Robert Paine removed the starfish Pisaster from a stretch of shore: mussels, freed from their predator, took over everything, and the rock pools went from 15 species to 8 in three years.
textes.Le loup de Yellowstone, réintroduit en 1: The Yellowstone wolf, reintroduced in 1995, is the famous example: by keeping elk in check, it is said to have let willows and aspens grow back along the rivers.
textes.En 2012, Emmanuelle Charpentier et Jenni: In 2012 Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna turned this system into a tool: a guide RNA leads the Cas9 enzyme to a chosen sequence, where it cuts the DNA.
textes.Les biologistes n'en sont pas à leur pre: This is not biologists' first ethical debate: as early as 1975, at Asilomar, they imposed a moratorium on themselves for the first genetic manipulations.
textes.Un Néandertal soigné par les siens, des: A Neanderthal cared for by his kin, skulls drilled and healed, a tattooed iceman: medicine is older than writing.
textes.À Shanidar, en Irak, un Néandertal au br: At Shanidar, in Iraq, a Neanderthal with a broken, withered right arm survived his injuries for a long time: others must have helped him.
textes.La trépanation, percer le crâne d'un viv: Trepanation, drilling the skull of a living person, goes back 7,000 to 10,000 years; it is perhaps the oldest attested surgery.
textes.Sur un site funéraire français de 6500 a: At a French burial site from 6500 BC, 40 skulls out of 120 bear a trepanation hole; many show bone that healed.
Ötzi, who died in the Alps around 3200 BC, bears 61 tattoos, perhaps linked to joint pain, and a medicinal fungus.
textes.Un trou dans un crâne n'est pas forcémen: A hole in a skull is not necessarily a successful operation: only healed edges prove that the patient survived.
textes.Le Néandertal qu'on a soigné: The Neanderthal who was cared for
textes.Dans la grotte de Shanidar, au Kurdistan: In Shanidar Cave, in Iraqi Kurdistan, Ralph Solecki unearthed between 1957 and 1961 the remains of nine Neanderthals, 65,000 to 35,000 years old. One of them, Shanidar 1, had a withered right arm, fractured in several places; he lost the forearm and hand.
textes.Pourtant ses blessures ont cicatrisé : i: Yet his injuries healed: he lived with them for a long time. For the palaeoanthropologist Erik Trinkaus, he must have been helped by others. It is one of the oldest clues of care: long before doctors, relatives feeding and protecting an injured man.
textes.Shanidar 1 a survécu longtemps à des ble: Shanidar 1 survived serious injuries for a long time: someone helped him.
textes.La trépanation consiste à percer un trou: Trepanation means drilling a hole in the skull of a living person. It goes back 7,000 to 10,000 years, and it is perhaps the oldest surgery archaeology has traces of. At a French burial site from 6500 BC, 40 skulls out of 120 bear its mark.
textes.On en a trouvé plus de 1 500 du Néolithi: More than 1,500 have been found from the Neolithic, in Europe, Siberia, China and the Americas; in Peru, the Incas still practised it. The edges of the holes prove it: on 70% of the skulls, the bone healed and the patient survived. Why? To treat a head wound, epilepsy, or to drive out an evil spirit.
textes.Trépanation : 7 000 à 10 000 ans, sur to: Trepanation: 7,000 to 10,000 years old, on every continent; 70% of skulls healed.
textes.Le 19 septembre 1991, des randonneurs tr: On 19 September 1991, hikers found in the Ötztal Alps a body mummified by the ice: Ötzi, who died more than 5,000 years ago, in the 4th millennium BC. An arrow had shattered his shoulder blade; he bled to death.
textes.Il porte 61 tatouages, de petits traits: He bears 61 tattoos, small lines often near the knees and ankles, where his joints were worn: perhaps a treatment for pain. In his kit, a birch polypore, a fungus with deworming properties. And his gut did host whipworms, parasitic worms.
textes.Ötzi : 61 tatouages près des articulatio: Ötzi: 61 tattoos near worn joints, a deworming fungus, and worms in his gut.
textes.Des papyrus qui trient les blessures, de: Papyri that sort injuries, recipes by the hundred, specialists for eyes and teeth: Egypt heals in writing.
textes.Edwin Smith l'achète à Louxor: Edwin Smith buys it in Luxor
textes.Hesy-Ra, chef des dentistes du roi Djése: Hesy-Ra, chief of dentists to King Djoser, is the oldest physician known by name.
The Edwin Smith papyrus, around 1600 BC, describes 48 injury cases from head to foot and gives each a verdict: treat, contend, or give up.
textes.Le papyrus Ebers, vers 1550 av. J.-C., l: The Ebers papyrus, around 1550 BC, 20 metres long, gathers over 800 remedies.
textes.Selon Hérodote, les médecins égyptiens é: According to Herodotus, Egyptian doctors were highly specialised: eyes, teeth, internal diseases.
textes.Merit-Ptah, « première femme médecin »,: Merit-Ptah, "the first woman doctor", never existed: she is a confusion born in a 1937 book. The real one was called Peseshet.
textes.Le papyrus Edwin Smith, copié vers 1600: The Edwin Smith papyrus, copied around 1600 BC from older texts, describes 48 cases of injuries, fractures, dislocations and tumours. It sorts them from top to bottom: the head first, then the neck, the arms, the torso.
textes.Pour chaque cas, le médecin examine, pui: For each case, the physician examines, then gives one of three verdicts: "an ailment which I will treat", "an ailment with which I will contend", or "an ailment not to be treated". It contains the first known descriptions of the meninges and the fluid around the brain.
textes.Edwin Smith : 48 cas de la tête aux pied: Edwin Smith: 48 cases from head to foot, three verdicts, the meninges described for the first time.
textes.Le papyrus Ebers, vers 1550 av. J.-C., e: The Ebers papyrus, around 1550 BC, is a 110-page scroll about 20 metres long. It gathers over 800 remedies, with chapters on contraception, diagnosing pregnancy and other gynaecological matters.
textes.Les Égyptiens soignaient notamment avec: The Egyptians treated notably with honey. And their doctors were highly specialised, Herodotus reports: there were distinct healers for the eyes, for the teeth and for internal diseases.
Ebers: 20 metres, over 800 remedies. Specialists for eyes, teeth, belly.
textes.Le plus ancien médecin connu par son nom: The oldest physician known by name is Egyptian: Hesy-Ra, chief of dentists to King Djoser, in the early Third Dynasty. He is also the first dentist whose name we know.
textes.On lit souvent que Merit-Ptah fut la pre: One often reads that Merit-Ptah was the first woman doctor. She never existed: she appears in a 1937 book by Kate Campbell Hurd-Mead, who had mixed up two women, and later authors copied the error. The real one is probably Peseshet, "lady overseer of the female physicians".
textes.Hesy-Ra, premier médecin connu ; Peseshe: Hesy-Ra, first known physician; Peseshet, first woman doctor; Merit-Ptah, a 1937 mistake.
textes.À Kos, vers 400 av. J.-C., la maladie ce: On Kos, around 400 BC, disease stops being a punishment from the gods: it has natural causes, which can be observed.
textes.Hippocrate naît vers 460 av. J.-C. sur l: Hippocrates was born around 460 BC on the island of Kos; he separated medicine from religion.
textes.Le Corpus hippocratique réunit environ s: The Hippocratic Corpus gathers about seventy treatises, written by many authors.
textes.La théorie des quatre humeurs, sang, phl: The theory of the four humours, blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile, dominated medicine until the 19th century.
textes.Le serment d'Hippocrate ne dit pas « d'a: The Hippocratic Oath does not say "first, do no harm"; it says: "I will do no harm or injustice".
textes.« Primum non nocere » n'est pas dans le: "Primum non nocere" is not in the oath, and the oath may not be by Hippocrates himself.
textes.On appelait l'épilepsie la « maladie sac: Epilepsy was called the "sacred disease": a god struck the patient. Around 400 BC, a treatise of the Hippocratic Corpus replied: "It is not, in my opinion, any more divine or more sacred than other diseases, but has a natural cause." What people think divine comes from men's inexperience.
textes.L'auteur place la cause dans le cerveau,: The author places the cause in the brain, which "has the greatest power over man". For Hippocrates, born around 460 BC on the island of Kos, disease is not a punishment from the gods: it comes from the environment, diet and way of life.
textes.L'épilepsie a une cause naturelle, dans: Epilepsy has a natural cause, in the brain: medicine separates from religion.
textes.Le traité De la nature de l'homme pose q: The treatise On the Nature of Man holds that the body contains four humours: blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile. Health is their balance. Each has its qualities: blood is hot and moist, yellow bile hot and dry, black bile cold and dry, phlegm cold and moist.
textes.Chaque humeur répond à une saison, et pl: Each humour matches a season, and later a temperament: sanguine, choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic. Galen took up the theory, and bloodletting flourished. It was not definitively abandoned until 1858.
textes.Sang, phlegme, bile jaune, bile noire :: Blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile: four humours, two thousand years of medicine, abandoned in 1858.
textes.Le serment d'Hippocrate s'ouvre ainsi :: The Hippocratic Oath opens: "I swear by Apollo Healer, by Asclepius, by Hygieia, by Panacea." It reads: "I will do no harm or injustice" to patients; the phrase "first, do no harm" is not in it.
textes.Le médecin y promet aussi de ne pas util: The physician also promises not to use the knife, "not even on sufferers from stone", although other texts of the Corpus describe operations. The oldest mention of the oath dates from the year 43, in Scribonius Largus. Today, no American medical school has graduates swear the original version.
textes.Le serment : « ni tort ni injustice ». «: The oath: "no harm or injustice". "First, do no harm" is not in it.
textes.Au IIIe siècle av. J.-C., Alexandrie est: In the 3rd century BC, Alexandria is the only place where human bodies are opened: nerves, brain and heart come out of the shadows.
textes.Hérophile de Chalcédoine, vers 335-280 a: Herophilos of Chalcedon, around 335-280 BC, was the first to dissect human cadavers methodically, in Alexandria.
textes.Il place l'intelligence dans le cerveau,: He placed the intellect in the brain, distinguished the cerebrum from the cerebellum, and named the duodenum.
textes.Érasistrate voit dans le cœur une pompe,: Erasistratus saw the heart as a pump, but believed the arteries carried air.
textes.Les livres d'Hérophile sont tous perdus: Herophilos' books are all lost: they are known through Galen and Celsus.
textes.Tertullien accuse Hérophile d'avoir diss: Tertullian accused Herophilos of vivisecting 600 prisoners; historians doubt it.
textes.Né vers 335 av. J.-C. à Chalcédoine, Hér: Born around 335 BC in Chalcedon, Herophilos lived in Alexandria, the only city where human cadavers could then be opened: everywhere else, it was forbidden. He was the first to dissect them methodically, sometimes in public to teach.
textes.Il distingue les nerfs des vaisseaux san: He distinguished nerves from blood vessels, and motor nerves from sensory nerves. He placed the intellect in the brain, not the heart, distinguished the cerebrum from the cerebellum, and gave the duodenum its name. To measure the pulse, he used a water clock.
textes.Hérophile : premières dissections humain: Herophilos: first human dissections, intellect in the brain, pulse timed by water clock.
textes.Érasistrate, né vers 304 av. J.-C., fond: Erasistratus, born around 304 BC, founded the school of anatomy of Alexandria with Herophilos. For him, the heart is not the seat of sensations: it is a pump, and he is credited with describing its valves. He too separated sensory and motor nerves, all linked to the brain.
textes.Il se trompe sur les artères, qu'il croi: He was wrong about the arteries, which he believed were filled with air, the "pneuma". He distrusted bloodletting and preferred diet and exercise. The story goes that he guessed Prince Antiochus' illness: a secret love for his stepmother Stratonice.
textes.Érasistrate : le cœur pompe, les artères: Erasistratus: the heart pumps, the arteries (he thinks) carry air, and bloodletting is worthless.
textes.Hérophile a écrit au moins neuf ouvrages: Herophilos wrote at least nine works, all lost. We know them only through those who quoted them, above all Galen, in the 2nd century. Celsus, a Roman encyclopaedist, also reports their work in his De medicina, published before the year 47.
textes.Celse et, plus tard, Tertullien accusent: Celsus and, later, Tertullian accused Herophilos of dissecting living convicts; Tertullian speaks of 600. Historians doubt it: Herophilos believed the arteries contained very little blood, which a vivisection would have shown him to be wrong.
textes.Leurs livres sont perdus ; l'accusation: Their books are lost; the vivisection charge, reported by Celsus and Tertullian, is doubtful.
textes.Médecin des gladiateurs puis des empereu: Physician to gladiators then emperors, Galen dissected apes and pigs and reigned over medicine for fourteen centuries.
textes.Galien naît en 129 à Pergame ; il soigne: Galen was born in 129 in Pergamon; he first treated gladiators, whose wounds were for him "windows into the body".
textes.La dissection humaine étant interdite, i: Human dissection being forbidden, he dissected mainly Barbary macaques, then pigs.
textes.En coupant un nerf du larynx d'un porc q: By cutting a nerve of the larynx of a squealing pig, he showed that the brain controls the voice.
textes.Ses erreurs, le sang fabriqué par le foi: His errors, blood made by the liver or holes in the heart's septum, were not challenged until 1543.
textes.Galien a beaucoup observé, mais sur des: Galen observed a great deal, but on animals: what holds for the ape does not always hold for man.
textes.Galien naît en septembre 129 à Pergame,: Galen was born in September 129 in Pergamon, today Bergama, in Turkey. As a young physician, he treated his city's gladiators; their wounds were, he said, "windows into the body".
textes.Il part ensuite pour Rome et devient le: He then left for Rome and became physician to several emperors. Marcus Aurelius summoned him to court, then left him in Rome as physician to his heir, Commodus. He wrote ceaselessly: what remains comes to about 3 million words, probably less than a third of his output.
textes.Gladiateurs à Pergame, empereurs à Rome,: Gladiators in Pergamon, emperors in Rome, 3 million words preserved.
textes.À Rome, ouvrir un corps humain est inter: In Rome, opening a human body was forbidden. So Galen dissected mainly Barbary macaques, then pigs, to avoid prosecution. His descriptions of the human body came largely from these animals.
textes.Sa démonstration la plus célèbre : penda: His most famous demonstration: while a pig squealed, he tied off the recurrent laryngeal nerve, and the animal fell silent. The voice is therefore controlled by the brain, through the nerves. He was also the first to distinguish dark venous blood from bright arterial blood.
textes.Un nerf coupé, un porc muet : le cerveau: A nerve cut, a silent pig: the brain controls the voice.
textes.Galien se trompe aussi. Il croit que le: Galen was also wrong. He believed blood originated in the liver, described in man a network of vessels at the base of the brain, the rete mirabile, and asserted that small holes in the septum of the heart let blood pass from right to left.
textes.Ses descriptions anatomiques restent pou: Yet his anatomical descriptions remained uncontested until 1543, when Vesalius published his plates drawn from human dissections. Galen also took up Hippocrates' theory of humours, and it was through him that it crossed the Middle Ages.
textes.Le foie fabrique le sang, la cloison du: The liver makes blood, the heart's septum is pierced: wrong, but uncontested until 1543.
textes.Refaire un nez avec la peau de la joue,: Rebuilding a nose with skin from the cheek, practising on gourds, dissecting: Indian surgery is written in the Sushruta Samhita.
textes.La Sushruta Samhita, commencée dans les: The Sushruta Samhita, begun in the last centuries BC, was revised around the 3rd-4th centuries AD.
textes.Elle compte 186 chapitres, décrit 1 120: It has 186 chapters and describes 1,120 illnesses and 700 medicinal plants.
textes.Elle contient la première description éc: It contains the first written description of a rhinoplasty, with a flap of skin from the cheek.
textes.Les élèves s'exercent sur des courges et: Students practised on gourds and dead animals, and had to dissect a body to learn anatomy.
textes.Le texte n'est pas d'un seul auteur ni d: The text is not by a single author or from a single era: it was built up over several centuries.
textes.La Sushruta Samhita contient la première: The Sushruta Samhita contains the first written description of a rhinoplasty: a nose is rebuilt with a flap of skin taken from the cheek. The text also describes protocols for eye surgery.
textes.Ces techniques auraient voyagé : en Sici: These techniques may have travelled: in Sicily, the Branca family, then in Bologna Gaspare Tagliacozzi in the 16th century, reportedly knew them. The evidence for this lineage is disputed.
textes.La première rhinoplastie écrite : un lam: The first written rhinoplasty: a cheek flap to rebuild the nose.
textes.Avant d'opérer, l'élève s'entraîne sur d: Before operating, the student trained on gourds and dead animals. And anyone who wants to know anatomy must prepare a body and dissect it himself: knowing from books is not enough.
textes.L'ouvrage est immense : 186 chapitres, 1: The work is immense: 186 chapters, 1,120 illnesses, 700 medicinal plants. It was built up over centuries, begun before the common era and revised around the 3rd-4th centuries.
textes.Courges, animaux morts, dissection : on: Gourds, dead animals, dissection: learning by doing. 186 chapters, 1,120 illnesses.
textes.Le manuscrit Bower, des IVe-Ve siècles,: The Bower manuscript, from the 4th-5th centuries, already counts Sushruta among the ten sages living in the Himalayas.
textes.Au début du VIIIe siècle, à Bagdad, le t: In the early 8th century, in Baghdad, the text was translated into Arabic under the title Kitab Shah Shun al-Hindi. Indian surgery thus entered the medicine of the Islamic world.
textes.Du manuscrit Bower à Bagdad : Sushruta p: From the Bower manuscript to Baghdad: Sushruta passed into Arabic in the 8th century.
textes.Un empereur qui questionne son médecin,: An emperor questioning his physician, a surgeon who puts his patients to sleep, smallpox blown up the nose: China heals in its own way.
textes.Le Huangdi Neijing, sans doute du Ier si: The Huangdi Neijing, probably from the 1st century BC, is a dialogue between the Yellow Emperor and his physicians, in two parts of 81 chapters.
textes.Il s'appuie sur le yin et le yang et les: It rests on yin and yang and the five elements; its Lingshu part details acupuncture.
textes.Hua Tuo, vers 140-208, utilise le mafeis: Hua Tuo, around 140-208, used mafeisan, considered the world's first anaesthetic.
textes.La variolation, souffler des croûtes de: Variolation, blowing smallpox scabs up the nose, is attested in China in the 16th century.
textes.Hua Tuo n'a pas opéré le bras du général: Hua Tuo did not operate on General Guan Yu's arm: the scene comes from a 14th-century novel, and Hua Tuo had died ten years earlier.
textes.Le Huangdi Neijing date sans doute du Ie: The Huangdi Neijing probably dates from the 1st century BC. It takes the form of a dialogue between the Yellow Emperor and his physician ministers, above all Qibo, in two parts, the Suwen and the Lingshu, of 81 chapters each.
textes.Il relie la santé du corps à l'ordre du: It links the body's health to the order of the world through yin and yang and the five elements. The Lingshu describes acupuncture in detail. In 762, after twelve years of work, Wang Bing reorganised the Suwen into 81 chapters.
textes.Huangdi Neijing : Ier s. av. J.-C., 2 ×: Huangdi Neijing: 1st century BC, 2 × 81 chapters, yin-yang, five elements, acupuncture.
textes.Le chirurgien qui endormait: The surgeon who put people to sleep
textes.Hua Tuo vit à la fin de la dynastie des: Hua Tuo lived at the end of the Eastern Han dynasty, around 140-208. Accounts credit him with the first anaesthesia in China, with a potion, mafeisan, considered the world's first anaesthetic. He also invented exercises imitating five animals: the tiger, the deer, the bear, the ape and the crane.
textes.Le seigneur de guerre Cao Cao le fait ex: The warlord Cao Cao had him executed. Awaiting death, Hua Tuo wrote down his techniques, then burned his book himself. As for the operation on Guan Yu's arm, it comes from a 14th-century novel: Hua Tuo had died ten years before the battle.
textes.Hua Tuo : le mafeisan, cinq animaux, un: Hua Tuo: mafeisan, five animals, a burned book; Guan Yu is fiction.
textes.En 1973, à Mawangdui, dans le Hunan, on: In 1973, at Mawangdui, in Hunan, a tomb sealed in 168 BC was opened: it contained unknown medical texts, including the Prescriptions for Fifty-Two Ailments.
textes.Bien plus tard, la Chine pratique la plu: Much later, China practised the oldest documented variolation, in the 16th century: powdered smallpox scabs were blown up the nostrils, to cause a mild form that protects. Joseph Needham dates it between 1567 and 1572. Only 1 to 2% of those variolated died, against 30% of those who caught smallpox.
textes.Variolation chinoise : croûtes en poudre: Chinese variolation: powdered scabs up the nose, 1 to 2% deaths against 30%.
textes.Bagdad, Ispahan, Le Caire : al-Razi comp: Baghdad, Isfahan, Cairo: al-Razi compares, Avicenna codifies, Ibn al-Nafis contradicts Galen on the heart.
textes.Al-Razi, vers 865-925, dirige des hôpita: Al-Razi, around 865-925, ran hospitals in Baghdad and Rey, and was the first to distinguish smallpox from measles.
textes.Le Canon d'Avicenne, achevé en 1025, cin: Avicenna's Canon, completed in 1025, five books, served as a textbook in Europe's universities for centuries.
textes.Le Canon donne sept règles pour essayer: The Canon gives seven rules for testing a new drug.
textes.Ibn al-Nafis, au XIIIe siècle, décrit le: Ibn al-Nafis, in the 13th century, was the first to describe pulmonary circulation: blood passes through the lungs, not through the heart's septum.
textes.La découverte d'Ibn al-Nafis est restée: Ibn al-Nafis' discovery remained unknown in Europe: his manuscript was only found in 1924.
textes.Al-Razi, né à Rey vers 865, dirige les h: Al-Razi, born in Rey around 865, ran the hospitals of Baghdad and Rey. To choose the site of a new hospital in Baghdad, he hung pieces of fresh meat in several districts, and had it built where the meat took longest to rot.
textes.Il est l'un des premiers à distinguer cl: He was one of the first to clinically distinguish smallpox from measles, in his treatise On Smallpox and Measles. To find out whether bloodletting helped against meningitis, he compared patients who were bled with others who were not. His notebooks, gathered after his death, form al-Hawi, in 23 volumes.
textes.Al-Razi : la viande qui pourrit le moins: Al-Razi: the meat that rots least chooses the hospital; smallpox and measles separated.
textes.En 1025, Avicenne achève le Canon de la: In 1025, Avicenna completed the Canon of Medicine, an encyclopaedia in five books. Translated into Latin, it became the textbook of European universities; in Padua, it was still taught in 1715.
textes.Le Canon pose sept règles pour essayer u: The Canon lays down seven rules for testing a new drug: for instance, test a remedy on a simple disease, and check that the effect is reproduced. The historian George Sarton also praised its idea that phthisis, tuberculosis, is contagious.
textes.Canon d'Avicenne : 1025, cinq livres, se: Avicenna's Canon: 1025, five books, seven rules for testing a drug, read until the 18th century.
textes.Galien affirmait que le sang passait du: Galen asserted that blood passed from the right side to the left side of the heart through small invisible holes in the septum. Ibn al-Nafis, born in Damascus around 1210, contradicted him in his Commentary on Anatomy in the Canon: the septum is thick, with no passage.
textes.Le sang doit donc aller du cœur droit au: So the blood must go from the right heart to the lungs, then back to the left heart: it is the first description of pulmonary circulation. He bequeathed his library to the Mansuri hospital in Cairo. His text remained unknown until 1924, when an Egyptian physician found a manuscript of it in Berlin.
textes.Ibn al-Nafis : pas de trous dans la cloi: Ibn al-Nafis: no holes in the septum, blood goes through the lungs. Found in 1924.
textes.En 1543, Vésale dissèque de ses mains et: In 1543, Vesalius dissected with his own hands and corrected Galen: bones, organs, breathing, digestion, the body as it is.
textes.En 1628, un médecin du roi d'Angleterre: In 1628, a physician to the King of England did a multiplication: the liver cannot make that much blood. Blood goes round in a circle.
textes.William Harvey publie De Motu Cordis en: William Harvey published De Motu Cordis in 1628: the heart pushes the blood, which comes back through the veins and goes round a closed circuit.
textes.Son argument est un calcul : à 1 000 bat: His argument is a calculation: at 1,000 beats per half hour, the liver would have to make 498 pounds of blood a day.
textes.Il a étudié à Padoue, où son maître Fabr: He studied in Padua, where his teacher Fabricius had described the valves of the veins.
textes.Les capillaires qui relient artères et v: The capillaries linking arteries and veins were seen by Malpighi in 1660, three years after Harvey's death.
textes.Harvey n'a pas prédit les capillaires :: Harvey did not predict capillaries: for him, blood soaks the flesh and is then taken up by the veins.
textes.William Harvey naît le 1er avril 1578 da: William Harvey was born on 1 April 1578 in Kent. In 1599, he went to study in Padua, the great school of anatomy, and became a doctor there on 25 April 1602. His teacher, Fabricius, had described the small valves that line the inside of the veins.
textes.De retour à Londres, il devient le 3 fév: Back in London, on 3 February 1618 he became Physician Extraordinary to King James I, then served Charles I. The king's hunts supplied him with deer carcasses to dissect.
textes.Harvey : Padoue, Fabricius et ses valvul: Harvey: Padua, Fabricius and his valves, then physician to kings.
textes.Depuis Galien, on pense que le foie fabr: Since Galen, people thought the liver constantly made new blood, which the body used up. Harvey counted: the heart beats about 1,000 times every half hour. With 48 half hours in a day, the liver would have to produce 498 pounds of blood a day. And Harvey deliberately chose low figures.
textes.Impossible : le même sang doit donc reve: Impossible: so the same blood must come back to the heart. The valves of the veins confirm it, they only let blood pass towards the heart. He published it all in 1628 in De Motu Cordis, "On the Motion of the Heart and Blood".
textes.Le calcul de Harvey : bien trop de sang: Harvey's calculation: far too much blood for one liver, so blood circulates.
textes.Le livre est attaqué, et Harvey « baisse: The book was attacked, and Harvey "fell mightily in his practice". He nevertheless pursued his career and died on 3 June 1657.
textes.Un trou reste dans sa théorie : comment: One gap remained in his theory: how does blood get from the arteries to the veins? Harvey did not predict small vessels. In 1660, Marcello Malpighi saw blood running in the capillaries of a frog's lung. Long before, in 1553, Michael Servetus had written that blood goes from the heart to the lungs.
textes.Harvey perd des patients ; Malpighi trou: Harvey lost patients; Malpighi found the capillaries in 1660.
textes.Des « cellules » de liège de Hooke aux a: From Hooke's cork "cells" to Leeuwenhoek's animalcules, then cell theory: all living things are made of cells.
textes.Des souris nées d'un chiffon sale, des a: Mice born from a dirty rag, maggots born from meat? Two centuries of jars, gauze and flasks to say no.
textes.La fin de la génération spontanée, dans: The end of spontaneous generation, in time
textes.On a longtemps cru que la vie naît toute: For a long time people believed that life arises by itself from matter: spontaneous generation.
textes.En 1668, Francesco Redi montre que les a: In 1668, Francesco Redi showed that maggots do not arise from meat: under gauze, the flies do not lay on it.
textes.Needham, en 1745, voit ses bouillons se: Needham, in 1745, saw his broths go cloudy; Spallanzani, in 1768, sealed his and saw nothing grow.
textes.En 1859, Pasteur fait bouillir un bouill: In 1859, Pasteur boiled broth in a swan-neck flask: the bend stops the dust, nothing grows.
textes.Le flacon de Pasteur reste ouvert à l'ai: Pasteur's flask stays open to the air: it is the bend in the neck that stops the particles, not a stopper.
textes.Pendant des siècles, on pense que des êt: For centuries, people thought that living things arose by themselves from mud, meat or waste: this is spontaneous generation.
textes.Au XVIIe siècle, le chimiste Jan Baptist: In the 17th century, the chemist Jan Baptist van Helmont even gave a recipe for making mice: a dirty rag and wheat, left for 21 days.
textes.Génération spontanée : la vie naîtrait d: Spontaneous generation: life would arise from matter, rag-born mice included.
textes.Francesco Redi naît à Arezzo le 18 févri: Francesco Redi was born in Arezzo on 18 February 1626; he became head physician to Ferdinando II de' Medici. In 1668, he put meat into six jars: three open, three covered with a fine gauze that let only air through.
textes.Les asticots apparaissent dans les bocau: Maggots appeared in the open jars, where flies landed, not under the gauze. Redi published his Experiments on the Generation of Insects. He also showed that snake venom comes from the fangs, not the gallbladder.
For microbes, the question came back. In 1745, John Needham boiled broths and sealed them: they still went cloudy. In 1768, Lazzaro Spallanzani sealed his while removing part of the air, and saw nothing grow.
textes.En 1859, Louis Pasteur fait bouillir un: In 1859, Louis Pasteur boiled meat broth in a flask with a neck bent into a swan neck. The bend prevented falling particles from reaching the broth, which stayed clear. In 1862, the Academy of Sciences awarded him a prize offered on the question.
textes.Pasteur, 1859 : l'air passe, les poussiè: Pasteur, 1859: air gets in, dust doesn't, nothing grows.
textes.Un Suédois donne deux noms à chaque plan: A Swede gave two names to every plant and animal, sent his students to the four corners of the world, and ended up labelled himself.
textes.Carl Linné, né le 23 mai 1707 à Råshult,: Carl Linnaeus, born on 23 May 1707 in Råshult, Sweden, published the first edition of Systema Naturae in 1735: twelve pages.
textes.Species Plantarum, en 1753, est le point: Species Plantarum, in 1753, is the starting point of the scientific names of plants.
textes.La 10e édition du Systema Naturae, en 17: The 10th edition of Systema Naturae, in 1758, is the starting point of animal names.
textes.Il appelle 17 de ses élèves ses « apôtre: He called 17 of his students his "apostles" and sent them out to collect plants around the world.
textes.Le spécimen type d'Homo sapiens, c'est L: The type specimen of Homo sapiens is Linnaeus himself: designated by Stearn in 1959.
textes.Carl Linné naît le 23 mai 1707 à Råshult: Carl Linnaeus was born on 23 May 1707 in Råshult, in Småland, Sweden. On 12 May 1732, he set out from Uppsala on a study trip to Lapland.
textes.En 1735, il fait imprimer aux Pays-Bas l: In 1735, he had the first edition of his Systema Naturae printed in the Netherlands, a twelve-page work that sorted the three kingdoms of nature. The following editions kept growing.
textes.Systema Naturae, 1735 : douze pages au d: Systema Naturae, 1735: twelve pages to begin with.
textes.Linné donne à chaque espèce un nom en de: Linnaeus gave each species a two-word name, genus then species, like Homo sapiens. His Species Plantarum, in 1753, is accepted worldwide as the starting point for plant names.
textes.Pour les animaux, le point de départ est: For animals, the starting point is the 10th edition of Systema Naturae, in 1758. An older name, however well chosen, does not count.
textes.Plantes : 1753. Animaux : 1758. Avant, ç: Plants: 1753. Animals: 1758. Before that, it doesn't count.
textes.Professeur à Uppsala, Linné appelle 17 d: A professor at Uppsala, Linnaeus called 17 of his students his "apostles" and sent them to collect plants on every continent. In 1761, he was ennobled and became Carl von Linné. His favourite plant, a small woodland flower, bears his name: Linnaea borealis.
textes.Il meurt le 10 janvier 1778. En 1959, le: He died on 10 January 1778. In 1959, the botanist William Stearn designated him as the type specimen of Homo sapiens: he is the only human Linnaeus is known to have examined.
textes.17 apôtres, un titre de noblesse, et Lin: 17 apostles, a noble title, and Linnaeus a specimen of his own species.
textes.Douze marins, six remèdes, deux oranges: Twelve sailors, six remedies, two oranges; an eight-year-old boy and a cow called Blossom. The 18th century learned to test.
textes.Premiers essais et vaccins, dans le temp: First trials and vaccines, in time
textes.Le 20 mai 1747, sur le Salisbury, James: On 20 May 1747, aboard the Salisbury, James Lind split 12 sailors with scurvy between 6 treatments: only the citrus works.
textes.Son Traité du scorbut, en 1753, est pres: His Treatise of the Scurvy, in 1753, was mostly ignored; the Royal Navy only issued lemon juice to the whole fleet after his death.
textes.Le 14 mai 1796, Edward Jenner inocule la: On 14 May 1796, Edward Jenner inoculated cowpox into James Phipps, aged 8.
textes.Jenner publie son Inquiry en 1798 ; l'OM: Jenner published his Inquiry in 1798; the WHO declared smallpox eradicated in 1980.
textes.Lind n'a jamais présenté les agrumes com: Lind never presented citrus as the single remedy: he believed scurvy had several causes.
textes.James Lind naît à Édimbourg le 4 octobre: James Lind was born in Edinburgh on 4 October 1716. A naval surgeon, on 20 May 1747, aboard HMS Salisbury patrolling the Bay of Biscay, he began a trial on twelve sailors with scurvy, split two by two.
textes.Chaque paire reçoit un traitement : du c: Each pair received one treatment: cider, elixir of vitriol, vinegar, seawater, two oranges and a lemon, or a spicy paste. The citrus eaters recovered. It is one of the first controlled clinical trials.
textes.En 1753, Lind publie son Traité du scorb: In 1753, Lind published his Treatise of the Scurvy, which was mostly ignored. And he himself never presented citrus as the single remedy: he believed scurvy had several causes.
textes.Médecin-chef de l'hôpital naval de Hasla: Chief physician of the Haslar naval hospital from 1758, he died on 13 July 1794. The following year, the Admiralty agreed to issue lemon juice to the whole fleet.
The right result, ignored for forty years.
textes.Contre la variole, on pratique déjà la v: Against smallpox, variolation was already practised: in 1721, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu imported it from Constantinople to Britain. And in 1774, the farmer Benjamin Jesty inoculated his wife and two children with cowpox, a mild disease of cows.
textes.Le 14 mai 1796, Edward Jenner prélève du: On 14 May 1796, Edward Jenner took pus from a milkmaid, Sarah Nelmes, infected by a cow called Blossom, and inoculated it into James Phipps, aged 8, his gardener's son. His first paper was not published; he published his Inquiry in 1798. In 1980, the WHO declared smallpox eradicated.
textes.Jenner, 1796 : de Blossom à Phipps ; var: Jenner, 1796: from Blossom to Phipps; smallpox eradicated in 1980.
textes.Au XIXe siècle, Semmelweis et Snow compt: In the 19th century, Semmelweis and Snow counted the dead to find causes: hypothesis, control group, falsifiability.
textes.En 1859, L'Origine des espèces : sélecti: In 1859, On the Origin of Species: natural selection, mutations, and the whole history of life.
textes.Des pois de Mendel à la double hélice :: From Mendel's peas to the double helix: genes, alleles, heredity, DNA and mutations.
textes.Bactéries, virus, vaccins, antibiotiques: Bacteria, viruses, vaccines, antibiotics: the late 19th century identified microbes, the 20th fought them.
textes.Le mot naît avec Haeckel ; Rachel Carson: The word was born with Haeckel; Rachel Carson raised the alarm: food chains, cycles, biodiversity and climate.
textes.De Dolly à CRISPR : ADN recombinant, PCR: From Dolly to CRISPR: recombinant DNA, PCR, cloning and RNA vaccines.
textes.Essai contrôlé : tirage au sort entre tr: Controlled trial: random draw between treatment and placebo, double-blind; only the difference counts
textes.double aveugle : ni patients ni médecins: double-blind: neither patients nor doctors know who gets what
textes.Vienne, 1847 : mortalité de 18,3 % en av: Vienna, 1847: mortality 18.3 % in April, 1.2 % in July after handwashing with chlorinated lime
textes.Bactérie sans noyau, cellule animale ave: Bacterium without nucleus, animal cell with nucleus, plant cell with wall and chloroplasts; a virus is not a cell
textes.sans cellule à détourner, il ne fait rie: without a cell to hijack, it does nothing
textes.La mitochondrie brûle glucose et oxygène: The mitochondrion burns glucose and oxygen to make ATP; it is an old bacterium swallowed by another cell
textes.Le cou de la girafe selon Lamarck (faux): The giraffe's neck according to Lamarck (wrong) and to Darwin
textes.Humains et chimpanzés partagent un ancêt: Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor 6 to 7 million years ago; birds are surviving dinosaurs
textes.Tiktaalik (2004) : entre poissons et ani: Tiktaalik (2004): between fish and four-legged animals
textes.Mendel : pois jaune × pois vert, premièr: Mendel: yellow pea × green pea, first generation all yellow, green returns in about a quarter of the next
textes.deux facteurs par caractère, un de chaqu: two factors per trait, one from each parent
textes.Le corps en chiffres : 206 os chez l'adu: The body in numbers: 206 bones in adults, about 300 at birth, 4.5 to 6 litres of blood, 60 to 100 beats per minute
textes.la mâchoire inférieure est un seul os, p: the lower jaw is a single bone, not two as in Galen
textes.Le vaccin entraîne le système immunitair: The vaccine trains the immune system, which keeps a memory and reacts fast to the real encounter
textes.Un antibiotique tue les bactéries sensib: An antibiotic kills the sensitive bacteria; the rare resistant ones survive and multiply
textes.pas d'antibiotique contre un virus ; all: no antibiotics against a virus; finish the course
textes.Paine retire l'étoile de mer Pisaster :: Paine removes the Pisaster starfish: mussels take over and species drop from 15 to 8 in three years
textes.CRISPR-Cas9 : un ARN guide mène l'enzyme: CRISPR-Cas9: a guide RNA leads the Cas9 enzyme to a chosen sequence, where it cuts the DNA
textes.Vaccin à ARN : la recette est lue hors d: mRNA vaccine: the recipe is read outside the nucleus, the protein trains the immune system, the RNA breaks down in a few days
textes.reste hors du noyau, dégradé en quelques: stays outside the nucleus, broken down in a few days
textes.Un crâne trépané : si les bords du trou: A trepanned skull: if the edges of the hole are sharp, the patient died during or soon after; if they are rounded by regrown bone, he survived
textes.Le papyrus Edwin Smith : examiner, puis: The Edwin Smith papyrus: examine, then give one of three verdicts
textes.Les quatre humeurs et leurs qualités : l: The four humours and their qualities: blood hot and moist, yellow bile hot and dry, black bile cold and dry, phlegm cold and moist
textes.Ce qu'Hérophile a distingué, à Alexandri: What Herophilos distinguished, in Alexandria: nerves from vessels, motor from sensory nerves, cerebrum from cerebellum
textes.Ce que Galien a vu juste et ce qu'il a v: What Galen got right and what he got wrong

textes.En 1628, William Harvey, médecin du roi: In 1628, William Harvey, physician to the King of England, published De Motu Cordis, a short book that overturned fourteen centuries of medicine. Since Galen, it had been believed that the liver constantly made new blood, used up by the body. Harvey did a calculation: at 72 beats a minute, the heart sends out 540 pounds of blood an hour. No liver could keep up. So the same blood must come back to the heart and leave again, in a closed circuit. The valves of the veins, described by his teacher Fabricius, prove it: they only let blood pass towards the heart. One piece was missing, the passage from arteries to veins: Malpighi would see the capillaries in 1660.

textes.Karl Popper fait de la réfutabilité le c: Karl Popper made falsifiability the criterion of science in The Logic of Scientific Discovery, in 1934. His example: no number of white swans proves that all swans are white, but a single black swan is enough to refute it.
textes.Le coefficient de corrélation a été mis: The correlation coefficient was developed by Karl Pearson from an idea Francis Galton introduced in the 1880s. The formula itself had been published by Auguste Bravais as early as 1844.
textes.Le 20 mai 1747, à bord du HMS Salisbury,: On 20 May 1747, aboard HMS Salisbury, physician James Lind split 12 sailors with scurvy into six pairs, each with a different remedy. Only those given citrus fruit really recovered: it was one of the first comparative trials in history.
textes.En 1835 à Nuremberg, un test de sel homé: In 1835 in Nuremberg, a test of diluted homeopathic salt run by Friedrich Wilhelm von Hoven was one of the first double-blind protocols. It challenged homeopathy.
textes.Popper visait des théories qui expliquai: Popper was targeting theories that explained everything, such as Freud's and Adler's psychoanalysis: in his view, a theory that rules out no observation predicts nothing. His 1934 book was only translated into English in 1959.
textes.« Placebo » est un mot latin qui veut di: "Placebo" is a Latin word meaning "I shall please". In 1955, a study with a now famous title, The Powerful Placebo, showed that the placebo effect really mattered in medicine.
textes.Le 23 mars 1989, Fleischmann et Pons ann: On 23 March 1989, Fleischmann and Pons announced cold fusion at a press conference. Laboratories around the world repeated the experiment and failed: the claim faded for lack of replication.
textes.Jacques Bernoulli a mis plus de 20 ans à: Jacob Bernoulli spent over 20 years proving the law of large numbers, published in 1713 in Ars Conjectandi. Poisson gave it the name "law of large numbers" in 1837.
textes.Guillaume d'Ockham, moine franciscain an: William of Ockham, an English Franciscan friar, lived c. 1287-1347. The phrase "Ockham's razor" only appeared centuries later: Libert Froidmont claimed to have coined it in 1649.
textes.La plus ancienne relecture avant publica: The oldest known pre-publication review dates from 1665, by Henry Oldenburg, founder of the Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions. Nature has only required outside reviewers since 1973.
textes.À la première clinique d'obstétrique de: At Vienna's First Obstetrical Clinic, mortality fell from 18.3% in April 1847 to 1.2% in July after washing with chlorinated lime. His colleagues still rejected him: it took Pasteur's germ theory to prove him right.
textes.Albert von Kölliker observe les mitochon: Albert von Kölliker observed mitochondria in insect muscles in 1857. Carl Benda named them in 1898, from the Greek for "thread-like granule". The "powerhouse" nickname dates from 1957.
textes.En 1683, Antoni van Leeuwenhoek décrit à: In 1683, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek described to the Royal Society bacteria taken from the human mouth, seen through his own microscopes. He called these tiny beings "little animals".
textes.Joseph Priestley montre qu'une plante «: Joseph Priestley showed that a plant "restores" air spoiled by a candle or a mouse. In 1779, Jan Ingenhousz repeated the experiment and found the key: sunlight is needed.
textes.En 1869 à Tübingen, Friedrich Miescher i: In 1869 in Tübingen, Friedrich Miescher isolated an unknown substance from the nuclei of white blood cells, taken from the pus on hospital bandages. He called it "nuclein": it was DNA.
textes.George Palade décrit les ribosomes en 19: George Palade described ribosomes in 1955 using the electron microscope. He received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1974 with Albert Claude and Christian de Duve.
textes.En 1958, John Gurdon clone une grenouill: In 1958, John Gurdon cloned a frog using nuclei from tadpole cells: the nucleus of an already specialised cell keeps the whole programme. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize with Shinya Yamanaka.
textes.Pendant plus de 30 ans, on a cru que l'h: For more than 30 years, humans were believed to have 48 chromosomes, as counted by Theophilus Painter in 1921. On 22 December 1955, in Lund, Joe Hin Tjio and Albert Levan counted 46.
textes.Micrographia, le livre où Hooke nomme le: Micrographia, the book in which Hooke named cells, came out in January 1665 under the aegis of the Royal Society. Samuel Pepys called it "the most ingenious book that ever I read in my life".
textes.Oscar Hertwig décrit la méiose en 1876 d: Oscar Hertwig described meiosis in 1876 in sea urchin eggs. August Weismann explained its role in heredity in 1890, and the word "meiosis" was coined in 1905.
textes.En 1892, Dmitri Ivanovsky montre que l'a: In 1892, Dmitri Ivanovsky showed that the agent of tobacco mosaic disease passed through porcelain filters that stop bacteria. In 1898, Martinus Beijerinck saw it as a new kind of agent and called it a virus.
textes.Entre 1885 et 1901, le chimiste allemand: Between 1885 and 1901, German chemist Albrecht Kossel isolated and named the bases of nucleic acids: adenine, cytosine, guanine, thymine and uracil. Nobel Prize in Medicine 1910.
textes.En 1838, le chimiste français Anselme Pa: In 1838, French chemist Anselme Payen isolated the material of plant cell walls. The word "cellulose" appeared in 1839, in Jean-Baptiste Dumas's report on his memoir.
textes.L'Origine des espèces paraît le 24 novem: On the Origin of Species came out on 24 November 1859 from John Murray, in a print run of 1,250 copies. All available copies were taken up at the booksellers' sale, and a second edition followed in January 1860.
textes.En 1871, dans La Filiation de l'homme, D: In 1871, in The Descent of Man, Darwin applied evolution to our species. He explained the gap between humans and the other primates by intermediate forms that have died out.
textes.La sélection naturelle est présentée pou: Natural selection was first presented on 1 July 1858 at the Linnean Society of London, with an essay by Wallace and extracts from Darwin read together.
textes.En 1956, le géochimiste Clair Patterson: In 1956, geochemist Clair Patterson dated the Earth at 4.55 billion years, using lead from the Canyon Diablo meteorite. Along the way he discovered lead pollution, and later fought against leaded petrol.
textes.Le botaniste Hugo de Vries forge le mot: Botanist Hugo de Vries coined the word "mutation" for sudden variations, in The Mutation Theory (1901-1903). He had spotted them in evening primrose, found in an abandoned potato field.
textes.L'archéoptéryx, fossile à plumes, est tr: Archaeopteryx, a feathered fossil, was found in 1861 in Germany. From 1868, Thomas Huxley linked it to dinosaurs, an idea revived in 1969 by John Ostrom and confirmed by the feathered dinosaurs of China in the 1990s.
textes.En 1858, Wallace écrit son essai sur l'î: In 1858, Wallace wrote his essay on the island of Ternate, in Indonesia, while recovering from a fever, and sent it to Darwin. Darwin received it on 18 June and wrote that Wallace "could not have made a better short abstract".
textes.C'est Georges Cuvier qui, en 1796, prouv: It was Georges Cuvier who, in 1796, proved that species really had died out, by comparing living elephants with fossil mammoths. Before him, extinction was still debated.
textes.Darwin passe environ cinq semaines aux G: Darwin spent about five weeks on the Galápagos during the Beagle voyage, but paid little attention to the small birds. In January 1837, ornithologist John Gould revealed that they were all finches of a new group.
textes.En 1980, Luis et Walter Alvarez trouvent: In 1980, Luis and Walter Alvarez found, in the end-Cretaceous layer all over the Earth, hundreds of times more iridium than normal. They concluded an asteroid had struck; the Chicxulub crater, in Yucatán, was found later.
textes.Entre 1856 et 1863, Mendel cultive envir: Between 1856 and 1863, Mendel grew about 28,000 plants, mostly peas, in the garden of St Thomas's Abbey in Brno. His work was ignored until 1900, when de Vries and Correns found the same laws.
textes.Le mot « gène » est forgé par le botanis: The word "gene" was coined by Danish botanist Wilhelm Johannsen, in a 1909 book where he also invented "genotype" and "phenotype". No one yet knew that genes were made of DNA.
textes.Mendel présente ses résultats en 1865 à: Mendel presented his results in 1865 to the Natural History Society of Brno and published them in 1866: a dominant trait always masks its recessive alternative. The paper stayed almost forgotten for more than thirty years.
textes.Le tableau qui sert à ce calcul porte le: The grid used for this calculation is named after Reginald Punnett, who devised it in 1905, a few years after Mendel's rediscovery. The first published diagrams date from 1906.
textes.L'article de Watson et Crick paraît dans: Watson and Crick's paper appeared in Nature on 25 April 1953, barely two pages long. It contains a famous understatement: "It has not escaped our notice" that this pairing suggests how DNA is copied.
textes.À la fin des années 1940, le biochimiste: In the late 1940s, biochemist Erwin Chargaff measured that there is always as much adenine as thymine, and as much guanine as cytosine. These "Chargaff's rules" guided Watson and Crick.
textes.Walther Flemming publie à partir de 1878: Walther Flemming published his observations of cell division from 1878 onwards, gathering them in a book in 1882. He named "chromatin" the material that takes up dyes; Wilhelm von Waldeyer later named chromosomes.
textes.Francis Galton utilise les jumeaux pour: Francis Galton used twins to untangle nature and nurture in the late 19th century. But it was only in 1924 that Hermann Siemens clearly distinguished identical from fraternal twins.
textes.En 1905, la biologiste américaine Nettie: In 1905, American biologist Nettie Stevens discovered in the mealworm a small chromosome, the future Y, whose presence decides sex. Edmund Wilson, working in parallel, long received the credit alone.
textes.En 1926, Hermann Muller montre que les r: In 1926, Hermann Muller showed that X-rays cause mutations in fruit flies. Awarded the Nobel Prize in 1946, he went on to warn about the dangers of fallout from nuclear tests.
textes.Avant le projet Génome humain, lancé en: Before the Human Genome Project, launched in 1990, our gene count was estimated at 80,000 to 140,000. The project, declared complete on 14 April 2003, found far fewer: about 20,000 protein-coding genes.
textes.Le prix récompense un article de 2012 da: The prize rewarded a 2012 paper in Science, in which Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed that Cas9 can be guided by an RNA to cut DNA wherever one wants.
textes.La Fabrica de Vésale, parue en 1543 quan: Vesalius's Fabrica, published in 1543 when he was 28, opens with the skeleton, which he saw as the framework of the body. Its plates come from human, not animal, dissections.
textes.Harvey publie De motu cordis en 1628 à F: Harvey published De motu cordis in 1628 in Frankfurt, home of a major book fair. One critic wrote that he would "rather err with Galen than proclaim the truth with Harvey": it took about twenty years for the idea to be accepted.
textes.En 1661, Marcello Malpighi observe au mi: In 1661, Marcello Malpighi looked at frog lungs under the microscope: he discovered capillaries and described the alveoli, which he compared to the holes of a honeycomb.
textes.Dès 1840, Friedrich Hünefeld décrit le r: As early as 1840, Friedrich Hünefeld described haemoglobin's role in carrying oxygen. In 1959, Max Perutz worked out its structure, earning him the 1962 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
textes.Dans la médecine d'Hippocrate puis de Ga: In the medicine of Hippocrates and later Galen, yellow bile and black bile were two of the body's four "humours", along with blood and phlegm. This theory dominated Western medicine for more than 2,000 years.
textes.En 1602, le médecin italien Santorio San: In 1602, Italian physician Santorio Santorio invented the pulsilogium, an instrument to measure the pulse, probably the first precision machine in the history of medicine.
textes.Le 30 juillet 1921 à Toronto, Banting et: On 30 July 1921 in Toronto, Banting and Best lowered a diabetic dog's blood sugar with a pancreatic extract. In January 1922, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson became the first patient treated.
textes.Le mythe des 10 % circule dès les années: The 10% myth was circulating by the 1920s in self-help books. In 1936, the foreword to a Dale Carnegie bestseller wrongly attributed it to psychologist William James.
Vesalius was 28 when the Fabrica came out. He then left Padua, where he had taught since 1537, to become a physician at the imperial court of Charles V.
textes.En 1628, William Harvey calcule que le c: In 1628, William Harvey calculated that the heart pumps about 225 kg of blood a day, more than the body's weight, even with low estimates. So the liver cannot be making all that blood, as Galen believed: blood goes round in a loop.
textes.Les petits filtres du rein portent le no: The kidney's small filters bear the name of Marcello Malpighi, the Italian anatomist who named them. He also discovered blood capillaries in 1661.
textes.C'est Jenner qui forge en 1798 l'express: It was Jenner who coined the phrase Variolae vaccinae, "smallpox of the cow", in 1798. In 1881, Louis Pasteur proposed calling all protective inoculations "vaccines", in Jenner's honour.
textes.Fleming découvre la pénicilline en septe: Fleming discovered penicillin in September 1928, a substance that kills bacteria. In his 1945 Nobel lecture, he already warned that a patient who underdoses himself can make microbes resistant.
textes.En 1898, Martinus Beijerinck appelle l'a: In 1898, Martinus Beijerinck called the tobacco mosaic agent a contagium vivum fluidum, a "contagious living fluid", and named it a virus. In 1935, Wendell Stanley crystallised it: it is a particle, not a liquid.
textes.Le « B » des lymphocytes B vient de la b: The "B" of B cells comes from the bursa of Fabricius, an organ found in birds, not from bone marrow. They were discovered there in chickens, in a 1956 paper.
textes.Semmelweis ne sait pas expliquer pourquo: Semmelweis could not explain why washing worked, and his colleagues rejected him. Committed to an asylum in 1865, he died fourteen days later; today he is called the "saviour of mothers".
textes.En 1885, Louis Pasteur, chimiste et non: In 1885, Louis Pasteur, a chemist rather than a doctor, inoculated Joseph Meister, aged 9, who had been bitten by a dog believed to be rabid. The boy did not develop rabies; as an adult, he became caretaker of the Pasteur Institute.
textes.Robert Koch annonce sa découverte le 24: Robert Koch announced his discovery on 24 March 1882 in Berlin, to a small group of scientists. That date has become World Tuberculosis Day.
textes.Le dernier cas naturel de variole est Al: The last natural case of smallpox was Ali Maow Maalin, a hospital cook in Merca, Somalia, in October 1977. After recovering, he went on to vaccinate children against polio.
textes.L'expression « immunité de troupeau » vi: The phrase "herd immunity" comes from vets: American Daniel Elmer Salmon used it as early as 1894 for herds of pigs. It moved on to human diseases in the late 1920s.
textes.En 1868, le médecin allemand Carl Wunder: In 1868, German physician Carl Wunderlich set normal temperature at 37 °C and stated that "fever is not a disease, but a symptom". Today the average is estimated a little lower, around 36.8 °C.
textes.En 1880, à l'hôpital militaire de Consta: In 1880, at the military hospital in Constantine, Algeria, Alphonse Laveran discovered the malaria parasite in a patient's blood (Nobel 1907). Ronald Ross proved the mosquito's role in 1898.
textes.En 1940, avant même que la pénicilline s: In 1940, even before penicillin was used on patients, Abraham and Chain isolated from E. coli an enzyme that destroys it, penicillinase. Resistance already existed in nature.
textes.En 1779, Jan Ingenhousz montre que les p: In 1779, Jan Ingenhousz showed that plants only "restore" spoiled air in sunlight: the first glimpse of photosynthesis, the engine of all producers.
textes.Le dernier livre scientifique de Darwin,: Darwin's last scientific book, published in October 1881, is about earthworms and how they recycle soil. Thousands of copies sold within weeks.
textes.Haeckel forge le mot dans un livre de 18: Haeckel coined the word in an 1866 book, General Morphology of Organisms. He took it from the Greek oikos, house: ecology is the study of living things' "home".
textes.La règle des 10 % vient de Raymond Linde: The 10% rule comes from Raymond Lindeman, in a 1942 paper based on his thesis about a small lake in Minnesota. First rejected as "too generalized", it was published thanks to Hutchinson's support; Lindeman died aged 26.
textes.Les derniers loups de Yellowstone avaien: Yellowstone's last wolves had been killed in 1926. In March 1995, 14 wolves captured in Canada were released in the Lamar Valley, then 17 more in 1996.
textes.Dès 1856, l'Américaine Eunice Foote mont: As early as 1856, American Eunice Foote showed that carbon dioxide and water vapour trap heat from the sun. In 1859, John Tyndall measured their absorption of infrared and proved the greenhouse effect experimentally.
textes.Robert Paine retire les étoiles de mer d: Robert Paine removed starfish from a rocky shore at Makah Bay, in the United States: mussels took over, and 15 species fell to 8 in three years. In 1969 he drew from it the idea of a keystone species.
textes.Printemps silencieux paraît le 27 septem: Silent Spring came out on 27 September 1962, and the chemical industry attacked Rachel Carson even before its release. The United States banned DDT for farm use in 1972.
textes.Le premier blanchissement massif reconnu: The first mass bleaching recognised worldwide dates from 1998: in the Indian Ocean, 80% of corals bleached and 20% died. In 2016, it killed 29 to 50% of the Great Barrier Reef's corals.
textes.En mars 1958, Charles David Keeling comm: In March 1958, Charles David Keeling began measuring carbon dioxide in the air atop Mauna Loa, Hawaii: 313 ppm. By November 2018, the curve had reached 406 ppm.
textes.En 1958, l'écologue anglais Charles Elto: In 1958, English ecologist Charles Elton published The Ecology of Invasions by Animals and Plants, the first book to warn about the damage done by invasive species. He was the one who had introduced the food chain in 1927.
textes.Le chiffre de 31 % vient des évaluations: The 31% figure comes from the FAO's global forest assessments. Between 1990 and 2020, the world's forests lost 178 million hectares, but net loss slowed: 7.8 million hectares a year in the 1990s, 4.7 million in 2010-2020.
textes.Mullis fait la démonstration de la PCR l: Mullis demonstrated PCR on 16 December 1983, at Cetus in California, and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. It became practical thanks to the enzyme of a bacterium found in 1969 in a Yellowstone hot spring.
textes.Les drôles de répétitions de l'ADN qu'on: The odd DNA repeats now called CRISPR were first described in 1987 in the bacterium E. coli, by a Japanese team. Nobody then knew what they were for.
textes.Dolly naît le 5 juillet 1996 à l'Institu: Dolly was born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute, in Scotland, after 277 attempts. Cloned from a mammary gland cell, she was named after the singer Dolly Parton.
textes.Katalin Karikó a longtemps travaillé sur: Katalin Karikó worked on messenger RNA for years without funding: her university demoted her in 1995. Her 2005 discovery with Drew Weissman, rejected by Nature and Science, won them the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
textes.L'insuline humaine fabriquée par génie g: Human insulin made by genetic engineering, developed by Genentech in 1978 and sold by Eli Lilly as Humulin, was approved in 1982: the first genetically engineered medicine.
textes.Lancé officiellement en 1990, le projet: Officially launched in 1990, the Human Genome Project was declared complete on 14 April 2003, two years ahead of schedule. It cost about $2.7 billion, less than the expected $3 billion.
textes.Le premier OGM est une bactérie rendue r: The first GMO was a bacterium made resistant to an antibiotic by Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen in 1973. Then came the transgenic mouse in 1974 and the Flavr Savr tomato, the first GM food sold, in 1994.
textes.En 1988, Colin Pitchfork devient le prem: In 1988, Colin Pitchfork became the first murderer convicted thanks to his DNA profile, for two murders in Leicestershire. An earlier suspect, who had confessed, was innocent.
textes.En 2006, Shinya Yamanaka transforme des: In 2006, Shinya Yamanaka turned adult mouse cells into stem cells with just four genes, then human cells in 2007. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize with John Gurdon.
textes.La découverte clé de Karikó et Weissman,: Karikó and Weissman's key discovery, in 2005, was to replace uridine in RNA with pseudouridine so it no longer alarms the immune system. It won them the Nobel Prize in Medicine, announced on 2 October 2023.
