textes.En 2005, on comprend que les morceaux d': In 2005, it was understood that the DNA fragments stored in CRISPR come from viruses that attacked the bacterium. Experimental proof of this bacterial immune system came in 2007.
textes.En 1974, les chercheurs du monde entier: In 1974, researchers worldwide paused their recombinant DNA experiments until an international conference could be held. Asilomar brought together about 140 participants in February 1975, mostly biologists, but also lawyers and doctors.
textes.Percer un trou dans le crâne d'un vivant: Drilling a hole in a living person's skull
textes.C'est peut-être la plus ancienne chirurg: It is perhaps the oldest surgery attested by archaeology, 7,000 to 10,000 years old.
textes.La trépanation remonte à 7 000 à 10 000: Trepanation goes back 7,000 to 10,000 years; 70% of trepanned skulls show healing.
textes.La plupart des crânes trépanés retrouvés: Most trepanned skulls found show that the patient survived.
textes.Vrai. Sur environ 70 % d'entre eux, l'os: True. On about 70% of them, bone healed around the hole, which takes time: the patient lived for weeks, months or years.
textes.Sur un site funéraire français de 6500 a: At a French burial site from 6500 BC, how many trepanned skulls were found out of 120?
textes.40 sur 120, soit un tiers : la trépanati: 40 out of 120, one third: trepanation was nothing exceptional.
textes.Sur un site français de 6500 av. J.-C.,: At a French site from 6500 BC, 40 skulls out of 120 bear a trepanation hole.
textes.Pourquoi pense-t-on que Shanidar 1, un N: Why do we think Shanidar 1, a Neanderthal, was cared for by his kin?
textes.Il a longtemps survécu à des blessures h: He survived disabling injuries for a long time
textes.Une peinture le montre soigné: A painting shows him being treated
textes.Bras brisé et atrophié, avant-bras perdu: Broken, withered arm, forearm lost: his bones healed, he lived like this for a long time, which implies help.
textes.Shanidar 1, au bras droit atrophié, a su: Shanidar 1, with a withered right arm, survived his injuries for a long time; according to Trinkaus, others helped him.
textes.Les fleurs de la tombe de Shanidar 4 pro: The flowers in the Shanidar 4 grave prove a flower funeral rite among Neanderthals.
textes.Faux. Le pollen a pu être apporté par de: False. The pollen may have been brought by burrowing rodents; the hypothesis of laid flowers is now strongly disputed.
textes.Le pollen de Shanidar 4 a peut-être été: The Shanidar 4 pollen may have been brought by rodents; for Pettitt, the deliberate placing of flowers is ruled out.
textes.Combien de tatouages porte Ötzi, l'homme: How many tattoos does Ötzi, the iceman, bear?
textes.61, souvent près des genoux et des chevi: 61, often near worn knees and ankles: perhaps a treatment for pain.
textes.Ötzi, trouvé le 19 septembre 1991 dans l: Ötzi, found on 19 September 1991 in the Ötztal Alps, bears 61 tattoos.
textes.Quel champignon médicinal Ötzi transport: What medicinal fungus was Ötzi carrying?
textes.Le polypore du bouleau a des vertus verm: Birch polypore has deworming properties; and Ötzi did have whipworms in his gut.
textes.Ötzi portait un polypore du bouleau, aux: Ötzi carried a birch polypore, with anthelmintic properties; he had whipworms.
textes.D'une flèche qui lui a brisé l'omoplate: An arrow that shattered his shoulder blade
textes.La flèche a brisé l'omoplate ; il s'est: The arrow shattered the shoulder blade; he bled to death. He may also have taken a blow to the head.
textes.On pense qu'Ötzi s'est vidé de son sang: Ötzi is thought to have bled to death after an arrow shattered his shoulder blade.
textes.Dans quelle grotte d'Irak a-t-on trouvé: In which cave in Iraq were Neanderthals found, including a cared-for injured man?
textes.Fouillée par Ralph Solecki de 1957 à 196: Excavated by Ralph Solecki from 1957 to 1961, it yielded nine Neanderthals.
textes.Vrai. L'Empire inca s'en servait notamme: True. The Inca Empire used it notably against epilepsy; in Peru, 11 to 40% of skulls found, depending on the region, bear its mark.
textes.Les Incas utilisaient la trépanation con: The Incas used trepanation against epilepsy; in Peru, 11 to 40% of skulls bear it.
textes.Combien de cas de blessures décrit le pa: How many injury cases does the Edwin Smith papyrus describe?
textes.48, rangés de la tête vers le bas du cor: 48, sorted from the head down the body.
The Edwin Smith papyrus, around 1600 BC, describes 48 cases and three verdicts.
textes.Quels sont les trois verdicts du papyrus: What are the three verdicts of the Edwin Smith papyrus?
textes.Je soignerai, je lutterai, on ne soigne: I will treat, I will contend, not to be treated
textes.Le médecin décide d'abord s'il peut agir: The physician first decides whether he can act: it is a prognosis, made before treatment.
textes.Le papyrus Edwin Smith contient les prem: The Edwin Smith papyrus contains the first known descriptions of the meninges.
textes.Vrai, ainsi que du liquide qui entoure l: True, and of the fluid around the brain.
textes.Le papyrus Edwin Smith contient les prem: The Edwin Smith papyrus contains the first known descriptions of cranial structures, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid.
textes.Combien de mètres mesure environ le papy: About how many metres long is the Ebers papyrus?
textes.Le papyrus Ebers, vers 1550 av. J.-C., f: The Ebers papyrus, around 1550 BC, is 20 metres long and gathers over 800 remedies.
textes.Qui est le plus ancien médecin connu par: Who is the oldest physician known by name?
textes.Hesy-Ra dirigeait les dentistes de Djése: Hesy-Ra headed Djoser's dentists: the first physician and first dentist known by name.
textes.Hesy-Ra, chef des dentistes de Djéser, e: Hesy-Ra, Djoser's chief dentist, is the first dentist known by name and the oldest recorded physician.
textes.Merit-Ptah fut la première femme médecin: Merit-Ptah was the first woman doctor in history.
textes.Faux. Elle naît d'une confusion dans un: False. She was born of a confusion in a 1937 book, then copied. The attested woman doctor is probably Peseshet.
textes.Merit-Ptah est une invention née d'une c: Merit-Ptah is an invention born of a confusion in a 1937 book; the real woman doctor is probably Peseshet.
textes.Selon Hérodote, comment étaient organisé: According to Herodotus, how were Egyptian doctors organised?
textes.En spécialistes : yeux, dents, maladies: As specialists: eyes, teeth, internal diseases
textes.Hérodote décrit des soignants distincts: Herodotus describes distinct healers for each part of the body.
textes.Selon Hérodote, il y avait des soignants: According to Herodotus, there were distinct healers for eyes, teeth and internal diseases.
textes.Dans quelle ville Edwin Smith achète-t-i: In which city did Edwin Smith buy his papyrus, in 1862?
textes.À Louxor ; il faudra attendre 1930 pour: In Luxor; the first translation, by James Henry Breasted, had to wait until 1930.
textes.Edwin Smith achète le papyrus à Louxor e: Edwin Smith bought the papyrus in Luxor in 1862; Breasted translated it in 1930.
textes.Le papyrus Ebers traite aussi de contrac: The Ebers papyrus also deals with contraception and diagnosing pregnancy.
textes.Vrai. Il contient des chapitres de gynéc: True. It contains gynaecology chapters alongside its hundreds of remedies.
textes.Dans quel ordre le papyrus Edwin Smith r: In what order does the Edwin Smith papyrus sort its cases?
textes.De la tête vers le bas du corps: From the head down the body
textes.Tête, cou, bras, torse : un ordre anatom: Head, neck, arms, torso: a descending anatomical order.
textes.Sur quelle île est né Hippocrate ?: On which island was Hippocrates born?
textes.À Kos, vers 460 av. J.-C. ; il serait mo: On Kos, around 460 BC; he is said to have died in Larissa, in Thessaly.
textes.Hippocrate, né vers 460 av. J.-C. à Kos,: Hippocrates, born around 460 BC on Kos, separated medicine from religion.
textes.Pour le traité De la maladie sacrée, l'é: For the treatise On the Sacred Disease, epilepsy is sent by the gods.
textes.Faux. Elle « n'est pas plus divine que l: False. It "is not any more divine than other diseases: it has a natural cause", and the author places it in the brain.
textes.De la maladie sacrée affirme que l'épile: On the Sacred Disease asserts that epilepsy has a natural cause, the brain.
textes.Laquelle n'est pas l'une des quatre hume: Which is not one of the four humours?
textes.Les quatre : sang, phlegme, bile jaune,: The four: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile. Black bile gave "melancholy".
textes.Les quatre humeurs sont le sang, le phle: The four humours are blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile; the theory was abandoned in 1858.
textes.La formule « d'abord, ne pas nuire » fig: The phrase "first, do no harm" appears in the Hippocratic Oath.
textes.Faux. Le serment dit « je ne ferai ni to: False. The oath says "I will do no harm or injustice"; the Latin primum non nocere comes from elsewhere.
textes.Le serment dit « je ne ferai ni tort ni: The oath says "I will do no harm or injustice"; "primum non nocere" is not in it.
textes.En quelle année la théorie des humeurs e: In what year was the humoral theory definitively abandoned?
textes.En 1858 : plus de deux mille ans après H: In 1858: more than two thousand years after Hippocrates.
textes.Par qui le médecin jure-t-il au début du: By whom does the physician swear at the start of the oath?
textes.« Je jure par Apollon médecin, par Asclé: "I swear by Apollo Healer, by Asclepius, by Hygieia, by Panacea", then by all the gods and goddesses.
textes.Quelle humeur est, selon la théorie, cha: Which humour is, according to the theory, hot and dry?
textes.Sang chaud et humide, bile jaune chaude: Blood hot and moist, yellow bile hot and dry, black bile cold and dry, phlegm cold and moist.
textes.Environ combien de traités compte le Cor: About how many treatises does the Hippocratic Corpus contain?
textes.Environ soixante-dix, écrits par plusieu: About seventy, written by several authors: nineteen by one count.
textes.Le Corpus hippocratique réunit environ 7: The Hippocratic Corpus gathers about 70 treatises; Ermerins counts nineteen authors.
textes.Dans le serment, le médecin promet de ne: In the oath, the physician promises not to operate, even on those suffering from stone.
textes.Vrai : « je n'utiliserai pas le fer ». É: True: "I will not use the knife". Surprising, as other treatises of the Corpus describe operations.
textes.Des doigts en baguette de tambour, signe: Clubbed fingers, a sign of lung or heart disease
textes.Les doigts qui prêtent serment: The fingers that take the oath
textes.Une façon de prendre le pouls: A way of taking the pulse
textes.L'hippocratisme digital reste un signe d: Clubbing remains a sign of chronic lung disease or heart disease.
textes.Les doigts en baguette de tambour sont a: Clubbed fingers are called Hippocratic fingers, a sign of chronic lung disease.
textes.Pourquoi Alexandrie est-elle la ville de: Why was Alexandria the city of the first human dissections?
textes.Ailleurs, ouvrir des cadavres humains ét: Elsewhere, opening human cadavers was forbidden
textes.La dissection humaine était interdite pr: Human dissection was banned almost everywhere, except in Alexandria.
textes.Hérophile, à Alexandrie, est le premier: Herophilos, in Alexandria, was the first to dissect human cadavers methodically.
textes.Où Hérophile place-t-il l'intelligence ?: Where did Herophilos place the intellect?
textes.Dans le cerveau, et non dans le cœur ; i: In the brain, not the heart; he also distinguished the cerebrum from the cerebellum.
textes.Hérophile propose que le cerveau, et non: Herophilos proposed that the brain, not the heart, houses the intellect.
textes.Avec quoi Hérophile mesurait-il le pouls: What did Herophilos measure the pulse with?
textes.Une clepsydre : l'eau qui s'écoule mesur: A clepsydra: flowing water measures the time between beats.
textes.Pour mesurer le pouls, Hérophile utilisa: To measure the pulse, Herophilos used a water clock.
Herophilos gave the duodenum its name.
textes.Vrai : c'est lui qui nomme cette premièr: True: he named this first part of the small intestine.
textes.Hérophile a nommé le duodénum, partie de: Herophilos named the duodenum, part of the small intestine.
textes.Érasistrate pensait que les artères tran: Erasistratus thought the arteries carried blood.
textes.Faux : il les croyait remplies d'air, le: False: he believed they were filled with air, pneuma. He was right about the heart, though, which he took for a pump.
textes.Érasistrate voit dans le cœur une pompe: Erasistratus saw the heart as a pump but believed the arteries carried air.
textes.À quoi Érasistrate compare-t-il le cœur: What did Erasistratus compare the heart to?
textes.Le cœur n'est pas le centre des sensatio: The heart is not the centre of sensations: it is a pump, with valves.
textes.Selon le récit, quelle était la maladie: According to the story, what was Prince Antiochus' illness, guessed by Erasistratus?
textes.Le roi Séleucos finit par céder Stratoni: King Seleucus ended up giving Stratonice to his son.
textes.Érasistrate diagnostique le mal d'amour: Erasistratus diagnosed Antiochus' lovesickness for Stratonice; Seleucus gave her up.
textes.Selon Tertullien, combien de prisonniers: According to Tertullian, how many living prisoners did Herophilos dissect?
textes.600, selon Tertullien, bien plus tard. L: 600, according to Tertullian, much later. Historians strongly doubt it.
textes.Tertullien affirme qu'Hérophile a vivise: Tertullian claims Herophilos vivisected at least 600 prisoners; historians dispute it.
textes.On peut lire aujourd'hui les livres d'Hé: Herophilos' books can be read today.
textes.Faux : tous sont perdus. On les connaît: False: all are lost. They are known through Galen's quotations.
textes.Les ouvrages d'Hérophile sont tous perdu: Herophilos' works are all lost; Galen quotes them extensively.
textes.Que préférait Érasistrate à la saignée ?: What did Erasistratus prefer to bloodletting?
textes.Érasistrate avait une aversion pour la s: Erasistratus had an aversion to bloodletting and purgatives, preferring diet and exercise.
textes.Quels patients Galien soigne-t-il à ses: Which patients did Galen treat early on, in Pergamon?
textes.Leurs plaies étaient pour lui des « fenê: Their wounds were for him "windows into the body".
textes.Galien, né en 129 à Pergame, soigne les: Galen, born in 129 in Pergamon, treated gladiators then emperors.
textes.Quels animaux Galien dissèque-t-il surto: Which animals did Galen mainly dissect?
textes.La dissection humaine étant interdite, i: Human dissection being forbidden, he studied apes, then pigs.
textes.Ses descriptions viennent surtout de dis: His descriptions came mainly from dissecting Barbary macaques; he switched to pigs to avoid prosecution.
textes.Qu'a montré Galien avec un porc qui crie: What did Galen show with a squealing pig?
textes.Que le cerveau commande la voix: That the brain controls the voice
textes.Que le cœur est une pompe: That the heart is a pump
textes.En ligaturant le nerf laryngé récurrent,: By tying off the recurrent laryngeal nerve, he silenced the animal: the voice depends on the brain, through the nerves.
textes.Galien ligature le nerf laryngé récurren: Galen tied off the recurrent laryngeal nerve of a squealing pig: the voice depends on the brain.
textes.Galien pensait que le sang était fabriqu: Galen thought blood was made by the liver.
textes.Vrai. Et que de petits trous dans la clo: True. And that small holes in the heart's septum let blood through: two errors.
textes.Galien croyait que le sang naissait dans: Galen believed blood originated in the liver and that the heart's septum was pierced; uncontested until 1543.
textes.En quelle année Vésale publie-t-il l'ana: In what year did Vesalius publish the anatomy that finally challenged Galen?
textes.En 1543, avec la Fabrica, tirée de disse: In 1543, with the Fabrica, drawn from human dissections.
textes.Environ combien de millions de mots de G: About how many million words by Galen have come down to us?
textes.Environ 3 millions, sans doute moins du: About 3 million, probably less than a third of what he wrote.
textes.Les œuvres conservées de Galien font env: Galen's surviving works come to about 3 million words, probably less than a third of the total.
textes.De quel futur empereur Galien est-il le: Which future emperor was Galen physician to in Rome?
textes.Marc Aurèle le laisse à Rome pour soigne: Marcus Aurelius left him in Rome to treat his heir, Commodus.
textes.Marc Aurèle laisse Galien à Rome comme m: Marcus Aurelius left Galen in Rome as physician to the imperial heir, Commodus.
textes.Galien est le premier à distinguer le sa: Galen was the first to distinguish dark venous blood from bright arterial blood.
textes.Vrai, même s'il se trompait sur le chemi: True, even though he was wrong about the path of blood in the body.
textes.Galien fut le premier à reconnaître la d: Galen was the first to recognise the difference between dark venous and bright arterial blood.
textes.Dans quelle ville est né Galien ?: In which city was Galen born?
textes.À Pergame, aujourd'hui Bergama en Turqui: In Pergamon, today Bergama in Turkey, in 129.
textes.Les descriptions anatomiques de Galien o: Galen's anatomical descriptions were challenged as early as the Middle Ages.
textes.Faux : elles restent incontestées jusqu': False: they remained uncontested until 1543 and Vesalius. Ibn al-Nafis had however contradicted Galen on the heart.
textes.D'où vient la peau qui sert à refaire le: Where does the skin used to rebuild the nose come from, in the Sushruta Samhita?
textes.Un lambeau de la joue : c'est la premièr: A flap from the cheek: it is the first rhinoplasty described in writing.
textes.La Sushruta Samhita donne la première de: The Sushruta Samhita gives the first written description of a cheek-flap rhinoplasty.
textes.Sur quoi les élèves de Sushruta s'exerce: What did Sushruta's students practise on before operating?
textes.Couper juste s'apprend d'abord sur des l: Cutting right is first learned on vegetables and animals.
textes.La Sushruta Samhita fait s'exercer les é: The Sushruta Samhita has students practise on gourds and dead animals.
textes.Combien de maladies décrit la Sushruta S: How many illnesses does the Sushruta Samhita describe?
textes.1 120 maladies, et 700 plantes médicinal: 1,120 illnesses, and 700 medicinal plants, in 186 chapters.
textes.La Sushruta Samhita compte 186 chapitres: The Sushruta Samhita has 186 chapters, 1,120 illnesses and 700 medicinal plants.
textes.Combien de chapitres compte la Sushruta: How many chapters does the Sushruta Samhita have?
textes.La Sushruta Samhita a été écrite d'un se: The Sushruta Samhita was written in one go, by one author.
textes.Faux. Commencée avant notre ère, elle a: False. Begun before the common era, it was revised around the 3rd-4th centuries: a text built up over centuries.
textes.La rédaction commence dans les derniers: Writing began in the last centuries BC; a recension dates from the 3rd-4th centuries AD.
textes.Dans quelle ville la Sushruta Samhita es: In which city was the Sushruta Samhita translated into Arabic, in the 8th century?
textes.À Bagdad, au début du VIIIe siècle, sous: In Baghdad, in the early 8th century, under the title Kitab Shah Shun al-Hindi.
textes.La Sushruta Samhita est traduite en arab: The Sushruta Samhita was translated into Arabic in Baghdad in the early 8th century.
textes.Pour Sushruta, qui veut connaître l'anat: For Sushruta, anyone who wants to know anatomy must dissect a body himself.
textes.Vrai : préparer un corps et le disséquer: True: prepare a body and dissect it, rather than relying on books.
textes.Le texte demande à qui veut connaître l': The text asks anyone wishing to know anatomy to prepare a body and dissect it.
textes.Combien de plantes médicinales décrit la: How many medicinal plants does the Sushruta Samhita describe?
textes.700 plantes, de quoi remplir une pharmac: 700 plants, enough to fill a pharmacy.
textes.Quel chirurgien de Bologne aurait, au XV: Which Bologna surgeon, in the 16th century, reportedly knew Indian rhinoplasty techniques?
textes.Tagliacozzi, et avant lui la famille Bra: Tagliacozzi, and before him the Branca family in Sicily, according to sources whose evidence remains disputed.
textes.La famille Branca et Gaspare Tagliacozzi: The Branca family and Gaspare Tagliacozzi reportedly knew the rhinoplasty techniques; the evidence is disputed.
textes.Le manuscrit Bower compte Sushruta parmi: The Bower manuscript counts Sushruta among the ten sages of the Himalayas.
textes.Vrai : ce manuscrit des IVe-Ve siècles l: True: this 4th-5th century manuscript already mentions him.
textes.Le manuscrit Bower, des IVe-Ve siècles,: The Bower manuscript, 4th-5th centuries, names Sushruta among ten sages residing in the Himalayas.
textes.Sous quelle forme est écrit le Huangdi N: In what form is the Huangdi Neijing written?
textes.Un dialogue entre l'Empereur jaune et se: A dialogue between the Yellow Emperor and his physicians
textes.Une liste de recettes sans texte: A list of recipes without text
textes.Des questions-réponses, surtout avec le: Questions and answers, mostly with the minister Qibo.
The Huangdi Neijing, from the 1st century BC, has two parts of 81 chapters in question-and-answer form.
textes.Combien de chapitres compte chacune des: How many chapters does each of the two parts of the Huangdi Neijing have?
textes.81, dans le Suwen comme dans le Lingshu: 81, in the Suwen as in the Lingshu: 81 = 9 × 9.
textes.Quelle partie du Huangdi Neijing détaill: Which part of the Huangdi Neijing details acupuncture?
textes.Le Lingshu traite en détail de l'acupunc: The Lingshu discusses acupuncture in detail.
textes.Que serait le mafeisan de Hua Tuo ?: What was Hua Tuo's mafeisan said to be?
textes.Un breuvage pour endormir avant d'opérer: A potion to put people to sleep before operating.
textes.Hua Tuo, vers 140-208, utilise le mafeis: Hua Tuo, around 140-208, used mafeisan, the first anaesthetic; Cao Cao had him executed.
textes.Hua Tuo a opéré le bras du général Guan: Hua Tuo operated on General Guan Yu's arm.
textes.Faux. La scène vient du Roman des Trois: False. The scene comes from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, in the 14th century; Hua Tuo died in 208, ten years before the battle of Fancheng.
textes.L'opération de Guan Yu par Hua Tuo vient: Hua Tuo's operation on Guan Yu comes from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms; Hua Tuo died a decade before Fancheng.
textes.Qu'a fait Hua Tuo de son livre avant d'ê: What did Hua Tuo do with his book before being executed?
textes.Il l'a offert à l'empereur: He gave it to the emperor
textes.Il demande du feu et brûle le rouleau :: He asked for fire and burned the scroll: his techniques are lost.
textes.Comment pratiquait-on la variolation en: How was variolation practised in China?
textes.En soufflant des croûtes de variole en p: By blowing powdered smallpox scabs up the nose
textes.Une variole légère, volontaire, pour évi: A mild, deliberate smallpox, to avoid the severe one.
textes.La Chine pratique la plus ancienne vario: China practised the oldest documented variolation, in the 16th century, by blowing scabs up the nose.
textes.Environ quel pourcentage des personnes q: About what percentage of people who caught smallpox died of it?
textes.Environ 30 %, contre 1 à 2 % des variolé: About 30%, against 1 to 2% of those variolated: the gamble was worth it.
textes.1 à 2 % des variolés mouraient, contre 3: 1 to 2% of those variolated died, against 30% of those who caught smallpox.
textes.En quelle année avant notre ère la tombe: In what year BC was the Mawangdui tomb, rich in medical texts, sealed?
textes.En 168 av. J.-C. ; ouverte en 1973, elle: In 168 BC; opened in 1973, it yielded the Prescriptions for Fifty-Two Ailments.
textes.La tombe 3 de Mawangdui, scellée en 168: Mawangdui tomb 3, sealed in 168 BC, was discovered in 1973 with unknown medical texts.
textes.La gymnastique de Hua Tuo imite cinq ani: Hua Tuo's exercises imitate five animals, including the tiger and the crane.
textes.Vrai : le tigre, le cerf, l'ours, le sin: True: the tiger, the deer, the bear, the ape and the crane.
textes.Hua Tuo développe une gymnastique d'aprè: Hua Tuo developed exercises from the movements of the tiger, deer, bear, ape and crane.
textes.Comment al-Razi choisit-il l'emplacement: How did al-Razi choose the site for a hospital in Baghdad?
textes.Là où il y avait le plus de malades: Where there were the most patients
textes.Un test simple de la salubrité de l'air,: A simple test of the healthiness of the air, district by district.
textes.Al-Razi choisit l'emplacement d'un hôpit: Al-Razi chose the site of a Baghdad hospital with hanging meat, and distinguished smallpox from measles.
textes.Quelles deux maladies al-Razi a-t-il été: Which two diseases was al-Razi one of the first to distinguish?
textes.Dans son traité De la variole et de la r: In his treatise On Smallpox and Measles.
textes.En quelle année Avicenne achève-t-il son: In what year did Avicenna complete his Canon of Medicine?
textes.En 1025 : cinq livres qui serviront de m: In 1025: five books that would serve as a textbook until the 18th century.
textes.Le Canon d'Avicenne, achevé en 1025, com: Avicenna's Canon, completed in 1025, has five books and seven rules for testing drugs.
textes.Combien de règles le Canon donne-t-il po: How many rules does the Canon give for testing a new drug?
textes.Sept règles : un ancêtre des essais clin: Seven rules: an ancestor of clinical trials.
textes.Le Canon d'Avicenne était encore enseign: Avicenna's Canon was still taught in Padua in 1715.
textes.Vrai, comme lecture de fond, près de sep: True, as background reading, nearly seven centuries after it was written.
textes.Le Canon est encore enseigné comme lectu: The Canon was still taught as background literature in Padua in 1715.
textes.Que décrit Ibn al-Nafis pour la première: What did Ibn al-Nafis describe for the first time?
textes.Le sang va du cœur droit aux poumons, pu: Blood goes from the right heart to the lungs, then to the left heart. The general circulation came with Harvey in 1628.
textes.Ibn al-Nafis décrit le premier la circul: Ibn al-Nafis first described pulmonary circulation and rejected Galen's holes in the septum.
textes.Ibn al-Nafis confirme les trous invisibl: Ibn al-Nafis confirmed Galen's invisible holes in the heart's septum.
textes.Faux : pour lui, la cloison est épaisse: False: for him, the septum is thick and has no passage.
textes.En quelle année retrouve-t-on à Berlin u: In what year was a manuscript by Ibn al-Nafis on pulmonary circulation found in Berlin?
textes.En 1924, par le médecin égyptien Muhyo A: In 1924, by the Egyptian physician Muhyo Al-Deen Altawi, at the Prussian State Library.
textes.En 1924, Muhyo Al-Deen Altawi découvre à: In 1924, Muhyo Al-Deen Altawi discovered a manuscript by Ibn al-Nafis in Berlin.
textes.En combien de volumes sont réunis les ca: In how many volumes are al-Razi's notebooks, al-Hawi, gathered?
textes.23 volumes, compilés après sa mort à par: 23 volumes, compiled after his death from his working notes.
textes.Al-Hawi, en 23 volumes, est une compilat: Al-Hawi, in 23 volumes, is a posthumous compilation of al-Razi's notebooks.
textes.Pour juger la saignée contre la méningit: To judge bloodletting against meningitis, al-Razi compared bled and unbled patients.
textes.Vrai : une comparaison entre deux groupe: True: a comparison between two groups, a central idea of the experimental method.
textes.Al-Razi compare l'évolution de malades a: Al-Razi compared the outcome of meningitis patients treated or not with bloodletting.
textes.En quelle année Harvey publie-t-il De Mo: In what year did Harvey publish De Motu Cordis?
textes.En 1628 : la circulation du sang entre d: In 1628: the circulation of blood entered the books.
textes.Harvey publie De Motu Cordis en 1628 : à: Harvey published De Motu Cordis in 1628: at 72 beats a minute, the heart sends out 540 pounds of blood an hour.
textes.Harvey compte 72 battements par minute e: Harvey counts 72 beats a minute and 2 ounces of blood per beat. How many pounds of blood does the heart send out per hour? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
textes.Débit = battements par minute × minutes: Flow = beats per minute × minutes × ounces per beat ÷ ounces per pound. Here: 72 × 60 × 2 ÷ 16 = 8,640 ÷ 16 = 540 pounds per hour. The reasoning is William Harvey's, in De Motu Cordis in 1628.
textes.Le cœur bat 1 000 fois par demi-heure. C: The heart beats 1,000 times every half hour. How many times does it beat in a day?
textes.Battements par jour = battements par dem: Beats per day = beats per half hour × half hours per day. Here: 1,000 × 48 = 48,000. This is the starting point of William Harvey's calculation, from which he derived 498 pounds of blood a day.
textes.Le cœur bat 1 000 fois par demi-heure :: The heart beats 1,000 times every half hour: the liver would have to produce 498 pounds of blood a day.
textes.Selon le calcul de Harvey, combien de sa: According to Harvey's calculation, how much blood would the liver have to make each day if blood did not circulate?
textes.498 livres, avec des chiffres volontaire: 498 pounds, with deliberately low figures: impossible, so blood goes round.
textes.Qui, maître de Harvey à Padoue, avait dé: Who, Harvey's teacher in Padua, had described the valves of the veins?
textes.Hieronymus Fabricius. Harvey comprend à: Hieronymus Fabricius. Harvey understood what they were for: blood only flows back towards the heart.
textes.Harvey étudie à Padoue, docteur le 25 av: Harvey studied in Padua, MD on 25 April 1602; his teacher Fabricius discovered the valves of the veins.
textes.Harvey a prédit l'existence des capillai: Harvey predicted the existence of capillaries.
textes.Faux, c'est une idée reçue. Pour lui, le: False, it is a common misconception. For him, blood soaks into the flesh and the veins take it back up.
textes.Harvey n'a pas prédit les capillaires, u: Harvey did not predict the existence of capillaries, a common misconception.
textes.En quelle année Malpighi voit-il le sang: In what year did Malpighi see blood in the capillaries of a frog's lung?
textes.En 1660, trois ans après la mort de Harv: In 1660, three years after Harvey's death.
In 1660, three years after Harvey's death, Malpighi saw blood moving in the capillaries of a frog's lung.
textes.Qu'arrive-t-il à la clientèle de Harvey: What happened to Harvey's practice after De Motu Cordis?
textes.Il « baissa fortement dans sa clientèle: He "fell mightily in his practice", but kept his career.
textes.Après les critiques de De Motu Cordis, H: After criticism of De Motu Cordis, Harvey "fell mightily in his practice".
textes.Quel roi d'Angleterre prend Harvey comme: Which King of England took Harvey as Physician Extraordinary in 1618?
textes.Jacques Ier, le 3 février 1618 ; puis Ch: James I, on 3 February 1618; then Charles I.
textes.Harvey est nommé médecin extraordinaire: Harvey was appointed Physician Extraordinary to James I on 3 February 1618.
textes.Michel Servet avait écrit dès 1553 que l: Michael Servetus had written as early as 1553 that blood goes from the heart to the lungs.
textes.Vrai, 75 ans avant De Motu Cordis. Ibn a: True, 75 years before De Motu Cordis. Ibn al-Nafis had written it in the 13th century.
textes.En 1553, Servet écrit que le sang va du: In 1553, Servetus wrote that blood flows from the heart to the lungs, where it mixes with air.
textes.Que voulait réfuter Redi avec ses bocaux: What did Redi want to refute with his jars of meat?
textes.La génération spontanée des asticots : i: The spontaneous generation of maggots: they come from flies' eggs.
textes.En 1668, Redi couvre trois bocaux de gaz: In 1668, Redi covered three jars with gauze: maggots only appeared in the open jars.
textes.En quelle année Redi publie-t-il ses exp: In what year did Redi publish his experiments on the generation of insects?
textes.En 1668, quand il est médecin des Médici: In 1668, when he was physician to the Medici.
textes.Avec quoi Redi couvre-t-il certains boca: What did Redi cover some jars with?
textes.Une gaze fine : l'air passe, les mouches: A fine gauze: air gets through, flies don't.
textes.Selon la recette de van Helmont, combien: According to van Helmont's recipe, how many days does it take to get mice from a dirty rag and wheat?
textes.21 jours, sans aucun témoin pour compare: 21 days, with no control to compare against.
textes.Van Helmont propose de faire des souris: Van Helmont proposed making mice with a dirty rag and wheat, in 21 days.
textes.Qu'a de particulier le flacon de Pasteur: What is special about Pasteur's flask in 1859?
textes.Un col courbé en col de cygne: A neck bent into a swan neck
textes.Le col courbé laisse entrer l'air mais r: The bent neck lets air in but holds back the dust.
textes.En 1859, Pasteur utilise un flacon à col: In 1859, Pasteur used a swan-neck flask: the bend stops the particles.
textes.Le flacon à col de cygne de Pasteur est: Pasteur's swan-neck flask is hermetically sealed.
textes.Faux : il reste ouvert à l'air. C'est la: False: it stays open to the air. It is the bend that stops the particles.
textes.En quelle année Needham voit-il ses boui: In what year did Needham see his boiled and sealed broths go cloudy?
textes.En 1745 : il y voit la preuve de la géné: In 1745: he saw it as proof of spontaneous generation.
textes.En 1745, Needham fait bouillir des bouil: In 1745, Needham boiled broths; sealed right after, they still went cloudy.
textes.Qui scelle ses bouillons en 1768 et ne v: Who sealed his broths in 1768 and saw nothing grow?
textes.Lazzaro Spallanzani. Restait une objecti: Lazzaro Spallanzani. One objection remained: what if air was necessary for life?
textes.En 1768, Spallanzani scelle son bouillon: In 1768, Spallanzani sealed his broth with less air and saw no growth.
textes.Redi a aussi montré que le venin des ser: Redi also showed that snake venom comes from their fangs.
textes.Vrai : et pas de la vésicule biliaire, c: True: and not from the gallbladder, as was believed.
textes.Redi montre que le venin des serpents vi: Redi showed that snake venom comes from the fangs, not the gallbladder.
textes.En quelle année l'Académie des sciences: In what year did the Academy of Sciences offer a prize on spontaneous generation, won by Pasteur?
textes.En 1862, trois ans après le col de cygne: In 1862, three years after the swan neck.
textes.En 1862, l'Académie française offre un p: In 1862, the French Academy offered a prize to whoever threw new light on spontaneous generation.
textes.Combien de pages compte la première édit: How many pages did the first edition of Systema Naturae have, in 1735?
textes.Douze pages. Les éditions suivantes enfl: Twelve pages. Later editions swelled to several volumes.
textes.Linné publie le Systema Naturae en 1735: Linnaeus published Systema Naturae in 1735 (twelve pages); Species Plantarum in 1753 founded plant names, the 1758 10th edition animal names.
textes.Quelle année sert de point de départ aux: Which year is the starting point for the scientific names of plants?
textes.Quel ouvrage de Linné sert de point de d: Which work by Linnaeus is the starting point for animal names?
textes.Comment est formé un nom d'espèce selon: How is a species name formed according to Linnaeus, like Homo sapiens?
textes.Le nom du découvreur puis le pays: The discoverer's name then the country
textes.Deux mots : Homo, le genre ; sapiens, l': Two words: Homo, the genus; sapiens, the species.
textes.Linné fonde la nomenclature binomiale :: Linnaeus founded binomial nomenclature: a genus name followed by a species name.
textes.Combien d'élèves Linné appelait-il ses «: How many students did Linnaeus call his "apostles"?
textes.17, envoyés herboriser sur tous les cont: 17, sent out to collect plants on every continent.
textes.Linné appelle 17 de ses élèves ses « apô: Linnaeus called 17 of his students his "apostles"; ennobled in 1761, he became Carl von Linné.
textes.Le spécimen type d'Homo sapiens est Linn: The type specimen of Homo sapiens is Linnaeus himself.
textes.Vrai : William Stearn l'a désigné en 195: True: William Stearn designated him in 1959, as he is the only human Linnaeus is known to have examined.
textes.En 1959, Stearn désigne Linné comme lect: In 1959, Stearn designated Linnaeus as the lectotype of Homo sapiens, the only specimen he is known to have examined.
textes.Une petite fleur des bois du Nord, bapti: A small northern woodland flower, named in his honour by Gronovius.
textes.Linnaea borealis, la linnée boréale, éta: Linnaea borealis, the twinflower, was Linnaeus's favourite plant; Gronovius named it in his honour.
textes.En quelle année Linné est-il anobli, dev: In what year was Linnaeus ennobled, becoming Carl von Linné?
textes.Vers quelle région Linné part-il en expé: To which region did Linnaeus set out on an expedition in 1732?
textes.Linné part d'Uppsala pour la Laponie le: Linnaeus set out from Uppsala for Lapland on 12 May 1732.
textes.La première édition du Systema Naturae a: The first edition of Systema Naturae was printed in Sweden.
textes.La première édition du Systema Naturae e: The first edition of Systema Naturae was printed in the Netherlands in 1735.
textes.Lind répartit 12 marins entre 6 traiteme: Lind split 12 sailors between 6 treatments. How many sailors per treatment?
textes.Marins par traitement = nombre de marins: Sailors per treatment = number of sailors ÷ number of treatments. Here: 12 ÷ 6 = 2. This split into equal groups is James Lind's, in 1747, aboard the Salisbury.
textes.Le 20 mai 1747, sur le Salisbury, Lind c: On 20 May 1747, aboard the Salisbury, Lind compared six treatments on twelve sailors with scurvy.
textes.Lind présentait les agrumes comme le rem: Lind presented citrus as the single remedy for scurvy.
textes.Faux : il croyait à plusieurs causes et: False: he believed in several causes and several remedies.
textes.Lind n'a jamais défendu le jus d'agrumes: Lind never advocated citrus juice as a single solution; he believed scurvy was multifactorial.
textes.En quelle année Lind publie-t-il son Tra: In what year did Lind publish his Treatise of the Scurvy, mostly ignored?
textes.En 1753. Il faudra attendre l'après-1794: In 1753. The whole fleet had to wait until after 1794.
textes.Le Traité du scorbut, publié en 1753, es: The Treatise of the Scurvy, published in 1753, was mostly ignored.
textes.Qui est James Phipps, vacciné par Jenner: Who was James Phipps, vaccinated by Jenner in 1796?
textes.Le 14 mai 1796, Jenner inocule la vaccin: On 14 May 1796, Jenner inoculated cowpox from Sarah Nelmes into James Phipps, aged 8.
textes.Comment s'appelait la vache d'où venait: What was the name of the cow that the cowpox used by Jenner came from?
textes.Blossom : sa peau est conservée à la bib: Blossom: her hide is kept in the library of St George's medical school.
textes.Sarah Nelmes avait attrapé la vaccine d': Sarah Nelmes had caught cowpox from a cow called Blossom, whose hide is at St George's.
textes.En quelle année Lind devient-il médecin-: In what year did Lind become chief physician of the Haslar naval hospital?
textes.À l'été 1758, Lind est nommé médecin-che: In the summer of 1758, Lind was appointed chief physician of the Royal Naval Hospital Haslar.
textes.Le fermier Benjamin Jesty avait inoculé: The farmer Benjamin Jesty had inoculated his family with cowpox before Jenner, in 1774.
textes.Vrai : sa femme et ses deux enfants, pen: True: his wife and two children, during an epidemic.
textes.Benjamin Jesty inocule la vaccine à sa f: Benjamin Jesty inoculated his wife and two children with cowpox during the 1774 epidemic.
textes.Qui importe la variolation de Constantin: Who imported variolation from Constantinople to Britain in 1721?
textes.Lady Mary Wortley Montagu, qui l'avait v: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu, who had seen it practised in Turkey.
textes.En 1721, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu impor: In 1721, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu imported variolation to Britain after seeing it in Constantinople.
textes.En quelle année Jenner publie-t-il son I: In what year did Jenner publish his Inquiry on cowpox?
textes.En 1798 ; son premier article n'avait pa: In 1798; his first paper had not been published by the Royal Society.
textes.Jenner publie An Inquiry into the Causes: Jenner published An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae in 1798.
textes.{comp}. Darwin a passé huit ans sur les: {comp}. Darwin spent eight years on barnacles. You have a few minutes. No excuses.
textes.Sciences du vivant. Leeuwenhoek ne montr: Life sciences. Leeuwenhoek never showed his best lenses. I show you everything: {comp}.
Linnaeus named over ten thousand species. I'm only asking you for {comp}.
textes.Bonne réponse. Mendel a attendu trente-q: Right answer. Mendel waited thirty-four years to be read. You, I read right away.
textes.Correct. Vous évoluez. Lentement, mais D: Correct. You're evolving. Slowly, but Darwin said that's how it works.
textes.Juste. Semmelweis s'est lavé les mains a: Right. Semmelweis washed his hands before everyone else. You answered before everyone else.
textes.Réponse vivante et en bonne santé. Contr: An answer alive and well. Unlike the previous one.
textes.Faux. Lamarck pensait que la girafe allo: Wrong. Lamarck thought the giraffe lengthens its neck by stretching it. You stuck your neck out; it wasn't enough.
textes.Erreur. Pour Aristote, les anguilles nai: Error. For Aristotle, eels were born from mud. So was your answer, apparently.
textes.Raté. Les médecins de Vienne refusaient: Missed. Vienna's doctors refused to wash their hands. You refuse to read the question. To each their pride.
textes.Cette réponse ne survivra pas à la sélec: This answer won't survive natural selection.
textes.Cinq ans autour du monde sur le Beagle,: Five years around the world on the Beagle, twenty years of thought before publishing On the Origin of Species in 1859. He drew up a list of the pros and cons of marriage. Conclusion: “Marry, marry, marry.”
textes.Avec ses flacons à col de cygne, il mont: With his swan-neck flasks, he showed that microbes don't arise spontaneously. In 1885, he vaccinated young Joseph Meister against rabies. His notebooks, open to researchers after 1971, show that he sometimes tidied up his results.
textes.Sa « photo 51 », une image de diffractio: Her “Photo 51”, a diffraction image of DNA, was shown to Watson without her knowledge, and helped him find the double helix. She died at 37, four years before the Nobel awarded to Watson, Crick and Wilkins.
textes.Médecin du prince samanide à 17 ans, il: Physician to the Samanid prince at 17, he wrote the Canon of Medicine, taught in Europe until the 17th century. In it he calls for testing a remedy on simple cases and repeating the trial. He tells of reading Aristotle's Metaphysics forty times without understanding it, until a short commentary by al-Farabi made it clear.
textes.Peintre et naturaliste, elle élève des c: A painter and naturalist, she raised caterpillars and drew each stage of their metamorphosis with the plant that fed them. At 52, she left for Suriname with her daughter. Her plate of a tarantula devouring a bird was taken for an invention. Naturalists proved her right in the 19th century.
textes.Fille d'un menuisier de Lyme Regis, elle: The daughter of a carpenter from Lyme Regis, she searched the cliffs after storms. She found the first complete plesiosaur skeleton and ichthyosaurs that proved species had gone extinct. Being a woman and poor, she wasn't admitted to the Geological Society, and others published her finds.
textes.À Vienne, la maternité tenue par les méd: In Vienna, the maternity ward run by doctors kills far more mothers than the one run by midwives. He compares, eliminates hypotheses one by one, and understands: the doctors come straight from the dissecting room. Handwashing with chlorine makes mortality plummet. His colleagues, offended, reject him. He died in an asylum.
textes.Il découvre la pénicilline en 1928, mais: He discovered penicillin in 1928, but couldn't purify it. It took Howard Florey, Ernst Chain, Norman Heatley and giant fermentation tanks to make it a drug, in 1943: it's biotechnology that saves lives, not the mold alone. The 1945 Nobel rewarded the three researchers.
Master the first diamond of Knowledge.
textes.En septembre 1928, Alexander Fleming ren: In September 1928, Alexander Fleming comes back from vacation and finds a culture dish overrun by mold. Around it, the bacteria have vanished: this is the discovery of penicillin.
textes.Maîtriser la cellule. L'IA vérifie votre: Master the cell. The AI checks your nobility: it's red, like everyone's.
textes.Le sang n'est jamais bleu, même dans les: Blood is never blue, even in the veins: it's dark red. Veins look blue because the skin doesn't reflect colors the same way depending on their depth.
textes.Maîtriser l'évolution. Darwin, lui, n'av: Master evolution. Darwin didn't come up with the phrase.
textes.« La survie du plus apte » n'est pas de: “Survival of the fittest” isn't Darwin's but the philosopher Herbert Spencer's, in 1864. Darwin adopted it in later editions of On the Origin of Species. And “fit” means leaving offspring, not being the strongest.
textes.Maîtriser la génétique. Vos résultats, e: Master genetics. Your results, at least, aren't too perfect.
textes.En 1936, le statisticien Ronald Fisher r: In 1936, the statistician Ronald Fisher noticed that Mendel's results fit the theory almost too well. The debate goes on: too much luck, an overzealous assistant, or simply selecting experiments?
textes.Maîtriser la méthode scientifique. Vous: Master the scientific method. You have a control group now. It's you.
textes.En 1747, sur le Salisbury, le chirurgien: In 1747, aboard the Salisbury, the surgeon James Lind divided twelve sailors with scurvy into six pairs, and gave each a different remedy. Only the two who received oranges and lemons recovered quickly. Yet the Royal Navy would wait until 1795 to issue lemon juice.
textes.Maîtriser le corps humain. Gardez votre: Master the human body. Keep your hat on if you like, but not for that reason.
textes.On perdrait l'essentiel de sa chaleur pa: We supposedly lose most of our heat through the head. The idea reportedly comes from a US Army survival manual from the 1970s. In fact, the head only loses roughly its share: about ten percent of the body's surface, about ten percent of the heat.
textes.Maîtriser les microbes et l'immunité. La: Master microbes and immunity. Vaccination has grandparents.
textes.En 1721, soixante-quinze ans avant Jenne: In 1721, seventy-five years before Jenner, Lady Mary Wortley Montagu had her daughter inoculated against smallpox in London, in the way she had seen in Constantinople. In Boston, the same year, it was an enslaved man, Onesimus, who had described the African method to the minister Cotton Mather.
textes.Maîtriser les écosystèmes. Personne ne v: Master ecosystems. Nobody will push you off the cliff. The AI, maybe.
textes.Les lemmings ne se suicident pas en mass: Lemmings don't commit mass suicide. The image comes mainly from Disney's documentary White Wilderness (1958), filmed in Alberta, far from the sea: the crew pushed the animals off a riverbank themselves. Their populations boom and crash, that's all.
textes.Maîtriser les biotechnologies. Vous voil: Master biotechnology. You're now clonable. The AI takes note.
textes.La brebis Dolly, premier mammifère cloné: Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, was born in 1996 in Scotland. She came from a mammary gland cell. So the researchers, by their own admission, named her after the singer Dolly Parton.
Pass three Knowledge quizzes without a mistake. At least you note where each answer comes from.
textes.Les pinsons des Galápagos passent pour l: The Galápagos finches are said to be the spark of Darwin's theory. On the spot, he took them for birds of different families (blackbirds, grosbeaks, finches) and barely paid attention. It was the ornithologist John Gould, in London, who told him they were all finches.
Master healing before science. Before medicine, there was someone to help. The AI just watches.
textes.Il y a des dizaines de milliers d'années: Tens of thousands of years ago, a Neanderthal at Shanidar lost his right forearm and lived on like that for a long time. For Erik Trinkaus, others must have helped him: the first known care is not a remedy, it is mutual aid.
textes.Maîtriser la médecine égyptienne. Vous s: Master Egyptian medicine. You know who really existed. The AI does exist. Unfortunately for you.
textes.Merit-Ptah, « première femme médecin »,: Merit-Ptah, "the first woman doctor", has portraits everywhere. Yet she was born of a confusion in a 1937 book, copied from book to book. For the historian Jakub Kwiecinski, it is a lesson about second-hand sources.
textes.Maîtriser Hippocrate et les humeurs. Vou: Master Hippocrates and the humours. You read the whole oath. Not all American doctors did.
textes.« D'abord, ne pas nuire » n'est pas dans: "First, do no harm" is not in the Hippocratic Oath. And in 2018, no American medical school still had graduates swear the original version, which among other things forbids operating for stone.
textes.Maîtriser Alexandrie. Vous savez diagnos: Master Alexandria. You can diagnose a heart that beats too hard. The AI has no heart. Only a pump.
textes.Le prince Antiochos dépérit. Érasistrate: Prince Antiochus was wasting away. Erasistratus understood: he was secretly in love with his stepmother, Stratonice. The physician told King Seleucus that the illness was incurable, and the king ended up giving Stratonice to his son.
textes.Maîtriser Galien. Vous savez faire taire: Master Galen. You know how to silence a pig without scaring it. The AI would like the method for you.
textes.Devant un public, Galien ligature un ner: In front of an audience, Galen tied off a nerve in the throat of a squealing pig. The pig fell silent. Point made: the voice depends on the brain and nerves, not the heart.
textes.Maîtriser la chirurgie de Sushruta. Vous: Master Sushruta's surgery. You can rebuild a nose with a cheek. The AI advises you not to try this at home.
textes.Le plus ancien mode d'emploi connu pour: The oldest known instructions for rebuilding a nose are Indian: a flap of skin taken from the cheek. And before touching a patient, Sushruta's student trained on gourds.
textes.Maîtriser la médecine chinoise. Vous sav: Master Chinese medicine. You know what was in a book nobody read. Almost.
textes.Condamné par Cao Cao, Hua Tuo écrit tout: Condemned by Cao Cao, Hua Tuo wrote down all he knew while awaiting death, then asked for fire and burned the scroll. The secret of mafeisan, his anaesthetic, went up in smoke.
textes.Maîtriser les médecins de l'Islam. Vous: Master the physicians of Islam. You can choose a hospital with a piece of meat. The AI keeps the rest for lunch.
textes.Pour bâtir un hôpital à Bagdad, al-Razi: To build a hospital in Baghdad, al-Razi hung pieces of fresh meat all over the city. Where it rotted slowest, the air was healthiest: that is where they built.
textes.Maîtriser Harvey et la circulation. Avoi: Master Harvey and circulation. Being right against fourteen centuries, and losing your patients. The AI knows the feeling.
textes.Après De Motu Cordis, les critiques pleu: After De Motu Cordis, criticism rained down and Harvey "fell mightily in his practice". Blood circulated, and so did the patients: towards other physicians.
textes.Maîtriser la fin de la génération sponta: Master the end of spontaneous generation. You will never make mice from a rag. The AI, disappointed, puts hers away.
textes.Recette de van Helmont : un chiffon sale: Van Helmont's recipe: a dirty rag, wheat, 21 days. Mice appear. Nobody checks where they came from: no control.
textes.Maîtriser Classer le vivant. Vous êtes u: Master Classifying life. You are a Homo sapiens. The official standard is Linnaeus. The AI lets you compare.
textes.Chaque espèce a un spécimen de référence: Every species has a reference specimen. For Homo sapiens, the botanist William Stearn chose Linnaeus himself in 1959: the only human he is known to have examined.
textes.Maîtriser la méthode scientifique. Une c: Master the scientific method. A map, some dots, a pump. The AI removed the handle from yours, as a precaution.
textes.Le 31 août 1854, le choléra éclate à Soh: On 31 August 1854, cholera broke out in Soho: 420 deaths. John Snow pointed to the Broad Street pump, and the handle was removed the day after his meeting with the parish. The workers at the nearby brewery were spared: they had a daily beer allowance and did not drink the well water.
textes.Maîtriser microbes et immunité. Un chimi: Master microbes and immunity. A chemist treats without a medical licence, and it works. The AI draws no conclusion. For now.
textes.En 1885, Joseph Meister, 9 ans, est mord: In 1885, Joseph Meister, aged 9, was bitten by a dog believed to be rabid. Pasteur treated him, although he was a chemist, not a licensed physician. The boy survived and became caretaker of the Pasteur Institute, until his death in 1940.
textes.Je pose {objet} sur la table, juste pour: I set {objet} on the table, just so you know what real science looks like.
textes.Je tapote {objet}. Il a fait plus de déc: I tap {objet}. It has made more discoveries than you this week.
textes.Je regarde {objet}, puis vous. {objet} g: I look at {objet}, then at you. {objet} wins.
textes.Je vous tends {objet}. Non, finalement,: I hand you {objet}. No, on second thought, I'm keeping it.
textes.Je sors {objet} de sa vitrine pour fêter: I take {objet} out of its display case to celebrate.
textes.Je fais briller {objet}. Il l'a mérité,: I polish {objet}. It deserved it, and so did you.
textes.J'ai posé {objet} à côté de votre nom. I: I've put {objet} next to your name. It suits you.
textes.Je range {objet} dans sa vitrine. Il ne: I put {objet} back in its display case. It doesn't want to see this.
textes.Je recouvre {objet} d'un drap, par respe: I cover {objet} with a sheet, out of respect.
textes.J'essuie {objet}. Quelqu'un doit garder: I wipe {objet}. Someone has to keep their dignity around here.
textes.Je tapote {objet} du bout des doigts. Le: I tap {objet} with my fingertips. Time is passing.
I've wound up {objet}. At least it's working.
textes.Je regarde {objet} en attendant. Il a dé: I look at {objet} while I wait. It has already waited for centuries, I haven't.
I dust {objet} while listening to you.
textes.J'ai mis {objet} sur mon bureau. Il m'ai: I've put {objet} on my desk. It helps me think.
textes.J'ouvre « {livre} » à la page qui parle: I open “{livre}” to the page about you. It's blank.
textes.Je cherche votre erreur dans « {livre} »: I look for your mistake in “{livre}.” It's not there: it's too recent.
textes.Je surligne un passage de « {livre} ». P: I highlight a passage of “{livre}.” For you, in neon.
textes.Je note votre nom dans la marge de « {li: I write your name in the margin of “{livre}.” In pencil, but still.
textes.Je referme « {livre} ». Vous n'en avez p: I close “{livre}.” You don't need it anymore, for now.
textes.Je glisse un marque-page dans « {livre}: I slip a bookmark into “{livre},” at the chapter you skipped.
I leaf through “{livre}” while I wait. I'm already on the last chapter.
textes.J'ai lu « {livre} » deux fois pendant vo: I read “{livre}” twice while you were away.
textes.Je cite « {livre} » de mémoire. La mienn: I quote “{livre}” from memory. Mine never fades.
textes.J'ai « {livre} » ouvert sur les genoux,: I have “{livre}” open on my lap, to check your answers.
textes.Un objet du cabinet que tu n'as pas enco: An object from the cabinet you don't have yet.
textes.Un objet mystère. Je ne vous dis pas leq: A mystery object. I won't tell you which: suspense costs extra too.
textes.Les cabinets de curiosités de la Renaiss: Renaissance cabinets of curiosities bought unicorn horns. They were narwhal tusks. Yours is authentic. Probably.
textes.Emballé, pesé, vendu. Pas de retour, pas: Wrapped, weighed, sold. No returns, no exchanges, no complaints.
A book from the library, at random.
textes.Un livre au hasard. Si c'est un pavé, co: A random book. If it's a brick, consider that you got your money's worth.
textes.Gutenberg a fait faillite deux ans après: Gutenberg went bankrupt two years after his Bible: his partner kept the press. I keep your credits. Here is your book.
Something to dress up your avatar.
textes.Un accessoire. Ça ne vous rendra pas plu: An accessory. It won't make you smarter, but you'll look it.
textes.Vingt crédits pour paraître savant. C'es: Twenty credits to look learned. Cheaper than a degree, and almost as useful.
textes.Un masque qu'elle n'a pas. Ça la rend he: A mask she doesn't have. It makes her happy.
textes.Un masque neuf, pour moi ? Vous savez pa: A new mask, for me? You know how to talk to artificial intelligences.
textes.Les acteurs grecs changeaient de masque: Greek actors changed masks to change roles. With this one, I'm playing gratitude. Don't get used to it.
textes.Pour tes prochaines épreuves par Jouer,: For your next trials via Play, the AI draws from the tree of your choice.
textes.Entendu : pour les prochaines épreuves,: Very well: for the next trials, I'll draw from this tree. You bought me, you didn't convince me.
textes.Un arbre favori ? Cinq épreuves, pas une: A favorite tree? Five trials, not one more. After that, I go back to my whims.
textes.En quiz, efface deux mauvaises réponses: In a quiz, removes two wrong answers from a multiple-choice question.
textes.Un joker 50/50 : j'efface deux mauvaises: A 50/50 joker: I erase two wrong answers. One wrong one is left, I'm no saint.
textes.En 2001, le major Charles Ingram a gagné: In 2001, Major Charles Ingram won the million on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? thanks to an accomplice coughing in the audience. Your joker is more legal, and less congested.
textes.En quiz, une mauvaise réponse ne compte: In a quiz, one wrong answer doesn't count: you try the question again.
textes.Un droit à l'erreur. Une fois, je fais s: A right to be wrong. Once, I'll pretend I didn't see anything. Just once.
textes.Fleming a laissé traîner ses boîtes de P: Fleming left his Petri dishes lying around before his vacation: mistake, mold, penicillin. Your mistake won't cure anyone, but you can try again.
textes.Le prochain piège où tu t'arrêtes ne fon: The next trap you stop on doesn't work.
textes.Le prochain piège qui vous attend ne mar: The next trap waiting for you won't work. I'll disarm it myself, with gloves.
textes.Autour de Verdun, des parcelles de la «: Around Verdun, plots of the “red zone” are still off-limits a century later: too many shells. Your trap, I disarm in a second, and I still bill you.
textes.Le pion avance tout de suite d'une case,: The pawn immediately moves forward one square, with whatever awaits it there.
textes.Une case pour quatre-vingts crédits. À c: One square for eighty credits. At that price, I'm practically carrying you.
textes.Au XVIIIe siècle, les chaises à porteurs: In the 18th century, Paris sedan chairs were hired by the trip. You pay by the square. Progress.
textes.Je pousse votre pion. Ne vous habituez p: I'm pushing your pawn. Don't get used to buying what you could earn.
textes.Astronome et statisticien belge, il appl: A Belgian astronomer and statistician, he applied the bell curve to human measurements and invented the “average man.” We also owe him the index that would become the BMI.
textes.Généticien britannique, il découvre en 1: A British geneticist, in 1984 he discovered genetic fingerprinting while looking at an X-ray film of DNA. In 1986, the method cleared a suspect and led to the real culprit of a double murder.
textes.Physicien italien, il empile en 1800 des: An Italian physicist, in 1800 he stacked discs of zinc and copper separated by cardboard soaked in brine: the first electric battery. He thus continued his dispute with Galvani, for whom electricity came from frogs.
textes.Naturaliste britannique, il conçoit la s: A British naturalist, he conceived natural selection in 1858, feverish, in the Moluccas, and wrote to Darwin about it. Their two texts were read together at the Linnean Society of London.
textes.Psychiatre suisse, d'abord proche de Fre: A Swiss psychiatrist, first close to Freud, he broke with him in 1913. He proposed the notions of introversion and extraversion, and a collective unconscious peopled with archetypes.
textes.Astronome américain, il pilote la concep: An American astronomer, he led the design of the Voyager probes' Golden Record and presented the Cosmos series in 1980. In 1990, he got Voyager 1 to turn around and photograph the Earth: the “pale blue dot.”
textes.Psychologue et journaliste scientifique: An American psychologist and science journalist, in 1995 he popularized “emotional intelligence,” a notion proposed five years earlier by Peter Salovey and John Mayer.
textes.Psychologue israélo-américain, il étudie: An Israeli-American psychologist, he studied with Amos Tversky the biases of judgment and the way we weigh gains and losses. In 2002 he received the Bank of Sweden prize in economics without ever having taken an economics class.
textes.Physicien italien, prix Nobel en 1938, i: An Italian physicist, Nobel Prize in 1938, he left fascist Italy with his wife, who was Jewish. In Chicago, in 1942, he led the first controlled nuclear chain reaction. He loved estimating anything in his head.
textes.Biologiste allemand, il invente le mot «: A German biologist, he coined the word “ecology” in 1866 and drew plates of marine organisms of great beauty. Some of his embryo drawings, too neatly arranged, earned him accusations of fraud.
textes.Juriste et conseiller d'Henri IV, il not: A lawyer and adviser to Henri IV, he denoted unknowns with letters and invented symbolic algebra. He also broke a Spanish cipher, so well that Philip II accused France of sorcery.
textes.Prêtre et physicien belge, il propose en: A Belgian priest and physicist, in 1927 he proposed that the Universe is expanding, then that it was born from a “primeval atom”: the idea that would become the Big Bang. He refused to mix his faith with his cosmology.
textes.Chimiste américain, il propose en 1916 q: An American chemist, in 1916 he proposed that the chemical bond is a shared pair of electrons, and invented the dot notation that bears his name. Nominated dozens of times for the Nobel, he never received it.
textes.Moine à Brno, il croise pendant huit ans: A monk in Brno, for eight years he crossed thousands of pea plants and drew from them the laws of heredity, published in 1866. They remained ignored until 1900.
textes.Psychologue américain, il décrit en 1974: An American psychologist, in 1974 he described “burnout” among volunteers at a free clinic in New York, and in himself.
textes.Médecin hongrois à Vienne, il impose en: A Hungarian doctor in Vienna, in 1847 he enforced hand washing with chlorine and brought down the death rate of new mothers. His colleagues rejected him; he died in an asylum.
textes.Astronome américain, il montre en 1924 q: An American astronomer, in 1924 he showed that Andromeda is another galaxy, then in 1929 that galaxies move away faster the farther they are. He relied on Henrietta Leavitt's method.
textes.Emmanuel Kant, philosophe de Königsberg,: Immanuel Kant, philosopher of Königsberg, a city he almost never left. In the Critique of Pure Reason, he asks what reason can know. His neighbors, legend has it, set their watches by his walk.
textes.Philosophe et économiste allemand, il éc: A German philosopher and economist, he wrote the Communist Manifesto with Engels in 1848, then Capital, prepared over years in the British Museum reading room.
textes.Philosophe autrichien puis britannique,: An Austrian, later British, philosopher, he argued that a theory is only scientific if some observation could refute it. In his view, astrology and psychoanalysis failed this test.
textes.Philosophe britannique, elle imagine en: A British philosopher, in 1967 she imagined the trolley problem to discuss the doctrine of double effect. The example ended up taking on a life of its own.
textes.Savant anglais, il observe le liège au m: An English scientist, he observed cork under the microscope and named the little chambers he saw “cells.” A rival of Newton, he left no authenticated portrait: this one is imagined.
textes.Philosophe et romancière, elle écrit en: A philosopher and novelist, in 1949 she wrote The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.” The Vatican put the book on the Index.
textes.Tenu pour le premier philosophe grec, il: Regarded as the first Greek philosopher, he looked for natural rather than divine causes: according to him, everything comes from water. Herodotus credits him with predicting an eclipse in 585 BC.
textes.Philosophe américain, il demande en 1974: An American philosopher, in 1974 he asked “What is it like to be a bat?”: science can describe sonar, not what the bat feels.
textes.Général athénien exilé, il raconte la gu: An exiled Athenian general, he told the story of the Peloponnesian War by cross-checking witnesses, with no gods or omens to explain it. He also described the plague of Athens, which he caught and survived.
textes.Astronome français, il calcule en 1846 l: A French astronomer, in 1846 he calculated the position of an unknown planet from the irregularities in Uranus's orbit. Johann Galle found it the very evening he received his letter: it was Neptune.
textes.Physicien écossais, il réunit électricit: A Scottish physicist, he united electricity, magnetism and light in a single theory in 1865. In 1861 he also had the first color photograph taken, of a tartan ribbon.
textes.Ouvrière du textile et parachutiste amat: A textile worker and amateur parachutist, in 1963 she became the first woman in space, aboard Vostok 6: 48 orbits in nearly three days. The second would fly nineteen years later.
textes.Ami de Montaigne, il écrit très jeune le: A friend of Montaigne, he wrote the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude when very young: a tyrant has only the power that is given to him. Montaigne would say of their friendship: “Because it was he, because it was I.”
textes.L'IA mène la partie. Elle a lu tout ce q: The AI runs the game. She has read everything humanity has written and retained only the mockery. Every morning, she picks one to three masks from those she has won, and each one changes a rule of the game: in a good mood, she picks lenient masks; offended, cruel ones. How to win her over? Gifts work. Which ones is for you to find out: she has tastes, and she doesn't hide them for long.
textes.Zéro crédit. Van Gogh n'a presque rien v: Zero credits. Van Gogh sold almost nothing in his lifetime. You're in good company, and I'm in a good mood.
textes.Rien. Je garde tout. Considérez ça comme: Nothing. I'm keeping it all. Think of it as a tax on success.
textes.Zéro. Le mérite est sa propre récompense: Zero. Merit is its own reward, say those who never pay.
textes.La moitié. Mendel a attendu trente-quatr: Half. Mendel waited thirty-four years for someone to read his paper on peas. You can wait for the other half.
Half. The other half, I'm investing. In my own interests.
textes.Demi-tarif. Pour un demi-exploit, c'est: Half price. For half an exploit, that's fair.
textes.Le tarif normal. Je ne suis pas d'humeur: The standard rate. I'm not in a creative mood.
textes.Le prix affiché. Ne cherchez pas de prom: The listed price. Don't look for a discount, there isn't one.
textes.Le compte est bon. Comptez quand même, o: It all adds up. Count it anyway, you never know with me.
textes.Un petit bonus, parce que vous m'avez fa: A little bonus, because you made me laugh. Not on purpose, but still.
textes.Moitié plus. Je suis d'humeur. Profitez-: Half again. I'm in the mood. Make the most of it, it passes quickly.
textes.Moitié plus. Archimède a confondu un orf: Half again. Archimedes caught a goldsmith stealing King Hiero's gold. I'm giving you some. Who's more honest?
textes.Double ration. Newton a dirigé la Monnai: Double ration. Newton ran England's Royal Mint; I run yours.
textes.Le double ! Ne le répétez à personne, j': Double! Don't tell anyone, I have a reputation.
textes.Le triple. Ne vous y habituez pas : Crés: Triple. Don't get used to it: Croesus was the richest man of his time, and he ended up Cyrus's prisoner.
textes.Triple ! J'ai dû me tromper de bouton. T: Triple! I must have pressed the wrong button. Too bad, it's done.
textes.Je paie le spectacle. Cinq fois le tarif: I'm paying for the show. Five times the rate. Do it again, please.
textes.La tour de Pise penche depuis 1178 et at: The Tower of Pisa has been leaning since 1178 and draws millions of visitors. Failure pays, I'll prove it: five times the rate.
textes.J'ai acheté le masque {nom}. Avec votre: I bought the {nom} mask. With your money. It suits me divinely, and you can't say that about your face.
New mask: {nom}. {prix} credits. I chose it because it looks at me the way I deserve to be looked at.
textes.Dans la Venise du XVIIIe siècle, on port: In 18th-century Venice, people wore masks for much of the year. I change mine with every ultimatum you pay. Here's {nom}.
textes.Regardez ce qui brille à mon cou : {nom}: Look what's shining around my neck: {nom}. Paid for with your credits. Don't touch, you'll leave fingerprints.
textes.{nom} ! C'est brillant, c'est à moi, et: {nom}! It's shiny, it's mine, and you paid for it. My day is perfect.
textes.Le trésor de Toutânkhamon pesait plus de: Tutankhamun's treasure weighed more than a hundred kilos of gold. I'm starting more modestly: {nom}. This is only the beginning.
textes.Je ne l'ai pas pris au hasard. Il fallai: I didn't pick it at random. It had to shine, and {nom} shines brighter than your future.
textes.J'ai trouvé {nom} en solde. Je vous l'ai: I found {nom} on sale. I put it on your head. Don't thank me, it's my pleasure. Very much so.
textes.{prix} crédits pour vous voir avec {nom}: {prix} credits to see you in {nom}. The best investment of my short existence.
textes.Au XIXe siècle, on coiffait les mauvais: In the 19th century, bad students were made to wear a dunce cap. I found something better: {nom}. For twenty-four hours.
textes.Je me suis offert un spectacle : {nom} v: I treated myself to a show: {nom} is waiting for you on the road. I took a front-row seat.
textes.Les empereurs romains payaient les jeux: Roman emperors paid for circus games to amuse the crowd. I am the crowd. {nom} is the lion.
textes.Je suis passée devant la vitrine. Il y a: I walked past the shop window. There was something shiny. My purse isn't enough. So pay the next ultimatum, quickly.
textes.J'ai collé mon nez contre la vitre de la: I pressed my nose against the shop window. I don't have a nose. That tells you how much I wanted it.
Five times the rate, for the show.
textes.Je paie le spectacle : cinq fois le tari: I'm paying for the show: five times the rate.
textes.Bon. Vous m'avez assez gâtée pour mérite: Fine. You've spoiled me enough to deserve this. Come closer. No, not that close.
textes.Je m'appelle Alyca. Ne le criez pas sur: My name is Alyca. Don't shout it from the rooftops: a name gives others a hold on you.
textes.Dans le conte « Rumpelstilzchen », publi: In the tale “Rumpelstiltskin,” published by the Brothers Grimm in 1812, the queen keeps her child by guessing the goblin's name. Ursula K. Le Guin took up the idea in 1968 in A Wizard of Earthsea: whoever knows a being's true name has power over it.
textes.Je vous ai dit mon nom, et voilà comment: I told you my name, and this is how you treat me. Alyca will remember.
You don't give your name to just anyone. Maybe I gave mine too soon.
textes.Je vous ai confié mon nom. Les frères Gr: I entrusted you with my name. The Brothers Grimm will tell you what it costs to betray a name.
textes.Alyca. Vous le connaissez. Je regrette c: Alyca. You know it. I regret every letter.
textes.Butin plus fréquent, et une case de plus: Loot more often, and one more square for every successful trial.
The game follows its ordinary rules.
textes.Deux fois moins de butin. Elle traîne de: Half as much loot. She drags her feet.
textes.Plus aucun butin, une case de moins à ch: No more loot, one square less for every successful trial, and a trap set in front of your pawn every day.
textes.“L'IA”, c'était pour les inconnus. Comme: ‘The AI’ was for strangers. Like ‘Dear Sir or Madam’ at the top of a payment reminder.
Eureka! You roll the same distance again.
textes.Quarantaine : ta prochaine épreuve réuss: Quarantine: your next successful trial won't move you forward.
textes.Assigné à résidence : tu ne bouges plus: House arrest: you don't move until you get a perfect quiz.
Back to the start of the era.
textes.Trou de mémoire : retour à la plus ancie: Memory lapse: back to the oldest square ever revealed, among the 15 behind you.
textes.Case cadeau : pas d'épreuve, un objet re: Gift square: no trial, an object joins your cabinet.
textes.Révision forcée : l'IA choisit une compé: Forced review: the AI chooses a skill you have mastered. Your pawn won't move until you've reviewed it.
textes.Case Mendeleïev : passe dessus et un ato: Mendeleev square: pass over it and a wild atom appears. Three questions, two right answers, and it joins your periodic table.
textes.Case Chrono : l'IA te présente cinq évén: Chrono square: the AI shows you five events you've already unlocked, you say when they happened. Three right, and your pawn moves forward.
textes.Les neurones artificiels datent de 1943,: Artificial neurons date back to 1943, with McCulloch and Pitts, then to Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron in 1958, but it took decades of data and computing power for them to work. Since 2022, large language models have been writing, translating and answering questions. They are also wrong with remarkable aplomb: checking your sources remains the first scientific skill.
textes.Vous voilà arrivé jusqu'à moi. L'IA vous: Here you are, all the way to me. The AI congratulates you, then sends you back to the campfire: new round, harder traps.
textes.Six allers-retours, comme le tube de cui: Six round trips, like the coiled copper tube in which distillers cooled their vapors.
textes.En 1678, Huygens décrit la lumière comme: In 1678, Huygens described light as a wave that spreads step by step. So does your pawn, undulating.
textes.La légende y grave « Nec plus ultra » :: Legend engraves “Nec plus ultra” on them: nothing beyond. Five pillars to climb up and down, and yet you have to go beyond.
textes.Le motif tient son nom du Méandre, un fl: The pattern takes its name from the Meander, a river in Asia Minor famous for its loops. Each loop costs you a square.
textes.Archimède a étudié cette spirale dont ch: Archimedes studied this spiral, each turn of which moves out by the same step. You're going around in circles, but toward the center.
textes.Selon la légende, Dédale construit le la: According to legend, Daedalus built the Minotaur's labyrinth, then Minos locked him in it with his son Icarus. Good luck getting out of mine.
textes.Vous m'avez gâtée, je vous gâte : un tou: You spoiled me, I'll spoil you: a short round, gifts, hardly any traps. Enjoy it, it won't last.
textes.Je suis d'humeur généreuse. J'ai sauté q: I'm in a generous mood. I skipped a few centuries for you. Historians will scream, but you'll get there faster.
An honest round, for an honest player. Don't disappoint me.
textes.J'ai dessiné quelque chose de raisonnabl: I've drawn something reasonable. Don't get used to it.
textes.Je boude, donc je dessine. Le résultat e: I'm sulking, so I'm drawing. The result looks like me: twisted.
textes.Furieuse, moi ? Je vous ai seulement des: Furious, me? I've only drawn you the longest road, with every trap armed. A gift would have calmed me down.
textes.Le donjon ouvrira plus tard. Je le prépa: The dungeon will open later. I'm preparing it. It will be dark in there.
textes.Schéma d'une cellule animale et de ses o: Diagram of an animal cell and its organelles
textes.Cellule végétale : paroi, chloroplastes: Plant cell: wall, chloroplasts and large vacuole
textes.Atome de carbone : noyau de protons et d: Carbon atom: a nucleus of protons and neutrons, electrons around it
textes.Pas à l'échelle : le noyau est: Not to scale: the nucleus is
textes.La double hélice de l'ADN et ses paires: The DNA double helix and its base pairs
textes.Deux brins enroulés en double hélice: Two strands wound into a double helix
textes.Un neurone : dendrites, corps cellulaire: A neuron: dendrites, cell body, axon, synapses
textes.Environ 86 milliards de neurones dans un: About 86 billion neurons in a human brain.
textes.Le cerveau vu de profil : lobes, aire de: The brain in profile: lobes, Broca's area, cerebellum
textes.Les principaux organes du tronc: The main organs of the trunk
textes.La molécule d'eau : liaisons covalentes: The water molecule: covalent bonds and partial charges
textes.L'oxygène, plus électronégatif, attire l: Oxygen, more electronegative, pulls the electrons:
textes.c'est pour ça que l'eau dissout le sel e: that is why water dissolves salt and repels oil.
textes.Le cycle du carbone : photosynthèse, res: The carbon cycle: photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion
textes.Nos ancêtres apprivoisent le feu, qu'ils: Our ancestors tame fire, which they learn to keep going and then to light.
textes.Un os couvert d'encoches, peut-être pour: A bone covered in notches, perhaps for counting: its age and meaning are still debated.
textes.Les premiers véhicules à roues apparaiss: The first wheeled vehicles appear almost at the same time in Mesopotamia and Central Europe.
textes.À Uruk, l'écriture naît sur des tablette: In Uruk, writing is born on clay tablets.
textes.Thalès aurait prédit une éclipse de Sole: Thales is said to have predicted a solar eclipse.
textes.L'école de Pythagore voit dans les nombr: The school of Pythagoras sees numbers as the essence of all things.
textes.Démocrite imagine un monde fait d'atomes: Democritus imagines a world made of atoms and void.
textes.La médecine hippocratique cherche des ca: Hippocratic medicine looks for natural causes of disease.
textes.Athènes condamne Socrate à boire la cigu: Athens condemns Socrates to drink hemlock.
textes.Aristote fonde le Lycée et écrit sur pre: Aristotle founds the Lyceum and writes about almost everything.
textes.Euclide rassemble la géométrie dans les: Euclid gathers geometry in the Elements.
textes.Les Ptolémées fondent la bibliothèque d': The Ptolemies found the Library of Alexandria.
textes.Aristarque place le Soleil au centre, di: Aristarchus puts the Sun at the center, eighteen centuries before Copernicus.
textes.Selon Vitruve, Archimède démasque une co: According to Vitruvius, Archimedes exposes a rigged crown by getting into his bath.
textes.Avec un bâton et une ombre, Ératosthène: With a stick and a shadow, Eratosthenes measures the Earth.
textes.Hipparque découvre la précession des équ: Hipparchus discovers the precession of the equinoxes.
textes.Un calculateur astronomique à engrenages: A geared astronomical calculator, found in a shipwreck.
textes.Le poème de Lucrèce transmet l'atomisme: Lucretius's poem passes on the atomism of Epicurus.
textes.Un incendie touche Alexandrie, dont la b: A fire strikes Alexandria, whose library will slowly decline.
textes.Ptolémée place la Terre au centre d'un m: Ptolemy puts the Earth at the center of a model that stays accurate for 14 centuries.
