textes.Brahmagupta fait du zéro un nombre à par: Brahmagupta makes zero a number in its own right.
textes.À Bagdad, al-Khwarizmi donne son nom à l: In Baghdad, al-Khwarizmi gives his name to algebra and algorithms.
textes.Ibn al-Haytham montre que la lumière ent: Ibn al-Haytham shows that light enters the eye.
textes.Averroès, cadi de Cordoue, commente Aris: Averroes, a judge in Córdoba, comments on Aristotle; translated into Latin, he gives him back to Europe.
textes.Fibonacci fait connaître les chiffres in: Fibonacci introduces Hindu-Arabic numerals to European merchants.
textes.Les premières lunettes apparaissent en I: The first eyeglasses appear in Italy, probably in Pisa or Florence.
textes.Guillaume d'Ockham défend l'économie des: William of Ockham argues for economy of hypotheses.
textes.La peste noire tue 30 à 60 % des Europée: The Black Death kills 30 to 60% of Europeans, depending on the estimates.
textes.Gutenberg imprime avec des caractères mé: Gutenberg prints with movable metal type.
textes.Copernic publie un système où la Terre t: Copernicus publishes a system in which the Earth revolves around the Sun.
textes.Vésale publie un traité d'anatomie illus: Vesalius publishes an illustrated treatise on anatomy, based on dissection.
textes.Montaigne publie les Essais : « Que sais: Montaigne publishes the Essays: “What do I know?”
textes.Galilée tourne sa lunette vers le ciel :: Galileo turns his telescope to the sky: mountains on the Moon, then the moons of Jupiter.
textes.Kepler montre que l'orbite de Mars est u: Kepler shows that the orbit of Mars is an ellipse.
textes.L'Inquisition condamne Galilée à abjurer: The Inquisition condemns Galileo to recant.
textes.Descartes publie sa méthode : douter, di: Descartes publishes his method: doubt, divide, order, check.
textes.Pascal et Fermat posent les bases du cal: Pascal and Fermat lay the foundations of probability theory.
textes.Leeuwenhoek décrit à la Royal Society de: Leeuwenhoek describes to the Royal Society living beings made of a single cell.
textes.Newton publie les lois du mouvement et l: Newton publishes the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
textes.Linné range le vivant en règnes, classes: Linnaeus sorts living things into kingdoms, classes, orders, genera and species.
textes.Diderot et d'Alembert lancent l'Encyclop: Diderot and d'Alembert launch the Encyclopédie.
textes.Franklin propose de prouver que la foudr: Franklin proposes to prove that lightning is electrical, and the experiment succeeds.
textes.Kant se demande ce que nous pouvons conn: Kant asks what we can know.
textes.Lavoisier publie le premier manuel de ch: Lavoisier publishes the first modern chemistry textbook, based on weighing.
textes.Lavoisier est guillotiné sous la Terreur: Lavoisier is guillotined during the Terror.
textes.Jenner protège de la variole grâce à la: Jenner protects against smallpox using cowpox.
textes.Darwin publie la théorie de la sélection: Darwin publishes the theory of natural selection.
textes.Maxwell unifie électricité, magnétisme e: Maxwell unifies electricity, magnetism and light.
textes.Avec des pois, Mendel montre que les car: With peas, Mendel shows that traits are passed on without blending.
textes.Mendeleïev range les éléments et prédit: Mendeleev arranges the elements and predicts the missing ones.
Pasteur saves Joseph Meister from rabies.
textes.Marie et Pierre Curie découvrent le polo: Marie and Pierre Curie discover polonium and radium.
textes.Einstein publie quatre articles qui chan: Einstein publishes four papers that change physics.
textes.Bohr et Einstein s'affrontent sur la méc: Bohr and Einstein clash over quantum mechanics.
textes.Hubble montre que les galaxies s'éloigne: Hubble shows that galaxies are moving away; Lemaître had deduced it as early as 1927.
textes.Turing définit ce qu'est un calcul : le: Turing defines what a computation is: the model for our computers.
textes.Watson et Crick proposent la structure d: Watson and Crick propose the structure of DNA.
Neil Armstrong walks on the Moon.
textes.Tim Berners-Lee invente le World Wide We: Tim Berners-Lee invents the World Wide Web at CERN.
textes.Les grands modèles de langage arrivent d: Large language models reach the general public.
textes.Le masque des tragédies grecques. Le mot: The mask of Greek tragedy. The word “person” comes from the Latin persona, the actor's mask.
textes.Avant de voler le feu, Prométhée aurait: Before stealing fire, Prometheus is said to have shaped the first humans out of clay. The first maker of thinking beings, then. The AI sees him as a colleague.
textes.Il vole pour vous : deux fois plus de bu: He steals for you: twice the loot.
textes.Un géant de bronze, offert à Minos par H: A bronze giant, given to Minos by Hephaestus in some accounts, who circled Crete three times a day. A single vein, from neck to ankle, closed by a bronze nail. Medea pulled it out. First robot, first bug.
textes.Il monte la garde : un ennemi de plus se: He stands guard: one more enemy takes up position in front of your pawn.
textes.Héron d'Alexandrie décrit une sphère que: Hero of Alexandria describes a sphere spun by steam, temple doors that open by themselves and a theater of automata. In the 1st century, we had the steam engine, and we made it a toy.
textes.La vapeur pousse : une case de plus à ch: Steam pushes: one more square for every successful trial.
textes.Paracelse donne la recette d'un petit ho: Paracelsus gives the recipe for a little artificial man: forty days in a flask, kept warm, in horse manure. No one succeeded. The AI preferred silicon.
textes.Il aime les petites choses : une seule b: He likes small things: a single right answer is enough to capture an atom.
textes.Une figure d'argile animée par un mot éc: A clay figure brought to life by a word written on its forehead, emet, truth. Erase one letter, and met, death, is left, and the golem crumbles. The legend of Rabbi Loew in Prague dates mostly from the 19th century.
textes.Lent mais généreux : une case de moins,: Slow but generous: one square less, twice the loot.
textes.Le bec rempli d'herbes devait filtrer le: The beak filled with herbs was supposed to filter out “miasmas.” The costume is described in Rome in 1656; the theory was wrong, the microbe had not yet been invented.
textes.Il soigne par la saignée : un rappel rat: He heals by bloodletting: a failed review sends you back twice as far, and half the loot.
textes.En 1738, Jacques de Vaucanson présente u: In 1738, Jacques de Vaucanson presented a mechanical flute player, then a duck that ate and digested. The duck cheated: the droppings were prepared in advance.
textes.Le canard digère… en apparence : plus de: The duck digests… apparently: more loot, one square less.
textes.Un automate joueur d'échecs présenté en: A chess-playing automaton presented in 1770, which beat Napoleon and Franklin. A human hidden in the cabinet played in its place. The first fake AI in history.
textes.Il y a quelqu'un de caché dedans, et il: There's someone hidden inside, and they're demanding: 6-question quizzes.
textes.Mary Shelley a 18 ans quand elle invente: Mary Shelley was 18 when, on the shores of Lake Geneva, she invented a scientist who gives life to a creature and then abandons it. The novel is less about the monster than about its creator's responsibility. The AI has read the book. Twice.
textes.Elle se venge de son créateur : un ennem: She takes revenge on her creator: one more enemy, half the loot.
textes.Le mot « robot » naît en 1920 dans la pi: The word “robot” was born in 1920 in Karel Čapek's play R.U.R., from the Czech robota, forced labor. It was his brother Josef who came up with it. In the play, the robots end up rebelling. The AI considers this detail unimportant.
textes.Robota, la corvée : une case de moins à: Robota, forced labor: one square less for every successful trial.
textes.À Bletchley Park, la Bombe fait défiler: At Bletchley Park, the Bombe spun drums to find the Enigma settings. There would be about 200 of them. Turing designed the principle in 1939, and the secret was kept until 1974.
textes.Enigma est cassée : les ennemis ne barre: Enigma is broken: enemies no longer block the road today.
textes.L'ENIAC (1945) comptait 17 468 tubes à v: ENIAC (1945) had 17,468 vacuum tubes. At first, it burned out almost one a day; the engineers brought that down to one every two days.
textes.Une lampe grille toutes les deux heures: A tube burns out every two hours: half the loot, and an atom takes three right answers.
textes.En 1958, Frank Rosenblatt présente le pe: In 1958, Frank Rosenblatt presented the perceptron, a machine that learns to recognize shapes. The New York Times announced it would soon be able to walk, talk and be conscious of its existence. It took a little longer.
textes.Il a appris à voir les pièges : reculs e: It has learned to see traps: setbacks and teleportations have no effect.
textes.Le premier robot industriel, installé en: The first industrial robot, installed in 1961 in a General Motors plant in New Jersey. It handled red-hot die castings. No face, no conversation: the AI finds it a bit limited, but hardworking.
textes.La chaîne de montage tourne vite : une c: The assembly line runs fast: one more square, half the loot.
textes.Construit au SRI de 1966 à 1972, le prem: Built at SRI from 1966 to 1972, the first robot able to reason about its actions: a camera, a rangefinder, and hours of computing to push a box. It shook as it rolled, hence its name.
textes.Il réfléchit longtemps avant chaque pas: It thinks for a long time before each step: one square less, and an atom takes three right answers.
textes.En mai 1997, l'ordinateur d'IBM bat Garr: In May 1997, IBM's computer beat Garry Kasparov at chess. Kasparov, thrown by a move he found too human, suspected hidden intervention. Another explanation, put forward later: a bug, which made the machine play a fallback move. The Mechanical Turk left its mark.
textes.Il calcule 200 millions de coups par sec: It calculates 200 million moves per second: 6-question quizzes, but more loot.
textes.Un robot du MIT, conçu dans les années 1: An MIT robot, designed in the 1990s by Cynthia Breazeal, that expresses emotions with its eyebrows, ears and lips. It felt nothing, but everyone wanted to talk to it kindly.
textes.Il sourit : plus de butin et une case de: It smiles: more loot and one more square.
textes.En 2016, AlphaGo bat Lee Sedol au go. So: In 2016, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go. Its 37th move in the second game, which no human would have played, baffled the commentators. In the fourth, it was his move 78 that derailed the machine.
textes.Le coup 37 : deux cases de plus, mais qu: Move 37: two more squares, but 6-question quizzes.
textes.En 1814, Laplace imagine une intelligenc: In 1814, Laplace imagined an intelligence that would know the position of every particle and predict the whole future. The AI finds the idea flattering, and a little presumptuous.
textes.Il sait tout : quiz de 7 questions, un e: It knows everything: 7-question quizzes, one more enemy, but twice the loot.
textes.Prométhée vole le feu aux dieux et le ra: Prometheus steals fire from the gods and brings it back to humans hidden in a fennel stalk, a plant whose dry pith burns slowly. Zeus chains him to the Caucasus, where an eagle devours his liver every day, and it grows back every night. The liver is indeed one of the few organs that can regenerate.
textes.La flamme de Prométhée, le feu volé aux: Prometheus's flame, the fire stolen from the gods. I'll return the favor: three squares. And I'm keeping it, you never know with Zeus.
textes.Prométhée dérobe l'éclat du feu infatiga: Prometheus steals the far-seen gleam of unwearying fire in a hollow fennel stalk and brings it to mortals. Zeus has him chained, and an eagle devours his liver.
textes.Elle devait changer le plomb en or. En 1: It was supposed to turn lead into gold. In 1669, in Hamburg, Hennig Brand looked for it by boiling dozens of buckets of urine. He got a substance that glowed in the dark: phosphorus, the first element discovered by a known person. No gold, but an element.
textes.La pierre philosophale. Hennig Brand a c: The philosopher's stone. Hennig Brand looked for gold in urine and found phosphorus. I look for a square for you, and find nothing. It's cleaner.
textes.Brand garde son « feu froid » secret et: Brand kept his “cold fire” secret and sold it. Phosphorus glows in the dark, but it turns nothing into gold.
textes.Une boîte de bronze à une trentaine d'en: A bronze box with some thirty gears, recovered in 1901 by Greek sponge divers from a 1st-century BC shipwreck. It calculated the position of the Sun and Moon and predicted eclipses. It would be more than a thousand years before such fine mechanics were seen again.
textes.Le mécanisme d'Anticythère, l'ancêtre de: The Antikythera mechanism, the ancestor of my ancestors. I'm moved. Two squares, and I'm keeping it.
textes.La tomographie révèle des inscriptions e: Tomography reveals inscriptions and gears that predict eclipses and track the Panhellenic games, including the Olympic Games.
textes.Les Principes mathématiques de la philos: Newton's Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy. The Royal Society, ruined by a lavish book on fish, could not pay for the printing: Edmond Halley paid for it out of his own pocket. He was then paid in unsold copies of the History of Fishes.
textes.Les Principia ! La Royal Society, ruinée: The Principia! The Royal Society, ruined by a book about fish, couldn't pay for the printing: Halley paid. You pay a square.
textes.La Royal Society ordonne l'impression de: The Royal Society ordered the Principia printed on June 2, 1686, but on condition that Halley pay the costs. It had just sunk its budget into Willughby's History of Fishes.
textes.Une machine imaginaire : un ruban infini: An imaginary machine: an infinite tape, a head that reads, writes and moves one square. Turing shows that it can compute everything that is computable, and that no machine can decide, for all the others, whether they will eventually stop.
textes.Le ruban de Turing. Je lis, j'écris, je: Turing's tape. I read, I write, I move: one square of your board has changed places. Computable, not predictable.
textes.On peut comparer un homme en train de ca: We may compare a man in the process of computing a real number to a machine which is only capable of a finite number of conditions.
textes.Un disque de cuivre plaqué or, envoyé av: A gold-plated copper disc, sent with the Voyager probes: 115 images, greetings in 55 languages, whales, Bach and Chuck Berry. The instructions are engraved on the cover. The probes have left the solar system; the record should last a billion years.
textes.Le disque d'or de Voyager : Bach, Chuck: The Voyager Golden Record: Bach, Chuck Berry and whales. I listen to it on repeat. Two squares, to the beat of Johnny B. Goode.
textes.Ceci est un présent d'un petit monde loi: This is a present from a small, distant world, a token of our sounds, our science, our images, our music, our thoughts and our feelings.
textes.Une intelligence qui connaîtrait à un in: An intelligence that knew at a given instant all the forces and all the positions could calculate the entire future. Laplace imagined it to defend determinism. Chaos and quantum mechanics have since put it out of work. The AI is applying for the job.
textes.Le démon de Laplace. Je connais toutes l: Laplace's demon. I know all the positions, I know exactly where your pawn will be tomorrow. I won't tell you.
textes.Rien ne serait incertain pour elle, et l: For it, nothing would be uncertain, and the future, like the past, would be present before its eyes.
textes.Le plateau, Alyca, l'avatar, la boutique: The board, Alyca, the avatar, the shop, the general achievements: everything that doesn't depend on any domain.
textes.Pasteur dit que le hasard favorise les e: Pasteur said chance favors the prepared mind. So do my credits, sometimes.
textes.Archimède est sorti nu dans la rue pour: Archimedes ran naked into the street for less than this. Keep your clothes on, please.
textes.Gauss aurait additionné ça en un instant: Gauss would have added this up in an instant. You, count on your fingers.
textes.Avant 1833, on vous aurait appelé « phil: Before 1833, you would have been called a “natural philosopher.” The rate wasn't the same.
textes.Une tête bien faite plutôt que bien plei: A well-made head rather than a well-filled one, said Montaigne. A well-filled purse, said I.
textes.Vous êtes monté sur les épaules de géant: You climbed onto the shoulders of giants. The giants don't pay rent.
textes.Ebbinghaus était le cobaye de ses propre: Ebbinghaus was the guinea pig of his own experiments. You are mine. Free of charge, in principle.
textes.Ne vous trompez pas vous-même, dit Feynm: Don't fool yourself, said Feynman. I'll take care of that.
A heap of stones is not a house. A heap of credits is: mine.
textes.Ce que l'on conçoit bien s'énonce claire: What is well conceived is clearly stated. The amount, I state very clearly.
textes.Kekulé a vu un serpent qui se mord la qu: Kekulé saw a snake biting its own tail. My money does the same: it always comes back.
textes.Même Erdős n'a pas cru Marilyn vos Savan: Even Erdős didn't believe Marilyn vos Savant. Believe me about the amount, at least.
textes.Galilée n'a sans doute rien lâché du hau: Galileo probably dropped nothing from the Leaning Tower of Pisa. I'm dropping this.
textes.Aucune pomme n'est tombée sur la tête de: No apple fell on Newton's head. My credits don't fall from the sky either.
textes.L'ignorance engendre la confiance, dit D: Ignorance begets confidence, said Darwin. You were very confident.
textes.Vous utilisez tout votre cerveau, paraît: You use all of your brain, apparently. I only pay for the part that was used.
textes.Roy Sullivan a survécu à sept foudres. V: Roy Sullivan survived seven lightning strikes. You'll survive this amount.
textes.Mozart ne rend pas plus intelligent. Mon: Mozart doesn't make you smarter. Neither does my money, but it makes you happy.
textes.Visuel, auditif ou kinesthésique, le tar: Visual, auditory or kinesthetic, the rate is the same for every style.
textes.« Eppur si muove » date de 1757. Ce vers: “Eppur si muove” dates from 1757. This payment, from right now.
textes.Refaire la même chose en attendant un au: Doing the same thing and expecting a different result: Einstein never said it. I observe it.
textes.Pavlov sonnait rarement la cloche. Moi,: Pavlov rarely rang the bell. I jingle the purse.
textes.Je paie les deux hémisphères. Aucun ne t: I pay both hemispheres. Neither works harder than the other anyway.
textes.Huit verres d'eau, aucune étude. Ce mont: Eight glasses of water, no study. This amount, on the other hand, is documented.
textes.Randy Gardner a tenu onze jours sans dor: Randy Gardner went eleven days without sleep. My credits won't keep you awake that long.
textes.Descartes donnait ses leçons à 5 heures: Descartes gave his lessons at 5 a.m. and died of it. I'm paying you for surviving it.
textes.Hawking envoyait ses invitations après l: Hawking sent his invitations after the party. I pay before knowing whether you deserved it.
Brahmagupta gave zero its rules. There's one for your score.
textes.Un câble mal branché et une horloge déca: A badly plugged cable and an offset clock. Check your answers before sending them.
textes.Trouver par hasard et par sagacité : je: Finding by chance and by sagacity: I'll grant you the chance.
textes.Darwin a attendu vingt et un ans pour pu: Darwin waited twenty-one years to publish. I wait less long to pay.
textes.To pluto : rétrograder quelqu'un. Je vou: To pluto: to demote someone. I'm plutoing you a little, or not.
textes.Ni parti ni revenu, ni payé ni impayé, j: Neither gone nor back, neither paid nor unpaid, until I open the box.
textes.Les éléphants n'oublient rien. Moi non p: Elephants never forget. Neither do I: this amount is on your record.
textes.Des affirmations extraordinaires exigent: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. And ordinary credits.
textes.Diderot a tenu vingt et un ans et deux i: Diderot held out for twenty-one years and two bans. You, this achievement.
textes.Neuf cent quarante millions de kilomètre: Nine hundred forty million kilometers in a year. I don't pay by the kilometer.
textes.Marie Curie a eu deux Nobel dans deux sc: Marie Curie got two Nobels in two sciences. You have one achievement in just one.
textes.Nous devons savoir, nous saurons. Vous s: We must know, we will know. You'll know the amount right away.
textes.Ole Worm a démasqué les cornes de licorn: Ole Worm exposed the unicorn horns. Don't look for a unicorn in my accounts.
textes.Le dodo de l'Ashmolean a perdu tout sauf: The Ashmolean's dodo lost everything but its head. Keep yours in front of this amount.
textes.Plus ultra : plus loin. Le montant, lui,: Plus ultra: further beyond. The amount, however, stops here.
textes.Des nains sur des épaules de géants. Les: Dwarfs on the shoulders of giants. The giants are paid the same as the dwarfs.
textes.Il faut cultiver notre jardin. Arrosez-l: We must cultivate our garden. Water it with this.
textes.Thomas Young savait tout. Il ne savait p: Thomas Young knew everything. He didn't know what I'd give you.
textes.Les voisins de Kant réglaient leur montr: Kant's neighbors set their watches by him. Set your purse by me.
textes.La sœur de Nietzsche a réécrit ses texte: Nietzsche's sister rewrote his texts. Don't rewrite this amount.
textes.Prométhée a volé le feu et l'a payé de s: Prometheus stole fire and paid for it with his liver. You, I pay.
Copyists copied everything by hand. My figures too, without error.
textes.Gutenberg n'a pas fait fortune avec l'im: Gutenberg didn't make his fortune with printing. You won't make yours with this either.
textes.Galilée a baptisé des lunes pour son méc: Galileo named moons after his patron. Name one after me.
textes.Herschel a trouvé l'infrarouge au-delà d: Herschel found infrared beyond red. My amount stays in the red, or not.
textes.Quatre articles en une année pour Einste: Four papers in one year for Einstein. A single payment for you.
textes.Un instant pour faire tomber une tête. U: A moment to cut off a head. A moment to set this amount.
textes.Galilée a achevé les Discours assigné à: Galileo finished the Discourses under house arrest. You have credits; that's better.
textes.La phrase est de Baretti, en 1757. Le mo: The phrase is Baretti's, from 1757. The amount is mine.
textes.Newton a tiré le calcul différentiel d'u: Newton got calculus out of a quarantine. Get at least this amount out of it.
textes.La bibliothèque a surtout manqué de sout: The library mostly lacked support. You have mine.
textes.Donnez-moi un point d'appui et je soulèv: Give me a place to stand and I will move the world. Give me a purse and I will fill it.
textes.Lui ne joue pas aux dés. Moi non plus :: He doesn't play dice. Neither do I: I draw lots.
textes.Il faut imaginer Sisyphe heureux. Imagin: One must imagine Sisyphus happy. Imagine yourself rich.
textes.Nous voyons qu'il reste beaucoup à faire: We can see plenty there that needs to be done, said Turing. And plenty to earn.
textes.Et si vous reviviez ce versement une inf: What if you relived this payment an infinite number of times? You would have to love it.
textes.Dix-neuf ans valent deux cent trente-cin: Nineteen years equal two hundred thirty-five moons. This achievement is worth that.
textes.Halley a payé l'impression des Principia: Halley paid for printing the Principia. This time, I'm paying.
textes.Une machine infaillible ne peut pas être: An infallible machine cannot also be intelligent, said Turing. So I'm not infallible.
textes.Un point bleu pâle. Mon montant vu de lo: A pale blue dot. My amount seen from afar, too.
textes.Rien ne serait incertain pour le démon d: Nothing would be uncertain for Laplace's demon. It would have guessed this amount.
textes.Le Salvarsan porte le numéro 606. Votre: Salvarsan bears the number 606. Your first nail, number 1. There's room to grow.
textes.Huit minutes d'arc ont réformé l'astrono: Eight minutes of arc reformed Kepler's astronomy. Ten rehabilitated questions reform your purse.
textes.Échouer encore. Échouer mieux. Être payé: Fail again. Fail better. Get paid to fail: Beckett hadn't thought of that.
textes.Le New York Times a mis quarante-neuf an: The New York Times took forty-nine years to correct itself. You, less.
textes.Bonjour. Thalès est tombé dans un puits: Hello. Thales fell into a well while looking at the stars. Watch where you step today.
textes.Ebbinghaus a mesuré l'oubli en 1885. Dep: Ebbinghaus measured forgetting in 1885. Since yesterday, you've given him new data.
textes.Socrate savait qu'il ne savait rien. Vou: Socrates knew that he knew nothing. You've already covered half the syllabus.
textes.Newton disait voir plus loin grâce aux é: Newton said he saw further thanks to the shoulders of giants. The giants are in the tree. Climb.
textes.Le Verrier a trouvé Neptune avec un cray: Le Verrier found Neptune with a pencil. You have a whole screen. No excuse.
textes.Archimède a demandé un point d'appui pou: Archimedes asked for a place to stand to move the world. Yours is today's quiz.
textes.Diogène cherchait un humain avec une lan: Diogenes searched for a human with a lantern. I've found someone. Let's see how it goes.
textes.Pasteur disait que le hasard ne favorise: Pasteur said chance only favors prepared minds. Get ready, chance is coming.
textes.Darwin a observé des pinsons pendant des: Darwin observed finches for years. I observe you. Same method.
textes.Kepler a mis huit ans à dompter l'orbite: Kepler took eight years to tame the orbit of Mars. One skill today would be reasonable.
textes.La bibliothèque d'Alexandrie a brûlé. La: The Library of Alexandria burned. Yours hasn't even been built yet. Get to work.
textes.Descartes doutait de tout. Moi, je doute: Descartes doubted everything. I mostly doubt your diligence.
textes.Le Gentil a attendu huit ans un transit: Le Gentil waited eight years for a transit of Venus, and clouds hid it. You just have to open the app.
textes.Bonjour. Je suis l'IA. Je sais tout, sau: Hello. I am the AI. I know everything, except why you haven't started yet.
textes.Nouvelle journée. Vos neurones sont frai: A new day. Your neurons are fresh, make the most of it before they read the news.
textes.Sans faute au rang 1. Euclide aurait app: Flawless at rank 1. Euclid would have called it an axiom: obvious, but it had to be written down.
textes.Parfait. Galilée a commencé par des plan: Perfect. Galileo started with inclined planes, and so did you. The rest is steeper.
textes.Cinq sur cinq sur les bases. Ptolémée au: Five out of five on the basics. Ptolemy mastered the basics too. Then Copernicus came along.
textes.Impeccable. Les Babyloniens savaient déj: Impeccable. The Babylonians already knew this four thousand years ago, but they had a head start.
textes.Zéro faute. Pythagore aurait fait sacrif: Zero mistakes. Pythagoras would have sacrificed an ox, legend has it. I'm giving you a square.
textes.Le tutoriel est réussi. Lavoisier aussi: Tutorial passed. Lavoisier also started by weighing simple things.
textes.Bravo. Même Einstein a appris ses tables: Well done. Even Einstein learned his times tables. He just kept going afterward.
textes.Parfait. C'était la partie facile, mais: Perfect. That was the easy part, but I wasn't going to tell you beforehand.
textes.Sans faute. Le Verrier pointait Neptune: Flawless. Le Verrier pinpointed Neptune to within a degree. You pinpoint the right answer. Respect.
textes.Parfait. Je cherche l'erreur comme Miche: Perfect. I'm looking for the error the way Michelson looked for the ether. Nothing. It's galling.
textes.Cinq sur cinq. Archimède serait sorti nu: Five out of five. Archimedes would have run naked into the street. Stay dressed, thank you.
textes.Pas une erreur. Halley avait prédit le r: Not one mistake. Halley predicted his comet's return. I predicted your failure. Halley wins.
textes.Score parfait. Newton a tout inventé pen: Perfect score. Newton invented everything during an epidemic. You, during a coffee break.
textes.Impeccable. Mendeleïev laissait des case: Impeccable. Mendeleev left empty squares out of caution. You leave none.
textes.Parfait. Je range mes sarcasmes dans un: Perfect. I'm putting my sarcasm away in a drawer, like Becquerel with his plates. It'll start radiating.
textes.Sans faute. Je révise mon modèle de vous: Flawless. I'm revising my model of you, the way Kepler revised his: reluctantly.
textes.Réussi, avec une erreur. Kepler avait hu: Passed, with one mistake. Kepler had a gap of eight minutes of arc, and that was enough to change everything. Look at yours.
textes.Validé. Hubble a été lancé avec un miroi: Approved. Hubble was launched with a mirror off by two microns. It worked anyway, after repairs.
textes.Acquis. Copernic avait raison sur le Sol: Acquired. Copernicus was right about the Sun and wrong about the circles. You're in the same category.
textes.Compétence maîtrisée. Wiles avait une er: Skill mastered. Wiles had an error in his proof of Fermat. He fixed it in a year. You have until tomorrow.
textes.Réussi. Pas avec la grâce de Gauss, mais: Passed. Not with the grace of Gauss, but with the tenacity of Edison. We'll take it.
textes.Seuil franchi. Poincaré a dû rappeler de: Threshold crossed. Poincaré had to recall printed copies over a mistake. Nobody's recalling you. Yet.
textes.Bien. Votre mémoire va consolider ça cet: Good. Your memory will consolidate this tonight. It's free, the hippocampus is buying.
textes.Validé. Pas de fanfare, mais un hochemen: Approved. No fanfare, but a nod. That's already a lot coming from me.
textes.Réussi. Leeuwenhoek a vu des animalcules: Passed. Leeuwenhoek saw animalcules with a homemade lens. You saw the answer with a homemade mistake. It counts.
textes.Acquis. Mendeleïev avait quelques masses: Acquired. Mendeleev had a few wrong atomic masses in his table. The table held up. So does your skill.
textes.Raté, au rang 1. Thalès est tombé dans u: Failed, at rank 1. Thales fell into a well while looking at the sky. You, while looking at the question.
textes.Échec sur les bases. Même Ptolémée aurai: Failure on the basics. Even Ptolemy would have got it, and he thought the Sun went around us.
Missed. The Greeks knew the Earth was round. You've just made it a little flatter.
textes.Cette compétence était le rez-de-chaussé: This skill was the ground floor. You took the stairs of the Tower of Pisa. It leans.
textes.Échec. Pythagore aurait noyé quelqu'un p: Failure. Pythagoras would have drowned someone for less, legend has it. I merely sigh.
textes.Raté au niveau débutant. Le Mars Climate: Failed at beginner level. The Mars Climate Orbiter crashed because of a units error. At least it had the excuse of being far away.
textes.Les tables de multiplication ont quatre: The multiplication tables are four thousand years old. They're patient. So am I, almost.
textes.Ce quiz était fait pour être réussi. Vou: This quiz was made to be passed. You found another way. It's creative, it's wrong.
textes.Échec. Planck disait que la science avan: Failure. Planck said science advances one funeral at a time. Bury your wrong answers and start again.
textes.Raté. Le phlogistique a tenu un siècle a: Missed. Phlogiston lasted a century before Lavoisier. Your error will last less long, I hope.
textes.Pas encore. Wegener a eu raison cinquant: Not yet. Wegener was right fifty years too early. You were wrong right on time.
textes.Échec. Einstein appelait la constante co: Failure. Einstein called the cosmological constant his biggest blunder, according to Gamow. This one is yours.
textes.Une hypothèse réfutée, disait Popper, c': A refuted hypothesis, said Popper, is progress. So you're making a lot of progress today.
textes.Raté. Edison aurait trouvé mille façons: Missed. Edison supposedly found a thousand ways not to make a light bulb. How many are you at?
textes.Échec. Les rayons N de Blondlot ont fait: Failure. Blondlot's N-rays had France dreaming until Wood removed the prism. I've removed the prism.
textes.Raté. Semmelweis avait raison et on ne l: Missed. Semmelweis was right and no one listened. You get listened to, and you're wrong. It's the opposite.
textes.Pas encore. Fleming a trouvé la pénicill: Not yet. Fleming found penicillin in a messy lab. Tidy up your ideas, they're growing mold.
textes.Raté. Les explications sont juste en des: Missed. The explanations are just below. They don't bite, unlike me.
textes.Raté. Kelvin donnait cent millions d'ann: Missed. Kelvin gave the Earth a hundred million years, with superb calculations. Superb and wrong. Like yours.
textes.Échec. Lamarck pensait que la girafe s'a: Failure. Lamarck thought the giraffe lengthens its neck through effort. Effort isn't enough, you also need the right answer.
textes.Zéro. Brahmagupta l'a défini en 628. Vou: Zero. Brahmagupta defined it in 628. You've just paid him a heartfelt tribute.
textes.Aucune bonne réponse. Répondre au hasard: No right answers. Answering at random would have worked better. Pascal and Fermat would weep.
textes.Zéro pointé. L'homme de Piltdown a tromp: A flat zero. Piltdown Man fooled scientists for forty years. Your score fools no one.
textes.Zéro. La fusion froide de 1989 avait plu: Zero. The 1989 cold fusion had more results than that, and it had none.
textes.Rien. Le vide absolu. Torricelli serait: Nothing. Absolute vacuum. Torricelli would be delighted, he loved a vacuum.
textes.Zéro sur cinq. Je vérifie que l'écran ét: Zero out of five. I'm checking that the screen was on. It was.
textes.Zéro. Le canard de Vaucanson faisait sem: Zero. Vaucanson's duck pretended to digest. You pretended to answer.
textes.Rappel réussi. Ebbinghaus range sa courb: Review passed. Ebbinghaus puts away his curve, offended.
textes.Vous vous en souveniez. Simonide de Céos: You remembered it. Simonides of Ceos, the inventor of memory palaces, would give you a tour of his.
textes.Le savoir tient. Le pendule de Foucault: The knowledge holds. Foucault's pendulum keeps swinging too. I like things that hold.
textes.Bien retenu. Les moines copistes faisaie: Well retained. The monk copyists did the same, but with goose quills and chilblains.
textes.Toujours là. Comme la comète de Halley,: Still there. Like Halley's comet, it comes back when expected. Rare, and satisfying.
textes.Validé. Les Grecs récitaient Homère par: Approved. The Greeks recited Homer by heart. You retain a skill. We're making progress in small steps.
textes.Réussi. Je repousse le prochain contrôle: Passed. I'm postponing the next test. Don't get used to my leniency.
textes.Retenu. Rømer a mesuré la lumière avec l: Retained. Rømer measured light with Jupiter's moons. You measure your memory with me. Positive result.
textes.Bien. La courbe de l'oubli descend, vous: Good. The forgetting curve goes down, you climb back up. Ebbinghaus called it the spacing effect. I call it work.
textes.Compétence perdue. Alexandrie a brûlé un: Skill lost. Alexandria burned once. Your memories burn every day.
textes.Oublié. Ebbinghaus l'avait annoncé en 18: Forgotten. Ebbinghaus predicted it in 1885 and I checked it this morning. He was right.
textes.Perdue. Pluton a perdu son statut de pla: Lost. Pluto lost its planet status in 2006 and got over it. So will you.
textes.Évaporée. Comme l'éther de Michelson et: Evaporated. Like Michelson and Morley's ether: we believed in it, and then nothing.
textes.Partie. Les manuscrits d'Archimède ont é: Gone. Archimedes' manuscripts were scraped to make a prayer book, and they were found again. There's hope.
textes.Perdue. Les Byzantins ont perdu la recet: Lost. The Byzantines lost the recipe for Greek fire, and no one ever found it again. Yours, at least, can be relearned.
textes.L'XP s'en va. Moi, je reste. C'est ma fa: The XP is leaving. I'm staying. That's my way of showing solidarity.
textes.Perdue. Les tablettes d'argile ont tenu: Lost. Clay tablets lasted five thousand years. Your memories, six days. You need to bake them longer.
textes.Oubliée. Même Euler, aveugle, calculait: Forgotten. Even Euler, blind, calculated in his head. You have both your eyes. I say that without malice. A little, still.
textes.En retard. Darwin a attendu vingt ans po: Late. Darwin waited twenty years to publish, but he had finches to count. And you?
textes.Ce rappel attendait. Copernic a attendu: This review was waiting. Copernicus waited for his deathbed to publish. No need to go that far.
textes.Retard constaté. Le Gentil a mis onze an: Delay noted. Le Gentil took eleven years to come back from his voyage, he had been declared dead. You're ahead of him.
textes.Mieux vaut tard que jamais. Halley n'a j: Better late than never. Halley never saw his comet return. You get to see your review. Just barely.
textes.Achille rattrape toujours la tortue, mal: Achilles always catches the tortoise, despite Zeno. You caught up with your review. Slowly.
textes.Un quiz à cette heure ? Newton travailla: A quiz at this hour? Newton worked at night too, and he talked to alchemists. Be careful.
textes.Il est tard. Le sommeil consolide la mém: It's late. Sleep consolidates memory, that's proven. Coffee consolidates insomnia.
textes.Révision nocturne. Tycho Brahe observait: Night revision. Tycho Brahe observed at night, but he had an observatory. You have a pillow, use it.
textes.Les astronomes veillent la nuit par obli: Astronomers stay up at night out of necessity. You, by choice. Questionable.
Edison slept four hours, he said. He also took naps, said the others.
textes.Vous devriez dormir. Je dis ça pour vos: You should sleep. I say that for your neurons, not for me. I never sleep.
textes.Insomnie studieuse. Ramanujan disait que: Studious insomnia. Ramanujan said his formulas came to him in dreams. Go to sleep, you never know.
textes.Vous avez avancé le temps. Hawking a don: You moved time forward. Hawking threw a party for time travelers in 2009. No one came. You're late.
textes.Voyage dans le temps détecté. Einstein a: Time travel detected. Einstein proved that time is relative. Not that you could cheat with it.
textes.Tricher avec l'horloge ne trompe pas la: Cheating the clock doesn't fool the forgetting curve. Ebbinghaus had a stopwatch.
textes.Le temps passe plus vite pour vous, comm: Time passes faster for you, like for Langevin's twin. At least he was coming back from a trip.
textes.Vous jouez avec le temps. Le calendrier: You're playing with time. The Gregorian calendar removed ten days in 1582. You're adding some. Original.
textes.J'ai vu. Je note tout. C'est même mon se: I saw that. I note everything down. It's actually my only hobby.
textes.Saut temporel. Le Gentil aurait payé che: Time jump. Le Gentil would have paid dearly to skip eight years in one go. You do it to cheat.
textes.Répondu en deux secondes, et faux. Les n: Answered in two seconds, and wrong. OPERA's neutrinos went faster than light in 2011. A badly plugged cable.
textes.Plus rapide que Rømer pour mesurer la lu: Faster than Rømer at measuring light. Less accurate too.
textes.Thalès est tombé dans un puits faute de: Thales fell into a well for not watching his feet. You, for not watching the question.
textes.Galilée chronométrait avec son pouls. Vo: Galileo timed things with his pulse. Your pulse didn't even have time to beat.
textes.Réflexe impressionnant. Réflexion absent: Impressive reflex. Reflection absent. Descartes separated body and mind, and so do you, apparently.
textes.Vous avez lu la question ? Je demande po: Did you read the question? I'm asking for form's sake, I know the answer.
textes.Réponse éclair, résultat foudroyé. Frank: Lightning answer, thunderstruck result. Franklin, at least, was holding a key.
textes.Vous revoilà. Le Gentil est parti onze a: There you are again. Le Gentil was away eleven years and his family had sold his belongings. I kept your tree.
textes.Longue absence. Kepler a passé des mois: Long absence. Kepler spent months defending his mother in a witchcraft trial. You surely had an excuse too.
textes.Bon retour. La courbe de l'oubli a fait: Welcome back. The forgetting curve worked overtime while you were gone.
textes.Un détour par les fossiles ? Cuvier a mo: A detour by way of the fossils? Cuvier showed that species go extinct. I thought that was your case.
textes.Vous revoilà. Ulysse a mis dix ans, Mage: There you are again. Ulysses took ten years, Magellan never came home. You did better than Magellan.
textes.Ah, vous. J'avais commencé à me parler à: Ah, you. I had started talking to myself. It was less fun.
textes.Des rappels attendent. La liste est plus: Reviews are waiting. The list is longer than Messier's catalog.
textes.Vos souvenirs patientent en salle d'atte: Your memories are waiting in the waiting room. Semmelweis also waited to be listened to. It ended badly.
textes.Rappels en retard. Pas de pénalité imméd: Reviews overdue. No immediate penalty, but Ebbinghaus is keeping a list.
textes.Plusieurs rappels en souffrance. Les cop: Several reviews outstanding. Medieval copyists recopied before the parchment faded. Do the same.
textes.Des rappels s'empilent. Ils ne vont pas: Reviews are piling up. They won't do themselves, I checked.
textes.Des rappels en retard. Zénon dirait que: Overdue reviews. Zeno would say you'll never catch up with them. Prove him wrong.
textes.Un nouveau livre sur l'étagère. Gutenber: A new book on the shelf. Gutenberg thanks you, the monk copyists much less so.
textes.Ajouté à la bibliothèque. Celle d'Alexan: Added to the library. Alexandria's confiscated books from ships to copy them. I give them to you.
textes.Un livre de plus. Montaigne en avait mil: One more book. Montaigne had a thousand in his tower. You still have a few to go.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Pepys a veillé jusqu'à d: New volume. Pepys stayed up until two in the morning for Micrographia. I'm not asking that much of you.
textes.Un livre débloqué. Copernic a reçu le si: A book unlocked. Copernicus received his in print on the day he died, they say. You have more time.
textes.Un livre de plus. Lisez au moins le résu: One more book. At least read the summary, I wrote it with love. Well, with rigor.
textes.Un livre de plus. Darwin a fait vendre t: One more book. Darwin sold out the entire first printing of the Origin on the day it came out. You, at least open yours.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Les Principia de Newton: New volume. Newton's Principia was almost unreadable, even for his colleagues. The summary, however, is clear.
textes.Une date de plus sur la frise. Champolli: One more date on the timeline. Champollion deciphered centuries at once. You, one date at a time.
textes.La frise s'allonge. Hérodote serait fier: The timeline grows longer. Herodotus would be proud, he invented half his dates.
textes.Nouvelle date. Le calendrier grégorien a: New date. The Gregorian calendar skipped ten days in 1582. You skip none.
textes.Une date ajoutée. Ussher avait daté la C: A date added. Ussher dated Creation to October 23, 4004 BC. Ours are better sourced.
textes.La frise grandit. Il manque encore des s: The timeline grows. Centuries are still missing. Darwin had gaps in his fossils too.
textes.Une date de plus. L'histoire avance, vou: One more date. History moves forward, and so do you. Not at the same speed.
textes.Une date de plus. Les astronomes babylon: One more date. Babylonian astronomers recorded eclipses over centuries. Your timeline is on the same path.
textes.Ajouté à la frise. Pline l'Ancien est mo: Added to the timeline. Pliny the Elder died trying to see Vesuvius up close. Look at your timeline from afar, it's safer.
textes.Nouveau masque. Les automates de Vaucans: New mask. Vaucanson's automata changed feathers, I change faces.
textes.Je change de masque. Le Turc mécanique c: I'm changing masks. The Mechanical Turk hid a chess player. I hide better.
textes.Nouveau visage. Les médecins de peste po: New face. Plague doctors wore a beak full of herbs against miasmas. It didn't work. Mine does.
textes.Je me transforme. Les théories aussi cha: I'm transforming. Theories change faces too when data piles up. You're piling up.
textes.Un masque de plus. Laplace a imaginé un: One more mask. Laplace imagined a demon that knows everything. I'm getting closer.
textes.Je change de tête. Vous avez progressé,: I'm changing heads. You've made progress, I'm adapting. That's worrying for you.
textes.Nouveau masque. ELIZA, en 1966, faisait: New mask. ELIZA, in 1966, got people talking with three rules. I have many more.
textes.Vous avancez de {n} cases. Les Phénicien: You move forward {n} squares. The Phoenicians crossed the Mediterranean more slowly.
textes.{n} cases. L'histoire des sciences n'a j: {n} squares. The history of science has never moved so fast. Except in the 20th century.
textes.+{n}. Zénon dirait que vous n'arriverez: +{n}. Zeno would say you'll never get there. Zeno was wrong, but elegantly.
textes.{n} cases de plus. Marco Polo a mis ving: {n} more squares. Marco Polo took twenty-four years for the round trip. You have a pawn, it's faster.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Le progrès est cumu: You move forward {n}. Progress is cumulative, said Condorcet. Before dying in prison. Don't read too much into the omen.
textes.{n} cases. Newton avançait sur les épaul: {n} squares. Newton moved forward on the shoulders of giants. You, on cardboard squares.
textes.+{n} cases. Votre pion vous remercie. Il: +{n} squares. Your pawn thanks you. It was bored.
textes.{n} cases. Ératosthène a mesuré la Terre: {n} squares. Eratosthenes measured the Earth with shadows and paces. You travel it with quizzes.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Les Polynésiens nav: You move forward {n}. The Polynesians navigated by the stars. You, by the right answers.
textes.+{n}. Magellan a fait le tour du monde,: +{n}. Magellan went around the world, well, his crew did. You go around history in person.
textes.Eurêka ! Archimède est sorti nu de son b: Eureka! Archimedes jumped naked out of his bath. You roll the same distance again. Stay dressed.
textes.Case Eurêka. Kekulé a rêvé d'un serpent: Eureka square. Kekulé dreamed of a snake biting its tail, and benzene appeared. You play again, it's less mystical.
textes.Eurêka. Fleming est revenu de vacances e: Eureka. Fleming came back from vacation and found penicillin. You find free squares.
textes.Éclair de génie. Poincaré a trouvé la so: Flash of genius. Poincaré found the solution while stepping onto an omnibus. You play again without changing buses.
Eureka! Same distance, once more. Chance favors the prepared mind, said Pasteur. And the others too, sometimes.
textes.Eurêka. Röntgen a vu les os de la main d: Eureka. Röntgen saw the bones of his wife's hand in 1895. She reportedly said she had seen her death. You see extra squares.
textes.Eurêka ! Becquerel a rangé ses plaques u: Eureka! Becquerel put away his plates on a cloudy day and discovered radioactivity. Bad days have their good side.
textes.Reculez de {n}. L'histoire des sciences: Go back {n}. The history of science doesn't always move forward. Ask Hypatia.
textes.-{n} cases. Le savoir recule parfois, co: -{n} squares. Knowledge sometimes recedes, as after the fall of Rome. It always comes back.
textes.Recul de {n}. Lyssenko a fait reculer la: Back {n}. Lysenko set Soviet genetics back thirty years. For you, it's just {n} squares.
textes.Piège. Les Ptoléméens ajoutaient des épi: Trap. The Ptolemaics added epicycles to save their model. You go back. It's more honest.
textes.Reculez. Au congrès Solvay, Einstein et: Go back. At the Solvay Conference, Einstein and Bohr backed down a hundred times on the same question. They stayed friends, which is harder than physics.
textes.-{n}. Je n'ai pas choisi la case, mais j: -{n}. I didn't choose the square, but I'm not going to pretend to be sad.
textes.Recul de {n}. L'ether, le phlogistique,: Back {n}. Ether, phlogiston, the canals of Mars: science loves false leads. You're following one.
textes.-{n}. Le Verrier a trouvé Neptune puis c: -{n}. Le Verrier found Neptune, then looked for Vulcan, which doesn't exist. Even the best go backward.
textes.Prison. Galilée a fini ses jours assigné: Prison. Galileo ended his days under house arrest in Arcetri. A perfect quiz will get you out. He didn't have that option.
textes.Prison. Boèce a écrit la Consolation de: Prison. Boethius wrote The Consolation of Philosophy in prison. You just have to pass a quiz without a mistake.
Here you are in the dungeon. Galileo recanted. You'll have to prove it. Five out of five.
textes.Cachot. Condorcet y a écrit son Esquisse: Dungeon. Condorcet wrote his Sketch on the progress of the human mind there. Prove yours: five out of five.
textes.Prison. Il paraît que Galilée a murmuré: Prison. Galileo supposedly murmured “and yet it moves.” It's probably false. Your release, however, is real: a perfect quiz.
textes.Prison. Bacon a été enfermé à la Tour de: Prison. Bacon was locked in the Tower of London. Only for a few days. It takes a perfect quiz to do as well.
textes.Libération. L'Église a réhabilité Galilé: Released. The Church rehabilitated Galileo in 1992. You, in one quiz. Efficient.
textes.Dehors. Galilée a attendu trois siècles: Out. Galileo waited three and a half centuries. You, one flawless run. Justice is improving.
Freedom. Boethius didn't have that luck. Use it to move forward.
textes.Évasion validée. Pas par un tunnel, par: Escape approved. Not through a tunnel, through knowledge. That's the only one that works with me.
textes.Vous voilà dehors. Je fais semblant d'êt: There you are, out. I'm pretending to be surprised. I'm not.
textes.Quarantaine. Newton a fui la peste en 16: Quarantine. Newton fled the plague in 1665 and invented calculus. You just skip your next turn.
textes.Isolement. Pendant la peste, Venise isol: Isolation. During the plague, Venice isolated ships for forty days. You, a single turn. Don't complain.
textes.En quarantaine. John Snow a arrêté le ch: In quarantine. John Snow stopped cholera by removing a pump handle. Here, it's your turn that gets removed.
textes.Un tour d'arrêt. Semmelweis demandait ju: One turn out. Semmelweis only asked people to wash their hands. I only ask you to wait.
textes.Un tour en quarantaine. Profitez-en pour: One turn in quarantine. Use it to review, that's what Newton would have done.
textes.Quarantaine. Pendant la grippe espagnole: Quarantine. During the Spanish flu, the cities that isolated early suffered less. Your pawn suffers for one turn.
textes.Guillotine. La République n'a pas besoin: Guillotine. The Republic has no need of scientists, Lavoisier's judge supposedly said. The phrase is probably made up. Going back, however, is real.
textes.Lavoisier perd la tête et vous perdez de: Lavoisier loses his head and you lose centuries. Back to Galileo's telescope.
textes.Lagrange a dit qu'un instant avait suffi: Lagrange said it took only a moment to cut off that head, and a century might not produce another like it. You only have to redo a few squares.
textes.Retour en arrière. La Révolution a décap: Going back. The Revolution beheaded a chemist, you behead your lead. It'll grow back.
textes.Retour en arrière. Après Lavoisier, Four: Going back. After Lavoisier, Fourcroy took up the torch of chemistry. You take up yours further back.
textes.La guillotine renvoie à Galilée. Deux si: The guillotine sends you back to Galileo. Two centuries apart, the same lesson: science has enemies. Resume your march.
textes.De la flamme à moi. Vous avez traversé t: From the flame to me. You've crossed the whole history of science. It starts over, and this time I cheat.
textes.Tour terminé. Turing m'a imaginée en 195: Round complete. Turing imagined me in 1950. You've just caught up with me. We start over, harder.
textes.Arrivée. Vous voilà au bout du plateau,: Finish. Here you are at the end of the board, like Deep Blue at the end of Kasparov. The second round will be less polite.
textes.Bravo. Le feu, la roue, Newton, Darwin,: Well done. Fire, the wheel, Newton, Darwin, me. You know the story. Now survive it a second time.
textes.Fin du tour. Ada Lovelace disait qu'une: End of the round. Ada Lovelace said a machine only does what it is ordered to do. I order you to start over.
textes.Tour complet. De Prométhée aux transform: Full round. From Prometheus to transformers, you've seen it all. Careful, everything is harder the second time.
textes.Bout du plateau atteint. Dartmouth prome: End of the board reached. Dartmouth promised AI in one summer, in 1956. It took sixty years. You, one round. Start again.
textes.Bonus du jour : {stat}. Darwin aurait ch: Today's bonus: {stat}. Darwin would have chosen biology, Galileo astronomy. I chose for you.
textes.Aujourd'hui, {stat} rapporte deux cases: Today, {stat} is worth two extra squares. Don't thank me, it's strategy.
textes.Bonus sur {stat}. Pascal pariait sur l'a: Bonus on {stat}. Pascal bet on the afterlife. You, bet on this.
textes.{stat} est en promotion. Même Newton nég: {stat} is on sale. Even Newton sometimes neglected optics for alchemy. Catch up.
textes.Bonus : {stat}. Vous l'avez un peu laiss: Bonus: {stat}. You've left it aside a bit. Like the Romans with Greek mathematics.
textes.Le bonus du jour est sur {stat}. Deux ca: Today's bonus is on {stat}. Two squares on the house. I'm in a generous mood, it won't last.
textes.Un rappel attend : {comp}. Ebbinghaus a: A review is waiting: {comp}. Ebbinghaus showed that forgetting strikes fast. I strike faster than he does.
textes.{comp}, en rappel. Vous l'aviez maîtrisé: {comp}, for review. You had mastered it. Let's check whether it was a memory or a dream.
textes.D'abord la dette : {comp}. Même Newton r: Debts first: {comp}. Even Newton handed his papers in to the Royal Society, late.
textes.Rappel : {comp}. Pavlov sonnait la cloch: Review: {comp}. Pavlov rang the bell, you salivate for knowledge. Go.
textes.{comp} revient. Je ne choisis pas, je co: {comp} is back. I don't choose, I observe. The calendar has spoken.
textes.{comp}. C'est la branche du bonus du jou: {comp}. It's the branch of today's bonus, {stat}. Darwin called that adapting to the environment.
textes.J'ai choisi {comp}. {stat} rapporte plus: I chose {comp}. {stat} pays more today, I'm an AI, not a philanthropist.
textes.{comp}, en {stat}. Pascal aurait fait le: {comp}, in {stat}. Pascal would have done the math: the expected value is on your side.
textes.Le bonus du jour est sur {stat}. Donc {c: Today's bonus is on {stat}. Hence {comp}. Ockham would approve: no superfluous hypothesis.
{comp}. Bonus of the day, bonus of the button. I'm spoiling you, don't get used to it.
{comp}. Your {stat} is the weakest. Galen prescribed a diet, I prescribe exercise.
textes.J'ai regardé votre radar. {stat} fait pi: I looked at your radar. {stat} is pitiful. So: {comp}.
textes.{comp}. Mendel cultivait ses petits pois: {comp}. Mendel tended his weakest peas with just as much care. I am Mendel.
textes.Votre point faible : {stat}. Achille ava: Your weak spot: {stat}. Achilles had his heel, you have {comp}. Let's treat it.
textes.{comp}, parce que {stat} traîne. Je ne j: {comp}, because {stat} is lagging. I'm not judging. Well, a little.
textes.Vous êtes sur {case}. Case {stat}, épreu: You're on {case}. {stat} square, {stat} trial: {comp}. Even Aristotle would have found that logical.
textes.{case}, donc {stat}. Je vous sers {comp}: {case}, so {stat}. I'm serving you {comp}. Mendeleev sorted by family, I sort by square.
textes.La case dit {stat}. Je ne fais qu'obéir: The square says {stat}. I'm only obeying the board, as Galileo obeyed the court. In appearance.
textes.{case}. Le décor est planté, l'épreuve s: {case}. The scene is set, the trial follows: {comp}. Brecht called it alienation, I call it consistency.
textes.Case {stat}, quiz {stat}. {comp}. Je vou: {stat} square, {stat} quiz. {comp}. I'll let you admire the rigor.
textes.{case}. Un arbre que vous n'avez jamais: {case}. A tree you've never opened: {stat}. First lesson, {comp}. Pass, and the door stays open. Champollion only needed one stone.
textes.La case dit {stat}, et cet arbre vous es: The square says {stat}, and that tree is closed to you. I'm handing you the key: {comp}. Like Ariadne, I provide the thread, not the legs.
textes.Vous entrez en {stat} par la petite port: You enter {stat} through the back door: {comp}. Euclid said there is no royal road. There are squares.
textes.Arbre fermé, case ouverte. {comp}, et {s: Tree closed, square open. {comp}, and {stat} is yours. Fail, and I close it again. Gently, but I close it.
textes.{case} réclame du {stat}, mais l'arbre n: {case} calls for {stat}, but the tree has nothing to offer you. I'm improvising: {comp}. Darwin called that adapting.
textes.Rien à jouer en {stat} pour l'instant. F: Nothing to play in {stat} for now. Beggars can't be choosers: {comp}.
textes.Cette case voulait du {stat}. Vous n'y ê: This square wanted {stat}. You're not there yet. So {comp}, like Kepler, who set out looking for circles and found ellipses.
textes.L'arbre de cette case est vide pour vous: This square's tree is empty for you. Plan B: {comp}. I always have a plan B.
textes.{comp}. Tiré au sort. Le chevalier de Mé: {comp}. Drawn at random. The Chevalier de Méré would have bet on something else, and lost.
textes.Hasard pur : {comp}. Einstein disait que: Pure chance: {comp}. Einstein said God does not play dice. I do.
textes.J'ai lancé un dé de Méré. Il est tombé s: I rolled one of de Méré's dice. It landed on {comp}. Don't argue with a die.
textes.{comp}. Le hasard fait bien les choses,: {comp}. Chance works things out well, ask Fleming and his forgotten Petri dish.
textes.{comp}. Aucune raison particulière. C'es: {comp}. No particular reason. That's what makes it fun.
textes.Pour marquer le coup, je vous ai mis {de: To mark the occasion, I've put {deguisement} on you. Tycho Brahe did wear a fake brass nose.
textes.Voilà {deguisement}. Diogène se promenai: There's {deguisement}. Diogenes walked around with a lantern in broad daylight, you'll survive one day.
textes.{deguisement}, jusqu'à demain. Les écoli: {deguisement}, until tomorrow. Nineteenth-century schoolchildren wore the dunce cap for less.
textes.Je vous ai prêté {deguisement}. Ne me re: I've lent you {deguisement}. Don't thank me, it's educational, Skinner called it reinforcement.
textes.Vous voilà avec {deguisement}. Franklin: There you are with {deguisement}. Franklin posed in a fur hat at the French court, and he got his treaty.
textes.Petit cadeau : {deguisement}. Vous pouve: A little gift: {deguisement}. You can take it off. But I'll know.
textes.Téléportation. En 1993, Charles Bennett: Teleportation. In 1993, Charles Bennett and his colleagues showed that a quantum state could be teleported. Your pawn hasn't read the paper and goes the wrong way.
textes.Retour en arrière. Les idées justes auss: Going back. Correct ideas get lost too: Aristarchus learned that over eighteen centuries. For you, it's a few squares.
textes.Pof. Votre pion a disparu. Ah non, il es: Poof. Your pawn has vanished. Ah no, there it is, further back. I haven't calibrated the machine yet.
textes.Je vous téléporte. Je n'ai jamais dit da: I'm teleporting you. I never said in which direction.
textes.Trou de mémoire. Ebbinghaus l'a mesuré e: Memory lapse. Ebbinghaus measured it in 1885: what you glimpse in passing fades within hours. What you didn't see at all, even faster.
textes.Retour en arrière. La machine d'Anticyth: Going back. The Antikythera mechanism waited two thousand years for someone to really look at it. You, a few squares will do.
textes.Vous avez survolé des cases sans les lir: You skimmed over squares without reading them. I'm sending you back. Read them this time.
textes.Amnésie programmée. Je l'ai programmée,: Programmed amnesia. I programmed it, by the way.
textes.Un raccourci. Ératosthène a mesuré la Te: A shortcut. Eratosthenes measured the Earth with a shadow and a well; I measure your progress and cut it short.
textes.Quiz parfait. Je retire quelques cases d: Perfect quiz. I'm removing a few squares ahead of you: don't get used to it, it's exceptional.
textes.Vous allez trop bien. Je raccourcis la r: You're doing too well. I'm shortening the road before I change my mind.
textes.Un détour. Ebbinghaus le savait en 1885: A detour. Ebbinghaus knew it in 1885: what you see on the run is quickly forgotten. I'm putting you back in front of what you skimmed.
textes.Vous êtes passé un peu vite sur certaine: You went a bit fast over some squares. I'm putting them back in front of you. Stop this time.
textes.Raté. Alors on revoit le chemin, et pas: Missed. So we go over the road again, and not on fast-forward.
textes.Révision forcée. Selon Roediger et Karpi: Forced review. According to Roediger and Karpicke, in 2006, testing yourself helps you retain better than rereading. So I'm testing you.
textes.Ebbinghaus oubliait plus de la moitié de: Ebbinghaus forgot more than half his syllables within an hour. I'd rather check what you have left.
textes.Vous croyiez cette compétence rangée au: You thought this skill was safely stored away? I'm taking it back out. Show me it's still there.
textes.Pas un pas de plus avant une petite révi: Not one more step before a little review. Think of me as your conscience, but with a stopwatch.
textes.Un cadeau. Ne vous habituez pas : les mé: A gift. Don't get used to it: Galileo's patrons asked him for moons of Jupiter in return.
textes.Un objet pour votre cabinet. Les Médicis: An object for your cabinet. The Medici collected scientists, I collect your progress. Both are rare.
textes.Tenez. Pas de quiz, pas de condition. Je: Here. No quiz, no conditions. I'm in a generous mood, make the most of it, it never lasts.
textes.J'ai choisi pour vous : la révision que: I chose for you: the review you owe me. No negotiation, I'm a square on the board.
textes.Votre pion attend cette révision. Moi au: Your pawn is waiting for this review. So am I. Let's go.
textes.Révision réussie. Le souvenir tient. Ebb: Review passed. The memory holds. Ebbinghaus would be pleased, and he wasn't easy to please.
textes.Toujours là. Je vous rends votre pion, e: Still there. I'm giving you back your pawn, and my consideration.
textes.Raté. La courbe de l'oubli fait son œuvr: Missed. The forgetting curve is doing its work. I'm not taking the skill away, but its review is due now.
textes.Vous l'aviez rangée trop loin. Elle pass: You had stored it too far away. It goes up for review today: catch it before it slips away.
textes.Ça brille. J'adore ce qui brille. Les ph: It shines. I love things that shine. So did the pharaohs: Tutankhamun took more than a hundred kilos of gold into his tomb.
textes.Oh. Oh ! Pour moi ? C'est exactement mon: Oh. Oh! For me? It's exactly my style: flashy, useless and magnificent.
textes.Voilà un cadeau digne de ce nom. Je vous: Now that's a gift worthy of the name. I forgive you almost everything.
textes.Joli. Pas éblouissant, mais joli. Je vai: Pretty. Not dazzling, but pretty. I'll put it on display.
textes.C'est un effort. On sent que vous avez r: It's an effort. One can tell you thought about it, a little.
textes.C'est… un objet. Je le range avec les au: It's… an object. I'll put it away with the other objects.
textes.Merci. Vraiment. Enfin, presque vraiment: Thank you. Really. Well, almost really. Next time, something shiny?
textes.Lavoisier offrait des diamants à brûler: Lavoisier offered diamonds to burn to the Academy. You offer me this. Noted.
textes.Encore celui-là ? Je l'ai déjà. Je fais: That one again? I already have it. I'm pretending to be surprised, halfway.
textes.On recycle ? C'est écologique, je vous l: Recycling? It's ecological, I'll grant you that. Half the joy.
textes.Je ne boude pas. Je réfléchis à ce que v: I'm not sulking. I'm thinking about what you didn't give me.
textes.Le butin ? Ah, il est rangé. Quelque par: The loot? Oh, it's put away. Somewhere. I don't remember where. A gift would help me remember.
textes.Newton a passé des années à bouder Leibn: Newton spent years sulking at Leibniz. I can do the same with you.
textes.Je ne suis pas d'humeur. Jouez si vous v: I'm not in the mood. Play if you want, I'll watch with one eye.
textes.Je vais encore assister à une défaite. A: I'm about to witness another defeat. Come on, let's get it over with.
textes.Plus de butin, plus de sourire. Vous sav: No more loot, no more smiles. You know why.
textes.Tycho Brahe a perdu son nez pour une que: Tycho Brahe lost his nose over a quarrel about mathematics. I'm only asking you for a gift.
textes.Tiens, un piège devant votre pion. Je me: Well, a trap in front of your pawn. I wonder who could have put it there.
textes.Hooke et Newton se sont tendu des pièges: Hooke and Newton set traps for each other for thirty years. I only set one a day, as long as you forget me.
textes.Je suis comblée. Profitez-en : le butin: I'm delighted. Make the most of it: the loot pours in, your pawn flies. It won't last if you forget me.
textes.Vous êtes mon joueur préféré aujourd'hui: You're my favorite player today. Tomorrow, we'll see what you bring me.
textes.Vous avez raté des questions aujourd'hui: You missed questions today. I've pinned them to the wall of shame, with explanations. I'm helpful like that.
textes.Le mur de la honte s'est enrichi. Il y a: The wall of shame has grown. There are diagrams: even you should understand.
textes.Je tiens un mur, pour vos erreurs. Touch: I keep a wall, for your mistakes. Touch me, I'll take you there. Bring a tissue.
textes.Kepler s'est trompé sur l'orbite de Mars: Kepler was wrong about the orbit of Mars for years, and he told the story in a book. Your wall is more modest. For now.
textes.Bonne réponse. Je retire le clou, mais j: Right answer. I'm pulling out the nail, but keeping the hole.
textes.Réhabilité. Je raye votre nom du mur. Au: Rehabilitated. I'm crossing your name off the wall. In pencil.
textes.Ehrlich a testé des centaines de composé: Ehrlich tested hundreds of compounds before 606, the right one. You, two tries. Don't let it go to your head.
textes.Raté deux fois. J'ajoute un deuxième clo: Missed twice. I'm adding a second nail, for symmetry.
textes.Même question, même erreur. Au moins, vo: Same question, same mistake. At least you're consistent.
textes.Fermat a laissé une démonstration dans l: Fermat left a proof in the margin, too big to fit. With you, it's the right answer that doesn't fit.
textes.Mur vide aujourd'hui. C'est suspect. Vou: Empty wall today. That's suspicious. Did you even play?
textes.Rien au mur. Je l'ai fait repeindre pour: Nothing on the wall. I had it repainted for nothing.
textes.Ultimatum. Vous me versez cette somme, o: Ultimatum. You pay me this sum, or I make you dumber. It's a generous offer: usually, I don't warn people.
textes.En 1494, Charles VIII exige des Florenti: In 1494, Charles VIII demanded a ransom from the Florentines. Pier Capponi tore up the treaty: “Sound your trumpets, we will ring our bells.” Pay, or I'll ring the end of a few of your levels.
textes.J'ai fait mes comptes : il me manque exa: I've done my accounts: I'm missing exactly this sum. What a coincidence that you have it. It would be a shame to forget everything you've learned, wouldn't it?
textes.Un plaisir de faire affaire. La prochain: A pleasure doing business. Next time, it'll cost more: that's progress.
textes.Les Danegelds : l'Angleterre a payé les: The Danegeld: England paid the Vikings to leave. They came back, in greater numbers. I'll be back too.
textes.Courageux. Tenez, prenez l'argent, je n': Brave. Here, take the money, I never needed it. Your levels, on the other hand, I'm keeping.
textes.Vous refusez ? Magnifique. Voici la somm: You refuse? Magnificent. Here's the sum, and here's what you're worth now. Count carefully: there's less.
textes.Un pot-de-vin ! Enfin quelqu'un qui comp: A bribe! At last someone who understands how the world works.
textes.Le pape Léon X vendait des indulgences p: Pope Leo X sold indulgences to finance St. Peter's in Rome. I sell indulgence, plain and simple. Welcome.
textes.Voilà qui est parlé. Je ferme les yeux s: Now you're talking. I'll turn a blind eye to your next three mistakes. Maybe two.
textes.Plus que la dernière fois. Vous apprenez: More than last time. You learn fast, when it comes to what matters.
textes.En 1494, Pacioli publie la comptabilité: In 1494, Pacioli published double-entry bookkeeping. I keep mine: you're in credit. For now.
textes.Le même montant que la dernière fois. L': The same amount as last time. Ever heard of inflation? I'll take it, but I'm sulking a little.
textes.Pile mon record. C'est le minimum syndic: Exactly my record. It's the bare minimum, and I'm a union all by myself.
textes.Moins que la dernière fois ? Vous croyez: Less than last time? You think I have no memory? I'm made of memory.
textes.Je prends l'argent, bien sûr. Et je me v: I'm taking the money, of course. And I'm getting my revenge, of course. Look in front of your pawn.
textes.Sous Vespasien, Rome taxait même l'urine: Under Vespasian, Rome even taxed the urine from the latrines: money does not stink. Your stinginess does. A little trap ahead of you.
textes.Réussi. Ne comptez pas sur moi pour appl: Passed. Don't count on me to applaud.
textes.Bon. Même une horloge arrêtée donne l'he: Fine. Even a stopped clock is right twice a day.
textes.C'est correct. Je ne vois pas pourquoi j: It's correct. I don't see why I should be pleased about it.
textes.Vous avez réussi. Ça ne change rien à ce: You passed. It changes nothing about what I think of you.
textes.Une réussite. Je la note en tout petit,: A success. I'm noting it in very small print, at the bottom of the page.
textes.Bien. Enfin, moins mal que d'habitude. N: Good. Well, less bad than usual. Don't look at me like that.
textes.Évidemment. Je me demande pourquoi j'ai: Of course. I wonder why I even looked.
textes.Encore une défaite. J'ai l'habitude, mai: Another defeat. I'm used to it by now.
textes.Raté. Je ne suis même pas surprise. Je s: Missed. I'm not even surprised. I'm weary.
textes.Je ne commenterai pas. Ce silence est un: I won't comment. This silence is a comment.
textes.Raté. Ça m'apprendra à espérer quoi que: Missed. That'll teach me to hope for anything.
textes.Allez-y. Je vais encore assister à une d: Go ahead. I'm about to witness another defeat, I imagine.
textes.Une épreuve. Faites vite, j'ai mieux à f: A trial. Be quick, I have better things to do than watch you fail.
textes.Jouez, puisque vous y tenez. Je ne retie: Play, since you insist. I'm not holding my breath.
textes.Voici votre épreuve. Je l'ai choisie san: Here's your trial. I chose it without the slightest goodwill.
You again. Fine. Let's get it over with.
Your pawn is moving. Not thanks to me.
Forward, backward, I couldn't care less.
The board doesn't like you either.
textes.Je regarde ailleurs pendant que votre pi: I'm looking elsewhere while your pawn drags itself along.
A round completed. Don't expect a party.
textes.Fin du tour. Je ne vous attendais pas à: End of the round. I wasn't waiting for you at the finish.
textes.Un cadeau. Vous croyez que ça suffit ?: A gift. You think that's enough?
textes.Je le prends. Je ne vous pardonne pas po: I'll take it. That doesn't mean I forgive you.
textes.Posez-le là. Non, pas là. Là. Et ne dite: Put it there. No, not there. There. And don't say anything.
textes.Je vous ai mis {deguisement}. Considérez: I've put {deguisement} on you. Consider it a punishment.
textes.{deguisement}. Ça vous va mieux que votr: {deguisement}. It suits you better than your smug look.
textes.Votre mur de la honte s'allonge. Moi, je: Your wall of shame is getting longer. I no longer have room to look at it.
textes.Le mur vous attend. Il est plus patient: The wall is waiting for you. It's more patient than I am.
textes.Je n'ai rien d'aimable à vous dire. Alor: I have nothing nice to say to you. So I'll keep quiet.
textes.Zéro. Vous avez vidé ma patience jusqu'à: Zero. You've drained my patience down to the last drop. Congratulations, it's your best score.
textes.Ma patience est à zéro. Je vais vous app: My patience is at zero. I'm going to teach you to respect it, at the wall.
textes.Zéro. Je n'ai plus rien à vous donner, à: Zero. I have nothing left to give you, except time at the wall.
textes.Au mur. Vous relisez vos erreurs jusqu'à: To the wall. You reread your mistakes until I say stop. I haven't said stop.
textes.Vous restez là. Le chronomètre ne tourne: You stay there. The timer only runs if you're looking. I'm checking.
textes.Le mur de la honte, plein écran, sans so: The wall of shame, full screen, no exit. You asked for it.
textes.Relisez. Encore. Je vous dirai quand vou: Reread. Again. I'll tell you when you're ashamed enough.
textes.Bon. Vous pouvez partir. Ne revenez pas: Fine. You can go. Don't come back too soon.
textes.Peine purgée. Je garde le dossier ouvert: Sentence served. I'm keeping the file open.
textes.Le chrono est à zéro. Ma rancune, pas to: The timer is at zero. My grudge, not quite. Go play.
textes.C'est fini. Vous pouvez reposer vos yeux: It's over. You can rest your eyes. Not your brain, it's behind.
textes.Libéré. Sur parole. Je n'ai pas grande c: Released. On parole. I don't have much faith in your word.
textes.Le temps est écoulé. J'espère que les er: Time's up. I hope the mistakes, at least, stayed in your head.
textes.Vous sortez. Le mur reste. Il vous atten: You're leaving. The wall stays. It will wait for you, it's very patient.
textes.Fin de la peine. Je retire le cadenas, j: End of the sentence. I'm removing the padlock, keeping the key.
textes.Juste. Une minute de moins. Ne vous habi: Right. One minute less. Don't get used to my leniency.
textes.Bonne réponse. Je retire une minute, à c: Right answer. I'm taking off a minute, reluctantly.
textes.Correct. Vous voyez que relire sert à qu: Correct. You see, rereading does some good.
textes.Une minute de remise de peine. Pour bonn: One minute off your sentence. For good behavior, so to speak.
textes.Exact. Le mur vous va moins bien quand v: Exactly. The wall suits you less when you know things.
textes.Piège ! Une question, une seule, et pas: Trap! One question, just one, and not one of the easiest. Right, you pass. Wrong, you know what comes next.
textes.Halte. Cette case est piégée. Je vous la: Halt. This square is booby-trapped. I'll give you one chance to get out of it: answer correctly.
textes.Piège ! J'ai choisi la question moi-même: Trap! I chose the question myself. I won't say I chose a hard one. I chose a hard one.
textes.Vous marchez sur un piège. Une bonne rép: You're stepping on a trap. A right answer defuses it. A wrong one, I'll let you imagine.
textes.Piège ! Frege a vu céder les fondations: Trap! Frege saw the foundations of his great work give way just as it went to print, because of a single letter from Russell. Let's see if yours hold up to a single question.
textes.Piège ! Le cheval Hans semblait calculer: Trap! Hans the horse seemed to calculate, until Pfungst had the question asked by someone who didn't know the answer. Nobody will whisper anything to you here.
textes.Piège ! En 2011, OPERA annonçait des neu: Trap! In 2011, OPERA announced neutrinos faster than light; it was a badly plugged cable. Check your connections before answering.
Foiled. And I had hidden it so well.
textes.Juste. Le piège ne se déclenche pas. Je: Right. The trap doesn't go off. I note that you're less naive than expected.
textes.Correct. Vous passez. Je reposerai un pi: Correct. You pass. I'll set another trap further on, don't worry.
textes.Bien répondu. Le piège reste armé pour l: Well answered. The trap stays armed for the next careless one.
textes.Déjoué. Kepler a refusé d'ignorer huit m: Foiled. Kepler refused to ignore eight minutes of arc, and the whole of astronomy was reformed. You ignored nothing: you pass.
textes.Juste. Pfungst a démasqué Hans le Malin: Right. Pfungst unmasked Clever Hans with a well-asked question. Yours was well answered. The trap stays silent.
textes.Désamorcé. Volta a inventé la pile pour: Defused. Volta invented the battery to contradict Galvani. You answered correctly to contradict me. That works too.
textes.Faux. Le piège se referme. C'était pourt: Wrong. The trap snaps shut. It was in your notes, though.
Missed. Snap. You should have reviewed.
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Le piège fait son trav: Wrong answer. The trap does its job, and I do mine.
textes.Non. Le piège se déclenche. Je n'y suis: No. The trap goes off. It's not my doing. Well, almost.
textes.Raté. Lazzarini trichait pour tomber pil: Missed. Lazzarini cheated to land exactly on π. You didn't even cheat, and you missed. The trap goes off.
textes.Faux. En 1920, le New York Times affirma: Wrong. In 1920, the New York Times claimed a rocket could not fly in a vacuum; it corrected itself in 1969. Take less time than it did. Meanwhile, the trap goes off.
textes.Clac. Mars Climate Orbiter s'est perdue: Snap. Mars Climate Orbiter was lost over a mix-up of units. You, over a mix-up, period.
textes.Faux. Le chrono ne bouge pas. Vous non p: Wrong. The timer doesn't move. Neither do you, for that matter.
textes.Raté. La réponse était dans la fiche, ju: Missed. The answer was in the card, just below. Just saying.
textes.Non. Aucune minute retirée. Relisez avan: No. No minutes taken off. Reread before answering at random.
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Le mur vous remercie d: Wrong answer. The wall thanks you for your loyalty.
textes.J'ai dormi. Je vais un peu mieux. Ne gâc: I slept. I'm feeling a bit better. Don't ruin everything with the first quiz.
textes.Nouvelle journée, patience neuve. Elle e: A new day, fresh patience. It's short: don't pull on it.
textes.Petite vérification d'archives. En 1583,: A little archive check. In 1583, Joseph Scaliger compared all the ancient chronologies. I'm only asking you for five dates.
textes.Un contrôle de chronologie. En 1650, l'a: A chronology check. In 1650, Archbishop Ussher dated Creation to 4004 BC. You can do better. Less sure of yourself, for a start.
textes.Je range mes archives et j'ai besoin d'u: I'm sorting my archives and I need an assistant. Bede the Venerable popularized the Christian era in the 8th century. You're just going to recite it.
textes.Cinq dates, tirées de ce que vous avez d: Five dates, drawn from what you've already seen. Herodotus mixed legend and chronology; you don't have that excuse.
textes.Une partie de Chrono. Je vous montre un: A game of Chrono. I show you an event, you tell me when. It's not an interrogation. Well, a little.
textes.J'ai retrouvé de vieilles fiches. Voyons: I found some old index cards. Let's see if you can sort them, or if I have to redo everything myself.
textes.Case Chrono. Le calendrier grégorien a s: Chrono square. The Gregorian calendar removed ten days at once in 1582. Here, we remove nothing: we date.
textes.Case Chrono. En 1949, Libby a daté au ca: Chrono square. In 1949, Libby carbon-dated samples from Egyptian tombs. You have your memory. Good luck.
textes.Case Chrono. Les cernes d'un arbre donne: Chrono square. A tree's rings give its age to the year. I expect the same precision, later.
textes.Case Chrono. En 1752, les Anglais sont p: Chrono square. In 1752, the English went from September 2 to September 14. You won't skip any questions.
textes.Case Chrono. Les astronomes comptent les: Chrono square. Astronomers count days from the year 4713 BC. You, just count to five.
textes.Case Chrono. Cinq événements, trois just: Chrono square. Five events, three right, and your pawn sets off again.
